# Azion WebKit

> The Vue 3 design system of Azion (`@aziontech/webkit` 5.13.0): components, screen blocks with guidelines, and the design foundations, written for agents that build Azion product, marketing and docs screens.

Start every screen from a block (a reviewed, copyable screen), then fill gaps with components. Import each component from its own subpath (`@aziontech/webkit/<name>`), style only through tokens, and keep strings in the locale catalogs. These pages are generated from `catalog.json`; agents with MCP get the same data from `@aziontech/webkit-mcp` (`search_blocks`, `get_block`, `suggest_component`, `get_component`, `list_assets`). The names a component takes for its artwork (illustrations, diagrams, brand marks, icon classes) are listed in the asset foundation pages below; never guess one from a file in `src/`.

Installed copy: `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/llms/`. Every component also has a JSON API next to its page (`components/<name>.json`).

## How this file is cut

- Each component appears with its first example only, its sub-component notes cut to their first sentence, related names without links, and without its right-to-left, internationalization and responsive notes.
- Each block appears with its guidelines, its building blocks as names and its variants as names; the code is on the block page.
- Classes on a component tag: Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot. A component marked style seam says so on its own entry.
- Every page under `llms/` is complete: open it (the path is in the comment above each entry) for every example, part and variant.

# Design tokens

> Every visual decision comes from a token: the token groups, what to use and what lint blocks.

## 1. Foundations — design tokens

**Every visual decision comes from a token.** Raw values are blocked; the token is always
the answer, and using it is what makes light/dark theming work for free.

| Foundation | ✅ Use | ❌ Never |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Color | `var(--primary)` · `var(--bg-surface)` · `var(--text-default)` · `var(--border-default)` · feedback `--success/--warning/--danger/--info` (+ `-contrast`/`-border`) | `#f3652b` · `rgb(…)` · `hsl(…)` · Tailwind palette (`text-blue-600`, `bg-gray-500`) |
| Typography | generated classes — `text-heading-md`, `text-body-sm`, `text-button-lg`, `text-label-md`, `text-overline-md` (font + size + line-height + tracking bundled) | `text-sm` · `leading-*` · `tracking-*` · `font-family` · `text-[length:…]` |
| Spacing | the semantic scale `var(--spacing-2xs…2xl)` — `p-(--spacing-md)`, `gap-(--spacing-sm)` | the primitive numeric scale (`--spacing-1…-96`) · `p-4` when a token applies · `p-[13px]` |
| Shape | `rounded-(--shape-button)` · `--shape-card` · `--shape-control` · `rounded-[inherit]` for pseudo-elements | `rounded-lg` · numeric radii |
| Shadow | `shadow-(--shadow-md)` | bare `shadow-md` · hex/rgb elevation · legacy `--card-shadow` |
| Motion | catalogued `animate-*` utilities + `transition-*` with token durations; **every** motion class pairs with `motion-reduce:` | local `@keyframes` · `animate-[…]` / `duration-[…]` arbitrary values · animation libraries |

If a design needs a color/size that has no token, that is a **theme gap**: record it and
propose the token — never inline the raw value "until the theme catches up".

**Enforced by:** `validate-tokens` (write-time + the CI ratchet) · `webkit/no-hardcoded-color` + the
stylelint config (consumer lint).

---

## The rule

The design system ships tokens. Use them. Never hardcode a raw color or an off-scale value.

## Do

- Use CSS variables from `@aziontech/theme` for color: `var(--primary)`, `var(--bg-surface)`, `var(--text-default)`, `var(--border-default)`, and the other semantic tokens.
- Use one orange, the logo orange `#F3652B`, and never as a text colour: it misses WCAG AA as text on light surfaces. It is `var(--primary)`: a fill behind `--primary-foreground` text (the button, `Tag variant="primary"`, the `HeroTitle` highlight), or a bar, underline, glyph or glow beside text in `--text-default` (the `Quote` name bar, `LinkDirectory` column underlines). The `Eyebrow` carries no orange mark: its only mark is the `//` prefix on marketing headers. A glow starts from `--primary` and fades to transparent, never to a lighter or darker orange.
- Put text on a fill with that fill's pair: every fill colour has a `-foreground` text colour (`--primary` / `--primary-foreground`, `--danger` / `--danger-foreground`); the inverted surface `--bg-contrast` takes `--text-contrast`.
- Use the theme's semantic spacing and radius tokens: `var(--spacing-xs)`, `var(--spacing-md)` (scale `2xs…2xl`), `var(--shape-button)`.
- Use the generated typography classes / tokens for text (`text-button-lg`, and the other named type scales), not raw font sizes.
- Let the class pick the family: headings, titles, body copy and buttons are sans (`text-heading-*` except `text-heading-code-md`, `text-title-*`, `text-body-*`, `text-button-*`); eyebrows, big numbers and code are mono (`text-overline-*`, `text-big-number-*`, `text-label-code-*`, `text-body-code-sm`, `text-body-code-lg`, and `text-heading-code-md` for a code the reader compares by eye, such as a device code). Code that wraps or runs over several lines takes a `text-body-code-*` class, which has a real line height; the `text-label-code-*` set is one row per line, with no leading. The heading and big-number classes change size by breakpoint, so a page never sets its own type scale. A big number never wraps: inside a size container (`@container`) it shrinks to fit `--text-big-number-characters` glyphs (less the `--text-big-number-inset` gap width) on one line, which `Stats` sets for you.
- Weight lives in the role, never in a `font-*` utility. Every role is regular (400) except the `text-title-*` set, which is medium (500): the title of a contained surface, such as a dialog or drawer (`text-title-lg`), a side panel (`text-title-md`), or a popover, card, alert or toast (`text-title-sm`). Those parts already apply it; a page or section heading stays `text-heading-*`, regular, so large display type keeps the brand's light look.
- Keep heading letter spacing in `em`: the heading classes shrink on phones, and a tracking in `rem` stays the same width while the letters get smaller, so a small display heading runs its words together. `text-heading-3xl` tracks at `-0.046em` and `text-heading-2xl` at `-0.053em` from `md` up (2.56px at their desktop size) and both open to `-0.035em` on phones, so word spaces stay readable at 30px; a new heading role with tracking takes `em` or `0`, never `rem` or `px`.
- Import the styles once, near your app entry: `import './webkit.css'` (the theme, `@aziontech/theme/fonts.css` for the Azion font faces, and `./webkit.sources.css`, the WebKit files Tailwind compiles; `npx @aziontech/webkit init` writes it) and `import '@aziontech/icons'` for icons (the colour logos come with `./webkit.css`, compiled only for the logos your sources name).

## Don't

- No hex: never `#fff`, `#0a0a0a`, `text-[#1e40af]`.
- No `rgb(...)` / `rgba(...)` / `hsl(...)` literals for design colors.
- No orange text and no second orange: never `--text-primary` or `--text-brand` (both removed in 6.0, use `--text-default` with a `--primary` mark), `--color-orange-<step>`, `--color-brand-primary-<step>` or `--color-alpha-orange-<step>` other than the logo step `500`. The lighter and darker oranges stay inside the theme (the chart and severity scales use them as data colours). The `off-brand-orange` token check blocks them in components, examples, blocks and the docs and demos apps.
- No raw Tailwind palette: never `bg-blue-600`, `text-red-500`, `border-gray-200`. Those are not the design system's colors.
- No off-scale magic numbers for spacing (`p-[13px]`) when a spacing token exists.
- No inline hex for a colour the theme lacks: that is a design-system gap. Raise it; the full catalog is generated by `@aziontech/theme`.
- No zero with a length unit: write `0`, never `0px` / `0rem` / `0em`. A zero is identical in every unit, so the unit is noise — and it makes the same value read three different ways. This covers tokens, arbitrary values (`p-[0px]`), inline `style`, and authored CSS. Units that carry meaning at zero are fine: `0%`, `0s`, `0deg`, `0fr`. One exception: inside `calc()`/`min()`/`max()`/`clamp()` CSS requires a unit on the zero — there, write `0rem` (never `0px` / `0em`).

## Values and purposes

Every semantic token ships with its value and a one-line purpose: a colour has a light and a dark
value, a length or type class has a base value and the breakpoints it steps to. Ask the MCP
`list_tokens` (a group such as `bg` or `chart`, or one name such as `--bg-surface`), or read
`tokens.values` in `catalog.json` or `llms/foundations/tokens.md`. Pick a token by its purpose, never
by its value: two tokens can share a value today and part tomorrow.

## Design intent

The rules behind the groups, which no single token's purpose states:

- **Surfaces stack in one order.** `--bg-canvas` is the page, `--bg-surface` sits on it (cards,
  panels, tables) and `--bg-surface-raised` floats above a surface (menus, popovers, the chart
  tooltip). A raised layer also takes a shadow through its variable, `shadow-(--shadow-md)`, never
  Tailwind's `shadow-md`: the dark theme redefines every step.
- **Placeholders are translucent.** A loading placeholder uses `--bg-placeholder` and its sweep
  `--bg-placeholder-highlight`, never an opaque surface token: the translucent fill reads on every
  surface, an opaque one only on the surface it was picked against.
- **Two rhythm steps.** `--layout-section-gap` between the sections of a parent,
  `--layout-group-gap` between the parts of one section; tighter `--spacing-*` steps only inside one
  unit. The `--spacing-*` scale grows by breakpoint on its own, so never restate it per breakpoint.
- **Radius by role.** `--shape-card` for cards, panels and dialogs, `--shape-button` for buttons,
  `--shape-control` for fields and chips, `--shape-flat` for a surface that meets an edge.
- **Type by role.** A text class carries family, size, line height and tracking, and steps up by
  breakpoint (the headings and big numbers): choose the class for the job and never add a size,
  `leading-*` or `tracking-*` beside it.
- **Every colour token is a plain colour.** No token is an opacity or a `color-mix()` of another,
  so canvas charts and contrast checks can read it; never fake a lighter step with `opacity`.

## Which color token does which job

A color token names a job, not a hue. Use the component that already does the job, and pick a token
by hand only for your own elements. The table lists what each group is for and the components that
use it, so you can check a choice against a real one.

| Job | Tokens | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main action | `--primary`, `--primary-foreground` | `Button variant="primary"`, `Checkbox` checked, `Progress` fill, `Tag variant="primary"`, `StatusIndicator severity="alt"` |
| Second action | `--secondary`, `--secondary-foreground` | `Button variant="secondary"`, `IconButton`, `Badge variant="secondary"` |
| Brand tint | `--primary-mask`, `--primary-selected` | `RadioGroup` selected card |
| Accent: a live state or connection, never an action | `--accent`, `--accent-foreground` | `Switch` on, `Slider` fill, `Tag variant="accent"`, resize handles in `Sidebar` and `Resizable`, a dragged `Table` row, `FlowDiagram` edges and ports |
| Brand marks: the logo colours | `--primary`, `--brand-blue`, `--brand-blue-foreground` | the logo orange as a mark beside text in `--text-default` or a fill behind `--primary-foreground`, never as text (owner, 2026-11-22): the `Quote` name bar, `LinkDirectory` column underlines, the `HeroTitle` highlight fill, the `CompetitorComparisonSection` group bar, `Tag variant="primary"`, the hovered linked `FeatureItem` underline; the `Eyebrow` cursor in the brand blue (`--brand-blue`, `#0072F5`, the azion.com blue) |
| Selected item | `--bg-selected`, `--border-selected` | selected rows and options in `Table`, `MenuItem`, `DropdownMenu`, `ToggleGroup`, `Select`, `Combobox`, `Trace`; `RadioGroup` card and `Chip` borders |
| Selected tab | `--secondary-mask` | the sliding indicator in `Tabs` |
| Hover and press | `--bg-hover`, `--bg-active`, `--bg-mask` | every interactive component (`--bg-mask` is the hover layer on `Button variant="outline"` and `variant="ghost"`) |
| Surfaces | `--bg-canvas`, `--bg-surface`, `--bg-surface-raised` | page, cards and panels, `Avatar`, striped `Table` rows |
| Inverted surface | `--bg-contrast`, `--text-contrast` | `Tooltip`, `Tag variant="contrast"` |
| Behind a modal | `--bg-backdrop` | `Dialog`, `Drawer` |
| Status message | `--success`, `--warning`, `--danger`, `--info` with `-border`, `-foreground`, `-mark` and `-mask` | `Tag`, `Badge`, `Trace` spans, `Button variant="danger"`. The fill is the box, `-border` its edge, `-foreground` its icon or text. A status mark or icon that stands on the page (the `StatusIndicator` dot, the `OutcomeIcon` disc, the check and cross of a Do / Don't pair) is `-mark`; `-foreground` is near black in light, made for its pale fill, and reads as no colour on a surface. An `Alert` (and the `Tracker` error line) is a soft tint: `-mask` behind `--text-default` text, its `-border`, the icon in `-mark`; an info `Alert` is neutral (`--bg-surface-raised`, `--border-default`, icon `--info-mark`) because it stays on screen (ALERT-1). |
| Severity | `--severity-critical`, `-high`, `-medium`, `-low` | the bars of `SeverityTag` only |
| Links | `--text-link`, `--text-link-hover` | `Button variant="link"`, links in text |
| Error text on the page | `--text-danger` | `FieldError` message, a field error in `FieldDescription`, any error sentence on a surface (red.600 in light, red.200 in dark). Not `--danger-foreground`, which is text on the `--danger` fill |
| Form field outline | `--border-input` | the resting and disabled outline of `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `NumberInput`, `PasswordInput`, `OtpInput`, the date fields, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch` |
| Charts | `--chart-*` | the chart components; series, status and severity colors are not interchangeable |

Defined but not used by any component yet: `--accent-mask`, `--accent-selected`,
`--bg-surface-overlay`, `--severity-info`. Do not build on them until a component does.

## Contrast: APCA and WCAG 2

Every colour pair passes **both** WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text, icons and UI marks) and
APCA (0.0.98G-4g, the `|Lc|` value):

| What sits on the colour | APCA target | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Body text | Lc 75 | `--text-default` on the surfaces |
| Other text (labels, captions, button text) | Lc 60 | `--text-muted`, links, `--text-danger`, every `-foreground` on its fill |
| Icons | Lc 45 | a status icon standing on a surface in `--success-mark`, `--warning-mark`, `--danger-mark` (the Do / Don't check and cross); `-foreground` only on its own fill |
| Solid marks (dots, bars, chart series) | Lc 30 | `--chart-series-*`, `--severity-*`, `--border-selected`, the ring |
| Borders and dividers | Lc 15 | `--border-default`, `--border-muted`, `--border-input`, `--danger-border` (also WCAG 3:1, the invalid field outline) |

The theme test `packages/theme/test/apca-contrast.test.mjs` computes Lc for these pairs on
`--bg-canvas`, `--bg-surface` and `--bg-surface-raised` in light and dark, and fails a pair below
its target unless it is listed here. A new token pair, or a value change, must pass before it ships.

Exceptions (the one list; `accepted` means the owner chose the look, `open` waits for a decision):

| Pair | Theme | Lc | Status | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--primary-foreground` on `--primary` | light, dark | 46.6 | accepted | The black label on the logo orange `#F3652B` matches the logo (2026-11-14). WCAG 6.71:1 passes. |
| `--border-default` on the surfaces | dark | 0 | accepted | Dark dividers keep the original `#2B2B2B` look (2026-11-16). Form outlines stay `--border-input` `#535353`. |
| `--border-muted` on the surfaces | dark | 0 | accepted | Dark muted dividers keep the original `#242424` look (2026-11-16). |
| `--border-muted` on `--bg-canvas` | light | 13.3 | accepted | Light muted divider on the page canvas, target Lc 15: kept as is (owner decision 2026-11-16). |
| `--text-muted` on `--bg-surface-raised` | dark | 59.9 | accepted | Dark muted text in menus and popovers, target Lc 60: kept as is (owner decision 2026-11-16). |
| `--border-input` on `--bg-surface-raised` | dark | 14.6 | accepted | Dark field outline inside a raised panel, target Lc 15: kept as is (owner decision 2026-11-16). |

Do not "fix" an accepted pair; do not add a pair to this list without the design owner's decision.

## Chart palettes

WebKit ships **one** chart palette: the values of the `--chart-*` tokens. There are no alternate
palettes in `@aziontech/theme`. An app that offers other palettes (the console API's palette picker)
sets these variables on the dashboard's root element, and every chart inside re-colours:

| A palette may set | A palette never sets |
| --- | --- |
| `--chart-series-1` … `--chart-series-8` | `--chart-series-other` (the grey a ninth series folds into) |
| `--chart-sequential-1` (lowest) … `--chart-sequential-7` | `--chart-status-*` and `--severity-*` (they mean a state) |
| `--chart-diverging-negative` (`-2`, `-3`), `--chart-diverging-neutral`, `--chart-diverging-positive` (`-3`, `-2`) | `--chart-grid`, `--chart-axis`, `--chart-label`, `--chart-crosshair`, `--chart-tooltip-*` (the chrome) |

- **Gridlines are half a border.** `--chart-grid` (the lines behind the marks) sits halfway, in
  perceived lightness, between `--border-default` and `--bg-surface`: it keeps half the border's
  contrast, so the card edge reads before the grid and the grid never competes with the data. Light
  `#E5E5E5`, dark `#1A1A1A`. The axis baseline stays `--chart-axis`, at full border strength. The
  value is a primitive step, never `color-mix()` or an opacity: tokens resolve to a plain colour so
  canvas charts and the contrast tests can read them. If `--border-default` or `--bg-surface`
  changes, pick the new halfway step; `chart-role.test.mjs` fails until you do.
- **Both themes.** A palette supplies a light and a dark value for every variable it sets (set the
  dark values under `[data-theme='dark']`); a half palette breaks the theme switch.
- **Same checks as the default.** Every series value clears 3:1 (WCAG) and Lc 30 (APCA) on
  `--bg-surface`, `--bg-canvas` and `--chart-tooltip-bg` in its theme, the eight series are eight
  distinct colours, and a series keeps its hue family across the theme switch. These are the checks
  `packages/theme/test/chart-role.test.mjs` and `apca-contrast.test.mjs` run on the default.
- **Diverging runs in three or seven steps.** Three: `--chart-diverging-negative`, `-neutral`,
  `-positive`. Seven, from the negative end to the positive end: `-negative`, `-negative-2`,
  `-negative-3`, `-neutral`, `-positive-3`, `-positive-2`, `-positive`. The intermediate steps keep
  the end's hue and lose chroma toward the neutral; every coloured step clears 3:1 and Lc 30 on the
  chart surfaces, and neighbours stay at least 0.05 apart in OKLab (`chart-role.test.mjs`). A palette
  that sets the diverging variables sets all seven.
- **Eight series, then Other.** A palette has at most eight series; a chart with more folds the
  rest into `--chart-series-other`. A palette never adds `--chart-series-9`.
- **Where.** On your own root element, or on a webkit tag as a static `style`, an object-literal
  `:style` or `[--chart-series-1:…]` classes; `webkit/no-style-override` allows exactly these
  variables (`CHART_PALETTE_VARIABLES` in `@aziontech/webkit/eslint-plugin`) and nothing else.

## One outline per toolbar

Outlined controls side by side in a header or a toolbar share one border colour: the toolbar's
`--border-default`, the outline of `IconButton variant="outline"`, `Button variant="outline"` and
`SearchTrigger`. `--border-input` is the form field outline; it belongs to a text field you type in
and to a field in a form, never to a button-like control in a header. A header language switch is
`LanguageSelect variant="ghost"`, not a field-sized `Select`; a header switcher of any other kind is
`Select variant="ghost"`.

- **Do:** a search field, a ghost `LanguageSelect`, outline icon buttons: one border colour in the row.
- **Don't:** a field-sized `Select` (`--border-input`) between outline icon buttons (`--border-default`).

The styled visual suite checks it on every docs page, example and block (`toolbar-outlines.spec.ts`).

## One height per toolbar row

Controls side by side in one toolbar row are the same height, border included: give them all
the same `size` (`medium` is 32px for a button, an input, a select and a date picker). Never mix
sizes in one row, and never stretch one control with a class.

- **Do:** a filter field, a `DateRangePicker` and outline icon buttons, all `size="medium"`.
- **Don't:** a `size="large"` select between `size="medium"` buttons, or an `h-9` on one control.

The styled visual suite checks it on every docs page, example and block (`toolbar-heights.spec.ts`).

## Use a variant only when the component has it

A token pair is not a variant. `--accent` and `--accent-foreground` exist, but `Button` has no accent
kind, so there is no accent button: an "Upgrade" or "New" call to action is `Button variant="primary"`
or `variant="secondary"`. Before you draw or build a variant, check that the component lists it in its
`variant` or `severity` union in `catalog.json` (or the MCP `get_component`). If it is not there, use
one that is.

- No `--accent` fill on a button, link or call to action.
- No `--accent` or `--primary` for a selected row, item or option: that is `--bg-selected`.
- No status colors (`--success`, `--danger`, …) to tell categories apart: they mean a state.
- No `--severity-*` outside a severity scale.

## Example

### Do

```html
<div class="bg-(--bg-surface) text-(--text-default) p-(--spacing-md) rounded-(--shape-card)">
  ...
</div>
```

### Don't

```html
<div class="bg-[#161616] text-white p-[13px] m-[0px] rounded-md">...</div>
```

## Semantic tokens

200 semantic tokens with their value and a one-line purpose: pick a token by its purpose, never by its value. `catalog.json` holds the same export under `tokens.values`, and the MCP tool `list_tokens` returns it per group or per token.

### Colours (light and dark)

| Token | Light | Dark | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--primary` | `#F3652B` | `#F3652B` | The main action fill: the primary button, a checked checkbox, a progress fill. |
| `--primary-mask` | `#FE601F33` | `#FE601F33` | A translucent primary tint behind brand-highlighted content. |
| `--primary-selected` | `#FE601F33` | `#FE601F33` | The translucent primary tint of a selected brand card. |
| `--primary-foreground` | `#000000` | `#000000` | Text and icons on a --primary fill. |
| `--secondary` | `#0A0A0A` | `#FFFFFF` | The second action fill: the secondary button and the icon button. |
| `--secondary-mask` | `#00000005` | `#FFFFFF1A` | The sliding indicator under the selected tab. |
| `--secondary-selected` | `#0A0A0A` | `#FFFFFF` | The selected day of a date picker, drawn in the secondary fill. |
| `--secondary-foreground` | `#FFFFFF` | `#000000` | Text and icons on a --secondary fill. |
| `--accent` | `#005FCC` | `#99C9FF` | A live state or a connection, never an action: a switch on, a slider fill, diagram edges. |
| `--accent-mask` | `#0072F51A` | `#0072F51A` | A translucent accent tint; defined, not used by any component yet. |
| `--accent-selected` | `#005FCC` | `#99C9FF` | A selected accent mark; defined, not used by any component yet. |
| `--accent-foreground` | `#FFFFFF` | `#000000` | Text and icons on an --accent fill. |
| `--brand-blue` | `#0072F5` | `#0072F5` | The azion.com blue for brand marks only, such as the eyebrow cursor. |

# Color

> Semantic color roles, light and dark themes, and the color tokens by group.

## Purpose

A screen that "looks right" is only half-verified — it looks right in the theme you happened to open.
The `@aziontech/theme` tokens make both themes free **if** you style through them: a token names a
**role** (`--bg-surface`, `--text-default`, `--border-default`), and its value flips per theme
automatically. The moment a hex, an `rgb()`, or a Tailwind palette color (`bg-zinc-900`,
`text-white`) lands on an element, you have hard-coded one theme and broken the other. This skill
fixes the discipline that keeps every screen theme-correct with no per-theme branches.

## How to use

- `/webkit-theming-dark-mode` — apply the token discipline to any screen you build in this
  conversation, and switch to the dark check before declaring it done.
- `/webkit-theming-dark-mode <file>` — review the file and report, per gap: the quoted line, the
  hard-coded color, and the semantic token that replaces it.

## How to find the tokens and components

Never guess a token or an import path. Resolve both from the contract, not from memory:

- Token names: read **`node_modules/@aziontech/theme`** (the semantic color set) — a name that is not
  defined there does not exist. Roles you will reach for most: `--bg-canvas`, `--bg-surface`,
  `--bg-surface-raised`, `--bg-surface-overlay`, `--text-default`, `--text-secondary`,
  `--border-default`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`.
- Components: ask the **webkit MCP** (`suggest_component`) or read
  **`node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/catalog.json`** — every key under `imports` is a real subpath.

## How theming works — the device decides, an attribute pins

With no theme pinned, the tokens **follow the device**: light values by default, dark values while the
OS prefers dark (`prefers-color-scheme`, in CSS alone, so there is no flash). **Pin a theme** with
`data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"` on the `<html>` element (the tokens also respond to a
`.dark` class on any ancestor). Nothing else changes; the same `var(--bg-surface)` resolves to the
value of whichever theme applies. So every screen must work in both themes from day one: a user on a
dark device sees dark without you doing anything.

```html
<!-- an app that has not been checked in dark yet: pin light -->
<html data-theme="light"></html>
```

A runtime toggle is just a write to that attribute — the whole tree re-themes with no re-render:

```ts
function toggleTheme() {
  const el = document.documentElement
  el.dataset.theme = el.dataset.theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark'
}
```

`data-theme="system"` follows the device explicitly (the same as no attribute; useful on a subtree
inside a pinned page). Each theme sets `color-scheme`, so native scrollbars and form controls match, and
Tailwind's `dark:` variant follows the same three hooks. For a settings control, let
`useColorMode()` store the choice (`system`, `light` or `dark`) and bind it to `ThemeSwitcher`; inline
`colorModeScript` in the document head so the stored choice applies before the first paint:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  import ThemeSwitcher from '@aziontech/webkit/theme-switcher'
  import { useColorMode } from '@aziontech/webkit/use-color-mode'

  const { mode } = useColorMode()
</script>

<template>
  <ThemeSwitcher
    v-model="mode"
    aria-label="Theme"
  />
</template>
```

Under a Content-Security-Policy that blocks inline scripts, allow this one script by its hash instead of
`'unsafe-inline'`. The hash covers the exact text of `colorModeScript`, and a WebKit test fails when the
script changes without this line:

```text
script-src 'self' 'sha256-Mr2TXUqeQwYxZgSb0xwpzGaZroVMkDVGwawpZp7IcjY='
```

A starting policy for an app built on WebKit, sent as response headers by the server or the edge:

```text
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'sha256-Mr2TXUqeQwYxZgSb0xwpzGaZroVMkDVGwawpZp7IcjY='; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
```

`object-src 'none'` also stops `FilePreview` from showing a PDF; where an app previews documents (an AI chat that draws document parts), use `object-src 'self' blob:` instead.

`style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is there because components set a few inline styles and custom properties;
add the origins your app frames (`frame-src`, for `Embed`) or fetches (`connect-src`).

## The core rule — style through the role, never the value

A token carries the role; its value is the theme's job. Reference the role and both themes are handled
at once. Bind a raw color and you have pinned one theme.

```vue
<!-- ✅ role-based: correct in both themes, no branches -->
<div class="bg-(--bg-surface) text-(--text-default) border border-(--border-default)">
  <span class="text-(--primary)">Active</span>
</div>

<!-- ❌ value-based: legible in one theme, broken in the other -->
<div class="bg-white text-[#1a1a1a] border border-zinc-200">
  <span class="text-blue-600">Active</span>
</div>
```

This is the same token catalog the design-system components render with, so a screen built on tokens
sits seamlessly next to `<Button>`, `<Card>`, and the rest in either theme.

## Elevation in dark = a lighter surface, not a heavier shadow

Shadows barely read on a dark ground — stacking depth comes from **surface lightness**, not from a
bigger `box-shadow`. That is exactly what the surface tokens encode: `--bg-surface-raised` and
`--bg-surface-overlay` are _lighter_ than `--bg-surface` in dark, and correctly _shadowed/tinted_ in
light. Use the role for the layer and both themes get the right depth cue. Discover the exact surface
names from the theme package; never invent a `surface-3`.

```vue
<!-- page → card → menu: each layer is a role, depth reads in both themes -->
<div class="bg-(--bg-canvas)">
  <div class="bg-(--bg-surface)">...</div>
  <div class="bg-(--bg-surface-raised)">popover / menu</div>
</div>
```

## Loading placeholders use a translucent role, not a surface

A surface token is opaque and tuned for one background, so a skeleton built from one is only legible on
the surface it was picked against — and it inverts badly across themes. `--bg-placeholder` (the fill)
and `--bg-placeholder-highlight` (the sweep) are **translucent**: they composite over whatever layer
they sit on, so the same token holds its contrast on canvas, surface, raised and overlay alike, in both
themes. Keep the fill as `background-color` and put the sweep in a gradient whose other stops are
`transparent`, so the animated and static states share one base tone.

```vue
<!-- ❌ opaque surface as a placeholder: near-invisible on a card in light -->
<div class="bg-(--bg-surface-overlay)" />
<!-- ✅ translucent placeholder role, correct on any layer in both themes -->
<div class="bg-(--bg-placeholder)" />
```

Prefer the design system's `Skeleton` component over hand-rolling this — it already pairs the tokens
with the shimmer animation and its reduced-motion fallback.

## Don't fight the tokens with `dark:` overrides

If a role has a token, the token already handles both themes — adding `dark:bg-…` on top is redundant
at best and drifts the two themes apart at worst. Reach for Tailwind's `dark:` variant **only** for
the rare property no token expresses (and even then, prefer proposing the missing token). A screen
full of `dark:` overrides is a screen that stopped trusting the tokens.

```vue
<!-- ❌ re-implements what --bg-surface already does per theme -->
<div class="bg-white dark:bg-zinc-900 text-black dark:text-white">
<!-- ✅ one role, no per-theme branch -->
<div class="bg-(--bg-surface) text-(--text-default)">
```

## A card that needs zero changes across themes

Every color here is a role. Toggle `data-theme` and it re-themes with no edit — surface, text, border,
and accent all move together.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'

  function toggleTheme() {
    const el = document.documentElement
    el.dataset.theme = el.dataset.theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark'
  }
</script>

<template>
  <article
    class="rounded-(--shape-card) p-(--spacing-md)
           bg-(--bg-surface) text-(--text-default)
           border border-(--border-default)"
  >
    <h3 class="text-(--text-default)">Workload health</h3>
    <p class="text-(--text-secondary)">Requests are within normal range.</p>
    <span class="text-(--primary)">View details</span>
    <Button
      label="Toggle theme"
      variant="secondary"
      class="mt-(--spacing-sm)"
      @click="toggleTheme"
    />
  </article>
</template>
```

## Accents that appear on both grounds

A brand accent tuned for a white page can vibrate or wash out on a dark one. Use the theme's own
accent tokens (`--primary` and friends), which are already balanced per theme; if you must introduce a
new accent, verify its **contrast against both** `--bg-canvas` values and desaturate it until it reads
on both — do not ship a single saturated hex for both grounds.

## Validate BOTH themes before "done"

A screen tested in one theme is **not done**. The `webkit-ui-verify` runtime check screenshots the
view in light **and** dark — run it, look at both, and confirm text contrast, surface separation, and
accents all hold. A regression that only shows in dark is invisible until someone opens dark mode in
production; the two-theme screenshot is what catches it first.

## Hard rules

- Style through **semantic tokens** only — no hex, `rgb()`/`hsl()`, or Tailwind palette color
  (`bg-white`, `text-zinc-900`, `border-slate-200`) anywhere on the screen.
- With no attribute the theme follows the device; `data-theme="light"` / `data-theme="dark"` on
  `<html>` (or a `.dark` ancestor) pins it. Don't ship a second stylesheet or a JS color map for dark.
- Depth in dark comes from **lighter surface tokens** (`--bg-surface-raised` / `--bg-surface-overlay`),
  not a heavier shadow.
- No `dark:` override for a role a token already covers; reserve `dark:` for the property no token
  expresses, and prefer proposing the token.
- Every new accent is contrast-checked and desaturated for **both** grounds.
- A screen is done only after it is verified in **both** themes (`webkit-ui-verify` two-theme
  screenshots).

## Review output

For `/webkit-theming-dark-mode <file>`, list gaps grouped by element. Each:

```
✗ WorkloadCard.vue:14  class="bg-white text-zinc-900 border-slate-200"
  theme: hard-coded light values — dark renders white-on-dark, unreadable.
  fix: bg-(--bg-surface) text-(--text-default) border-(--border-default)
```

End with: `theme-safe (both themes)` or `N gaps — fix before verifying`.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Every color on the screen is a semantic token — zero hex / rgb / palette / one-theme values.
- [ ] Dark is driven by `data-theme` / `.dark`, not a duplicate stylesheet or JS color branch.
- [ ] Stacked layers use surface-role tokens; depth reads correctly in dark without heavier shadows.
- [ ] No `dark:` override stands in for a role a token already carries.
- [ ] The screen was screenshotted and checked in **both** light and dark before being called done.

# Typography

> The generated typography classes: font, size, line height and tracking in one class.

Text uses the generated classes from `@aziontech/theme`. Each one bundles font family, size, line height and tracking, so a raw Tailwind size (`text-sm`), `leading-*`, `tracking-*` or a `font-family` is never needed and lint blocks them.

## Classes

| Class | Base size | Steps to | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text-amount-lg` | `1.875rem` | sm: 3rem, md: 3.5rem | The largest price or amount. |
| `text-amount-md` | `1.25rem` | md: 1.5rem | A price or amount in a card. |
| `text-amount-sm` | `1rem` |  | A compact price or amount. |
| `text-big-number-lg` | `1.5rem` | sm: 2.25rem, md: 3.5rem | The largest numeric figure on one line, shrunk to fit its container. |
| `text-big-number-md` | `1.25rem` | sm: 1.5rem, md: 2.25rem | A numeric figure in a stat card, on one line, shrunk to fit. |
| `text-big-number-sm` | `1rem` | sm: 1.25rem | A compact numeric figure, on one line, shrunk to fit. |
| `text-big-number-unit` |  |  | A word unit in a big-number figure (ms, Tbps), in the text face so it keeps its case. |
| `text-body-2xs` | `0.75rem` |  | The smallest body text, such as footnotes. |
| `text-body-code-lg` | `1rem` |  | Wrapping or multi-line code at the 16px touch size, with a real line height. |
| `text-body-code-sm` | `0.75rem` |  | A monospace paragraph that wraps. |
| `text-body-lg` | `1rem` | md: 1.125rem | Lead paragraphs. |
| `text-body-md` | `1rem` |  | Body copy. |
| `text-body-prose-md` | `1rem` |  | Long-form prose at a relaxed line height. |
| `text-body-sm` | `0.875rem` |  | Secondary body copy and descriptions. |
| `text-body-xs` | `0.75rem` |  | Captions and helper text. |
| `text-button-lg` | `0.875rem` |  | The label of a large button. |
| `text-button-md` | `0.75rem` |  | The label of a medium or small button. |
| `text-heading-2xl` | `1.875rem` | sm: 2.25rem, md: 3rem -0.053em 0 | A marketing section heading. |
| `text-heading-2xs` | `0.875rem` |  | A small title or a wordmark written in type, a flat 14px. |

# Spacing and layout

> Page levels, the five measures, the two rhythm steps and the spacing scale.

## 1. Three levels, and no fourth

Every page is the same three nested decisions. Each level owns exactly one, and no level restates
another's.

```vue
<template>
  <!-- the page body, in the layout's <main> -->
  <div class="layout-column layout-boundary flex min-w-0 flex-col">
    <PageHeader title="Applications" />

    <section class="layout-section-start flex flex-col gap-(--layout-section-gap)">
      <section class="flex flex-col gap-(--layout-group-gap)">…</section>
      <form class="flex flex-col gap-(--layout-group-gap)">…</form>
    </section>
  </div>
</template>
```

- **The heading** is `PageHeader` (`@aziontech/webkit/page-header`): the page's only h1, its
  description, and the page's own actions. A band inside the page is titled by a `Subheader`
  (`@aziontech/webkit/subheader`), or by a `SettingsGroup` (`@aziontech/webkit/settings-group`)
  on a settings page — never by a second hand-written header block.
- **The boundary** (`layout-boundary`) sets the page's inset from the app chrome — sides, top and
  bottom — and its top inset is the space above the heading.
- **The parent section** spaces the sections inside it with `--layout-section-gap`. Every page carries
  one, whether it holds one section or seven, so the shape reads the same everywhere and a second
  section needs no rework.
- **Each section** spaces its own parts with `--layout-group-gap`: its title over its card, its
  controls row over the table those controls narrow.

**The page stack never carries a vertical `gap`.** It holds the heading and one element below it, and
that element carries the step. A `gap` is right on the parent section (within it, every child _is_ a
section, so one rule spaces them all) and wrong on the page stack (the heading and the parent are
different kinds of thing).

**`layout-section-start` goes on exactly one element per page stack** — the parent section directly
below the heading. Never on a section _inside_ the parent: `gap` and `margin` both apply in a flex
column, so the two add up and that section lands at twice the step.

It is safe to carry unconditionally. The utility zeroes its own margin when it happens to render
first, so a page with no heading, or one whose opening band is a `v-if`, opens at exactly the
boundary step. `v-if` bands are absent from the DOM, so `:first-child` reads the rendered truth.

## 2. The measure — five columns, picked by the payload

A page does not pick its own `max-w-*`. It carries one of five column classes, chosen by **what the
page's payload is**.

| Class | Measure | Today | Payload |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layout-column` | `--layout-measure` | 1620px | **The standard page container.** Lists, home, product overviews, detail dashboards |
| `layout-column-focused` | `--layout-measure-focused` | 1024px | One task, still multi-column — a deploy hero, a running log, a review column |
| `layout-column-form` | `--layout-measure-form` | 1024px | Settings and in-page edit forms — a single stacked column of fields |
| `layout-form-create` | `--layout-measure-form-create` | 1192px | Dedicated create pages (also retunes the control cap — see §7) |
| `layout-column-content` | `--layout-measure-content` | 876px | Prose — documentation, blog |

`layout-column` is the default. Take a different one only when the payload is **narrower**, never
wider.

Three things worth internalizing about the choice:

- **A form is capped for pairing, not for legibility.** Past ~1200px the extra width lands entirely
  inside the controls: the label sits at the far left of a 1600px row from the input it names, and
  the eye travels the whole measure to pair them.
- **Prose is capped by typography, not by layout.** Past ~90 characters the eye loses the start of
  the next line on the return sweep. That limit has nothing to do with how wide the payload is, which
  is why it is far tighter than every other measure and why it does **not** move when a rail collapses
  and frees up room.
- **The cap is named for the payload, never for the section.** A documentation _article_ takes the
  content measure; the documentation _home_ — a directory of cards, not read line by line — takes a
  wider one. What picks the column is the payload, never the URL.

**Full-bleed is the absence of all five**, never a `w-full`.

**The band picks the class, not the file.** A tab showing a table is measured as data even when the
tab beside it is a form. And within one band the class must be the same everywhere it has to align —
the scrolling body _and_ its sticky bar — or the footer's buttons drift right of the form they submit.

**Keep the measure identical across sibling states.** A page that changes width when the account
gains its first resource reads as two different pages; give the empty state the same column as the
populated one.

### Why the numbers are what they are

The measures are rungs of the shared container ladder — an anchored geometric progression. A page
snaps to the scale; the scale does not bend to a page. If a review asks for "about 1300", the answer
is the rung, not a new number.

## 3. The boundary is not part of the measure

`layout-boundary` sets all three insets; `layout-boundary-inline` sets the sides only, for a band
that takes the page's side inset but owns its own vertical padding (a sticky bar, whose `py` is a bar
height, not a page boundary).

Who carries it depends on the shell:

- Inside `ConsoleLayout` (and every app layout) the page carries the boundary **itself**: the layout
  pads nothing, so the body puts `layout-boundary` on the same block as the measure.
- A **padded** container you own (a split view's pane, a scroll box around a capped block) can carry
  the boundary _outside_ the capped block instead, so the measure lands as content width.

Those two would normally disagree. With `box-sizing: border-box`, 1620px of cap minus 24px a side is
a 1572px content column — 48px narrower than the same measure gives a padded page. That is the
measure describing something other than content, which is the one job it has.

**So when the boundary rides along, the cap grows by exactly the inset it now contains.** Both shapes
resolve to the same content column at every viewport, which means a page can gain or lose its own
boundary — pick up a tab bar, drop one, move from padded to self-padded — without moving a pixel.

This is automatic, and it is the reason a sticky bar works:

```vue
<template>
  <div class="overflow-auto">
    <form class="layout-column-form layout-boundary-inline flex flex-col pt-(--layout-section-gap)">
      …
    </form>
  </div>

  <footer
    class="layout-column-form layout-boundary-inline sticky bottom-0 flex justify-end gap-(--spacing-sm) py-(--spacing-md)"
  >
    <Button
      variant="ghost"
      label="Cancel"
    />
    <Button label="Save" />
  </footer>
</template>
```

Same column class, same inline boundary, on both — so the bar's buttons land inside the form's own
right edge by construction. `SaveBar variant="plain"` (`@aziontech/webkit/save-bar`) is this footer,
already carrying `layout-column-form layout-boundary-inline`; reach for it instead of writing the bar. Naming the inline half is what lets the measure rule see a self-inset
band and treat it exactly like the scrolling body it sits under.

**The boundary is padding, never margin.** A top margin on an `h-full` child of a padded scroll box
overflows by exactly the margin — `h-full` resolves against the parent's content box, the margin sits
outside it — and the overflow lands as a silent clip at the bottom of a table.

## 4. Rhythm — two steps, and no third

| Token | Today | Between |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--layout-section-gap` | `--spacing-xl` | the sections of a parent |
| `--layout-group-gap` | `--spacing-md` | the parts inside one section |

That is the whole scale. A third step is how a page starts drifting from its siblings.

The section step is deliberately one stop larger than the boundary step: the page opens tight under
its heading, then separates its sections more firmly than the parts inside any one of them. The space
_above_ the first section belongs to the boundary and the space _between_ sections belongs to the
parent, so either retunes without the other — and every page follows, because no page restates a step.

**Prefer the `gap` form.** The band element is normally the wrapper, and `gap-(--layout-group-gap)` on
it names the group in the markup.

**`layout-group-start` is the fallback** for the one case a parent cannot cover: a group whose parts
are already direct siblings of the page stack, where adding a wrapper is the wrong answer.

A tab strip and its panel are one band too: the panel starts one group step below the strip.
`Tabs.Content` carries that top padding itself (a Markdown `<Tabs>` in `DocMarkdown` renders on it too), so never add a margin or a
`gap` between `Tabs.List` and the panels.

A common miss: a controls row and the table it narrows are **one band**, joined at the group step.
The section step is the gap _above_ the band, not inside it.

**A filter sits above everything it changes, and changes nothing above it.** The eye reads a filter
as acting on what follows it, so a control that also changes content above it (a year picker beside a
chart that also rewrites the metric tiles over the chart) breaks the link between cause and effect. A
page-wide filter opens the band it filters, over every metric, chart and list it narrows; a filter in
a card header narrows that card and what sits below it, never a card above. When a part above must
stay unfiltered, its label says so ("this year", "all categories").

**The group step is the floor.** No two regions of a page — a banner (`Alert`), a card, a framed
table, a section heading — ever sit closer than `--layout-group-gap`. The usual way to break it is a
parent section with no `gap` of its own: a page-level `Alert` above the first `SettingsGroup` lands
flush against that section's heading, because the band only spaces itself from the bands before it.
A banner that speaks for the whole page is a child of the parent section like any band, and the
parent's `gap-(--layout-section-gap)` spaces it. Tighter steps belong _inside_ one unit — a card's
rows, a list's items, a chat message's parts, a label over its own field.

## 5. Every value is a reference

Layout tokens are a **derived** group: each one is a `var()` reference to the spacing or container
scale. Never a literal length.

That indirection is the point. The spacing scale is already fluid — `--spacing-lg` is 1rem, then
1.5rem from `sm` — and `var()` is substituted at _use_ time on the element, so a layout token follows
the breakpoint override without owning a breakpoint map of its own. A layout token with its own map
would duplicate the spacing scale and let the two drift.

Practical consequence: you never write a responsive variant for the boundary or the rhythm. They are
already responsive.

## 6. The site frame

The marketing site has its own column, and it is a **frame** rather than a content cap.

```vue
<template>
  <div class="layout-column-site border-x border-(--border-default)">…</div>
</template>
```

`layout-column-site` is inset from the window **at every width**, which is the whole reason it is a
utility rather than a `max-w-()`. On a wide screen the inset is free: the measure is narrower than the
window, the column centres, and its rules read as the page's vertical frame with canvas either side.
Below the cap that stops doing anything — the column becomes the window — and the rules land _on_ the
window edges, where a hairline is not a frame, it is a seam against the bezel.

One `min()` covers the whole range with no breakpoint: the cap is whichever binds first, the measure
or the window less a boundary a side. The two mechanisms hand off to each other, so a phone gets the
same framed column a desktop gets.

**It carries no padding, deliberately.** The inset belongs to the frame, not to the copy: the bands
inside are grids whose hairline rules have to reach the frame's own verticals, and a padding here
would pull them off it. A band that wants its content inset too adds `layout-boundary-inline` on top.

The site bar is **one rung wider** than the page, via `--layout-measure-site-header`. A bar is chrome,
not content: it carries the brand at one end and the account actions at the other, held apart by a
navigation region that ran out of room on a laptop when held to the reading frame. It is the one band
allowed outside the frame, and it says so in a token of its own — which is what keeps the exception
reviewable in both directions. Nobody widens the bar by retuning the page, and nobody widens the page
by retuning the bar.

The bar is **`--layout-header-height`** tall (56px, the `AppHeader` height). A band that fills the
first screen under it takes that token out of the screen: `HeroSection` does by default (`headerOffset`),
and a bare `Hero variant="screen"` takes `offset="var(--layout-header-height)"`. Never a literal.
A sticky part further down (a plan table's head row) sticks at **`--layout-sticky-top`**, which
defaults to the bar's height, so it stops right under the bar. Inside a scroller with no bar above
it (a preview card, an embedded frame) set `--layout-sticky-top: 0` on that scroller; otherwise the
sticky part is pushed down at rest and covers what follows it.

**A grid of cards fills its rows.** A framed or divided card grid (`CardGrid`, and every section
built on it) takes `columns` as the most a row may hold, not how many it must: by default
(`layout="balanced"`) it uses the fewest rows that cap allows on the narrowest track count that keeps
them, so a count that splits evenly fills every row — under three columns 2 → halves, 3 → thirds,
4 → 2 × 2. A short last row keeps the column width and leaves its trailing tracks empty, as azion.com
does (5 → 3 + 2, 7 → 3 + 3 + 1; under four, 7 → 4 + 3): a stretched last cell reads as a different,
wider card. `layout="fixed"` is for tiles whose width must not change (square logo walls, a cell
spanning rows or columns, a floor that keeps its track count).

**The footer closes the frame and nothing follows it.** `SiteLayout` places `SiteFooterSection` as its last
child, unwrapped — a page never adds one. The page ends on its bottom bar at every width: the brand
leads the social row from `md`; on phones there is no wordmark row and the status line stacks over
the language select.

## 7. The control cap in a field row

An item-group field row is two columns: the content names the field (title + guidance) on the left,
the actions hold the control on the right.

```vue
<template>
  <div class="layout-field-control">
    <Select
      v-model="region"
      :options="regions"
      class="w-full"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

`layout-field-control` is `flex-1` + `justify-end` capped at `--layout-measure-control`, so the row
stays two-column at every viewport — the control side yields to a long field name instead of wrapping
— and controls inside still pass `w-full` to fill the cap.

The cap decides where the control actually **sits**: raise it and the control grows leftward toward
the label that names it; lower it and the control pins to the right edge with the gap opening up in
between.

The default (256px) is deliberately tight, because a settings row reads as "name → current value" and
a narrow value column keeps a scannable right edge down the whole card. **A create page inverts that
priority** — the fields _are_ the payload, several carry their own descriptions, and the user is
filling them in rather than scanning them — so `layout-form-create` retunes the cap to 472px for
everything inside it. One token, retuned per band, instead of a width re-typed on every row.

# Motion

> The catalogued animate-* utilities, their timing, when to use each, and reduced motion.

Animation in UI built on `@aziontech/webkit` is constrained to the design system's motion
vocabulary: the `animate-*` utilities and the `duration-*` / `ease-*` / `curve` tokens from
`@aziontech/theme`. Motion confirms an action or guides attention — it never decorates — and it
always has a reduced-motion escape. This is the invariant behind the `/webkit-motion-polish` skill
(which is the how-to); this rule is the constraint.

## Do

- Animate with the catalogued `animate-*` utilities (`animate-fade-in`, `animate-slide-down`,
  `animate-popup-scale-in/out`, …) — discover the catalog via the webkit MCP or
  `node_modules/@aziontech/theme`. For `animate-popup-scale-*`, set `--popup-origin` per instance.
- Take timing only from tokens: `duration-fast-01/02`, `duration-moderate-01/02`,
  `duration-slow-01/02`; curves `ease-productive-entrance/exit`, `ease-expressive-entrance/exit`.
- Animate **only compositor props** — `transform` and `opacity` (plus the catalogued
  `animate-slide-down` for disclosure height). Interaction feedback is ≤ `duration-moderate-01`
  (150ms): `ease-out` on entrance, `ease-in` on exit.
- Pair **every** motion-bearing class with a `motion-reduce:*` escape on the same class string:
  `motion-reduce:transition-none` / `motion-reduce:transform-none` / `motion-reduce:animate-none`.
- For `data-state="open|closed"` overlay motion, read `duration` + `curve` from the tokens and emit
  the inline `transition` per phase; keep transform/opacity in classes, only timing inline.

## Don't

- A hardcoded duration (`duration-[180ms]`, `transition: opacity 200ms`) or an inline
  `ease-[cubic-bezier(...)]` — the values live in the theme tokens.
- Animating layout props (`width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `margin`, `padding`) — they thrash
  layout (exception: the catalogued `animate-slide-down`).
- A component-local `@keyframes`, or any external animation library (`gsap`, `framer-motion`,
  `motion`, `@vueuse/motion`, `@formkit/auto-animate`, lottie, popmotion). Use the utilities above +
  Vue `<Transition>` / `<TransitionGroup>`.
- A motion class with no `motion-reduce:*` fallback.

## The panel recipe (sidebar / drawer / any v-if region)

A conditionally rendered region never animates by itself — wrap the `v-if` in a Vue `Transition`
and hand the enter/leave phases to the catalogued utilities. For lateral panels the pair is
`animate-slide-in-start` / `animate-slide-out-start` (end-anchored drawers use the `-end` pair; both flip in right-to-left pages):

```vue
<Transition
  enter-active-class="animate-slide-in-start motion-reduce:animate-none"
  leave-active-class="animate-slide-out-start motion-reduce:animate-none"
>
  <aside v-if="sidebarOpen">...</aside>
</Transition>
```

Content or backdrops appearing in place use `animate-fade-in` / `animate-fade-out` in the same
shape; vertical disclosure uses `animate-slide-down`. Ask the webkit MCP
(`list_tokens` with category `animations`) for every utility, its timing, and when to use it.

## Enforcement

- The mandatory `motion-reduce:*` escape overlaps the shipped `webkit-accessibility` rule (motion is
  an a11y concern) and is verified at runtime by the `webkit-ui-verifier` agent (it exercises
  `prefers-reduced-motion`).
- The no-external-lib constraint holds because the forbidden packages are never installed — an import
  fails the build.
- The token discipline (no hardcoded ms / inline `cubic-bezier` / layout-prop animation) is the
  `/webkit-motion-polish` review pass; where a stylelint rule can catch a raw `cubic-bezier(` or a
  bare `transition: all`, wire it as the mechanical floor. Suggestion is not the ceiling: what a lint
  can block, block.

### Known `no-hardcoded-motion` gaps (review still owns these)

The lint is a heuristic over class and style strings; three shapes are known to slip past it and
stay a review concern:

- **Tailwind arbitrary properties** bypass the timing check: in `[transition:opacity_200ms]` the
  underscore defeats the word boundary, and `[animation-delay:2s]` sits outside the `animation:`
  prefix — while `[transition:all]` is caught.
- **Tailwind v4's dynamic numeric scale**: `duration-937` passes (only the bracketed
  `duration-[937ms]` form is flagged).
- **The `motion-reduce:` pairing check reads only the static `class` attribute** — when the escape
  lives in a coexisting bound `:class` fragment, the static-side motion class is flagged even
  though the element is correctly paired.

## Animation utilities

| Class | Value | Use when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `animate-autoplay-progress` | `autoplayProgress 2100ms linear forwards` | The hairline that fills while a rotating band (tabs, quotes, highlights) waits to advance. Set animation-duration ON THE ELEMENT to the rotation interval, key the element on the slide so it restarts, pause it with animation-play-state while the rotation holds, and anchor its transform origin at the inline start. |
| `animate-blink` | `blink 1s step-end infinite` | Text caret / terminal cursor blink while text is being typed or streamed (stops when the typing does). |
| `animate-blink-settle` | `blink 1s step-end 4` | Four caret blinks, then a solid caret (4s): a decorative cursor that must stop by itself within 5 seconds (WCAG 2.2.2). |
| `animate-bounce` | `bounce 1s infinite` | Playful attention bounce (scroll-down hints); use sparingly. |
| `animate-brand-marquee` | `brandMarquee 59s linear infinite` | A strip of logos looping forever (client trust strips, framework strips). Apply to a track holding its row exactly twice, the duplicate aria-hidden, and set animation-duration ON THE ELEMENT from the mark count so every strip on a site moves at one speed rather than one duration — a var in this shorthand would resolve at :root and never see it. Pause it on hover and focus-within so a linked mark can be reached. |
| `animate-content-enter` | `contentEnter 240ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1) var(--content-enter-delay, 0s) backwards` | Content settling INSIDE a page that is already on screen — a loading window resolving, a filtered list swapping, a step changing. Never on first paint of a page whose own entrance is already running (use it after that entrance, or after a wire). Stagger a follower with --content-enter-delay. |
| `animate-fade-in` | `fadeIn 220ms ease-in-out` | Content or backdrop appearing in place (no directional origin). |
| `animate-fade-out` | `fadeOut 220ms ease-in-out` | Content or backdrop leaving in place (pair of fade-in). |
| `animate-flow-dash` | `flowDash 700ms linear infinite` | Flowing connection along an SVG connector stroke in a node-based / network diagram. Set a stroke-dasharray whose cycle divides 24 (e.g. 4 4) so the loop is seamless. |
| `animate-flow-dash-settle` | `flowDash 700ms linear 6` | Marching dashes along a decorative SVG connector, six cycles then still (4.2s, WCAG 2.2.2); same stroke-dasharray contract as flow-dash. Keep the infinite flow-dash for a stroke that shows a live status. |
| `animate-highlight-fade` | `highlight 1100ms ease-in forwards` | Row/item briefly highlighted after an update (recently changed). |
| `animate-page-enter` | `pageEnter 240ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1)` | A page arriving on a route change — on the CONTENT ZONE only, never the shell. The chrome is the same before and after, and sliding it announces a reload that did not happen. Key it on the route path so a component serving several paths still replays it. Nothing inside the page may animate on mount at the same time: the two run in lockstep and read as one element travelling on a diagonal. |
| `animate-ping` | `ping 1s cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1) infinite` | One-off attention ring radiating from a small element (notification dot). |
| `animate-ping-settle` | `ping 1s cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1) 3` | Three attention rings radiating from a small element, then still (3s): draws the eye once without looping (WCAG 2.2.2). Remount the element to replay it. |
| `animate-popup-scale-in` | `popupScaleIn 150ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1)` | Anchored overlays opening (dropdown, popover, tooltip, menu); set --popup-origin. |
| `animate-popup-scale-out` | `popupScaleOut 110ms cubic-bezier(0.55, 0.09, 0.68, 0.53)` | Anchored overlays closing (pair of popup-scale-in). |
| `animate-progress-indeterminate` | `progressIndeterminate 2100ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1) infinite` | Indeterminate linear progress bar (primary sweep). |
| `animate-progress-indeterminate-short` | `progressIndeterminateShort 2100ms cubic-bezier(0.17, 0.84, 0.44, 1) 1100ms infinite` | Indeterminate linear progress bar (secondary short sweep). |
| `animate-pulse` | `pulse 2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1) infinite` | Skeleton/placeholder opacity pulse while content loads. |
| `animate-pulse-settle` | `pulse 2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1) 2` | Two opacity pulses, then still at full strength (4s): a decorative pulse that must stop by itself within 5 seconds (WCAG 2.2.2). Keep any stagger delay under 1s so the last pulse still ends within 5 seconds. |
| `animate-shimmer` | `shimmer 1.6s linear infinite` | Skeleton shimmer sweep while content loads. |
| `animate-slide-down` | `slideDown 220ms ease-in-out` | Vertical disclosure expanding (accordion panel, expandable row). |
| `animate-slide-in-end` | `slideInEnd 240ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1)` | End-anchored panel entering (settings/detail drawer); flips with the reading direction. |
| `animate-slide-in-start` | `slideInStart 240ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1)` | Start-anchored panel entering (sidebar, navigation drawer); flips with the reading direction. Wrap the v-if region in a Vue Transition with enter-active-class. |
| `animate-slide-out-end` | `slideOutEnd 150ms cubic-bezier(0.55, 0.09, 0.68, 0.53)` | End-anchored panel leaving (pair of slide-in-end). |
| `animate-slide-out-start` | `slideOutStart 150ms cubic-bezier(0.55, 0.09, 0.68, 0.53)` | Start-anchored panel leaving (pair of slide-in-start; use as leave-active-class). |
| `animate-spin` | `spin 1s linear infinite` | Indeterminate circular spinners (loading icons). |
| `animate-spin-settle` | `spin 4200ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` | One eased revolution, then still (4.2s): a decorative rotating glow that must stop by itself within 5 seconds (WCAG 2.2.2). Ends on its start frame. |
| `animate-status-pulse` | `pulse 2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1) infinite` | A small status mark (a live dot, a streaming sparkle) pulsing for as long as the status it shows lasts: the signal is the motion, so it stops when the status ends. Never for loading placeholders (pulse, on Skeleton) or decoration (pulse-settle). |
| `animate-texture-wave-a` | `textureWaveA 4800ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1) forwards` | One of the two crossing bands of a pixelate texture, drifting left and easing to a stop (4.8s, WCAG 2.2.2), holding where it lands. Set --texture-wave-shift on the element to one period of its banding measured along X, and overhang the element by that much on the side it travels toward, or the field uncovers. |
| `animate-texture-wave-b` | `textureWaveB 4800ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1) forwards` | The counter-drifting band of that pair (pair of texture-wave-a; same --texture-wave-shift contract, opposite direction). |

<!-- foundations/internationalization.md -->

# Languages (internationalization)

> Built-in strings in en, pt-BR and es, the provider, useLocale and locale-aware formatting.

WebKit ships every built-in string in three catalogs: `en` (built into the provider), `pt-BR` and `es` (opt-in entries `@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR` and `@aziontech/webkit/locales/es`). Wrap the app in `ConfigProvider` with a `locale` and the catalogs it offers (`:catalogs="{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }"`) and every component follows it; `useLocale()` from `@aziontech/webkit/use-locale` gives your own code the same `t`, `dir` and `Intl` formatters.

## App-level setup (`setup` in the catalog)

A few components need **one-time wiring in the app entry before first use** — the catalog entry (and `get_component` on the MCP) carries it in a `setup` field. When `setup` is non-null, apply it BEFORE emitting code that uses the component, and check whether the project already has it (do not duplicate).

- **Toast**: fire-from-anywhere (`toast.success('Saved')`) only renders if a region is mounted. Wire the service once in the entry — `import { ToastPlugin } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast'` and chain `.use(ToastPlugin)` onto `createApp()`; the plugin mounts the region automatically (options: `app.use(ToastPlugin, { duration: 6000 })`; leave `position` at its `bottom-end` default, where every app puts toasts). A manually mounted Toaster also counts — never add both blindly (the store keeps only the first region active, but one wiring is enough). `npx webkit doctor` flags toast usage with no wired region.

- **Theme (light or dark)**: with no `data-theme` the theme follows the device (`prefers-color-scheme`). An app that is always dark sets `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` in `index.html` (`<html lang="en" data-theme="dark">`), so the first paint is dark, and an app that is always light sets `data-theme="light"`; a toggle writes `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` (`'dark'` / `'light'`), and a `.dark` class on an ancestor works too. Every token switches with it — never add per-theme classes (`/webkit-theming-dark-mode`).

- **ConfigProvider (languages)**: mount it once at the app root; pass `locale` when the user chose one, or leave it unset to follow the device locale (`en-US` on the server and until mount, then `navigator.language`). Every built-in string a component ships (close buttons, pagination, empty states, assistive labels) then reads from the locale's catalog, and dates, numbers, file sizes and plurals format with `Intl` for that locale; `dir` follows the locale (`ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur` are right-to-left). English is built in; Portuguese and Spanish are opt-in: import them from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR` and `@aziontech/webkit/locales/es` and pass them through `catalogs` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`), or the provider falls back to English and warns in development. With no provider every component formats for the device locale and reads English text. Only what people read follows the locale: send the `v-model` value to your server (DatePicker a `Date`, DateRangePicker ISO 8601 instants, TagEditor `key`/`value` pairs), never a printed label. A label prop you pass still wins over the catalog; `messages` renames a built-in string for the whole app. Import it as `import ConfigProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/config-provider'`.

```vue
<!-- App.vue -->
<script setup>
  import { es } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/es'
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import ConfigProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/config-provider'

  const catalogs = { 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }
</script>

<template>
  <ConfigProvider
    :locale="user.locale"
    :catalogs="catalogs"
  >
    <RouterView />
  </ConfigProvider>
</template>
```

In your own components, `useLocale()` from `@aziontech/webkit/use-locale` returns the active `locale`, `dir`, `t(key, params)` and the `Intl` helpers (`formatNumber`, `formatDate`, `formatRelativeTime`, `formatList`, `formatFileSize`, `plural`), so your numbers and dates match WebKit's. `t` reads the provider's catalog; pass the English messages it should fall back to when no provider is mounted (`useLocale(en)`, with `en` from the same import).

WebKit components carry their own interface text: close buttons, pagination, empty states,
calendar fields, keycaps, wizard steps, screen-reader labels. Each one is read from a locale
catalog (`en`, `pt-BR`, `es`) through `useLocale`, so it follows the language set on
`ConfigProvider`. A string typed by hand next to the component, or passed into a prop to repeat the
default, is stuck in one language and drifts from the rest of the product.

## Do

- Leave a component's built-in text alone. `<Pagination>` already says "Previous page" and
  "Página anterior"; `<Dialog>` already names its close button; `<Kbd key-name="escape" />` prints
  `Esc` from the catalog.
- Set the language once, at the app root: `<ConfigProvider locale="pt-BR" :catalogs="{ 'pt-BR': ptBR }">`,
  with `ptBR` from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR` (`es` from `/locales/es`; English is built
  in). Every component below it switches, dates and numbers included (`Intl` through the same
  locale).
- Let people change the language with `LanguageSelect` (`@aziontech/webkit/language-select`)
  bound to the same `locale` the provider reads: `<LanguageSelect v-model="locale" variant="ghost" />`
  in a header, a toolbar or a footer (a round flag and the language tag, `EN` or `PT-BR`), and the default full field
  `<LanguageSelect v-model="locale" />` on a settings page or in a form. Name every option with a
  BCP 47 tag: the bare language for its main variant (`en`, `es`) and the ISO 3166-1 region for a
  regional one (`pt-BR`, `en-GB`, never `en-UK`). A regional variant reads its language's catalog
  (`en-GB` → `en`) unless you register one under its own tag. Your own
  screen copy follows it too: read `useLocale().locale` and pick the text from a table keyed by
  locale, as the `auth/auth-sign-in` block does.
- Rename a built-in string for the whole app with `messages` on `ConfigProvider`:
  `:messages="{ wizard: { submit: 'Deploy' }, kbd: { ctrl: 'Strg' } }"`. The keys are the
  catalog's (`group.key`): `group` is the component's camelCase name (`sidebarMenu`,
  `feedbackReasonDialog`) and strings several components share are in `common` (`common.copy`,
  `common.newTab`); anything you leave out keeps the built-in text.
- Pass a prop only when the text is product copy specific to that screen (a dialog title, a field
  label, the action of this form), and write it by the `webkit-microcopy` skill: sentence case, one
  word per concept, no em dash.
- Format dates, numbers, file sizes, relative times and lists with `useLocale()`
  (`formatDate`, `formatNumber`, `formatFileSize`, `formatRelativeTime`, `formatList`), not with
  string concatenation.

## Don't

- Re-type a built-in string into a prop to "make sure": `close-label="Close"`,
  `placeholder="Select a Date Range"`, `next-label="Next"`. It freezes the English text and stops
  the provider's locale from reaching it.
- Fork a component, or wrap it, only to change one of its words: use `messages`.
- Hard-code key names (`Ctrl`, `Esc`, `Enter`) next to a `Kbd`: use its modifier props and
  `key-name`; `⌘`, `⌥` and `⇧` stay symbols on macOS.
- Build a sentence from fragments (`'Step ' + n + ' of ' + total`): plural rules and word order
  differ by language. WebKit's catalog keys take parameters (`Step {step} of {total}`).

## Example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import ConfigProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/config-provider'
  import Wizard from '@aziontech/webkit/wizard'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const step = ref(0)
  const messages = { wizard: { submit: 'Implantar' } }
</script>

<template>
  <ConfigProvider
    locale="pt-BR"
    :catalogs="{ 'pt-BR': ptBR }"
    :messages="messages"
  >
    <Wizard
      v-model="step"
      aria-label="Criar aplicação"
    >
      <Wizard.Step title="Configurar">…</Wizard.Step>
      <Wizard.Step title="Revisar">…</Wizard.Step>
    </Wizard>
  </ConfigProvider>
</template>
```

## Notes

- A `scope: general` standard: it applies to any screen in an app that uses webkit, not only to
  webkit's own components.
- Inside the package the same check runs at write time (the authoring hook) and in CI
  (`scripts/check-authoring.mjs`): a literal UI string in a component template attribute, or an
  English prop default, is blocked; the text goes to `src/locales/*.ts`.
- Product copy, the text no component ships, follows the `webkit-microcopy` skill.

<!-- foundations/right-to-left.md -->

# Right-to-left

> Logical sides only, so every screen mirrors under dir="rtl"; what mirrors and what does not.

UI built on `@aziontech/webkit` works in right-to-left languages (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu)
without a second stylesheet. The page sets `dir="rtl"` (on `<html>` or the app root) and the
layout mirrors because nothing in it names a physical side. Text that is always left-to-right —
code, URLs, domains, IDs, keyboard shortcuts — stays left-to-right inside it.

## Do

- Use the **logical** utilities: `ms-*`/`me-*` (margin), `ps-*`/`pe-*` (padding), `start-*`/`end-*`
  (inset), `text-start`/`text-end`, `border-s`/`border-e`, `rounded-s`/`rounded-e` and the corners
  `rounded-ss`/`rounded-se`/`rounded-es`/`rounded-ee`, `float-start`/`float-end`,
  `scroll-ms-*`/`scroll-ps-*`.
- Center with `left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2`: the one physical pair allowed, because the result is the
  same in both directions.
- Mirror what points along the reading direction: arrows, chevrons, carets, "back"/"next", sign-in /
  sign-out. WebKit components already do it (`Button`/`IconButton`/`Link`/`Breadcrumb` `icon` props,
  and `@aziontech/webkit/styles` for any `az az-chevron-right`-style glyph); on your own glyph add
  `rtl:-scale-x-100`. Never add `rtl:rotate-180` to an `az-*` arrow, chevron or caret: the
  stylesheet already mirrors it, the rotation flips it a second time and it points the wrong way
  (blocked inside the package by the `rtl-double-flip` check).
- Place overlays with `side` and `align` (`Tooltip`, `Popover`, `HoverCard`, `DropdownMenu`,
  `Hint`, `NavigationMenu.Viewport`): `side="end"` opens on the right in `ltr` and on the left in
  `rtl`, and `align="start"` lines the panel up with the trigger's start edge in both. Select,
  Combobox, the date pickers and menus anchor at `bottom` + `start` and mirror on their own.
- Mirror horizontal motion with the `rtl:` variant: a panel that slides in with
  `-translate-x-full` also gets `rtl:translate-x-full`.
- Read the direction in script with `useDirection` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-direction`) whenever an
  arrow key or a pointer delta means "next" or "previous": under `rtl`, ArrowLeft moves forward.
  `logicalArrowKey(event.key, dir.value)` does the swap.
- Isolate user and system values printed inside sentences: `<bdi>{{ name }}</bdi>`, or
  `dir="ltr"` on values that are always left-to-right (code, URLs, domains, IDs, hashes, file
  paths). WebKit's `Input`, `Textarea`, `NumberInput` and `PasswordInput` already use
  `dir="auto"`; pass `dir` to override.
- Set `lang` with `dir` (`<html lang="ar" dir="rtl">`): the theme's sans stack falls back to Noto
  Sans Arabic and Arabic text gets a taller line height through `:lang(ar)`.

## Don't

- `ml-*`, `mr-*`, `pl-*`, `pr-*`, `left-*`, `right-*`, `text-left`, `text-right`, `border-l`,
  `border-r`, `rounded-l`, `rounded-tr`… in a class string. They stay put under `dir="rtl"` and the
  layout breaks: an icon gap on the wrong side, a drawer that opens from the wrong edge.
- Mirroring what does not point along the text: external-link arrows (`az-arrow-up-right`,
  `az-external-link`), play/pause and other media controls, logos, clocks, checkmarks, charts'
  value axes, code.
- Comparing `event.key === 'ArrowRight'` to mean "next" without the direction.
- Reading `scrollLeft` as a distance from the start: it is `0` or negative under `rtl`; use
  `Math.abs(el.scrollLeft)`.

## Example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { logicalArrowKey, useDirection } from '@aziontech/webkit/use-direction'

  defineProps<{ label: string; domain: string }>()
  const emit = defineEmits<{ next: [event: KeyboardEvent]; previous: [event: KeyboardEvent] }>()

  const dir = useDirection()
  const onKeydown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
    const key = logicalArrowKey(event.key, dir.value)
    if (key === 'ArrowRight') emit('next', event)
    if (key === 'ArrowLeft') emit('previous', event)
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div
    tabindex="0"
    class="flex items-center gap-(--spacing-xs) ps-(--spacing-md)"
    @keydown="onKeydown"
  >
    <span class="truncate">{{ label }}</span>
    <span
      dir="ltr"
      class="ms-auto text-label-code-sm"
      >{{ domain }}</span
    >
    <i
      class="az az-chevron-right rtl:-scale-x-100"
      aria-hidden="true"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

## Notes

- A `scope: general` standard: it applies to any component in an app that uses webkit, not only to
  webkit's own.
- Blocked by the `webkit/no-physical-direction` ESLint rule (error, autofix to the logical utility)
  in the consumer presets, and inside the package by `scripts/check-authoring.mjs` over
  `src/components`, `blocks` and `examples`.
- The rule reads class strings: static `class`, `:class`, `class`/`className` in JSX and Astro, and
  `cn`/`clsx`/`cva`/`tv` arguments. A class assembled from variables is a review concern.
