<!-- foundations/devices.md -->

# Devices

> Viewport breakpoints for the shell, container queries for the content, touch targets and reflow at 320 px.

## 8. Devices — the window, the box, the finger

A component does not know whether it is on a 1440 px page or in a 400 px drawer, so it must not
ask the window. Two scales (both in `@aziontech/theme`, "Breakpoints and container sizes"):

| Question | Scale | Variants | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| How big is the window? | `--breakpoint-*` | `sm:` `md:` `lg:` `xl:` `2xl:` | the shell (sidebar ↔ drawer), overlays as sheets, page boundary |
| How big is my box? | `--container-*` | `@container` + `@sm:` `@md:` … | everything inside a band, a card, a drawer, a split view |

```vue
<template>
  <section class="@container/usage flex flex-col gap-(--layout-group-gap)">
    <div class="grid grid-cols-1 gap-(--spacing-md) @xl/usage:grid-cols-2">…</div>
  </section>
</template>
```

The components that live in panels already do this, so a page gets it for free: `Table` (the grid
scrolls sideways inside its own viewport; `stackable` opts a short list into label/value cards),
`PageHeader` and `Subheader` (actions drop under the title, full width), `SettingsRow` (a field moves
under its copy on a phone, the description wraps in full; `stackable` stacks it in a drawer-width box too), `SettingsGroup`, `SaveBar` (actions stack full width, Save on top),
`Card` (its content is `@container/card`), `Alert` (the action takes its own line), `EmptyState`,
`Pagination` (the strip and page-size control wrap under the info text; the page list stays whole), `Wizard` (the rail hides when the
wizard is narrow), `HelpPanel`, `ChartCard`, `StatTile`, and the body of every dialog and drawer
(`@container/panel`). `KeyValueList` picks its column count from its own width, and
`Field orientation="responsive"` follows whichever container encloses it.

The window still owns the shell:

- `ConsoleLayout` measures its own width (through `AppLayout`): below 768 px the rail moves into
  the layout's navigation drawer, opened from the header's menu button; on a header under its `@xs`
  (a 320 px phone) the brand mark drops out of the header and stays in the drawer. `DocLayout` moves its rail
  into a drawer below `lg` and shows the outline rail from `xl`.
- Below `md` a `Dialog` or `Drawer` is a bottom sheet; below `sm` it is a full-height, full-width
  sheet, and its `PanelFooter` actions stay pinned and stretch.
- Ultra-wide (1920, 2560 px): the column classes of section 2 cap the content, so wide screens add
  margin. Never widen a band to "use the space".

Containment has one cost: a box with `@container` has no intrinsic width. Put it only on a box whose
width comes from its parent (block, grid track, `flex-1`), never on `inline-flex`, `w-fit` or a
popover.

Touch: every target is at least 24 × 24 px, 44 × 44 px on a coarse pointer. The webkit controls do
it without changing their drawn size (an invisible hit area under `pointer-coarse:`); in your own
markup prefer a larger hit area over a larger control. Anything shown on hover is also shown on
focus and under `[@media(hover:none)]:`.

Reflow (WCAG 1.4.10): the page works at 320 px with no horizontal page scroll. Only code, logs,
tables in scroll mode and marquees scroll sideways, inside their own box. Give fixed-width demo
wrappers `w-full max-w-*`, rows that hold several controls `flex-wrap`, and flex items that hold
truncating text `min-w-0`.

<!-- foundations/accessibility.md -->

# Accessibility

> WCAG 2.1 AA rules every component and screen follows: names, focus, keyboard, contrast, motion.

WebKit components are accessible by construction: drop in a `Dialog` or `Table` and its
role, keyboard model, focus management, and reduced-motion fallback come with it. Anything
you build around them — custom components, views, composed overlays — must hold the same
contract. In this project accessibility is **convention + code review**; two parts are
mechanically enforced: color — raw colors (including focus rings) are blocked by the
stylelint config and the `webkit/no-hardcoded-color` ESLint rule — and the accessible name of
an icon-only control, which `webkit/require-accessible-name` requires on every `IconButton`.

## Do

- Use the **native element** whose semantics match before reaching for `role`, through the
  WebKit component that renders it: `Button` / `IconButton` for a `<button>`, `Link` for an
  `<a href>` (`Link inline` inside a sentence), `Input` and its family for an `<input>`. A raw
  one outside its owner is flagged by `webkit/no-unowned-element`. Add `role` only when no
  native element fits.
- Mirror ARIA state with the element's `data-*` state (`aria-expanded` with
  `data-state="open"`, `aria-disabled` with `data-disabled`, `aria-invalid` with
  `data-invalid`).
- Name a webkit control in the template with the **kebab attribute**: `aria-label="Delete domain"`
  (`:aria-label` when it changes, `aria-labelledby` when visible text already names it). Vue maps
  it onto the component's `ariaLabel` prop. An `IconButton` (or `ButtonGroup`) with no name is
  flagged by `webkit/require-accessible-name`.
- On your own components, name the accessible-name prop **`ariaLabel`** (prefixed
  `xAriaLabel` for sub-parts), make it **optional with a `''` default**, and bind it to the
  `aria-label` attribute internally (`ariaLabel || undefined`). vue-tsc does not camelize
  `aria-*` attributes onto props, so a required `ariaLabel` makes `aria-label="…"` fail to
  type-check in a fresh create-vue app; require the name with a lint rule or a test instead.
- Give every interactive piece a **keyboard map** and implement exactly that
  (dialog: `Esc` closes, `Tab` is trapped; menu: arrows move, `Enter` selects,
  `Esc` closes). Anything clickable must be reachable and operable by keyboard.
  The screen around the pieces follows one console-wide contract (focus on open, `Esc`,
  `⌘ S`, `/`, `?`, list keys): rule `webkit-keyboard`.
- Put help beside a label in a **`Hint`** (the small info glyph that opens a short note on click),
  a short explanation in the field or section description, and a long one in a `HelpPanel`. A
  `Tooltip` only names a control in a few words. A typed `?`, an info icon inside a `Tooltip` or
  `Popover` trigger, a `Tooltip` over 80 characters and a `Hint` over 280 are flagged by
  `webkit/prefer-hint`.
- Generate ids with Vue's **`useId()`** for every `for` / `aria-labelledby` /
  `aria-describedby` association — stable across SSR.
- Style focus with a **`focus-visible`** ring using the ring token
  (`focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`).
- Make overlays **trap focus and restore it**: focus moves into the overlay on open,
  stays trapped while open, and returns to the trigger on close — use a focus-trap
  composable (e.g. VueUse), not a hand-written trap.
- Pair every motion-bearing class with **`motion-reduce:`**
  (`motion-reduce:transition-none` / `motion-reduce:animate-none`).
- Keep hit targets at **24px or more**, and at **40px or more** on touch layouts (the WebKit
  floor: its controls draw at least 40px where they are tapped, and a button's invisible touch
  area reaches 44px on a coarse pointer), even when the visible glyph is smaller.
- Announce async results politely: inline validation and status updates go to an
  `aria-live="polite"` region (the webkit `Toast` and `Alert` already do this). Only an error
  interrupts: a `danger` toast is announced assertively by the `Toaster`, every other kind politely.
- Give in-page link targets a scroll offset (`scroll-mt-(--spacing-2xl)`) so a sticky header never
  covers the heading the link jumps to.
- Wrap brand names, product names and code tokens in `translate="no"` so browser translation does
  not rewrite them.

## Don't

- Never add `role`/ARIA to fake an interactive element when a native one fits.
- Never put `@click` on a non-interactive element without a matching key handler.
- Never hand-roll ids — use `useId()`.
- Never use a raw color for the focus ring — use the ring token; hardcoded colors are
  blocked by `webkit/no-hardcoded-color` and the stylelint config.
- Never open an overlay without trapping focus and restoring it to the trigger on close.
- Never ship a motion class without its `motion-reduce:` fallback.
- Never name the accessible-name prop `aria-label` — use `ariaLabel`.
- Never write the camelCase `ariaLabel="…"` attribute in a template — write `aria-label="…"`.
- Never add `vueCompilerOptions.htmlAttributes` to a tsconfig to make `aria-label` type-check;
  the webkit types already accept it.
- Never disable browser zoom (`user-scalable=no`, `maximum-scale=1`).
- Never rely on color alone for a status: pair it with a label or an icon with a name.
- Never pick a colour pair by eye. Every pair passes **both** WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 icons
  and marks) and APCA: Lc 75 body text, Lc 60 other text, Lc 45 icons, Lc 30 solid marks, Lc 15
  borders. Use the theme's token pairs (they pass); the few accepted exceptions are listed in
  `webkit-tokens.md` § "Contrast: APCA and WCAG 2".
- Never strip the underline from a link inside a sentence (`no-underline` on a `Link inline`): the link
  blue is only 1.1–1.3:1 against muted body text and 3:1 against default text, so color alone fails
  WCAG 1.4.1. `Link inline` renders the `text-link` style, which keeps a quiet underline at rest and
  strengthens it on hover. A standalone `Link` (not in a sentence) underlines on hover only.

## Example

### Do

```vue
<script setup>
import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'
import { ref, useId } from 'vue'
const open = ref(false)
const hintId = useId() // stable id for the ARIA association
</script>

<template>
  <!-- a native button with the token focus ring and the reduced-motion fallback built in;
       the ARIA state mirrors what the toggle shows -->
  <Button
    label="Show details"
    variant="secondary"
    :aria-expanded="open"
    @click="open = !open"
  />

  <Input
    type="email"
    aria-label="Email"
    :aria-describedby="hintId"
  />
  <p :id="hintId">We never share your email.</p>
</template>
```

### Don't

```html
<!-- clickable div: fake semantics, unreachable by keyboard -->
<div role="button" @click="open">Open settings</div>

<!-- hand-rolled id, raw-color focus ring, motion without a reduced-motion fallback -->
<label for="email-1">Email</label>
<input id="email-1" class="transition-all focus-visible:ring-[#f3652b]" />

<!-- overlay that neither traps focus nor restores it to the trigger on close -->
<div v-if="open" role="dialog">…</div>
```

<!-- foundations/keyboard.md -->

# Keyboard

> The console keyboard contract: focus on open, Esc, Enter and Cmd+Enter, Cmd+S, Cmd+K, /, ?, list keys, and no single-key shortcut while typing.

## The contract

| Moment | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Opening a task (create page, drawer, form dialog) | Focus lands in the first field. |
| Opening a chat (assistant page, chat drawer) | Focus lands in the message box, the field the next message is typed in. |
| Opening a page you browse (list, detail, settings) | Focus lands on the page `h1` (`tabindex="-1"`, no visible ring), so a screen reader announces the page. |
| `Esc` | Closes the top layer only: menu, then dialog, then drawer. On a full-page task it means Cancel, through the unsaved-changes guard. On a browse page it does nothing. |
| `Enter`, `⌘ Enter` (`Ctrl Enter` off Apple) | `Enter` submits a short single-line form; `⌘ Enter` submits from a textarea or the code editor. |
| `⌘ S` (`Ctrl S`) | Saves a page that has a `SaveBar`, and stops the browser's own save. |
| `⌘ K` (`Ctrl K`) | Opens the command palette (rule [`webkit-header-search`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/rules/webkit-header-search.md)). |
| `/` | Focuses the page's search field, when the page has one. |
| `?` (`Shift /`) | Opens the list of every shortcut the current screen offers. |
| Lists and tables | Arrow keys move between rows, `Enter` opens, `Space` selects, `Delete` asks before it deletes. |
| After an action | Closing returns focus to the trigger; deleting moves focus to the next row, else the previous row, else the list. |
| Always | A single-key shortcut never fires while typing in a field (`input`, `textarea`, `contenteditable`, a combobox) or with a modifier held. |

`⌘` is the Command key on Apple platforms; everywhere else the same shortcut is `Ctrl`. Write the
shortcut once with the Apple key in code (`meta`) and let `Kbd` print the platform's key: `⌘` on
macOS, `Ctrl` on Windows, Linux and ChromeOS.

Do, Don't, the Vue samples and what enforces each key, in full: `foundations/keyboard.md`.

# Site pages (Web Design Guide)

> The Web Design Guide, SD-01 to SD-25 (SD-07 headline lines, SD-04 action labels): sections, heroes, line budgets and assets of every Azion web page.

## Index

| ID | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| SD-01 | Sections come only from the WebKit page sections |
| SD-02 | A page starts from the section's own site JSON |
| SD-03 | Section copy is frozen until someone asks |
| SD-04 | Action labels come from the WebKit list |
| SD-05 | A band hero is followed by no gap |
| SD-06 | The client marquee belongs to the screen hero |
| SD-07 | A short headline breaks in two lines, a long one in three |
| SD-08 | Retired; the ID is not reused |
| SD-09 | Every hero has an eyebrow with the `//` prefix |
| SD-10 | Section eyebrows are optional and plain |
| SD-11 | A band no section covers becomes a section first |
| SD-12 | Creative pages keep the content base |
| SD-13 | Assets come from the WebKit asset bank |
| SD-14 | Brand marks in colour first |
| SD-15 | The page speaks the project language |
| SD-16 | Marketing facts come from the knowledge base |
| SD-17 | Product names and terms follow the knowledge base |
| SD-18 | Pick an illustration by what it draws, not by its name |
| SD-19 | A missing illustration is reported, not approximated |
| SD-20 | Illustrations side by side carry the same visual weight |
| SD-21 | A framed box checks its containers before drawing its edges |
| SD-22 | A product page follows the product pattern |
| SD-23 | A Solution page follows the Solution pattern |
| SD-24 | Copy fits its rendered line budget |
| SD-25 | A section prop holds plain text, never markdown |

## Where the content comes from

WebKit owns the design: which sections a page uses, the hero, the frame, the assets, the action
labels. Marketing owns the content, in its own toolkit, and WebKit only points there:

| Content | Source (marketing) |
| --- | --- |
| Positioning, claims, metrics, use cases, personas, customers | the `azion-kb` knowledge base (`product-marketing/`, `gtm-definitions/`) |
| Voice, headline patterns, every label not listed in SD-04 | the `azion-brand-voice` skill |
| Product names | `azion-kb` `company-definitions/product-naming.md` |
| Required, forbidden and deprecated terms; editorial style | `azion-kb` `brand-guidelines/terminology.md`, `editorial-style.md` |
| Translation into pt-BR and es | the `translate-content` skill |

When this rule and any other design document disagree about a design decision, this rule wins
and the other document is fixed.

Four parts are the marketing site's own decisions: the action labels (SD-04), the product and
Solution page patterns (SD-22, SD-23), the line budgets (SD-24) and Photography and generated
art. The site's documentation decides them. WebKit keeps them here as the sample its examples,
blocks and demos follow, and updates them when the site's documentation changes; for the site,
its documentation wins.

Each rule in full, with Incorrect, Correct, Why and Exceptions: `foundations/site-pages.md`.

# Using WebKit in an app

> Start from a block, find a component, import it tree-shakeably, app-level setup and the quality checklist.

## Overview

`@aziontech/webkit` is the Azion design system: a set of themed, accessible Vue 3 components. This project depends on it. When you build or review UI here, reach for a webkit component first, import it with the flat path, and style with `@aziontech/theme` tokens. This skill is the paste-safe reference for doing that right.

## Start here: one app layout, then each screen is a page body

The chrome is composed **once**, in `App.vue`, around `RouterView`, from the layout of the surface:

```vue
<script setup>
  import ConsoleLayoutRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/console-layout-root'
  import { navigation } from './navigation'
</script>

<template>
  <ConsoleLayoutRoot
    :navigation="navigation"
    :breadcrumbs="$route.meta.breadcrumbs ?? []"
    :account="{ name: 'Jane Doe', email: 'jane.doe@example.com' }"
  >
    <RouterView />
  </ConsoleLayoutRoot>
</template>
```

- **Console:** `ConsoleLayout` — navigation rows `{ id, label, icon, href }` (an in-app `href` is
  followed with the app's router, no `@navigate` wiring needed) and the active row follows the
  route; `actions`, `account-menu`, `search`, `header-leading`, `breadcrumbs`, `notifications` and `tools` slots. A page
  opens the shared palette with `useConsoleLayout().openSearch()`
  (`@aziontech/webkit/use-console-layout`); a body that also renders on its own calls
  `useConsoleLayout({ optional: true })`, which returns `null` outside a layout. Bind `v-model:navigation-open` to persist the rail or
  to offer `Collapse sidebar` in the palette (`search` slot + `@search-select`). A page sets its own
  trail, control crumb included, with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`, and a full-height workspace puts
  `data-layout-fill` on its root (never `calc(100dvh - …)`).
- **Site:** `SiteLayout` — `navigation` and `footer` are the `SiteHeaderSection` and `SiteFooterSection` data. The
  site is dark: `<html data-theme="dark">`. `SiteFooterSection` binds its language select (the compact
  `LanguageSelect`, round flag and language tag; `languages` are BCP 47 tags) with
  `v-model:language`; switch the locale from that value.
- **Docs:** `DocLayout` — the docs tree, section links, `outline-groups`, and `actions`,
  `navigation-footer`, `aside`, `footer` slots. The document scrolls. The page feeds the "On this
  page" rail by itself: every `DocHeading` with an `anchor` (level 2 or 3) and every
  `DocChangelogEntry` registers with the layout, in document order, so App.vue passes nothing per
  page and a page never renders `DocLayout`; a page with no anchored heading (the docs home) shows no
  outline rail and no `aside`. A drill row
  (`type: 'drill'`) opens in place and the rail's Back reads `Back to Docs` (`rootLabel` renames it);
  never add a hand-made Back row.

The shell blocks (`shell/shell-console`, `shell/shell-site`, `shell/shell-docs`) are these layouts with
the real navigation: copy one as your `App.vue` and replace its stand-in body with `<RouterView />`.
`npx @aziontech/webkit add shell/shell-console` writes the block into your views folder and prints the
path (`src/views/console.vue`): move that file to `src/App.vue`, and skip the route it suggests.
A page never renders its own `<main>`, `AppLayout`, `Sidebar`, `AppHeader`, `SiteHeaderSection`,
`SiteFooterSection` or `Command`. Every platform block is a page body; the one exception is a screen with no rail — a
create flow (`create/*`, headed by the `top-bar/top-bar-creation` bar) or a
signed-out screen (`auth/auth-sign-in`): route it outside the layout (a route meta `App.vue` reads), and
it keeps its own bar and `<main>` (`webkit-navigation`). An app with two surfaces (a marketing site
and its docs) does the same: `App.vue` picks `SiteLayout` or `DocLayout` from a route meta
(`meta: { layout: 'docs' }`) around one `RouterView`, and every page stays a body. The `shell/shell-docs`
variants are such bodies: `webkit add shell/shell-docs --variant Article` copies the shell (your App.vue
or docs layout) and the page side by side.

## A screen begins from a block

Before composing anything, check whether the screen already exists as a block:
`npx @aziontech/webkit search <the screen in plain words>` ("login", "account settings", "delete
confirmation"), or the `webkit` MCP `search_blocks`. Read the best one with
`npx @aziontech/webkit view <block-id>` (or `get_block`), then start the screen with
`npx @aziontech/webkit add <block-id>` (`--variant <state>` for another state): it copies the SFC
into the views directory, checks its imports, records it in `webkit.blocks.json` and prints the
route entry. `npx @aziontech/webkit diff <block-id>` later shows what you changed against the
canonical block, and `npx @aziontech/webkit remove <block-id>` (`--dry-run` first) deletes a copy you
no longer need with its `webkit.blocks.json` entry, then lists the imports left to remove. Before adapting it, read the guidelines (`view`, or the `guidelines` field
`get_block` returns): when to use the screen and when another block fits better, what each building block (A,
B, C…) is for, do and don't, the copy rules and the accessibility rules. If "When not to use"
matches your case, switch to the block it names. Then change only the content of the copy,
keeping to the guidelines. Only when no block fits, compose from components (below).

A block takes its data through props and emits its actions; it fetches nothing. `add` copies its
data files beside it (`<name>.sample.ts`, and an API adapter when the block ships one) and its parts
as kebab SFCs (`<name>-<part>.vue`). To go live,
do not rewrite the block: render it from the routed page that owns the request and pass what the
request returns (its `## Data` guidelines list the props and events):
`<TableView :resources="rows" :loading="pending" :error="message" @refresh="load" @retry="load" />`.
A data prop left out renders the sample; pass `[]` for none, and delete the `.sample.ts` file and
its import once real data flows. A state variant (`--variant Empty`) is the same block with other
props, so it imports the primary instead of copying it. A marketing band is a page section, not a block (rule
`webkit-sections`).

## Headers and the docs home — never hand-build these

- **Every app header has search.** A console, demo, docs or site header puts `SearchTrigger`
  (`@aziontech/webkit/search-trigger`) first in `AppHeader.End`, opening a `Command` palette;
  it draws `Search … ⌘K` (`Ctrl K` off macOS) on a wide bar and the magnifier on a narrow one, and
  binds the shortcut. `ConsoleLayout`, `SiteLayout` and `DocLayout` already carry it, wired to
  their palette (rule `webkit-header-search`, lint `webkit/require-header-search`).
- **A docs home is `shell/shell-docs --variant Landing`.** It opens on `DocHero` (display
  title with air above it, deck, `Get started` then `CopyPromptButton` — the dark "Copy prompt"
  chip carrying the Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Cursor marks — and a note), then the first section
  opens on `DocAgentCard` ("Your AI agent, fluent in Azion" with the inline Copy prompt; "Prefer the
  guided route?" with the orange Agent setup over a halftone) above the Console, CLI and API
  `DocCard`s (`az az-azion`, `az az-azion-cli`, `az az-azion-api`). Framework templates use the
  brand-colour icons (`az-color az-react`). Do not substitute `DocPageHeader`, a `DocPrompt` or a
  `DocCard` with an overline for these.

## Read the pattern first

A **pattern** is the written guidance for one kind of screen or problem: how a form, a table, a
state or an error is built here. A **block** is the copyable screen that already follows it. Before
composing a screen, read the pattern for the job, then start from its block. Each pattern is the
`SKILL.md` named below (in `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/skills/`), and the same file is the page
on the docs site:

| Job | Pattern | Docs page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A whole product screen, end to end (the routing table) | `webkit-product-screens` | `/patterns/product-screens` |
| An Azion web page (rule `webkit-site-pages`, SD-01 to SD-25) | `webkit-site-pages` | `/patterns/site-pages` |
| A form, and the control each value takes (dates in `DatePicker`, periods in `DateRangePicker`, references in a searchable picker, never an ID or ISO date typed as text) | `webkit-form` | `/patterns/form` |
| Where a create lives: page, drawer or dialog | `webkit-create-surface` | `/patterns/create-surface` |
| A data table: columns, toolbar, scroll, cell recipes | `webkit-tables` | `/patterns/tables` |
| The list page around a table: filters, collection, selection | `webkit-lists` | `/patterns/lists` |
| A chart, a stat or a figure | `webkit-data-viz` | `/patterns/data-viz` |
| API data: references by name, remote pickers, fresh lookups, typed records | `webkit-api-data` | `/patterns/api-data` |
| Loading, empty, error and success; async behaviour | `webkit-ui-states` | `/patterns/ui-states` |
| Where a failure goes: field, section, toast, signed-out screen | `webkit-errors` | `/patterns/errors` |
| Explaining a field, section or page in place | `webkit-in-product-help` | `/patterns/in-product-help` |
| Shells, levels, breadcrumb, and drawers: never the way into a resource; `large`, then at most one `medium` | `webkit-navigation` | `/patterns/navigation` |
| Page width, inset and rhythm | `webkit-layout` | `/patterns/layout` |
| Every interface string | `webkit-microcopy` | `/patterns/microcopy` |
| AI chat, streamed answers and actions the reader approves | `webkit-ai-surfaces` | `/patterns/ai-surfaces` |
| Calling the Azion API: CORS, the dev and edge proxy, the token | `webkit-azion-api` | `/patterns/azion-api` |
| A Metrics or Events GraphQL explorer | `webkit-query-explorer` | `/patterns/query-explorer` |

The working steps are skills you run, not pages to read. Structure and states first, polish last:

- **Right component per moment:** `/webkit-ux-heuristics`
- **Foundation:** `/webkit-quick-cleanup` (tokens, typography, spacing rhythm) ·
  `/webkit-theming-dark-mode`
- **Polish:** `/webkit-motion-polish` → `/webkit-final-polish`
- **Verify:** `/webkit-ui-verify` (real browser, both themes, several widths, axe)
- **Adopting WebKit in an existing app:** `/webkit-adoption`

## Pick the component for the job

Name the job first, then take the component made for it. A plain `Input`, a string in a `<span>`
or a `Button` with extra markup is the answer only when no row below fits. For a form field, the
table is in `/webkit-form` ("Pick the control from the kind of value"); for a chart,
`/webkit-data-viz`; for an AI conversation, `/webkit-ai-surfaces`.

### Showing a value

| The screen shows | Use | Never |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A moment in time (created, updated, expires, ran at) | `Timestamp`; in a `DataTable` column, `TableCellTime`; inside a sentence, `useLocale().formatRelativeTime(date)` | a string such as `'Nov 10'` or `'5 minutes ago'` |
| A monetary amount | `CurrencyAmount` | `'$' + value.toFixed(2)` |
| A number, a file size, a percentage, a list of words | the `useLocale()` formatters (`formatNumber`, `formatFileSize`, `formatList`) | `toFixed`, `toLocaleString` or a hand-made unit ladder |
| The state of a resource (Active, Failed, Paused) | `StatusIndicator` | a coloured `Tag`, a coloured dot drawn by hand |
| How severe a finding is (critical, high, medium, low) | `SeverityTag` | a `Tag` with a hand-picked colour |
| An HTTP method and status (`GET 200`) | `StatusCode` | a `Tag` |
| A category or label word | `Tag` | a `Chip` (a chip is removable or selectable) |
| A count attached to something (unread, items in a section) | `Badge` | a `Tag` with a number |
| The first value of a list and "+3" for the rest | `OverflowCount` | a truncated string |
| A short value the reader pastes elsewhere (ID, CNAME, token name) | `CopyText` (the value shown) or `CopyButton` beside your own markup | a hand-written clipboard call |
| Code, config or JSON to read or copy | `CodeBlock` | a `pre` element, a read-only `Textarea` |
| Build, deploy or runtime log lines | `LogViewer` | a `CodeBlock` |
| The facts of one resource (ID, region, created at) | `KeyValueList` | a two-column `Table` |
| A person, or the people on something | `Avatar`, `AvatarGroup` | an `img` in a circle |
| A key or a shortcut | `Kbd` | a styled `code` element |
| A value a phone must pick up (an authenticator URI, a link) | `QrCode` | an image from a third-party service |
| A payment card network | `PaymentBrand` | a logo file of your own |
| Another company's mark | `ThirdPartyLogo` | a hand-picked SVG |
| Usage against a limit | `Progress` | a hand-drawn bar |
| A file opened from a list (image, text, JSON, PDF) | `FilePreview` | an `iframe` or `img` by hand |
| How urgent a ticket or task is (urgent, high, medium, low) | `PriorityTag` | a `Tag` with a hand-picked colour |
| Time left before a deadline (a response target, an expiry) | `Countdown` | a relative-time string you refresh by hand |
| The events of one record in order (ticket activity, audit history) | `Timeline` | a list of dated paragraphs |
| The messages of a ticket or case (replies, internal notes) | `MessageThread` | chat bubbles built from `Card` |

### Look-alikes: which one

| Pair | Use the first when | Use the second when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DataTable` / `DataGrid` | people read rows and act on them (sort, filter, select, open) | people edit many cells of many records in place, like a spreadsheet |
| `DataTable` / `Table` | the rows come from data (`data` + `columns`), with sort and pages | a small static table composed by hand |
| `DataTable` / `CardList` | records compare column by column | each record reads as a card (a logo, a title, a few facts) |
| `Wizard` / `Stepper` | an ordered create needs steps, content and Cancel, Previous, Next | only the step rail is needed and the footer and gating are your own |
| `CodeBlock` / `CodeEditor` | the person reads or copies the code | the person edits the code |
| `DropdownMenu` / `SplitButton` | a button opens a list of actions | one default action has a few related alternatives |
| `DropdownMenu` / `ContextMenu` | the menu opens from a button | the same actions open by right-click or long-press on an item |
| `Button` / `IconButton` | the action has a text label | the action is an icon alone (it needs `aria-label`) |
| `Button` / `HighlightButton` | every action | the one AI entry point of the screen |
| `ButtonGroup` / `ToggleGroup` | several separate actions sit joined in one bar | one of several views or modes is chosen and stays selected |
| `CopyButton` / `CopyText` | you already show the value and need only the copy control | the component should show the value and copy it |
| `Tabs` / `Accordion` | one of a few peer views is visible at a time | sections expand and collapse in place, several may be open |
| `Tabs` / `PageTabs` | the views switch inside a page region | the tabs are the second-level strip of a resource page, under its header, with the resource's actions |
| `Tree` / `SidebarMenu` | the person browses or picks from nested data (files, folders) | the rows are the app's navigation |
| `Dialog` / `Drawer` | a short question or confirmation interrupts the task | a form or a detail opens over the screen that owns it |
| `ConfirmDialog` / `Dialog` | the person confirms one action, most often a destructive one | the dialog holds anything else |
| `Tooltip` / `Popover` | a short hint shows on hover or focus and holds no control | the panel holds controls or longer content and opens on click |
| `Tooltip` / `Hint` | an existing control needs a hint | a label needs an info glyph that explains it |
| `Alert` / `Toast` | the message belongs to the page or a section and stays | the message confirms something that just happened and leaves |
| `Skeleton` / `Spinner` | content is loading and its shape is known | a short action is running inside a control |
| `Progress` / `UploadProgress` | one measured value against a total | file transfers keep running while the person works elsewhere |
| `EmptyState` / `ErrorBoundary` | there is no data, or a load failed and you render the message | a region may throw while rendering and must not take the page down |
| `Timestamp` / `DatePicker` | the person reads a date | the person picks a date |
| `Select` / `Combobox` | the value must be one of the options | the list only suggests and a typed value is valid |
| `Card` / `IntegrationCard` | any framed content | a catalog tile for an integration: logo, vendor, installed state, one action |
| `HelpPanel` / `TutorialPanel` | static help for the page | a guided tutorial whose steps point at real controls |
| `ScrollArea` / plain overflow | a bounded region scrolls inside the page (a panel body, a wide table) | the page itself scrolls |

Also in the app shell: `SkipLink` is the first child of every page shell (the layouts place it
for you). For a plan row use `PricingCard`; for an official product scene, `Illustration`; to run
real components in a device-sized viewport in docs, `BrowserFrame`.

## How to find a component

Do not guess a component name or import path. Look it up.

1. Ask the webkit MCP. The server exposes tools grounded in the exact webkit version this project installed. Arguments are JSON fields of the call; required ones are in bold, and `surface` is `app`, `site` or `docs` (console screens: `app`):
   - `search_blocks` — **`query`** (the screen in plain words), `surface`, `fragments` (boolean). Start every screen here.
   - `get_block` — **`id`**, `variant`, `sections` (`["guidelines"]` or `["sfc"]`).
   - `suggest_component` — **`need`** (what you are building, e.g. `"a ranked top list"`), `surface`; the block, section or component that fits, with alternatives.
   - `search_components` — **`query`**, `surface`.
   - `get_component`, `get_import`, `get_usage_example`, `get_best_practices` — **`name`** (kebab-case, e.g. `"bar-list"`).
   - `list_components` — `category`, `surface`, `cursor`, `limit`; `list_categories` — none; `list_tokens` — `category` (a group such as `bg`, or one token name such as `--bg-surface`; each semantic token comes with its light and dark value and its purpose); `list_assets` — `kind`, `query`.
   - `validate_usage` — `import`, `classes`, `component`: confirm a subpath is real and a class string is allowed.
2. No MCP? Read `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/llms/llms.txt`. It links one Markdown page per block (`llms/blocks/<id>.md`: guidelines, variants, the primary SFC), per component (`llms/components/<name>.md`: props, events, slots, examples, accessibility, do and don't, with the same data as JSON in `<name>.json`) and per foundation (`llms/foundations/`: tokens, color, typography, spacing, motion, i18n, RTL, devices). `llms-full.txt` is every page in one file.
3. Read the catalog directly. `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/catalog.json` has an `imports` object; every key is a real published subpath (`button`, `empty-state`, `table`, ...). If a subpath is not a key there, it does not exist.

## App-level setup (`setup` in the catalog)

A few components need **one-time wiring in the app entry before first use** — the catalog entry (and `get_component` on the MCP) carries it in a `setup` field. When `setup` is non-null, apply it BEFORE emitting code that uses the component, and check whether the project already has it (do not duplicate).

- **Toast**: fire-from-anywhere (`toast.success('Saved')`) only renders if a region is mounted. Wire the service once in the entry — `import { ToastPlugin } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast'` and chain `.use(ToastPlugin)` onto `createApp()`; the plugin mounts the region automatically (options: `app.use(ToastPlugin, { duration: 6000 })`; leave `position` at its `bottom-end` default, where every app puts toasts). A manually mounted Toaster also counts — never add both blindly (the store keeps only the first region active, but one wiring is enough). `npx webkit doctor` flags toast usage with no wired region.

- **Theme (light or dark)**: with no `data-theme` the theme follows the device (`prefers-color-scheme`). An app that is always dark sets `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` in `index.html` (`<html lang="en" data-theme="dark">`), so the first paint is dark, and an app that is always light sets `data-theme="light"`; a toggle writes `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` (`'dark'` / `'light'`), and a `.dark` class on an ancestor works too. Every token switches with it — never add per-theme classes (`/webkit-theming-dark-mode`).

- **ConfigProvider (languages)**: mount it once at the app root; pass `locale` when the user chose one, or leave it unset to follow the device locale (`en-US` on the server and until mount, then `navigator.language`). Every built-in string a component ships (close buttons, pagination, empty states, assistive labels) then reads from the locale's catalog, and dates, numbers, file sizes and plurals format with `Intl` for that locale; `dir` follows the locale (`ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur` are right-to-left). English is built in; Portuguese and Spanish are opt-in: import them from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR` and `@aziontech/webkit/locales/es` and pass them through `catalogs` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`), or the provider falls back to English and warns in development. With no provider every component formats for the device locale and reads English text. Only what people read follows the locale: send the `v-model` value to your server (DatePicker a `Date`, DateRangePicker ISO 8601 instants, TagEditor `key`/`value` pairs), never a printed label. A label prop you pass still wins over the catalog; `messages` renames a built-in string for the whole app. Import it as `import ConfigProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/config-provider'`.

```vue
<!-- App.vue -->
<script setup>
  import { es } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/es'
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import ConfigProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/config-provider'

  const catalogs = { 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }
</script>

<template>
  <ConfigProvider
    :locale="user.locale"
    :catalogs="catalogs"
  >
    <RouterView />
  </ConfigProvider>
</template>
```

In your own components, `useLocale()` from `@aziontech/webkit/use-locale` returns the active `locale`, `dir`, `t(key, params)` and the `Intl` helpers (`formatNumber`, `formatDate`, `formatRelativeTime`, `formatList`, `formatFileSize`, `plural`), so your numbers and dates match WebKit's. `t` reads the provider's catalog; pass the English messages it should fall back to when no provider is mounted (`useLocale(en)`, with `en` from the same import).

## Must Have

- ✅ Flat import: `import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'`.
- ✅ PascalCase binding matching the last path segment: `@aziontech/webkit/icon-button` -> `IconButton`.
- ✅ One `ConfigProvider` at the app root with the user's locale and the catalogs of every language the app offers.
- ✅ Color, spacing, radius, and typography from `@aziontech/theme` tokens (`var(--primary)`, `var(--spacing-md)`, `text-button-lg`).
- ✅ `import './webkit.css'` (the theme, the fonts and `./webkit.sources.css`, as `webkit init` writes it) and `import '@aziontech/icons'` once near the app entry (e.g. `src/main.ts`).
- ✅ `webkit()` from `@aziontech/webkit/vite-plugin` in `vite.config`: it keeps `src/webkit.sources.css`, the WebKit files Tailwind compiles, in step with your imports. Without Vite, run `npx @aziontech/webkit css` after adding or removing a WebKit import.
- ✅ The tree-shakeable `<name>-root` path (or specific sub-components) when you only need the root.
- ✅ Icons via the `@aziontech/icons` font: side-effect import once (`import '@aziontech/icons'`) + the icon CSS classes.
- ✅ Colour logos (`az-color az-<name>`) need no import: `./webkit.css` compiles the ones your sources name, so write the whole class in the code (`'az-color az-react'`, never `` `az-color az-${name}` ``). A logo named only in fetched data goes in `@source inline("az-react");` in `webkit.css`; the whole set (`import '@aziontech/icons/azionicons-color'`, about 85 KB gzip) is only for a page that shows every logo.
- ✅ Artwork and icon names from the published lists: `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/llms/foundations/` (`illustrations.md`, `diagrams.md`, `brand-marks.md`, `icons.md`) or the MCP `list_assets` (`variant`, plus a `query` such as "ddos" or "delete"). Icon classes are `az az-<name>`, and `az-color az-<name>` for a colour logo; pick one by what it stands for (`list_assets` gives each icon's group, category and meaning, and a product icon names only that product). WebKit 6 uses only the Azion set: write `az az-check`, never the removed `pi pi-check` set (the default `@aziontech/icons` entry no longer loads it; `webkit migrate v6` rewrites old classes).
- ✅ A webkit component reused instead of a hand-rolled or third-party equivalent.
- ✅ A control that matches the value's type: `DatePicker` (`show-time` for an instant) or `DateRangePicker` for dates and periods, a searchable picker for a reference to another resource, a `Select` or `RadioGroup` for an enum (`/webkit-form`, Pick the control from the kind of value; the lint rule `prefer-value-control` fails a typed date, and `prefer-date-picker` and `no-raw-id-input` warn on the text fields it cannot see).

## Must Not Have

- ❌ Category-prefixed import: `@aziontech/webkit/feedback/skeleton`.
- ❌ `/src/` or deep-internal imports: `@aziontech/webkit/src/components/...`.
- ❌ Barrel import: `import { Button } from '@aziontech/webkit'` (no barrel exists).
- ❌ Binding that disagrees with the path: `import Chip from '@aziontech/webkit/chips'`.
- ❌ Hardcoded color: `#fff`, `rgb(...)`, `hsl(...)`, `text-[#1e40af]`, or raw Tailwind palette (`bg-blue-600`).
- ❌ Restyling a webkit component: `<Button class="bg-(--primary)">`, `:class`, `style` on its tag. Use its props; put your classes on your own wrapper or in its slots. Only layout utilities (size, flex and grid placement, order, logical margins) may sit on the tag, each optionally behind a breakpoint prefix (`sm:` to `2xl:`): `w-full`, `h-full`, `max-w-*`, `min-w-*`, `max-h-*`, `min-h-*`, `flex-1`, `flex-auto`, `flex-initial`, `flex-none`, `grow`, `grow-*`, `basis-*`, `shrink-0`, `self-*`, `justify-self-*`, `place-self-*`, `order-*`, `col-span-*`, `col-start-*`, `col-end-*`, `row-span-*`, `row-start-*`, `row-end-*`, `m-*`, `mx-*`, `my-*`, `mt-*`, `mb-*`, `ms-*`, `me-*`.
- ❌ An illustration, diagram, figure or mark name guessed from a file in `src/` or from the page title: an unknown illustration renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder, an unknown diagram or figure draws nothing.
- ❌ `ai ai-<name>`, `ai-cor ai-<name>` or `ai-color ai-<name>`: the old base classes are gone in WebKit 6. Use `az az-<name>` and, for a colour logo, `az-color az-<name>` (never `az-<name>-color`).
- ❌ A default/namespace binding of `@aziontech/icons` (`import Icons from '@aziontech/icons'`) — it is a font; import it for side effects only.
- ❌ A custom Button, Modal, Table, Tooltip, etc. when webkit ships one.
- ❌ Passing a translated label to every instance (`aria-label="Fechar"` on each close button) instead of setting the locale on `ConfigProvider`.

## Common Patterns

### Import + tokens

Pick a token by its purpose, not its value: `list_tokens` gives every semantic token's light and
dark value and a one-line purpose, and the rule `webkit-tokens` holds the design intent behind the
groups (the surface order, the two rhythm steps, radius and type by role).

Tokens style **your own** markup around a component. The component keeps its own look and changes
it only through its props (`variant`, `size`); a class or style on its tag is restyling it (rule
`webkit-style-override`):

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
</script>

<template>
  <section
    class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md) rounded-(--shape-card) bg-(--bg-surface) p-(--spacing-lg)"
  >
    <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">Changes apply to every domain.</p>
    <Button
      variant="primary"
      label="Save"
    />
  </section>
</template>
```

### Compound vs tree-shakeable root

`Table` (and every other composition component) has two import shapes. Lead with the compound, the
form the examples and blocks use; reach for the root path only when you render the root alone:

```ts
import Table from '@aziontech/webkit/table' // compound: Table.Row, Table.Cell, ...
import TableRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/table-root' // root only, no dot-notation parts
import TableRow from '@aziontech/webkit/table-row' // one part on its own
```

Bind each import to the PascalCase of its path: `table-root` is `TableRoot`, never `Table`, so
`<Table.Row>` never appears on a binding that has no parts.

### Lazy-load a heavy overlay

```js
import { defineAsyncComponent } from 'vue'

const Dialog = defineAsyncComponent(() => import('@aziontech/webkit/dialog'))
```

### Docs pages: code samples and diagrams

- A code sample is `DocCodeGroup`. Set `language` on every sample; the block shows a label header
  with its readable name (Shell, JavaScript, JSON) by default.
- A **command** block holds only what the reader runs; its copy control copies exactly that (a
  leading `$ ` prompt is drawn but not copied). What the command prints goes in the sample's
  `output` field, drawn as a separate muted "Output" block with no copy control, or in prose. Never
  write output into the command as `# HTTP/2 200` (lint `webkit/no-output-in-command`, rule
  `webkit-code-samples`).
- A standalone printout (a deploy log) is `<DocCodeGroup type="output" …>`, not a "Text" sample.
- A flow diagram in a docs column is `Diagram` with one `row`: in the docs column it stacks, the
  nodes are centred, connectors run through the centre of each node and an edge label sits on its
  line. Do not offset nodes or labels to fake that.

### Logos, badges and photos

Logos, compliance badges and illustrations ship in the package: import the file and pass the URL
(`import magalu from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/magalu-extended-color.svg'`, then
`logo: magalu`). Names follow `<brand>-<extended|symbol>-<color|mono|reversed>` (`extended` is the
wordmark, `symbol` the mark; `color` for light surfaces, `reversed` for dark ones, `mono` in one
ink); `catalog.json` lists every file under `imports` with `"kind": "asset"`. A client wall
(`ClientQuotesSection`, `LogoWall`) on the dark site shows each brand in colour: `-extended-color` where it
reads on black (GPA, Zoop, HeroSpark, Magalu), `-extended-reversed` where the colour logo has dark
lettering (Axur, Contabilizei, Dafiti, Global Fashion Group); a one-ink registry `mark` only for a client with no
logo file. Photos, covers,
banners and clips are your content: pass URLs your app serves, or
`@aziontech/webkit/assets/placeholder-image.svg` / `placeholder-clip.webm` until you have them.
Never copy a root-relative `/marketing-components/…` or `/media/…` URL from azion.com or the docs
site: your app does not serve it (lint `webkit/no-root-relative-asset`).

### Large data and server rendering

- Pass the whole list: `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `LogViewer` and `CodeBlock` mount long lists (over 300 rows) in chunks as they scroll into view, and `Tree` renders collapsed children only when expanded. Do not page or slice the data yourself to make them fast.
- `Chart` takes 10k points per series; its hidden data table keeps an even sample of 1,000 rows, so turn on `tableView` when people need every value on screen.
- `PhoneInput` loads its flag sprite the first time the country list opens; the closed field costs no image download.
- Every block and example renders on the server (`renderToString`). Keep `window` and `document` out of `setup` in your own screens: read them in `onMounted`.

### App entry (styles + icons)

```ts
// src/main.ts
import './webkit.css' // the theme, the fonts and the WebKit files this app imports
import '@aziontech/icons'
```

`src/webkit.css` imports `./webkit.sources.css`, one `@source` per WebKit file the app imports, so
the stylesheet holds only the classes of the components you use. A bare `import '@aziontech/theme'`
compiles no component class: the components render unstyled.

## Quality Checklist

Before you finish UI work in this project:

- [ ] Every webkit import is flat (`@aziontech/webkit/<name>`), no category, no `/src/`, no barrel.
- [ ] Every binding is PascalCase of its subpath's last segment.
- [ ] No hardcoded colors — all color/spacing/typography via `@aziontech/theme` tokens.
- [ ] Icons imported individually; the whole set is never bulk-imported.
- [ ] Root-only usage takes the `-root` path; heavy overlays are lazy-loaded.
- [ ] No custom component reinvents something webkit already provides (checked via MCP or `catalog.json`).
- [ ] `./webkit.css` and `@aziontech/icons` are imported once at the app entry, and `npx @aziontech/webkit css --check` passes (the Vite plugin keeps it so).
- [ ] `ConfigProvider` wraps the app once with the user's locale, and `catalogs` registers every non-English language the app offers.

## Part B — using a webkit component in your project

Install the ESLint plugin and enable the `recommended` preset — **every rule is `error`**, so
off-pattern usage fails your lint.

```js
// eslint.config.js
import webkit from '@aziontech/webkit/eslint-plugin'
export default [...webkit.configs.recommended]
```

| Do this | ❌ Avoid | ✅ Do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Import** | `import { Button } from '@aziontech/webkit'` | `import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'` |
| **No internal / typo** | `@aziontech/webkit/src/…` · `…/buton` | `@aziontech/webkit/button` |
| **Tree-shaking** | `import Table` (compound) when you only render the root | `import TableRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/table-root'` |
| **Don't override styles** | `<Button class="p-8" />` | compose inside its slots, or use a `styleSeam` component |
| **No deprecated** | importing a deprecated component | the suggested replacement |
| **Tokens, not colors** | `class="text-[#fff]"` | `class="text-(--text-default)"` |
| **Icons** | `import Icons from '@aziontech/icons'` | `import '@aziontech/icons'` (side-effect) |

**Discover the API before you write it:** the webkit MCP server (`npx -y @aziontech/webkit-mcp@^6`, wired
into `.mcp.json` by `init`) answers
`list_components`, `get_component`, `list_tokens`, `suggest_component`, `get_best_practices`,
and `validate_usage` — so an AI (or you) gets the right import / token / prop _before_ the lint
has to reject the wrong one.

# AccountActivityHistory (`account/account-activity-history`)

> The account's audit log: a `PageHeader` with Documentation over one controls row (`PropertyFilter` on event, category, user and IP address; a `DateRangePicker` for the period, last 30 days by default; Refresh, Downloa…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/account/account-activity-history/account-activity-history.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("account/account-activity-history")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, ConfigProvider, CopyButton, DataTable, `DataTablePagination`, DateRangePicker, EmptyState, IconButton, PageHeader, PropertyFilter, Table, `TableCellTime`, Tag, Tooltip, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

activity history; audit log; audit trail; account activity; security log; who did what; user activity; event history; histórico de atividades; log de auditoria; trilha de auditoria; atividade da conta

The account's audit log. An admin or a security reviewer answers "who did this, from where, and when": a token that was revoked, a role that changed, a sign-in that failed, a plan that was upgraded. They narrow the log by period, category, person and address, read the newest events first, copy an IP address into another tool, and export what they found. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The account or organisation audit log: sign-ins, security changes, member and role changes, billing changes, deploys.
- Any append-only list of events people search by who, what, where and when.

## When not to use

- Request logs or metrics explored over time with a chart: use `view/view-events-explorer`.
- The deploy history of one resource: use `detail/detail-deployment-logs` or the details page's history tab.
- A short "recent activity" card on a dashboard: use `Item` rows in a `Card` and link here with View all.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `ConfigProvider`, `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)
- C. Period — `DateRangePicker` (required)
- D. Listing actions — `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- E. Event table — `Card`, `DataTable`, `DataTablePagination`, `TableCellTime`, `Tag`, `CopyButton`, `useCollection` (required)
- F. No match and empty period — `EmptyState` (required)
- G. Load failure — `Alert` (conditional)

What each part takes: [blocks/account/account-activity-history.md](blocks/account/account-activity-history.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `ActivityHistoryEvent` and `ActivityHistoryProps` are exported from `account-activity-history.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample events and the fixed clock the block renders when `events` and `now` are left out (the events never show while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `events`, `now`, `range`, `loading`, `error`.

Event: `refresh`, `retry`, `update:range`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/account/account-activity-history.md](blocks/account/account-activity-history.md).

## Do

- Write each event as a past-tense sentence with the object's name: `Revoked personal token “Nightly export”`.
- Show the newest first and keep the exact time on the tooltip.
- Keep IP addresses left to right and copyable.
- Keep the period and the filters in the controls row, the export last but one, preferences last.

## Don't

- Don't let anyone edit or delete an event from this page.
- Don't put the period in the property filter, or show a period with no events as an error.
- Don't truncate the event sentence without the full text on the row.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Activity history`. **Filter:** `Filter activity`. **Period:** `Activity period`.
- **Categories:** `Sign-in`, `Security`, `Users`, `Billing`, `Deploy`.
- **Empty period:** `No activity in this period`, then `Nothing happened in the account in the selected period. Select a longer period to see older events.` and `Show the last <next preset>`; at 90 days, `Nothing happened in the account in the last 90 days, the longest period events are kept.` with no action.
- **No match:** `No matching events`, `No event in this period matches these filters.`, `Clear filters`.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- No `main` of its own (the layout's is the only one); the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`; the table is named `Activity history`.
- The filter and the period picker carry `aria-label`s; icon buttons have names that match their tooltips.
- Category is text in a tag, never colour alone; the relative date has the exact time on its tooltip.
- User and IP cells keep their own direction (`dir="auto"`, `dir="ltr"`) inside a right-to-left page.
- `/` focuses the property filter from anywhere on the page, except while typing in a field.

## States

- Default: ten events over three weeks, the last 30 days selected, with filter, period, refresh, export, preferences, sorting and paging wired.
- Empty: the period (`range`, the last 15 minutes) holds no event; a flush empty state offers the next longer period, the last hour.
- Loading: the first load (`loading` with no `events`); the controls and the table's loading rows.
- Error: the log did not load (`error` is set); a danger Alert with the message and Retry.

## Related

- `view/view-table` — the list page this one follows.
- `account/account-personal-tokens` and `account/account-team-permissions` — the screens whose changes are logged here.
- `view/view-events-explorer` — events over time with a chart and a document pane.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Empty` · `Loading` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/account/account-activity-history.md](blocks/account/account-activity-history.md), `get_block("account/account-activity-history", { variant })`.

# AccountBilling (`account/account-billing`)

> The Billing page of the account settings: a `PageHeader` with the last update, Refresh and Documentation over `PageTabs` (Bills, Payment methods).

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/account/account-billing/account-billing.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("account/account-billing")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, CurrencyAmount, DataTable, `DataTablePagination`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, IconButton, KeyValueList, Link, PageHeader, PageTabs, PaymentBrand, PropertyFilter, Skeleton, StatusIndicator, Subheader, Table, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellStatus`, Tabs, Tag, Toast, Tooltip, `use-collection`, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

billing; billing page; invoices; invoice history; download invoice; subscription plan; current plan; payment methods; default card; billing email; faturamento; faturas; histórico de faturas; plano de assinatura; métodos de pagamento; cobrança

What the account pays, what it paid and which card it is charged to. An admin checks the current plan and the next charge, moves to another plan, finds and downloads an invoice, and keeps the cards on file current: which one is the default, which ones to remove. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The billing page of an account or organisation: plan, invoice history and payment methods.
- Downloading or exporting past invoices.
- Choosing the card invoices are charged to.

## When not to use

- Comparing plans and upgrading: use `account/account-change-plan-drawer`, which this page opens from Change plan.
- Entering a new card: use `account/account-payment-method-card`.
- Usage charts and quotas: use a `dashboard` block.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Button` (required)
- B. Tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)
- C. Load failure — `Alert` (conditional)
- D. Subscription plan — `Card`, `Skeleton`, `Tag`, `KeyValueList`, `CurrencyAmount`, `PaymentBrand` (required)
- E. Upgrade card — `Card`, `Link` (required)
- F. Invoices controls — `Subheader`, `PropertyFilter`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- G. Invoices table — `DataTable`, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellStatus`, `useCollection` (required)
- H. No invoices and no match — `EmptyState` (conditional)
- I. Payment information — `StatusIndicator` (required on the Payment methods tab)
- J. Payment methods — `DropdownMenu`, `ConfirmDialog` (required on the Payment methods tab)
- Outcomes — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/account/account-billing.md](blocks/account/account-billing.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `BillingProps`, `BillingInvoice`, `BillingPaymentMethod`, `BillingSubscription` and `BillingPaymentInformation` are exported from `account-billing.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample plan, invoices, cards and payment information the block renders when a prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `invoices`, `paymentMethods`, `subscription`, `paymentInformation`, `updatedAt`, `defaultQuery`, `tab`, `loading`, `error`.

Event: `refresh`, `retry`, `set-default`, `remove`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/account/account-billing.md](blocks/account/account-billing.md).

## Do

- Show the next charge date and value next to the plan, in the account's currency.
- Name the card by brand and last four everywhere: the plan card, the invoices and the methods table.
- Keep the default card from being removed; ask for another default first by disabling Remove on it.
- Keep the filter first, the export last but one and preferences last in the controls row.

## Don't

- Don't show a full card number or the card's security code.
- Don't stamp the last update with the clock at render; show the time the data was fetched.
- Don't treat an account with no invoices yet as an error.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Billing`. **Tabs:** `Bills`, `Payment methods`.
- **Plan card:** `Subscription plan`, `Current plan`, `Change plan`; facts `Plan start date`, `Next charge date`, `Next charge value`, `Payment method`.
- **Invoices:** `Filter invoices`; statuses `Paid`, `Refunded`, `Overdue`; empty `No invoices yet`, `Your first invoice appears here when the first billing cycle closes.`; no match `No matching invoices`, `Clear filters`.
- **Payment methods:** `Set as default`, `Remove`; confirm `Remove payment method`; toasts `Mastercard •••• 1702 is now the default.`, `Visa •••• 4431 removed.`
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- No `main` of its own; the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`, the cards and bands use `h2`.
- The tabs follow the tablist keyboard model from `Tabs`; both tables are named (`Invoices`, `Payment methods`).
- Icon buttons have names that match their tooltips; each download names its invoice and each row menu names its card.
- The `PaymentBrand` plate is decorative wherever the brand is written next to it, and named in the methods table.
- Invoice IDs, card digits and the billing email keep left-to-right direction inside a right-to-left page.
- `/` focuses the invoices property filter from anywhere on the page, except while typing in a field.
- The payment methods rows are one tab stop: Arrow Up and Arrow Down move between rows, Home and End jump to the first and last, and Delete or Backspace opens the remove dialog for a card that is not the default. After a removal, focus lands on the next row.

## States

- Default: the Bills tab (`tab` is `bills`) with the Pro plan, the Enterprise upgrade card and twelve monthly invoices, with filter, refresh, export, preferences, sorting and paging wired.
- Loading: the first load (`loading`); skeletons in the plan card and the invoices table's loading rows.
- Error: the billing data did not load (`error` is set); a danger Alert with the message and Retry.
- NoInvoices: no invoice yet (`invoices` is `[]`); a flush empty state says when the first one appears.
- NoMatch: a filter that matches no invoice (`defaultQuery` is Status = Overdue); No matching invoices with Clear filters.
- PaymentMethods: the Payment methods tab (`tab` is `payment-methods`) with payment information and three cards.

- **Unscoped failure:** a toast with Retry: `The upgrade failed. The account is still on Free.`, described by `The payment service did not answer. Your entries are kept.`
- **Success:** `The account was upgraded to Pro.`

- Each fieldset has a visually hidden legend (`Payment method`, `Address information`).
- After a failed Update or Upgrade, focus moves to the first field in error; after a decline, to the card number.
- The billing period toggle is labelled; a price change is visible text, not color only.

## States

# AccountDeploymentSettings (`account/account-deployment-settings`)

> The account's Build and deployment settings.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/account/account-deployment-settings/account-deployment-settings.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("account/account-deployment-settings")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, DataTable, `DataTablePagination`, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, IconButton, Input, Item, Kbd, PageHeader, Pagination, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PropertyFilter, RadioGroup, SaveBar, Select, SettingsGroup, SettingsRow, Skeleton, Switch, Table, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellLink`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTime`, Tag, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-lists`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

build and deployment; deployment settings; deployment defaults; binding policy; deployment policy; environment bindings; rebind environment; shared deployment setting; build e deploy; configurações de deploy; padrões de deploy; política de deploy; vincular ambiente

How every deploy in the account routes. A Deployment Setting holds a binding policy (whether a version locks the resource IDs it shipped with) and a deployment policy (one live version, or a URL per version); every environment of every service publishes with exactly one, linked automatically to a setting that matches its own deployment policy. On this page an admin sets the defaults the next service starts with, sees which environment publishes with which setting, points two environments at the same setting so one deploy reaches both, and manages the settings themselves. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Account-wide defaults for how new resources deploy, saved together.
- An overview of which environment uses which shared configuration, with a way to rebind each one in place.
- Managing a list of reusable deployment or routing configurations.

## When not to use

- The deployment settings of one service: use `edit/edit-resource#DeployableSettings`.
- Only the create form: use `create/create-drawer#DeploymentSettings`.
- Running a deploy: use `create/create-deploy-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. What a Deployment Setting is — `Alert` (required)
- C. New service defaults — `SettingsGroup`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Select`, `Switch`, `SaveBar` (required)
- D. All services — `Accordion`, `Input`, `Tag`, `Select`, `Pagination`, `TableCellLink` (required)
- E. Deployment Settings controls — `PropertyFilter`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- F. Deployment Settings table — `DataTable`, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTime`, `Card`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu`, `ConfirmDialog`, `EmptyState`, `useCollection` (required)
- G. Create and edit drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `Field`, `Textarea`, `RadioGroup` (required)
- H. Loading and no services — `Skeleton` (conditional)
- Outcomes — through `toast`
- I. Shortcut keycap — `Kbd` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/account/account-deployment-settings.md](blocks/account/account-deployment-settings.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `DeploymentSettingsProps`, `DeploymentSettingsSetting`, `DeploymentSettingsService` and the other types are exported from `account-deployment-settings.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample settings, services and defaults the block renders when those props are left out (and never while `loading` is set).

Prop: `settings`, `services`, `defaults`, `defaultDraft`, `currentUser`, `loading`, `saving`, `error`.

Event: `save`, `discard`, `refresh`, `bind`, `create`, `update`, `clone`, `delete`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/account/account-deployment-settings.md](blocks/account/account-deployment-settings.md).

## Do

- Offer only settings whose deployment policy matches the environment's; an environment cannot publish with any other.
- Say when a setting is shared, in the table and on every environment row, and warn when a rebind makes a deploy reach more services.
- Keep the defaults behind one SaveBar, and say that Default is never changed when Apply to existing is on.
- Say how many services fall back to Default before a setting is deleted.

## Don't

- Don't offer Edit, Clone or Delete on Default; every environment falls back to it.
- Don't apply the defaults to existing settings without the explicit switch.
- Don't let the deployment policy change on an existing setting; the environments bound to it depend on it.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Build and deployment`. **Action:** `Create Deployment Setting`; the drawer titles `Create Deployment Setting` and `Edit Deployment Setting`, the submits `Create Deployment Setting` and `Save changes`. The label does not change on the way in.
- **No match:** `No matching services`, `No service or setting matches “…”.`, `Clear search`.
- **Sections:** `New service defaults`, `All services`, `Deployment Settings`.
- **Policies:** `Strict`, `Flexible`; `Single`, `Versioned`.
- **Tags:** `System`, `Shared`, `Linked automatically`, `Shared · 2 services`, `1 on a shared setting`.
- **Toasts:** `Deployment defaults saved.`, `checkout-api · Production now publishes with storefront-production.`, `preview-versioned created.`, `legacy-rollout deleted.`
- **Errors:** `This field is required.`, `A Deployment Setting with this name already exists.`
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Each section title is an h2 with an anchor; the services accordion trigger is an h3 under it.
- Every environment `Select` is named `Deployment Setting for <service> <environment>`; the default `Select`s and the Switch take their row's title as their name.
- The services search is named, and a search with no match is announced as a status.
- The filter is named Filter Deployment Settings; Refresh and Download CSV are icon buttons with an accessible name and a tooltip; the row menu is named `Actions for <setting>`.
- The Services cell is focusable so its tooltip with the service names is reachable by keyboard.
- The SaveBar motion has a `motion-reduce` fallback.
- `⌘ S` (`Ctrl S` off Apple) saves the deployment defaults while the `SaveBar` shows unsaved changes, the same as Save, and stops the browser's own save; with no changes it does nothing. Save carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and a `Kbd` keycap.

## States

## Accessibility

Arrow Up and Arrow Down move between rows, Home and End go to the first and last, Arrow Right opens a row or moves into it, Arrow Left closes it or goes to its parent (mirrored right to left), Enter toggles it, Space selects it, and Delete or Backspace opens the delete dialog for it (with what it holds); after the delete, focus lands on the next row. Tab reaches the checkbox, ID copy and row menu of the focused row.
- The chevron is pointer-only and hidden from assistive technology; the row's `aria-expanded` is the state.

## Accessibility

- The fields sit in a `fieldset` with a hidden legend.
- The Wizard's `Step 1 of 3` line is a polite live region, so the step change is announced.

Check your connection, then retry. Your answers are kept.`) with Retry.

- **Field errors:** what is wrong and what to do: `This field is required.`, `Enter the month and year as MM/YY.`, `Enter the 3 or 4 digits on the back of the card.`
- **Decline:** `The card was declined, so the payment method was not changed. Check the number or use another card.`

- When Change opens the form, move focus to the first field; on Cancel or Update, back to Change.

## States

- Editing: after Change (`editing`), the card form over the PCI notice, with Cancel and Update. Update validates every field, focuses the first one in error and emits `submit`; `error` shows the decline.
- Disabled: while the upgrade submits (`disabled`), the Change action is disabled.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/account/account-personal-tokens/account-personal-tokens.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("account/account-personal-tokens")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, ConfigProvider, ConfirmDialog, CopyButton, DataTable, `DataTablePagination`, `DatePickerRoot`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, `FieldDescription`, IconButton, Input, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PasswordInput, PropertyFilter, Select, SettingsGroup, Table, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTime`, Textarea, Tooltip, `use-collection`, `use-locale`

## Asked as

personal tokens; personal access tokens; api tokens; api keys; access tokens; create token; revoke token; copy token once; token expiration; date and time field in a form; expiry date picker; tokens pessoais; token de acesso; chaves de api; criar token; revogar token

The Personal tokens page of the account settings. A person creates a token for a script, a CI job or the CLI, copies its secret the one time it is shown, sees which tokens are still alive and when each expires or was last used, and revokes one that leaked or is no longer needed. The secret never comes back: the list shows only the name, status and dates, and a lost secret means a new token. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Credentials a person creates for themselves to call the API: personal tokens, API keys, deploy keys.
- Any secret the server returns once: the same reveal dialog (warning, masked value, copy) applies.

## When not to use

- Team or service credentials with roles and scopes managed by an admin: start from `account/account-team-permissions` and add a scope field to the create drawer.
- Secrets the product stores and shows again (environment variables): use `edit/edit-variables` with masked values.
- A single key shown on a resource's details page: use `CopyButton` beside the value in `detail/detail-resource`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `ConfigProvider`, `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Controls row — `PropertyFilter`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- C. Token table — `Card`, `DataTable`, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTime`, `useCollection` (required)
- D. Row actions — `DropdownMenu` (required)
- E. No match and empty — `EmptyState` (required)
- F. Load failure — `Alert` (conditional)
- G. Create drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelBody`, `SettingsGroup`, `PanelFooter` (required)
- H. Fields — `Field`, `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `DatePickerRoot`, `FieldDescription` (required)
- I. One-time reveal — `Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `PasswordInput`, `CopyButton` (required)
- J. Confirmations and outcomes — `ConfirmDialog` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/account/account-personal-tokens.md](blocks/account/account-personal-tokens.md).

## Data

The block takes its tokens through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing and never makes a secret. `PersonalTokensToken`, `PersonalTokensCreateValues`, `PersonalTokensSecret` and `PersonalTokensProps` are exported from `account-personal-tokens.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample tokens and clock the block renders when `tokens` and `now` are left out (the tokens never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `tokens`, `loading`, `error`, `creating`, `now`, `secret`.

Event: `refresh`, `retry`, `create`, `revoke`, `delete`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/account/account-personal-tokens.md](blocks/account/account-personal-tokens.md).

## Do

- Show the secret once, masked by default, with a copy button and a warning that says it will not be shown again.
- Say the exact expiry date while the person picks the duration.
- Warn in the Status column a week before a token expires.
- Revoke behind a confirmation that names the token and what breaks.

## Don't

- Don't show a secret, or part of one, in the list.
- Don't let a token be edited or extended; create a new one.
- Don't offer Delete on a live token; revoke it first.
- Don't toast the reveal; the secret belongs in the dialog, where it can be copied.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Personal tokens`. **Create:** `Create Personal Token` on the page, as the drawer title and on the footer submit.
- **Status:** `Active`, `Expires in 3 days`, `Expired`, `Revoked`. **Last used:** relative time, or `Never used`.
- **Reveal:** title `Copy your new token`; warning `Copy the token and store it somewhere safe, such as a secret manager. After you close this dialog, it cannot be shown again; create a new one if it is lost.`
- **Revoke:** title `Revoke token`; description `Scripts and tools that use “<name>” stop working right away. You cannot undo this.`; button `Revoke token`; toast `Token “<name>” revoked. Requests that use it are now refused.`
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- No `main` of its own (the layout's is the only one); the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`.
- The `PropertyFilter` (Filter tokens) and every icon-only button carry an `aria-label`; the row menu is named `Actions for <token>`.
- The drawer and the dialogs trap focus, are named by their titles and return focus to their trigger; the first invalid field takes focus after Create.
- The reveal labels the secret field `Token`; the copy result is announced once, by the `CopyButton`.
- `/` focuses the property filter from anywhere on the page, except while typing in a field.
- The rows are one tab stop: Arrow Up and Arrow Down move between rows, Home and End jump to the first and last, and Delete or Backspace asks to revoke an active token or to delete a revoked or expired one, as the row menu does. After a delete, focus lands on the next row.

## States

- Default: `tokens` holds four tokens (active, expiring in 5 days, expired, revoked) with the property filter, Refresh, Download CSV, preferences, sorting, row menus, the create drawer, the reveal, revoke and delete wired.
- Empty: no token (`tokens` is `[]`); the heading and a flush empty state with Create Personal Token.
- Loading: the first load (`loading` with no `tokens`); controls row and the table's loading rows.
- Error: the list did not load (`error` is set); a danger Alert with the message and Retry replaces the table.
- Created: the one-time reveal dialog open after Create (`secret` holds the returned token).

> Teams and their permissions.

Who can do what in the account. An admin keeps one team per role (Administrators, Developers, Security, Finance), sees what each grants and how many people it covers, and creates or edits a team by ticking View and Edit per resource in one matrix. ## Do

## Accessibility

- The team rows are one tab stop: Arrow Up and Arrow Down move between rows, Home and End jump to the first and last, Enter edits the focused team as the row menu's Edit does, and Delete or Backspace opens the delete dialog. After a delete, focus lands on the next row.
