- Components: Alert, Avatar, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, DataTable, `DataTablePagination`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerDescription`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, IconButton, Input, KeyValueList, MultiSelect, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PropertyFilter, Select, Table, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTime`, Tag, Toast, Tooltip, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

users; users management; invite user; invite teammates; members; account members; assign teams; resend invitation; remove user; usuários; gerenciar usuários; convidar usuário; membros da conta; atribuir times; edit role; change role; user roles; view profile; alterar papel; papel do usuário

Who can sign in to the account, with which role and through which teams. An admin invites a teammate by email, chooses their teams, sees who has not accepted yet, resends or cancels an invitation, changes a person's role, moves a person between teams and removes people who left. The role decides what a person can do on the account itself (Admin manages people, teams and billing; Developer and Viewer do not); resource permissions come only from teams (`account/account-team-permissions`), so this page never grants a single permission to a person. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Inviting people to an account or organisation, choosing their role and assigning them to teams.
- Following pending invitations: resend or cancel.
- Removing a person's access.

## When not to use

- Defining what a team can do: use `account/account-team-permissions`.
- Credentials that act as a person: use `account/account-personal-tokens`.
- Who turned on multi-factor authentication: use `account/account-mfa-settings`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Controls row — `PropertyFilter`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- C. Users table — `Card`, `DataTable`, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTime`, `Avatar`, `Tag`, `useCollection` (required)
- D. Teams per person — `MultiSelect`, `Tooltip` (required)
- E. Row actions — `DataTable`, `DropdownMenu`, `ConfirmDialog` (required)
- F. Profile and role dialogs — `Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `KeyValueList`, `Select` (required)
- G. Invite drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerDescription`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `Field`, `Input`, `MultiSelect`, `Button` (required)
- H. Only the owner, no match and load failure — `EmptyState`, `Alert` (conditional)
- Outcomes — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/account/account-users.md](blocks/account/account-users.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `UsersUser`, `UsersTeam`, `UsersInvitation` and `UsersProps` are exported from `account-users.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the people and teams the block renders when `users` or `teams` is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `users`, `teams`, `loading`, `error`, `defaultInviteOpen`, `defaultEditRoleId`.

Event: `invite`, `refresh`, `retry`, `role-change`, `teams-change`, `resend-invitation`, `remove`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/account/account-users.md](blocks/account/account-users.md).

## Do

- Show pending invitations in the same list, marked Invited, with Resend and Cancel.
- Name the teams in the invitation toast and in every team change, and offer Undo for a team change.
- Say what stays when a person is removed (their teams and the resources they created).
- Keep the owner's row visible, with its controls locked and the reason on the tooltip; the owner keeps View profile.
- Say in the role dialog what the chosen role allows, and that teams still decide the resources.

## Don't

- Don't grant a resource permission to one person here; teams are the only way. The role covers account settings only.
- Don't offer Owner in the role list; ownership is transferred elsewhere.
- Don't apply an invitation without a team silently; a person with no team gets no access, so the form asks for one.
- Don't hide the email of an invited person; it is the only name they have until they accept.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Users`. **Action:** `Invite User`; the drawer title `Invite User`, the submit `Send invitation`.
- **Roles:** `Owner`, `Admin`, `Developer`, `Viewer`; the dialog `Edit role` with `Save role`.
- **Statuses:** `Active`, `Invited`, `Inactive`; **Last active** for an invitation: `Not signed in yet`.
- **Errors:** `Enter the email address to invite.`, `Enter an email address like name@example.com.`, `This person is already in the account.`, `Choose at least one team, or they get no access.`
- **Toasts:** `Invitation sent to sam.okafor@example.com.`, `Teams updated for Priya Nair.`, `Jordan Reyes is now Developer.`, `Invitation sent again to sam.okafor@example.com.`, `Jordan Reyes removed from the account.`
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The filter is named Filter users; Refresh and Download CSV are icon buttons with an accessible name and a tooltip.
- Each Teams control is named `Teams of <person>`; the row menu is named `Actions for <person>`.
- The role form is a `form` named Edit role; the `Select` is labelled Role and described by what the role allows.
- The invite form is a `form` named Invite User; each `Field` ties its label, description and error to the control, and `Field.Error` is announced when it appears.
- After a failed Send, focus moves to the first invalid control.
- The owner's locked controls are disabled and the reason is on the tooltip, not only in color.
- `/` focuses the property filter from anywhere on the page, except while typing in a field.
- The rows are one tab stop: Arrow Up and Arrow Down move between rows, Home and End jump to the first and last, Enter opens the person's profile, and Delete or Backspace opens the remove (or cancel invitation) dialog; the owner's row ignores Delete. After a removal, focus lands on the next row.

## States

- Default: six people (the owner, four active or inactive, one invited) with the property filter, Refresh, Download CSV, preferences, inline team changes, View profile, Edit role, resend, cancel and remove wired.
- Invite: the invite drawer open (`defaultInviteOpen`).
- EditRole: the Edit role dialog open for Jordan Reyes (`defaultEditRoleId`).
- OnlyOwner: the owner alone (`users` holds only the owner) and the invite empty state.
- Loading: the first load (`loading` with no `users`).
- Error: the list did not load (`error` is set); a danger Alert with the message and Retry.

## Related

- `account/account-team-permissions` — what each team can do.
- `account/account-mfa-settings` — who has multi-factor authentication on.
- `account/account-activity-history` — where invitations and removals are audited.
- `state/state-form-validation` (SectionRejected) — the error pattern the invite form follows.

# AiActionApproval (`ai/ai-action-approval`)

> A user-authorized action inside a generative AI conversation, from the messages of TanStack AI's `useChat`: the read-only call shows as a completed `ToolCall`, the explanation in `StreamingResponse`, and the call that…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/ai/ai-action-approval/ai-action-approval.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("ai/ai-action-approval")`
- Components: AgentQuestion, Alert, Button, ChatMessage, CodeBlock, Conversation, ImageGallery, `PromptInputAttachButton`, `PromptInputContextPicker`, `PromptInputDictateButton`, `PromptInputModelPicker`, PromptInput, StreamingResponse, ToolApproval, ToolCall, `use-locale`, `utils/ai-chat`
- Skills: `webkit-ai-surfaces`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

ai action approval; approve ai action; user authorized action; agent asks permission; human in the loop; tool call approval; confirm agent command; allow tool; aprovar ação da ia; autorizar ação do agente; confirmar comando; aprobar acción de la ia; approve an agent action; tool approval in chat

The moment an assistant needs permission. The reader asked for something that changes their account — a deployment, a purge, a deletion — and the assistant stops before doing it: it says what it found, shows exactly what will run, and waits for Approve or Deny. The decision stays in the thread as text, and the assistant reports what happened next, so the conversation is also the record of what ran and who allowed it. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: it fills the layout's content region (`grow basis-0 min-h-0`, never `h-dvh`), so only the log scrolls, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use ai-action-approval when an AI assistant proposes an action with side effects inside a conversation (ToolApproval).
- The assistant is about to call a tool or run a command with side effects: deploy, purge, change a rule, delete.
- A one-time decision about a consequential action, made inside the conversation.
- An irreversible action: add a typed confirmation to the card.

## When not to use

- Read-only calls (listing, reading metrics): record them with `ToolCall` and continue without asking.
- Tools the reader already allowed for this conversation: record the call, do not ask again.
- A destructive action the reader started from the UI, not the assistant: use `ConfirmDialog` (see `edit/edit-delete-dialog`).
- Several fields to fill before acting: link to the create or edit page; the card only approves or denies.

## Building blocks

- A. Conversation frame — `Conversation`, `PromptInput`
- B. Request — `ChatMessage`
- C. What the assistant checked — `ToolCall`, `StreamingResponse`
- D. Authorization card — `ToolApproval`, `CodeBlock`
- E. The action running — `ToolCall`, `ImageGallery`
- F. Outcome — `ChatMessage`, `Button`
- G. Questions and failed decisions — `AgentQuestion`, `Alert`
- H. Structured answers — `CodeBlock`, `Alert`

What each part takes: [blocks/ai/ai-action-approval.md](blocks/ai/ai-action-approval.md).

## Data

The block draws a conversation in the message shape of TanStack AI: each message has an `id`, a `role` and its `parts` in order (`text`, `thinking`, `tool-call`, `tool-result`, `structured-output`), so the values `useChat` from `@tanstack/ai-vue` returns go straight into its props, with no conversion. The block calls no model and runs no AI library; `@aziontech/webkit/utils/ai-chat` names TanStack AI's own message types, imported from `@tanstack/ai` as types only (an optional peer, `^1.5.0`), with the helpers that read them (`AiChatMessage`, `AiChatPart`, `AiChatTool`, `AiChatInterrupt`; import the types from there), so the shape follows TanStack when you update it, and any source that produces it works. Parts it does not draw (images, audio) are skipped. `sample.ts` holds the sample threads the variants pass. The draft in the composer stays local.

What TanStack AI does not carry, the app adds in `metadata`: `sources` (the documents the response cites, numbered in order), `reasoningSeconds` (left out, the block measures the thinking time) and `stopped` (the block also marks the response that Stop ended). A message's time is its `createdAt`, formatted in the reader's locale.

Prop: `messages`, `loading`, `error`, `tools`, `interrupts`, `interruptErrors`, `attachable`.

Event: `send`, `stop`, `retry`, `approve`, `deny`, `answer-interrupt`, `retry-interrupts`.

A tool that needs approval is declared once with `toolDefinition({ name, inputSchema, needsApproval: true })`, run on the server with `.server(...)` and passed to `useChat({ tools: [definition] })` too, so the client can match the approval request to the call. Then delete `sample.ts` and its import. `apps/demos` runs this block on `useChat` with TanStack AI's `fakeText` model (`src/lib/assistant-model.ts`), no server and no key.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/ai/ai-action-approval.md](blocks/ai/ai-action-approval.md).

## Do

- Show exactly what will run, with the real identifiers.
- Label the approve button with the verb of the title.
- Give a tool that waits for approval a neutral title in the imperative (`Deploy storefront to production`), never the progressive (`Deploying…`): the same title stays on the call after Denied, where an in-progress verb would claim it ran.
- Dismiss the buttons as soon as the reader decides and show the outcome in text.
- Acknowledge a denial and say nothing ran.
- Expire a request the reader leaves undecided and say nothing ran.
- Require typing the resource name before an irreversible action.

## Don't

- Don't run anything before Approve.
- Don't focus or pre-select Approve, and don't trap focus in the card; it is part of the conversation, not a dialog.
- Don't ask again for a tool the reader allowed for this conversation.
- Don't hide the command behind a summary; show it.
- Don't show secrets or tokens in the command or the tool details.

## Copy

- **Title:** a question naming the action, with the command or tool in code: ``Allow `azion deploy --env production`?``, "Delete the domain `old.example.com`?".
- **Description:** what changes and what stays, e.g. "Deploys build `b-4821` of storefront to production. The current version stays available for rollback."
- **Buttons:** Deny and the verb of the title (Deploy, Delete); "Approve" only for a generic tool call.
- **Typed confirmation:** "Type old.example.com to confirm" (built in).
- **Outcomes:** Approved, Denied (built in).
- **Decision not sent:** `Your decision was not sent` with the reason and Retry.
- **Assistant after a denial:** "Got it, nothing was deployed."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", present tense.

## Accessibility

- The card is a group named by its title and described by its description; it does not trap or take focus.
- Outcomes are text announced through a polite live region; status color is never the only signal.
- Tool calls announce their status changes (Running, Completed, Failed) through `StatusIndicator`.
- The typed confirmation has a visible label; Approve is disabled until it matches.
- Keyboard order: request, tool calls, response text, command, phrase field, Deny, approve.

## States

- Pending: the deployment call in `approval-requested`, waiting for Deny or Deploy; Deploy emits `approve` and resolves the matching interrupt, and the run goes on.
- Irreversible: a domain deletion whose tool has `variant: 'danger'` and `confirmationPhrase` in `tools`, so Delete enables only after the domain name is typed.
- Running: the call approved (`approval.approved: true`) and still running under the card, with `loading`, so the composer shows Stop.
- Approved: the call `complete` with its output, and the assistant's report after it.
- Denied: `approval.approved: false` and a `tool-result` with `outcome: 'denied'`; the card reads Denied, the call is recorded as denied and the assistant says nothing ran.
- Questions and failed decisions: a generic or unbound interrupt asks its `AgentQuestion` after the conversation; `interruptErrors` shows the alert with Retry.
- Error: the approved call in `error` with its `tool-result` error, and a report that says what failed and that `b-4790` still serves, with Deploy again.

## Related

- `ai/ai-chat` — the conversation this card lives in.
- `ai/ai-chat-drawer` — the same flow in a drawer over a resource page.
- `edit/edit-delete-dialog` — confirming a destructive action the reader started.
- `skills/webkit-ai-surfaces` — when to ask, what to show and how to record the outcome.

## Variants

`Pending` (primary) · `Irreversible` · `Approved` · `Denied` · `Running` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/ai/ai-action-approval.md](blocks/ai/ai-action-approval.md), `get_block("ai/ai-action-approval", { variant })`.

# AiChat (`ai/ai-chat`)

> The full-page generative AI assistant in the chat-app look: a thread history grouped by date (search, a project filter, New thread; each row shows its project, the Azion product it started on with how many it touches…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/ai/ai-chat/ai-chat.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`

- Components: AgentActivity, AgentQuestion, Alert, ArtifactCanvas, ArtifactPreview, `branches`, `placeholderClip`, `usageChart`, AudioPlayer, Button, ChatMessage, ChatMessage, CodeBlock, ConfirmDialog, Conversation, ConversationHistory, `DrawerBody`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerHeader`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem`, DropdownMenu, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, FeedbackReasonDialog, FilePreview, `HoverCardContent`, HoverCard, `HoverCardTrigger`, IconButton, ImageGallery, Input, McpAppFrame, `PopoverContent`, Popover, `PopoverTrigger`, `PromptInputAttachButton`, `PromptInputContextPicker`, `PromptInputDictateButton`, `PromptInputModelPicker`, PromptInput, PromptQueue, Reasoning, `ResizableHandle`, `ResizablePane`, Resizable, ResponseBranches, Skeleton, Sources, StatusIndicator, StreamingResponse, SubagentCard, SuggestionGroup, Toast, ToolApproval, ToolCall, Tooltip, `use-ai-chat-tools`, `use-ai-chat-versions`, `use-locale`, `utils/ai-chat`, VideoPlayer
- Skills: `webkit-ai-surfaces`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

ai chat; ai assistant; chatbot; copilot; chat with ai; generative ai chat; assistant page; ask ai; llm chat; conversational ui; prompt and response; streaming response; chat de ia; assistente de ia; assistente virtual; conversa com ia; chat con ia; asistente de ia; artifact; artifact canvas; generated file; code canvas; canvas de artefato; artefato gerado; full page chat; tanstack ai; usechat; agent activity; subagent; agent question

A full page where a person talks with the generative AI assistant about their account: they ask in their own words, watch the response arrive, check where it came from, and keep going with a follow-up or a new question. The page is the conversation: one reading column the thread scrolls in, with the header controls and the composer floating over it. Beside it, the conversation history. Use it as the assistant's home; on a resource page, open the same conversation in a drawer with `ai/ai-chat-drawer`. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: its root carries `data-layout-fill`, so it fills the layout's content region (`grow basis-0 min-h-0`, never `h-dvh`), only the log scrolls, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use ai-chat when the conversation is the page (an assistant page).
- A dedicated assistant page (Console → AI assistant) where the conversation is the main task.
- Open-ended questions across the whole account: how-to, troubleshooting, explaining settings or metrics.
- A conversation the reader expects to scroll back through and continue.

## When not to use

- Help about the page the reader is on, next to their work: use `ai/ai-chat-drawer`.
- The assistant proposes an action that changes the account: add `ai/ai-action-approval` to the conversation, never run it from a response.
- One generated paragraph in a page (a summary of a chart): render `StreamingResponse` in place, no chat.
- Searching documentation by keyword: a search field and results list are faster than a conversation.

## Data

The block draws a conversation in the message shape of TanStack AI: each message has an `id`, a `role` and its `parts` in order (`text`, `thinking`, `tool-call`, `tool-result`, `image`, `audio`, `video`, `document`, `activity`, `subagent`, `structured-output`, `ui-resource`), so the values `useChat` from `@tanstack/ai-vue` returns go straight into its props, with no conversion. The block calls no model and runs no AI library; `@aziontech/webkit/utils/ai-chat` names TanStack AI's own message types, imported from `@tanstack/ai` as types only (an optional peer, `^1.5.0`), with the helpers that read them (`AiChatMessage`, `AiChatPart`, `AiChatTool`, `AiChatInterrupt`, `AiChatSendContent`; import the types from there), so the shape follows TanStack when you update it, and any source that produces it works. A part of another type is skipped. `sample.ts` holds the sample threads the variants pass. The draft in the composer stays local.

An activity step reads, by convention, `content.title` (else its `activityType`), `content.status` (`pending`, `running`, `success` or `complete`, `error`, `canceled` or `cancelled`, `skipped`; left out, running) and `content.detail` as the line under it.

What TanStack AI does not carry, the app adds in `metadata`: `sources` (the documents the response cites, numbered in order), `reasoningSeconds` (left out, the block measures the thinking time) and `stopped` (the block also marks the response that Stop ended). The open conversation of the history is `v-model:activeKey` (`string | null`): picking a row sets it, New chat clears it; load that conversation's messages when it changes. The model of the composer is `v-model:modelKey` and the tools turned on in the "+" menu are `v-model:toolKeys`: pass both with each message, `sendMessage(content, { body: { model: modelKey, tools: toolKeys } })`, and read them from `forwardedProps` on the server.

Two slots let a state add to the shell without a second copy of it: `turn-end` (`{ turn }`) puts content after an assistant response, such as the `ArtifactPreview` of a file it wrote, and `canvas` puts a `Resizable.Handle` and `Resizable.Pane` beside the conversation (variant Artifact).

Event: `send`, `stop`, `voice-start`, `retry`, `new-chat`, `feedback`, `share`, `edit`, `version-change`, `branch`, `share-chat`, `rename-chat`, `archive-chat`, `remove-chat`, `approve`, `remove-queued`, `app-message`, `load-more`, `deny`, `answer-tool`, `answer-interrupt`, `retry-interrupts`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import. `apps/demos` runs this block on `useChat` with TanStack AI's `fakeText` model (`src/lib/assistant-model.ts`), no server and no key.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/ai/ai-chat.md](blocks/ai/ai-chat.md).

## Do

- Show the loading text only after a second; a response that arrives faster streams directly.
- Keep actions visible on every complete response, not on hover.
- Cite sources inline with site-name chips and open the list from the Sources pill.
- Let the reader stop a response and keep what streamed, marked as stopped.
- Keep the composer usable while a response streams so the reader can draft the next prompt.
- Return focus to the composer when a response finishes.

## Don't

- Don't auto-scroll while the reader is reading an older message.
- Don't render model output as HTML; `StreamingResponse` renders Markdown as elements only.
- Don't show actions or feedback on a response that is still loading or streaming.
- Don't use the feedback thumbs for anything but the AI response.
- Don't put more than five support prompts or three follow-ups on screen.
- Don't call the assistant by a person's name or make it apologize; state what happened.

## Copy

- **Title of the page:** `AI assistant`, with the chosen model after it on desktop.
- **Empty state:** "What can I help with?".
- **Support prompts and follow-ups:** written as the reader would ask, under 72 characters, e.g. "How do I purge the cache of one URL?".
- **Placeholder:** `Ask a question`, no end punctuation.
- **Disclaimer (hint):** "The AI assistant can make mistakes. Check important information before you act on it." The three AI blocks share this sentence; `ai/ai-action-approval` appends "It runs nothing in your account without your approval."
- **Loading:** `Generating a response` (built in); `Loading <what>` when fetching data.
- **Error:** what happened, in one sentence, e.g. "The connection was interrupted before the response finished.", with Try again.
- **Stopped:** "You stopped this response."
- **Feedback:** the Feedback menu with Good response and Bad response (built in); the toast says Thanks for your feedback.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, "select" not "click", "response" not "answer", no "please".
- **Connection:** `Reconnecting`; `Connection lost` with "Your messages send when the connection returns."
- **Elsewhere and failed answers:** `Responding in another tab`; `Your answer was not sent` with the reason and Retry; `The structured answer failed`.

## Accessibility

- The log is a named `role="log"` whose own live behavior is off; a polite live region reads each finished response once, with its author.
- Each message is an `article` named by author and time; the author and time are visually hidden, never removed.
- Responses are `aria-busy` while loading or streaming; the caret is hidden.
- The composer is named Prompt, described by its counter and disclaimer; Enter submits and an IME composition never does.
- Feedback is a menu button (`aria-haspopup="menu"`) whose chosen item is `aria-checked`, and the rating is confirmed by a visually hidden status message and the toast; the row shows no text.
- A prompt's Copy and Edit are transparent until hover or focus, never removed from the tab order; the editor's field is named Edit your message, `Escape` cancels and `Ctrl`/`Cmd` + `Enter` sends.
- Keyboard order: history panel, header, log (focusable to scroll), each message's links and actions, follow-ups, composer. On the welcome page: header, heading, support prompts, composer.
- The More and "+" menus are `DropdownMenu`s: arrows, typeahead, Escape and focus return come from it; the composer's model picker is a `Popover` whose trigger's name is its visible text.
- The phone history is a `Drawer` named Conversation history that returns focus to the menu button; the desktop toggle names what it does and carries `aria-expanded`.
- Alignment never carries meaning alone: every message's accessible name says who wrote it.
- Reconnecting is a polite status and Connection lost an alert; the queued messages are a list named Queued messages, each with Remove from queue; a question card is a group named by its question; the placeholders while restoring are a status named Loading the conversation.

## States

- Empty: `messages` left out or `[]`, with the welcome heading, the composer and four support prompts; selecting one emits `send`.
- Streaming: `loading` with the last assistant message part-way written: its caret, the busy region and Stop in the composer.
- Error: `error` set: the last response keeps its partial text, with the error line and Try again; with no response yet, a pending response shows the error.
- Tools: a `tool-call` part draws as a `ToolCall` titled from `tools`, its input and output in code; one with `approval` draws the `ToolApproval` card first (see `ai/ai-action-approval`).
- Artifact: two turns that wrote top-orders.sql in two versions, the canvas open beside them on version 2, in the same chat shell as the other states.
- LongThread: six earlier turns as `messages` that overflow the log, opened on the newest response with its Sources pill, with `followUps`.
- Media: an answer with two charts in an `ImageGallery`, a CSV report in a `FilePreview` and an audio summary.
- Agent: activity steps, a finished `SubagentCard` and a pending `AgentQuestion`; answering it resolves the interrupt and the card keeps the answer.
- Restoring: `hydrating` with no messages yet shows `Skeleton` bubbles and lines and a disabled composer.
- History: the side panel on desktop, the start drawer on a phone, with New chat and search.
- Attachments, structured answers and rich tool results: a prompt with an image and a PDF, a `structured-output` part as JSON and a tool result with text and an image (variant Media).
- Queue, older messages and connection: `queue` shows a `PromptQueue` over the composer, `moreMessages` a Load earlier messages button, and `connection` a Reconnecting status or a Connection lost alert.

## Related

- `artifact-canvas` — the side panel of the Artifact variant; `artifact-preview` — its card in the message.
- `ai/ai-chat-drawer` — the same conversation in a drawer over a resource page.
- `ai/ai-action-approval` — when a response proposes a change the reader must authorize.
- `state/state-async-submit` — long-running work outside a conversation.
- `skills/webkit-ai-surfaces` — the rules this block follows: loading stages, streaming, citations, feedback, authorization.

`Empty` (primary) · `Streaming` · `Error` · `LongThread` · `Artifact` · `Media` · `Agent`. Code: [blocks/ai/ai-chat.md](blocks/ai/ai-chat.md), `get_block("ai/ai-chat", { variant })`.

# AiChatDrawer (`ai/ai-chat-drawer`)

> The generative AI assistant in a right-side drawer over a resource page, so the reader asks about what they are looking at without leaving it: a workload page (`PageHeader` with an Agent `Button`, the name the console…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/ai/ai-chat-drawer/ai-chat-drawer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("ai/ai-chat-drawer")`
- Components: AgentActivity, AgentQuestion, Alert, AudioPlayer, Button, Card, ChatMessage, ChatMessage, CodeBlock, Conversation, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, EmptyState, FeedbackReasonDialog, FilePreview, IconButton, ImageGallery, KeyValueList, McpAppFrame, PageHeader, `PanelHeader`, `PromptInputAttachButton`, `PromptInputContextPicker`, `PromptInputDictateButton`, `PromptInputModelPicker`, PromptInput, PromptQueue, Reasoning, ResponseBranches, Skeleton, Sources, StatusIndicator, StreamingResponse, SubagentCard, SuggestionGroup, Tag, Toast, ToolApproval, ToolCall, `use-ai-chat-tools`, `use-ai-chat-versions`, `use-locale`, `utils/ai-chat`, VideoPlayer

## Asked as

ai assistant drawer; ask ai about this page; contextual ai help; copilot panel; ai side panel; chat drawer; assistant over console page; ai help drawer; assistente de ia na gaveta; perguntar à ia; painel lateral de ia; asistente de ia en panel lateral; ask about this page; assistant side panel; tanstack ai; usechat

The generative AI assistant beside the work: the reader is on a resource page — here a workload whose error rate is up — and opens the assistant in a drawer to ask about what they see, without losing the page. The drawer carries the same conversation as the full assistant page, laid out for a narrow column: every message at the inline start, a shorter composer, and support prompts written about this resource. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use ai-chat-drawer when the questions are about the page the user is on and they should keep it in view.
- A resource or list page where questions are about what is on screen: why a metric moved, what a setting does, how to fix a status.
- A global Agent entry point in the console header, when the reader should keep their place.
- A short exchange that ends back on the page (the reader acts on the answer there).

## When not to use

- Long, open-ended work with the assistant as the main task: use `ai/ai-chat`.
- Static help about the page that does not need a conversation: use `HelpPanel` in a drawer.
- An action the assistant proposes: show `ai/ai-action-approval` inside this conversation; never let the drawer change the page on its own.
- A create or edit form: use `create/create-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page behind — `PageHeader`, `Card`, `KeyValueList`, `StatusIndicator`
- B. Entry point — `Button`
- C. Drawer frame — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`
- D. Header — `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `Tag`, `IconButton`
- E. Empty state — `EmptyState`, `SuggestionGroup`
- F. Message log — `Conversation`
- G. Messages — `ChatMessage`, `Reasoning`, `StreamingResponse`, `Sources`, `ResponseBranches`, `FeedbackReasonDialog`
- H. Follow-up questions — `SuggestionGroup`
- I. Composer — `PromptInput`, `PromptInputAttachButton`, `PromptInputDictateButton`
- J. Tool calls — `ToolCall`, `ToolApproval`, `CodeBlock`
- K. Media — `ImageGallery`, `AudioPlayer`, `VideoPlayer`, `FilePreview`
- L. Agent work — `AgentActivity`, `SubagentCard`, `AgentQuestion`
- M. Queue and connection — `PromptQueue`, `StatusIndicator`, `Alert`
- N. Tool widgets — `McpAppFrame`
- O. Structured answers — `CodeBlock`, `Alert`
- P. Restoring — `Skeleton`

What each part takes: [blocks/ai/ai-chat-drawer.md](blocks/ai/ai-chat-drawer.md).

## Data

The block draws a conversation in the message shape of TanStack AI: each message has an `id`, a `role` and its `parts` in order (`text`, `thinking`, `tool-call`, `tool-result`, `image`, `audio`, `video`, `document`, `activity`, `subagent`, `structured-output`, `ui-resource`), so the values `useChat` from `@tanstack/ai-vue` returns go straight into its props, with no conversion. The block calls no model and runs no AI library; `@aziontech/webkit/utils/ai-chat` names TanStack AI's own message types, imported from `@tanstack/ai` as types only (an optional peer, `^1.5.0`), with the helpers that read them (`AiChatMessage`, `AiChatPart`, `AiChatTool`, `AiChatInterrupt`, `AiChatSendContent`; import the types from there), so the shape follows TanStack when you update it, and any source that produces it works. A part of another type is skipped. `sample.ts` holds the sample threads the variants pass. The draft in the composer stays local.

An activity step reads, by convention, `content.title` (else its `activityType`), `content.status` (`pending`, `running`, `success` or `complete`, `error`, `canceled` or `cancelled`, `skipped`; left out, running) and `content.detail` as the line under it.

What TanStack AI does not carry, the app adds in `metadata`: `sources` (the documents the response cites, numbered in order), `reasoningSeconds` (left out, the block measures the thinking time) and `stopped` (the block also marks the response that Stop ended). A message's time is its `createdAt`, formatted in the reader's locale.

Prop: `messages`, `suggestions`, `followUps`, `loading`, `error`, `tools`, `interrupts`, `interruptErrors`, `queue`, `moreMessages`, `loadingMore`, `connection`, `resuming`, `hydrating`, `sessionGenerating`, `attachable`, `accept`, `maxFiles`, `maxFileSize`, `resolveAppUrl`, `toolOptions`, `v-model:open`.

Event: `send`, `stop`, `retry`, `edit`, `version-change`, `share`, `branch`, `new-chat`, `feedback`, `approve`, `remove-queued`, `app-message`, `load-more`, `deny`, `answer-tool`, `answer-interrupt`, `retry-interrupts`.

A tool that needs approval is declared once with `toolDefinition({ name, inputSchema, needsApproval: true })`, run on the server with `.server(...)` and passed to `useChat({ tools: [definition] })` too, so the client can match the approval request to the call. Then delete `sample.ts` and its import. `apps/demos` runs this block on `useChat` with TanStack AI's `fakeText` model (`src/lib/assistant-model.ts`), no server and no key.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/ai/ai-chat-drawer.md](blocks/ai/ai-chat-drawer.md).

## Do

- Write support prompts and the placeholder about the resource on screen.
- Keep the page visible and unchanged while the drawer is open.
- Keep the conversation when the drawer closes and reopens during the visit.
- Use `layout="start"` for every message in the drawer.

## Don't

- Don't change the page from a response; propose the change and ask for approval.
- Don't stack a second drawer from the assistant; link to the page that does the job.
- Don't open the drawer on its own; the reader opens it.
- Don't repeat the page title in every response; the context is implied.

## Copy

- **Entry point:** `Agent`, the name the console header's `HighlightButton` gives the same assistant; the panel title says what it is, `AI assistant`.
- **Drawer title:** `AI assistant`, with the Preview tag while in preview.
- **Empty state:** "Ask about <resource>" and one sentence saying the assistant reads this resource's settings and metrics.
- **Placeholder:** "Ask about <resource>".
- **Disclaimer:** "The AI assistant can make mistakes. Check important information before you act on it.", word for word the one `ai/ai-chat` uses; `ai/ai-action-approval` adds "It runs nothing in your account without your approval."
- Errors, loading and feedback strings follow `ai/ai-chat` and `skills/webkit-microcopy`.
- **Connection:** `Reconnecting`; `Connection lost` with "Your messages send when the connection returns."
- **Elsewhere and failed answers:** `Responding in another tab`; `Your answer was not sent` with the reason and Retry; `The structured answer failed`.

## Accessibility

- On open, focus goes to the prompt, never to New chat, so a stray Enter sends nothing and wipes nothing. The drawer returns focus to Agent when it closes; `DrawerTitle` names the dialog.
- Agent exposes `aria-expanded`.
- The log is a named `role="log"` with live behavior off; finished responses are announced once through the conversation's polite region.
- New chat is an icon button with an accessible name; it is disabled while the thread is empty.
- Keyboard order inside the drawer: header controls, log, message actions, follow-ups, composer.
- Reconnecting is a polite status and Connection lost an alert; the queued messages are a list named Queued messages, each with Remove from queue; a question card is a group named by its question; the placeholders while restoring are a status named Loading the conversation.

## States

- Empty: the drawer open with `messages` left out, on the empty state with three support prompts about storefront.
- Streaming: `loading` with a response part-way written about the errors of the workload behind the drawer.
- Error: `error` set: a failed response with its partial text and Try again.
- Tools: a `tool-call` part draws as a `ToolCall` titled from `tools`; one with `approval` draws the `ToolApproval` card first (see `ai/ai-action-approval`).
- LongThread: six earlier turns as `messages` that overflow the drawer's log.
- Media and agent parts, attachments, structured answers, rich tool results, the queue, older messages, restoring and the connection draw as in `ai/ai-chat` (its Media and Agent variants).

## Related

- `ai/ai-chat` — the full-page assistant.
- `ai/ai-action-approval` — authorization of an action the assistant proposes.
- `create/create-drawer` — the drawer for forms, not conversations.

# AuthSignIn (`auth/auth-sign-in`)

> The signed-out screens of a platform app, frame included: a full-height page with the signed-out `AppHeader` (the product mark and a Documentation button) over a centred column that holds one `Card` and the prompt and…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/auth/auth-sign-in/auth-sign-in.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("auth/auth-sign-in")`
- Components: Alert, AppHeader, Avatar, Brand, Button, Card, Checkbox, CopyButton, Field, `FieldError`, IconButton, Input, Item, KeyValueList, Link, OtpInput, PageHeader, PasswordInput, PasswordRequirements, PasswordRequirements, QrCode, Separator, Skeleton, Tag, Tooltip, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

login; log in; sign in; signin; login page; authentication; auth; forgot password; reset password; new password; entrar; tela de login; acessar conta; esqueci a senha; redefinir senha; signup; sign up; register; registration; create account; new account; free account; cadastro; cadastrar; criar conta; tela de cadastro; registrar; check inbox; check your email; verify email; email verification; confirm email; verification sent; resend email; verificar e-mail; confirmar e-mail; confira seu e-mail; session expired; auth errors; sessão expirada; erro de login; mfa; authenticator app; one-time code; verification code; totp; recovery code; autenticação em dois fatores; código de verificação; código de autenticação; loading sign-in providers; providers loading; carregando provedores de login; oauth consent; authorize app; authorize application; app authorization; consent screen; allow access; grant access; scopes; permissions requested; third-party app access; device authorization; device code; cli login; connect cli; device flow; autorizar aplicativo; tela de consentimento; conceder acesso; autorizar dispositivo; login pela cli; token sign in; api token sign in; personal token; personal token sign in; sign in with token; sign in with api key; api key login; paste token; access token login; token login; entrar com token; login com token; token pessoal

The signed-out screens of a platform app: sign in, sign up, reset password and check your inbox, frame included. The user has one job here, to get into their account, and one object on the page to do it with: a single card under the signed-out bar. Every step of the flow (`email`, `password`, `reset`, `sent`, `new-password`) swaps the contents of that card in place, and every answer the server gives lands inside it: a credential the user retypes (the password, an MFA code, a token) takes its error on its own field, and every other answer, success included, lands in one `Alert` in the card. Auth never toasts. It is a full page with its own focused header: the app routes it outside `ConsoleLayout`, never into the layout's default slot.

## When to use

- `/login`, `/signup` and `/signup/verify`, and the reset-password link the user follows from their inbox.
- Re-entering after a session expired: the same card opens on the password step with the address already filled.
- Any signed-out step that asks for credentials (sign in, MFA, set a new password).
- The OAuth authorize screen (`OauthConsent`): a third-party app asks to act on the signed-in account, and the person allows or denies the scopes it lists.
- Device and CLI sign-in (`DeviceAuthorization`): a terminal or a device without a browser printed a code, and the person confirms it here.
- An app with no accounts of its own that calls the Azion API with the person's personal token (PersonalToken): an internal console, a dashboard, a storage browser.

## When not to use

- First-run steps after the account exists (profile, plan, organization): use `account/account-onboarding-form`.
- Changing the password or email of a signed-in user: use `settings/settings-form` (Profile).
- Signing out an expired session over a console page: the shell wire is `state/state-page-skeleton` (Session); this block is where it lands.
- Any signed-in form: use `state/state-form-validation` for the submit states and `settings/settings-form` for settings.
- Listing or revoking the apps a person already authorized: that is a settings table, not this card.

## Building blocks

- A. Signed-out bar — `AppHeader` (required)
- B. Product mark — `Brand` (required)
- C. Actions — `Button` (required)
- D. The card — `Card`, `Link` (required)
- E. Card notice — `Alert` (conditional)
- F. Social divider — `Separator` (email step only)
- G. Field label — `Field`, `Field.Label` (required)
- H. Email — `Input` (required)
- I. Field message — `FieldError` (conditional)
- J. Step hint — `Tooltip` (password and reset steps)
- K. Back control — `IconButton` (password and reset steps)
- L. Password field — `Field` (password and new-password steps)
- M. Password — `PasswordInput` (password and new-password steps)
- N. Password rules — `PasswordRequirements` (new-password step, sign up)
- O. Last used — `Tag` (email step only)
- P. Card heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- Q. Provider placeholder — `Skeleton` (while `providersLoading`)
- R. Personal token — `PasswordInput` (PersonalToken, RejectedToken and NoAccessToken)

What each part takes: [blocks/auth/auth-sign-in.md](blocks/auth/auth-sign-in.md).

## Data

The block takes its starting values and the request state through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing and fakes no answer. `SignInProps`, `SignInValues`, `SignInStep`, `SignInMethod`, `SignInFailure` and `SignInNoticeKind` are exported from `auth-sign-in.vue`. The card keeps its own draft (the email, the password, the reset fields) and sends it with `submit`; the outcome comes back as `loading`, then `error` or `notice`. It has no sample records: the variants pass the props of each state. PersonalToken, RejectedToken and NoAccessToken render their own card, `token-sign-in.vue` (listed in `files`), not the primary: it takes no account fields, and its contract is below the primary's.

Prop: `step` (`v-model:step`), `defaultValues`, `loading`, `error`, `notice`, `providersLoading`, `lastUsed`, `homeHref`, `docsHref`, `signUpHref`, `termsHref`, `privacyHref`.

Event: `provider-click`, `continue`, `submit`, `reset-request`, `resend`, `password-reset`.

The token card, `token-sign-in.vue` (`TokenSignInProps` and `TokenSignInFailure` are exported from it):

Prop: `loading`, `error`, `remember` (`v-model:remember`), `homeHref`, `docsHref`.

Event: `sign-in`, `update:remember`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/auth/auth-sign-in.md](blocks/auth/auth-sign-in.md).

## Do

- Keep one card and one notice slot for the whole flow; swap the step body, not the page.
- Validate on submit only, then clear a field's error as the user types in it.
- After a 401, clear the password, put the message on the password field and move focus back to it.
- Keep the credentials after a 503, a 500 or a timeout; Retry re-sends the same request.
- Carry the email between steps (sign in to reset, reset back to sign in) so the user never types it twice.
- While a request is in flight, show the primary `Button` `loading`, disable the step's `fieldset` and mark the form `aria-busy`; release the lock on every outcome so Retry can run again.
- Enter the card column once, on mount: it slides in from the inline start with a fade (`starting:-translate-x-6 starting:opacity-0`, `rtl:starting:translate-x-6`, `transition-[translate,opacity] duration-slow-01 ease-expressive-entrance`). Steps inside the card do not replay it.
- Let the card height follow the step: a `ResizeObserver` on the form sets the wrapper height, which eases with `transition-[height] duration-moderate-02 ease-productive-entrance` and clips only while it moves.
- While the identity providers load, hold their place with two `Skeleton` bars of the buttons' height in a `role="status"` region named `Preparing sign-in providers`; keep email sign-in usable.

- On a code screen, put the code in one `OtpInput` (autofill reads `autocomplete="one-time-code"`), submit on `complete`, and keep a Verify button.
- Give every QR code a typed alternative: the setup key with a copy button.

- On the consent screen, name the app, its publisher and site in the heading block, the account it will act on (with Switch account), and every scope as a row with a glyph, a title that starts with a verb and one sentence of what it covers.
- Say where Allow sends the person (the redirect URL as code text) and where to revoke access later.
- Put Deny and Allow side by side at the foot of the card, Allow on the inline end; lock both while either answer is in flight, and keep both locked once the notice reports the outcome.
- On device authorization, show the code the terminal printed in large mono type, grouped `XXXX-XXXX`, with the request details (application, device, IP address, time) so the person can spot a request they did not start.

## Don't

- Don't toast. Not for errors, not for success, not for the session-expired notice.
- Don't show the session-expired notice to someone who never signed in. A route guard that finds no session can't tell a first visit from an ended session by itself: send `reason=expired` only when the 401 came on a request that carried a credential, or when the server says the session it received has ended (an HttpOnly cookie is invisible to the page, so the server has to say it).
- Don't say which half of the pair was wrong after a 401; it confirms the address exists.
- Don't put a Retry button on a 401, and don't raise a card notice for it: the password field is the retry.
- Don't put client-side validation in the `Alert`; it belongs on the field.
- Don't call a timeout a failure (`danger`) or say the account was not created; the request may have landed.
- Don't stack notices: a new outcome replaces the one in the slot.
- Don't keep a personal token in `localStorage`, a URL or a log, and don't echo it back on the page after sign-in.
- Don't hide or disable the email field while the providers load, and don't show a spinner in place of the provider buttons.

- Don't split a one-time code into separate inputs or move focus between them by hand; `OtpInput` is one field.
- Don't toast a rejected code; it is the field's reason, and the field is cleared and focused.

- Don't preselect or let the person untick single scopes on the consent screen; the app asked for a set, and Allow grants that set or Deny grants nothing.
- Don't hide which account will be authorized; Switch account sits beside it before Allow.
- Don't make the device code an input on the confirm step; it is text to compare. Typing it is the fallback, behind the link.

## Copy

- **Card heading:** names the step, sentence case, no punctuation: `Welcome back`, `Reset your password`, `Check your inbox`, `Sign up for a free account`. The lead under it is one full sentence: `Sign in to your account.`
- **Primary action:** a verb for what happens: `Continue with email`, `Sign in`, `Send reset link`, `Reset password`, `Return to sign in`.
- **Field labels:** one to two words, no colon, no parentheses: `Email`, `Work email`, `Password`, `New password`, `Confirm password`.
- **Links:** sentence case: `Forgot your password?`, `Resend email`.
- **Field errors:** what is wrong or what to enter, with a period: `Enter your email address.`, `Enter your password.`, `Enter a valid email address.`, `Passwords don't match.`
- **401 notice:** `Incorrect email or password. Check both and try again.`
- **503 notice:** says what is down and what is not lost, never a claim the server did not check (it never read the credentials): `Sign-in is unavailable right now. What you entered is kept; retry in a few minutes.`
- **500 notice:** says what failed and what state the user is in, code last: `Sign-in failed on our side. You are still signed out. Error 500.`
- **Timeout notice:** names the unknown, never a failure: `The server did not answer in time. Your session may already be open.`
- **409 on sign-up:** never said on screen, because it tells anyone which addresses have an account. The card answers exactly as for a new address, and the email sent to the owner explains how to sign in: `Check your inbox at jane.doe@example.com to finish. If this address already has an account, the email explains how to sign in instead.`
- **Session expired:** `Your session expired. Sign in again to pick up where you left off.`
- **Providers loading:** the status name says what is happening, no ellipsis: `Preparing sign-in providers`.
- **Action in a notice:** `Retry`, never "Try again" (the console and assistant blocks use the same word).
- **Consent heading:** `Authorize Acme Deploy`; the lead names publisher and site: `Acme Deploy by Acme Inc. (deploy.example.com) wants to access your account.`
- **Scope rows:** title starts with a verb (`Read your workloads`, `Deploy your applications`), the description says what is in and, when it matters, what is not: `Names, domains and status. Not their settings or secrets.`
- **Consent actions:** `Deny` and `Allow`. Outcomes: `Access granted. Returning to Acme Deploy.` / `Access denied. Returning to Acme Deploy with no access to your account.`
- **Device actions:** `Cancel` and `Confirm`. Outcomes: `Device connected. Go back to your terminal; you can close this tab.` / `Request cancelled. The device was not connected.`
- **Personal token:** heading `Sign in with a personal token`; lead `Paste a personal token from your Azion account. It is sent only to the Azion API.`; rejected `Azion did not accept this token. Check that you copied all of it and that it has not expired or been revoked.`; no access `This token is valid but cannot read what this app needs. Create a token with access to the account and paste it here.`; rate limited `Azion is limiting requests from this token. Wait a moment and retry.`; unreachable `We could not reach Azion to check the token. Your entry is kept.`; option `Remember for this tab` / `Closing the tab signs you out.`
- **Device code errors:** `Enter the code your terminal shows.`, `Enter all 8 characters of the code.`, `That code is not valid or has expired. Check your terminal, or start the sign-in again there.`
- **Languages:** the sign-in card (`auth-sign-in.vue`) carries its copy in a `COPY` table keyed by locale (`en`, `pt-BR`, `es`) and reads the active locale with `useLocale`, so a `ConfigProvider` around the page translates the block's copy together with WebKit's own strings (the password show and hide labels, the requirements). An unknown locale falls back to its language, then to English. Add a language by adding one entry to `COPY`; keep the English row as the source and keep the terms sentence split into its link parts.

## Accessibility

- The form has an accessible name (`aria-label="Sign in to your account"`) and `novalidate`, so the browser does not show its own bubbles over the field messages.
- Each input has a visible `Field.Label` tied to it by its `Field`; each error is linked with `aria-describedby` (or through `Field.Error` inside `Field`).
- Use the right `autocomplete` on every field (`username`, `current-password`, `new-password`, `email`) so password managers and autofill work.
- Icon-only back buttons have an `aria-label` equal to their tooltip.
- After a submit with errors, focus the first field that needs attention; after a 401, the password.
- The notice uses the `Alert` role from the component; don't add a second live region for the same message.
- Every transition sets `motion-reduce:transition-none` and `motion-reduce:transform-none`.
- Under reduced motion the column appears in place (no slide, no fade) and the card height jumps.
- The provider placeholder is announced once by its status name; the `Skeleton` bars are decorative.
- Social buttons are `type="button"` so Enter in the email field submits the email, not a provider.

- MFA: the code field is named by its label (`Authentication code`, `Recovery code`), keeps its help text, and shows the reason in its `Field.Error` when rejected; the QR code is an image named after the account, and the setup key is real text.
- Consent and device authorization: the card body is a `section` named by its `h1` (`aria-labelledby`); the scope list is an `Item.List` named by its heading (`Acme Deploy will be able to`), each scope a `listitem` with a decorative glyph; the request details are a `KeyValueList` named `Request details`.

## States

- Login: the default props, the sign-in flow on the email step, with Google and GitHub over the `or` divider; the same file walks through password, reset, sent and new-password.
- SignUp: create an account with a work email (and a password checked by `PasswordRequirements`), Google or GitHub.
- SessionExpired: `step="password"`, the email in `defaultValues` and `notice="session-expired"`; opens on the password step for the same email, with an info notice that clears on the next action.
- Submitting: `loading` on the password step; Sign in in flight: the primary `Button` loading, the fieldset disabled, the form `aria-busy`.
- ProvidersLoading: `providersLoading`; the Login card while the identity providers load; two `Skeleton` bars in a `role="status"` region (`Preparing sign-in providers`) replace Google and GitHub over the `or` divider, and the email step works meanwhile.
- CheckInbox: the `/signup/verify` card: where the link went, the resend prompt and a secondary Return to sign in.
- IncorrectCredentials: `error="bad-credentials"`; 401 on Sign in, on the password step of the same two-step card; a danger notice under the heading, no action, the password cleared.
- ServiceUnavailable: `error="service-unavailable"`; 503 on Sign in; a warning notice with Retry, credentials kept.
- ServerError: `error="server-error"`; 500 on the request; a danger notice with Retry in the card instead of a toast.
- Timeout: `error="timeout"`; no response; the same notice as the 500 in warning, with Retry, because the request may have gone through.
- EmailAlreadyRegistered: 409 on Sign up; the same Check your inbox notice as a new address, so the screen reveals nothing.
- MfaSetup: turning on multi-factor authentication: three numbered steps, a `QrCode` of the `otpauth://` URI the API returns (issuer, account and secret) with the setup key and its `CopyButton` for people who cannot scan, then an `OtpInput` in a `Field`. The code submits on `complete` or Verify code; a wrong code (`000000` in the demo) clears it, marks the field invalid with the reason and keeps focus; no answer (`999999`) is a warning notice with Retry; success is a success notice, then the recovery codes the API issues once: eight 8-character codes in a monospace list with Download and Copy, and an `I saved these codes` checkbox that Continue to Console waits for, so the recovery path MfaCode offers always has codes behind it.
- MfaCode: the sign-in challenge after the password: a 6-digit `OtpInput`, focused when the challenge opens (not with `autofocus`), that submits on `complete`, Use a recovery code (an 8-character alphanumeric `OtpInput` grouped by 4) and Sign in with another account. Same outcomes as MfaSetup: field reason for a rejected code, warning notice with Retry when the check does not answer.
- OauthConsent: the authorize screen. The app (square `Avatar` with its initials, name, publisher, site), the signed-in account in an outlined `Item` with Switch account, the scopes in an `Item.List`, the redirect URL and where to revoke, then Deny / Allow. The pressed answer shows its loading state and locks the other; the outcome lands in the notice slot (`success` for Allow, `info` for Deny) and both stay locked.
- DeviceAuthorization: device or CLI sign-in. The code the terminal printed (`WDJB-MJHT`) in large mono text, the request details in a split `KeyValueList`, the account and the two scopes, Cancel / Confirm. `Code does not match? Enter the code` swaps to an 8-character alphanumeric `OtpInput` grouped by 4: a rejected code (`00000000` in the demo) is the field's reason, cleared and focused; no answer (`99999999`) is a warning notice with Retry; an accepted code returns to the confirm step showing it. Confirm reports `success`, Cancel `info`.

- PersonalToken: sign in with an Azion personal token. One masked, monospace field with show and hide, a link to how tokens are made, required and no-spaces checks, Remember for this tab (off), then `sign-in` `(event, token)`; the app answers with `loading` and `error`.
- RejectedToken: `error="rejected"`, the card after a 401, the danger notice under the heading and the empty field focused.
- NoAccessToken: `error="no-access"`, the card after a 403, a danger notice that asks for a token with access, the empty field focused.

## Related

- `top-bar/top-bar-auth` — the signed-out bar this block renders at the top.
- `account/account-onboarding-form` — where a new account goes after it verifies its email.
- `state/state-page-skeleton` — the session wire painted while an expired session signs out, before this screen.
- `state/state-form-validation` — the same field mechanics (required versus invalid, validate on submit) in a signed-in form, where unscoped failures do toast.
- `PasswordRequirements` — the live password checklist used on sign up and reset.

## Steps

- email
- password
- reset
- sent
- new-password

## Variants

Code: [blocks/auth/auth-sign-in.md](blocks/auth/auth-sign-in.md), `get_block("auth/auth-sign-in", { variant })`.

# CreateDeployDrawer (`create/create-deploy-drawer`)

> The drawer a platform deploys from, opened by the outlined Deploy button on a service or a project.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-deploy-drawer/create-deploy-drawer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-deploy-drawer")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Avatar, Button, Card, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Input, Item, Kbd, Link, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Popover, RadioGroup, Separator, SettingsGroup, Skeleton, Spinner, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, `use-locale`, `use-shortcuts`
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

deploy drawer; deploy panel; deploy service; choose versions to deploy; dependencies before deploy; release drawer; gaveta de deploy; implantar serviço; escolher versão

The drawer a platform deploys from, opened by Deploy on a service or a project. The user is about to put a version into traffic and needs to confirm exactly what goes out (each resource and dependency at a version), where it goes (a project and one of its environments) and what else it reaches (every project that shares the environment's Deployment Settings). One Deploy at the foot commits all of it.

## When to use

- A service or a project has a ready version and the user deploys it from its page or list.
- The deploy reaches more than the resource itself: dependencies at their own versions, or other projects through shared Deployment Settings.
- A service deploys to a project that may not exist yet; the Project section creates it in place.

## When not to use

- A release of several resources reviewed together: use `create/create-release-impact`. This drawer is the canonical surface for deploying one service or one project.

- Creating or editing an item inside a resource: use `create/create-drawer`.
- The first deploy at the end of a create flow: use `create/create-deploy-template` or `create/create-wizard` (CreateAndDeploy), which stream the create-flow card of `detail/detail-deployment-logs` in the page.
- Reading what a past deploy did: use `detail/detail-deployment-logs` or `detail/detail-version`.
- Binding one resource to another without deploying: use `create/create-resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

- A. Trigger and frame — `Drawer`, `DrawerTrigger`, `Button`, `DrawerContent` (required)
- B. Panel header — `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle` (required)
- C. Sections — `PanelBody`, `SettingsGroup`, `Skeleton`, `Alert`, `Spinner` (required)
- D. Resources card — `Card`, `Separator`, `Item`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu`, `Input`, `Avatar`, `Button` (required)
- E. Dependencies — `Accordion`, `Item`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu` (required)
- F. Project — `ToggleGroup`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Link`, `Tooltip`, `Popover`, `DropdownMenu` (required on a service)
- G. Environment — `RadioGroup`, `Tag` (required)
- H. Projects impacted and commit — `Item`, `Tag`, `Link`, `Tooltip`, `Popover`, `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required on a service)
- I. Shortcut keycap — `Kbd` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-deploy-drawer.md](blocks/create/create-deploy-drawer.md).

## Data

The block takes the deploy targets through props and emits every action; it fetches and deploys nothing. The record types (`DeployDrawerResource`, `DeployDrawerProjectGroup`, `DeployDrawerEnvironment`, `DeployDrawerImpact`, `DeployDrawerBuild`, `DeployDrawerValues`) and `DeployDrawerProps` are exported from `create-deploy-drawer.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample records the Service drawer renders when they are left out (never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `resources`, `projectGroups`, `newProject`, `environments`, `impacted`, `defaultValues`, `build`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:open`, `dependenciesOpen`, `dependenciesLoadingKeys`, `impactedLoading`, `blocker`, `v-model:versions`, `v-model:environment`.

Event: `submit`, `retry`.

The `environment-alerts` slot renders under the environment choices with `{ environment, project }`, for alerts about what the chosen environment changes. A dependency with `sharedWith` carries a Shared `Tag` in a `Tooltip` naming the other services, and one info `Alert` above the list says it deploys at one version; Projects impacted shows only when there are projects, with an environment heading and a count per group once they span more than one environment.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/create-deploy-drawer.md](blocks/create/create-deploy-drawer.md).

## Do

- Show every resource and dependency with the version that will go out, even when the user changes nothing.
- Preselect the last used project and environment, and say so with a tag.
- List every project a shared Deployment Setting reaches before the user deploys, not after.
- When no version is pinned, open as Build and deployment with a Building row, keep the other sections faded and `inert`, and disable Deploy until the build lands.
- On a project, warn with an `Alert` above the environments when its Deployment Settings also deploy elsewhere.
- Keep an environment that Strict Deployment Settings lock visible but disabled, with a Strict tag and one sentence naming the settings and the service they keep bound.
- Tag an environment Also deploys (warning) when the chosen environment's shared settings reach it, and say once, in a warning `Alert`, how many environments go live at once.
- Say in an info `Alert` when the deploy replaces another service on the chosen project, naming both.
- When a choice changes what the deploy reaches, reload that section in place: `Skeleton` rows, `aria-busy` on the region and one `role="status"` line; never clear the whole drawer.
- Tag a dependency other services reference as Shared, name them in a `Tooltip`, and say once that a shared dependency deploys at one version.
- Resolve the drawer in place: while the resources and environments load, keep the section titles and render `Skeleton` blocks shaped like the Resources card and the environment cards, with `aria-busy` and one status line, and Deploy disabled.
- When the targets fail to load, replace the sections with one danger `Alert` saying what failed and an outlined Retry; Deploy stays disabled.
- When the project has no environment, show the Environment section as a bordered small `EmptyState` with Add environment, and say in the footer why Deploy is disabled. A Resources card with nothing bound says so in one line instead of disappearing.
- When a dependency has no ready version, disable Deploy and say why in the footer, next to the button it disables.
- After Deploy, follow `state/state-async-submit`: the drawer closes and one toast per run turns from Deploying… into the outcome, with Edit (reopens the drawer with the same choices) and Redeploy.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/shell-console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't deploy one service from a dialog, or ask for confirmation after Deploy; the drawer is the review. This is the one confirmation rule across the deploy surfaces: the surface that shows what goes live is the review, and nothing confirms it again. A release of several resources is reviewed on a page (`create/create-release-impact`, whose single `ConfirmDialog` states the reach); a dropped folder is reviewed in the Drop confirm of `create/create-deploy-progress-dialog`.
- Don't hide dependencies or impacted projects behind a second step.
- Don't let Change version list hundreds of versions at once; search plus Load more.
- Don't add a second commit such as Save as draft; one Deploy.
- Don't print the shared-settings warning on each impacted row; it belongs once, above them.
- Don't hide a locked environment, or let it be picked and fail at deploy time.
- Don't offer View deployments in the outcome toast; it carries Edit and Redeploy.

## Copy

- **Trigger, title, commit:** "Deploy" on all three; "Build and deployment" as the title only while a build runs first.
- **Section hints:** one sentence on what the section decides, e.g. "The project whose domains serve the service."
- **Version control:** "Change version", named "Change version of <resource>" for assistive technology; search placeholder and `aria-label` "Search versions"; footer "Load 10 more".
- **Project modes:** "Use existing" and "Create new".
- **Environment descriptions:** one sentence on how it serves, e.g. "Live traffic. One version serves the domain, and deploying replaces it."
- **Footer summary:** "1 change goes live in Production." or "3 changes go live in Production."
- **Load failure:** "The deploy targets for project-01 couldn't be loaded. Check your connection and try again." with "Retry".
- **No environment:** "No environment on this project", one sentence on why there is no target, and "Add environment"; footer "Add an environment to deploy."
- **Tags:** one or two words, e.g. "Ready", "Active", "Last used", "Selected", "New".
- **In progress:** the progressive verb with `…`, e.g. "Building…".
- **Run toast:** "Deploying web-app…" with "<version> to <environments>. It keeps running if you leave."; the outcome "web-app is live in Production." or "web-app wasn't deployed." with what failed and that nothing changed; actions "Edit" and "Redeploy".
- **Locks and reach:** "<settings> is Strict, so <service> stays bound to <environment>."; "Also deploys"; "<settings> is shared, so it deploys at one version."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: Deploy, never publish or activate; sentence case; no em dash.

## Accessibility

- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to the Deploy trigger on close.
- Opening the drawer moves focus to its first control.
- **⌘ Enter deploys (`Ctrl Enter` off Apple)** through the form's submit, the same path as Deploy. It stays inert while Deploy is disabled (loading, load error, a build running, no environment); Deploy carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and an `aria-hidden` `Kbd`, and the `?` dialog lists it under Drawer.
- The `form` and the `ToggleGroup` carry `aria-label`s; the environment group is named by its `aria-label`.
- The version menu is a `role="menu"` moved with the arrow keys, each version a `menuitem` named by its version, author and age; the current one carries `aria-current`; search inputs have an `aria-label` that matches the placeholder.
- Each impacted environment group has an `aria-label` with its count, e.g. "Projects impacted in Production (3)".
- Faded sections during a build are `inert`, so keyboard users cannot reach controls that do nothing yet.
- A section that reloads carries `aria-busy="true"` with its `Skeleton` rows `aria-hidden`, and a `role="status"` line reads Loading the projects this deployment reaches, or Loading dependencies.
- A locked environment's radio is `disabled`; its reason is the card's description, so it is read with the choice.
- The Shared tag sits in a focusable wrapper so its `Tooltip` opens from the keyboard, and its name already says who else references it.
- A disabled Deploy is described by the footer line that explains why (`aria-describedby`).
- Run progress and outcome reach screen readers through the toast region, so the user hears them from any page.
- Glyphs in rows are decorative and carry `aria-hidden="true"`; tags give the state in words.

## States

- Service: a service deploying environment first (the records passed in, or the sample); Resources, Project with the last used project, Environment and Projects impacted, and the footer counting the one version change that goes live in Production.
- Building: no pinned version (`build` is set); titled Build and deployment with a Building row in place of Resources, the other sections faded and inert, Deploy disabled.
- ServiceProjectFirst: the project-first flow, its own SFC on the sample resources; Resources, the Project card with the last used project and a Change popover, then every environment.
- Project: deploying a project; its service and storage in Resources, Production and Preview, and a warning about other projects that share its storefront settings.
- Environment: a locked Strict environment, an Also deploys tag, the replace and multi-environment `Alert`s, Projects impacted grouped per environment and reloaded on switch; the run ends in a success toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- Loading: the resources and environments resolving (`loading` on the Service drawer; this variant shows the project drawer); `Skeleton` blocks under the Resources and Environment titles, an `aria-busy` region with a status line, Deploy disabled.
- LoadError: the deploy targets failed to load (`error` on the Service drawer, with `retry`; this variant shows the project drawer); a danger `Alert` with Retry, which reloads them as Skeletons, and Deploy disabled.
- NoEnvironment: nothing bound and no environment; a one-line empty Resources card, an `EmptyState` with Add environment, and Deploy disabled with the reason in the footer.
- Dependencies: the open Dependencies disclosure with a Shared dependency, a not-versioned integration and a dependency with no ready version that blocks Deploy; changing the service version reloads the list. The first run fails and its toast offers Edit and Redeploy; Redeploy succeeds.

## Related

- `create/create-drawer` — the drawer that creates items rather than deploying.
- `detail/detail-deployment-logs` — the run a deploy streams once it starts.
- `state/state-async-submit` — the toast and outcome rule every deploy started here follows.
- `detail/detail-deployment-logs` — the logs of a deploy after it ran.
- `detail/detail-version` — what a version contains before it is deployed.
- `create/create-resource-picker` — the Existing or New pattern the Project section follows.
- `SettingsGroup` — the band each section uses; see `skills/webkit-create-surface` for the drawer commit model.

## Variants

`Service` (primary) · `Building` · `ServiceProjectFirst` · `Project` · `Environment` · `Dependencies` · `Loading` · `LoadError` · `NoEnvironment`. Code: [blocks/create/create-deploy-drawer.md](blocks/create/create-deploy-drawer.md), `get_block("create/create-deploy-drawer", { variant })`.
