# CreateDeployProgressDialog (`create/create-deploy-progress-dialog`)

> The modal progress of one deploy that sends several Deployment Settings live, each on its own, and the drop-to-deploy confirm that starts it.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-deploy-progress-dialog/create-deploy-progress-dialog.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-deploy-progress-dialog")`
- Components: Button, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, EmptyState, Item, OutcomeIcon, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Progress, Spinner, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

deploy progress; deploy progress dialog; drop to deploy; deploy a folder; multi deploy progress; progresso do deploy; arrastar e implantar; progreso del despliegue

The modal progress of one deploy that sends several Deployment Settings live, each on its own, and the drop-to-deploy confirm that starts it. The user dropped a folder (or started a deploy whose environment deploys through several Deployment Settings) and wants to see each one go live, know which failed and why, and retry only those. The page behind the dialog is a page body for `ConsoleLayout` (the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`); the dialog teleports over it.

**The toast stays the standard.** Every deploy reports through one toast with Edit and Redeploy (`state/state-async-submit`). This dialog is only for the drop-to-deploy path and for a deploy that fans out to several Deployment Settings; even there the outcome still reaches the user through the toast, so they can close the dialog and leave.

## When to use

- A folder dropped on a service deploys straight to an environment.
- One deploy sends several Deployment Settings live that can succeed or fail independently.

## When not to use

- A deploy of one service or project: use `create/create-deploy-drawer`, which closes and reports through the toast.
- A deploy with build steps and logs: use `detail/detail-deployment-logs`.
- Reviewing what a multi-resource release reaches before it runs: use `create/create-release-impact`.

## Building blocks

- A. Drop confirm — `Dialog`, `PanelHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `Tag`, `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required on the drop path)
- B. Progress frame — `Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `OutcomeIcon` (required)
- C. Progress — `PanelBody`, `Progress` (required)
- D. Filter — `ToggleGroup` (required)
- E. Rows — `Item`, `OutcomeIcon`, `Spinner`, `Tag`, `EmptyState` (required)
- F. Footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)
- Outcome toast — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-deploy-progress-dialog.md](blocks/create/create-deploy-progress-dialog.md).

## Data

The block takes the run through props and emits every action; it runs no deploy and fakes no progress. `DeployProgressDialogItem` and `DeployProgressDialogProps` are exported from `create-deploy-progress-dialog.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample runs (`sampleRunningItems` renders when `items` is left out; `sampleDeployedItems` and `samplePartialItems` are what the variants pass). The page updates each row's `status` as the deploy reports it; the title, the bar, the filter counts and the toast follow from the rows.

Prop: `items`, `resourceName`, `v-model:open`.

Event: `retry`, `redeploy`.

Slot: `actions`.

A run whose rows are all queued has not started: the block raises no toast for it. Drop renders the block with its two Deployment Settings queued, opens its own confirm beside it, and on Deploy to Production opens the progress dialog and moves the rows through the run.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/create-deploy-progress-dialog.md](blocks/create/create-deploy-progress-dialog.md).

## Do

- Let each Deployment Setting settle on its own and keep the ones that succeeded live.
- Say why a row failed on the row itself.
- Offer Retry failed for the failed rows only.
- Report the run through the toast while the dialog is hidden, so the user can hide it and leave; never raise the toast over the open dialog.

## Don't

- Don't use this dialog for a single deploy; the toast is enough.
- Don't trap the user in the dialog while the run goes on; let them hide it (the toast keeps reporting) and reopen it with Show progress.
- Don't roll back the settings that succeeded because another failed.

## Copy

- **Drop:** "New production deployment", "Dropped files", "Deploy to Production".
- **Title:** "Deploying… 2 of 5 done", "Deployed 5 Deployment Settings", "Deployed 4 of 5 Deployment Settings".
- **Tally:** "4 succeeded, 1 failed. Each Deployment Setting deploys on its own, and the ones that succeeded stay live."
- **Tags:** Queued, Deploying, Done, Failed. **Actions:** Retry failed, Hide (while running), Close.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, the progressive verb with `…`.

## Accessibility

- The dialog traps focus and is named by its title and described by the tally.
- The `Progress` bar is named; a `role="status"` line announces the outcome once settled.
- `OutcomeIcon` names its outcome; tags give the state in words, glyphs are `aria-hidden`.
- The dropped files list is a focusable scroll region with an `aria-label`; paths are `dir="ltr"`.
- Motion: the marks honour reduced motion and the `Spinner` stops under it.

## States

- Running: `items` has two settled, one deploying and two queued; it advances as the page updates their `status`.
- Drop: the confirm that starts a drop-to-deploy run.
- PartialError: `items` settled with one failed row and its `message`; Retry failed. The dialog shows the outcome, so no toast covers it; the error toast appears only for a run that settles while the dialog is hidden.
- Success: every row in `items` is done; the dialog shows the outcome, and the success toast appears only for a run that settles while the dialog is hidden.

## Related

- `state/state-async-submit` — the toast rule this block follows.
- `create/create-deploy-drawer` — the standard way to deploy.
- `create/create-release-impact` — what a release reaches, before it runs.
- `OutcomeIcon` — the settled mark.

## Variants

`Running` (primary) · `Drop` · `PartialError` · `Success`. Code: [blocks/create/create-deploy-progress-dialog.md](blocks/create/create-deploy-progress-dialog.md), `get_block("create/create-deploy-progress-dialog", { variant })`.

# CreateDeploySuccess (`create/create-deploy-success`)

> The outcome screen a create flow ends on, in the terminal column of the wizard page: a heading with its lead and, for a Git source, the scope as a Tag; the deployment card with the service name with a Live Tag and its…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-deploy-success/create-deploy-success.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-deploy-success")`
- Components: Button, Card, CodeBlock, IntegrationCard, Item, Link, Tag, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

deploy success; deployment successful; deployed; success page; deployment complete; next steps after deploy; wizard finish; deploy concluído; sucesso do deploy; aplicação publicada

The screen a create flow ends on. The user has just watched a deploy finish and needs three answers before leaving: is it live and where, what exactly was created or bound along the way, and what to do next. The page answers them in that order in the terminal column of the wizard, then offers one way out to manage the resource.

## When to use

- A create flow (a template deploy, an import from Git, a source or provision wizard) has finished and the resource is serving, or was created for the first time.
- The flow created or bound more than one resource and the user should see each one.
- A resource was made from the CLI and nothing serves it yet: the CliCreated state shows how to deploy it.

## When not to use

- The run is still going or has failed: keep the create-flow card of `detail/detail-deployment-logs` (InCreateFlow) on screen.
- A resource created from a form that does not deploy: end on the resource's page with a success toast that names it, as `skills/webkit-create-surface` describes; there is no outcome screen.
- An item added inside a resource from a drawer: use `create/create-drawer` and close it on save.
- The onboarding steps for a CLI resource on its Overview tab: use `detail/detail-get-started`.

## Building blocks

- A. Outcome heading — `Tag` (required)
- B. Deployment card — `Card`, `Tag`, `Button`, `Link`, `Tooltip` (required)
- C. Resources list — `Card`, `Item`, `Tag` (required)
- D. Next steps — `IntegrationCard` (required)
- E. Get started — `ToggleGroup`, `CodeBlock`, `Card` (optional)
- F. Manage — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-deploy-success.md](blocks/create/create-deploy-success.md).

## Data

The block takes what the flow made through props and emits its actions; it fetches nothing. `DeploySuccessProps`, `DeploySuccessDeployment`, `DeploySuccessResource` and `DeploySuccessNextStep` are exported from `create-deploy-success.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample deployment, resources and next steps the block renders when a data prop is left out.

Prop: `title`, `description`, `deployment`, `resources`, `nextSteps`, `getStarted`.

Event: `next-step`, `manage`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/create-deploy-success.md](blocks/create/create-deploy-success.md).

## Do

- Lead with the outcome and the live address; the user came to see it work.
- Tag every resource Created or Bound so the list doubles as a receipt of what the flow touched.
- Open the domain and the repository in a new tab with `Link target="_blank"`, and a `Tooltip` saying so.
- Drop the scope tag and the repository row when the flow had no Git source.
- In CliCreated, replace the deployment card with next steps that deploy the resource, and add the Get started paths for the CLI and GitHub Actions.

## Don't

- Don't celebrate: no confetti, no exclamation, no emoji. State the fact.
- Don't put more than one Recommended tag among the next steps.
- Don't add a Deploy again or Create another action; the user starts a new flow from the Creation Center.
- Don't leave the screen without a way into the resource; Manage is required.
- Don't repeat the resource list inside the deployment card.

## Copy

- **Heading:** the object and the past-tense result in sentence case, e.g. "Resource deployed", or "Resource created" when nothing serves it.
- **Lead:** one sentence with a period, e.g. "You deployed a new resource." followed by "Source:" and the source tag. Never a dangling fragment after the period.
- **Status tag:** one word, e.g. "Live"; resource tags "Created" or "Bound".
- **Links:** verb first, e.g. "Visit site", "Add custom domain"; tooltips name the target, e.g. "Open acme/web-app in a new tab".
- **Next steps:** title verb first in two or three words, e.g. "Customize domain", "View analytics"; description one sentence with a period.
- **Exit:** "Manage service", or "Manage resource" when nothing serves it yet: the verb and its object.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no ampersand, no "please".

## Accessibility

- The heading is the page's only `h1`; the service name and the section titles are `h2`.
- Links that open a new tab say so in their `Tooltip`, not only with the external-link glyph.
- Glyphs in rows and cards are decorative and carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the Created or Bound tag gives the state in words.
- A next-step card is one focusable link or button with a visible focus ring; its title and description are its name.
- Focus order follows reading order: heading, deployment card, resources, next steps, Manage.

## States

- Default: a deployed service from a Git source (`deployment` with a `source`), with the scope, the deployment card, four `resources` and three `nextSteps`.
- CliCreated: a resource made from the CLI that nothing serves yet; `:deployment="null"` leaves out the deployment card, one resource row, next steps to deploy it here or on a new service, and `get-started` shows the Get started paths.

- `detail/detail-deployment-logs` — the run this screen follows (InCreateFlow).
- `create/create-deploy-template` — a flow that ends here.
- `create/create-wizard` — its CreateAndDeploy variant ends here with its own title.

# CreateDeployTemplate (`create/create-deploy-template`)

> The deploy template page, a focused flow outside the console shell: the creation header with Back to Creation Center and the Start from a template crumb, the template preview card naming the repository it clones from,…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-deploy-template/create-deploy-template.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-deploy-template")`
- Components: Accordion, AppHeader, `AppHeaderAccount`, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, Checkbox, ConfirmDialog, EmptyState, Field, IconButton, Input, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupInput`, `InputGroupRoot`, Item, Kbd, Link, Select, Skeleton, Switch, Tag, Tooltip, `use-escape-to-cancel`, `use-locale`, `use-shortcuts`, `use-unsaved-changes`, `utils/focus-invalid`, `utils/radio-list`
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

deploy template; clone template; template deploy page; connect git provider; deploy from template; one click deploy; start from a template; implantar template; clonar template; conectar git; deploy uploaded project; deploy imported repository; implantar projeto enviado; import from git form; import from git; importar do git; where it runs; select a service; choose service to deploy to; install integration template; integration template; add integration to service; origin proxy template; instalar integração

A focused page, outside the console shell, where the user turns a template into a running project. They chose a template in the Creation Center and now need to see what it clones, connect a Git provider if they have none, name the repository it creates, fill the settings the template requires and deploy. The same column then shows the build and the outcome, so the user never leaves the page.

## When to use

- Use create-deploy-template for the configure-and-deploy step once the source (repository, template or uploaded folder) is chosen.
- The user picked a template, a Git import or an upload from `create/create-hub`, and the next step is to deploy it.
- The flow creates a repository from a source in the user's Git account and deploys from it on every push.
- The template needs a few settings (tokens, a domain) before its first build can run.
- The project must first say which service it runs on (WhereItRuns), or the template is an integration that adds records and a rule to a service instead of cloning code (InstallIntegration).

## When not to use

- Choosing what to start from: use `create/create-hub`.
- A first-level resource created from a form with no source code: use `create/create-page`.
- Provisioning a resource and binding it to another: use `create/create-wizard` (CreateAndDeploy).

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `AppHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `AppHeaderAccount` (required)
- B. Template and Git step — `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Button`, `Link` (required)
- C. Browse templates — `Button` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-deploy-template.md](blocks/create/create-deploy-template.md).

## Data

The block takes the template and the account through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `DeployTemplateProps` and `DeployTemplateTemplate` are exported from `create-deploy-template.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample template and account the block renders when a prop is left out, and the imported repository, uploaded project and integration the variants pass. Every variant renders a step from `parts/` that renders the block: the header, the preview card, Back and Escape come from it, and the step fills the default slot and keeps its own records.

Prop: `template`, `account`, `providersHref`, `crumb`, `service`.

Slot: `default`, `details`.

Event: `back`, `account`, `connect`, `skip-git`, `browse`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/create-deploy-template.md](blocks/create/create-deploy-template.md).

## Do

- Leaving with typed work: on every form state (Form, BuildSettings, SettingsLoading, ImportFromGit, Upload, InstallIntegration) the header Back asks first once a field differs from what the form opened with (the scope, the repository name, its visibility, the build preset, a setting or a variable): `useUnsavedChanges` tracks them, Back `await`s `guard.confirmLeave()` before it leaves, and one `ConfirmDialog v-bind="guard.dialogProps"` asks "Unsaved changes" with Keep editing and Discard changes. An untouched form leaves at once. In a router app pair it with `onBeforeRouteLeave(() => guard.confirmLeave())`.
- Keep the template preview card at the top of the column through every phase, so the user always sees what is being deployed.
- Ask for Git first; show the form only once a provider is connected.
- Let Deploy check the form: show each missing required value under its field and open the collapsed group that holds it. Disable Deploy only while the settings load, or on an upload until a Root (/) is picked.
- Keep build and variable settings in their collapsible groups, prefilled with defaults, so a template that needs nothing more deploys in one press.
- Mark a secret variable with the locked Secret checkbox and mask its value, with a show control beside it.
- Hand the same column to the create-flow card of `detail/detail-deployment-logs` (InCreateFlow) on Deploy, then to `create/create-deploy-success`.
- Trim the form to the repository fields for Import from Git, and to the uploaded files for Upload a Project.

## Don't

- Don't open this flow inside the console shell or a drawer; it is a page with its own header.
- Don't ask for settings the template does not use, or move a required setting out of view.
- Don't create the repository before Deploy is pressed.
- Don't replace the page with a new route for the build; the column changes, the page stays.
- Don't put a Cancel next to Deploy; the back control and Browse templates already leave.

## Copy

- **Breadcrumb:** the entry point, then the template name, e.g. "Start from a template" then "Nuxt E-commerce".
- **Back control:** `aria-label` names the destination, e.g. "Back to Creation Center".
- **Git step:** title states the task, e.g. "Connect a Git provider"; description one sentence saying what happens, e.g. "Nuxt E-commerce is cloned into a repository in your account, then deployed from it on every push."
- **Provider buttons:** verb first, e.g. "Continue with GitHub"; the link names the place, e.g. "Manage connected providers".
- **Form heading:** e.g. "Deploy your project"; settings labels 1 to 3 words with the constraint in the description, e.g. "You can find this token in the API credentials of your store."
- **Groups:** "Build and output settings", "Environment variables"; rows "Key", "Value", "Secret"; the reveal control "Show value" or "Hide value".
- **Errors:** "<label> is required.", e.g. "Root directory is required."
- **Upload:** breadcrumb "Upload a project"; "Project files"; "Root (/)" with "Select a file".
- **Import:** breadcrumb "Import from Git"; preview "Import and deploy the acme-web repository from GitHub."
- **Commit:** "Deploy", the same verb on the button and in the run that follows.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash in labels or `aria-label`s, no parentheses in labels.

## Accessibility

- **Escape on the page = Cancel.** Escape runs the same path as Back to Creation Center: `useEscapeToCancel` in the block emits `back` on every state, and a form state handles `back` with `guard.confirmLeave()`, so an edited form opens the Unsaved changes dialog. It stays inert while an IME is composing, when another handler already used the key, while a menu, listbox, popover, tooltip or dialog is open, and when focus is in a control that uses Escape itself. Edit and settings pages are places, not tasks: Escape stays inert there.
- **Every form state opens with the cursor in its first field** (Scope on the Form).
- **⌘ Enter deploys (`Ctrl Enter` off Apple)** through the same function as the Deploy button, from any field, on Form, BuildSettings and ImportFromGit, and runs Add to service-01 on InstallIntegration; the button carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and an `aria-hidden` `Kbd`, and the `?` dialog lists the action.
- One `main` landmark under the header; the step title is an `h2` and the settings group an `h3`.
- The back `IconButton`, the brand link and the account button each have an `aria-label`.
- The repository name has a visible `Field.Label` tied to its input by its `Field`; the privacy switch sits in its own row with a visible Public repository label and a description of what it means, and announces its on or off state.
- Settings use `Field` labels and descriptions, so each input announces its name and constraint.
- Required fields carry the Required marker; a failed Deploy puts each error in a `Field.Error` (`role="alert"`) tied to its input.
- Each `Accordion` trigger is a button that announces its expanded state; the Value input is labelled by its Value label, the Key row by its Key label (on a phone the key is a read-only line above a full-width Value field), and the show control is a toggle with `aria-pressed`.
- The uploaded files list is a `ul` named by the folder, inside a focusable scroll region (`role="region"`, `tabindex="0"`) so it scrolls from the keyboard; while settings load the region is `aria-busy` with one status line.
- The page enter animation stops under reduced motion.

## States

- ConnectGit: no Git provider yet; the `template` preview over the Connect a Git provider card and Browse templates.
- Form: GitHub connected; scope and repository name side by side, public by default, over the store domain setting and the Build and output settings and Environment variables groups; Deploy shows the missing access token under its field.
- BuildSettings: after a failed Deploy; both groups open, a Build preset on the detected Nuxt preset, and the required access token in error.
- SettingsLoading: the template settings loading as Skeleton bands, Deploy disabled.
- ImportFromGit: a repository imported from GitHub; scope and repository name over one collapsed Build and output settings group.
- Upload: a dropped folder; project name and build preset, the Project files card and a required Root (/) for a static project with no index.
- WhereItRuns: the service chooser before the Git step, with search, Create Service and Continue without a service.
- InstallIntegration: the Origin Proxy integration on service-01; its settings, What gets added and Add to service-01, which shows the required origin message.

# CreateDrawer (`create/create-drawer`)

> The right-side form drawer every item created or edited inside a resource opens, such as a domain, a record, an environment, a variable or a rule: a panel header with the title, a muted one-line description and the cl…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-drawer/create-drawer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-drawer")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CodeEditor, ConfirmDialog, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, Field, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`, Hint, IconButton, Input, InputGroup, Item, Kbd, KeyValueList, Link, NumberInput, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, RadioGroup, SchemaForm, Select, SettingsGroup, SettingsRow, StatusIndicator, Switch, Textarea, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, `use-file-picker`, `use-locale`, `use-shortcuts`, `use-unsaved-changes`, `utils/focus-invalid`
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

create domain; add domain; create domain form; add domain drawer; edit domain; new domain; create drawer; custom domain; criar domínio; adicionar domínio; novo domínio; create in drawer; add record; add environment; criar em gaveta; form drawer; side drawer form; add item drawer; edit drawer; dns record form; nested resource form; gaveta de formulário; adicionar registro; formulário lateral; add origin drawer; form in drawer; formulário em gaveta; nested drawer; stacked drawers; drawer on drawer; create related item; create option in select; child form; gaveta aninhada; gavetas empilhadas; criar item relacionado; add rule; create origin in drawer; build and deployment; build deployment settings; deployment settings; deployment defaults; deploy configuration; workload deployment defaults; build settings; configurações de build; configurações de deploy; implantação; create deployment settings; deployment settings drawer; criar configuração de deploy; certificate; upload certificate; tls certificate; pem; certificate expiry; certificado; importar certificado; certificado tls; create environment; environment form; ip allowlist; branch tracking; function instance; function arguments; schema form in drawer; criar ambiente; instância de função

The right-side drawer that adds or edits something that only exists inside another resource: a domain, a DNS record, an environment, a variable, a rule. The user is working on the resource behind it and must keep it in view, so the form slides over the page instead of replacing it. They fill a few sections, press the one commit button and land back where they were, with the new item in the list. The drawer opens over a console page: ItemRows and NestedDrawer draw that page as a page body for `ConsoleLayout` (the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`).

## When to use

- The item belongs to a resource that is already open (a domain on a workload, a record in a zone, a rule or an origin on a resource), per the surface rule in `skills/webkit-create-surface`.
- Editing that same item from its row menu; the drawer opens on its values and saves them.
- A first-level tuple normally created in bulk, such as variables, the one exception the surface rule allows.
- A select needs another item of the same resource that may not exist yet, such as the origin a new rule sends requests to: the NestedDrawer shape creates it in a second drawer and selects it back.
- A form needs a resource that does not exist yet, first-level ones included, such as the digital certificate of a workload being created: offer `Create certificate` in the field, and the drawer holds that resource's own create form (`large` over a page, `medium` over a drawer) and selects it back. The reader never leaves the form to create it.

## When not to use

- A resource the sidebar routes to: create it on a page with `create/create-page`, or `create/create-wizard` when it needs several pages.
- A blocking yes or no question, or a destructive guard: use `edit/edit-delete-dialog`.
- Deploying what exists: use `create/create-deploy-drawer`, which commits a deployment rather than a record.
- Binding a whole resource that may be reused or created in a create flow: use `create/create-resource-picker`.
- A missing resource whose creation takes several steps, such as a project imported from a repository: open its create page in a new tab and give the field a `Refresh` option.
- Editing the settings of the resource itself: use `edit/edit-resource`.

## Building blocks

- A. Trigger — `Button` (required)
- B. Drawer frame — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent` (required)
- C. Panel header — `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle` (required)
- D. Sections — `PanelBody`, `SettingsGroup` (required)
- E. Environment select — `Field`, `Select` (required)
- F. Domain source — `Field`, `RadioGroup` (required)
- G. Domain name — `Field`, `InputGroup` (required)
- H. Certificate — `Field`, `Select`, `FieldDescription` (optional)
- I. Context alert — `Alert` (optional)
- J. Footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)
- K. Certificate import — `SettingsGroup`, `Field`, `Button`, `PanelFooter` (optional)
- L. Discard guard — `ConfirmDialog` (required)
- M. Shortcut keycap — `Kbd` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-drawer.md](blocks/create/create-drawer.md).

## Data

The block takes its option lists, its starting values and the save state through props and emits the values; it fetches and saves nothing. `CreateDrawerProps`, `CreateDrawerValues`, `CreateDrawerEnvironment` and `CreateDrawerCertificate` are exported from `create-drawer.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the environments and certificates the block renders when those props are left out.

Prop: `environments`, `connectedEnvironments`, `certificates`, `defaultValues`, `title`, `description`, `submitLabel`, `open` (`v-model:open`), `defaultOpen`, `environmentOpen` (`v-model:environment-open`), `loading`, `error`.

Event: `submit`, `update:open`, `update:environmentOpen`.

The `trigger` slot replaces the Add button (an environment menu, a row menu) and receives `open` to call.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/create-drawer.md](blocks/create/create-drawer.md).

## Do

- Open on a blank form every time, or on the edited item's values, and clear every error on open.
- Lock the `fieldset` and pass `:disabled` to every control from the same flag while saving; release it on success and on failure.
- Validate on submit only: a required field shows the Required marker from the start, and turns `invalid` with a `Field.Error` only after Save is pressed with it empty.
- Close the drawer on success and show the new item in the list behind it, with a toast that names it (every variant does).
- On a failed save keep the drawer open with the values, release the fieldset and show a danger `Alert` with Retry above the footer (SaveError).
- Stack a second, medium drawer for a missing item of the same resource, such as an origin for a rule, and select the new one back into the parent.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/shell-console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't create in a dialog, or open a page for an item that lives inside a resource.
- Don't add Cancel next to the commit button.
- Don't flag fields while the user is still typing, or colour a required field before a failed submit.
- Don't hide a required field inside a collapsed section.
- Don't reset the form on close; the content would jump while the drawer slides out.
- Don't deploy or publish as a side effect of Save.

## Copy

- **Trigger, title, commit:** one string, `Add <Product Module>` inside a resource, e.g. "Add Domain"; editing keeps the verb the row menu used.
- **Description:** one or two muted sentences with a period under the title, e.g. "A domain is what puts an environment on this resource. Say where it answers, and name the address."
- **Section hints:** one sentence on what the section decides, e.g. "Where the domain answers."
- **Options:** labels name the choice, descriptions one sentence, e.g. "Use your own DNS and point it to this resource."
- **Helper text:** states the consequence of the current value, e.g. "Production publishes with the Deployment Settings set to Single."
- **Required:** "This field is required."
- **Create option:** `Create <Object>` at the foot of the select, e.g. "Create Environment".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy` and `skills/webkit-errors`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", select rather than pick.

## Accessibility

- The drawer traps focus while open, moves it to the first field on open and returns it to the trigger on close.
- **⌘ Enter submits the drawer (`Ctrl Enter` off Apple).** `useShortcuts` binds `meta+enter` to the drawer form's `requestSubmit()`, with the form as the shortcut's element, so with two drawers stacked only the top one submits. It stays inert while saving; the submit button carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and an `aria-hidden` `Kbd`, and the `?` dialog lists the action under Drawer.
- The `form` has an `aria-label` that matches the title; `DrawerTitle` names the dialog.
- Every select trigger is described by its `Field.Description` (or its `Field.Error`) through the `Field`, so the consequence is read with the value.
- Required fields carry the Required marker from the start; an error is a `Field.Error` with `role="alert"` and the control is `aria-invalid`.
- The choice cards are a radio group named by the Domain source label; each card's title and description are the radio's name and description.
- The loading button keeps its label and announces the busy state; the disabled `fieldset` keeps keyboard users out of the form while saving.
- Escape, the close button and the overlay all dismiss; none of them submit. With typed input they open the Unsaved changes `alertdialog` first, focused on Keep editing; Escape there closes only the alert and the drawer keeps the form.

## States

- Default: Add Domain opened from the resource's Settings tab, blank, on the free domain option; `loading` spins the button while the page saves.
- AddEnvironment: the same form opened from the environment menu (the `trigger` slot), titled and saved as Add Environment (`title`).
- EditDomain: opened from a domain row menu on www.example.com (`defaultValues`, `title`, `submitLabel`), with the Certificate select showing the covering wildcard.
- AddRecord: the DNS zone record form; Name and Value carry the Required marker from the start and turn invalid only after an empty Add Record.
- ItemRows: Add Origin on the Origins page of the storefront resource, a large drawer whose sections are `Item` rows in flush cards, saved together by one Add Origin.
- NestedDrawer: Add Rule on the storefront resource's Rules Engine, with an Origin select whose Create Origin option opens a second, medium drawer and selects the new origin back.
- DeploymentSettings: the drawer that creates a Deployment Setting, with General and Routing and policy sections.
- Certificate: Create Certificate opened with shop.example.com pasted as a server certificate: the details panel reads Issued to shop.example.com, Issued by Example Test CA and the expiry with the days left; the private key is empty, so Save flags it.
- CreateEnvironment: Create Environment with General, Settings, Protection and Branch tracking sections; the IP allowlist and Branch tracking switches each reveal their fields, a duplicate name or an invalid address is flagged only after Create Environment. Opened from Add Domain's Environment select it stacks at medium size above that drawer and selects the new environment back.
- SaveError: Add Domain after a failed save (`error` set, `defaultOpen`, `defaultValues`): the drawer stays open with acme-store and Production kept, the fieldset released, and a danger Alert with Retry above the footer.
- FunctionInstance: Add Function Instance (or Edit from a row) with a Function `Select`, a Name, and the arguments as a `SchemaForm` of the chosen function's schema with a Fields or JSON `ToggleGroup`; the JSON `CodeEditor` marks a parse error, and required arguments are flagged only after submit.

## Do

- Keep template sections in the same order on every visit; Recommended first.

## Don't

- Don't replace the list with a spinner while a scope loads; use skeleton rows in its shape.
- Don't add a Continue or Next button; each Import and each template card starts its flow.
- Don't let the template gallery push the page into a long scroll on large screens; it scrolls inside its own area.
- Don't show templates as a dense table; the glyph and sentence are what the user scans.
- Don't hand-write the file and folder links or underline them at rest; use `Button variant="link"`.

## Copy

- **Heading:** a verb phrase for the task, e.g. "Start a new project"; description one sentence with a period, e.g. "Start from a repository or use a framework template."
- **Column titles:** short fragments, e.g. "Import from GitHub".
- **Connect state:** title states the task, e.g. "Connect your repository"; description one sentence, e.g. "Select a Git provider to connect your repository and start the deployment process."
- **Buttons:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Continue with GitHub", "Import", "Load more", "Clear search".
- **Search:** placeholder and `aria-label` name what it takes, e.g. "Search repositories or paste a repository URL".
- **Template cards:** title is the template name; description one sentence, e.g. "Compile Rust to WebAssembly and run it."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, select rather than choose or pick, no em dash.

## Accessibility

- The `PageHeader` title is the page's only `h1`; column titles are `h2`, the template section labels `h3`, and template titles sit below them (the `IntegrationCard` title, and `h4` on a Recommended card).
- The back `IconButton`, the brand link, the account button, the scope `Select` and the search each have an `aria-label`.
- Each template tile is reached through its title link, which covers the tile; Enter follows it. Each Import button is named after its repository.
- The loading region sets `aria-busy="true"` with one `role="status"` line; skeleton rows are hidden from assistive technology.
- Upload works from the keyboard: the file and folder buttons in the description open the system picker.
- The `ScrollArea` is named so screen reader users know which region scrolls.

## States

- Default: no Git account connected (`accounts` is `[]`); the connect state beside the template gallery.
- Connected: `accounts` is passed and jane-doe, the first, is the selected scope; its ten most recently pushed repositories are listed, with Load more for the rest.
- RepositoriesLoading: a scope was just picked (`loading`); six skeleton rows stand in for the repositories.
- ConnectError: the GitHub connection failed (`connectError` is set); a danger Alert under Continue with GitHub.
- LoadError: the repositories failed to load (`error` is set); a danger Alert with Retry in place of the list.

## Related

- `create/create-deploy-template` — where a template card or Import leads.
- `state/state-project-intake` — the drop target and upload overlay for a dropped folder.
- `top-bar/top-bar-creation` — the header this page uses.
- `dashboard/dashboard-home` — Home, where the back control returns.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Connected` · `RepositoriesLoading` · `ConnectError` · `LoadError`. Code: [blocks/create/create-hub.md](blocks/create/create-hub.md), `get_block("create/create-hub", { variant })`.

# CreatePage (`create/create-page`)

> The page a first-level resource is created on in one screen: its own creation header with no sidebar, a centred form column opening with a small page heading, then stacked sections, each a heading with a Hint over a f…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-page/create-page.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-page")`
- Components: Alert, AppHeader, `AppHeaderAccount`, Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, ConfirmDialog, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`, IconButton, Input, Item, Kbd, MultiSelect, NumberInput, PageHeader, RadioGroup, RadioGroup, SaveBar, Select, SettingsGroup, SettingsRow, Switch, Tag, TagEditor, Textarea, Toast, `use-escape-to-cancel`, `use-file-picker`, `use-shortcuts`, `use-unsaved-changes`, `utils/focus-invalid`
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

create page; create resource page; create zone; full page create form; top-level create page; new resource form; creation page; página de criação; criar recurso; formulário de criação; single page create; create purge; create service page; criação em uma página; sectioned form; single column form; form with sections; formulário em seções; formulário de uma coluna; import zone file; create dns zone; importar arquivo de zona; create organization; new organization form; organization mark; criar organização; one page create; create form page

The page a first-level resource is created on when everything it needs fits on one screen. The user arrives from the module's `Create <Object>` button, answers the required fields at the top, leaves the defaulted ones folded under Advanced, and commits from a bar that never scrolls away. The page has its own URL, its own creation header and no sidebar, so it survives a reload and the back button, and leaving it returns to the list.

## When to use

- Use create-page only to create a first-level resource on one page; its settings page is edit-resource (`edit/edit-resource`).
- The resource is one the sidebar routes to (a domain, a service, a purge) and the user came only to create it (`skills/webkit-create-surface`).
- Its fields fit in a few sections without depending on each other's answers step by step.
- An action that takes a form and runs once, whose submit names what it does (Save, Purge, Deploy).

## When not to use

- The fields split into steps that unlock in order, or one answer adds a step: use `create/create-wizard`.
- The resource binds another one and then deploys: use `create/create-wizard` (CreateAndDeploy).
- Deploying a repository, a template or an uploaded folder: start at `create/create-hub` and deploy with `create/create-deploy-template` (ImportFromGit covers a Git import).
- The thing is created inside another resource (a record in a zone, a rule in an application): use `create/create-drawer`.
- The settings page of an existing resource, with the save bar that mounts only after a change: use `edit/edit-resource`.
- Never put a create form in a dialog.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `AppHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `AppHeaderAccount` (required)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Sections — `SettingsGroup`, `Card`, `Item` (required)
- D. Field rows — `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `FieldError` (required)
- E. Switch rows — `Switch` (optional)
- F. Tags — `TagEditor` (optional)
- G. Commit bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)
- H. Failed request — `Alert` (required)
- I. Leaving with typed work — `useUnsavedChanges`, `ConfirmDialog` (required)
- J. Shortcut keycap — `Kbd` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-page.md](blocks/create/create-page.md).

## Data

The block keeps the form as a local draft, validates it and emits `submit` with the values; it sends no request. `CreatePageValues` and `CreatePageProps` are exported from `create-page.vue`. The page owns the request: it sets `loading` while it runs, and on failure sets `error`, which the block shows in a danger `Alert` with Retry under the page heading; on success the page shows the toast and opens the new domain.

Prop: `defaultValues`, `loading`, `error`.

Event: `submit`, `cancel`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/create-page.md](blocks/create/create-page.md).

## Do

- Put every required field in the first band; never inside Advanced, so a failed submit always points at something on screen.
- Validate on submit only, then clear each message as soon as its field is edited.
- Give every control an `aria-label` that repeats its row title.
- Keep Cancel and the submit in the same bar, submit last, and name the submit after what it does (Save, Purge, Deploy).
- Lock the whole `fieldset` and every control with one `loading` flag while the request is in flight, and put `:loading` on the submit.
- On success, show a toast that names the resource and opens it; on failure, an error toast with Retry that keeps the values (`skills/webkit-errors`). Every submit in this block models the request: Default, CreateZone, CreatePurge, CreateService and CreateOrganization.

## Don't

- Don't show the sidebar on this page, or open it as a modal over the list.
- Don't stretch the commit bar across the page or build the centred card by hand; it is `SaveBar variant="centered"`.
- Don't print the band's guidance as a paragraph under its title; use the `hint`.
- Don't mark fields invalid before the first submit; `required` is set from the start and draws no colour.
- Don't make Save deploy, publish or charge as a side effect; creating is not deploying.
- Don't add a validation summary at the top; each message sits at its field.
- Don't squeeze a textarea or radio group into the right-hand cell; stack the row.

## Copy

- **Title and breadcrumb:** the create label, verb first with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Domain". Identical to the button that opened the page.
- **Description:** one sentence on what the resource is, e.g. "A domain holds the DNS records that answer authoritatively for a hostname."
- **Section titles:** the domain, not the widget, e.g. "General", "Target", "Delivery settings", "Advanced".
- **Row descriptions:** a full sentence with a period, saying what the value does, e.g. "Identifies the domain in this list. It is not the hostname."
- **Submit:** one verb, e.g. "Save", "Purge", "Deploy". Cancel is always exactly "Cancel".
- **Required message:** "This field is required."
- **Invalid message:** what to enter, with an example, e.g. "Enter a valid domain name. Example: example.com."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no parentheses in labels, no "please".

## Accessibility

- **Escape on the page = Cancel.** `useEscapeToCancel(onCancel)` runs the same path as the Cancel button: a clean form leaves at once, an edited one opens the Unsaved changes dialog. It stays inert while the create request is in flight, while an IME is composing, when another handler already used the key, while a menu, listbox, popover, tooltip or dialog is open (the open Select or DatePicker closes first, and Escape on the Unsaved changes dialog only keeps editing) and when focus is in a control that uses Escape itself (an open combobox, a search field). Edit and settings pages are places, not tasks: Escape stays inert there.
- **The page opens with the cursor in the first field.** `onMounted` focuses Name (CreatePurge: the chosen Layer card), so a keyboard user types at once.
- **⌘ Enter and ⌘ S submit (`Ctrl` off Apple).** The bar reads as a save bar, so ⌘ S saves too instead of opening the browser's Save page dialog. `useShortcuts` binds `meta+enter` and `meta+s` to the form's `requestSubmit()`, the same path as the bar's submit button, from any field and from the Purge list textarea, where a bare Enter only adds a line. It stays inert while the request is in flight and lists the action (Create domain, Purge…) in the `?` dialog. The submit button carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and an `aria-hidden` `Kbd` that prints the platform's key.
- One `main` landmark holding one `form`, labelled by the `PageHeader` title through `aria-labelledby`, with `novalidate` so the page's own messages replace the browser's.
- A `fieldset` with a visually hidden `legend` groups the sections.
- Each message is tied to its control with `aria-describedby` and appears only on submit; `required` and `invalid` are announced through the control's own state.
- The collapsed Advanced region is `inert` while closed, so keyboard focus never lands in hidden fields.
- The back `IconButton` and the account trigger have `aria-label`s; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Focus order follows reading order: header, heading, General, Tags, Advanced toggle, then the bar's Cancel and Save (CreateZone adds Import before them).

## States

- Default: the Create Domain page at rest (no `defaultValues`, not `loading`); General holds Name and Domain name, Tags holds a `TagEditor` (key and value tags with key suggestions, checked on submit with `validate()`; never a comma-separated text field), Advanced is collapsed, the bar shows Cancel and Save. `loading` locks the form and spins Save, and `error` raises the error toast with Retry. Importing a zone file belongs to CreateZone, not to this page.
- CreateZone: Create Zone after a zone file is imported; a Records section lists each imported record (type `Tag`, value, TTL) with a Remove `IconButton` per row and Discard import in the card footer; each removal and the discard confirm in a toast with Undo, which puts the records back. Import in the bar and a paste into Domain name both read a BIND zone file, skip the SOA and nameserver records, fill an empty Name and Domain name from `$ORIGIN`, and confirm in a toast; a file with no records raises an error toast. The list previews the first 50 records with an "and N more" line, and a re-import skips records already listed.
- CreateOrganization: General with Name and a Mark color chosen from six compact `RadioGroup` cards (`variant="card"`, three per row on a phone and one row of six from the small breakpoint) (each color built from semantic tokens: primary, warning, danger, success, info and the text grays, never palette primitives), each an `Avatar` with `pattern="marble"` seeded by the name in that color's `colors`, above an In the header preview drawn the same way, an Owner `Item` with Owner and Active `Tag`s, First workspace and a collapsed Advanced of `Select`s; a name already in use is invalid on submit, and the request ends in a success toast or an error toast with Retry.
- CreatePurge: a Target band of radio choice cards for Layer and Purge type, an Arguments textarea that follows the type, a warning alert and a bar with Cancel and Purge.
- CreateService: a long create with a small `PageHeader` (Create Service, breadcrumb Services / Create Service) and five groups of rows, each under an `h2`, under the same centred `SaveBar` with Cancel and Save.
- RequiredFields: Create Service after Save on the empty form; Name and Address show "This field is required." until edited.

## Related

- `create/create-wizard` — the same job split into steps.
- `create/create-drawer` — create inside a resource without leaving it.
- `settings/settings-form` — the edit page that reuses these sections.
- `state/state-form-validation` — required and invalid states on submit.
- `view/view-table` — the list whose `Create <Object>` button opens this page.
- `SettingsRow` — the field row every section is built from; see `skills/webkit-form`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `CreateZone` · `CreateOrganization` · `CreatePurge` · `CreateService` · `RequiredFields`. Code: [blocks/create/create-page.md](blocks/create/create-page.md), `get_block("create/create-page", { variant })`.

# CreateReleaseImpact (`create/create-release-impact`)

> The Review and deploy page of a release that carries several resources at once.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-release-impact/create-release-impact.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-release-impact")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Badge, Button, Card, Checkbox, ConfirmDialog, EmptyState, Field, Input, Kbd, KeyValueList, OverflowCount, PageHeader, SaveBar, Select, Skeleton, Spinner, Switch, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, `use-locale`, `use-shortcuts`
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

release impact; review and deploy; release composer; what a deploy changes; dependency versions; deployment impact; impacto do release; revisar e implantar; impacto del despliegue

The Review and deploy page of a release that carries several resources at once: a service, the policy in front of it, its storage, its error page and every dependency they reference. The user is about to put all of it into traffic and needs to see, before deploying, which version of each resource goes out, which dependencies go with it, and every Deployment Setting, environment and project the release reaches. One Deploy release at the foot commits it, after one confirmation.

## When to use

- A release spans several resources that deploy together, each at its own version.
- The release reaches projects through shared Deployment Settings, and the user must see how far it goes before it goes.
- Dependencies are detected from the resources and may be shared between them.

## When not to use

- Deploying one service or project from its page: use `create/create-deploy-drawer`, which is the default way to deploy.
- Watching several Deployment Settings activate after a deploy started: use `create/create-deploy-progress-dialog`.
- Reading what a past deploy did: use `detail/detail-deployment-logs`.
- Switching one resource back to an earlier version: use `detail/detail-version` (Revert).

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Outcome — `Alert`, `Button` (required after a run)
- C. Resource cards — `Card`, `Switch`, `Tag`, `Tooltip` (required)
- D. Resource and version — `KeyValueList`, `Field`, `Select`, `Tag` (required)
- E. Dependencies — `Badge`, `Accordion`, `Alert`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `Select` (required when a resource references others)
- F. Impact — `Card`, `ToggleGroup`, `Spinner`, `Skeleton`, `Alert`, `Button` (required)
- G. Footer and commit — `SaveBar`, `Button`, `ConfirmDialog` (required)
- Before the review: choosing the Deployment Settings
- H. Shortcut keycap — `Kbd` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-release-impact.md](blocks/create/create-release-impact.md).

## Data

The block takes the release and its impact through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing and runs no deploy of its own. `ReleaseImpactResource`, `ReleaseImpactSettings` and `ReleaseImpactProps` (with the version, dependency, environment and project types) are exported from `create-release-impact.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample resources and Deployment Settings the block renders when `resources` or `impact` is left out (the impact sample never renders while `loading` or `error` is set). The switches and version selects edit a local copy of `resources`; `deploy` carries the included resources at the versions picked.

Prop: `resources`, `impact`, `loading`, `error`, `truncated`, `deploying`, `deployed`, `deployError`.

Event: `deploy`, `retry`, `edit`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/create-release-impact.md](blocks/create/create-release-impact.md).

## Do

- Show every resource and dependency with the version that goes out, including the ones the user did not touch.
- Say what tracking the latest Ready version resolves to now.
- Block Deploy release only for something the user can fix here, and say what it is in the footer.
- Keep Deploy possible when the impact cannot be computed; say the impact is unknown.
- Report the outcome in the page `Alert` with Edit and Redeploy; dismiss the loading toast when the run ends and raise no outcome toast over the docked bar.

## Don't

- Don't hide shared dependencies; changing one changes it everywhere in the release.
- Don't confirm twice: the page is the review, the `ConfirmDialog` is the only step before the run. Deploying one service or one project is `create/create-deploy-drawer`, which confirms nothing after Deploy; this page is only for a release of several resources.
- Don't keep the user on the page while it runs; the run reports wherever they are.
- Don't draw the Flow view with `FlowDiagram` until its list semantics pass axe.

## Copy

- **Title:** "Review and deploy". **Commit:** "Deploy release"; in progress "Deploying…".
- **Confirmation:** "Deploy this release?" and one sentence with the resources, versions and reach.
- **Selecting settings:** title "Select Deployment Settings"; search "Search 6 Deployment Settings"; "2 selected", "Select all", "Clear"; workloads "4 workloads affected" or "No workloads deploy with it yet"; no match "No Deployment Settings match" with "Clear search"; footer "Select at least one Deployment Setting to continue."
- **Versions:** "Track latest Ready", "resolves at deploy", "Pin a ready version", tag "Current".
- **Blockers:** "<name> has no Ready version, so the release cannot be deployed."
- **Outcome:** "Release deployed." / "The release wasn't deployed." with the cause and that nothing changed in traffic.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: Deploy, never publish; sentence case; no em dash.

## Accessibility

- Each resource card is a `section` named by its type and resource; the Resources heading takes focus on Edit.
- Every `Select` is labelled through its `Field` (visible for the resource, `sr-only` for dependencies).
- The include `Switch` has an `aria-label`; its `Tooltip` repeats it for pointer users.
- The Shared `Tag` sits in a focusable wrapper so its `Tooltip` opens from the keyboard.
- The Impact region is `aria-busy` while loading and announces it in a `role="status"` line.
- In ChooseSettings each group is a `role="group"` named by its heading, each choice card is a `label` around its `Checkbox`, the selected count is a polite live region, and a loading workloads count is read as text rather than a bare `Skeleton`.
- The `ConfirmDialog` traps focus and returns it to Deploy release.
- `⌘ Enter` (`Ctrl Enter` off Apple) opens the deploy confirmation, the same as Deploy release, and does nothing while the release can't be deployed; the release is only deployed from the confirmation. Deploy release carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and a `Kbd` keycap.

## States

- ChooseSettings: the step before the review; grouped checkbox choice cards with search, Select all and Clear, a loading workloads count, an inactive setting with its activate link, and Continue disabled until one is selected.
- Ready: `resources` all have a version and `impact` is computed; Tree view.
- Loading: `loading` is set while the impact is computed.
- Unavailable: `error` says the impact could not be read; Retry emits `retry`, and a truncated answer sets `truncated`.
- MissingVersion: a resource in `resources` has no `versions`, which blocks the deploy.
- Error: `deployError` says the last run was refused; the danger page `Alert` announces it with Edit and Redeploy, and no toast covers the bar.

## Related

- `create/create-deploy-drawer` — deploying one service or project.
- `create/create-deploy-progress-dialog` — several Deployment Settings activating after the deploy.
- `state/state-async-submit` — the toast rule every deploy follows.
- `detail/detail-version` — one version, its history and revert.

## Variants

`Ready` (primary) · `ChooseSettings` · `Loading` · `Unavailable` · `MissingVersion` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/create/create-release-impact.md](blocks/create/create-release-impact.md), `get_block("create/create-release-impact", { variant })`.

# CreateResourcePicker (`create/create-resource-picker`)

> The card a create flow uses to bind one resource to another: a lead, a ToggleGroup choosing between an existing resource and a new one, then either a hint over a searchable list of the existing resources with a select…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-resource-picker/create-resource-picker.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-resource-picker")`
- Components: Button, Card, Field, `FieldError`, Input, Item, SettingsRow, Skeleton, Switch, ToggleGroup, `utils/radio-list`
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

resource picker; select existing or new; choose resource; bind resource; searchable picker; pick application; seletor de recurso; escolher recurso; existente ou novo; optional binding; opt-in binding; protect with firewall; bind firewall; vincular firewall

The band a create flow uses when the resource being created needs another resource that may already exist. The user either reuses one of theirs or makes a new one on the spot, and answers it in one place: an Existing / New choice, then a searchable, paged list of what exists or the few fields that create a new one. The chosen row is marked, every search and load is announced, and a missing answer is flagged above the list where it is seen first. When the binding itself is optional (a firewall in front of a project), the same band sits behind an opt-in switch row and unfolds in place when it is turned on.

## When to use

- Use create-resource-picker inside a create flow to bind one resource the user may reuse or create; it is a card, not a page.
- A create flow binds a whole resource that the user may reuse or create: the project a service serves, the deployment a release is cut against, the firewall that protects a workload.
- The candidates can run past seven, so the list needs search, paging and a no-match line.
- Creating the bound resource takes one or a few fields that fit in the same card.
- The binding is optional and off by default: wrap the band in the opt-in switch row (OptionalBinding).

## When not to use

- A single field that references an existing resource (a certificate, an environment, a function): use a select row inside the form, as `create/create-wizard` (CreateAndDeploy) does for Environment.
- Choosing where a resource runs as a step of its own, with module tags and an inline create row: use the chooser in `create/create-wizard` or `create/create-deploy-template` (WhereItRuns).
- Browsing or managing the resources themselves: use `view/view-table`.
- Creating the bound resource needs its own full form: New opens that form in a drawer over the page (`create/create-drawer`) instead of nesting it in the band. Only a create of several steps opens its page in a new tab.

## Building blocks

- A. Band card — `Card` (required)
- B. Existing / New choice — `ToggleGroup` (required when something exists)
- C. New resource fields — `Field`, `Input` (required in New)
- D. Search and required message — `Input`, `FieldError` (optional)
- E. Resource list — `Item`, `Skeleton` (required in Existing)
- F. Load more — `Button` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-resource-picker.md](blocks/create/create-resource-picker.md).

## Data

The block takes its resources through props, keeps the answer in `v-model`s and emits Load more; it fetches nothing. `ResourcePickerOption`, `ResourcePickerMode` and `ResourcePickerProps` are exported from `create-resource-picker.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample projects the block renders when `projects` is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop / model: `projects`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model`, `v-model:mode`, `v-model:name`.

Event: `load-more`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/create-resource-picker.md](blocks/create/create-resource-picker.md).

## Do

- Default to Existing when anything exists, and drop the toggle entirely when nothing does.
- Mark the chosen row three ways: background, filled trailing radio circle and `aria-checked`.
- Keep the required message above the rows, under the search, so it is read before the list is scanned.
- Offer the other mode in the no-match line, so an empty search leads to creating one.
- Keep the chosen value when the user switches to New and back.
- Keep an optional binding off by default, and prefill the new resource's name from the resource being created.
- Build the band once and pass the noun, icon and options; every flow that binds a resource reads the same (see `skills/webkit-create-surface`).

## Don't

- Don't use radio buttons or a select for a whole resource the user may also create; that is this band.
- Don't show the search for a list that fits in one batch.
- Don't validate the Name while it is being typed, or mark it invalid before Next is pressed.
- Don't render a loading spinner in place of the rows; show skeleton rows in the row shape and keep the visible ones.
- Don't put the create fields in a dialog or a second page; they belong in the same card.
- Don't hide a locked module or leave it looking editable; disable it, keep it on and say why in its row description, never only in a tooltip.

## Copy

- **Card title:** the bound noun, singular, e.g. "Project".
- **Lead:** one sentence on what the binding does, e.g. "What this service serves on each environment, so one service can serve different projects on Production and Preview."
- **Toggle options:** `Existing <noun>` and `New <noun>`, e.g. "Existing project", "New project".
- **Search:** placeholder and `aria-label` name the collection, e.g. "Search projects".
- **Load more:** the verb and the batch size, e.g. "Load 5 more".
- **No match:** the fact, then both ways out, e.g. "No project matches “api”. Create one instead, or clear the search."
- **Required:** what to do, as a sentence, e.g. "Select the project this service serves, or create a new one."
- **Name guidance:** the allowed characters, e.g. "Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens."
- **Opt-in row:** the action as the title, e.g. "Protect with a firewall", and what it does and that it is off by default as the description. A locked module's description ends with the fact, e.g. "Always on."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: "Select", never "Pick" or "Choose"; sentence case; no em dash.

## Accessibility

- The `ToggleGroup` has an `aria-label` that states the question, e.g. "Where the project comes from".
- Each row is a native `button` with `role="radio"` and `aria-checked` reflecting the selection, inside a `radiogroup` named for the list; the radio circle is `aria-hidden`.
- Search has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder.
- A `role="status"` region announces the count after every search, load and no-match, e.g. "5 of 19 projects".
- Skeleton rows are `aria-hidden`; the Load more `Button` carries `:loading` so its busy state is announced.
- The required message is tied to the search group by `data-field-invalid`, and focus stays where it was when it appears.
- The opt-in `Switch` and every module `Switch` carry an `aria-label` equal to their row title; the folded body is `inert`, so its controls leave the tab order while the switch is off; the reveal honours reduced motion.

## States

- Existing: `projects` holds resources; the toggle sits on Existing with the `v-model` row chosen in the first batch.
- New: `mode` is `new` (the user switched to New); the list gives way to the Name field with the allowed characters as helper text.
- Loading: `loading` is set after Load more; five skeleton rows follow the visible ones and the button spins.
- Required: `error` holds the required message after Next was pressed with nothing chosen; the required message sits under the search, above the list.
- Empty: `projects` is `[]`, nothing exists to bind; no toggle, one line saying a new project is created, and the Name field.
- OptionalBinding: the Protect with a firewall switch is on and New firewall is selected; the Name is prefilled from the project and the Firewall modules list has DDoS Protection locked on.

## Related

- `create/create-wizard` — its CreateAndDeploy variant binds its project with this band on the first step and reuses the list for the deployment.
- `create/create-wizard` — the step wizard whose Where it runs chooser follows the same list rules.
- `state/state-form-validation` — how required and invalid messages appear on submit.
- `Item` — the selectable row the list is built from; see `skills/webkit-form`.
- `ToggleGroup` — the Existing / New segment; see `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

## Variants

`Existing` (primary) · `New` · `Loading` · `Required` · `Empty` · `OptionalBinding`. Code: [blocks/create/create-resource-picker.md](blocks/create/create-resource-picker.md), `get_block("create/create-resource-picker", { variant })`.

# CreateTicket (`create/create-ticket`)

> The page a support agent creates a ticket on, on behalf of a customer: the creation header with Back, the brand, Tickets › Create Ticket and the account, then a centred form column with a small `PageHeader` and three…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-ticket/create-ticket.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-ticket")`
- Stability: preview. The API may still change in a minor release, named in the changelog, until the owner marks it GA.
- Components: Alert, AppHeader, `AppHeaderAccount`, Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, Combobox, ConfirmDialog, `FieldError`, FileTokenGroup, IconButton, Input, Item, Kbd, MarkdownEditor, MultiSelect, PageHeader, PriorityTag, SaveBar, Select, SettingsGroup, SettingsRow, Skeleton, Toast, `use-escape-to-cancel`, `use-file-picker`, `use-locale`, `use-shortcuts`, `use-unsaved-changes`, `utils/focus-invalid`
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

create ticket; new ticket; new support ticket; log a ticket for a customer; agent creates ticket; helpdesk new ticket form; support request form; ticket form with requester and assignee; create and add another; add new contact inline; criar ticket; novo ticket; novo chamado; abrir chamado em nome de alguém; formulário de chamado; criar chamado de suporte; registrar solicitação de suporte

The page a support agent opens a ticket on, on behalf of a customer who called, chatted or wrote in. The agent's job is to say who asked, what they need and who owns it, then create the ticket and either go to it or log the next one. It follows the Zendesk and Freshdesk new-ticket forms on the house create page (`create/create-page`): its own creation header with no sidebar, a centred form column, three bands of rows, and a raised commit card at the bottom with Cancel, Save and add another, and Save.

A ticket creates on a page, not in a drawer: it is a first-level resource the inbox routes to (`/tickets/new`, the Create Ticket button of `view/view-ticket-inbox`), one ticket is one deliberate act rather than a small tuple created in bulk, and the description needs the full measure (`skills/webkit-create-surface`).

## When to use

- An agent logs a request for a customer: a phone call, a chat that needs a follow-up, an email forwarded from another inbox.
- Any first-level work item with a requester, a written description, an owner and a priority (an abuse report, an onboarding case).

## When not to use

- A record created inside another resource without leaving it (a note on a ticket, a macro in a group): use `create/create-drawer`.
- A short create with a handful of fields and no sections: use `state/state-form-validation`.
- Replying to an existing ticket: use the `message-thread` component with a `markdown-editor` on the ticket's own page.
- The queue the agent comes from: use `view/view-ticket-inbox`.
- A customer filing their own request on a public help center: no block covers it yet; it is a short form without assignment, not this agent page.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `AppHeader`, `AppHeaderAccount`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `IconButton` (required)
- B. Heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Loading rows — `Card`, `Skeleton` (loading only)
- D. Requester band — `SettingsGroup`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Combobox`, `Avatar`, `Button`, `Input`, `FieldError`, `MultiSelect` (required)
- E. Request band — `SettingsGroup`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `FieldError`, `MarkdownEditor`, `IconButton`, `FileTokenGroup`, `Select`, `PriorityTag` (required)
- F. Assignment band — `SettingsGroup`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Combobox`, `Avatar`, `MultiSelect` (required)
- G. Failure — `Alert` (conditional)
- H. Commit — `SaveBar`, `Button`, `Kbd` (required)
- Leaving — `ConfirmDialog`
- Result — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-ticket.md](blocks/create/create-ticket.md).

## Data

The block keeps the form as a local draft, validates it on submit and emits `create`; it sends no request and fakes none. `CreateTicketValues`, `CreateTicketPayload`, `CreateTicketContact`, `CreateTicketGroup`, `CreateTicketAgent`, `CreateTicketCreated`, `CreateTicketChannel`, `CreateTicketType`, `CreateTicketPriority` and `CreateTicketProps` are exported from `create-ticket.vue`. `sample.ts` holds the contacts, groups, agents and tags the pickers offer when their props are left out (none of them while `loading`), plus the filled ticket and the created ticket the variants pass. `lib/ticket-form.ts` holds the option lists, the empty draft and the validation messages.

Prop: `contacts`, `groups`, `agents`, `tagOptions`, `defaultValues`, `defaultSubmitted`, `loading`, `submitting`, `error`, `created`.

Event: `create`, `cancel`, `open`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/create-ticket.md](blocks/create/create-ticket.md).

## Do

- Keep only Requester, Subject and Description required; the rest is triage the team can do later.
- Validate on create only, and move focus to the first field in error.
- Keep every value after a failed request, and show the failure where the commit happens.
- Offer Save and add another for agents logging several calls in a row, and put focus back on Requester.

## Don't

- Don't preselect a channel, type, priority, group or assignee: a blank form starts empty.
- Don't show an error summary or an `Alert` for field errors; each field says what it needs.
- Don't accept a typed name as a group or an assignee.
- Don't send the agent away to create a missing contact: Add new contact stays on the page.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Create Ticket`; description `Log a request on behalf of a customer. They get an email with the ticket number.`
- **Bands:** `Requester`, `Request`, `Assignment`, each with a one-sentence Hint. **Rows:** a noun title and one sentence of guidance (`The customer who asked. Search by name or email address.`).
- **Requester:** placeholder `Search contacts`, no match `No contact matches. Add a new contact instead.`, actions `Add new contact` and `Search contacts`.
- **Placeholders:** `Select a channel`, `Select a type`, `Select a priority`, `Search groups`, `Search agents`; Assignee no match `No agent in this group matches.`
- **Errors:** `Select the customer who asked, or add a new contact.`, `Enter the contact’s name.`, `Enter the contact’s email address.`, `Enter an email address such as name@example.com.`, `<entry> is not an email address. Fix it or remove it.`, `Enter a subject.`, `Describe what the customer needs.`
- **Attachments:** `Attach files`; the list is named `Attachments`.
- **Failure:** title `The ticket wasn't created.`, the page's message, `Retry`.
- **Success:** `Ticket #4840 was created.`, the subject, `Open ticket`.
- **Commit:** `Cancel`, `Save and add another`, `Save`. The discard dialog uses the built-in `useUnsavedChanges` labels.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Landmarks: the creation header, then `main` holding a `form` named by the `Create Ticket` h1; the bands are h2s (Requester, Request, Assignment).
- Focus: on load the Requester search, with its list closed until the agent types or presses Arrow Down (the first invalid field instead when the form opens with messages); Tab runs header, then the fields in band order, then Cancel, Save and add another, Save. A create press with gaps moves focus to the first invalid field; after Save and add another, focus returns to Requester. Add new contact focuses Contact name; Search contacts focuses the search.
- Each control takes its row title as `aria-label`, its error through `aria-describedby`, and `aria-invalid` once a create press finds a problem; the required rows carry the required mark and `aria-required`.
- Keyboard: ⌘ Enter (Ctrl Enter) creates from anywhere in the form, Escape cancels; the editor's own shortcuts are Ctrl/⌘ B, I and K.
- Announcements: the failure `Alert` is re-mounted after each attempt; the success toast is announced by the app's toast region; presence is spoken in the avatar's name, never the dot alone.
- Names and addresses keep their own direction (`dir="auto"`) on a right-to-left page; the rows stack below the row's container width, so the form reflows at 320 px.

## States

- Default: every field empty, the sample contacts, groups, agents and tags in the pickers, focus on Requester.
- ValidationErrors: `defaultSubmitted` with only a Subject and a CC entry that is not an address; Requester, Description and CC show their messages.
- ContactError: `defaultSubmitted` on a new contact whose email has no domain ending; Contact email, Subject and Description show their messages.
- Submitting: `submitting` on the filled sample ticket; Save spins and the form locks.
- SubmitError: `error` on the filled sample ticket; the danger Alert with Retry, every value kept.
- Success: `created` after Save and add another; the success toast with Open ticket and an empty form.
- Loading: `loading`; skeleton bands and disabled create buttons.
