# CreateWizard (`create/create-wizard`)

> The page a first-level resource is created on one step at a time, built on the `Wizard` component: the creation header, a page heading, then the Wizard with its step rail on the start side (completed steps reachable,…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-wizard/create-wizard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-wizard")`
- Components: Alert, AppHeader, `AppHeaderAccount`, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, ConfirmDialog, Field, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`, Hint, IconButton, Input, Item, PageHeader, RadioGroup, RadioGroup, Select, SettingsGroup, SettingsRow, Skeleton, Subheader, Switch, Tag, Textarea, Toast, ToggleGroup, `use-escape-to-cancel`, `use-shortcuts`, `use-unsaved-changes`, `utils/radio-list`, Wizard, Wizard
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

multipage create; multi-step create page; stepper create; create wizard; step by step form; criação em etapas; formulário em etapas; review step; review and create; confirm before create; wizard review; summary before submit; revisar; etapa de revisão; revisão antes de criar; review before create; summary step; revisar antes de criar; provision wizard; create service wizard; two-step wizard; create and deploy; bind domain and deployment; create resource in steps; assistente de criação; criar serviço; asistente de creación; crear en pasos

The page a first-level resource is created on one step at a time. It is the `Wizard` component in a creation page: the user first says where the resource runs, then answers each step's fields in order, and only reaches the create action on the last step. The Wizard's rail shows how far they are and lets them return to any step already passed; if the host they chose lacks a module the resource needs, a step is inserted that offers to turn it on, so nothing is created that would silently never be read. The same frame creates a resource that must be bound and deployed in one act (CreateAndDeploy).

## When to use

- Use create-wizard when a first-level resource is created in ordered steps (a later answer changes what is asked); it is the Wizard component in a creation page.
- A first-level resource whose fields fall into groups that make sense one at a time (general, then type, then entries) and where a later group depends on an earlier answer.
- The resource must first bind to a host (a policy, an application) and that choice can change what is asked next.
- A resource that is useless until it is bound to another and deployed, such as a service that serves a project on a domain: use the CreateAndDeploy variant, whose last action creates and deploys.
- A code resource whose editor needs a whole step to itself.

## When not to use

- Everything fits on one screen without order: use `create/create-page`.
- The resource is created inside another one: use `create/create-drawer`.
- A new project from a code source (Git, a template, an upload): start at `create/create-hub` and deploy with `create/create-deploy-template`.
- Binding an existing or new resource inside a form step: use `create/create-resource-picker`.
- Deploying an existing package from inside a resource: use `create/create-deploy-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `AppHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `AppHeaderAccount` (required)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Wizard — `Wizard`, `Wizard.Step` (required)
- D. Where it runs — `Input`, `Item`, `Tag`, `FieldError`, `Button` (required)
- E. Module step — `Card`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Switch` (conditional)
- F. Field steps — `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `FieldError` (required)
- G. Choice cards — `RadioGroup` (optional)
- H. Long entry — `Textarea`, `FieldError` (optional)
- I. Review — `Subheader`, `Alert`, `Card`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Button` (required)
- J. Create and deploy — `Card`, `Field`, `Input`, `Item`, `RadioGroup` (CreateAndDeploy)
- K. Leaving with typed work — `useUnsavedChanges`, `ConfirmDialog` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-wizard.md](blocks/create/create-wizard.md).

## Data

The block keeps the form as a local draft, validates each step and emits `submit` with the values; it sends no request. `CreateWizardPolicy`, `CreateWizardValues`, `CreateWizardSubmission` and `CreateWizardProps` are exported from `create-wizard.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample policies the chooser lists when `policies` is left out. The page owns the request: it sets `loading` while it runs, and on failure sets `error`, which the block shows in an error toast with Retry; on success the page shows the toast and opens the list.

Prop: `policies`, `defaultStep`, `defaultPolicy`, `defaultValues`, `loading`, `error`.

Event: `submit`, `cancel`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/create-wizard.md](blocks/create/create-wizard.md).

## Do

- Ask where the resource runs first, and insert the module step only when the chosen host needs it.
- Validate one step at a time in the `next` handler, and show the message under the field that failed.
- Keep Cancel apart from Previous and Next, on the opposite side; the Wizard footer does this.
- Keep the create action on the last step only; every step before it says Next.
- Keep the chosen host visible in the chooser even when it falls outside the first six.
- Label the final action with every act it performs: "Create and deploy" when it also deploys.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/shell-console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't build the rail, the step heading or the footer by hand; the `Wizard` owns them.
- Don't let the user skip ahead to steps not reached yet.
- Don't block the create when a module is off; warn, offer the switch and let the user go on.
- Don't repeat the step title as a second heading inside the card.
- Don't validate fields of later steps, or judge a field while it is being typed.
- Don't put a required field inside Advanced, or show both the existing list and the new fields at once.

## Copy

- **Title, breadcrumb and last submit:** the create label with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Access List"; "Create and deploy" when the last step also deploys.
- **Step titles:** short nouns, e.g. "Where it runs", "General", "List settings", "Project", "Domain and deployment".
- **Step descriptions:** one sentence with a period, e.g. "Select the policy whose rules match it. It needs IP filtering on."
- **Chooser:** the search placeholder and `aria-label` name what is searched, e.g. "Search policies"; Next with no answer says "Select a policy, or continue without one."
- **Module tag:** the missing module and its state, e.g. "IP filtering off".
- **Module alert:** the consequence in one sentence, e.g. "acme-staging has IP filtering off, so no rule reads this list until the module is on."
- **Escape routes:** verb first, e.g. "Create a policy", "Continue without a policy".
- **Required message:** "This field is required.", or what to do, e.g. "Select the project this service serves, or create a new one."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: "Select", never "Choose"; no em dash; no "simply".

## Accessibility

- **Escape on the page = Cancel.** `useEscapeToCancel(onCancel)` runs the same path as the Wizard's Cancel, in every step and in CreateAndDeploy: a clean form leaves at once, an edited one opens the Unsaved changes dialog. It stays inert while the create request is in flight, while an IME is composing, when another handler already used the key, while a menu, listbox, popover, tooltip or dialog is open (the open Select or DatePicker closes first, and Escape on the Unsaved changes dialog only keeps editing) and when focus is in a control that uses Escape itself (an open combobox, a search field). Edit and settings pages are places, not tasks: Escape stays inert there.
- **The page opens with the cursor in the first field of its step** (Search policies, the checked choice, or the Project choice in CreateAndDeploy).
- **⌘ Enter runs the Wizard's primary button (`Ctrl Enter` off Apple):** Next with the same step check, Create Access List or Create and deploy on the last step. It fires from any field, a textarea included, stays inert while the create request is in flight and is listed in the `?` dialog as Next step or the create action.
- The `Wizard` takes an `aria-label` naming the flow; locked rail steps cannot be focused or activated, and focus moves to the new step's heading on every step change.
- The page has one `h1` (the `PageHeader`); each step heading is an `h2` drawn by the Wizard.
- Host rows are native `button`s with `role="radio"` and `aria-checked` inside one named `radiogroup`, so a screen reader hears "radio, 1 of 5, checked"; the chooser's search has an `aria-label` and Enter selects the first match.
- Choice cards are a `RadioGroup` named with `aria-label`; each `RadioGroup.Item` is labelled by its card.
- Required messages are tied to their control with `aria-describedby`; focus stays on the step after a failed Next.
- Step transitions honour reduced motion.

## States

- WhereItRuns: the first step (the default `defaultStep`); the chooser of policies with search, module tags and the two escape routes.
- ModuleOff: acme-staging was chosen with IP filtering off (`defaultStep="module"`, `defaultPolicy="acme-staging"`), so the IP filtering step shows the warning, the switch card and the note.
- ListSettings: the settings step (`defaultStep="settings"`, a `defaultPolicy` and a Name in `defaultValues`); Type as radio choice cards and the List textarea, with Previous and Next (Review follows). Next with an empty list stays and shows the message.
- Review: the last step (`defaultStep="review"` with a `defaultPolicy` and `defaultValues`), read-only, with the create action in the footer. Where it runs is one `Alert` whose severity says whether anything will read the resource; What gets created lists each value under its plain label (never the API property name) and shows long lists as their first five `Tag`s and a count; What can reference it names the consumers. Each band that maps to a step has an outlined Edit (`aria-label` names the band) that jumps back to that step. Create re-validates every step and, on a failure, opens the first step with an error; on success it emits `submit`, `loading` spins it and `error` raises the error toast with Retry.
- CreateAndDeploy: Create Service on its Project step with the paged project list; Next is gated on the project, and step two ends on Create and deploy with its loading state. Cancel and Back to Services emit `cancel`, asking first once anything is answered.

## Review step

- Add a Review step when the create has three or more steps or binds the resource to something; skip it for a one-step create.
- Show values as they will be sent, under plain labels (no API property names or dotted paths), and never show secrets in clear.
- Put Edit on each band, and on a value whose step differs from its band's (Name, on General); after the edit, Next walks forward through the later steps, already filled, back to Review.
- Say plainly when nothing will read the resource yet (unbound, or a module off) with a warning `Alert`, not a disabled create.

## Related

- `Wizard` — the component this block is built on; see `skills/webkit-form`.
- `create/create-page` — the same job when the fields fit one screen.
- `create/create-hub` and `create/create-deploy-template` — a new project from Git, a template or an upload.
- `create/create-resource-picker` — the Existing or New band CreateAndDeploy binds its project with.
- `detail/detail-deployment-logs` — the build log Create and deploy hands the column to (InCreateFlow).
- `create/create-deploy-success` — the screen a create-and-deploy ends on.
- `edit/edit-function` — the editor a code resource can use as one step.
- `state/state-form-validation` — required and invalid states on Next.

- where-it-runs
- module
- general
- settings
- review

## Variants

`WhereItRuns` (primary) · `ModuleOff` · `ListSettings` · `Review` · `CreateAndDeploy`. Code: [blocks/create/create-wizard.md](blocks/create/create-wizard.md), `get_block("create/create-wizard", { variant })`.

# DashboardAlerts (`dashboard/dashboard-alerts`)

> An alerts dashboard: what is open, how severe it is, what kind it is and who is involved.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/dashboard-alerts/dashboard-alerts.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-alerts")`
- Components: Alert, BarList, Button, Card, Chart, ChartCard, DataTable, `DataTablePagination`, EmptyState, Hint, PageHeader, Select, SeverityTag, Skeleton, StatTile, `TableCellStatus`, Tag, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

alerts dashboard; open alerts; alerts by severity; incident dashboard; false positive rate; alert triage; painel de alertas; alertas abertos; alertas por severidade; triage open alerts

The page a security or operations lead opens to triage: what is open, how severe it is, what kind of
alert it is and which entities are involved. It leads with the open counts, shows how many alerts were
raised each day by severity, and ends in the open alerts table, ordered from critical to info, where
the reader picks what to work on next. Severity reads on one scale everywhere: tiles, chart, tags
and tables.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use dashboard-alerts to triage open alerts by severity.
- Alerts carry a severity level and the reader has to decide which to handle first.
- The reader needs both the trend (are we raising more?) and the queue (what is open now?) on one page.
- Alerts name entities (hosts, users, accounts) whose accumulated risk is worth ranking.

## When not to use

- Every request and the rule that decided it, not only alerts: use
  `dashboard/dashboard-security` (ByActor).
- Service health with latency and error thresholds and a short alert rail: use
  `dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring`.
- Items waiting for a verdict from an analysis engine: use `dashboard/dashboard-scan-results`.
- Only the list of alerts with filters: use `view/view-table`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Period — `Select` (required)
- C. Summary tiles — `StatTile` (required)
- D. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)
- E. Alerts per day — `ChartCard` (required)
- F. Daily stack — `Chart` (required)
- G. Open by severity — `Card` (required)
- H. Loading rows — `Skeleton` (required)
- I. Severity — `SeverityTag` (required)
- J. Empty regions — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- K. Alerts by type — `BarList` (required)
- L. Highest risk and Open alerts — `DataTable` (required)
- M. Alert status — `TableCellStatus`, `Tag` (required)
- N. Load failure — `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-alerts.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-alerts.md).

## Data

The block takes its figures and records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `AlertsDashboardProps` and the record types (`AlertsDashboardKpis`, `AlertsDashboardLevelCount`, `AlertsDashboardEntity`, `AlertsDashboardAlert`) are exported from `dashboard-alerts.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample period the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `kpis`, `labels`, `series`, `openByLevel`, `types`, `entities`, `alerts`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:period`.

Event: `retry`, `update:period`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-alerts.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-alerts.md).

## Do

- Use one severity ramp for every severity on the page, in the same order.
- Sort the open queue by severity first, then by age.
- Mark every count where growth is bad as `inverse`.
- Give each region its own empty state that says why it is empty.

## Don't

- Don't color severity with categorical series tokens, and don't use the severity ramp for anything else.
- Don't show a donut for open by severity; the reader needs exact counts.
- Don't add a per-card period selector.
- Don't collapse the page into one empty state when only some regions are empty; each region speaks for itself.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Alerts`.
- **Description:** one sentence on the page's job. `What is open, how severe it is, what kind it is and who is involved.`
- **Tile labels:** sentence case, no parentheses. `Critical or high open`, `False positives`.
- **Hint:** one sentence definition ending with a period. `Alerts nobody has closed yet, at any severity.`
- **Empty states:** state the fact, then the next step. `No alerts in this period` / `Nothing was raised in the last 30 days. Select a longer period.`, with the chosen period named in the sentence
- **Severity labels:** the level only. `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info`.

## Accessibility

- The period `Select` has `aria-label="Period"`; the tile row is a region labelled `Summary`.
- Severity is always a word in the `SeverityTag`, never a color alone; the chart tooltip lists every level by name.
- Counts and shares use `tabular-nums`.
- The `BarList` carries an `aria-label` naming what it ranks.

## States

- Default: the populated page for the selected period (`v-model:period`).
- Loading: `loading` is set; tiles, chart, bar list and both tables render their own `Skeleton`; Open by severity holds Skeleton rows.
- Empty: a period with no alerts (`kpis` is `{}` and every list is `[]`); tiles show a dash with no delta, and every region keeps its box with an `EmptyState` that says why and what to do next.
- Error: `error` is set; one danger `Alert` under the heading names what did not load, carries the message and offers Retry; tiles show a dash over a quiet band and every region keeps its header over `Not available.`

## Related

- `dashboard/dashboard-security` (ByActor) — every request and its outcome, not only alerts.
- `dashboard/dashboard-security` — blocked traffic and the rules that block it.
- `dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring` — threshold alerts beside service health.
- `SeverityTag` — the one severity scale the page shares.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-alerts.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-alerts.md), `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-alerts", { variant })`.

# DashboardAnalytics (`dashboard/dashboard-analytics`)

> The analytics dashboard pattern: KPI tiles, charts and a table that all read the same period, so one change of range moves every region together: the Period Select in the PageHeader actions sets the comparison of ever…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/dashboard-analytics/dashboard-analytics.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-analytics")`
- Components: Alert, Chart, ChartCard, DataTable, `DataTablePagination`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Hint, IconButton, Input, Link, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelBody`, `PanelHeader`, Select, Spinner, StatTile, StatTileGroup, Tabs, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, `use-collection`, `use-locale`, `utils/clipboard`, `utils/csv`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

metrics; metric panel; kpi tiles; sparkline; real-time metrics; analytics dashboard; painel de métricas; indicadores; analytics; traffic analytics; requests over time; period comparison; painel analítico; análise de tráfego; real-time metrics per product; product metrics; metrics by product; period filter; métricas por produto; métricas en tiempo real; expand chart; chart dialog; export csv; copy query; metrics overview; metrics landing; sub-dashboards; status class filter; visão geral de métricas; data dashboard; metrics dashboard; kpi dashboard; stat tiles; data transferred; usage dashboard; usage per project; consumption; breakdown charts; métricas; painel de dados; painel de uso; traffic and usage dashboard

The page a developer or operator opens to see how much traffic their services handled and how well
they handled it: requests, data transferred, success rate and server errors for the period, then the
charts and the table that explain those totals. Every tile, chart and the table read the same period,
so one change of range moves every region together. It is the reference grammar for the other
dashboards: KPI row first, a 12-column grid of `ChartCard`s below, one shared card header.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use dashboard-analytics for KPI tiles, charts and a table over one shared period: Traffic (requests, status codes) by default, Usage for consumption per product or project.
- The reader monitors volume and quality of traffic (requests, bytes, status codes) over a period.
- Several metrics share one time window and one set of dimensions (host, country, status code).
- The reader needs to move from a total to the breakdown and then to the rows behind it.

## When not to use

- Latency percentiles and live service health with an alert rail: use
  `dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring`.
- Blocked and allowed requests and the rules behind them: use `dashboard/dashboard-security`.
- The reader arranges the cards themselves: use `dashboard/dashboard-configurable`.
- Money split by category over time: use `dashboard/dashboard-breakdown`.
- Real-user web vitals or one banded score: use `dashboard/dashboard-health-score`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading and period — `PageHeader`, `Select` (required)
- B. KPI row — `StatTileGroup`, `StatTile` (required)
- C. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)
- D. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- E. Aggregation and variation — `Tag` (required)
- F. Line or Bar — `ToggleGroup` (optional)
- G. Control labels — `Tooltip` (required)
- H. Expand — `IconButton`, `Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `PanelBody` (optional)
- I. More options — `DropdownMenu`, `toast` (optional)
- J. Charts — `Chart` (required)
- K. Table search — `Input` (optional)
- L. Top hosts — `DataTable` (required)
- M. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)
- N. Product and period — `PageHeader` (optional)
- O. Sub-dashboards and breakdowns — `ToggleGroup`, `Input`, `DataTable`, `EmptyState` (optional)
- P. Overview landing — `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (optional)
- Q. Usage — `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `DataTable`, `Hint`, `Input`, `EmptyState` (optional)
- R. Failure — `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-analytics.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-analytics.md).

## Data

The block takes its figures through props and emits its actions; it fetches nothing. `AnalyticsDashboardProps` and the record types (`AnalyticsDashboardKpis`, `AnalyticsDashboardCountry`, `AnalyticsDashboardHost`, `AnalyticsDashboardChanges`, `AnalyticsDashboardRange`) are exported from `dashboard-analytics.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample figures the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set). The tile labels, hints and formats, the card titles and the period options stay in the SFC.

Prop: `v-model:period`, `kpis`, `intervals`, `requestSeries`, `statusSeries`, `countries`, `hosts`, `changes`, `range`, `defaultExpanded`, `loading`, `error`, `refetching`.

Event: `update:period`, `retry`.

The queries the card menus copy run as-is against the Azion Real-Time Metrics API
(`POST /v4/metrics/graphql`). What the API expects, so a live page asks for the right shapes:

Card: Requests over time, Status codes, Requests by country, Top hosts.

- Every query takes `limit` and `filter: { tsRange: { begin, end } }`; an aggregate needs `groupBy`, and a ranked list orders by the aggregate (`sum_DESC`), never by the measured field (`requests_DESC` is rejected).
- Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC **without** the trailing `Z` (`2026-11-13T11:00:00`); the block strips a `Z` and milliseconds from `range` before it writes the query.
- `resample: { function: sum, points: 96 }` returns a fixed number of points for a time series, so a long period does not come back as thousands of rows.
- One query returns at most 10,000 rows (`limit: 10000`).
- Data transferred is `aggregate: { sum: bytesSent }`; the Functions product reads `functionsMetrics` (`sum: invocations`) and Edge DNS reads `idnsQueriesMetrics`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-analytics.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-analytics.md).

## Do

- Keep the KPI row to the four numbers the reader checks first; put the rest in cards.
- Use one card header layout for every card, so the controls are in the same place.
- Let one period drive every region.
- Keep the period when the product tab changes, so the reader compares products over the same window.
- Give each product the same grammar: four tiles, then cards of two per row.
- Distinguish "nothing recorded" from "nothing matches the search" in the empty copy.

## Don't

- Don't give a card its own period selector.
- Don't offer Line or Bar on a ranked breakdown; bars are the only form there.
- Don't put more than one search on the page header; table search belongs to its table.
- Don't use status colors for categorical series such as countries or hosts.
- Don't sum a rate or a percentile in a legend total; Metrics turns totals off for those cards.
- Don't nest product tabs inside a card; the product is a page-level choice.
- Don't put a product's sub-dashboard switch inside a card; it sits under the product tabs and changes the whole page.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Analytics`. **Description:** `Requests, data transferred and errors your services handled in the period.`
- **Card titles:** noun phrase, sentence case. `Requests over time`, `Status codes`, `Top hosts`.
- **Tile labels:** the metric name only. `Data transferred`, never `Data transferred (GB)`; the unit belongs to the value.
- **Hint:** one sentence ending with a period. `Requests that ended in a server error. A rise is a regression.`
- **Menu items:** verb first. `Copy query`, `Export CSV`.
- **Overview:** footer links read `Open <Product> dashboard`; breakdown searches name what they match (`Search addresses, networks or countries`).
- **Toasts:** `Query copied.` / `Paste it into any GraphQL client that sends your token.`; `The query could not be copied.`; `CSV exported.` with the file name.
- **Metrics:** title `Real-time metrics`; tab labels are product names; the aggregation names the math in muted text (`Sum`, `Median`, `Percentile`).
- **Usage:** title `Data usage`, description `What your projects consumed in the period, against the previous period.`; card titles say what is compared (`Data transferred, this period vs previous`); series `This period`, `Previous period`.
- **Empty state:** `No traffic yet` / `Metrics appear here once a service serves requests.`
- **No-match state:** `No matching rows` / `Change the search.`

## Accessibility

- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` that names its card, plus a `Tooltip`.
- The expanded `Dialog` traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus to the Expand button; its title and description name the card.
- The `ToggleGroup` is labelled with the card it controls.
- The search `Input` has an `aria-label` equal to its placeholder, since there is no visible label.
- Figures use `tabular-nums`; deltas carry a sign and a word, not color alone.
- The product strip is a tab list (`PageTabs`); the region under it is named after the product and the period (`Functions metrics, Last 24 hours`).
- Charts expose their table twin and keyboard model through `Chart`; do not replace them with a bare SVG.

## States

- Default: the populated dashboard for the period (`kpis`, `intervals`, `requestSeries`, `statusSeries`, `countries`, `hosts`, `changes`).
- Loading: `loading`; every tile, chart and the table hold their place with a `Skeleton`; the grid does not reflow.
- Refetching: `refetching`; the period reloads (a new period, a Refresh) over figures already shown: the tiles, charts and table keep their data and every chart holds its previous render at reduced opacity until the new figures arrive. Use `loading` only for the first response.
- Empty: `kpis` is `{}` and the series and rows are `[]`; no traffic in the period, tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and each card keeps its box with an `EmptyState`.
- Metrics: real-time metrics per product, a `PageTabs` strip of products and a `Period` `Select` in the header; each product shows four tiles and four area, line or stacked bar cards, and products with sub-dashboards switch them with a `ToggleGroup`, adding breakdown table cards.
- Expanded: `defaultExpanded="requests"`; the Requests over time card open in the large `Dialog`, with the Line or Bar choice and a 420px plot.
- MetricsOverview: six cross-product tiles and six highlight cards, each with a footer link to its product dashboard.
- Usage: the Data usage page, consumption per meter and per project against the previous period.
- Error: `error` is set; one danger `Alert` under the heading names what did not load, carries the message and offers Retry; tiles show a dash over a quiet band and every region keeps its header over `Not available.`

- `account/account-change-plan-drawer` — where usage limits are changed.

# DashboardBreakdown (`dashboard/dashboard-breakdown`)

> A composition dashboard: how a total breaks down into its parts and how that mix moved over time, here the organization’s monthly spend by category.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/dashboard-breakdown/dashboard-breakdown.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-breakdown")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Chart, ChartCard, DataTable, DonutChart, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Hint, IconButton, PageHeader, Progress, Select, StatTile, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, `use-locale`, `utils/csv`

## Asked as

composition dashboard; spend breakdown; cost by category; donut chart dashboard; stacked area chart; top contributors; mix over time; painel de composição; gastos por categoria; custos por categoria; total by category over time; spend by category

The page that answers "what is this total made of, and how did the mix move?". The block's example is
the organization's monthly spend: the total and its three largest categories first, then the mix over
12 months, the current month's split, and the resources that drive it, ranked. The same shape fits any
total that breaks down into exclusive parts (storage by type, requests by product, seats by team).

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use dashboard-breakdown when a total breaks into categories over time.
- One total splits into a small number of exclusive categories (up to six, plus Other).
- The reader needs both the current split and how it changed over time.
- The reader has to find the individual items that drive the largest share.

## When not to use

- The parts are not exclusive or do not sum to the total: use a multi-series line in
  `dashboard/dashboard-analytics` instead of a stack or a donut.
- The reader tracks progress against targets: use `dashboard/dashboard-executive-summary`.
- Changing the plan that drives the spend: use `account/account-change-plan-drawer`.

- K. Current split — `DonutChart` (required)

- P. Load failure — `Alert` (required)

## Do

- Keep the category order and colors identical across tiles, stacked chart, donut and table.
- Put the total first in the tile row, then the parts.
- Show a percentage next to every share bar.
- Mark spend tiles as `inverse`.

## Don't

- Don't use a donut for more than six slices; fold the tail into Other.
- Don't stack series that overlap or do not sum to the total.

## Copy

- **Empty state:** `No spend in this range` / `Nothing was billed to the organization in the selected period.`

- The donut has an `aria-label` (`Current split`) and its legend lists every category with its value.
- Each `Progress` names its resource; the percentage is visible text, not only the bar.
- Amounts and shares use `tabular-nums`.

## States

# DashboardConfigurable (`dashboard/dashboard-configurable`)

> A configurable dashboard: the reader arranges the cards.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/dashboard-configurable/dashboard-configurable.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-configurable")`
- Components: Alert, BarList, Button, Chart, ChartCard, DashboardGrid, DonutChart, EmptyState, Hint, IconButton, PageHeader, Tag, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-layout`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

configurable dashboard; custom dashboard; drag and drop dashboard; resizable cards; edit layout; dashboard-grid; dashboard grid; dashboard builder; painel configurável; painel personalizado; reorganizar cards; rearrange cards; resize dashboard cards

A dashboard the reader arranges: they move cards, change how many columns a card spans and how tall it
is, and keep that layout. It serves readers who come back to the same page every day and care about
different cards than the default puts first. The page owns the layout (an array of id, span and
height, in order) and binds it to `DashboardGrid`, which moves, resizes, clamps and announces; the
`ChartCard` inside each `DashboardGrid.Item` provides the drag handle and the resize corner.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use dashboard-configurable only when each reader rearranges and resizes the cards.
- The same dashboard serves readers with different priorities, and each comes back often.
- The cards are independent: none depends on its position to make sense.
- The product has somewhere to store per-user preferences.

## When not to use

- A dashboard read once to answer one question, or one whose order tells a story: use a static
  dashboard such as `dashboard/dashboard-analytics` or
  `dashboard/dashboard-executive-summary`.
- The reader needs to add or remove widgets from a palette; this block only rearranges and resizes the
  cards it has.
- A single chart with editable settings: use `ChartCard` alone.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Edit layout, Done and Reset layout — `Button` (required)
- C. Grid — `DashboardGrid` (required)
- D. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- E. Card definitions — `Hint` (required)
- F. Span while editing — `Tag` (required in edit mode)
- G. Split cards — `DonutChart` (optional)
- H. Ranked cards — `BarList` (optional)
- I. Time series cards — `Chart` (optional)
- J. Load failure — `Alert` (required)
- K. Move up and Move down — `IconButton` (required in edit mode on one column)
- L. Empty dashboard — `EmptyState` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-configurable.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-configurable.md).

## Data

The block takes its series through props and emits every change; it fetches nothing. `ConfigurableDashboardProps` and `ConfigurableDashboardSeries` are exported from `dashboard-configurable.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample period the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set). The layout is a model, so the page can save it per user.

Prop: `labels`, `series`, `sources`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:layout`, `v-model:editing`.

Event: `retry`, `update:layout`, `update:editing`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-configurable.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-configurable.md).

## Do

- Keep the layout as data (id, span, height, order) owned by the page, bind it to `DashboardGrid`, and persist
  it wherever the product stores preferences.
- Give every `DashboardGrid.Item` the card title as its `label`; it is what moves and resizes announce.
- Announce a reset yourself in a polite live region (`Layout reset to the default.`); the board
  announces only what it did.
- Keep every card at its place and size in loading and partly empty states, so the reader can arrange it
  before data arrives.

## Don't

- Don't show handles outside edit mode; a dashboard that can be dragged by accident is worse than a static one.
- Don't let a card shrink below a span where its content stops reading (3 columns here).
- Don't put card menus, toggles or exports in the header; they conflict with the drag handle.
- Don't hide Reset layout behind a menu once the layout is customized.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Traffic overview`. **Description:** `Requests, regions, errors and response time for the period, in the layout you set.`
- **Mode button:** `Edit layout`, then `Done`. Never `Save`; changes apply as they happen.
- **Reset:** `Reset layout`.
- **Help line:** two short sentences on how, no layout positions. `Drag a card by its handle to move it, or by its corner to resize it. Focus a handle to use the arrow keys.`
- **Handle labels:** verb plus card title. `Move Requests over time`, `Resize Requests over time`.
- **Announcements:** full sentences with a period. `Layout reset to the default.`
- **Empty state:** `No requests yet` / `Metrics appear here once a service serves requests.` for one card; the page-level one says what fills the page and offers Create Application.

## Accessibility

- The drag handle moves a card with the arrow keys; the resize corner changes span with Left and Right and height with Up and Down (`DashboardGrid` handles both and mirrors them under right-to-left).
- Focus returns to the moved card's handle after a reorder.
- `DashboardGrid` announces every move and resize in its own polite live region; the page announces the reset in an `aria-live="polite"` `sr-only` region.
- The board is a list named `Traffic overview cards`, one item per card.
- `Edit layout` exposes its mode with `aria-pressed`.
- Charts carry an `aria-label` equal to the card title.

## States

- Default: the arranged dashboard, read-only (`v-model:layout`).
- Editing: `v-model:editing` is `true`; handles and resize corners on every card, span tags in the headers, help line visible.
- Loading: `loading` is set; every chart renders its own `Skeleton` inside its card; the layout holds its shape.
- Empty: nothing recorded yet (`series` is `{}`, `sources` is `[]`); one bordered page-level `EmptyState` (`No requests yet`, with Create Application as the next step) replaces the grid and the layout controls, instead of the same empty state in every card. A card left empty while others have data keeps its place and size and shows its own empty state.
- Error: `error` is set; one danger `Alert` under the heading names what did not load, carries the message and offers Retry; tiles show a dash over a quiet band and every region keeps its header over `Not available.`

## Related

- `dashboard/dashboard-analytics` — the static version of the same cards.
- `dashboard/dashboard-analytics` — a fixed dashboard when the order tells the story.
- `DashboardGrid` — the grid component: layout model, bounds, reorder, resize and announcements.
- `ChartCard` — the card inside each item, with the drag handle and resize corner.

- M. Notes — `Item` (required)

The block takes its figures and records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `ExecutiveSummaryDashboardProps` and the record types (`ExecutiveSummaryDashboardKpis`, `ExecutiveSummaryDashboardGoal`, `ExecutiveSummaryDashboardTrends`, `ExecutiveSummaryDashboardNote`) are exported from `dashboard-executive-summary.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample quarter the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

## Do

- Keep every trend card the same size and form so shapes compare.
- Show the target next to the current value for every goal; a bar alone hides the gap.
- Use status words for goals (`On track`, `At risk`, `Off track`), with color as reinforcement.
- Link from each metric to the dashboard that explains it, when one exists.

## Don't

- Don't add more than about six scorecard tiles; the page is read, not explored.
- Don't give trend cards different periods or sizes.
- Don't mark growth metrics `inverse`; only cost and error style metrics read a rise as bad.
- Don't leave commentary empty without saying who fills it.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Executive summary`.
- **Description:** `Headline results for the quarter, progress on its goals, twelve-month trends and notes from the leads.`
- **Tile labels:** spelled-out metric, acronyms uppercase. `Net revenue retention`, `NPS`.
- **Goal status:** two words at most. `On track`, `At risk`, `Off track`.
- **Empty states:** name the period. `No goal results for Q3` / `Progress appears once the quarter reports its first month.`

## Accessibility

- The quarter `Select` trigger has `aria-label="Quarter"`; tiles and trends are regions labelled `Scorecard` and `Trends`.
- Each goal `Progress` has an `aria-label` with the goal name; current and target are visible text.
- Goal status is a word in a `Tag`, never color alone.
- Figures use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: the reported quarter (`v-model:quarter`).
- Loading: `loading` is set; tiles and charts render their own `Skeleton`; goals and commentary hold Skeleton rows.
- Empty: a quarter with nothing reported (`kpis` and `trends` are `{}`, `goals` and `notes` are `[]`); tiles show a dash with no delta, and one page-level `EmptyState` names the quarter and offers the next later one in place of the trend cards, goals and commentary.
- Error: `error` is set; one danger `Alert` under the heading names what did not load, carries the message and offers Retry; tiles show a dash over a quiet band and every region keeps its header over `Not available.`

## Related

- `dashboard/dashboard-breakdown` — where a cost metric breaks down.
- `dashboard/dashboard-analytics` — the detail behind a traffic metric.

# DashboardHealthScore (`dashboard/dashboard-health-score`)

> A health score dashboard: how well something performs for the people who use it, read as one score out of 100 and its bands.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/dashboard-health-score/dashboard-health-score.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-health-score")`
- Components: Alert, BarList, Card, Chart, ChartCard, EmptyState, Hint, Item, PageHeader, Select, Skeleton, StatTile, Tag, Tracker, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

health score; health dashboard; performance score; web vitals; score bands; quality score; pontuação de saúde; painel de saúde; nota de desempenho; real user monitoring; rum; core web vitals; page load time; monitoramento de usuário real; banded score

The page that answers "how well does this work for the people who use it, and where is it worst?".
Experience is reduced to one score out of 100 with three bands (Good at 80 or more, Fair from 50 to 79,
Poor under 50). The page shows the overall score and its trend, ranks applications and locations
lowest first with the top cause of poor samples, gives each application an hour-by-hour strip, and ends
in the open incidents that need someone's attention.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use dashboard-health-score when many signals roll up into one banded score (including real-user web vitals).
- Many raw signals (latency, packet loss, DNS time, Wi-Fi signal) are combined into one score the
  reader can act on.
- The score has fixed bands that mean the same thing everywhere on the page.
- The reader's job is to find the worst application or place and the cause behind it.

## When not to use

- The raw metrics themselves (p50, p95, error rate) matter more than a score: use
  `dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring`.
- A pass or fail verdict per item: use `dashboard/dashboard-scan-results`.
- Alerts triaged by severity: use `dashboard/dashboard-alerts`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Period — `Select` (required)
- C. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- D. Definitions — `Hint` (required)
- E. Overall figure — `Skeleton` (required)
- F. Band — `Tag` (required)
- G. Loading placeholders — `Skeleton` (required)
- H. Score per hour — `Chart` (required)
- I. Rankings — `BarList` (required)
- J. Hourly strips — `Tracker` (required)
- K. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)
- L. Open incidents — `Card` (required)
- M. Incident rows — `Item` (required)
- N. Real-user monitoring — `PageHeader`, `Select`, `StatTile`, `Hint` (optional)
- O. Load failure — `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-health-score.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-health-score.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `HealthScoreOverall`, `HealthScoreHourlyRow`, `HealthScoreIncident`, `HealthScoreBand`, `HealthScorePeriod` and `HealthScoreDashboardProps` are exported from `dashboard-health-score.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample score, rankings, hourly rows and incidents the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set). The RealUser variant is a separate page and keeps its own sample figures.

Prop / model: `overall`, `applications`, `locations`, `hourly`, `incidents`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:period`.

Event: `retry`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-health-score.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-health-score.md).

## Do

- Use the same three bands, with the same thresholds and words, in every region.
- Sort rankings lowest first.
- Name the top cause next to every poor score, so the reader knows what to fix.
- State the band thresholds in the overall `Hint`.

## Don't

- Don't show a score without its band word.
- Don't use the status colors for anything other than the bands on this page.
- Don't average away the worst hour; the hourly strip exists to show it.
- Don't sort rankings best first.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Experience score`.
- **Band words:** one word each. `Good`, `Fair`, `Poor`.
- **Cause:** subject, a middle dot, the cause in lowercase. `CRM · slow DNS lookups`.
- **RealUser:** title `Real-user monitoring`, description `Real-user timings collected in the browser, for the selected period.`; tile labels are the timing in sentence case (`First input delay`); the aside of a trend tile is the period name (`Last 24 hours`).
- **Empty state:** name the period. `No open incidents in the last 24 hours` / `An incident opens when an application or a location stays poor for several samples in a row.`

## Accessibility

- Each `Tracker` has an `aria-label` naming its application, and each block a label with time, score and band.
- Bands are always words; the strip is never color alone.
- Rankings carry an `aria-label` (`Score per application`, `Score per location`).
- Loading regions set `aria-busy="true"`.
- Scores use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: the scored period.
- Loading: `loading`; the chart, rankings and trackers render their own `Skeleton`; incidents hold Skeleton rows.
- Empty: a period with no samples (`overall.score: null`, every list `[]`); the score shows a dash with no band, and every region keeps its box with an empty state that names the period and says what fills it.
- RealUser: the real-user monitoring page; the vitals and the trend tiles follow the Period select.
- Error: `error` is set; one danger `Alert` under the heading names what did not load, carries the message and offers Retry; tiles show a dash over a quiet band and every region keeps its header over `Not available.`

## Related

# DashboardHome (`dashboard/dashboard-home`)

> The whole Home page body, in both of its states.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/dashboard-home/dashboard-home.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-home")`
- Components: Alert, `claudeMark`, `codexMark`, `cursorMark`, `geminiMark`, Button, Card, DataTable, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem`, EmptyState, Hint, IconButton, Illustration, Input, Item, Item, Link, Popover, SearchTrigger, Skeleton, Spinner, StatTile, StatTileGroup, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellLink`, `TableCellTime`, Tag, ThirdPartyLogo, Toast, Tooltip, `use-console-layout`
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

home; home page; home dashboard; console home; usage overview; página inicial; início do console; first access; home empty state; new account home; welcome screen; first run; brand-new account; getting started home; primeiro acesso; tela de boas-vindas; home vazia; classic overview; overview dashboard; account summary; recent activity; monthly usage; visão geral; account landing overview

The Console's Home page: the first screen a signed-in user lands on. Its job
is to get them back to work fast. For an account that owns resources it shows a short usage band and
the resources they touch most (projects, resources, domains, recents), every row a link. For a
brand-new account it becomes the first-access screen: a greeting, the command prompt and three doors
to a first project, a first domain and a coding agent. It is not an analytics page; detail lives on
each resource's own dashboard.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header, the search palette and the `main`. The populated Home fits the screen at `xl` (each resource panel scrolls its own rows), so its root carries `data-layout-fill` and scrolls itself (`overflow-y-auto`): below `xl` the root scrolls as one page, its content centred while it fits (`justify-center-safe`). The first-access screen (Empty) is a centred page with nothing pinned; it does not fill, and the layout's `main` scrolls it (`h-dvh` on the populated root only sizes a standalone preview).

## When to use

- Use dashboard-home for the account's landing overview.
- The landing page after sign-in in the Console.
- The reader needs to resume work (open a recent resource) more than to analyse data.
- The same page must serve both a populated and a brand-new account.

## When not to use

- Analysing traffic or usage: use `dashboard/dashboard-analytics`
  (Traffic by default, Usage for consumption).
- The empty first page of one resource list: use `state/state-first-use`.
- Only the shell, with another page inside: use `shell/shell-console`.
- A placeholder while Home loads: use the Overview and Onboarding wires of `state/state-page-skeleton`.

## Building blocks

- A. Control labels — `Tooltip` (required)
- B. Icon-only controls — `IconButton` (required)
- C. Usage band — `StatTileGroup`, `StatTile`, `Hint` (required)
- D. Agent onboarding — `Card`, `Item`, `ThirdPartyLogo` (optional)
- E. Resource rows — `Item`, `Link`, `EmptyState` (required)
- F. Failure — `Alert` (required)
- G. Classic summary — `StatTile`, `Card`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (optional)
- H. Loading — `Skeleton` (required)
- I. First access — `SearchTrigger`, `Card`, `Illustration`, `Button`, `Input`, `Popover`, `Spinner` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-home.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-home.md).

## Data

The block takes its figures and rows through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `HomeDashboardProps` and the record types (`HomeDashboardMetrics`, `HomeDashboardResource`, `HomeDashboardDomainAvailability`) are exported from `dashboard-home.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample name, figures and rows the block renders when a prop is left out (the figures and rows never while `loading` or `error` is set). The tile labels, units and hints and the panel headings stay in the SFC.

Prop: `userName`, `greeting`, `metrics`, `projects`, `resources`, `domains`, `recents`, `domainAvailability`, `v-model:agent-setup`, `loading`, `error`.

Pass `[]` for all four lists on an account that owns nothing: the page becomes the first-access screen.

Event: `retry`, `update:agentSetup`, `create-project`, `check-domain`, `register-domain`, `copy-prompt`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-home.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-home.md).

## Do

- Greet by first name in a muted heading; it is the only personal line on the page.
- Make every resource row a single link (`Item` with `href`) and keep row actions on the resource's page.
- Let the user dismiss the agent card for good.
- Show the first-access screen, not a grid of empty panels, when the account owns nothing.
- Open the layout's palette from the first-access prompt with `useConsoleLayout({ optional: true })` and `layout?.openSearch()` (the body also renders alone, in its preview and test, where the call returns `null`); never wrap `useConsoleLayout()` in `try` / `catch`, and never mount a second `Command`.
- Mark the populated page root with `data-layout-fill` and let it scroll, so the panels scroll their rows at `xl` and the page scrolls as one below it.

## Don't

- Don't add charts to Home; link to the dashboard that has them.
- Don't put more than four usage tiles in the band.
- Don't hand-build the band's card, grid or dividers around the tiles; `StatTileGroup` draws them.
- Don't pass figures as strings or flags as `'true'` / `'false'`: a tile's `value` and `delta` are
  numbers, and the string `'false'` is truthy.
- Don't nest the dismiss button inside the card's link.
- Don't show a second highlighted button next to `Agent`.

## Copy

- **Greeting:** time of day and first name. `Good morning, Alex`.
- **Tile labels:** the metric in sentence case. `Data transferred`, `Requests per second`.
- **Tile tooltips:** one sentence with a period. `Total bytes delivered across all your resources.`
- **Agent card:** imperative title plus one sentence. `Set up your coding agent` / `Give your editor a prompt that teaches it to build and deploy here.`
- **Empty panel:** `No <things> yet` with one sentence (`Domains you create show up here.`); Recents: `Nothing opened yet`.
- **Failure:** `Couldn't load <thing>. Check your connection and retry.` with Retry.
- **Prompt label:** `Search resources, pages and commands`.
- **Summary:** section headings `Metrics`, `Resources`, `Recent activity`; card titles `Monthly usage`, `Marketplace trends`; footer links `View all <thing>` in sentence case (`View all DNS zones`).

## Accessibility

- The usage band is labelled `Usage` and the panels `Resources`; the layout owns the header, the rail and the one `main`.
- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` and a `Tooltip`.
- Every resource row is one link in the tab order; its focus ring is the row's.
- On a new account the prompt opens the layout's command palette, which also opens with ⌘K / Ctrl K.
- Entrance animations and the card's dismiss transition honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- Default: populated Home for an account that owns resources (`metrics`, `projects`, `resources`, `domains`, `recents`): usage band, agent card, resource panels.
- Error: `error` is set; one danger `Alert` under the heading names what did not load, carries the message and offers Retry; tiles show a dash over a quiet band and every region keeps its header over `Not available.`
- Empty: `projects`, `resources`, `domains` and `recents` are all `[]`; a brand-new account gets the first-access screen with the greeting, the command prompt that opens the palette, and the three doors (create a project, add a domain with an availability check, set up an agent).
- Summary: the classic overview; metric tiles with the window caption, the resources and recent activity tables, and the aside with monthly usage and a featured marketplace template.

## Related

- `shell/shell-console` — the shell Home renders inside.
- `state/state-page-skeleton` — the Overview and Onboarding wires that hold Home while it loads.
- `state/state-first-use` — the state-first-use state of one resource list.
- `dashboard/dashboard-analytics` — where usage detail lives.

## Variants

## Asked as

scan results; scan dashboard; analysis verdicts; malware scan; flagged items; submissions in analysis; resultados da análise; painel de varredura; itens sinalizados; waiting for a verdict; asynchronous analysis results

The page for a pipeline that sends items (files, attachments, packages) for analysis and gives each a
verdict. The reader checks what was submitted, what is still waiting, what was flagged, and above all
two exceptions: deliveries held until a verdict arrives, and items that were delivered before they

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `SecuritySummary`, `SecurityMetric`, `SecurityMatchedRequests`, `SecuritySourceIp`, `SecurityAttentionEntry`, `SecurityCardChanges`, `SecurityPeriodRange`, `SecurityPeriod`, `SecurityCardId` and `SecurityDashboardProps` are exported from `dashboard-security.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample figures, series, breakdowns, IPs and attention entries the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set). Export CSV and Copy query run in the browser on the data the block holds. The ByActor variant is a separate page and keeps its own sample log.

Prop / model: `summary`, `matchedRequests`, `categories`, `countries`, `sourceIps`, `attention`, `changes`, `range`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:period`.

Every region empty (`[]` lists and no series) is the no-rule-set state: one `EmptyState` with `Add rule set` replaces the grid.

Event: `retry`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-security.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-security.md).

## Do

- End every Needs attention entry with exactly one action.
- Mark blocking metrics as `inverse`.
- Replace the grid with one setup empty state when no rule exists; empty charts would only repeat it.
- Keep the attention list short; it is a queue, not a log.

## Don't

- Don't use the danger color for a categorical breakdown such as countries.
- Don't put more than one action on an attention entry.
- Don't show the full grid of empty charts when the cause is a missing rule set.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Security`. **Description:** `Requests your rules blocked and inspected, and the settings that need a decision.`
- **Attention title:** the problem as a statement. `Service without a rule set`.
- **Attention description:** one sentence of evidence with a figure. `SQL injection against the API rose 64% in the last hour.`
- **Attention action:** verb first. `Review rules`, `Attach a rule set`.
- **Kind tag:** two words at most. `Log only`, `Spike`, `No rules`.
- **ByActor:** title `Request activity`, description `What each actor requested through the rules and what the rules decided.`; outcome tags are one past participle (`Allowed`, `Blocked`, `Held`); no match `No requests match these filters` / `Clear the filters or pick other values.`
- **Setup empty state:** `No security rules protect your services` / `Security metrics and the Needs attention list appear once a rule set protects a service.`, action `Add rule set`.

## Accessibility

- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` that names its card, plus a `Tooltip`.
- The search `Input` has an `aria-label` equal to its placeholder.
- The expanded `Dialog` traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus to the Expand button.
- Severity is a word in the `Tag`, not color alone.
- Figures use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: rules in place, populated tiles, charts, attention list and table.
- Loading: `loading`; every tile, chart and the table hold a `Skeleton`; Needs attention shows three placeholder rows.
- Empty: no rule set yet (every list `[]`, tiles with `null` values); tiles read as dashes and one bordered `EmptyState` offers `Add rule set` instead of a grid of empty charts.
- ByActor: request activity per actor with the rule that decided each request; NoMatch is a state of it.
- Error: `error` is set; one danger `Alert` under the heading names what did not load, carries the message and offers Retry; tiles show a dash over a quiet band and every region keeps its header over `Not available.`

## Related

- `dashboard/dashboard-alerts` — the alert queue raised by these rules.
- `dashboard/dashboard-scan-results` — verdicts from an asynchronous analysis.
- `view/view-table` — the request log on its own, as a filterable list page.
- `edit/edit-rule-builder` — where a rule set is edited.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Error` · `ByActor`. Code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-security.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-security.md), `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-security", { variant })`.

# DashboardServiceMonitoring (`dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring`)

> The service monitoring dashboard pattern: a PageHeader with the one window ToggleGroup, status tiles with sparklines, multi-series charts and an alert rail.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring/dashboard-service-monitoring.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring")`
- Components: Alert, Chart, ChartCard, EmptyState, Hint, Item, Link, PageHeader, Skeleton, StatTile, StatusIndicator, Tag, ToggleGroup, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

service monitoring; monitoring dashboard; latency p95; error rate; uptime; service health; observability; monitoramento; painel de monitoramento; latência; latency percentiles; error rate per service

The page an on-call engineer keeps open: is every service up, how fast is it answering, how many
requests fail, and which alerts are open right now. One tile per service states its p95 latency and
its state in words; latency percentiles and error rates sit in two charts read over one window; the
open alerts live in a rail on the right that scrolls on its own, so the alerts stay in view while the
reader studies a chart.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`. Its root carries `data-layout-fill`, so the layout's `main` stops scrolling and the root fills it: from `xl` the charts column and the alerts rail scroll on their own; below `xl` the root itself scrolls, so the page still scrolls as one (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview).

## When to use

- Use dashboard-service-monitoring for latency percentiles, error rates and live state per service.
- The reader watches a known set of services for state changes and threshold breaches.
- Latency percentiles and error rates matter more than volume.
- Open alerts need to stay visible next to the evidence.

## When not to use

- Volume and status codes over a longer period: use `dashboard/dashboard-analytics`.
- Alert triage by severity with a full queue and trends: use `dashboard/dashboard-alerts`.
- One experience score with bands: use `dashboard/dashboard-health-score`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading and window — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Service tiles — `StatTile` (required)
- C. Service state — `StatusIndicator` (required)
- D. Charts — `ChartCard` (required)
- E. Definitions — `Hint` (required)
- F. Window — `ToggleGroup` (required)
- G. Latency and error rate — `Chart` (required)
- H. Alert level — `Tag` (required)
- I. Loading placeholders — `Skeleton` (required)
- J. Alert rail — `Item` (required)
- K. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)
- L. Load failure — `Alert` (required)
- M. Jump to the open alerts — `Link` (required below `xl`)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `ServiceMonitoringService`, `ServiceMonitoringSeriesData`, `ServiceMonitoringAlert`, `ServiceMonitoringWindow` and `ServiceMonitoringDashboardProps` are exported from `dashboard-service-monitoring.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample services, series and alerts the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop / model: `services`, `latency`, `errorRate`, `alerts`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:window`.

Event: `retry`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring.md).

## Do

- Write the service state in words in every tile.
- Keep alerts in a rail that stays in view; fold it below the charts on narrow screens.
- Title an alert with the threshold that tripped, not with a generic name.
- Drive every tile and chart from the one window in the page heading.
- Mark the page root with `data-layout-fill` and let it scroll (`overflow-y-auto`), so the panes scroll on their own at `xl` and the page scrolls as one below it.

## Don't

- Don't average latency into one line; show the percentiles.
- Don't use the status colors for percentile series.
- Don't make the rail scroll the page with it at wide screens.
- Don't give a chart a window of its own.
- Don't hide the rail when there are no alerts; say `No open alerts`.

## Copy

- **Service state:** one word. `Operational`, `Degraded`, `Down`.
- **Delta label:** what is compared. `p95 latency vs previous 24 hours`.
- **Alert title:** metric, comparison, threshold with unit. `p95 latency above 800 ms`.
- **Alert time:** relative. `12 minutes ago`.
- **Empty rail:** `No open alerts` / `Alerts appear here when a service crosses a threshold.`

## Accessibility

- The window `ToggleGroup` is named `Window`; the page has one `h1` from `PageHeader`, and `Open alerts` is an `h2` under it.
- The rail's `Item.Group` has `aria-label="Open alerts"`. An independently scrolling region must be reachable by keyboard.
- The rail's scroll container is a `region` labelled by the `Open alerts` heading with `tabindex="0"`, so a keyboard user can scroll it in every browser.
- State and level are words (`StatusIndicator`, `Tag`), never color alone.
- Latency figures use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: services reporting, both charts populated, open alerts in the rail.
- Loading: `loading`; every tile, both charts and the rail hold Skeletons; the window switch stays usable.
- Empty: no traffic yet (`latency: null` per service, no series, `alerts: []`); tiles show a dash, both charts say metrics appear once a service serves requests, and the rail reads `No open alerts`.
- Error: `error` is set; one danger `Alert` under the heading names what did not load, carries the message and offers Retry; tiles show a dash over a quiet band and every region keeps its header over `Not available.`

## Related

- `dashboard/dashboard-alerts` — the full alert queue with severity trends.
- `dashboard/dashboard-health-score` — the same services as one experience score.
- `dashboard/dashboard-analytics` — volume and status codes over a longer period.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring.md), `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring", { variant })`.

# DashboardSwitcher (`dashboard/dashboard-switcher`)

> The dashboards hub: one page that switches between every dashboard of the account.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher/dashboard-switcher.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-switcher")`
- Components: Alert, BarList, Chart, ChartCard, FilterMenu, Hint, IconButton, PageHeader, Select, StatTile, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-navigation`

## Asked as

dashboards; dashboard switcher; dashboards hub; dashboard picker; choose a dashboard; observability dashboards; switch dashboard; shared period filter; painéis; seletor de painel; trocar de painel; tableros; selector de tablero

The dashboards hub. The reader comes here to look at one of several prepared views of the account (traffic, usage, edge health, threats, business figures, or a layout of their own) without hunting for each page in the navigation. One control picks the dashboard, one shared period scopes it, and the body under them is the chosen dashboard. Switching keeps the period, so comparing traffic and threats over the same 7 days is two clicks.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- An account has several dashboards that share one time scope, and the reader moves between them often.
- The set mixes platform, security and business views, so a grouped list beats a long navigation menu.
- Some dashboards report on their own calendar (a quarter, a billing cycle) and must say so instead of following the shared period.

## When not to use

- A single dashboard with its own page: use the dashboard block directly (`dashboard/dashboard-analytics`, `dashboard/dashboard-security`, and the rest of `dashboard`).
- A dashboard the reader arranges by hand: use `dashboard/dashboard-configurable` (it is the body of the Custom entry).
- An overview of the whole account with resources and recent activity: use `dashboard/dashboard-home`.

## Pick the dashboard by the shape of the data

| Data shape | Block |
| --- | --- |
| Traffic volume and quality over one period (requests, status codes, hosts) | `dashboard/dashboard-analytics` |
| Consumption per product or project against the previous period | `dashboard/dashboard-analytics` (Usage) |
| Blocked vs allowed requests, attack categories, source IPs | `dashboard/dashboard-security` |
| Each request of known actors with the rule that decided it | `dashboard/dashboard-security` (ByActor) |
| Open alerts to triage by severity | `dashboard/dashboard-alerts` |
| Items waiting for a verdict from an asynchronous analysis | `dashboard/dashboard-scan-results` |
| One total split into categories over time | `dashboard/dashboard-breakdown` |
| Many signals rolled up into one banded score | `dashboard/dashboard-health-score` |
| Real-user web vitals | `dashboard/dashboard-health-score` (RealUser) |
| Latency percentiles, error rates and live state per service | `dashboard/dashboard-service-monitoring` |
| Cards each reader rearranges and resizes | `dashboard/dashboard-configurable` |
| The account's landing overview | `dashboard/dashboard-home` |
| A one-page roll-up of business KPIs for leadership | `dashboard/dashboard-executive-summary` |
| Several of these behind one picker and one shared period | `dashboard/dashboard-switcher` |

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Dashboard picker — `Select` (required)
- C. Shared period — `FilterMenu` (required)
- D. Own period — `ToggleGroup` (optional)
- E. Refresh — `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)
- F. Applied period — `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` (required)
- G. Dashboard body — `StatTile`, `Hint`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `BarList`, `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher.md).

## Data

The block takes its views and the selected view's data through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `DashboardSwitcherView`, `DashboardSwitcherFigure`, `DashboardSwitcherData`, `DashboardSwitcherFigureValue`, `DashboardSwitcherPeriod`, `DashboardSwitcherQuarter`, `DashboardSwitcherFormat`, `DashboardSwitcherMarkForm` and `DashboardSwitcherProps` are exported from `dashboard-switcher.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample views and a generator of their figures that the block renders when `views` or `data` is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop / model: `views`, `data`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:view`, `v-model:period`, `v-model:quarter`.

Event: `refresh`, `retry`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher.md).

## Do

- Keep the period when the reader switches dashboards; reset only the hover state.
- Load the body on a switch (Skeletons in the final boxes) and refetch it on a period change or Refresh (previous render held), so the controls never jump.
- Hide the shared period for a dashboard that owns its own, and show that dashboard's control in the same place.

## Don't

- Don't list the dashboards as tabs; twelve views in four groups need the grouped picker.
- Don't keep a Period chip that the body ignores.
- Don't put a second period control inside a card.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Dashboards`.
- **Description:** one sentence on what the views cover. `Traffic, security and business views across every workload, plus a layout of your own.`
- **Groups:** one word. `Platform`, `Security`, `Business`, `Yours`.
- **Dashboard names:** a noun phrase in sentence case. `Edge health`, `Funnel and cohorts`.
- **Chip:** the field, then its value. `Period: Last 7 days`.
- **Comparison:** `vs previous 24 hours`, `vs previous quarter`.

## Accessibility

- The picker trigger is named `Dashboard`; the controls sit in a section labelled `Dashboard controls`, the body in a section named after the dashboard, with `aria-busy` while it loads or refetches.
- The period lives in `FilterMenu`, which names its applied count on the Filter button and gives every row and chip its own name.
- Refresh is an icon-only button with `aria-label="Refresh"`.

## States

- Default: Traffic over the last 24 hours.
- OwnPeriod: `v-model:view` set to Executive summary; the shared filter and chip are hidden and the quarter `ToggleGroup` shows.
- Loading: `loading` with no `data`; tiles, chart and list render their Skeletons.
- Error: `error` is set; one danger `Alert` under the heading names what did not load, carries the message and offers Retry; tiles show a dash over a quiet band and every region keeps its header over `Not available.`
- Empty: `data` with no series and no bars; the tiles show dashes, the chart and the ranked list show their empty state (`No data in this period`).
- Refetching: `loading` while `data` is shown, after a period change or Refresh; the chart holds the previous render at reduced opacity and Refresh shows its spinner.

## Related

- `dashboard/dashboard-configurable` — the Custom entry, laid out by the reader.
- `dashboard/dashboard-analytics` (Default and Usage), `dashboard/dashboard-security` — the Traffic, Usage and Threats bodies on their own pages.
- `dashboard/dashboard-home` — the account overview.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `OwnPeriod` · `Loading` · `Error` · `Empty`. Code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher.md), `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-switcher", { variant })`.

# DetailCustomer (`detail/detail-customer`)

> The profile of one customer a support agent opens from a ticket or a search, as a page body for ConsoleLayout.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/detail/detail-customer/detail-customer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("detail/detail-customer")`
- Stability: preview. The API may still change in a minor release, named in the changelog, until the owner marks it GA.
- Components: Alert, Avatar, Button, Card, ConfigProvider, CopyButton, Countdown, DataTable, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, IconButton, KeyValueList, Link, MessageThread, PageHeader, PriorityTag, Rating, Skeleton, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTime`, Tabs, Tag, Textarea, Timeline, Tooltip, `use-locale`

## Asked as

customer profile; customer details; contact profile; requester profile; customer tickets; customer activity; customer notes; support customer; end user profile; perfil do cliente; detalhes do cliente; perfil do contato; perfil do solicitante; tickets do cliente; atividade do cliente; notas do cliente

## Do

- Lead with who the customer is and how to reach them: copy buttons on the email and the phone.
- Keep open tickets first in the table, with their next-reply countdown.
- Write the satisfaction in words next to the stars ("4.5 out of 5 from 12 surveys").
- Keep internal notes visibly internal: the `MessageThread` note band says Internal note.
- Show the customer's local time, so the agent knows whether a call is welcome now.

## Don't

- Don't color a ticket status or a priority without its word; `TableCellStatus` and `PriorityTag` carry both.
- Don't put a ticket's conversation on this page; the subject opens the ticket.
- Don't prefill the note field or disable Add note while it is empty; show the error instead.
- Don't show the sample while loading or failed, and don't wrap real data in a fixed clock.
- Don't add a count to a tab label; the table and the timeline already say how many.

## Copy

- **Heading:** the customer's full name, with the organization ("Acme Inc.") as the description; "Customer" while loading or failed.
- **Actions:** "Edit", "New ticket"; the menu "More actions" with "Merge customer", "Export data", "Delete customer".
- **Details:** "Details" over "Email", "Phone", "Local time" ("9:45 AM" then "America/New_York"), "Language" ("English (United States)"), "Organization", "Tags", "Customer since" ("March 12, 2024"); copy buttons "Copy email", "Copy phone number".
