# DetailVersion (`detail/detail-version`)

> One version of a resource, opened from its Versions tab, as a page body for ConsoleLayout: the layout's last crumb is a transparent select that switches between the resource versions, each with its state Tag, or creat…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/detail/detail-version/detail-version.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("detail/detail-version")`
- Components: Avatar, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, CodeEditor, ConfirmDialog, ConsoleLayout, DataTable, `DataTablePagination`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerDescription`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, `FieldError`, IconButton, Input, Item, Item, Link, MultiSelect, NumberInput, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Resizable, SchemaForm, ScrollArea, Select, SettingsGroup, SettingsRow, Skeleton, Spinner, SplitButton, Switch, `TableCellLink`, `TableCellTime`, Tabs, Tag, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip, `use-collection`, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

version detail; resource version; draft version; version history; version switcher; versioned settings; detalhe da versão; histórico de versões; versão rascunho; revert version; rollback version; reverter versão; revertir versión; environment switcher; environment crumb; switch environment; seletor de ambiente; creating version; version not found; device groups; cache settings list; functions instances; version source files; criando versão; versão não encontrada; grupos de dispositivos; instâncias de função

One version of a resource, opened from its Versions tab. The user is here to change a draft and ship it, or to read what a built version holds and redeploy it or branch a new version from it. The page keeps the version they are on in the breadcrumb, where they can switch to another, puts the version's settings in tabs, pins the state and the save or deploy action to the bottom, and opens the version history beside the work when they need to see what changed. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`. The workspace pins its own bars, so its root carries `data-layout-fill`: the layout's `main` stops scrolling, the root fills it (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview) and its panes scroll.

## When to use

- A resource whose configuration is versioned: drafts are edited, built and deployed, and built versions are read-only.
- The user opens a row of the Versions tab of `detail/detail-resource`, or creates a new version.
- The version has several areas of settings (Settings, Source, Device Groups, Cache Settings, Functions Instances, Rules Engine) that share one save and deploy action.

## When not to use

- The overview of the resource itself, its domains and deployments: use `detail/detail-resource`.
- A resource without versions whose settings save in place: use `edit/edit-resource` or `settings/settings-form`.
- The Rules Engine tab content: use `edit/edit-rule-builder`.
- Deploying from a list without opening a version: use `create/create-deploy-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Version switcher — `ConsoleLayout`, `Select`, `Input`, `Tag`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)
- B. Workspace — `Resizable` (required)
- C. Version tab bar — `PageTabs`, `Tabs`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton`, `EmptyState` (required)
- D. Settings panel — `ScrollArea`, `PageHeader`, `SettingsGroup`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `Switch`, `Tooltip`, `Skeleton`, `Link` (required)
- E. Version bar — `Tag`, `SplitButton`, `Button`, `Spinner` (required)
- F. Version history — `IconButton`, `Tag`, `Field`, `Textarea`, `Button`, `Avatar` (optional)
- G. Revert — `ConfirmDialog`, `Button`, `Tag` (optional, on an earlier Ready version)

What each part takes: [blocks/detail/detail-version.md](blocks/detail/detail-version.md).

## List tabs

Source, Device Groups, Cache Settings and Functions Instances are lists inside the version: a small `PageHeader` with an outlined add action, the controls row of `view/view-table` (search, Refresh, Download CSV, Columns) and a flush `DataTable` in a `Card`, paginated at 10. Its `#empty` slot tells a search that matches nothing (No matching, with Clear search) apart from a list with nothing yet (the add action). The name cell is a button that opens the edit `Drawer`, the same drawer the add action opens, built as in `create/create-drawer`: `SettingsGroup`s of `Field`s (Device Groups, Functions Instances) or of `SettingsRow`s in a `Card` (Cache Settings, reusing the rows of `edit/edit-resource#CacheSettings` plus Adaptive delivery and a Device groups `MultiSelect`). Functions Instances renders the arguments as a `SchemaForm` when the function declares a schema and as a JSON `CodeEditor` when it does not, and its function `Select` ends on Create Function. Source embeds the file browser: Upload Files in the heading, Open in Object Storage in the controls row, the folder path as a `Breadcrumb` and an `EmptyState` with Upload Files and Open Bucket. Saving a drawer changes the draft only; the version bar still deploys it.

## Creating and not found

While Add Version copies a built version into a new draft (`creating`), the workspace is drawn as `Skeleton` wires in a busy status region named "Creating a new version from <id>." and the version bar shows a `Spinner`, "Creating new version…", the copy line, Add Version loading and Redeploy disabled. A version link that points nowhere keeps the trail and renders a bordered `EmptyState` with View Versions.

## Data

The block takes its versions and settings through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `VersionDetailVersion`, `VersionDetailSettings`, `VersionDetailProps` and the other record types are exported from `detail-version.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample resource, versions, settings and revert diff the block renders when those props are left out. The viewed version's `state` decides the page: `draft` is editable, `deployed` is read-only with Redeploy, `ready` is an earlier version with Revert.

Prop / model: `resource`, `versions`, `settings`, `revertDiff`, `environments`, `creating`, `reverting`, `v-model:version-id`, `v-model:tab`, `v-model:history-open`, `v-model:environment`.

Event: `save`, `save-description`, `add-version`, `add-environment`, `redeploy`, `revert`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/detail/detail-version.md](blocks/detail/detail-version.md).

## Do

- Keep one primary action on the page, in the version bar; the tabs share it.
- Lock the settings fieldset, not each control one by one, when the version is built.
- Let the user switch versions from the breadcrumb without going back to the list.
- Set the trail from the page with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`, and mark the root with `data-layout-fill`.
- Show the state in three places that agree: the breadcrumb option, the tab row tag and the version bar.
- Keep the history pane collapsible and resizable so the settings keep their width when it is closed.
- Show what a revert changes before it runs: the settings with old and new values, and the rules added and removed.
- Report a revert like any deploy: on `revert`, one toast that turns into the outcome, with Edit and Redeploy.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/shell-console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't let a built version look editable; disable the fieldset and say Read-only.
- Don't size the body with `calc(100dvh - …)`.
- Don't put Save or Deploy in the tab row or the page header.
- Don't name a tab in the breadcrumb.
- Don't list every earlier version at once; show five and Show older.
- Don't save a description edit without Cancel and Save buttons.
- Don't edit a list row in place or on a new page; open the drawer, and let the version bar deploy.
- Don't show the settings form while a new version is still being copied; draw the wires.
- Don't revert without a confirmation, and don't make the diff depend on an arrow glyph or color alone.
- Don't delete or hide the version a revert replaces; it stays in history.
- Don't offer View deployments on the revert toast.

## Copy

- **Version state tags:** one word, e.g. "Draft", "Deployed", "Ready", "Editable", "Read-only".
- **Version bar:** one sentence on what the user can do, e.g. "This version is open for editing. Deploy it when ready." or "Viewing a deployed version".
- **Save actions:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Save and deploy", "Save and build", "Save".
- **Built version actions:** "Add Version", "Redeploy"; on an earlier version "Revert to <id>".
- **Revert:** bar "Viewing an earlier version"; dialog title "Revert to <id>?", description "Reverting deploys <id> to Production in place of <deployed>. <deployed> stays in the version history, so you can redeploy it later."; diff heading "What changes against <deployed>"; toasts "Reverting to <id>…" then "<id> is deployed.", actions "Edit" and "Redeploy".
- **List tabs:** add actions name the object, e.g. "Add Device Group", "Add Cache Settings", "Add Functions Instance"; drawer titles "Add …" or "Edit …"; success toasts "Device group \"mobile\" saved." with "The change is part of this draft until you deploy it."
- **Creating and not found:** "Creating new version…", "Copying <id> into a new draft."; "Version not found" with "View Versions".
- **Version picker:** search placeholder "Search versions", no-match line `No versions match "<query>".`, footer "Add Version".
- **Setting rows:** a noun title and one sentence with a period, e.g. "Active" with "When disabled, the resource stops serving traffic."
- **History:** "Current version", an empty changes line, e.g. "No changes yet. Each change you save shows up here.", description placeholder "What changed in this version?".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The body renders no `main`: the layout's single `main` holds the workspace; the Settings `PageHeader` title is its heading, and the history pane is a region labelled by its "Version history" `h2`.
- The resize handle has an `aria-label` and works with arrow keys.
- The version `Select` trigger is named "Switch version"; its search input is named "Search versions".
- Every `Switch` and `Input` in a setting row has an `aria-label` that matches the row title.
- A disabled control with a reason gets a `Tooltip` that the keyboard can reach.
- The revert dialog traps focus, is named by its title and returns focus to Revert on close. Each changed setting carries a visually hidden sentence ("changes from On to Off"); the struck-through values and the arrow are `aria-hidden`. The toasts live in the app's one `Toaster` region (the app mounts it; the page body only calls `toast`), and the bar's status line announces "Reverting to <id>…".
- Icon-only buttons (Version actions, Close version history, Edit version info) have an `aria-label`; decorative icons are `aria-hidden`.

## States

- Draft: the default render, a version with `state: 'draft'` on its Settings tab, with the Editable tag and the Save and deploy split button in the version bar.
- Deployed: `version-id` on the version with `state: 'deployed'`, read-only, the fieldset disabled and the version bar offering Add Version and Redeploy.
- Revert: `version-id` on an earlier version with `state: 'ready'` and `history-open`, read-only, Revert to <id> in the bar and a confirmation with the `revertDiff`; `reverting` shows the run.
- VersionHistory: `history-open` on the draft, the current version, the empty changes entry and the five newest earlier versions.
- EnvironmentCrumb: `environments` set, for a resource that is deployed to several environments. The page's `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb` ends on two control crumbs, environment then version, each a small transparent `Select` with a search field (`Switch environment`, `Switch version`). Environments carry their deployment policy as a `Tag` and Add Environment in the footer; picking an environment moves the version crumb to the version live there, and each version option says where it is live (Live in Production). The environment always comes before the version, because a version is chosen within an environment.
- Creating: `creating` on the deployed AEO25I38, the workspace as `Skeleton` wires and the version bar busy.
- NotFound: a version that does not exist, a bordered `EmptyState` with View Versions.
- Source: `tab="source"` with its panel in the `#source` slot, the file list of the version bucket with its folder path and Open in Object Storage.
- DeviceGroups: `tab="device-groups"` with its panel in the `#device-groups` slot, the groups table and the add or edit drawer with the User-Agent expression.
- CacheSettings: `tab="cache-settings"` with its panel in the `#cache-settings` slot, the cache settings table and the add or edit drawer with Adaptive delivery and Device groups.
- FunctionsInstances: `tab="functions-instances"` with its panel in the `#functions-instances` slot, the instances table and the add or edit drawer with the function `Select` and its arguments.

## Related

- `detail/detail-resource` — its Versions tab lists the versions that open here.
- `edit/edit-rule-builder` — the content of the Rules Engine tab.
- `view/view-file-browser` — the full storage page the Source tab embeds.
- `edit/edit-resource` — its CacheSettings variant holds the rows the Cache Settings drawer reuses.
- `create/create-drawer` — the add and edit drawers of the list tabs.
- `state/state-page-skeleton` — the skeleton wires Creating draws.

# EditDeleteDialog (`edit/edit-delete-dialog`)

> The destructive confirmation a resource list uses for Delete: a warning `Alert`, a sentence naming what goes with the resource and a Help Center link, then the typed confirmation `ConfirmDialog` draws from `confirmati…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/edit/edit-delete-dialog/edit-delete-dialog.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("edit/edit-delete-dialog")`
- Components: Alert, Button, ConfirmDialog, Item, Link, PageHeader, Toast
- Skills: `webkit-ux-heuristics`, `webkit-microcopy`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

delete; delete dialog; delete confirmation; delete resource; type to confirm; destructive confirmation; remove resource; excluir; confirmar exclusão; excluir recurso; apagar; delete with confirmation; excluir com confirmação; form in modal; dialog form; modal form; blocking decision; type name to delete; confirm in dialog; formulário em modal; formulário no diálogo; modal com formulário; type the name to delete; confirm deletion by name

The last stop before a resource is gone for good. The user chose Delete from a row menu or a settings page and now has to see what goes with the resource, take one deliberate step to prove they mean this one, and either confirm or back out. The dialog makes the irreversible action slow on purpose: Delete stays disabled until the typed name matches. SettingsRow draws the page it is opened from as a page body for `ConsoleLayout` (the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`).

## When to use

- Use edit-delete-dialog when the user deletes a resource from the UI and must type its name.
- Any permanent delete of a resource, a folder of files or a record, opened from the row Delete action of `view/view-table`, `view/view-file-browser` or `detail/detail-dns-zone`.
- The resource takes other things with it (settings, instances, files) and the user must read that before confirming.
- A delete that lives in a settings page as its own row (the danger zone): use the SettingsRow variant, a labelled field inside the same medium `ConfirmDialog` opened from an outlined `Item`.

## When not to use

- Detaching a reference while the object survives: that is Remove, a plain action with an undo toast, not this dialog.
- A reversible change such as disabling or archiving: save it through `settings/settings-form` or `edit/edit-resource`.
- A plain yes-or-no decision with nothing to type: use `ConfirmDialog` with its actions only, without the typed name.
- A long-running delete that reports back later (a purge, a teardown): the submit lifecycle is `state/state-async-submit`.

## Building blocks

- A. Dialog and trigger — `ConfirmDialog`, `Button` (required)
- B. Consequence — `Alert`, `Link` (required)
- C. Typed confirmation — `ConfirmDialog` `confirmation-phrase` (required)
- D. Trigger — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/edit/edit-delete-dialog.md](blocks/edit/edit-delete-dialog.md).

## Data

The block takes the resource name and the request state through props and emits the delete; it fetches nothing. `DeleteDialogProps` is exported from `edit-delete-dialog.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample name the block shows when `name` is left out.

Prop: `name`, `loading`, `error`, `defaultOpen`, `v-model:open`.

Event: `delete`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/edit/edit-delete-dialog.md](blocks/edit/edit-delete-dialog.md).

## Do

- Name the resource kind in the title and the resource itself in the chip, so the user knows exactly what goes.
- Keep the confirm button disabled until the trimmed value equals the name; that is the prevention, not a toast after the fact.
- Reset the typed value each time the dialog opens.
- Never block paste in the input.
- Put the consequence in the `Alert` and the sentence below it, before the input that asks for the decision.
- Use the SettingsRow variant on a settings page.

## Don't

- Don't delete on the first click, from a row menu or anywhere else.
- Don't enable Delete on a partial or case-insensitive match.
- Don't put the warning in the input's label or placeholder.
- Don't make Delete the only button, or use primary for it; it is `variant="danger"` beside Cancel.
- Don't close the dialog on a refused delete or clear the typed name; show why in the danger `Alert` and let Delete run again.
- Don't clear the input as the dialog closes; the field would flash empty during the exit.

## Copy

- **Title:** Delete plus the resource kind, in sentence case, e.g. "Delete workload"; the visible trigger and the confirm button repeat it.
- **Trigger:** verb and object, e.g. "Delete resource" on a visible button; "Delete" in a row menu.
- **Alert:** one fact, e.g. "Once confirmed, this action can't be reversed."
- **Consequence:** one sentence naming what goes with it, e.g. "The selected bucket will be deleted, along with all its files."
- **Prompt:** "Type `name` to confirm.", written by `ConfirmDialog` from the locale catalog; never a position such as "in the box below".
- **Confirm:** the title's verb and object, e.g. "Delete resource"; never "OK", "Confirm" or "Yes".
- **Cancel:** exactly "Cancel".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- `ConfirmDialog` traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus to the trigger.
- The input is named by the prompt through `aria-labelledby`, so a screen reader hears the name to type, and it takes focus when the dialog opens.
- Enter in the input confirms only when the name matches; otherwise focus moves on to Cancel and Delete in reading order.
- While the delete runs, the confirm button announces its busy state and the dialog stays open.

## States

- Default: the danger trigger is visible (`v-model:open` false); opening it shows the warning, the name chip and the empty input with Delete resource disabled.
- SettingsRow: the settings-page danger zone; an outlined `Item` row opens the medium `ConfirmDialog` asking for the name through `confirmation-phrase`, with Delete resource disabled until it matches and loading while it runs.
- Error: `error` set with `defaultOpen`: the server refuses the delete (the resource is still used by two workloads); the dialog stays open, a danger `Alert` says why, and Delete can run again (in a live flow the typed name stays in the field).

## Related

- `view/view-table` — the row menu Delete that opens this dialog.
- `view/view-file-browser` — Delete on a file or folder row.
- `detail/detail-dns-zone` — Delete on a record of a resource.
- `settings/settings-form` — where the SettingsRow variant sits.
- `state/state-async-submit` — a long-running request that reports back later.
- `ConfirmDialog` — the dialog this block fills; see `skills/webkit-form` for the Dialog form type.

## Variants

# EditFunction (`edit/edit-function`)

> The code editor page, a page body for ConsoleLayout (the layout's breadcrumb names the service): the Code and Settings tabs, an editor toolbar whose ToggleGroup switches between the Code document and the Arguments doc…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/edit/edit-function/edit-function.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("edit/edit-function")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CodeEditor, ConfirmDialog, CopyButton, EmptyState, `FieldError`, IconButton, Input, Item, Kbd, KeyValueList, Link, `LogViewerContent`, LogViewer, PageTabs, RadioGroup, `ResizableHandle`, `ResizablePane`, `ResizableRoot`, SaveBar, Select, SettingsGroup, SettingsRow, StatusIndicator, Switch, Tabs, Tag, Textarea, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, Trace, `use-shortcuts`, `use-unsaved-changes`, `utils/leave-link`
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-form`

## Asked as

code editor; code editor page; function code editor; editor page; code and arguments editor; split editor; monaco editor; editor de código; página do editor; editar código; function editor; edge function; function detail; function arguments; json schema arguments; function settings; editor de função; argumentos da função; detalhe da função; test run; function test; run trace; span waterfall; invocation trace; testar função; execução de teste; rastreamento da execução; function code page; edit function code; function arguments page

The editing page of a service whose behavior lives in source code. The user writes and saves the code, defines the argument form each instance of the service asks for (its fields, types and defaults), and adjusts the service's settings. The editor fills the page so the code has room, and one save bar commits code, arguments and settings together. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the Services breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`. The editor pins its own panes, so its root carries `data-layout-fill`: the layout's `main` stops scrolling and the root fills it (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview).

## When to use

- Use the edit-function block for the code and arguments page of a function; the editor itself is the CodeEditor component.
- A resource is mainly a document the user edits as text: function code, a schema, a configuration file.
- The document comes with a structured companion (an argument form) that is easier to edit as fields than as JSON, and the user wants both views side by side.
- The same resource also has a few settings, shown on a second tab of the same page.
- The user tests the code before saving it and needs to read where the run spent its time and what it printed (variant TestRun).

## When not to use

- A resource made only of settings: use `edit/edit-resource`.
- Ordered conditions and actions the user composes without code: use `edit/edit-rule-builder`.
- Free key and value pairs such as environment variables: use `edit/edit-variables`.
- Running queries and reading results: use `view/view-query-editor`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)
- B. Editor toolbar — `ToggleGroup`, `Button` (required)
- C. Code document — `CodeEditor`, `FieldError` (required)
- D. Test run — `ResizableRoot`, `ResizablePane`, `ResizableHandle` (optional)
- E. Arguments split — `ResizableRoot`, `ResizablePane`, `ResizableHandle`, `CodeEditor`, `Button`, `ConfirmDialog` (required)
- F. No fields — `EmptyState`, `Button`, `Link` (optional)
- G. Field list — `Card`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- H. Field settings — `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Textarea`, `FieldError` (required)
- I. Settings tab — `SettingsGroup`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `FieldError` (required)
- J. Save bar — `SaveBar`, `Button`, `Alert` (required)
- K. Shortcut keycap — `Kbd` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/edit/edit-function.md](blocks/edit/edit-function.md).

## Data

The block takes the saved service and the request state through props and emits the save; it fetches nothing. `FunctionEditorService`, `FunctionEditorField`, `FunctionEditorValues` and `FunctionEditorProps` are exported from `edit-function.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample service and fields the block renders when `service` or `fields` is left out. The editor keeps its own draft; Discard returns to the props. The page file is the wiring: `parts/` holds its regions (`function-arguments.vue` with `function-field-item.vue` and `function-field-settings.vue`, `function-settings-tab.vue`, `function-save-bar.vue`, and the TestRun pane `function-test-run-pane.vue`), `composables/use-function-fields.ts` the field list behavior (names, expand, add, duplicate, remove, move), `composables/use-function-test-run.ts` the TestRun run and save simulation, and `lib/function-editor.ts` the Monaco loader, the option lists and the field helpers. `webkit add` copies them all.

Prop: `service`, `fields`, `defaultDraft`, `v-model:tab`, `v-model:document`, `defaultOpenKeys`, `loading`, `error`.

Event: `submit`, `discard`, `editor-ready`.

Slot: `editor-actions`, `code-panel`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/edit/edit-function.md](blocks/edit/edit-function.md).

## Do

- Let the editor fill the pane; the page scrolls inside the editor, not around it.
- Mark the page root with `data-layout-fill`.
- Show the schema JSON and the fields form side by side, so the user can check one against the other.
- Keep collapsed fields as one-line summaries with their tags, and open settings only for the field being edited.
- Lock fields that cannot change after creation, with a lock glyph and a description that says so.
- Use one save bar for both tabs, and take the user to the tab that holds the error.
- Show a test run under the code it ran, on the same page: the trace and the logs on one clock, the summary first.
- Select the span the user most likely wants (the slowest or the failed one) when the run finishes.

## Don't

- Don't put the code editor inside a card, a drawer or a modal.
- Don't add a page heading above the tabs; the layout's breadcrumb names the service.
- Don't size the page with `calc(100dvh - …)`; it overflows under a notification.
- Don't save from inside the Arguments pane or a field; Save lives in the bar.
- Don't flag a new field's name before the user has touched it.
- Don't let the schema pane squeeze the fields pane below a usable width; collapse it instead.
- Don't open a test run in a dialog or a new page; it covers the code the user is about to fix.
- Don't save as a side effect of Run test; a test runs the code in the editor, saved or not.
- Don't report a test run with a toast; the result lives in the pane, where the user is looking.

## Copy

- **Tabs and documents:** single nouns, e.g. "Code", "Settings", "Arguments".
- **Field count:** a number and the noun, e.g. "1 field", "2 fields".
- **Buttons:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Add field", "Remove form", "Discard", "Save".
- **Empty state:** title states the fact, e.g. "This form has no fields"; description says what to do, e.g. "Add the first argument the service reads."
- **Errors:** short and specific, e.g. "This field is required.", "Another field already uses this name."
- **Save bar:** "You have unsaved changes."
- **Test run:** status as one word ("Completed", "Running", "Failed"); the outcome as the status code and what happened, e.g. "200, served from the transform and written to cache."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Both editors have an `aria-label` that names the document, e.g. "Source code", "Argument form schema, as JSON".
- The split is labeled "Argument form", its panes "Schema" and "Fields", and the handle "Resize the schema".
- Each field has native Move up and Move down buttons named with the field ("Move quality up"); moves are announced in a polite live region.
- The expand button sets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` and names the field it opens.
- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` that matches its `Tooltip`; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The save bar's motion respects reduced motion.
- In TestRun the vertical split is labeled "Code and test run", its panes "Source code" and "Test run", and the handle "Resize the test run". The pane is a `section` named by its Test run heading, with Trace and Logs as `h3`s.
- The trace is a `treegrid` with one tab stop (see `Trace`); the running state is announced by a `status` line.
- `⌘ S` (`Ctrl S` off Apple) saves while the `SaveBar` shows unsaved changes, the same as Save, and stops the browser's own save; with no changes it does nothing. Save carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and a `Kbd` keycap.
- In the Test run variant, `⌘ Enter` (`Ctrl Enter` off Apple) runs the test from anywhere on the Code tab, the source editor included, where a bare `Enter` stays a new line. Run test carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and a `Kbd` keycap.

## States

- Code: the default, `tab` `code`: the Code tab with the Code document filling the editor pane.
- Arguments: `document` `arguments` with `defaultOpenKeys`: the Arguments document of image-optimizer, the schema on the left and two fields on the right, one expanded.
- NoArguments: a `service` with an empty schema and `fields` `[]`: the Arguments document of a service with no form, the empty schema and the no fields empty state.
- TestRun: the Code document with a finished test run of image-optimizer under it, the origin fetch selected in the trace; Run test shows the running state.
- Settings: `tab` `settings`: the Settings tab with General, Runtime, Execution environment and Status; editing raises the save bar.
- Saving: `loading` with a `defaultDraft`: a change to the Code document is being saved; Save shows its loading state, Discard and the fields are disabled and the editors are read-only.

## Related

- `shell/shell-console` — the `ConsoleLayout` this page body renders in.
- `edit/edit-resource` — the settings form and save bar pattern the Settings tab follows.
- `view/view-query-editor` — an editor page that runs queries and shows results.
- `view/view-events-explorer` — the events explorer, where the logs of every run land.
- `Trace` — the span waterfall of the test run.
- `detail/detail-version` — reading a deployed version of the code.

# EditResource (`edit/edit-resource`)

> The settings page of a resource, a page body for ConsoleLayout (the layout's breadcrumb names the resource): a small Settings page heading over stacked `SettingsGroup` bands in the form column, each a heading with an…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/edit/edit-resource/edit-resource.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("edit/edit-resource")`
- Components: Alert, AttributeEditor, Button, Card, CodeBlock, CodeEditor, ConfirmDialog, ConsoleLayout, DataTable, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerDescription`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, Field, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`, IconButton, Input, Item, Kbd, Link, MultiSelect, NumberInput, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PasswordInput, RadioGroup, SaveBar, Select, SettingsGroup, SettingsRow, Switch, Tabs, Tag, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip, `use-locale`, `use-unsaved-changes`, `utils/focus-invalid`
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-layout`, `webkit-ux-heuristics`

## Asked as

settings page; resource settings; settings of one resource; resource settings page; settings tab; application settings; workload settings; firewall settings; edit settings; página de configurações; configurações do recurso; aba de configurações; save bar; unsaved changes bar; sticky save bar; discard and save; commit bar; barra de salvar; alterações não salvas; salvar alterações; edit resource; editar recurso; data stream; data stream settings; log streaming; stream destination; sampling; log template; configurações do data stream; envio de logs; streaming de logs; stale record; changed elsewhere; overwrite changes; conflict on save; danger zone; delete resource; type the name to confirm; zona de perigo; excluir recurso; alterado em outro lugar; leave page guard; unsaved changes dialog; cache settings; cache policy; browser cache; edge cache; tiered cache; configurações de cache; protocol settings; https ports; http/3; tls version; mutual authentication; mtls; autenticação mútua; waf settings; waf rule set; threat sensitivity; configurações do waf

The settings page of one existing resource. The user comes here to change how the resource is named, what it runs with and whether it is active, review the change, and commit it or throw it away. Every field sits in a labeled section of the form column, and one save band appears only once something has changed, so the page reads as the resource's current state until the user edits it. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the resource breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`; the save band sticks to the bottom of the layout's scrolling region.

## When to use

- Use edit-resource for the Settings tab or settings page of one resource, with anchored sections and a save bar that appears after the first edit.
- A resource has a Settings tab (or, with no tabs, its own `/<resource>/:id/settings` page) with fields grouped into a few sections.
- Changes are reviewed together and committed in one save, with a way to discard them all.
- Some settings are fixed or paid and must be shown locked, with the reason beside them.

## When not to use

- Creating the resource for the first time: use `create/create-page`, which shares this field list.
- Account or organization settings outside one resource (profile, preferences, notifications): use `settings/settings-form`.
- A resource whose content is code or a document: use `edit/edit-function`.
- Deleting the resource: the Danger zone action opens `edit/edit-delete-dialog`.
- A short list of attached records inside a section: use `detail/detail-domains-card` as that section's body.

## Building blocks

- A. Resource tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (optional)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Settings sections — `SettingsGroup`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `FieldError`, `Switch` (required)
- D. Locked settings — `Tooltip`, `Switch`, `Link` (optional)
- E. Save bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)
- F. Conditional fields — `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `FieldError` (optional)
- G. Template editor — `SettingsRow`, `FieldError` (optional)
- H. Section warnings and server errors — `SettingsGroup`, `Button` (optional)
- I. Leave guard — `Tabs`, `SaveBar` (optional)
- J. Changed elsewhere — `Alert`, `ConfirmDialog`, `Button`, `SaveBar` (optional)
- K. Danger zone — `SettingsGroup`, `Card`, `SettingsRow`, `Button`, `Input` (optional)
- L. Shortcut keycap — `Kbd` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/edit/edit-resource.md](blocks/edit/edit-resource.md).

## Data

ProjectSettings takes the saved settings through props and emits the values on Save; it fetches nothing and saves nothing. `EditResourceProject` and `EditResourceProps` are exported from `edit-resource.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample project the block renders when `resource` is left out. StaleRecord passes `defaultDraft` and `stale`, and DangerZone fills the `sections` slot; the other states are separate screens with their own fields.

Prop: `resource`, `defaultDraft`, `stale`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:tab`.

Event: `submit`, `discard`.

Slot: `sections`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/edit/edit-resource.md](blocks/edit/edit-resource.md).

## Do

- Show the save bar only while the form differs from the saved record.
- Hold every field read-only while saving, not disabled: the values stay readable at full contrast and no field can change under the save.
- Give every section a short hint that says what it controls, and an anchor so a link can land on it.
- Keep locked settings visible, disabled, with the reason and the way to unlock them.
- Put destructive actions in a Danger zone section at the end, never in the save bar.
- Check every field when Save is pressed and show errors only then; see `skills/webkit-errors`.
- Put the choice that decides other fields first, and show only the fields that choice needs.
- Show a preset document read-only, with Copy, beside the way to make it editable.
- Mark the tab that holds unsaved changes with `dirty`, and ask before leaving it while dirty.
- Offer Save changes in the leave dialog when the form can be saved from there; the user keeps their work without going back.
- Say when the record changed elsewhere as soon as it is known, and ask before Save overwrites it.
- Keep the edits on screen after a reload with an Undo, so a stale form never loses work silently.
- Ask for the resource name before a delete, through `ConfirmDialog` `confirmation-phrase`.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/shell-console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't place a permanent Save button at the top or bottom of the page; the save bar appears on demand.
- Don't save on each toggle; changes wait for Save.
- Don't hide fields the user cannot change; lock them and say why.
- Don't use `size="medium"` or larger for the Settings heading; the tab bar or breadcrumb already names the resource.
- Don't add a Cancel button that leaves the page; Discard restores the record in place.
- Don't report a rejected destination or credential in a toast; it belongs above the section it concerns.
- Don't echo a saved secret back into its field.
- Don't rely on the dot alone: the dirty tab also says "Unsaved changes" to screen readers.
- Don't overwrite a record that changed elsewhere without the overwrite confirmation.
- Don't put Delete in the save bar, the page heading or a menu of the form; it lives in the Danger zone.
- Don't enable the delete confirm button before the typed name matches.

## Copy

- **Heading:** "Settings", with one sentence ending in a period, e.g. "Core configuration for this project."
- **Section titles:** short nouns, e.g. "General", "Modules", "Subscription modules", "Status".
- **Row descriptions:** one sentence that says what the setting does, e.g. "When disabled, the project stops serving traffic."
- **Save bar:** state what changed and when it applies, e.g. "Project settings changed." with the hint "Saving publishes them on the next deployment."; buttons "Discard" and "Save".
- **Locked reason:** one sentence with the way out, e.g. "Contact sales to activate this module."
- **Server error on a section:** what happened, then what was kept, e.g. "The endpoint did not answer the test record, so the stream was not saved. Your other changes are still here."; the field reason is one line, e.g. "The endpoint did not answer within 10 seconds."
- **Leave dialog:** "Unsaved changes", "This page has changes you haven't saved. If you leave now, they're discarded." (with Save: "Save them before you leave, or discard them and continue."); buttons "Keep editing", "Discard changes", "Save changes". These are the built-in `unsavedChanges` messages in en, pt-BR and es.
- **Changed elsewhere:** "Changed elsewhere." + "This project was saved by someone else after you opened it. …"; button "Reload"; dialog "Overwrite changes made elsewhere?" with "Go back" and "Overwrite and save"; after a reload "Edits discarded." with "Undo".
- **Danger zone:** section "Danger zone" with "Actions that cannot be undone."; row "Delete this project"; dialog "Delete project", "Once confirmed, this action can't be reversed.", "Type <name> to confirm."; buttons "Cancel" and "Delete project".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The form has an `aria-label` and its `fieldset` a visually hidden `legend` with the same words, e.g. "Main settings".
- Every `Input` and `Switch` has an `aria-label` matching its row title.
- A disabled `Switch` keeps its `Tooltip`, so keyboard and pointer users can still read why it is locked.
- External links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and an icon marked `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The save bar enters after the form in reading order and its motion respects reduced motion.
- An invalid field points at its `FieldError` through `aria-describedby`; on Save the first invalid field takes the focus.
- A section `Alert` is announced by `Alert` itself; its recovery `Button` is a real button inside it.
- The `CodeEditor` and the read-only `CodeBlock` are named after their row (`Data set`, `Copy the data set as JSON`).
- The dirty tab mark is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden "Unsaved changes" joins the tab's accessible name, and under forced colors the dot paints in `CanvasText`.
- The leave dialog is a `ConfirmDialog`: focus moves into it, Escape and the close button count as Keep editing, and focus returns to the control that asked to leave.
- The changed-elsewhere notice sits in a polite live region and takes focus after Reload so the change of values is announced; both its actions are real buttons.
- The delete confirmation `Input` is labelled by the "Type … to confirm." sentence (`aria-labelledby`) and takes focus when the dialog opens.
- `⌘ S` (`Ctrl S` off Apple) saves while the `SaveBar` shows unsaved changes, the same as Save, and stops the browser's own save; with no changes it does nothing. Save carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and a `Kbd` keycap. Every variant with a `SaveBar` answers it the same way.

## States

- ProjectSettings: a project's Settings tab with General, Modules and Subscription modules from `resource` (the sample when left out); the save bar is hidden until an edit. Save emits `submit`; `loading` holds the fields read-only and spins Save, and `error` set when it ends raises the error toast with Retry.
- DeployableSettings: a deployable resource's Settings tab with General, Domains, collapsed Advanced settings and the Danger zone, whose Delete resource opens the type-to-confirm `ConfirmDialog` of `edit/edit-delete-dialog`.
- PolicySettings: a security policy's Settings tab with General, Modules with one locked on, Debug rules and Status.
- WafSettings: a WAF rule set's Main settings tab with General, Status (Active and the Blocking or Learning Mode `Select`) and Threats, one row per threat family with a Sensitivity `Select` beside its `Switch`; the Sensitivity is disabled while its threat is off, and Save confirms in a toast.
- ResourceSettings: a first-level resource with no tabs at its own settings route; Save checks every field before it commits.
- UnsavedChanges: after one edit; the save bar is up with Discard and Save.
- Saving: while the request is in flight; every field is read-only, so none can change under the save, Save is loading and Discard is disabled.
- DataStream: a data stream at its own settings route with General, Source, Sampling, Template and Destination; the destination fields follow the connector, Custom headers are `AttributeEditor` rows of Name and Value (up to 5) whose value turns into a masked `PasswordInput` when the name reads as a credential (Authorization, Cookie, a token, key, secret or password), Save sends one test record, and an endpoint that does not answer raises the section `Alert` of the state-form-validation rule.
- StaleRecord: the form holds edits and the record changed elsewhere; the warning notice with Reload is up, Save asks before overwriting, Reload turns the notice into Edits discarded with Undo.
- DangerZone: the settings end with the Danger zone; Delete project opens the typed-name confirmation, enabled only on a match, loading while the delete runs.
- CacheSettings: one cache setting of an application; General, Browser cache, Edge cache and the collapsed Advanced cache key. Rows that only apply under a switch or an override sit one level in (`SettingsRow` `level`). An edge TTL under 60 seconds and an empty allowlist or denylist are field errors with their reason, focused on Save. Save deploys and reports through the state-async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- Protocols: the protocol settings of a workload; ports per protocol, TLS version and cipher suite, then Mutual authentication. Mutual authentication stays off, with a helper line saying why, until HTTPS is on; once on it shows the mode as `Field` choice cards, the trusted CA picker (search, expiry beside each certificate, Upload certificate in its footer opening a `Drawer`) and the revocation lists. Save checks a port per protocol and a CA, then deploys through the state-async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- UnsavedChanges (leave guard): the Settings tab carries the dirty dot, and switching tabs while dirty opens the Unsaved changes dialog.

## Settings that deploy

Some settings only take effect once the resource is deployed (cache settings of an application, protocols of a workload). For those:

- Say so in the save bar hint, e.g. "Saving deploys storefront to Production."
- On Save, validate first (field errors per the state-form-validation rule), then run the deploy on its own: a loading toast while it runs, then the state-async-submit toast with **Edit** (back to the form, focus on its first field) and **Redeploy**. Never offer View deployments.
- Keep the form usable while it runs; the baseline moves to the saved values only when the deploy succeeds.
- Keep switches that depend on each other consistent in both directions, e.g. HTTP/3 turns HTTPS on and HTTPS off turns HTTP/3 and mutual authentication off.

# EditRuleBuilder (`edit/edit-rule-builder`)

> A rule builder drawer, the richest form pattern: a large right-side drawer with General, Phase, Criteria, Behaviors and Status sections over a single Save in the footer.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/edit/edit-rule-builder/edit-rule-builder.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("edit/edit-rule-builder")`
- Components: Alert, AttributeEditor, Button, Card, Combobox, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, Field, `FieldDescription`, Input, Item, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, RadioGroup, Select, SettingsGroup, SettingsRow, Switch
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-create-surface`

## Asked as

rules engine; rule form; add rule; criteria and behaviors; if then rules; conditional rules; rule builder; motor de regras; criar regra; regras condicionais

A drawer where the user writes one rule of a rules engine: when it runs (the phase), the conditions that decide whether it applies, and the ordered behaviors it performs when they match. The user composes groups of variable, operator and argument rows (every row in a group must match, any group is enough), picks behaviors that fit the phase, puts everything in order and saves, without leaving the resource's Rules tab.

## When to use

- A resource runs an ordered list of rules, each made of conditions and actions (request and response rules, firewall rules, routing).
- Conditions combine with And inside a group and Or across groups, and the order of behaviors matters.
- The rule is edited from a list inside the resource, so the drawer opens as `Add rule` or `Edit rule` and keeps the list in view behind it.

## When not to use

- Free-form pairs of a name and a value: use `edit/edit-variables`.
- A short create form of three fields or fewer: use `create/create-drawer`.
- A resource's own settings: use `edit/edit-resource`.
- Logic the user would rather write as code: use `edit/edit-function`.

## Building blocks

- A. Drawer and trigger — `Drawer`, `DrawerTrigger`, `Button`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelBody` (required)
- B. General — `SettingsGroup`, `Field`, `Input` (required)
- C. Phase — `SettingsGroup`, `Card`, `RadioGroup`, `FieldDescription` (optional)
- D. Criteria — `SettingsGroup`, `AttributeEditor` (grouped), `Combobox`, `Select`, `Input` (required)
- E. Behaviors — `SettingsGroup`, `Card`, `AttributeEditor`, `Select`, `Input`, `FieldDescription` (required)
- F. Status — `SettingsGroup`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Switch` (required)
- G. Footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button`, `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/edit/edit-rule-builder.md](blocks/edit/edit-rule-builder.md).

## Data

The block takes the rule it edits through props and emits the values on Save; it fetches nothing and saves nothing. `RuleBuilderRule`, `RuleBuilderCondition`, `RuleBuilderBehavior` and `RuleBuilderProps` are exported from `edit-rule-builder.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample rule the Composed state edits.

Prop: `rule`, `loading`, `error`, `defaultOpen`.

Event: `submit`.

With no `loading` set during the `submit` handler the block treats the save as done at once and closes the drawer.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/edit/edit-rule-builder.md](blocks/edit/edit-rule-builder.md).

## Do

- Show the Name error only after a failed Save, never on first render, and move focus to the first field in error.
- Read the logic aloud in the layout: and inside a group, or between groups, then the behaviors in order.
- Make every argument field follow what was picked before it, so the user never types a value the operator or behavior cannot take.
- Offer both drag and buttons to reorder behaviors and criteria; the buttons are the keyboard path.
- Filter variables and behaviors by phase, and lock the phase on an existing rule.
- Follow `skills/webkit-form` for fields and `skills/webkit-errors` for error timing.

## Don't

- Don't put a Cancel button beside Save; the drawer's close button and the overlay close it.
- Don't nest groups inside groups; one level of Or over And is the whole model.
- Don't draw criteria rows by hand; `AttributeEditor` grouped mode owns their labels, errors, limits and announcements.
- Don't let the user switch an existing rule's phase; tell them to create a rule in the other phase.
- Don't open the drawer in a medium size; condition rows need three columns side by side.
- Don't clear the form while the drawer is closing.

## Copy

- **Drawer title and trigger:** `Add rule` for a new rule, `Edit rule` for an existing one.
- **Section hints:** one sentence saying what the section decides, e.g. "The conditions that decide whether the rule runs."
- **Logic labels:** single words, e.g. "and", "or", "Then".
- **Add buttons:** verb first, e.g. "Add condition", "Add OR group", "Add behavior".
- **Errors:** "Name is required.", "Enter the variable to compare."
- **Reorder controls:** the editor names them with the row number ("Move item 2 up", "Remove behavior 2", "Reorder group 1").
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Every `Input` and `Select` trigger has a label: a `Field.Label` tied by `for`, or an `aria-label` such as "Behavior"; the criteria cells are `Field`s of the `AttributeEditor`, labelled Variable, Operator and Argument, and groups are `group`s named "Group n".
- The variable `Combobox` is a `combobox` with a `listbox` of `option`s; picking one keeps focus in the field.
- Behaviors and criteria reorder through `AttributeEditor`: a native grip button, Move up and Move down, and Alt+Arrow keys, each move announced.
- Decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to the trigger on close; motion respects reduced motion.

## States

- Default: `rule` left out; Add rule with an empty Name, the Request phase, one empty condition and one empty behavior, Active on.
- Composed: `rule` set to the sample; Edit rule for the seeded Docs rewrite rule, the phase locked with its note, one URI condition and two behaviors.
- In a list: `view/view-rule-list#EditRule` drives this drawer without its trigger (`v-model:open` from a rule's name and from Add rule) and writes the saved rule back to its row.

## Related

- `create/create-drawer` — the simpler drawer create this one extends.
- `edit/edit-variables` — a drawer for free key and value pairs; `AttributeEditor` is the component the criteria are built on.
- `view/view-rule-list` — the list of rules by phase this drawer opens from.
- `state/state-form-validation` — when errors appear after Save.
- `edit/edit-resource` — the resource settings that sit beside the Rules tab.
- `Drawer` — the side panel; see `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Composed`. Code: [blocks/edit/edit-rule-builder.md](blocks/edit/edit-rule-builder.md), `get_block("edit/edit-rule-builder", { variant })`.

# EditSchema (`edit/edit-schema`)

> The schema editing surface of a SQL database table, taken from the design sample's SQL database pages and the Console Kit's alter column and truncate dialogs: a flush `Card` holding the table's definition as a `DataTa…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/edit/edit-schema/edit-schema.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("edit/edit-schema")`
- Components: Alert, AttributeEditor, Button, Card, Checkbox, CodeEditor, ConfirmDialog, DataTable, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, Field, `FieldError`, FileDropzone, FileTokenGroup, IconButton, Input, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Select, SettingsGroup, Switch, `TableCellActions`, Tag, Toast, Tooltip, `use-file-picker`, `utils/csv`
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

schema editor; create table; add column; insert row; alter column; change column type; truncate table; table schema; database schema; column types; criar tabela; adicionar coluna; inserir linha; alterar coluna; esvaziar tabela; esquema do banco

The table schema of a SQL database: the definition of one table and the drawers and dialogs that change it. A developer creates a table with its columns, adds a column, inserts a row by hand, changes a column's type or empties a table, and stays on the same surface while each change runs. It sits behind the Create table, Add column, Insert and table menu buttons of `view/view-query-editor`. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

## When to use

- A SQL database's tables are created and changed from the console rather than only with SQL.
- A table's columns, types and constraints are shown and edited one change at a time.
- A row is added by hand to check a table, without writing an INSERT.

## When not to use

- Running SQL or reading query results: use `view/view-query-editor`.
- Rows of a resource that is not a database (variables, records): use `edit/edit-variables` or `detail/detail-dns-zone`.
- A form that creates a resource in its own page: use `create/create-page`.
- A generic item created inside a resource: use `create/create-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Definition surface — `Card`, `DataTable`, `TableCellActions`, `Tag`, `Button`, `DropdownMenu`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- B. Create table drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelBody`, `SettingsGroup`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Input` (required)
- C. Column rows — `AttributeEditor`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `FieldError` (required)
- D. CSV import and foreign keys — `FileDropzone`, `FileTokenGroup` (optional)
- E. Add column drawer — `Switch` (required)
- F. Insert row drawer — `PanelFooter` (required)
- G. Change type dialog — `ConfirmDialog`, `CodeEditor` (required)
- H. Truncate table dialog — `ConfirmDialog`, `CodeEditor`, `Input` (required)
- Outcome toasts — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/edit/edit-schema.md](blocks/edit/edit-schema.md).

## Data

The block takes its tables through props and emits every change; it runs no SQL and fakes no request. `SchemaEditorTable`, `SchemaEditorProps` and the payload types are exported from `edit-schema.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample database the block renders when `tables` is left out.

Prop: `tables`, `database`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:dialog`, `v-model:table`, `defaultDraft`, `defaultCsv`, `defaultColumn`, `defaultRow`, `defaultAlterColumn`, `defaultSubmitted`.

Event: `create-table`, `add-column`, `insert-row`, `change-type`, `truncate`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/edit/edit-schema.md](blocks/edit/edit-schema.md).

## Do

- Validate on submit, then keep each error next to what caused it: the field, the column row or the list.
- Keep the drawer open and its values intact when the server refuses; say so in the section `Alert`.
- Show the SQL a destructive or rebuilding change will run before it runs.
- Ask for the table name before truncating it.
- Build the column and foreign key rows on `AttributeEditor`, so drag, keyboard moves, focus and announcements match every other row editor.
- End every change with a toast whose action continues the work on the same table.

## Don't

- Don't validate column names on every keystroke; wait for the first submit.
- Don't put a deploy action (Edit, Redeploy, View deployments) on a schema change.
- Don't let a primary key be nullable; lock Not null while Primary key is on.
- Don't drop rows on a type change silently; warn that values that don't fit make it fail.
- Don't close the Create table drawer on a server error.

## Copy

- **Titles:** `Create table`, `Add column`, `Insert row`, `Change the type of <column>`, `Truncate <table>`.
- **Buttons:** the title's verb and object: `Create table`, `Add column`, `Insert row`, `Change type`, `Truncate table`; Cancel beside each.
- **Errors:** `This field is required.`, `Start with a letter or an underscore; use letters, numbers and underscores.`, `Another column is also named email.`, `Add at least one named column.`, `customers already has a column named email.`, `email cannot be NULL. Enter a value.`
- **Server rejection:** `The table wasn't created. A table named customers already exists in acme-store. Your columns are kept; pick another name and create it again.`
- **Toasts:** as in building block H.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case except the product's object names (`Create table`), no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Each drawer's content is a `form` named by its title; the `fieldset` carries a visually hidden `legend` and is disabled while the request runs.
- `Field` wires every label, description and error to its control; column row controls without a visible label are named `Name of column 2`, `Type of column 2`, `Default value of column 2`.
- Column reordering comes from `AttributeEditor`: a real grip `button`, Move up and Move down, and Alt+Arrow keys, so dragging is never the only way (WCAG 2.5.7); each move is announced and focus stays on the moved row.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label` that matches its `Tooltip`; the per-column menu trigger names its column.
- The read-only `CodeEditor`s are named (`Statements that will run`) and can be selected and copied.
- Drawers and dialogs trap focus, close on Escape and return focus to the button that opened them.

## States

- CreateTable: `dialog` left at `create`: the Create table drawer open on a new table, with the default id and created_at columns.
- AddColumn: `dialog="column"` with `defaultColumn` phone as varchar, in the Add column drawer.
- InsertRow: `dialog="row"` with `defaultRow` and `defaultSubmitted`: the Insert row drawer after a submit with email empty, showing the NOT NULL error.
- ChangeType: `dialog="alter"` with `defaultAlterColumn` email: the Change type dialog with the statements that will run.
- TruncateTable: `dialog="truncate"`: the Truncate customers dialog waiting for the typed name.
- ImportCsv: `defaultCsv` and `defaultDraft.relations`: Create table with subscribers.csv read (six columns, six rows, a quoted comma) and one foreign key, customer_id to customers.id on delete cascade.
- Error: `error` with `defaultDraft.name` customers: Create table refused by the server because customers already exists; Alert in General and the Name field invalid.

## Related

- `view/view-query-editor` — the database page whose buttons open these drawers and dialogs.
- `create/create-drawer` — the drawer recipe these drawers follow.
- `edit/edit-delete-dialog` — the typed confirmation Truncate table follows.
- `state/state-form-validation` (SectionRejected) — the rule for the server's name conflict.
- `state/state-async-submit` — the long-action rule; schema changes use item actions, not Edit and Redeploy.
- `CodeEditor`, `Select`, `Field` — see `skills/webkit-form` and `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

`CreateTable` (primary) · `AddColumn` · `InsertRow` · `ChangeType` · `TruncateTable` · `ImportCsv` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/edit/edit-schema.md](blocks/edit/edit-schema.md), `get_block("edit/edit-schema", { variant })`.

# EditVariables (`edit/edit-variables`)

> A key/value editor, drawn as a variables list page and the Create variable drawer its heading action opens.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/edit/edit-variables/edit-variables.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("edit/edit-variables")`
- Components: Alert, AttributeEditor, Button, Card, Checkbox, CollectionPreferences, ConfigProvider, ConfirmDialog, DataTable, `DataTablePagination`, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`, IconButton, Input, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupInput`, `InputGroupRoot`, Kbd, MultiSelect, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PropertyFilter, SettingsGroup, Switch, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellId`, `TableCellLink`, `TableCellTime`, Textarea, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, `use-collection`, `use-file-picker`, `use-shortcuts`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-create-surface`

## Asked as

variables; environment variables; env vars; secrets; create variable; edit variable; variables list; variáveis; variáveis de ambiente; segredos; criar variável; key value editor; attribute editor; .env upload; editor de chave e valor; delete variable; clone variable; paste .env; paste env file; import .env; colar .env; importar variáveis; dotenv; network list; ip list; asn list; country list; bulk paste; lista de rede; lista de ips; lista de red; variables page; variables block; environment variables page; list of variables; página de variáveis

A list of key and value pairs and the drawer that edits them, here environment variables. The user scans the variables already defined, then opens Create variable to type or paste several pairs at once, mark the sensitive ones as secret, and select where they apply (the whole account, or specific environments, projects, services or policies) before saving them in one step. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use the variables block for a list of key/value variables with a create/edit drawer; the key/value field itself is the AttributeEditor component.
- Users define many free-form pairs of a name and a value (environment variables, headers, metadata, tags) and often bring them from a file.
- Some values are sensitive and must be masked and write-only once saved.
- Each pair applies to a scope the user picks from existing resources.

## When not to use

- Conditions and actions evaluated in order: use `edit/edit-rule-builder`.
- A fixed set of named settings on one resource: use `edit/edit-resource` or `settings/settings-form`.
- A short read-only list of related records inside a settings tab: use `detail/detail-domains-card`.
- A long document or code the user edits as text: use `edit/edit-function`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `ConfigProvider`, `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Controls row — `PropertyFilter`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- C. Variables table — `Card`, `DataTable`, `TableCellId`, `TableCellLink`, `TableCellTime`, `Tooltip` (required)
- D. Row actions — `TableCellActions`, `DropdownMenu` (required)
- E. Create and edit drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelBody` (required)
- F. Variables section — `SettingsGroup`, `Button`, `ToggleGroup` (required)
- G. Key and value rows — `AttributeEditor`, `Field`, `InputGroupRoot`, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupInput`, `Input`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Checkbox`, `FieldError` (required)
- H. Paste .env panel — `Button`, `Textarea`, `FieldDescription` (optional)
- I. JSON view — `Textarea`, `FieldDescription` (optional)
- J. Scope — `SettingsGroup`, `InputGroupRoot`, `InputGroupAddon`, `MultiSelect`, `Input`, `Switch`, `FieldError` (required)
- K. Drawer footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)
- L. List states — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- M. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input`, `Button` (required)
- N. Network list drawer — `Drawer`, `SettingsGroup`, `ToggleGroup`, `Button`, `Textarea`, `FieldDescription`, `AttributeEditor`, `MultiSelect` (optional)
- O. Shortcut keycap — `Kbd` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/edit/edit-variables.md](blocks/edit/edit-variables.md).

## Data

The block takes its variables through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing and saves nothing. `VariablesVariable`, `VariablesScope`, `VariablesDraft`, `VariablesSavePayload` and `VariablesProps` are exported from `edit-variables.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample variables the block renders when `variables` is left out (and never while `loading` is set).

The block is a folder. `edit-variables.vue` is the wiring: the props, the list rows, the row actions and the save. `parts/` holds its regions: `variables-list.vue` (the controls row and the table, on `useCollection`), `variables-drawer-form.vue` (the drawer form with its header, alert, fieldset and Save), `variables-entries.vue` (the Variables section: rows, JSON view and import tools), `variables-scope-group.vue` (the Scope section), `paste-panel.vue` with `env-paste-panel.vue` (the inline paste panel), and `network-list-fields.vue` (the network list sections). `composables/use-variables-form.ts` owns the drawer form state and validation and provides it to the parts, `composables/use-network-list-form.ts` does the same for the network list, and `lib/` holds the pure helpers (the `.env` and JSON parsing, the scopes, the row updates, the network list rules). The PasteEnv and NetworkList variants render the same parts with their own sample text from `sample.ts`. `webkit add` copies every file listed in `block.json` `files`.

Prop: `variables`, `loading`, `saving`, `saveError`, `defaultOpen`, `now`.

Event: `refresh`, `save`, `clone`, `delete`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/edit/edit-variables.md](blocks/edit/edit-variables.md).

## Do

- Validate only after Save is pressed; then flag each empty, malformed or duplicated key under its own pair and move focus to the first field in error.
- Keep secret values masked in the list and in the drawer, and say in the hint that secrets are write-only once saved.
- Let users bring pairs in bulk: Upload, Paste .env, paste into a key, or edit as JSON.
- Before pasted pairs land, say how many were found, which lines are skipped and which keys will be replaced.
- Build the rows on `AttributeEditor` so add, remove, focus and announcements behave the same on every key and value editor.
- Keep the label of each field inside its `InputGroupAddon`, tied to the field by `for`.
- Reset the drawer on open so a closed and reopened drawer never shows stale rows.
- Follow `skills/webkit-form` for required states and `skills/webkit-lists` for the list page.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/shell-console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't show required errors on first render or while the user is still typing the first pair.
- Don't offer Remove on the last remaining pair.
- Don't drop invalid pasted lines silently, and don't add duplicate keys from a paste: replace the existing value and say so.
- Don't reveal a saved secret value in the table, a tooltip or the copy control.
- Don't add a Cancel button beside Save; the drawer's close button and the overlay close it.
- Don't keep Global on together with a specific scope.

## Copy

- **Title and create action:** "Variables" and "Create variable"; the drawer title repeats "Create variable", or reads "Edit variable" from a row.
- **Empty states:** "No variables yet" / "Create a variable to store a value your services read at runtime."; "No matching variables" / "No variable matches these filters."
- **Delete dialog:** title and danger button "Delete variable"; the prompt reads "Type API_BASE_URL to confirm."
- **Field placeholders:** show the format, e.g. "MY_VARIABLE" for the key, "my-variable-value" for the value.
- **Toasts:** "API_KEY created.", "3 variables created.", "API_KEY updated.", "API_KEY cloned as API_KEY_COPY.", "API_KEY deleted."; save failure "Variables not saved. You are offline; check your connection and save again."
- **Errors:** short and specific, e.g. "Key is required.", "Use only uppercase letters, numbers, and underscores.", "Select at least one resource for this scope."
- **Secret control:** "Mark as secret" and "Unmark as secret"; the hint states the rule, e.g. "Secret values are hidden and write-only after saving."
- **Network list:** title "Create network list"; types "IP/CIDR", "ASN", "Countries"; panel label "Paste one address per line"; report "7 entries found. Text after # is kept as the comment.", "Lines 4 and 8 are not an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range; they are added with an error to fix.", "Line 7 is already in the list and will be skipped."; row error "198.51.100.300 is not an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range."; toast "Office and partners created."
- **Paste panel:** label "Paste .env contents"; report "3 variables found. Lines starting with # are ignored.", "Line 5 is not KEY=value with an uppercase key and will be skipped.", "CACHE_TTL is already in the list; its value will be replaced."; buttons "Paste .env", "Add 3 variables", "Cancel".
- **Buttons:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Upload", "Add variable", "Save".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Every key and value field has a visible `label` in its addon; an invalid field sets `aria-invalid` and points to its `FieldError` through `aria-describedby`.
- Icon-only controls (Remove variable, Show value, Hide value, row actions, toolbar) carry an `aria-label` that matches their `Tooltip`.
- The Secret `Checkbox` and each scope `Switch` have an `aria-label` naming what they toggle, e.g. "Enable Project scope".
- The `ToggleGroup` is labeled "Variables view"; the Upload button opens the system file picker through `useFilePicker`, so no hidden input sits in the tab order.
- Adding a pair moves focus to its new Key field; removing one moves focus to the pair now in its place (or Add variable); both are announced in a polite live region by `AttributeEditor`.
- The paste panel's `Textarea` is described by its report, so skipped lines and replaced keys are read with the field; Paste .env exposes `aria-expanded`, and applying announces how many variables were added.
- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to Create variable on close.
- `/` focuses the property filter from anywhere on the page, except while typing in a field.
- The table rows are one tab stop: Arrow Up and Arrow Down move between rows, Home and End jump to the first and last, Enter opens the focused variable in the edit drawer as the row menu's Edit does, and Delete or Backspace opens the delete dialog. After a delete, focus lands on the next row.
- `⌘ Enter` (`Ctrl Enter` off Apple) submits the open drawer's form from any field, the same as Save, in the create and edit drawer, the Paste .env drawer and the network list drawer. Save carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and a `Kbd` keycap.

## States

- List: the variables list page with the controls row and table, from `variables` (the sample when left out); the drawer is closed. `loading` spins Refresh and puts the table in its loading state.
- First use: `variables` is `[]`; the card holds the state-first-use `EmptyState` with Create variable.
- No match: the filter matches nothing; the table shows the no-match `EmptyState` with Clear filters.
- Edit: a row's Edit opens the drawer on that variable; Save emits `save` with the variable and replaces it in the list and raises "<KEY> updated.".
- Save failed: `saveError` is set when the save ends; the drawer stays open with its rows and a danger `Alert` above the sections.
- Delete: a row's Delete opens the typed confirmation; confirming emits `delete`, removes the row and raises "<KEY> deleted.".
- Create: `defaultOpen`; the drawer open with one empty pair, the Form view and Global on; errors appear only after Save.
- PasteEnv: Create variable opens the drawer with one pair and the Paste .env panel holding a pasted file with a comment, an `export`, a skipped lowercase line and a repeated key that is already in the list; Add 3 variables merges them.
- NetworkList: Create network list opens the drawer named Office and partners, type IP/CIDR, with the Paste list panel holding nine lines: a comment line, two lines that are not valid addresses and one already pasted above; Add 7 entries appends them as rows, the two invalid ones showing their errors.

## Related

- `create/create-drawer` — the general drawer create pattern this drawer follows.
- `view/view-table` — the controls row and table recipe the list page reuses.
- `edit/edit-rule-builder` — a drawer for ordered conditions and behaviors instead of free pairs.
