# SettingsApiKey (`settings/settings-api-key`)

> Integration API key management: the reader picks an external provider or integration (such as GitHub, an AI model provider, or an observability service) in a `Select`, pastes a key in a masked `PasswordInput` (never p…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/settings/settings-api-key/settings-api-key.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("settings/settings-api-key")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, ConfirmDialog, `FieldError`, Item, PageHeader, PasswordInput, Select, SettingsRow, StatusIndicator, Subheader
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

integration api key; provider api key; external api key; github integration key; github api key; connect third party integration; bring your own key; byok; model provider api key; test api key; chave de api de integração; chave de api do github; usar minha própria chave de api; chave de api do provedor; clave de api de integración; usar mi propia clave de api

The place a reader connects an external service or platform integration with an API key — such as GitHub, an AI model provider (bring your own key), an observability tool, or any future third-party integration. They pick a provider, paste the key once, check that it works, and can replace or remove it later. The key is never shown again after it is saved; only its masked tail says which key is in place. The block stores nothing and calls no provider: it emits `save`, `test` and `remove`, and the app's key store does the work (a backend integration store, or TanStack AI's `useByok` for browser-held model keys). It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`, rendered in the layout's default slot; the same body fits a settings tab.

## When to use

- Any part of the platform that connects to an external service with a user-supplied API key or token: GitHub integration, AI model providers (BYOK), observability or alerting providers (Datadog, Slack), deployment services, or future third-party integrations.
- One key per provider, picked from a short list of supported integrations (or a single-item list for a dedicated integration settings page).
- A settings page or tab where the reader saves, replaces, tests and removes that key.

## When not to use

- Creating or revoking the platform's own access tokens for scripts and tools: use `account/account-personal-tokens`.
- A secret a resource needs at run time (an environment variable): use `edit/edit-variables`.
- Picking the model for one AI conversation: use the model picker in `ai/ai-chat`.
- General settings that are not about external provider keys: use `settings/settings-form`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Key card — `Subheader`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Select`, `PasswordInput`, `FieldError`, `StatusIndicator` (required)
- C. Actions — `Button` (required)
- D. Failure — `Alert` (Error only)
- E. Remove confirmation — `ConfirmDialog` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/settings/settings-api-key.md](blocks/settings/settings-api-key.md).

## Data

The block takes the providers, the saved keys' masked tails and the request states through props and emits what the reader asked for; it never holds a saved key, stores nothing and calls no provider. `SettingsApiKeyProvider`, `SettingsApiKeySavedKey`, `SettingsApiKeySaveValue`, `SettingsApiKeyStatus` and `SettingsApiKeyProps` are exported from `settings-api-key.vue`; `sample.ts` holds the providers and the saved key the page renders when `providers` and `savedKeys` are left out (`props.savedKeys ?? sampleSavedKeys`: `loading` and `error` here are a save or a test, not a load, so they do not empty the list).

Prop: `title`, `description`, `providers`, `savedKeys`, `status`, `loading`, `error`, `storageNote`.

Model: `v-model:provider`, `v-model:apiKey`.

Event: `save`, `test`, `remove`.

For browser-only AI bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with TanStack AI, wire the same events to `defineByok()` / `useByok(byok)` (`byok.update`, `byok.unlock`, `byok.clear`), await `byok.ready()` before rendering so the page does not flash `No key saved`, pass `title="Model provider keys"`, and set `storage-note="Saved in this browser only and sent with your own requests to the provider."`. For a single-integration screen such as GitHub settings, pass a one-item `providers` array (`[{ value: 'github', label: 'GitHub' }]`) and a tailored `title` and `description`. Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/settings/settings-api-key.md](blocks/settings/settings-api-key.md).

## Do

- Keep the key field empty on every visit; show only the masked tail of a saved key.
- Clear the field once the save succeeds, so the key does not stay in the page.
- Say where the key is kept in `storageNote`, and make it true for the app (workspace server vs browser).
- Report the test result in the status row and announce it; put the provider's message in the `Alert`.
- Ask before removing a key, and name what stops working.

## Don't

- Don't prefill the key field, put a sample key in a placeholder, or show a key format (`ghp_…`, `sk-…`).
- Don't store the key, log it or send it anywhere but the app's key store from the `save` handler.
- Don't test a key automatically on every keystroke; the reader runs Test connection.
- Don't render a `Sidebar`, `AppHeader` or `<main>` in the page; `ConsoleLayout` owns them.
- Don't toast a test failure; it stays on the page beside the key it is about.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Integration keys`; description: `Connect external services and integrations with your own API keys.` (Override per integration or surface.)
- **Card heading:** `Connection`. **Rows:** `Provider` — `The integration or service the key belongs to.`; `API key` — the storage note, by default `Encrypted and stored for your workspace; sent only with requests to the selected provider.`; `Status` — `Whether a key is saved for this provider and if it works.`
- **Status:** `No key saved`, `Saved`, `Testing`, `Connected`, `Connection failed`; the masked tail as given, e.g. `••••3f9a`.
- **Actions:** `Save key` (`Replace key` once a key is saved), `Test connection`, `Remove key`; in the `Alert`, `Test again`.
- **Field error:** `Enter an API key.`
- **Failure:** title `The key didn't work.` with the provider's message and the action `Test again` (test); title `The key wasn't saved.` with the message and no action (save).
- **Remove:** title `Remove the <provider> key?`; description `Features and integrations that use <provider> stop working until you save a new key.`; confirm `Remove key`.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- No `main` of its own (the layout's is the only one); the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`, the card's `Subheader` is an `h2`.
- The `form` is named by the page title; the Select trigger and the key field carry `aria-label`s matching their row titles, and the field's description is tied with `aria-describedby`.
- Focus order: Provider, API key, its reveal toggle, Remove key, Test connection, Save key / Replace key, then the `Alert`'s Test again.
- An empty submit sets `aria-invalid` on the field, adds the `FieldError` to its `aria-describedby` and moves focus to it.
- Focus is never lost: Save key / Replace key keeps focus while it spins; after a save or a confirmed removal, focus moves to the API key field.
- The status row is a `role="status"` region, so test results are announced; the `Alert` is announced when it appears.
- The `ConfirmDialog` traps focus, is named by its title and returns focus to Remove key.

## States

- Saved: the default props; GitHub has a saved key, not tested: Saved with its masked tail, Test connection, Remove key and Replace key.
- Empty: `savedKeys` is `[]`; the status reads No key saved and only Save key shows.
- Saving: `loading` with a typed replacement key (`v-model:apiKey`), the only way a save starts; every control but Replace key locks and Replace key spins.
- Testing: `status="running"`; Testing with a spinner, Remove key and the Provider lock, Replace key stays available.
- Success: `status="success"`; the status reads Connected.
- Error: `status="error"` with `error`; the status reads Connection failed and the danger `Alert` gives the provider's message with Test again.
- SaveError: `error` with `status="pending"` and the typed key still in the field (`v-model:apiKey`); the `Alert` says `The key wasn't saved.` with no action; Replace key retries.

- `settings/settings-form` — the settings layout and the per-card save this page follows.
- `account/account-personal-tokens` — the platform's own access tokens for scripts and tools.
- `edit/edit-variables` — runtime secrets and environment variables attached to a resource.
- `ai/ai-chat` — an AI surface that can run on a model provider key saved through this block.
- `skills/webkit-ai-surfaces` — where AI settings sit and what they disclose when used for BYOK.

# SettingsCannedResponses (`settings/settings-canned-responses`)

> The admin page for the saved replies support agents insert into a ticket (macros, canned responses, saved replies): a `PageHeader` with New response, a `PropertyFilter` that searches title and body and filters by fold…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/settings/settings-canned-responses/settings-canned-responses.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("settings/settings-canned-responses")`
- Stability: preview. The API may still change in a minor release, named in the changelog, until the owner marks it GA.
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, Combobox, ConfigProvider, ConfirmDialog, DataTable, `DataTablePagination`, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, IconButton, Input, MarkdownEditor, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PropertyFilter, RadioGroup, Select, Table, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellTime`, Tag, Tooltip, `use-collection`, `use-locale`, `use-unsaved-changes`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

canned responses; saved replies; macros; support macros; reply templates; response templates; email templates for agents; insert placeholder; template variables; respostas prontas; respostas salvas; macros de atendimento; modelos de resposta; respostas padrão

The admin page for the saved replies support agents insert into a ticket. Zendesk calls them macros, Freshdesk canned responses, Help Scout saved replies. An admin or an agent finds a response by its title or its text, files it in a folder, decides who can insert it, writes the reply in Markdown with placeholders the app fills in for each ticket (the requester's first name, the ticket number, the agent's signature), and can move the ticket to a status when the reply is sent. The list shows which replies the team actually uses. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Reusable replies, macros or snippets that agents insert into a ticket, a chat or an email.
- Any library of text templates with folders, a visibility scope and placeholders, managed from a list and edited in a drawer.

## When not to use

- Replies the product sends on its own when a rule matches (auto-replies, triggers): start from `edit/edit-rule-builder`.
- One notification email with a fixed set of options: use `settings/settings-form`.
- Answering a ticket: the agent's reply box is `MarkdownEditor` in the ticket view; the ticket list is `view/view-ticket-inbox`.
- Deleting with a typed confirmation, for a response library shared by many teams: open `edit/edit-delete-dialog` instead of the plain confirmation.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `ConfigProvider`, `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Search row — `PropertyFilter`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- C. Load failure — `Alert` (conditional)
- D. First use — `Card`, `EmptyState` (conditional)
- E. Response table — `DataTable`, `DataTablePagination`, `Tag`, `TableCellTime`, `useCollection`, `useLocale` (required)
- F. Row actions — `TableCellActions`, `DropdownMenu` (required)
- G. No match — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- H. Editor drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter` (required)
- I. Fields — `Field`, `Input`, `Combobox`, `RadioGroup`, `Select` (required)
- J. Reply and placeholders — `MarkdownEditor`, `DropdownMenu`, `Button` (required)
- K. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/settings/settings-canned-responses.md](blocks/settings/settings-canned-responses.md).

## Data

The block takes its responses through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing and saves nothing. `CannedResponsesResponse`, `CannedResponsesPlaceholder`, `CannedResponsesValues`, `CannedResponsesVisibility`, `CannedResponsesTicketStatus` and `CannedResponsesProps` are exported from `settings-canned-responses.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the six sample responses, the placeholders and the clock the block renders when `responses`, `placeholders` and `now` are left out (the responses never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `responses`, `placeholders`, `loading`, `error`, `saving`, `saveError`, `now`, `defaultQuery`, `editorOpen`, `editingKey`.

Event: `create`, `update`, `duplicate`, `remove`, `refresh`, `retry`.

Delete removes the row at once; when the request fails, the page says so in a toast and refreshes, and the fresh `responses` array brings the row back. Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/settings/settings-canned-responses.md](blocks/settings/settings-canned-responses.md).

## Do

- Name a response after the question it answers (`Ask for the request ID`), so an agent finds it by searching.
- Offer the placeholders from a menu that shows what each one stands for; few writers remember the paths.
- Show how often each response is used, so the team can retire the ones nobody sends.
- Keep the typed values when a save fails, and say the previous version still applies.

## Don't

- Don't use the `@` mention menu for placeholders; it inserts a handle, not a placeholder.
- Don't let two responses share a title; agents pick by title.
- Don't make Everyone the default visibility; a new response starts Personal.
- Don't close the drawer before the save succeeds.
- Don't drop a typed draft on Escape, an overlay tap or Cancel; ask with the unsaved-changes dialog first.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Canned responses`; description `Saved replies agents insert into a ticket, with the requester's details filled in.`
- **Actions:** `New response`, `Edit`, `Duplicate`, `Delete`, `Save response`, `Cancel`, `Insert placeholder`, `Retry`, `Clear filters`. Verb first, sentence case.
- **Drawer:** titles `New response`, `Edit response`; one sentence under the title that says where the response is used: `Agents insert it from the reply box of a ticket. Placeholders are filled in for each ticket.`
- **Fields:** `Title`, `Folder`, `Visibility`, `Reply`, `Also set the ticket status to`. Each description says how to fill the field, in one sentence: Title `Agents search for it by title, so name what the reply answers.`; Folder `Pick a folder or type a new name to create one. Leave it empty for no folder.`; Reply `Markdown. A placeholder such as the requester's name is written in double braces.`; status `Applied when the agent sends the reply.`; each visibility option says who can insert it (below). Errors say what to do: `Enter a title.`, `A response with this title already exists. Use another title.`, `Write the reply agents insert.`
- **Visibility:** `Personal` (Only you can insert it.), `Team` (Everyone in your team can insert it.), `Everyone` (Every agent of the account can insert it.).
- **Table:** `No folder`, `Never used`. The Uses column is the number formatted for the locale (`1,200`); the narrow summary picks the plural form with `plural` from `useLocale` (`1 use`, `12 uses`), never a word glued to a number.
- **First use:** `No canned responses yet`, then what they are and what they save. **No match:** `No matching responses`, `No canned response matches this search or these filters.`
- **Errors:** load `The canned responses could not be loaded. Nothing was changed; try again.`; save after an edit `The response wasn't saved. Agents still insert the previous version; save again to apply your changes.`; save of a new response `The response wasn't saved. Save again to create it.`
- **Delete:** title `Delete response`; description `Agents can no longer insert “<title>”. Replies already sent keep their text. You cannot undo this.`; button `Delete response`.
- **Toasts (sent by the page):** `Response “<title>” saved.` after a create or an update, `Copy of “<title>” created.` after Duplicate, `Response “<title>” deleted.` after Delete, and `“<title>” wasn't deleted. It is back in the list.` when a delete fails.
- **Placeholders:** the label says what is filled in (`Requester first name`); the token is code (`{{ticket.requester.first_name}}`) and is never translated.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- No `main` of its own (the layout's is the only one); the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`, and the drawer title names the drawer.
- Focus order: New response, the search, Refresh, the table rows (one tab stop: Arrow Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Enter opens Edit, Delete asks to delete), the row menus, the pagination.
- The search and Refresh carry an `aria-label`; each row menu is named `Actions for <title>`.
- The drawer traps focus, opens on its first field and returns focus to the control that opened it. After Save, the first invalid field takes focus and its `Field.Error` is announced (`role="alert"`). A save error is a danger `Alert` at the top of the body.
- Insert placeholder is a menu button; after a pick, focus returns to the reply field with the caret after the token. Each token renders `dir="ltr"` inside a `bdi`, so it reads in order in a right-to-left page.
- The delete dialog names the response; after it closes the focused row's place goes to the next row, as `DataTable` does. The page's toast announces the outcome of save, duplicate and delete; the block itself announces nothing else.
- User data reads in its own direction: the title, the reply excerpt and the folder render with `dir="auto"`, the Title field and the reply field set it too, and the delete dialog wraps the title in Unicode isolates (U+2068, U+2069) because its sentence is a string. Placeholder tokens are `dir="ltr"` in a `bdi`.
- Layout uses logical sides only; at 320 px the controls row wraps, the table keeps Title and the menu with the other values under the title, and the drawer takes the full width.

## States

- Default: six responses in four folders and three visibilities, sorted by use, with search, filters, row menus, the editor drawer, placeholders and delete wired.
- Empty: first use (`responses` is `[]`); the explanation and New response replace the search and the table.
- Loading: the first load (`loading` with no `responses`); the search row and the table's loading rows.
- Error: the list did not load (`error` is set); a danger Alert with Retry replaces the table.
- NoMatch: filters that match nothing (`defaultQuery` with folder Billing and visibility Personal); No matching responses with Clear filters.
- Editing: the drawer open on one response (`editorOpen` with `editingKey`).
- Saving: the drawer locked while the save runs (`saving`).
- SaveError: the save failed (`saveError` is set); the alert at the top of the drawer, values kept.

- `view/view-ticket-inbox` — the ticket list; its statuses are the ones a response can set.
- `account/account-personal-tokens` — the same list, drawer and confirmation pattern.

# SettingsForm (`settings/settings-form`)

> A settings form and its save strategy, one variant per strategy.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/settings/settings-form/settings-form.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("settings/settings-form")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, ConfirmDialog, CopyButton, Field, `FieldError`, Input, Item, Kbd, LanguageSelect, Link, PageHeader, SaveBar, Select, SettingsGroup, SettingsRow, Skeleton, Subheader, Switch, Tag, Textarea, Toast, `use-unsaved-changes`
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ux-heuristics`

## Asked as

account settings form; organization or account settings; save all; single save for the page; sticky footer save; save as one unit; cancel and save footer; salvar tudo; rodapé fixo com salvar; formulário de conta; save per group; save per section; preferences page; grouped settings save; section save button; independent groups; salvar por grupo; preferências; salvar por seção; save per card; card with its own save; project settings; configuration cards; independent saves; long settings page; salvar por card; configurações do projeto; salvar cada seção; account settings; account profile; profile page; user profile; my profile; my account; organization settings; company information; login settings; danger zone; configurações da conta; perfil; página de perfil; minha conta; configuración de la cuenta

The place the user goes to change how an account or a project behaves. They scan a few topics, change one or two values, and commit them knowing exactly what the save covers. The block is one layout with three save strategies: one save for a form that is one logical unit, one save per group, or one save per card on a long configuration page. The Profile variant is the full account profile page, the layout every account settings page (billing details, credentials, users, teams) follows. The save model follows how the page is partitioned, not the container. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the breadcrumbs, the ⌘K palette and the `<main>`.

## When to use

- Use settings-form for account or organization settings (profile, preferences, notifications), choosing SaveAll, SavePerGroup or SavePerCard.
- Account-level settings read as rows of a label, a description and a control (Profile, Preferences, Notifications): SaveAll.
- Topics on one page that the user commits independently, such as General and Notifications: SavePerGroup.
- A long configuration page where each topic needs an explanation and its own commit, such as Preview Toolbar and Deployment Protection: SavePerCard.
- The signed-in account's full profile page, with its sections, MFA link, source control and Delete account: Profile.

## When not to use

- The settings tab or settings page of one resource, with anchored sections and an unsaved-changes bar: use `edit/edit-resource`.
- Changing the plan: use `account/account-change-plan-drawer`.
- Creating a resource: use `create/create-page` or `create/create-drawer`.
- Walking every submit outcome (invalid fields, server rejection): use `state/state-form-validation`.
- Deleting the account or a resource from a settings page: open `edit/edit-delete-dialog` (its SettingsRow variant) from an outlined row.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. FeatureItem sections — `Subheader`, `Card`, `Item` (required)
- C. Setting rows — `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `FieldError`, `Select`, `LanguageSelect`, `Switch` (required)
- D. Save — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)
- E. Profile sections — `SettingsRow`, `Card`, `Item`, `Input`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Button` (Profile only)
- F. Shortcut keycap — `Kbd` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/settings/settings-form.md](blocks/settings/settings-form.md).

## Data

The SaveAll form takes the saved profile and the save request's state through props and emits the values; it fetches nothing and fakes no save. `SettingsFormProfile` and `SettingsFormProps` are exported from `settings-form.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample profile the form opens on when `profile` is left out. The form keeps its own draft; `profile` is the baseline that Discard returns to, and a new `profile` resets the form to it. The SavePerGroup, SavePerCard and Profile variants work the same way: they fetch nothing and fake no save. SavePerGroup takes `general` and `notifications`, SavePerCard takes `previewToolbar` and `deploymentProtection`, each an object of that card's `values`, `defaultDraft`, `loading` and `error`, and both emit `submit(event, { group | card, values })`. Profile takes `profile`, `loading` and `error` for the first load (Retry emits `retry`), `saving` and `saveError` for the save (Save emits `submit(event, values)`), and `deleting` for Delete account (the confirmed dialog emits `delete` and closes when `deleting` ends).

Prop: `profile`, `defaultDraft`, `loading`, `error`.

Event: `submit`, `discard`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/settings/settings-form.md](blocks/settings/settings-form.md).

## Do

- Pick the save strategy from how the page is partitioned: one logical unit gets one save.
- Disable only the fieldset being saved; the other groups or cards stay editable.
- Drive Save's `:loading` and the fieldset's `disabled` from one `submitting` flag.
- Validate on submit only, show the error at the field it belongs to, and move focus to the first field in error.
- Keep every control in a row at the same size, and every row title in sentence case.
- Explain a card's effect in an info `Alert` at the top of the card, before its fields.
- In Profile, keep preferences that apply immediately (Appearance) and external connections (Source control) out of Save, and say so in their section hints; put destructive actions in the last section, behind a type-to-confirm `ConfirmDialog`.

## Don't

- Don't render a `Sidebar`, `AppHeader`, `Command` palette or `<main>` in the page; `ConsoleLayout` owns them.
- Don't mix a page-level `SaveBar` with per-card Save buttons on the same page.
- Don't put Save in the page heading or float it beside a single field.
- Don't flag empty required fields before the user presses Save.
- Don't add an error summary block or an `Alert` for field validation; the field's own state is the feedback.
- Don't put a consequence or a constraint in the row title; it goes in the description or the `Alert`.
- Don't toast a field-level server rejection; it goes to an `Alert` in the owning section with the row's control invalid.

## Copy

- **Page title:** the page's name, e.g. "Profile"; description: one sentence with a period, e.g. "Define and manage personal account preferences."
- **Breadcrumb** (the route meta `ConsoleLayout` reads): the parent, then the page title exactly, e.g. "Account settings" › "Profile".
- **Choices:** sentence case and no parentheses, e.g. "Team default", "Standard protection".
- **Section heading:** a short topic noun, e.g. "General", "Notifications".
- **Row title:** names the setting in one to three words, e.g. "Timezone"; description: one sentence with a period, e.g. "Times across the app are shown in this zone."
- **Save:** exactly "Save" for the footer and every group or card; Discard is exactly "Discard", never "Cancel": it restores the saved values and the reader stays on the page.
- **Errors:** what is wrong plus what to do, e.g. "Enter a valid email address."
- **Docs link:** names the topic, e.g. "Learn more about the Preview Toolbar".
- **Profile:** section hints are one sentence on what the group affects ("The company that owns the account, as it appears on every invoice."); optional fields say it in the description ("Optional. Apartment, suite or floor."); the destructive row uses one verb for the title and the button ("Delete personal account" with "Delete account", never "Remove"); the save bar reads "You have unsaved changes."; the load failure reads "The profile could not be loaded. Nothing was changed; try again." with "Retry"; the app confirms the deletion itself once `deleting` ends
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The `form` is named by the `PageHeader` title through `aria-labelledby` and uses `novalidate`; the title is the page's only `h1`.
- Each group is a real `fieldset`; SaveAll gives it a visually hidden `legend` ("Profile settings").
- Every control has an `aria-label` that repeats its row title; errors are linked with `aria-describedby` only while they show.
- Disabling the `fieldset` while saving takes every control out of interaction at once; Save announces its loading state.
- Focus order follows reading order: the rows from top to bottom, then Discard and Save.
- `⌘ S` (`Ctrl S` off Apple) saves while the form has unsaved changes, the same as Save, and stops the browser's own save; with no changes it does nothing. Save carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and a `Kbd` keycap. The Profile variants answer it the same way.
- The save-per-card and save-per-group variants have no `SaveBar` and bind no `⌘ S`: each card or group keeps its own Save button.

## States

- SaveAll: the default props (`profile` left out renders the sample); Profile with General, Preferences and Notifications in one fieldset and one sticky Discard and Save footer.
- Saving: `loading` with an edit in `defaultDraft`; the whole fieldset and Discard are disabled and Save shows its loading state.
- SaveError: `error` with an edit in `defaultDraft`; the server rejects the save; an error toast with Retry says the changes are kept, and the form stays dirty with every entry.
- SavePerGroup: Preferences split into General and Notifications cards, each with its own secondary Save, disabled until that card changes.
- SavingOneGroup: General has an edit in flight (`loading` with a `defaultDraft`), its rows disabled while Notifications stays editable.
- SavePerCard: Project settings with Preview Toolbar and Deployment Protection cards, each with an info `Alert`, its fields and its own Save.
- SavingOneCard: Preview Toolbar has an edit in flight, its selects disabled while Deployment Protection stays editable.
- Profile: the profile filled from the account (Billing emails empty and required), save bar hidden until a saved field changes. `saveError` shows the failure toast with Retry; an empty Account name or a malformed billing address walks the field errors. Delete account opens the type-to-confirm dialog.
- ProfileLoading: the first load; `Skeleton` cards in place of the sections.
- ProfileError: the account did not load; a danger Alert with Retry.

## Related

- `edit/edit-resource` — settings of one resource, with anchored sections.
- `account/account-mfa-settings` — where Profile's Manage MFA row leads.
- `state/state-form-validation` — every outcome of a submit.
- `state/state-async-submit` — a save that runs long and reports back later.
- `edit/edit-delete-dialog` — the delete row a settings page can end with.

`SaveAll` (primary) · `Saving` · `SaveError` · `SavePerGroup` · `SavingOneGroup` · `SavePerCard` · `SavingOneCard` · `Profile` · `ProfileLoading` · `ProfileError`. Code: [blocks/settings/settings-form.md](blocks/settings/settings-form.md), `get_block("settings/settings-form", { variant })`.

# ShellConsole (`shell/shell-console`)

> The console shell as one component: `ConsoleLayout`, composed once in the app around RouterView, so a console page is only its body.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/shell/shell-console/shell-console.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("shell/shell-console")`
- Components: Alert, Avatar, Badge, Button, Card, Command, ConsoleLayout, `ConsoleLayoutRoot`, DataTable, `DataTablePagination`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, HelpPanel, HighlightButton, IconButton, Input, Item, Item, Link, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Select, StatusIndicator, `TableCellId`, `TableCellStatus`, Tabs, Tag, Toast, Tooltip, `use-color-mode`

## Asked as

platform shell; console shell; app shell; sidebar layout; navigation rail; dashboard layout; admin layout; app layout with sidebar; estrutura do console; layout com menu lateral; menu lateral; console; console layout; layout do console; notifications panel; notifications drawer; notification center; central de notificações; painel de notificações; switch account; account switcher; organization switcher; change organization; trocar conta; trocar organização; selecionar conta; console layout component; ConsoleLayout; app layout with router view; layout do console com RouterView; account list failed to load; switch account error; erro ao carregar contas; page help; help panel; info link; contextual help; ajuda da página; painel de ajuda

The application shell every signed-in page renders inside. The user browses and moves laterally between modules, so the shell keeps the whole product one step away: the navigation rail (wordmark, grouped navigation with drill-in levels, the account at its foot), one global header (breadcrumbs, search, the app's actions, the avatar) and the ⌘K palette. All of that is one component, `ConsoleLayout`: this block is the app's `App.vue` — compose it once around `RouterView` and every console page is only the body rendered through its default slot. The body here is a stand-in for `view/view-table`.

## When to use

- The root of a console app: every browse page (first-level lists, Home and dashboards, resource details with their tabs, settings) renders inside it.

## When not to use

- Create, edit and deploy flows: use the focused shell headed by `top-bar/top-bar-creation`, with no rail.
- Signed-out screens: `auth/auth-sign-in` with `top-bar/top-bar-auth`.
- Documentation and marketing: `shell/shell-docs`, `shell/shell-site`.
- A page needing the resizable split panel: compose `AppLayout` directly for that page.

## Building blocks

- A. Shell — `ConsoleLayoutRoot` (required)
- B. Actions — `Button` (required)
- C. Agent — `HighlightButton` (required)
- D. Hints — `Tooltip` (required)
- E. Icon actions — `IconButton` (required)
- F. Palette groups — `Command` (required)
- G. Account menu — `DropdownMenu` (required)
- H. Theme — `DropdownMenu.Item` radios (required)
- I. System status — `StatusIndicator` (required)
- J. Page title — `PageHeader` (stand-in body)
- K. Table frame — `Card` (stand-in body)
- L. Toast region — `Toaster` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/shell/shell-console.md](blocks/shell/shell-console.md).

## Data

`navigation`, `account` and `recents` are props (`ShellConsoleProps`, `ShellConsoleRecent` are exported from `shell-console.vue`); left out, the console tree, the account and the recents in `sample.ts` render. The app passes its navigation file and signed-in user, then deletes `sample.ts` and its import. The states render the shell and fill its slots instead of copying it:

Slot: default, `actions`, `sidebar-header`, `header-leading`, `notifications`, `tools`.

`v-model:tools-open` opens and closes the tools region, and `tools-label` names it. It emits one event:

Event: `sign-out`.

Handle it where the session lives: clear the token (`sessionStorage.removeItem`, the in-memory ref) and route to sign-in (`router.push('/login')`). When this block is the app's `App.vue`, there is no parent to listen, so either mount it with the handler (`createApp(App, { onSignOut })`) or render it from a thin `App.vue` (`<ConsoleShell @sign-out="signOut" />`). Never leave Log out as a menu item that does nothing.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/shell/shell-console.md](blocks/shell/shell-console.md).

## Do

- Compose `ConsoleLayoutRoot` once in `App.vue` and render every browse page through its default slot; replace this block's stand-in body with `<RouterView />`.
- Keep the navigation in one data file shared by the app; the rail and the palette both read it.
- Give every row an `href` (never `to` or `path`); derive a static `breadcrumbs` trail from the route.
- Let a detail page set its own trail, control crumb included, with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`.
- Open a page's help from `ConsoleLayout.ToolsTrigger` in its `PageHeader` `meta` slot, with the `HelpPanel` in `tools`.
- Frame a list or form body with `layout-boundary` + `layout-column`; open a detail body flush on `PageTabs`.

## Don't

- Don't render `AppLayout`, `Sidebar`, `AppHeader`, `SearchTrigger`, a `Command` palette or a `<main>` in a page; the layout owns them.
- Don't put a page's control crumb in `App.vue`, or size a body with `calc(100dvh - …)`.
- Don't render the rail on create, edit or deploy pages.
- Don't add page actions to the global header; they belong to the page's header, controls row or tab row.
- Don't hide the avatar when the rail is collapsed or in the drawer.
- Don't render the account switcher in both `sidebar-header` and `header-leading` at once; pick by the slots' `compact`.
- Don't leave an empty account table when the list fails to load; show the danger `Alert` with Retry in its place.
- Don't open the notifications region as a popover over the page; it is the layout's tools region beside the content.
- Don't open page help from a boxed `IconButton`, a typed `?` or a `Tooltip` beside the title; the page's `Info` link is the one way in.

## Copy

- **Palette groups:** `Recents`, `Actions`; the layout's placeholder `Search pages and commands` and its empty line come from the locale catalog.
- **Navigation and menu items:** nouns as the module pages are titled (`Personal tokens`, `Activity history`, `Build and deployment`, `Account settings`); Azion product names keep theirs (`Edge DNS`, `Real-Time Metrics`). No ampersand.
- **Status:** a short state, not a sentence: `All systems operational`.
- **Load failure:** what failed, as a sentence: `The account list could not be loaded.`; the action is `Retry`, the word every block uses (auth included).
- **Header actions:** `Create`, `Agent`.
- **Module create:** `Create` plus the entity: `Create Application`.

## Accessibility

- One `main` (the layout's), one `banner` (the header), the rail as a labelled navigation (`Main navigation`); the page body starts with its `h1` (`PageHeader`).
- ⌘K / Ctrl K opens the palette, announced through `aria-keyshortcuts` on the search; focus returns to the trigger on close.
- The rail's drawer traps focus while open, closes on `Escape` and when a row is chosen, and returns focus to the menu button.
- Icon-only controls have both an `aria-label` and a tooltip.
- The bell is a toggle (`aria-pressed`) and names the unread count; unread items carry a visually hidden `Unread:` prefix, not colour alone.

## States

- ListPage: a first-level list page in the `ConsoleLayout` default slot: no breadcrumb on a first level, the page opens on its `PageHeader` (title, description, Documentation and the create action) over the page body. The controls row and the table belong to `view/view-table`, which builds them from the Table toolbar parts; the shell does not draw them.
- DetailPage: a resource detail page rendered through `ConsoleLayout`. The page body sets its own trail with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`: Applications and the application as `items`, then the environment in its slot, a `Select` with `variant="ghost"` and `size="small"` labelled `Switch environment` (a search `Input`, each environment tagged with its deployment policy, a muted line when nothing matches, Add Environment at its foot). While compact the header hides the crumbs but keeps the environment `Select` in place of the brand, so Deploy always has its target in view; the body repeats the rest of the trail under `md` in its own `nav` row named Application (a ghost back `IconButton` to Applications and the application name). The default slot is flush and opens on a full-bleed `PageTabs` (Overview, Deployments, Settings, the outlined Deploy in `#actions`), sticky at the top of the layout's scrolling region so it stays in view while the tab content scrolls under it; no `main` of its own, the layout owns it.
- Notifications: the ListPage through `ConsoleLayout` with the bell after Create and Agent in the `actions` slot; it toggles the layout's tools region (`v-model:tools-open`, `tools-label="Notifications"`), a region beside the content and a drawer when narrow. The `tools` slot holds the list as `Item.List` of `Item` rows (`Item.Media type="icon"` toned through `data-type`, title, description, time, `Item.Actions`), five at a time with `Show older` for the rest: unread items marked with a `New` tag (and a visually hidden `Unread:` prefix), Edit and Redeploy on each deploy, Mark all as read, Clear all (it empties the list and toasts `Notifications cleared.` with Undo, which brings them back), and the EmptyState `You are all caught up` once cleared. The failed deploy also shows as a flash Alert (Edit, Redeploy) in the `notifications` slot above the page. The bell's `aria-label` carries the unread count, `aria-pressed` follows the region, and the `Badge` on it is hidden from assistive technology.
- PageHelp: the ListPage through `ConsoleLayout` with page help. `ConsoleLayout.ToolsTrigger` is first in the `PageHeader`'s `meta` slot, so the `Info` link (named `Info about applications`) sits right after the h1 on the same line; it toggles the layout's tools region (`v-model:tools-open`, `tools-label="Help"`, a drawer when narrow), carries `aria-expanded` and, while open, `aria-controls` on the region's body. The `tools` slot holds the `HelpPanel` topic: what an application is, when to create one, and the Learn more link to the documentation. The region's close button closes it as well; focus stays on the link.
- AccountSwitch: the ListPage through `ConsoleLayout` with the current account in the `sidebar-header` slot, full width in the rail under the wordmark (square `Avatar` with its initials, the name, a sort glyph), `Switch account (Ctrl+O)` on its tooltip (to the right) and `aria-keyshortcuts`; the rail slot renders nothing while `compact` is true, and the same switcher moves to the `header-leading` slot, before the breadcrumbs, with the avatar and the chevron only (the name stays in its `aria-label`). It and the shortcut open a large `Dialog`, rendered beside the layout, with a search `Input` (name, ID or client ID) over a `Table` of the account tree: organizations, groups and workspaces indented by depth, expand and collapse buttons with `aria-expanded`, each name a button that switches, `Current` on the active one, type as `TableCellStatus`, ID and client ID as `TableCellId`. Each name is a `Button` with `variant="link"`. The table pages ten rows at a time (`paginated`), and while the list loads on open it shows the `Table` loading rows. Switching closes the dialog and toasts `Switched to <name>.` with the IDs; the footer shows the current account and Account settings. A search with no match shows Clear search. The search `Input` takes its `id` from `useId()` so the dialog can focus it on open.
- AccountSwitchError: the AccountSwitch dialog when the account list fails to load. A danger `Alert` (`The account list could not be loaded.`, action `Retry`) takes the place of the account `Table` under the search; the search, the title and the footer stay. Retry loads the list again and shows the table.

## Related

- `top-bar/top-bar-creation` — the focused shell for create, edit and deploy.
- `view/view-table`, `detail/detail-resource`, `dashboard/dashboard-home` — the page bodies rendered in the slot.

`ListPage` (primary) · `DetailPage` · `Notifications` · `PageHelp` · `AccountSwitch` · `AccountSwitchError`. Code: [blocks/shell/shell-console.md](blocks/shell/shell-console.md), `get_block("shell/shell-console", { variant })`.

# ShellDocs (`shell/shell-docs`)

> The documentation shell is `DocLayout`, composed once around the app's router view: this block's primary is the app's `App.vue` and every variant is a page body (an `<article>` only, with no header, rail, outline or f…

## Asked as

docs shell; documentation layout; docs page layout; documentation site; docs sidebar; on this page outline; knowledge base layout; layout da documentação; página de documentação; estrutura da documentação; documentation shell; docs layout; documentation article; docs article page; tutorial page; getting started guide; how-to guide; product reference page; reference documentation; docs page with steps and code; documentation home; docs home page; docs landing page; developer portal home; artigo da documentação; página de tutorial; guia de primeiros passos; página de referência do produto; página inicial da documentação; home da documentação; docs home with copy prompt and AI agent logos; your AI agent fluent in Azion card; botão copiar prompt com logos de IA; docs layout component; DocLayout; agent setup page; coding agent setup; mcp setup guide; AI agent comparison table; configurar agente de IA; página de configuração do agente; agent setup index; connect an AI agent to the docs; docs page body; documentation page body; docs outline from headings

The documentation shell. A reader comes to learn one task and leave, so the shell keeps the page readable and the next page close. It is `DocLayout`, composed once in the app around `RouterView`: the layout owns the docs header, the navigation rail, the "On this page" rail, the search palette and the footer, and the document itself scrolls with the header and both rails sticky. This block's primary is that `App.vue`; every variant is a page body, only its `<article>`, rendered in the layout's default slot. A page feeds the outline by rendering its section headings as anchored `DocHeading`s: each one registers with the layout, so the app passes nothing per page.

## When to use

- Every documentation, guide or reference page, and the docs home.

## When not to use

- Marketing pages: `shell/shell-site`. Product pages: `shell/shell-console`.

## Building blocks

- A. Layout — `DocLayout` (required)
- B. Header actions — `IconButton` (required)
- C. Console — `Button` (required)
- D. Theme — `ThemeSwitcher` (required)
- E. Call to action — `DocCallToAction` (optional)
- F. Masthead — `DocPageHeader` (required)
- G. Running text — `DocProse` (required)
- H. Section headings — `DocHeading` (required)
- I. Footer — `Footer` (required)
- J. Brand — `Brand`, `Link` (required)
- K. System status — `StatusIndicator` (required)
- L. Language — `LanguageSelect` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/shell/shell-docs.md](blocks/shell/shell-docs.md).

## Data

The shell's data comes in through props (`ShellDocsProps`, `ShellDocsFooterColumn` and `ShellDocsSocial` are exported from `shell-docs.vue`): `sections`, `navigation`, `outline-groups`, `footer-columns` and `socials`. Left out, the sample docs tree, sections, outline links, footer columns and socials in `sample.ts` render; the app passes its own and deletes `sample.ts` and its import.

## Do

- Compose `DocLayout` once in the app's root around `RouterView` (the primary); each route renders only its `<article>`.
- For a real page, start from a variant (Article, Reference, Landing, AgentSetup, AgentGuide): each is a page body built from the `Doc*` parts only, with no layout of its own. `webkit add shell/shell-docs --variant Article` copies the shell and the page side by side; keep the shell as `App.vue` and route to the page.
- Give every section `DocHeading` an `anchor`; the layout lists those headings as the outline.
- Put everything under `DocPageHeader` in one `DocProse`.
- Give every navigation row an `id` and an `href` (an in-app path is followed with the router); keep the rail scoped to the current product; the header section links switch products.
- Build a docs home from the Landing variant: `DocHero` with `CopyPromptButton`, then `DocAgentCard` above the Console / CLI / API cards; its headings carry no `anchor`, so the page shows no outline rail.
- Build an index of peers (agents, SDKs, integrations) from AgentSetup: pick (a `Tabs` filter over a `DocCardGroup`, with `data-doc-block` on `Tabs` inside `DocProse`), compare (a `Table`), understand (glossary `DocCard`s). Give each peer its own page from AgentGuide.
- Render copy authored as Markdown with MDX tags (a content file, a CMS field, a sentence in data) with `DocMarkdown` inside `DocProse`; the headings it renders are `DocHeading`s with slug ids and join the outline on their own. AgentGuide uses it for its step bodies and accordion answers.
- Show a comparison of peers or a list of tools as a `DataTable` (`bordered`, imported from `data-table`) inside an element with `data-doc-block data-doc-chrome`, so the prose rules stay off it; a yes/no cell is a check or minus glyph with a visually hidden `Yes` / `No`, a category cell a `Tag` with `severity="neutral"`.
- Write the deck as the outcome (`By the end of this tutorial, …`), one action per `DocSteps.Step`, with its command as a `CodeBlock` inside the same step.

## Don't

- Don't put a `ScrollArea`, an `h-screen` frame or any inner scroll region around the article: the document scrolls, so find in page, scroll restoration and full-page captures work.
- Don't render a `<main>` in a page; the layout already renders the only one.
- Don't render `DocLayout` in a page, and don't repeat the header, the search, the navigation rail, the outline or the footer there.
- Don't hand-write the outline, the pager or the masthead; the layout's outline rail (fed by the anchored headings), `DocPreviousNext` and `DocPageHeader` own their markup and labels.
- Don't pass page data up to the layout through route meta or props: the page's headings register on their own.
- Don't put a `DocHeading` outside `DocProse` (it renders at body size), and don't drop a `Button` row straight into `DocProse`: wrap it in an element with `data-doc-chrome`.
- Don't measure the viewport in script to place the footer brand; put it in the `brand` slot and the footer places it in CSS.
- Don't reuse the console rail here; docs navigation is pages, not modules.

## Copy

- **Article headings:** verb-led tasks in sentence case: `Create the function`, `Verify the response`.
- **Navigation rows:** page titles exactly as the `h1` reads.
- **Step titles:** imperative, ending with a period when the step is a sentence: `Open Azion Console.`
- **Landing groups:** `Start by interface`, `Start by objective`, `Ready-made templates`, `Follow along`; card link labels are a verb and the object (`Install the CLI`).

## Accessibility

- A comparison table's yes/no glyphs are `aria-hidden` with a visually hidden `Yes` / `No` beside them; the agent name cell is a link with the mark `aria-hidden`.
- One main landmark: the layout's. The article is an `<article>` inside it, never a second `<main>`.
- One `h1` per article (the masthead or the hero); `DocHeading` levels follow it in order (2, then 3 under a 2), and outline entries target those ids.
- Landmarks: the header is a banner, the rail and the outline are labelled navigation regions, the footer is contentinfo; `Tab` runs header → rail → article → outline → footer.
- Choosing an outline entry moves focus to its heading and clears the sticky header.

## States

- Default: the chrome (the app's `App.vue`) around a stand-in guide; rail from `lg` (drawer below), outline from the guide's headings with the GitHub and Community groups and the `DocCallToAction` from `xl`, the full footer under the article. The preview renders every variant inside it.
- Article: a tutorial page body from the `Doc*` parts, pager in both directions, outline with an indented level 3 entry.
- Reference: a product reference page with a callout, the request-path diagram, a JSON rule and a term list; pager forward only.
- AgentSetup: an index page; the picker tabs filter the agent cards, the comparison table scrolls inside its frame on a narrow page, the outline indents its three level 3 entries.
- AgentGuide: one agent's page; steps with code, the tools table, prompts, accordions collapsed by default, pager in both directions.
- Landing: the documentation home page body; navigation rail, no outline rail (unanchored headings), `DocHero` with `CopyPromptButton`, `DocAgentCard`, entry-point grids, pager forward to the first page.

## Related

- `DocLayout` — the component this block shows.
- `shell/shell-console` (`ConsoleLayout`) and `shell/shell-site` (`SiteLayout`) — the console and marketing counterparts.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Article` · `Reference` · `Landing` · `AgentSetup` · `AgentGuide`. Code: [blocks/shell/shell-docs.md](blocks/shell/shell-docs.md), `get_block("shell/shell-docs", { variant })`.

# StateAsyncSubmit (`state/state-async-submit`)

> The async counterpart of the server rejection in the SectionRejected state of the `state/state-form-validation` block: a deploy that runs for about half a minute, so the user walks away before it ends.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/state/state-async-submit/state-async-submit.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/state-async-submit")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, EmptyState, LogViewer, PageHeader, StatusIndicator, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-form`

## Asked as

async submit; long running action; background job status; deploy in progress; async deploy result; operation status; envio assíncrono; ação demorada; status da operação; result reaches me later

The async-action pattern, and the standard for every build and deploy screen. A long-running action the user is free to walk away from: a deploy that runs for about half a minute and asks nothing while it does. The user's job is to start it, go on working anywhere in the console, and learn how it ended without coming back to check. The page that started the run shows its status in the heading, the logs while it runs and an inline outcome when it ends; in a full app the run lives outside the page, so its progress travels with the user as a toast, and its outcome comes back as a toast when the user is not looking at this page, on success and on failure.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

The run toast rides the app's one toast region, never the page's: the app installs `ToastPlugin` (`app.use(ToastPlugin, { position: 'bottom-end' })`) or mounts one `Toaster` near its root, beside `ConsoleLayout`, and this page body only imports `toast` from `@aziontech/webkit/toast`. A `Toaster` inside a page body is a second region for the whole app: only the first `Toaster` to mount is active, and it gives that up when it unmounts, so a page's copy is either inert or, when it mounted first, stops every toast once the user leaves the page, the opposite of a run toast that follows the user. The docs preview mounts one region around the block the way an app root does, so its frames show the toasts; a copy of the page shows them wherever the app has mounted the region.

The toasts are raised through `toast` with one id per run so each state replaces the last. Every outcome toast passes `actions: [{ label: 'Edit', onClick }, { label: 'Redeploy', onClick }]` and `closable: true`, so the app's `Toaster` renders both as `Toast.Action`s beside `Toast.Close`; the progress toast carries no action. The Running frame raises the progress toast. When the run ends while this page is on screen, the outcome `Alert` is the outcome and the progress toast is dismissed: a toast repeating the Alert would cover the failed step on a phone. When the page is out of view (`document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`), Error raises the permanent failure toast and Success the success toast; in an app, the run store raises them the same way when the user has moved to another page. Leaving the page dismisses the toast so the next story starts clean.

## When to use

- Use state-async-submit when the action runs long enough that the user leaves (build, deploy, import) and the result must reach them later.
- Any action that takes long enough to leave: build, deploy, redeploy, import, provision, a bulk change.
- When the outcome must reach the user on whatever page they are on when it lands.
- As the reference for the idle, running, failed and succeeded states of a run started from a page.

## When not to use

- A save that answers in about a second: use `state/state-form-validation`.
- A run the user watches to the end inside a create flow, or a deployment's own page: use `detail/detail-deployment-logs` (InCreateFlow, DeploymentDetail).
- Confirming a finished deploy with next steps: use `create/create-deploy-success`.
- A deploy configured in a side panel: use `create/create-deploy-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Actions — `Button` (required)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Run status — `Tag` (required)
- D. Nothing running — `EmptyState` (idle only)
- E. Outcome — `Alert` (error and success only)
- F. Deployment logs — `Card`, `StatusIndicator`, `LogViewer`, `ToggleGroup` (running and error only)

What each part takes: [blocks/state/state-async-submit.md](blocks/state/state-async-submit.md).

## Data

The block takes the run through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing and runs no timer. `AsyncSubmitStep`, `AsyncSubmitDeployment` and `AsyncSubmitProps` are exported from `state-async-submit.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the running and failed steps, the failure reason and the deployment the variants pass.

Prop: `loading`, `error`, `errorSummary`, `deployment`, `steps`.

With none of them set the block is Idle. `loading` wins over `error`, and `error` over `deployment`, so a redeploy after a failure reads Deploying.

Event: `deploy`, `redeploy`, `edit`, `open-service`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/state/state-async-submit.md](blocks/state/state-async-submit.md).

## Do

- Keep the run and its outcome outside the page component (a small module-scope store) and pass its state in, so leaving the page never cancels it or loses the result.
- Show progress as a `loading` toast (no duration, not closable) that follows the user through the app while the run lasts.
- Report the end wherever the user is, on success and on failure: inline when they are on the page that started the run, as a toast when they are not. A failure toast is permanent (`duration: 0`) and `closable`; a success toast is `closable` with the default 6 second duration.
- Raise the toasts through `toast` only; the app mounts the region once (`ToastPlugin` or one `Toaster` at its root), so the page body never renders a `Toaster`.
- Give both toasts the same two actions through `toast()`'s `actions` option: **Edit** for the item that was deployed, and **Redeploy**. Don't rebuild the toast body in the `Toaster` slot to get two actions.
- On the page that started the run, show the outcome inline instead of a toast, with the same two actions the toast would carry: a danger `Alert` with the reason, **Edit** and **Redeploy** over the stopped logs, or a success `Alert` naming the new address with **Edit**, **Redeploy** and **Open service**.
- Disable Deploy and the controls that would change the run while it is in progress, with Deploy in `loading`.
- Use one toast id per run, so the progress toast turns into the outcome toast in place, and a Redeploy turns it back into progress.
- Apply this to every build and deploy screen (deploy drawers, deployment flows, redeploys from a list, imports): the run lives outside the page, the page shows the status `Tag` and the outcome `Alert`, and the toast reports wherever the user is.

## Don't

- Don't tie the run to the component that started it; unmounting a page is not an event the run hears.
- Don't let a failure toast expire; the user was not there when it arrived.
- Don't point the toast at a list of runs ("View deployments"); it carries **Edit** and **Redeploy**.
- Don't block the page with a modal or overlay while the run is in progress; the user must be able to leave.
- Don't claim an outcome before the server confirms it; the heading reads `Deploying` until it does.

## Copy

- **Page heading:** names the action and the resource, sentence case: `Deploy web-app`. Lead: the static purpose only, `Builds acme/web-app and publishes it to production.`; the timing and that the user may leave are said once, in the empty state, and the running and outcome states carry their own lines.
- **Status tag:** one or two words: `Idle`, `Deploying`, `Failed`, `Deployed`.
- **Empty state:** title states the fact, description says what to do: `No deployment running` / `Start one above. It takes about half a minute.`
- **Progress toast:** present progressive with the single-character ellipsis, names the item: `Deploying web-app…`; description names the source and that the user may leave: `acme/web-app. It keeps running if you leave.`
- **Failure toast:** what failed and why, then the ways out: `web-app wasn't deployed.` / `The routing rules were refused.` Actions: `Edit`, `Redeploy`.
- **Success toast:** past tense, names the item and where it is live: `web-app is live.` / `It is available at web-app.example.com.` Actions: `Edit`, `Redeploy`.
- **Failure Alert:** the reason the server gave, as full sentences, with `Edit` and `Redeploy`.
- **Success Alert:** names the address and the attempts: `web-app is live at web-app.example.com. It took 1 attempt.`, with `Edit`, `Redeploy` and `Open service`.
- **Actions:** `Deploy`, `Redeploy` (never "Retry deploy" or "Try again"), `Edit`, `Open service`.

## Accessibility

- The run status is text in the heading's `Tag`, not color alone.
- Toasts are announced by the app's `Toaster`, politely except the failure toast (`danger`), which interrupts; the progress toast must not steal focus.
- The failure toast's actions and close button are reachable by keyboard, and it stays until closed.
- The logs card (Running and Error) streams into a `LogViewer`; do not announce every log line.
- Page entrance and the outcome `Alert` animate with `motion-reduce:animate-none`.

## States

- Idle: no prop set, nothing running; the heading reads Idle and the `EmptyState` offers Deploy.
- Running: `loading` with the running `steps`; the heading reads Deploying, the logs card streams under the Building status and the progress toast reads `Deploying web-app…`.
- Error: `error` and the failed `steps`, the routing rules were refused; the heading reads Failed, the danger `Alert` carries the reason with Edit and Redeploy, the permanent failure toast carries the same two actions, and the logs stay open on the failed step.
- Success: `deployment` is set, the run is live; the heading reads Deployed, the success `Alert` names the new address with Edit, Redeploy and Open service, the success toast carries Edit and Redeploy, and the logs card is gone.

## Related

- `state/state-form-validation` — the synchronous counterpart: field, section and toast placement for a save that answers right away.
- `detail/detail-deployment-logs` — the deployment logs card (`LogViewer.Steps`) the Running and Error states reuse, and the full logs of a run the page Edit or a failure leads into.
- `create/create-deploy-success` — the confirmation page after a deploy completes.
- `shell/shell-console` — the layout this body renders in, which the user moves through while the run reports back.

## Variants

`Idle` (primary) · `Running` · `Error` · `Success`. Code: [blocks/state/state-async-submit.md](blocks/state/state-async-submit.md), `get_block("state/state-async-submit", { variant })`.

# StateEdgeErrorPage (`state/state-edge-error-page`)

> The page Azion serves to a visitor of a customer's site when a request fails: a standalone page, no Azion product chrome, no account actions.

- Surface: edge
- Source: `blocks/state/state-edge-error-page/state-edge-error-page.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/state-edge-error-page")`
- Components: Brand, Button, CopyButton, FlowDiagram, KeyValueList, StatusCode, Timestamp
- Skills: `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

edge error page; 502 bad gateway page; 504 gateway timeout page; application unreachable page; application error page; origin unreachable page; 503 service unavailable page; firewall blocked page; waf blocked request page; rate limited page; 429 page for visitors; error page for site visitors; custom error page; página de erro do edge; aplicação indisponível; requisição bloqueada pelo firewall; página de error del edge

The page Azion serves to a visitor of a customer's site when the request fails: the site's application is down or slow, it answered with an error, the site's firewall blocked the request, or the visitor sent too many requests. The reader is not an Azion user: it is anyone on the internet who opened `www.example.com`. Their job is to learn, in one look, whose side the problem is on (their connection, Azion's infrastructure or the site's application), what they can do about it, and what to quote to the site owner. The page stands alone: it has no Azion product chrome, no navigation and nothing that needs an Azion account.

Two error page families, one per audience:

- **Edge** (this block, `surface: edge`): the visitors of your customers' sites. Diagnostic, left-aligned, with the request path.

- **Console, site and docs** (`state/state-error-page`, `surface: app`): Azion's own users on Azion's own pages. Quiet and centred, inside the product shell.

Words: the docs say **Azion's infrastructure**; the page itself says just **Azion**. The third hop is the **Application**, never "origin": the site's application may run on Azion's distributed infrastructure or on the customer's own servers, and the visitor does not need to know which.

## When to use

- The default error pages Azion serves when the site's application cannot answer: 502 (application unreachable, the primary), 504 (application timeout), 500 (application error) and 503 (application unavailable).
- A request a firewall or WAF rule on Azion blocked (Blocked, 403) or rate limited (RateLimited, 429).
- A 404 Azion serves for the site when the application has no page and the site has no page of its own (NotFound).
- As the starting point of a customer's own custom error page: the customer replaces the copy and keeps the structure.

## When not to use

- Any page of Azion Console, the Azion site or the docs: use `state/state-error-page`, which carries the account actions an Azion user needs (Sign in, Request access, Switch account) and sits in the product shell.
- An error inside a page that otherwise works: use `ErrorBoundary` or an `Alert` in the region that failed.
- A failed deploy or build: use `state/state-async-submit`.

## Building blocks

- A. Status line — `StatusCode`
- B. Request path — `FlowDiagram`
- C. Next steps — `Button`
- D. Request details — `KeyValueList`, `CopyButton`, `Timestamp`
- E. Footer — `Brand`

What each part takes: [blocks/state/state-edge-error-page.md](blocks/state/state-edge-error-page.md).

## Data

The block fetches nothing: Azion fills the props from the request it failed to serve.

Prop: `code`, `reason`, `title`, `cause`, `advice`, `host`, `requestId`, `time`, `location`, `path`, `recovery`.

Event: `retry`, `back`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/state/state-edge-error-page.md](blocks/state/state-edge-error-page.md).

## Do

- Answer with the real status code (502, 504, 500, 503, 403, 429, 404), so browsers, crawlers and monitors see it.
- Keep the three hops in every state, with the hop that failed marked, so every error reads the same way.
- Give every hop the same card size: one node per level and the same parts (type, status, name) on every card.
- Show the request ID and the time on every state; log the same ID on Azion so the site owner can find the request.
- Say plainly when the problem is not the visitor's fault (`nothing you did caused this`).

## Don't

- Don't offer Sign in, Switch account, Request access or any other account action: the visitor has no Azion account, and the site owner's account is not theirs.
- Don't show Azion Console links, the product navigation, an internal hostname, a stack trace or the application's IP address.
- Don't blame the visitor, and don't name Azion as the culprit when the application failed: the path shows which hop it was.
- Don't auto-redirect or auto-reload in a loop; Try again is the visitor's choice.
- Don't drop the path on a phone; stack it instead.
- Don't write "edge" or "origin" on the page: the visitor reads Azion and Application.

## Copy

- **Title:** what happened, from the visitor's side, no code: `The site's application could not be reached`, `This site's firewall blocked your request`, `Too many requests from your connection`.
- **What happened?:** one or two sentences naming the hop: `Azion received your request, but the application that serves this site did not accept the connection.`
- **What can I do?:** what the visitor can do now: `Try again in a few minutes. If it keeps happening, let the site owner know and quote the request ID below.`
- **Hop states:** one or two words: `Working`, `Error`, `Timed out`, `Unavailable`, `Blocked`, `Rate limited`, `Not reached`, `Not found`.
- **Actions:** `Try again`, `Go to home page`, `Go back`.
- **Facts:** `Request ID`, `Time`, `Data center`, `Host`; the request ID in `text-label-code-sm` inside `<bdi>`.

## Accessibility

- The block is the whole page: it owns the single `main`, one `h1` (the title) and an `h2` for each section (Request path, What happened?, What can I do?).
- The request path is a `FlowDiagram` (`role="group"`) named by the Request path heading (`aria-labelledby`), holding a list of hops; each card's Details button opens its explanation (`aria-expanded`). The connectors are decorative, and a hidden list reads the connections.
- Severity is never colour alone: every status dot has its label.
- Long hosts truncate on a phone and wrap in the details; hosts and IDs sit in `<bdi>` so they keep their order on right-to-left pages.
- The phone and wide layouts of the path are the same content; the hidden one is `display: none`, so a screen reader hears it once.

## States

- Default: 502 Bad gateway, the application could not be reached; the Application hop reads Error; Try again and Go back.
- ApplicationTimeout: 504 Gateway timeout; the Application hop reads Timed out.
- ApplicationError: 500 Internal server error; the application answered with an error.
- ApplicationUnavailable: 503 Service unavailable; the Application hop reads Unavailable.
- Blocked: 403 Forbidden; the site's firewall matched the request, the Azion hop reads Blocked and the Application Not reached; Go to home page.
- RateLimited: 429 Too many requests; the Azion hop reads Rate limited and the Application Not reached.
- NotFound: 404 Not found; every hop worked and the Application reads Not found; Go to home page.

## Related

- `state/state-error-page` — the error pages of Azion's own console, site and docs.
- `FlowDiagram` — the request path (`nodes` + `edges`, `uniform`, `orientation="responsive"`).
- `state/state-async-submit` — a failed build or deploy inside the console.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `ApplicationTimeout` · `ApplicationError` · `ApplicationUnavailable` · `Blocked` · `RateLimited` · `NotFound`. Code: [blocks/state/state-edge-error-page.md](blocks/state/state-edge-error-page.md), `get_block("state/state-edge-error-page", { variant })`.

# StateErrorPage (`state/state-error-page`)

> The error page of Azion's own surfaces (Console, the site, the docs) when a page cannot show what the user asked for.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/state/state-error-page/state-error-page.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/state-error-page")`
- Components: Button, CopyButton, EmptyState, StatusCode, Timestamp
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

404 page; not found page; page not found; 401 session expired page; sign in required page; 403 forbidden page; access denied page; 429 too many requests page; 500 error page; server error page; 503 maintenance page; error page; console error page; resource not found; página não encontrada; página de erro; acesso negado; sessão expirada; erro 404; erro 500

The page Azion's own surfaces (Console, the site, the docs) render when they cannot show what the user asked for: the address leads nowhere (404), the session ended (401), the user's role does not include the page (403), the account sent too many requests (429), the server failed (500) or the console is in maintenance (503). The reader is an Azion user. Their job is to understand, in one sentence, that the problem is the address, the access or Azion and not their work, to get somewhere useful in one click, and to have the reference support will ask for. Every state has the same quiet, centred shape; only the code, the words and the two buttons change.

Two error page families, one per audience:

- **Console, site and docs** (this block, `surface: app`): Azion's users on Azion's pages. Quiet and centred, inside the product shell, with the account actions an Azion user needs.
- **Edge** (`state/state-edge-error-page`, `surface: edge`): the visitors of Azion customers' sites. Diagnostic, standalone, with the request path and no account actions.

The block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), or of the site and docs shells, which own the navigation, the header and the `main`. SessionExpired renders signed out, without the rail.

## When to use

- A route that matches nothing: the catch-all route renders the primary (404).
- A session that ended while the user was away: SessionExpired (401). Never for a first visit with no session; that goes straight to sign-in with no notice.
- A route the user's role does not include: Forbidden (403), instead of hiding the page or sending them home.
- A request the API refused for the rate limit: RateLimited (429).
- A page whose server request failed as a whole: ServerError (500).
- Scheduled maintenance or an overloaded console: Maintenance (503).
- A valid route whose record does not exist (a deleted service, a stale link): ResourceNotFound.

## When not to use

- The page a visitor of a customer's site sees when Azion's edge cannot serve it: use `state/state-edge-error-page`.
- One region of a page failed to render while the rest works: wrap the region in `ErrorBoundary`; it shows a danger `Alert` with Try again in its place.
- A list with no items yet: use `state/state-first-use`. A list whose filter matched nothing: use the no-match state of `view/view-table`.
- A form the server rejected: use `state/state-form-validation` (SectionRejected).
- A build or deploy that failed: use `state/state-async-submit`.
- The sign-in screens themselves: see `auth/auth-sign-in`.

## Building blocks

- A. Code — `StatusCode`
- B. Message — `EmptyState`
- C. Actions — `Button`
- D. Reference line — `CopyButton`, `Timestamp`

What each part takes: [blocks/state/state-error-page.md](blocks/state/state-error-page.md).

## Data

The block shows no records and fetches nothing: the app passes the copy, the codes and the reference.

Prop: `code`, `errorCode`, `title`, `description`, `requestId`, `time`, `homeHref`, `docsHref`.

Slot: `actions`.

Event: `home`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/state/state-error-page.md](blocks/state/state-error-page.md).

## Do

- Render the block on the address the user asked for; do not redirect to `/404`, so reloading tries the real address again.
- Answer with the matching HTTP status when the server renders the page.
- Keep the shell around every state but SessionExpired, so the user can move on without the back button.
- Log the same request ID and error code on the server that the page shows.
- On 403, say who can grant access (an account admin) and offer Switch account when the user belongs to more than one account.

## Don't

- Don't blame the user or show a stack trace, a raw status line or an exception message.
- Don't hide a 403 behind a 404 inside the product; use 404 only where revealing that the page exists would leak information.
- Don't add a third button, a search box or a list of popular pages.
- Don't auto-redirect after a countdown; the user decides where to go.
- Don't put the code in the visible title; the `StatusCode` already shows it.
- Don't use this block for the pages the edge serves to customers' visitors; those have no Azion account to act on.

## Copy

- **Title:** what happened, sentence case, no code: `Page not found`, `Your session expired`, `You don't have access to this page`, `Too many requests`, `Something went wrong on our side`, `Back soon: scheduled maintenance`.
- **Description:** why, and what to do, in one sentence; on a 5xx, reassure: `Nothing you saved was lost.`
- **Actions:** where it goes (`Go to home`, `Back to services`) or what it does (`Sign in`, `Request access`, `Retry`).
- **Reference line:** `Code NOT_FOUND · ID req_7f3c91ab` with the time in UTC on the line below, codes in `text-label-code-sm` inside `<bdi>`, with a `CopyButton` (`Copy the request ID`).

## Accessibility

- Each state has exactly one `h1` (visually hidden) naming the error code, so the page has a heading and the code is announced even though the figure is decorative.
- Every state is a body inside the layout's `main`, with no `main` of its own.
- The `EmptyState` is `role="status"`, so a client-side route change to this page is announced.
- Retry shows the `Button` loading state while the page reloads; the button keeps its label.
- Buttons that open a new tab carry an icon; do not rely on colour.

## States

- Default: 404 Page not found, Go to home (`homeHref`) and Docs (`docsHref`).
- SessionExpired: 401 Your session expired, Sign in; rendered signed out.
- Forbidden: 403 You don't have access to this page, Request access and Switch account.
- RateLimited: 429 Too many requests, Try again and About rate limits.
- ServerError: 500 Something went wrong on our side, Retry and System status.
- Maintenance: 503 Back soon: scheduled maintenance, Retry and Status page.
- ResourceNotFound: 404 for a missing record, naming the service and its ID, with Back to services.

## Related

- `state/state-edge-error-page` — the error pages Azion's edge serves to visitors of customer sites.
- `shell/shell-console` — the shell around every state but SessionExpired.
- `state/state-first-use` — an empty list, which is not an error.
- `state/state-form-validation` (SectionRejected) — a server rejection scoped to a form section.
- `state/state-async-submit` — the outcome of a build or deploy.
- `auth/auth-sign-in` — the sign-in screens.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `SessionExpired` · `Forbidden` · `RateLimited` · `ServerError` · `Maintenance` · `ResourceNotFound`. Code: [blocks/state/state-error-page.md](blocks/state/state-error-page.md), `get_block("state/state-error-page", { variant })`.
