# StateFirstUse (`state/state-first-use`)

> The block a first-level list renders before the account owns any resource of that kind: a flush Card holding an EmptyState (the resource glyph, headline, lead and a Documentation link) over an Item.List of the ways to…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/state/state-first-use/state-first-use.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/state-first-use")`
- Components: `claudeMark`, `codexMark`, `cursorMark`, `geminiMark`, Button, Card, CopyButton, EmptyState, Input, `InputGroupRoot`, Item, Link, Skeleton, ThirdPartyLogo
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

empty state; empty list; first use; no resources yet; create first resource; product empty state; zero state; estado vazio; lista vazia; primeiro uso; first resource empty state

What a first-level list shows before the account owns any resource of that kind. The user's job is to create the first one, so the block replaces the empty table with a short explanation and every way to get started on the same screen: the methods to create one (import, CLI, from scratch), then the promotions that shortcut it (a Catalog template, a coding agent). Every list that is still empty renders this block with its own nouns, methods and promos.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use state-first-use on a list page before the account owns any resource of that kind.
- The first visit to a list page (Resources, Services, Domains…) when the account has none of that resource.
- When there is more than one way to create the first item and each deserves its own action.

## When not to use

- A list that has items but a filter or search matched none: use the no-match state of `view/view-table`.
- An empty panel inside a dashboard or detail page: use `EmptyState` alone, without the method list.
- Choosing what to create across every resource kind: use `create/create-hub`.
- The Home page before the first project: use `dashboard/dashboard-home` (its Empty state).
- A list that failed to load: that is an error, not first use; see `skills/webkit-ui-states`.

## Building blocks

- A. Frame — `Card` (required)
- B. Agent marks — `ThirdPartyLogo` (optional)
- C. Explanation — `EmptyState` (required)
- D. Documentation — `Link` (required)
- E. Methods — `Item` (required)
- F. Method action — `Button` (required)
- G. Command row — `InputGroupRoot` (CLI method)
- H. Command — `Input` (CLI method)
- I. Copy — `CopyButton` (CLI method)
- J. Placeholder — `Skeleton` (Loading)

What each part takes: [blocks/state/state-first-use.md](blocks/state/state-first-use.md).

## Data

The block shows no records and fetches nothing: a real app sets the copy and the links for its resource and listens for the two create methods. `FirstUseProps` is exported from `state-first-use.vue`; every prop defaults to the copy above.

Prop: `loading`, `title`, `description`, `docsHref`, `command`, `agentSetupHref`.

Event: `import`, `create`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/state/state-first-use.md](blocks/state/state-first-use.md).

## Do

- Rewrite the headline, lead, methods and promos for each resource kind; the structure stays, the nouns change.
- Show the Catalog template promo only for resource kinds that have a template catalog.
- Keep one primary action across the whole block, on the method most users take.
- Keep the documentation link as the only action in the `EmptyState`.
- Hold the block's own footprint while the account reloads (the empty-state band, one row per method and the promo cards, in `Skeleton`s), so it does not jump in.

## Don't

- Don't draw an agent mark by hand (an `img` or a CSS mask): `ThirdPartyLogo` already inks it for the theme.
- Don't show list controls (search, filters, pagination, column settings) over a list that has never had an item.
- Don't render this block for a filtered list with no matches; that state says how to clear the filter.
- Don't show it while the list is still loading; the user would see "create your first" for an account that has items.
- Don't add a second primary button to a promo card; the whole card is the action.

## Copy

- **Headline:** names the first action and the noun: `Create your first resource`.
- **Lead:** one sentence on the ways in: `Start from scratch, from a template or by importing your code.`
- **Method title:** two or three words for how: `From GitHub`, `Via CLI`, `From scratch`.
- **Method description:** one sentence on what happens: `Import a repository and deploy it on every push.`
- **Method action:** one verb: `Import`, `Create`.
- **Promo title:** sentence case, product names capitalized: `Start from a Catalog template`, `Set up your coding agent`.
- **Promo description:** one sentence on the result: `Deploy a framework starter and the resource that serves it, in one step.`
- **Documentation link:** `Documentation`.

## Accessibility

- The method icons and promo marks are decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`, `alt=""`); the titles carry the meaning.
- Each promo is a real link (`<a href>`) covering the card, because both navigate; the Catalog one opens a new tab, shows the external-link glyph and says so to screen readers.
- The command `Input` has an `aria-label`; the copy button has its own label and announces the copied state.
- The documentation link opens in a new tab; say so in the destination or let `Link` mark it.
- The headline is the page's first heading under the list title, not a second `h1`.

## States

- Default: `title` and `description`, three create methods and the two promos.
- Loading: `loading`; while the account reloads, `Skeleton`s draw the block's footprint (empty-state band, three method rows, two promo cards) in a busy status region.

## Related

- `view/view-table` — the list this block stands in for once the first item exists, and the home of the no-match state.
- `create/create-hub` — every create entry point across resource kinds.
- `create/create-deploy-template` — where the Catalog template promo leads.
- `state/state-project-intake` — the drop target and upload overlay an empty page can also render.
- `state/state-page-skeleton` — the skeleton painted before the page knows whether the list is empty.

`Default` (primary) · `Loading`. Code: [blocks/state/state-first-use.md](blocks/state/state-first-use.md), `get_block("state/state-first-use", { variant })`.

<!-- blocks/state/state-form-validation.md -->

# StateFormValidation (`state/state-form-validation`)

> A standalone form that walks through every state a submit can land in, one story per state, on a single Create Variable page with no card around it: a heading, then `Field`s wrapping `Input`, `Select` and `Textarea` s…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/state/state-form-validation/state-form-validation.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/state-form-validation")`
- Components: Alert, AppHeader, `AppHeaderAccount`, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, DropdownMenu, Field, `FieldError`, IconButton, Input, Item, Kbd, MultiSelect, NumberInput, PageHeader, RadioGroup, SaveBar, Select, SettingsRow, Skeleton, Subheader, Switch, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

form validation; validation errors; submit states; required fields; server error on submit; conflict error; saved state; validação de formulário; erros de validação; campos obrigatórios; submit outcomes; every submit outcome; server validation; server-side error; rejected save; field scoped error; section error; stale reference; linked resource deleted; api error on save; reload options; form error; erro de formulário; validação no servidor; erro da api; salvamento rejeitado; error de formulario; validación en el servidor

Every state a submit can land in, on one create form. The user's job is to create a resource and, when something stops the save, to know exactly which control to touch and that nothing they typed was lost. The primary is a short Create Variable page (heading, four fields straight on the canvas, Cancel and Create); the variants walk it through validation, the in-flight lock, an unscoped failure, a conflict, success and loading. The Section variants carry the same rules to a long sectioned create page, where the server rejects the save because of one section: another user deleted the origin the form links to, so the page takes the user to that section, says what happened and that nothing else was lost, offers the one action that recovers (Reload origins) and marks the field with its own reason. The Section variants are a focused create page with their own creation header and no rail.

This block is a page body for a create page: render it under the focused creation header (`top-bar/top-bar-creation`), not in `ConsoleLayout`.

## When to use

- Use state-form-validation as the reference for every submit outcome of a create or edit form: required, invalid, in flight, conflict, section rejected, unscoped failure, saved.
- As the reference for the submit states of any create or edit form: what happens on Create with gaps, while the request is in flight, and on each kind of answer.
- A short create form with a handful of fields and no sections (a variable, a key, a token).
- A long, sectioned create or edit form whose save can be rejected because of one section (a linked resource deleted or changed by someone else): SectionRejected, SectionReloading, SectionReloaded.

## When not to use

- A sectioned create page with many settings and a sticky save bar: build it from `create/create-page` and apply these states to it.
- A create that runs for tens of seconds and can be left (build, deploy, import): use `state/state-async-submit`.
- Settings of an existing object saved section by section: use `settings/settings-form`.
- Signed-out screens: use `auth/auth-sign-in`, where nothing toasts.
- A create launched from a list without leaving it: use `create/create-drawer`.

## Where the error renders

| Error | Where it renders | Variant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A value the user left empty or typed wrong (client-side) | On the field: `invalid`, its message in a `Field.Error` under the description, focus on the first field in error | ValidationErrors |
| A value the server refused that one field owns (a key already in use) | On the field (`invalid` with its reason) and in a danger `Alert` above the fields of its section; never a toast | Conflict |
| A rejection one section of a long form owns (a linked resource deleted) | A danger `Alert` under that section's heading with the recovery action, the field `invalid` with its own reason, the section scrolled into view and the field focused; never a toast | SectionRejected |
| A failure no field or section owns (network, timeout, 500) | `toast.error` with Retry, every entry kept | ServerError |
| A save that went through | `toast.success` naming the new object, the form cleared | Saved |

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Loading rows — `Skeleton` (loading only)
- C. Field — `Field` (required)
- D. Text value — `Input` (required)
- E. Choice — `Select` (required)
- F. Long text — `Textarea` (optional)
- G. Actions — `Button` (required)
- H. Section notice — `Alert` (conflict and rejection only)
- Section rejection (Section variants only)
- Result notices — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/state/state-form-validation.md](blocks/state/state-form-validation.md).

## Data

The block fetches nothing and fakes no request: Create validates the draft, then emits `submit` with the values, and the page that owns the request passes back what happened. `FormValidationValues`, `FormValidationSaved` and `FormValidationProps` are exported from `state-form-validation.vue`; the Section variants export `FormValidationOrigin`, `FormValidationService` and `FormValidationSectionProps` from `variants/section-rejected.vue`. `sample.ts` holds the filled entries, the origins and the rejection message the variants pass.

Prop: `loading`, `submitting`, `error`, `takenKey`, `saved`, `defaultValues`, `defaultSubmitted`.

Event: `submit`.

The Section form takes `origins`, `originError`, `reloading` and `submitting`, and emits `submit` `(event, values)`, `cancel` `(event)` and `reload-origins` `(event)`. A chosen origin missing from a new `origins` list is cleared and flagged with Select an origin to continue.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/state/state-form-validation.md](blocks/state/state-form-validation.md).

## Do

- Validate on submit, not on every keystroke; after the first submit, a field's message updates as the user fixes it.
- Move focus to the first field in error after a submit, after the lock is released.
- Lock the whole scope while the request is in flight: Create shows `loading`, every field and Cancel are disabled, `aria-busy` is on the form. Release it on success and failure alike.
- Keep every entry after a failed or rejected save, and say so in the copy.
- Clear the form after a success, so the next entry starts clean, and name the new object in the toast.
- On the one-section form, a key already in use raises the danger `Alert` above the fields as well as the `invalid` Key, and focus moves to Key.
- On a long form, put a section-scoped rejection in one danger `Alert` under that section's heading with the recovery on it, scroll the section into view (instant under `prefers-reduced-motion`) and focus the field with `preventScroll` after the lock is released. After the recovery, close the `Alert`, clear the stale value and keep the field `invalid` with a message that says what to pick.

## Don't

- Don't show a validation summary at the top; each field carries its own message.
- Don't write the message into `Field.Description`; the guidance stays and the message is its own `Field.Error`.
- Don't toast a rejection a field owns (a key already in use, a deleted origin). The toast dismisses itself and points nowhere.
- Don't colour a required field before a failed submit; `required` is static and only `invalid` turns the field red.
- Don't disable Create to signal missing values; let submit run and show the messages.
- Don't clear the form or send the user back to the start after a rejection, and don't open more than one `Alert` for one rejection.
- Don't auto-dismiss an `Alert` that names a required action; it stays until the user recovers (see SectionReloaded).

## Copy

- **Page heading:** `Create` plus the entity, matching the page it lists: `Create Variable`. Lead: one sentence on what it is for: `Add a key-value pair your services read at runtime.`
- **Field labels:** one to three words, no colon, no parentheses: `Key`, `Value`, `Environment`, `Description`.
- **Field descriptions:** a constraint or purpose, one sentence with a period: `Uppercase letters, digits and underscores, for example API_TOKEN.`, `Optional. Up to 200 characters.`
- **Required message:** the one sentence every block uses: `This field is required.`; for a select, the action: `Select an environment.`
- **Invalid message:** what is wrong and the rule: `Use uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.`
- **Conflict message:** the fact, on the field: `A variable named API_TOKEN already exists.` The section `Alert` adds what happened and what to do: `A variable named API_TOKEN already exists in this account, so it wasn't created. Your entries are kept: change the key and press Create again.`
- **Error toast:** what did not happen, then what was kept: title `The variable wasn't created.`, description `The request didn't reach the server. Your entries are kept.`, action `Retry`.
- **Success toast:** past tense, names the object and where it applies: `API_TOKEN was created.` / `It is available in Production.`
- **Section Alert:** the fact, the cause, what was not lost, what to do: `Origin "web-origin-prod" no longer exists. Another user deleted it while you were filling in this form, so the service wasn't created. Nothing else was lost: reload the origin list and select another one.` Field reasons: `This origin no longer exists.`, then `Select an origin to continue.`
- **Actions:** `Cancel`, `Create`, `Retry`; on the long form `Cancel`, `Save`, `Reload origins`.

## Accessibility

- The `<form>` is labelled by the heading (`aria-labelledby`), uses `novalidate`, and sets `aria-busy` while loading or submitting.
- Every control has a `Field.Label` bound by `for`; the description and the `Field.Error` are wired to the control by `Field` (`aria-describedby`), and `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`.
- The loading region is `role="status"` with an accessible name (`Loading the form`).
- Focus moves to the first field in error, only after the lock is released, since a disabled control cannot take focus.
- Toasts are announced by the app's `Toaster` region; the error toast keeps its Retry reachable by keyboard.
- A section `Alert` sits in reading order before the fields it governs; its action is a real button reachable by keyboard.
- In SectionRejected focus moves to the refused field with `preventScroll`, so the scroll to the section heading is the only movement; the reloading `Skeleton` has an accessible name.
- In Section rejected, `⌘ S` (`Ctrl S` off Apple) submits the form, the same as Save, and stops the browser's own save; it does nothing while the form submits or a section reloads. Save carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and a `Kbd` keycap.

## States

- Default: no prop set; the empty Create Variable form, idle.
- ValidationErrors: `defaultValues` with a malformed key and `defaultSubmitted`, as after Create pressed with gaps; empty Value and Environment and the malformed Key take `invalid`, each with its own `Field.Error` under the kept description, and focus moves to Key.
- Submitting: `submitting`, the request is in flight; Create shows `loading`, the fields and Cancel are disabled.
- ServerError: `error`, the request failed and no field owns it; an error toast with Retry, the lock released, every entry kept.
- Conflict: `takenKey`, the key is already in use; the danger `Alert` opens above the fields, Key takes `invalid` with its reason and focus, and nothing toasts.
- Saved: `saved`, the save went through; a success toast names the variable and where it is available, and the form is cleared.
- Loading: `loading`, the form data is still arriving; `Skeleton` rows hold the layout and Create is disabled.
- SectionRejected: `originError` on the long Create Service form, another user deleted the origin and Save was pressed; the page scrolls to Origin, the danger `Alert` opens under its heading with Reload origins, and focus lands on the Origin select, which reads This origin no longer exists.
- SectionReloading: `reloading`, Reload origins in flight; its button loads, the select gives way to a `Skeleton`, Save is disabled.
- SectionReloaded: `origins` without the deleted origin and an empty `originError`; the `Alert` closes, the select is cleared and stays invalid with Select an origin to continue.

## Related

- `state/state-async-submit` — the long-running counterpart: use it when the action runs long enough that the user leaves (build, deploy, import) and the result must reach them later.
- `skills/webkit-errors` — where every error renders, row by row.
- `create/create-page` — the sectioned create page these states apply to.
- `auth/auth-sign-in` — the signed-out version, where every outcome lands in one card `Alert` and nothing toasts.
- `settings/settings-form` — the same field states on an existing object.
- `Field` — the label, description, error and state every field here uses.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `ValidationErrors` · `Submitting` · `ServerError` · `Conflict` · `Saved` · `Loading` · `SectionRejected` · `SectionReloading` · `SectionReloaded`. Code: [blocks/state/state-form-validation.md](blocks/state/state-form-validation.md), `get_block("state/state-form-validation", { variant })`.

# StatePageSkeleton (`state/state-page-skeleton`)

> The skeleton wires an app paints while a page is still arriving: the Home overview (Overview), the first-access Home (Onboarding), the whole shell while an expired session signs out (Session, with one body per family…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/state/state-page-skeleton/state-page-skeleton.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/state-page-skeleton")`
- Components: Card, Item, Skeleton
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

page skeleton; loading skeleton; skeleton screen; page loading state; wireframe loading; carregando; esqueleto de carregamento; tela de carregamento; whole page loading; shell skeleton

The skeleton wires an app paints while a page is still arriving. The user's job does not change while they wait: they need to see the shape of the page they asked for, so the wire draws the real page's grid with `Skeleton` bands inside the same `Card` frames, and nothing shifts when the content lands. The set covers the Home overview, the first-access Home, and the whole shell while an expired session signs out, drawn over the family of page it covers (list, detail, create form or Home).

Overview and Onboarding are page bodies for the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`); the Session wires stand in for the whole app, layout included.

## When to use

- Use state-page-skeleton for the first paint of a whole page or shell; inside a block use that block's Loading variant.
- The first paint of a page whose data is still loading, when the layout is known.
- Home, before its metrics and recent activity arrive (Overview), or before the first project (Onboarding).
- Over the whole app while an expired session signs out (the Session wires), so the user sees the page dissolve into its frame instead of a blank screen.

## When not to use

- A single control or panel loading inside a ready page: use `Skeleton` or `Spinner` inside that panel only.
- A form whose options are loading: use the Loading state of `state/state-form-validation`.
- A dashboard's own loading: use the Loading variant of that dashboard block (for example `dashboard/dashboard-analytics`).
- A long upload or build: use `state/state-project-intake` or `state/state-async-submit`, which report progress.
- After the sign-out completes: `auth/auth-sign-in` (SessionExpired).

## Building blocks

- A. Bands — `Skeleton` (required)
- B. Frames — `Card` (required)
- C. Lists — `Item` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/state/state-page-skeleton.md](blocks/state/state-page-skeleton.md).

## Data

The wire shows no records and fetches nothing: the page renders it while its own request is pending and swaps in the real page when the data lands. `PageSkeletonProps` is exported from `state-page-skeleton.vue`.

Prop: `label`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/state/state-page-skeleton.md](blocks/state/state-page-skeleton.md).

## Do

- Draw the exact grid of the page that is coming: same columns, gaps and breakpoints.
- Use the real layout utilities (`layout-column`, `layout-boundary`, `--layout-section-gap`), not fixed sizes.
- Hide the bands from assistive technology and announce the wait once: `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-busy="true"`, with a short screen-reader text on every wire.
- Size the session wire to the measured header and rail in the app, so the frame does not move when it appears.
- Fade the session wire in with `motion-reduce:animate-none`.

## Don't

- Don't show a wire for less than a perceptible moment; if the data arrives within about 300 ms, paint the page directly.
- Don't use a generic spinner for a page whose layout is known.
- Don't animate each band independently; a shimmer comes from `Skeleton`.
- Don't mix real content and bands in one card; the card swaps in whole.
- Don't let the wire collapse to a few lines on wide screens; it holds the page's full footprint.

## Copy

- **Bands:** no visible text. The wire has nothing to read.
- **Screen-reader status (session):** states what is happening, as a sentence: `Session expired. Signing you out.`
- **Screen-reader status (page):** names what is loading: `Loading the overview.` on the Overview wire, `Loading Home.` on the Onboarding wire.

## Accessibility

- The bands are decorative (`aria-hidden="true"` on the wire's body).
- The region that stands in for the page is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-busy="true"`; clear `aria-busy` when the content lands.
- The wire takes no focus and traps none; the real page receives focus as it would on a normal load.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` on the entrance and on the shimmer.

## States

- Overview: the primary, its `label` naming what loads; the Home overview wire: heading, the four-metric strip, the side card, and the five-column row of list panels.
- Onboarding: the first-access Home wire: headline and prompt bands over three door cards, each with its illustration stage, three text lines and an action.
- Session: the whole shell as a wire over a list page: header bar, navigation rail with grouped items, the list controls row and a table card with header, eight rows and pagination.
- SessionDetail: the same over a detail page: tab bands under the header, a heading and two cards of field rows in the data column.
- SessionForm: the same over a create page: a heading and two cards of field rows in the create column, with the save bar held at the foot.
- SessionHome: the same over Home: the Overview wire centred in the data column.
- VersionDetail: the version page loading; form-column heading bands and two sectioned flush cards whose rows end in a switch band, one `role="status"` region with `aria-busy`, no tabs.

## Related

- `dashboard/dashboard-home` — the Home page the Overview and Onboarding wires stand in for.
- `view/view-table` — the list page the Session wire draws.
- `detail/detail-resource` — the detail page the SessionDetail wire draws.
- `create/create-page` — the create page the SessionForm wire draws.
- `detail/detail-version` — the version page the VersionDetail wire stands in for.
- `auth/auth-sign-in` — where the session wire lands once the sign-out completes.
- `shell/shell-console` — the header and rail the session wires reproduce.

## Variants

`Overview` (primary) · `Onboarding` · `Session` · `SessionDetail` · `SessionForm` · `SessionHome` · `VersionDetail`. Code: [blocks/state/state-page-skeleton.md](blocks/state/state-page-skeleton.md), `get_block("state/state-page-skeleton", { variant })`.

# StateProjectIntake (`state/state-project-intake`)

> The surfaces a project passes through when it is dropped on the page: the drop target (`FileDropzone` with `directories`, its title saying what dropping does and Choose a folder and Choose files `Button`s as the keybo…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/state/state-project-intake/state-project-intake.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/state-project-intake")`
- Components: Alert, Button, FileDropzone, UploadProgress, `use-file-picker`, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-motion-polish`

## Asked as

drop zone; drag and drop upload; upload project; folder upload; initializing project; file drop; arrastar e soltar; enviar projeto; upload de arquivos

The surfaces a project passes through when the user drops it on the page. The user's job is to deploy a folder they already have without filling in a form: a drop target fills the page body and says what will happen, with Choose a folder and Choose files buttons for anyone not dragging (a phone, which has no folder picker, shows only Choose files); once it is dropped, a full-screen Initializing overlay lists the received files with their status until the upload is done and the deploy takes over.

DropZone is a page-body overlay inside the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`); Initializing covers the whole screen.

## When to use

- Pages where dropping a project is a shortcut to deploying it: Home, its empty state, a creation hub, and a project detail page.
- Showing upload progress per file, when the files are few enough to list.

## When not to use

- Choosing a single file as a form value: use a file upload field inside the form (`skills/webkit-form`).
- Browsing or managing stored files: use `view/view-file-browser`.
- The build and deploy that follow the upload: use `state/state-async-submit` and `detail/detail-deployment-logs`.
- Importing from a repository: use the From GitHub method in `state/state-first-use` or `create/create-deploy-template` (ImportFromGit).

## Building blocks

- A. Drop target — `FileDropzone` (required)
- B. Keyboard way in — `Button` (required)
- C. Upload list — `UploadProgress` (Initializing, UploadError)
- D. Failure summary — `Alert` (UploadError)

What each part takes: [blocks/state/state-project-intake.md](blocks/state/state-project-intake.md).

## Data

The block fetches and uploads nothing: it hands the chosen files to the page and renders the upload the page reports back. `ProjectIntakeUpload` and `ProjectIntakeProps` are exported from `state-project-intake.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the two sample uploads the Initializing and UploadError variants pass.

Prop: `uploads`, `title`, `description`.

Event: `select`, `retry`, `cancel`.

Keep `uploads` `undefined` until the first file arrives, so the drop target shows. Then delete `sample.ts` with the variants.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/state/state-project-intake.md](blocks/state/state-project-intake.md).

## Do

- Keep the drop target where a drop does something, with Choose a folder and Choose files beside the message.
- Say what dropping does, not how to drop: the user is already dragging.
- Render Initializing over the page the drop came from (Home, its empty state, the creation hub), so the user keeps their place.
- Advance the rows in order and keep finished rows visible while the list is short; past 50 files list only what is still moving.
- Keep the choose buttons in the drop target; drag and drop is a shortcut, never the only way.

## Don't

- Don't use a percentage bar alone for a handful of files; the per-file rows say more.
- Don't hide a failed file in the list; say it in the `Alert` and keep Retry on its row.
- Don't show the drop target on pages where a drop does nothing.
- Don't keep the overlay up after the upload ends; hand over to the deploy's own progress.

## Copy

- **Drop heading:** what the drop does, one line: `Drop your project to deploy it`. On a project page: `We build a new version of web-app, then you choose where it goes live.`
- **Drop lead:** what is accepted, full sentences: `A project folder, or the files inside one. We detect what it is built with.`
- **Overlay heading:** one word for the phase: `Initializing`; `Upload paused` while a file has failed, with the danger `Alert` as the only summary of the failure. The `UploadProgress` header is the one place that counts the files; while paused it follows the heading: `Paused: 2 of 5 uploaded, 1 failed`.
- **Overlay progress:** what is happening and how far, with a period: `Setting up your deployment. 2 of 5 files.`
- **Summary:** count and total size, formatted with `formatFileSize` from `useLocale` like the rows: `5 files, 8.2 kB`.
- **Failure:** what failed and what to do: `1 file could not be uploaded. Retry it, or remove it from the folder and drop the project again.`

## Accessibility

- The drop target names itself through its title and description; the choose buttons are the keyboard and screen reader path, and the number of received files is announced once.
- `UploadProgress` announces the transfer summary in its own status region, without stealing focus; the overlay itself is not a live region, so rows changing are not re-announced.
- Each row says its status in words; glyphs are decorative.
- Every fade and the row advance honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- DropZone: `uploads` left out; the drop target fills the page body with the drop message, Choose a folder and Choose files.
- Initializing: `uploads` set; the overlay mid-upload, two files uploaded, the third uploading, two queued, each row with its status in words, path and size.
- UploadError: `uploads` holds a file with `status: 'error'`; one file failed, its row shows the reason and Retry, and a danger `Alert` above the list sums it up with Retry.

## Related

- `state/state-first-use` — an empty list page that can also render the drop target.
- `create/create-hub` — a creation hub that renders the drop target and Initializing.
- `dashboard/dashboard-home` — Home and its empty state, which render both surfaces.
- `state/state-async-submit` — how the deploy that follows reports back.

## Variants

`DropZone` (primary) · `Initializing` · `UploadError`. Code: [blocks/state/state-project-intake.md](blocks/state/state-project-intake.md), `get_block("state/state-project-intake", { variant })`.

# TopBarAuth (`top-bar/top-bar-auth`)

> The console bar for the signed-out and onboarding screens: sign in, sign up, password recovery and the first-run steps.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/top-bar/top-bar-auth/top-bar-auth.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("top-bar/top-bar-auth")`
- Components: AppHeader, Brand, Button
- Skills: `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

auth header; signed-out header; login page header; onboarding header; public console header; header without navigation; logged-out top bar; cabeçalho de login; cabeçalho deslogado; barra do topo sem navegação; top bar; auth bar; signed-out top bar; barra de autenticação

The top bar of every signed-out and first-run screen: sign in, sign up, password recovery and the onboarding steps. The user has no session yet, so the bar has one job: say where they are (Azion) and offer the one way out that needs no account, the documentation. Everything a signed-in bar carries (navigation, search, Create, the account avatar) is left out because there is nothing to act on.

## When to use

- Use top-bar-auth on signed-out and onboarding screens (brand + Documentation, no navigation).
- Above the auth card on sign in, sign up, reset password and MFA screens (`auth/auth-sign-in`).
- Above the onboarding steps that run before the organization exists (`account/account-onboarding-form`).

## When not to use

- Any page with a session: `ConsoleLayout` already renders the console bar (`shell/shell-console`); a create, edit or deploy flow uses `top-bar/top-bar-creation`.
- Documentation pages: `DocLayout` renders their bar (`shell/shell-docs`). Marketing pages: `SiteLayout` and `SiteHeaderSection` render theirs (`shell/shell-site`).

## Building blocks

- A. Bar — `AppHeader` (required)
- B. Brand — `Brand` (required)
- C. Documentation — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/top-bar/top-bar-auth.md](blocks/top-bar/top-bar-auth.md).

## Data

The bar shows no records and fetches nothing; a real app sets only where its two links go. `AuthBarProps` is exported from `top-bar-auth.vue`.

Prop: `homeHref`, `docsHref`.

Event: `docs`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/top-bar/top-bar-auth.md](blocks/top-bar/top-bar-auth.md).

## Do

- Keep the bar identical across every signed-out step so the user knows they are still in the same flow.
- Let the page under it own the heading and the primary action (the auth card).

## Don't

- Don't add an avatar, a menu or a search: a control that implies a session reads as broken when there is none.
- Don't put the Sign in or Sign up switch in the bar; it lives in the card as a link.

## Copy

- **Documentation button:** one noun, sentence case, no icon-only variant: `Documentation`.
- **Brand link label:** names the destination: `Azion home`.

## Accessibility

- The `AppHeader` is a landmark with its own label (`Console`); keep one per page.
- The brand is a link with an accessible name, not a decorative image.
- Tab order is brand, then Documentation; nothing else in the bar takes focus.

## States

- Default: the only state; the bar never changes between signed-out steps, and `homeHref` / `docsHref` only move its links.

## Related

- `auth/auth-sign-in` — the sign-in and sign-up card this bar sits above.
- `account/account-onboarding-form` — the first-run steps render the same bar.
- `shell/shell-console` — the bar once the user is signed in, rendered by `ConsoleLayout`.
- `top-bar/top-bar-creation` — the bar of a signed-in focused flow.

## Variants

`Default` (primary). Code: [blocks/top-bar/top-bar-auth.md](blocks/top-bar/top-bar-auth.md), `get_block("top-bar/top-bar-auth", { variant })`.

# TopBarCreation (`top-bar/top-bar-creation`)

> The console bar for the focused creation shell: create, edit and deploy flows that run without the navigation rail.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/top-bar/top-bar-creation/top-bar-creation.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`

- Components: AppHeader, `AppHeaderAccount`, Brand, Breadcrumb, DropdownMenu, IconButton, Tooltip

## Asked as

creation header; focused shell header; create flow header; flow header with back button; header without sidebar; edit flow header; deploy flow header; cabeçalho de criação; cabeçalho de fluxo; barra com botão voltar; create page header; create zone header; wizard header; header with back and breadcrumb; creation flow top bar; focused page header; cabeçalho da página de criação; cabeçalho do assistente; top bar; creation bar; top navigation without rail; focused top bar; barra de criação

The top bar of the focused creation shell: create, edit and deploy flows that run without the navigation rail. The user is doing one task with a start and an end, so the bar gives them a linear way out (the back button and the breadcrumb to the list the flow started from) and keeps their identity visible (the avatar), and nothing else. No search, no Create, no Agent: the flow is the only thing on screen.

## When to use

- Use top-bar-creation on focused create, edit and deploy pages that run without the navigation rail.
- Every one-screen create page (`create/create-page`) and stepped one (`create/create-wizard`, including its CreateAndDeploy wizard).
- The deploy flows (`create/create-deploy-template`) and the Creation Center (`create/create-hub`).

## When not to use

- Browse pages (lists, dashboards, details, settings): `ConsoleLayout` renders their bar (`shell/shell-console`).

- Signed-out screens: use `top-bar/top-bar-auth`.

## Building blocks

- A. Bar — `AppHeader` (required)
- B. Back — `IconButton` (required until the flow is terminal)
- C. Brand — `Brand` (required)
- D. Breadcrumb — `Breadcrumb` (required until the flow is terminal)
- E. Account — `DropdownMenu` + `AppHeaderAccount` (required)
- F. Hint — `Tooltip` (required)

Event: `account-select`, `navigate`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/top-bar/top-bar-creation.md](blocks/top-bar/top-bar-creation.md).

## Do

- Confirm before leaving when the form has unsaved input (the flow owns that dialog, not the bar).
- Keep the avatar even when back and crumb are gone.

## Don't

- Don't render the navigation rail or a second header under this one.
- Don't add Create, search or the Agent button: they invite the user to start a second task.
- Don't make the last crumb a link.

## Copy

- **Back label:** `Back to` plus the list name, matching the first crumb: `Back to Resources`.
- **Breadcrumb:** the module as the sidebar names it, then the create action with the entity capitalized: `Create Resource`, `Create Network List`.

- `Breadcrumb` renders a labelled `nav`; the last crumb is the current page (`aria-current`).

- Terminal: `back-href=""` and `:breadcrumb="[]"` keep only the brand and the avatar on the provisioning and success screens, with no back control and no crumb.

# ViewCard (`view/view-card`)

> The card form of a first-level list page, for resources people recognise by a few fields rather than compare column by column: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description and the outlined…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/view/view-card/view-card.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("view/view-card")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CardList, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, EmptyState, Link, PageHeader, Pagination, PropertyFilter, Tag, `use-collection`, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

card view; cards view; card list; cards list; resource cards; grid of cards; card grid page; gallery of resources; applications as cards; selectable cards; cards with filters; cards with pagination; visualização em cards; lista em cards; cartões de recursos; grade de cards

The first-level index of one resource type, in cards. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource they recognise by its name and a few fields (its status, domain, region, traffic), narrow the list by those fields, open one, or select several and act on them together. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page, the selection across pages and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row, the cards and the pagination.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The module the sidebar routes to lists resources people tell apart by a handful of fields or a picture rather than by comparing one column across many rows (applications, sites, images).
- Each item has a short, stable set of fields (four to six) that reads well as label and value pairs.
- Users act on several items at once (delete, move, tag) and need the selection to survive paging and filtering.
- The filtered list must survive a reload or a shared link, and each person's page size and visible fields must survive the next visit.

## When not to use

- Records compared and sorted column by column, or more than six fields per item: use `view/view-table`.
- A list nested inside one resource (a tab of a details page): use `detail/detail-resource` or `detail/detail-dns-zone`, with `Add <Module>` instead of `Create`.
- Templates to start from: use `view/view-template-browser`.
- Choosing a starting point to create from (products): use `create/create-hub` or `create/create-deploy-template`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `view/view-file-browser`.
- An account that has never created the resource: use `state/state-first-use`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Property filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)
- C. Bulk action — `Button` (required)
- D. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert` (required)
- E. Card preferences — `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- F. CardList — `CardList`, `Link`, `Tag` (required)
- G. Pagination — `Pagination` (required)
- H. No matching applications — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- I. Empty listing and load failure — `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Alert`, `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/view/view-card.md](blocks/view/view-card.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `CardViewApplication` and `CardViewProps` are exported from `view-card.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample cards the block renders when `applications` is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `applications`, `loading`, `error`.

Event: `create`, `retry`, `delete`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/view/view-card.md](blocks/view/view-card.md).

## Do

- Run the whole list on one `useCollection` call with `selection: { mode: 'multiple' }` and bind `cardListProps`, `paginationProps`, `propertyFilterProps` and `preferencesProps` with `v-bind`.
- Keep the controls row, the cards and the pagination in one band at the group gap; the heading sits one section step above.
- Name every card with a link to the resource in the `header` slot, and keep its fields to the few that tell one item from another.
- Render the fields from `preferences.columns`, so the order and visibility set in the dialog reach every card.
- Count the selection in the bulk action's label and disable it at zero.
- Put every Delete behind the confirmation dialog, with the count in its title and the names in its body.
- Set `url: true` so the tokens and the page live in the query string, and give the list a `storageKey` of its own.
- Choose page sizes that fill whole rows of four.
- Branch on `status`: `empty` replaces the cards with the create state, `no-match` fills the `#empty` slot with Clear filters.

## Don't

- Don't add a search `Input`, a filter popover or a row of `Select`s beside the `PropertyFilter`.
- Don't make the whole card a link or a click target when it is also selectable; the name link opens it and the checkbox selects it.
- Don't put row-style action menus on every card for actions the bulk action already covers.
- Don't vary a card's height or field order from one card to the next; every card shows the same fields in the same order, with a dash for a missing value.
- Don't truncate the name in the header to fit a badge; the status lives in the fields.
- Don't hide Delete when nothing is selected; disable it so its place in the row stays put.
- Don't show the state-first-use empty state when filters hide every card, or Clear filters when the account has none.

## Copy

- **Title:** the module name as the sidebar shows it, e.g. "Applications". Description: one sentence with a period.
- **Create action:** `Create <Object>` with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Application"; never "New" or a bare noun. The empty state uses the same label and is the only Create while the list is empty.
- **Filter:** placeholder and `aria-label` name what is filtered, e.g. "Filter applications".
- **Bulk action:** the verb, then the count in parentheses, e.g. "Delete", "Delete (3)".
- **Field labels:** one or two words, sentence case, no colon, e.g. "Status", "Domain", "Region", "Requests in 24h", "Owner". Preferences title: "Card preferences".
- **Delete dialog:** title `Delete <n> applications`, consequence `The selected applications will be deleted, along with their domains and settings:` followed by the names, prompt `Type <name> to confirm.` for one, `Type delete to confirm.` for several, actions `Cancel` and `Delete applications` (singular for one).
- **No match:** "No matching applications", then "No application matches these filters.", and the action "Clear filters".
- **Empty:** title states the fact, e.g. "No applications yet"; description is one sentence with what to do, e.g. "Create an application to start serving traffic."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The layout owns the one `main` landmark; the `PageHeader` title is the page's only `h1`.
- `CardList` is a list named by its `aria-label`; each card is labelled by its header, and its checkbox is named by the same text.
- Select all items is a visible, labelled checkbox, not an icon; its state is mixed when part of the page is selected.
- Field labels and values are a `dl`, so each value is read with its label; status is a `Tag` with text, never color alone.
- The `PropertyFilter` has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder, and the match count is announced after each change.
- Focus order follows reading order: heading actions, filter, Delete, Preferences, Select all items, each card's checkbox and link, pagination.
- The delete dialog traps focus, names itself by its title, labels its input by the prompt and returns focus to Delete (n) when it closes.
- The preferences dialog traps focus, is named by its title and returns focus to its trigger when it closes.
- `/` focuses the property filter from anywhere on the page, except while typing in a field.
- Cards are reached with Tab (each card's checkbox and link); Space toggles the focused checkbox. Delete deletes nothing on its own: select the cards, then Delete (n) asks before it deletes.

## States

- Default: applications exist; the cards show them with the property filter, multi-select with Delete (n) behind its confirmation dialog, preferences and pagination wired, and filtering to nothing shows No matching applications with Clear filters.
- Loading: the first load (`loading` with no `applications`); the heading stays, the filter, Delete and preferences are disabled, and `CardList` shows its placeholder cards (`loading`, `aria-busy`).
- Error: the applications could not load (`error` is set); the heading and the disabled controls stay and a danger `Alert` with Retry takes the cards' place. Every view block's error state follows one rule: the filter or search stays in place, disabled; Download CSV and the preferences are disabled; Refresh stays live.
- Empty: the account has no applications (`applications` is `[]`); `useCollection` reports `empty`, the heading and controls stay, and a flush card holding a medium empty state with Create Application replaces the cards.

## Related

- `view/view-table` — the same collection, rendered as a sortable table.
- `edit/edit-delete-dialog` — the dialog behind Delete (n).
- `create/create-page` — where the Create action leads for a short form.
- `detail/detail-resource` — where a card's name leads.
- `state/state-first-use` — the module before its first resource.
- `useCollection`, `CardList` and `Pagination` — see `skills/webkit-lists`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Error` · `Empty`. Code: [blocks/view/view-card.md](blocks/view/view-card.md), `get_block("view/view-card", { variant })`.

# ViewEventsExplorer (`view/view-events-explorer`)

> The events explorer (the app marks its Events navigation entry active): the controls row (`FilterMenu`, event search, the time zone, Refresh and Download CSV) over the applied `FilterMenu.ChipGroup`, and the explorer.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/view/view-events-explorer/view-events-explorer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("view/view-events-explorer")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Button, Chart, Checkbox, Chip, CodeBlock, CopyButton, DataTable, `DataTableLoadMore`, `DataTablePagination`, DateRangePicker, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, FilterMenu, FilterMenu, IconButton, Input, Item, `PanelHeader`, Popover, PropertyFilter, Resizable, Select, Sidebar, Skeleton, Tabs, Tag, Toast, Tooltip, Trace, `use-collection`, `use-locale`, `use-shortcuts`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

real-time events; events visualizer; event explorer; log explorer; logs viewer; request logs; events search; eventos em tempo real; visualizador de eventos; explorador de logs; split view; master detail; list and detail panes; visão dividida; query language; events query; saved searches; saved queries; query history; date range; time range picker; investigation tabs; event document; request trace; trace waterfall; critical path; trace de requisição; consulta de eventos; buscas salvas; intervalo de datas

The events explorer. The user comes here to answer what happened on their traffic: how many events, how many errors, when they spiked, and what one event looked like in full. They narrow the log by fields and time, scan the rows, and open one event beside the log without losing their place. The fields, the log and the event document are three panes of one workspace, and every filter acts on all of them at once.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`. The explorer is a workspace: its root carries `data-layout-fill`, so the layout's `main` stops scrolling, the root fills it, and the fields panel, the log and the event document each scroll on their own at every width (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview).

## When to use

- Events or logs explored over time, where the volume chart and the rows must agree on one period and one set of filters.
- Users pivot on field values (level, source, status, host) to find a pattern, then read one event's full document.
- The record has more fields than a table row can hold, so the full document opens beside the list instead of in a details page.

## When not to use

- A first-level list of resources the user creates and manages: use `view/view-table`.
- The log of one deployment or build run: use `detail/detail-deployment-logs`.
- Metrics and charts without a row-level log: use `dashboard/dashboard-analytics`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `view/view-file-browser`.
- Querying a database with SQL: use `view/view-query-editor`.

## Building blocks

- A. Filter — `FilterMenu` (required)
- B. Search and toolbar — `Input`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- C. Applied filters — `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` (optional)
- D. Fields panel — `Sidebar`, `Input`, `Field`, `Checkbox`, `Popover`, `Item`, `Accordion`, `Tag` (optional)
- E. Log — `Chart`, `Skeleton`, `DataTable`, `Tag`, `EmptyState`, `Alert` (required)
- F. Event document — `Resizable`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Tag`, `Trace`, `CodeBlock` (required)
- G. Narrow document — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `Tag`, `Trace`, `CodeBlock` (required)
- H. Query bar — `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (optional)
- I. Saved and recent queries — `Popover`, `IconButton`, `Input`, `Item`, `Tooltip` (optional)
- J. Investigation tabs — `IconButton`, `Input`, `Tooltip` (optional)
- K. Document tools — `Chip`, `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/view/view-events-explorer.md](blocks/view/view-events-explorer.md).

## Data

The block takes its events through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `EventsExplorerEvent`, `EventsExplorerField`, `EventsExplorerBucket`, `EventsExplorerProps` and the other types are exported from `view-events-explorer.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample events, fields and clock the block renders when `events` is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set). The filters (the period included), the search and the page are models the page can own, so it can run them on the server.

Prop / model: `events`, `fields`, `categories`, `buckets`, `summary`, `total`, `now`, `moreRows`, `loadingMore`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:filters`, `v-model:search`, `v-model:page`, `v-model:page-size`, `timeZone`, `match`, `v-model:exclusions`, `v-model:selected-key`.

Slot: `toolbar`, `document-fields`.

Event: `refresh`, `retry`, `select`, `load-more`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/view/view-events-explorer.md](blocks/view/view-events-explorer.md).

## Do

- Drive the summary, the chart and the table from one filtered set, so every number agrees.
- Let a click or drag on the chart set the period, and show the period as a filter the user can clear.
- Keep the row selected while its document is open, and switch between pane and drawer by the explorer's width, not the viewport's.
- Let `FilterMenu` count the applied fields on its trigger and `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` show each one in field order.
- Pick the empty message that matches why the log is empty.
- In query mode, keep the applied query text as the user typed it, and save and list that text.
- Keep each investigation tab self-contained: its own filters, search and period.
- Let the document act on the log (Filter by, Exclude), so a pivot is one click from the value.
- Mark the page root with `data-layout-fill`, so the panes scroll on their own instead of the page.

## Don't

- Don't navigate away to read one event; the document opens beside the log.
- Don't add a second filter surface (a row of `Select`s, a filter bar in the fields panel) beside the Filter menu.
- Don't hide the controls row or the summary when the log is empty.
- Don't encode level by colour alone; the chart has a card with level names and counts, and the table shows level as text.
- Don't let a wide log scroll the page sideways.
- Don't size the root with `calc(100dvh - …)`; `data-layout-fill` fits it to the layout's `main`.
- Don't offer the query bar and the Filter menu at once; pick the one that fits the users.
- Don't guess the meaning of a query that mixes AND and OR; say so and let the user fix it.
- Don't let investigation tabs grow without a limit, and never close the last one.

## Copy

- **Search:** placeholder names what is searched, e.g. "Search events, hosts, paths or addresses"; `aria-label` "Search events".
- **Summary labels:** short nouns, e.g. "Events", "Errors", "Avg request time".
- **Chart hint:** one instruction, e.g. "Drag across the chart, or hold Shift with the arrow keys and press Enter, to filter the log to a span."
- **Empty log:** title states the fact and the description says what to do, e.g. "No events in this window" with "Widen the period or clear a filter to see more of the log."
- **Fields panel:** controls name the panel, e.g. "Hide the fields panel", "Show the fields panel".
- **Document:** drawer title "Event"; close button "Close the event document".
- **Query bar:** `aria-label` "Query events"; placeholder with one real example; the range "Events time range".
- **Saved queries:** "Name the current query", Save, "Delete <name>"; empty "No saved queries yet. Name the current query to keep it."
- **Tabs:** "New investigation", "Actions for <name>", Rename, Duplicate, "Close investigation"; limit "Up to 5 investigations stay open. Close one to start another."
- **Document tools:** "Search in this event", "Filter by <field> <value>", "Exclude <field> <value>", "Copy the fields shown as JSON"; no match "No field matches “<text>”."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The explorer sits in the layout's one `main` landmark; each `Sidebar` is named (Fields, Event document) with its own collapse, expand and resize labels.
- The chart is `Chart`'s one tab stop with an `aria-label` that carries the summary (busiest bucket) and the instruction; arrow keys move between buckets, Shift extends a span, Enter commits it, and the tooltip follows keyboard focus as it follows the pointer.
- The Errors value carries an `aria-label` with its share of all events.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`; decorative glyphs are `aria-hidden="true"`. The row detail button names its event and carries `aria-expanded`.
- Value options in the fields-panel popovers are buttons with `aria-pressed`, so applied values are announced; the Filter menu's own rows come from `FilterMenu`.
- The log rows are one tab stop: Arrow Up and Arrow Down move between rows, Home and End jump to the first and last, and Enter opens the focused event's document, as a click on the row does.
- The document drawer traps focus while open and closes on Escape; motion is turned off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Query: `/` focuses the query bar from anywhere on the page, except while typing in a field; the bar is a `combobox` whose invalid state sets `aria-invalid` and points `aria-describedby` at the reason; the mixed AND / OR message and the saved-query confirmations are `role="status"`.
- Sessions: the tabs follow the `Tabs` keyboard map (arrows, Home, End); F2 renames and Delete closes the focused tab, and the same actions sit in a named menu for pointer and screen-reader users; focus returns to the tab after rename or close.
- EventDocument: Filter by and Exclude are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`) named with the field and value; the match count of the document search is announced in a `role="status"`.

## States

- Default: live traffic with the summary, the chart and the log filled, and no filters applied; while the page refreshes (`loading` with `events`) the summary values and the chart show `Skeleton`s and the table its loading rows.
- Loading: the first load (`loading` with no `events`); `Skeleton`s hold the summary values and the chart band and the table shows its loading rows.
- Filtered: errors from the Security and Access Control sources (`v-model:filters` seeded with them); the Filter button counts three fields and each shows as a `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` chip.
- Empty: a workspace with no traffic yet (`events` is `[]`); the summary reads zero, the chart is flat and the log shows No events yet.
- Error: the event request failed (`error` is set); the fields panel stays and the log pane shows a danger `Alert` with the message and Retry, which emits `retry`. The filter menu and the search stay, disabled, Download CSV is disabled and Refresh stays live. Every view block's error state follows one rule: the filter or search stays in place, disabled; Download CSV and the preferences are disabled; Refresh stays live.
- Query: `level = Error AND host = api.example.com` over the last 24 hours, with two saved and two recent queries.
- Sessions: three investigation tabs, API errors active; the tabs sit above the block, which each tab feeds through `v-model:filters` and `v-model:search`.
- EventDocument: an error event's document open, with Host is not legacy.example.com applied.

## Related

- `view/view-table` — the same controls row over a resource list.
- `detail/detail-deployment-logs` — logs of one deployment run.
- `dashboard/dashboard-analytics` — the metrics view for the same traffic.
- `shell/shell-console` — the layout this explorer renders in.
- `DataTable` — the log table; see `skills/webkit-tables`, `skills/webkit-data-viz` and `skills/webkit-ui-states`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Filtered` · `Empty` · `Loading` · `Error` · `Query` · `Sessions` · `EventDocument`. Code: [blocks/view/view-events-explorer.md](blocks/view/view-events-explorer.md), `get_block("view/view-events-explorer", { variant })`.

# ViewFileBrowser (`view/view-file-browser`)

> The file browser a storage resource opens on: one flush `Card` holding a borderless `DataTable` whose toolbar is the whole page header.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/view/view-file-browser/view-file-browser.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("view/view-file-browser")`
- Components: Alert, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, Combobox, ConfirmDialog, DataTable, `DataTablePagination`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem`, EmptyState, Field, FileDropzone, FileTokenGroup, IconButton, Input, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, SplitButton, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellTime`, `TableSearch`, Toast, Tooltip, UploadProgress, `use-file-picker`, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-tables`, `webkit-lists`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

file browser; file manager; storage browser; bucket browser; object storage; folders and files; upload files; navegador de arquivos; gerenciador de arquivos; arquivos do bucket; upload progress; move files; move objects; drag and drop upload; enviar arquivos; mover arquivos; file preview; preview a file; object preview; visualizar arquivo

The contents of one storage resource. The user opens a bucket to find a file, walk into a folder and back out, upload something or add a folder, and download or delete what is there. The table's toolbar is the whole page header, so the storage name, search, the folder path and Add to files all sit on the one surface the files live on.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- A storage resource (an Object Storage bucket, a build output) opens on its files and folders.
- Users move through a folder tree and need to know where they are and how to go back up.
- Files are compared by name, size and last change, and acted on one at a time: open, download, delete.

## When not to use

- A first-level list of resources of one type: use `view/view-table`.
- Rows of one resource that are records, not files (database rows, variables): use `detail/detail-dns-zone`.
- Events or logs explored over time: use `view/view-events-explorer`.
- Tables and queries of a database: use `view/view-query-editor`.
- Picking an existing resource inside a create form: use `create/create-resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

- A. Surface — `Card`, `DataTable`, `DataTablePagination` (required)
- B. Storage title and search — `TableSearch` (required)
- C. Toolbar actions — `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (optional)
- D. Columns — `CollectionPreferences` (optional)
- E. Path and create — `Breadcrumb`, `SplitButton` (required)
- F. Cell recipes — `TableCellTime` (optional)
- G. Row actions — `TableCellActions`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem` (required)
- H. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert` (required)
- I. Empty folder — `EmptyState`, `SplitButton` (required)
- J. Upload — `Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `FileDropzone`, `FileTokenGroup` (required)
- K. Transfer card — `UploadProgress`, `Button` (optional)
- L. Selection and Move — `DataTable`, `DropdownMenuItem`, `Field`, `Combobox` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/view/view-file-browser.md](blocks/view/view-file-browser.md).

## Data

The block takes the open folder through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `FileBrowserEntry`, `FileBrowserTransfer` and `FileBrowserProps` are exported from `view-file-browser.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds a sample storage the block browses when `entries` is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set). `azion-storage.ts` maps an Azion Object Storage listing to entries. `lib/file-rows.ts` turns entries into table rows (glyph, size, sort, folders first) and checks a Move destination; the regions are private parts in `parts/`: the storage title, the search row, the selection bar, the name cell, the row menu, the empty folder, the error card, the upload, move and delete dialogs and the transfer card.

Prop / model: `storageName`, `v-model:path`, `entries`, `loading`, `error`, `destinations`, `movable`, `v-model:selected-keys`, `defaultMoveOpen`, `transfers`, `transferOperation`.

Event: `open`, `download`, `delete`, `upload`, `add-folder`, `move`, `refresh`, `retry`, `cancel-transfer`, `retry-transfer`, `close-transfer`.

`api.listObjects` stands for the app's own authenticated client (it returns the response body, `AzionStorageObjectsResponse`). Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/view/view-file-browser.md](blocks/view/view-file-browser.md).

## Do

- Keep the storage name, search, path and Add to files inside the table toolbar, on the same surface as the rows.
- Sort folders before files, keep `..` first under any sort, and sort Size and Last modified on numbers, never on display strings.
- Show the path as a `Breadcrumb` and keep the `..` row while inside a folder.
- Use one Add to files `SplitButton` for every way of adding content.
- Put Delete last in the row menu, in its own group, and confirm it with `edit/edit-delete-dialog`.
- Give every icon-only control a `Tooltip` and an `aria-label` with the same words.
- Keep refused files in the upload dialog with their reason, and leave them out of the upload count.
- Run every transfer in the one floating `UploadProgress` card and let the person keep working.
- End every transfer with a toast whose action fits the files: Open folder or Retry failed.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/shell-console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't add a `PageHeader` above the card; the toolbar is the header.
- Don't split Upload file and Add folder into two primary buttons.
- Don't give the `..` row a row menu, a size or an author.
- Don't let the table scroll the page sideways; on a phone the grid scrolls sideways inside its card, never the page.
- Don't replace the toolbar with a full-page empty state when a folder is empty; only the table area changes.
- Don't block the page with a modal progress dialog while files upload or move.
- Don't offer View deployments, Edit or Redeploy after a storage transfer; nothing is deployed.
- Don't drop a refused file silently, and don't send a file the dialog marked as refused.

## Copy

- **Storage name:** the resource name as created, e.g. "acme-assets"; never prefixed with the type.
- **Search:** placeholder names the scope, e.g. "Search in folder".
- **Add action:** "Add to files", with options "Upload file" and "Add folder".
- **Row menu:** one verb per option, e.g. "Open", "Download", "Delete"; the trigger is named "Actions for <file>".
- **Delete dialog:** title and confirm `Delete file` or `Delete folder`, consequence `The selected folder will be deleted, along with all its files.`, prompt `Type <name> to confirm.`
- **Column headers:** short fragments, e.g. "Name", "Size", "Last modified".
- **Empty folder:** title states the fact, e.g. "This folder is empty"; description is one sentence, e.g. "Upload files or create a folder to get started."
- **Upload dialog:** title `Upload files`, primary `Upload file` or `Upload 3 files`, refusal `Larger than 300 MB, the limit per file`.
- **Drop overlay:** `Drop files to upload them to <folder>`, description `Up to 300 MB per file.`
- **Move dialog:** title `Move <name>` or `Move 2 files`, field `Destination folder`, placeholder `/ (storage root)`, errors `Use letters, numbers, dots, hyphens and slashes only.`, `A destination cannot go up with "..". Type the full path.`, `The files are already in this folder. Pick another one.`
- **Toasts:** `5 files uploaded to acme-assets.` with Open folder; `1 of 5 files weren't uploaded.` with Retry failed; `2 files moved to logs/.` with Open folder.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The card sits in the layout's one `main` landmark; the storage name is the page's `h1`.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`; file and folder glyphs carry `aria-hidden="true"`, so the name cell reads as the name alone.
- The `Breadcrumb` crumbs are links the keyboard reaches in order; the last crumb is the current folder.
- Folder and `..` names are buttons, so a keyboard user opens a folder or goes up with Tab and Enter; the row click is the pointer shortcut and the Open option in the row menu repeats it.
- Focus order follows reading order: search, Refresh, Download CSV, Columns, path, Add to files, the rows.
- `/` focuses the folder search from anywhere on the page, except while typing in a field.
- The rows are one tab stop: Arrow Up and Arrow Down move between rows, Home and End jump to the first and last, Enter opens the focused folder or file (or goes up from `..`), Space selects a file when moving is on, and Delete or Backspace opens the delete dialog for a file or folder. After a delete, focus lands on the next row.
- `TableCellTime` names the author and reads the absolute time to screen readers.
- The drop overlay is `aria-hidden`: dragging is a pointer path, and Add to files with Browse files is the keyboard path to the same upload.
- `UploadProgress` is a region named File transfers with a polite status that announces each file finishing and the outcome; percentages are not announced. The toast repeats the outcome for people who collapsed the card.
- In the upload dialog each refused file's reason is the `aria-describedby` of its Remove button, and removing a file moves focus to the next one.
- The Move dialog's `Field` wires the label, description and error to the `Combobox`; the error is read when focus returns to it.

## States

- Default: the storage root (`path` is empty) with folders first, then files, and the full toolbar.
- InsideAFolder: `path` is a build folder; the crumb gains the folder, a `..` row leads back up and files show glyph, size, editor and age.
- Uploading: `transfers` holds a running upload in the floating card; Add to files opens the upload dialog and the page drop overlay adds more.
- Empty: `entries` is `[]` inside `assets/` of a build; the `..` row stays and the empty state offers Add to files.
- Error: `error` is set; the storage name, the search row (search, Download CSV and the column settings disabled, Refresh live) and the path stay, Add to files is disabled and a danger `Alert` with the message and Retry takes the table's place. Every view block's error state follows one rule: the filter or search stays in place, disabled; Download CSV and the preferences are disabled; Refresh stays live.
- MoveObject: `movable` with two files in `selectedKeys` and `defaultMoveOpen`; the Move dialog is open and Move emits `move`.

## Related

- `view/view-table` — the first-level list a storage resource is opened from.
- `edit/edit-delete-dialog` — the dialog behind Delete on a file or folder.
- `detail/detail-resource` — the storage resource's own details and settings.
- `detail/detail-dns-zone` — records of a resource, not files.
- `FileTokenGroup`, `FileDropzone` and `UploadProgress` — the upload pieces; see their component docs.
- `state/state-async-submit` — the rule for long actions; storage transfers follow it with item actions instead of Edit and Redeploy.
- `DataTable` — the data-driven table this page wraps; see `skills/webkit-tables` and `skills/webkit-lists`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `InsideAFolder` · `Uploading` · `Empty` · `Error` · `MoveObject`. Code: [blocks/view/view-file-browser.md](blocks/view/view-file-browser.md), `get_block("view/view-file-browser", { variant })`.

# ViewMarketplace (`view/view-marketplace`)

> The marketplace page: a medium page heading with the outlined Documentation action over the integration catalog, the integrations installed into an existing application (templates live in `view/view-template-browser`)…

- Surface: app

- Components: Alert, Button, Card, DataTable, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, EmptyState, Field, Input, IntegrationCard, Item, Kbd, KeyValueList, Link, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PropertyFilter, SaveBar, Select, SettingsGroup, SettingsRow, Skeleton, Switch, `TableCellStatus`, Tabs, Tag, Toast, `use-collection`

## Asked as

marketplace; integration catalog; integrations marketplace; install an integration; browse integrations; extensions catalog; plugin catalog; app store page; integration detail; installed integrations; configure integration; marketplace de integrações; catálogo de integrações; instalar integração; loja de extensões

The page where people find something made by Azion or a partner and add it to what they run. It lists integrations, installed into an existing application; templates, which start a new project, live in `view/view-template-browser`. People browse by need ("block bots", "split traffic"), compare by publisher and context, read what an integration does and what it may touch, then install it on one application and keep working while it installs. One `useCollection` call holds the search and the filters; one drawer holds the detail and the install; the install reports by toast wherever the person is.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/shell-console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use marketplace for installable integrations into an existing resource; templates live in view-template-browser.
- A catalog of installable add-ons (integrations, extensions, plugins) with a publisher, a category and an installed state per account.
- Installing means choosing a target (an application) and waiting for an asynchronous run.

## When not to use

- The catalog of templates a project starts from: use `view/view-template-browser`.
- Deploying a chosen template: use `create/create-deploy-template`.
- The resources the account already created: use `view/view-card` or `view/view-table`.
- Changing the settings of an installed integration on one application: use `edit/edit-resource` from Configure.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Featured — `IntegrationCard` (required)
- C. Search and filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)
- D. Integration tiles — `IntegrationCard`, `Button` (required)
- E. No matching integrations — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- F. Integration drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter` (required)
- G. Install outcome — `Alert` (required)
- H. Integration facts — `KeyValueList` (required)
- I. Install form — `Field`, `Select` (required)
- J. Solution page — `Card`, `Select`, `Field`, `KeyValueList` (optional)
- K. Configure screen — `Field`, `Select`, `Alert`, `Button` (optional)
- L. Loading catalog — `Card`, `Skeleton` (required)
- Install toast — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/view/view-marketplace.md](blocks/view/view-marketplace.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing and runs no install itself. `MarketplaceIntegration`, `MarketplaceInstall` and `MarketplaceProps` are exported from `view-marketplace.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample catalog and applications the block renders when `integrations` and `applications` are left out (the catalog never while `loading` is set).
