<!-- components/icon-button.md -->

# Icon Button

> A square control that triggers an action with a glyph and no visible text: close, refresh, delete, more. It shares the variants, sizes and loading state of `Button`, takes its accessible name from `aria-label`, can swap between two icons in place, and renders as an anchor when `href` is set.

- Import: `import IconButton from '@aziontech/webkit/icon-button'`
- Category: action · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Compact actions in toolbars, table rows, card headers and overlay close controls where the glyph is widely understood (close, refresh, delete, more).
- Swapping between two icons in place (copy to check, show to hide), with `iconTransition` animating the change.
- An icon-only link: set `href` and it renders as an anchor.

## Do

- Always name it with the kebab attribute `aria-label="Delete domain"` (`:aria-label` when the name changes, `aria-labelledby` when visible text already names it). Describe the action ("Delete domain"), not the glyph ("Trash"). Write `aria-label`, never the camelCase `ariaLabel` attribute: Vue maps the kebab attribute onto the `ariaLabel` prop, and it is the form every other attribute takes in a template.
- The `ariaLabel` prop is optional in the types on purpose: vue-tsc does not camelize `aria-*` attributes onto props, so a required `ariaLabel` made the obvious `aria-label="…"` fail to type-check in a fresh create-vue app. The lint rule `webkit/require-accessible-name` keeps the name required instead: it flags an `IconButton` with neither `aria-label` nor `aria-labelledby`.
- Wrap it in `tooltip` when the glyph is not self-evident, so pointer users see the name screen readers hear.
- Use `variant="ghost"` in dense rows and toolbars; keep `primary` for a lone emphasized action.
- Set `iconTransition` only when `icon` changes at runtime; with a static icon it adds nothing.
- Use `iconClass` for glyph-level tweaks instead of styling the root.

## Don’t

- The action needs a visible label → use `button`.
- Copying a value to the clipboard → use `copy-button`, which already wires the icon swap, the tooltip and the `copy` event.
- Choosing one of a few mutually exclusive options → use `toggle-group`.

## Related

- `button` — labelled counterpart; sizes line up and its `text` variant matches `ghost` here.
- `copy-button` — IconButton plus Tooltip with the clipboard write built in.
- `tooltip` — wrap an IconButton to show its name on hover and focus.
- `split-button` — uses an IconButton as its chevron menu toggle.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `string` | `—` | true | Azion icon class for the leading/trailing icon. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the icon-only control, written as the `aria-label` attribute. Empty only when `aria-labelledby` names the button; then no `aria-label` renders. |
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'outline' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger'` | `'primary'` | false | Visual variant. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token; affects height, padding, and typography. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows loading state and disables activation. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | When set to a safe URL, renders as a link (`<a>`); an unsafe URL is ignored, and a `download` attribute keeps `blob:` / `data:` (see Accessibility). |
| `target` | `'_blank' \| '_self'` | `'_self'` | false | Link target when `href` is set. |
| `iconTransition` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Animates icon swaps with enter/leave transitions. |
| `iconClass` | `string` | `''` | false | Extra classes applied to the icon glyph. |
| `type` | `'button' \| 'submit' \| 'reset'` | `'button'` | false | Native button type. `submit` lets an icon-only control submit its form (a search submit, a chat send); `disabled` and `loading` still block it. Ignored when `href` is set. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `MouseEvent` | — |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop (or a focusable-disabled `aria-disabled`); `data-loading` the `loading` prop; `data-inert` is set while disabled or loading
- While inert, a `ghost` or `outline` button drops its fill and frame and only its glyph takes `--text-disabled`, so an unavailable toolbar control is never louder than the enabled controls beside it; `primary`, `secondary` and `danger` take `--bg-disabled`
- Focusable disabled: an `aria-disabled="true"` attribute (with `disabled` false) keeps the control in the tab order but makes it inert: `data-disabled` and `data-inert` are set, it takes the disabled look and a click emits nothing. Use it for a control whose availability changes while focus moves past it (the carousel step controls), so the tab order stays fixed
- `data-variant` mirrors `variant` and `data-size` mirrors `size` on the root; the variant utilities switch on them (no class presets)
- `IconButtonType` is exported beside `IconButtonVariant`, `IconButtonSize` and `IconButtonTarget`
- Touch: the drawn size is unchanged (28/32/40 px); on a coarse pointer an invisible `[data-slot=touch-target]` span extends the hit area to at least 44 × 44 px.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated states; the icon swap also starts from `scale-100` under reduced motion.
- Accessible name: `aria-label` (static or bound) or `aria-labelledby` is mandatory; `webkit/require-accessible-name` flags an IconButton with neither, and an empty name renders no `aria-label` attribute.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.
- Unsafe `href` (`javascript:`, `data:`, any non-web scheme, `//host`): stays a native button (with `download`, `blob:` and `data:` are kept).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import IconButton from '@aziontech/webkit/icon-button'
</script>

<template>
  <IconButton
    variant="primary"
    size="large"
    icon="az az-plus"
    aria-label="Add"
  />
</template>
```

# Search Trigger

> The field-shaped button in a top bar that opens search: a magnifier, a muted label (`Search` by default) and the keycap of the shortcut that opens the same palette (`⌘K` on macOS, `Ctrl K` elsewhere, drawn by `Kbd`). It looks like an input so the bar reads "you can search here", but it is one `<button>` that emits `open` — on click and on the shortcut itself, which it binds on the window unless a mounted `Command` already listens for it. The consumer opens `Command` (or its own search) from `open`. Every app header — console, demo, docs and site — carries one: it is the single way search is offered in a top bar. With `collapsible` it folds to the magnifier alone inside a narrow container (with its label as a tooltip), so one element serves the wide and the narrow bar.

- Import: `import SearchTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/search-trigger'`
- Category: action · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use SearchTrigger only in the top bar to open the ⌘K palette (Command); search over one table is TableSearch.
- The search entry of every app header — console, demo, docs or site top bar (`AppHeader.End`) — that opens the `Command` palette or a search dialog. A header without it is incomplete.
- Anywhere a shortcut-backed launcher should look like a field without being one.

## Do

- Wire `@open` to the same state the shortcut opens (`<Command v-model:open="open">`), so the button and ⌘K never disagree. Without a `Command` on the page, `@open` also fires on ⌘K / Ctrl K, so a custom search dialog gets the shortcut for free.
- Keep `shortcut` equal to the key the `Command` root listens for (`K`), or clear it (`shortcut=""`) when no shortcut exists.
- Do not hand-roll the field (`<button>` + magnifier + `Kbd`) or put a bare magnifier `IconButton` in a header: the `webkit/require-header-search` lint rule flags both.
- With `collapsible`, put the bar inside an `@container` (the header blocks do); the trigger folds while that container is narrower than 47rem (752 px, the `--container-2xl` token) and without a container it stays folded. Do not add your own breakpoint around it: 47rem is the one threshold every header uses.
- With `collapsible`, the button sits inside the `Tooltip` wrapper, so put layout classes (`ms-auto`, `order-*`) on a parent, not on the trigger.
- Name the target in the label when the scope is narrow (`Search docs`); the label is also the accessible name.
- Leave the accessible name to the label: to name a narrower scope, change `label` (`Search docs`), not `aria-label`. An `aria-label` attribute replaces the name and must start with the visible text, or a voice-control user who says what they see cannot activate the button (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name).

## Don’t

- To type a query in place (filter a list, search a table) → use `Input` with a search icon, `PropertyFilter`, or the `Table` search part.
- For the palette itself → use `Command`; this only opens it.
- For an icon-only toolbar action that is not search → use `IconButton`.

## Related

- `Command` — the palette this button opens; when it is mounted it owns the global ⌘K / Ctrl+K listener and `v-model:open`, and the trigger stands its own listener down.
- `Kbd` — draws the keycap with the OS-aware modifier glyph.
- `IconButton` — the shape the trigger folds to when `collapsible` and the container is narrow.
- `Tooltip` — shows the label over the folded magnifier on hover and focus.
- `AppHeader` — the bar it sits in, usually in `AppHeader.End`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible muted text and accessible name; empty uses the catalog's `Search`. |
| `shortcut` | `string` | `'K'` | false | Key that opens search with ⌘ or Ctrl: drawn in the keycap, announced through `aria-keyshortcuts` and bound on the window unless a mounted `Command` already listens for it; empty removes all three. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Folds to the magnifier alone while the nearest container is narrower than 47rem (752px, the `--container-2xl` token); the label stays the accessible name and shows as a tooltip on hover and focus. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the button and its shortcut; `open` is not emitted. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent` | Fires when the button is activated (pointer, Enter or Space) and on ⌘K / Ctrl K when no mounted `Command` claims that shortcut; not while `disabled`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (border strengthens), `focus-visible` (ring), `disabled`.
- `data-disabled` mirrors `disabled`; `data-collapsible` mirrors `collapsible`.
- Folded (`collapsible` in a container narrower than 47rem): a `Tooltip` (`side="bottom"`, test id `<testid>__tooltip`) shows the label on hover and focus. It is disabled while the trigger is unfolded or `disabled`; the trigger measures its own label with a `ResizeObserver` to know which form is drawn.
- Not applicable: `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `open`/`closed` (the palette owns open state).

## Accessibility

- Pattern: a WAI-ARIA APG **button** (`<button type="button">`) named from its content: a visually hidden span (`sr-only`, test id `<testid>__name`) carries the label, and the drawn label, the magnifier and the keycap are `aria-hidden`. The name is exactly the visible label (`Search`), in the wide and in the folded form, and the button carries no `aria-label`, so the visible text (`Search ⌘K`) never disagrees with an author-supplied name (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name; axe `label-content-name-mismatch` only applies to `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`). A consumer `aria-label` attribute still wins and must start with the visible text.
- Shortcut: `aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K Control+K"` (both chords `Command` listens for, in ARIA key syntax, so the server and the client render the same attribute) when `shortcut` is set; the keycap is `aria-hidden`, so the shortcut is announced once, through `aria-keyshortcuts`, and stays out of the name.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter` and `Space` activate; `⌘K` / `Ctrl K` anywhere on the page opens search (handled by `Command` when one is mounted, otherwise by the trigger, which emits `open`).
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Disabled: native `disabled` (out of the tab order, not announced as actionable); text and border keep ≥ 3:1 against the surface.
- Contrast: muted label ≥ 4.5:1 on `--bg-surface` in light and dark; magnifier ≥ 3:1.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the colour transition.
- Touch target: drawn 32 px tall in the wide form and 32 × 32 px folded on every pointer, the same box as the header's `IconButton` medium neighbours. On a coarse pointer an invisible `aria-hidden` span (`data-slot="touch-target"`, `inset-[min(0rem,calc(50%-22px))]`, the `IconButton` technique) grows the hit area to at least 44 × 44 px without changing the drawn size.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Command from '@aziontech/webkit/command'
  import SearchTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/search-trigger'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const open = ref(false)
  const pages = ['Workloads', 'Applications', 'Functions', 'Firewall']
</script>

<template>
  <SearchTrigger @open="open = true" />
  <Command
    v-model:open="open"
    shortcut="meta+k"
    @select="open = false"
  >
    <Command.Input placeholder="Search pages" />
    <Command.List>
      <Command.Empty>No results.</Command.Empty>
      <Command.Group label="Pages">
        <Command.Item
          v-for="page in pages"
          :key="page"
          :value="page"
          >{{ page }}</Command.Item
        >
      </Command.Group>
    </Command.List>
  </Command>
</template>
```

# Split Button

> A primary command button visually joined to a chevron toggle that opens an overlay menu of related actions defined by an `items` array. The primary button runs the default action; the joined toggle composes `dropdown-menu` to present the remaining actions. Opt into `updateLabelOnSelect` to have the primary segment mirror the last-chosen menu action (label + icon), turning the control into a "default is the last selection" pattern; the primary `click` then reports that mirrored action as its second argument, so a single handler can run whichever action is active. Use it when one action is the default and related actions belong in an attached menu; for a single action use `Button`, and for a standalone menu use `DropdownMenu`.

- Import: `import SplitButton from '@aziontech/webkit/split-button'`
- Category: action · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use SplitButton when one default action has a few related alternatives; for a list of actions opened from a button use DropdownMenu, and for a toolbar of icon actions use ButtonGroup.
- One default action with a few related alternatives (Save and Save as draft, Deploy and Deploy to staging).
- A "repeat the last choice" control: set `updateLabelOnSelect` so the primary segment mirrors the last action picked.

## Do

- Give every `items` entry a stable `value`; without one the `label` identifies the action, so renaming it changes what handlers receive.
- Handle the default action in `@click` and the menu actions in `@item-click`; both receive `(event, item)`.
- With `updateLabelOnSelect`, read the second argument of `click` (the mirrored item, `null` until one is picked) to run whichever action is active.
- Set `loading` while the action runs: it disables both segments and keeps the menu closed.
- Disable a single action with `disabled: true` on its model entry instead of removing it, so the menu does not shift.

## Don’t

- A single action → use `button`.
- A menu with no default action → use `dropdown-menu`.
- Picking one of a few visible, mutually exclusive options → use `toggle-group`.

## Related

- `button` — the primary segment; `variant` here is limited to `primary`, `secondary` and `outline`.
- `dropdown-menu` — the overlay menu the toggle composes; use it alone when there is no default action.
- `icon-button` — the chevron toggle segment.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible label text on the primary command button. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Azion icon class for the primary button's leading icon. |
| `items` | `SplitButtonItem[]` | `[]` | false | Actions rendered as rows in the attached overlay menu. Same name as ButtonGroup's actions. |
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'outline'` | `'primary'` | false | Visual variant applied to both joined segments. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token; affects height, padding, and typography. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables both segments and prevents the menu from opening. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a spinner on the primary button and takes the disabled status: both segments are disabled and the menu cannot open while it resolves. |
| `updateLabelOnSelect` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, selecting a menu action updates the primary button's label and icon to mirror that action and marks it as selected in the menu. Opt-in; the mirrored action is also reported as the primary `click`'s second argument, so the consumer decides what each segment does. |
| `selectedKey` | `string \| null` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:selectedKey`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: SplitButtonItem \| null)` | Fired by the primary command button on activation. `item` is the action currently mirrored on the primary segment when `updateLabelOnSelect` is on, otherwise `null`. Never fires while `disabled` or `loading`. |
| `item-click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, item: SplitButtonItem)` | Fired when a menu action is selected. `event` is the pointer/keyboard event that activated the option; `item` is the matched `items` entry. The menu cannot open while `disabled` or `loading`, so it never fires in those states. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:selectedKey` | `string \| null` | `null` | `update:selectedKey` | Value (`value`, else `label`) of the action the primary button mirrors when `updateLabelOnSelect` is on, via `defineModel('selectedKey')`. Bind it to read or restore the mirrored action; unbound, the control keeps its own. `null` shows the default `label` and `icon`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`, `loading`
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-loading` mirrors the `loading` prop
- `data-state` on the menu toggle: `open` | `closed` (provided by the composed `DropdownMenu.Trigger`)
- The menu opens below the whole control, its start edge lined up with the primary segment's start (the segments' wrapper is the `dropdown-menu-anchor`); where that would overflow the viewport it is clamped inside it
- When `loading`, the control takes the disabled status: the primary button shows the spinner over the disabled tokens and blocks activation (owned by `Button`), the menu toggle is natively disabled with the disabled tokens, and the composed `DropdownMenu` is disabled so the menu cannot open. No `click` or `item-click` is emitted while loading.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on both segments; the focused segment raises its z-index so the ring is not clipped by its neighbor.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses each segment; `Enter`/`Space` activates the primary button; on the toggle `Enter`/`Space`/`Down` open the menu, arrows navigate items, `Esc` closes and returns focus to the toggle (behavior owned by `DropdownMenu`).
- ARIA: the primary button is a native `button`; the toggle exposes `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` via `DropdownMenu.Trigger` and carries an `aria-label`; the chevron icon is `aria-hidden`; `aria-busy` reflects the loading state. While `loading`, the toggle is a natively disabled button, so the menu cannot be opened by pointer or keyboard and assistive tech perceives the whole control as non-interactive.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px at the large size.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SplitButton from '@aziontech/webkit/split-button'

  const items = [
    { label: 'Update', value: 'update', icon: 'az az-refresh' },
    { label: 'Duplicate', value: 'duplicate', icon: 'az az-copy' },
    { label: 'Delete', value: 'delete', icon: 'az az-trash', disabled: true }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <SplitButton
    variant="primary"
    size="large"
    label="Save"
    icon="az az-check"
    :items="items"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/split-button.md](components/split-button.md).

<!-- components/toggle-group.md -->

# Toggle Group

> ToggleGroup is a connected group of buttons that picks exactly one value out of a small set of related options, with a selection indicator that slides to the active segment. It renders as a `radiogroup` whose segments are `radio` buttons, is driven by an `options` array plus `v-model`, and works uncontrolled through `defaultValue`. It differs from `tabs`, which switches between content panels it owns: a segmented button only holds the chosen value and leaves rendering what that value means to the consumer.

- Import: `import ToggleGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/toggle-group'`
- Category: action · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ToggleGroup (segmented control) to switch a view or mode in place (Table/Chart, 1h/24h), with two to five short segments; it is not a form field. For one choice in a form use RadioGroup; for an on/off setting use Switch; for the theme in app chrome use ThemeSwitcher.
- Switch in place between two to five related modes, views or ranges (a time range, a list/grid view, a filter scope) where exactly one is always active.
- Offer a compact single choice in a toolbar or a card header where a radio list would take too much room.
- Show a choice that is currently unavailable as a disabled segment instead of hiding it; mark it `locked` when it is unavailable because of a plan or a permission.

## Do

- Keep labels to one or two words. When the options do not fit their container they flow onto another row, and a label breaks across lines only when one option alone is wider than the group; a label is never cut off.
- Give every option a unique `value`; values are coerced to strings and used as the list key and the selection identity, so duplicates collide.
- Pass `ariaLabel` whenever no visible label names the group.
- Use `fluid` to make the group fill a narrow container and share its width across segments, instead of styling the width at the call site.
- Bind `v-model` when the selection lives in the parent; use `defaultValue` only to seed an uncontrolled group.

## Don’t

- The choice switches between content panels that belong to the control → use `tabs`.
- The choice is a form field with a label, helper text or validation → use `radio-group` (`variant="card"` when each option needs a description).
- The value is a binary on/off setting → use `switch` (in a horizontal `field` inside a form).
- The user can pick more than one option → use `checkbox` (in a horizontal `field`).
- The control triggers an action instead of holding a value → use `button` or `split-button`.

## Related

- `tabs` — tabs that own their panels; reach for it when each option reveals its own content region.
- `radio-group` — the form-field single choice; `variant="card"` when each option carries a description.
- `theme-switcher` — the system / light / dark choice in app chrome.
- `switch` — a single boolean toggle.
- `button` — a lone action; the segments here hold a value instead of firing one.
- Naming: Radix and shadcn `ToggleGroup` is a group of `aria-pressed` toggles with `type="single" | "multiple"`. This component is the single-select segmented control (Cloudscape and Geist call it a segmented control): one value is always selected and the segments are radios. There is no multiple mode; for several independent toggles use `checkbox`es or `ButtonGroup` toggles.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | ``ToggleGroupOption[]` (`{ label?: string \| number; value?: string \| number; disabled?: boolean; locked?: boolean; icon?: string }`)` | `[]` | false | Segmented choices shown as a mutually exclusive group. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name when no visible group label is associated. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Initial selection when `v-model` is not set. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token, on the same 28 / 32 / 40 rhythm every other control uses. |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Stretches the group to its container and lets the options share that width. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables every option of the group. |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | false | Form field name. Set, a hidden input carries the selected value so a native `form` submits it; `disabled` leaves it out. |
| `showLabels` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows each option's label beside its icon. Set false for icon-only segments: the label stays as the option's accessible name and its hover title. |
| `modelValue` | `TValue \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `TValue \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | Selected option value via `defineModel`. While unbound (`undefined`) the group is uncontrolled: it starts at `defaultValue`, else the first non-disabled option. Emits only when the selection changes to a different value, always as the string-coerced option `value`. |

**Generic.** The component is generic over `TValue extends string` (default `string`), inferred from the bound `v-model`: on a `Ref<'day' | 'week'>`, `update:modelValue` sends `'day' | 'week' | undefined` (the `undefined` of an unbound model), so `v-model` binds the union with no cast. `ToggleGroupOption<TOptionValue = string | number>` types a list against the same union (`ToggleGroupOption<'day' | 'week'>[]`); the `options` prop itself stays `ToggleGroupOption[]`, so a list typed `{ label: string; value: string }[]` still binds. `ToggleGroupOption` and `ToggleGroupSize` are exported by `@aziontech/webkit/toggle-group`.

## States

- Visual states per segment: `default`, `focus-visible`, `selected`, `disabled`.
- Root: `role="radiogroup"`; consumer attributes (`id`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, …) land on it; `data-disabled` when `disabled`; `data-size` mirrors `size` (`small` | `medium` | `large`); `data-fluid` is present only when `fluid` is set.
- Segment: `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`; `data-state="active"` on the selected segment and `"inactive"` on the others; `data-disabled` and the native `disabled` attribute on a disabled option (or every option when the root is `disabled`); a trailing lock icon (`az az-lock`) and `data-locked` on a locked option (see Locked options). Each segment carries a touch-target span that grows its hit area to 44px tall under `pointer-coarse`, never sideways into a neighbour.
- Indicator: an `aria-hidden` span positioned under the selected segment from its measured size and offset; hidden when nothing is selected or the selected segment is not rendered. It re-measures on option, selection and size changes (`ResizeObserver`).
- Option normalization: a missing `label` falls back to `value`, then to `Option <n>`; a missing `value` falls back to `label`, then to the index.
- Test ids: root `toggle-group` (consumer `data-testid` wins), `<testId>__indicator`, `<testId>__option`, `<testId>__option-lock`.
- Reflow: the root is capped at the width of its container (`max-w-full`, `min-w-0`) and wraps (`flex-wrap`): options that do not fit move to another row, the selected-option indicator follows them, and a label wraps inside its option only when that option alone is wider than the group. Heights are minimums (28 / 32 / 40 px for one row), so a wrapped group grows instead of clipping.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` with `focus-visible:outline-none` on each segment.
- Keyboard map: the group is one tab stop (roving `tabindex`): `Tab` lands on the selected segment, or on the first enabled one when nothing is selected, and the next `Tab` leaves the group; `Enter` / `Space` select the focused segment; `ArrowRight` / `ArrowDown` and `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowUp` move the selection to the next / previous enabled segment, wrapping at the ends, and `Home` / `End` to the first / last enabled one (the APG radio group map), and focus moves with it so the newly checked radio is announced.
- ARIA: root `role="radiogroup"` named by `ariaLabel` (`aria-label` is omitted when it is empty) or by a consumer `aria-labelledby` pointing at a visible label; each segment `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`; the indicator and the lock icon are `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Icon-only segments (`showLabels` false): the icon is `aria-hidden="true"` and the option label stays in the segment as visually hidden text, so the radio keeps its accessible name; the same label is the segment's `title`.
- Disabled options use the native `disabled` attribute, so they are skipped by arrow navigation, never take the tab stop and cannot be clicked.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons): selected text uses `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-selected)`, unselected text `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-surface)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the segment color transition and on the indicator slide.
- Touch target: segments fill the group height minus its padding (40px group at `size="large"`); under `pointer-coarse` a touch-target span extends each segment's hit area to 44px tall.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ToggleGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/toggle-group'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const options = [
    { label: 'Overview', value: 'overview' },
    { label: 'Requests', value: 'requests' },
    { label: 'Errors', value: 'errors' },
    { label: 'Latency', value: 'latency' },
    { label: 'Bandwidth', value: 'bandwidth' }
  ]

  const selected = ref('overview')
</script>

<template>
  <ToggleGroup
    v-model="selected"
    :options="options"
    aria-label="Metrics view"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/agent-activity.md -->

# Agent Activity

> Shows what an agent is doing while it works (Cloudscape progressive steps, AI Elements Chain of Thought): the current step with a running indicator (`Searching the docs`, `Reading 3 files`) and, behind a disclosure, the list of every step with its status from the shared status set. It is the display of the short progress updates an agent streams (TanStack AI `activity` parts and `role: 'activity'` messages), filled from plain props so it stays library-neutral. Screen readers hear a step only when it has been the current one for a second, and the outcome once, never every tick.

- Import: `import AgentActivity from '@aziontech/webkit/agent-activity'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- An agent works through several steps before or while it answers, and the reader should see which step it is on (`Searching the docs`, `Reading 3 files`, `Writing the answer`).
- A plan the agent ticks over, step by step, inside a chat message.

## Do

- Title each step `<Verb>ing <what>` in the reader's words, no end punctuation: `Searching the docs`, never a tool identifier.
- Keep one step `running` at a time; later steps stay `pending` until they start.
- When a step fails, mark it `error` and the steps that will no longer run `canceled`.
- Keep the steps collapsed in a chat once the answer arrives; the answer is the main content.
- Key each step by something stable, such as the id of the activity message it comes from.
- Use 3 to 7 steps; merge fine-grained ticks into one step and update its `description` instead.

## Don’t

- Nothing to report but that an answer is coming → `response-loading`.
- The model's free-text thinking trace → `reasoning`.
- A call with side effects, its input and output → `tool-call`; one asking for approval → `tool-approval`.
- A build or deploy run with log lines per step → `log-viewer-steps`.
- Moving through the pages of a form or wizard → `stepper`.

## Related

- `response-loading` — the waiting state before the first step arrives.
- `reasoning` — thinking, not doing.
- `tool-call` — one call in detail; an activity step can summarize it.
- `chat-message` — the bubble the activity sits in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `AgentActivityStep[]` | `[]` | false | The steps of the work, in order: each has a `key`, a `title`, a `status` from the shared status set and an optional `description`. The current step is the first running one, else the first failed one, else the last canceled one of a stopped run, else the last one that is not pending. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state of the step list when uncontrolled; collapsed shows only the current step. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the activity. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Agent activity`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | The step list was expanded or collapsed. Unbound, the state is local and starts from `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- `data-status` on the root mirrors the current step's status; `data-state="open|closed"` when there is more than one step.
- Current step (the one rule): the first `running` step, else the first `error` step, else, when the run is stopped (see Outcomes), the last `canceled` step, else the last step that is not `pending` (between two steps, the one just finished, so the root reads `success` while the next step has not started), else the first step (a plan that has not started). Collapsed shows only it, so a failed run shows the failed step, never a trailing `canceled` one; open shows every step in order, the current one marked `aria-current="step"`. `data-status` mirrors the same step.
- The step list `ol` (id from `useId()`) is always rendered: collapsed it holds only the current step's `li`, open it holds every step.
- The disclosure (`{count} steps`, chevron) appears only with two or more steps.
- Step glyphs: `running` a `Spinner`; `success` `az az-circle-check`; `error` `az az-circle-x`; `canceled` `az az-circle-stop`; `skipped` `az az-circle-minus`; `pending` a CSS ring at the glyph size (`rounded-full border border-dashed border-(--text-muted)`), not an icon. Pending, canceled and skipped titles are muted.
- Outcomes: the run is failed when a step is `error`; stopped when no step is `running`, `pending` or `error` and at least one is `canceled` (the reader or the owner stopped it; the current-step rule then picks the last `canceled` step, so `data-status` is `canceled`); finished when every step is `success` or `skipped`.
- No steps: the root renders no rows and no `data-status`; the polite region stays in the DOM, so the first step announced after an empty mount is heard.
- `loading`, `disabled`, `readonly` and `invalid` do not apply: progress is carried by the `running` step status, and the toggle is the only control.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the toggle.
- Pattern: the toggle and the step list follow the WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure (Show/Hide) pattern; the step list is a static ordered list.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` to the toggle, `Enter` / `Space` expands or collapses the step list. The steps are not focusable.
- ARIA: the root is a `role="group"` named by `ariaLabel`; the steps are an ordered list (`ol`); the current step has `aria-current="step"`; each glyph is `aria-hidden` and a visually hidden status word (`Done`, `Failed`, …) follows each title; the toggle is a `button` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, which always targets the step list `ol` (rendered in both states).
- Announcements: one visually hidden `aria-live="polite"` region, outside the list. It announces a running step's title once it has stayed current for one second (fast ticks are never read), then the outcome once: `Finished {count} steps` when the run becomes finished, `Stopped after {count} steps` when it becomes stopped ({count} is the number of `success` steps in both), or `Failed: {title}` when a step errors. A stopped run is never announced as finished. An outcome is announced only when it changes after mount: an instance mounted with a finished or failed run (a chat history re-render) announces nothing; a step already running at mount is live work and is announced after the same one-second dwell. The one-second timer is cleared on every step change and on unmount (`onScopeDispose`). The list itself is not live.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 on titles and the muted text; every glyph colour (`--success-mark`, `--danger-mark`, `--text-muted`) meets 3:1 and APCA Lc 45 for icons.
- Reduced motion: the spinner and the chevron stop moving; the status words carry the state.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import AgentActivity from '@aziontech/webkit/agent-activity'

  const steps = [
    { key: 'search', title: 'Searching the docs', status: 'success' },
    { key: 'settings', title: 'Reading the cache settings', status: 'success' },
    {
      key: 'read',
      title: 'Reading 3 files',
      status: 'running',
      description: 'cache-settings.md'
    },
    { key: 'write', title: 'Writing the answer', status: 'pending' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <AgentActivity :steps="steps" />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/agent-question.md -->

# Agent Question

> A question the agent asks the reader in the middle of a run, before it can go on (a human-in-the-loop interrupt, Cloudscape follow-up input, the "ask the user" step of coding agents): pick one of a few options, type a short answer, or say yes or no. The card states the question, says why the agent asks, shows the answer control the question needs (`type`: options as radios, a one-line text field, or Yes and No buttons), and offers Submit and, when the run can go on without an answer, Skip. While the answer is sent the controls are inert and Submit shows its loading state; once answered, the controls give way to the answer in text (`Answered: Staging`) so the exchange stays in the thread; a failed send keeps the controls and shows the error line under them. It differs from `tool-approval`, which approves or denies a tool call with consequences: this card collects information the agent needs, and nothing runs on the reader's behalf. It also says "answer in flight" with `status="running"` instead of tool-approval's `loading` boolean, on purpose: the pause it renders already has a lifecycle (TanStack AI's `pending`, `validating` / `submitting`, `error`), and one `status` maps onto it without a second flag that could disagree with it. A block maps the interrupt like this: `pending` → `pending`; `validating`, `staged` and `submitting` → `running`; `error` → `error`, with the first of `errors[]` as `error`; a resolved interrupt → `success`; `cancel()` after Skip → `skipped`; an interrupt the run dropped → `canceled`. It is a card in the conversation, not a dialog: it does not trap focus and does not take initial focus; `focus()` moves focus to its heading when the owner wants to bring the reader to it.

- Import: `import AgentQuestion from '@aziontech/webkit/agent-question'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use AgentQuestion only inside an AI conversation, when the agent pauses a run to ask the reader for information it cannot infer (a TanStack AI generic interrupt, an "ask the user" tool).
- A choice between two to six named options: which environment, which plan, which of two fixes (`type="choice"`).
- A short free-text answer: a name, a domain, a value the agent is missing (`type="text"`).
- A yes-or-no question where both answers let the run go on (`type="confirm"`).

## Do

- Ask one thing per card, as a question that ends with a question mark; put names and values in backticks (code).
- Keep options short and mutually exclusive; give an option a `description` only when the label alone does not say what happens.
- Offer Skip (`skippable`) only when the agent can continue without the answer, and have it say what it assumed.
- Name the submit action after the outcome when it is not a generic answer (`Use this domain`).
- Do not leave a question pending forever: when the run no longer needs it, set `status="canceled"`.
- Offer at most six options; more than that is a search or a form, not a question.

## Don’t

- The agent asks permission to run a tool or command with consequences → `tool-approval`.
- Follow-up prompts the reader may send or ignore, with no paused run → `suggestion-group`.
- A destructive action the reader started in the UI → `confirm-dialog`.
- A form with several fields → `schema-form` in the page, not a chat card.

## Related

- `tool-approval` — approve or deny an agent's tool call; same card language, different decision.
- `suggestion-group` — optional follow-ups that start a new message instead of answering a paused run.
- `chat-message` — the card sits in the assistant message; the assistant goes on in the next one.
- `radio-group`, `input`, `button`, `status-indicator` — the parts the card is built from.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The question the agent asks, ending with a question mark. Backticks render as code. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One or two sentences on why the agent asks or what it does with the answer; backticks render as code. |
| `type` | `'choice' \| 'text' \| 'confirm'` | `'choice'` | false | The answer control: `choice` lists `options` as radios, `text` shows a one-line field, `confirm` shows No and Yes buttons. |
| `options` | `AgentQuestionOption[]` | `[]` | false | The answers of a `choice` question: `{ value, label, description?, disabled? }`. Ignored by the other types. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Short example shown in the empty field of a `text` question. |
| `status` | `'pending' \| 'running' \| 'success' \| 'error' \| 'canceled' \| 'skipped'` | `'pending'` | false | `pending` asks; `running` sends the answer; `success`, `skipped` and `canceled` replace the controls with the outcome; `error` asks again. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Why the last answer was not accepted, shown under the controls. Empty with `status="error"` uses the locale catalog. |
| `skippable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Offers Skip, for a question the agent can go on without. |
| `submitLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the submit button (Yes on a `confirm` question). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Submit`, `Yes`). |
| `declineLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the No button of a `confirm` question. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No`). |
| `skipLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the Skip button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Skip`). |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: Event, value: string)` |  |
| `skip` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Context the reader needs to answer, between the question and the control: a `CodeBlock`, a `KeyValueList`. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./agent-question"`; types `AgentQuestionType`, `AgentQuestionStatus`,
`AgentQuestionOption`. Composed DS components: `radio-group`, `input`, `button`, `status-indicator`;
the title and description render through the shared `ai/lib/markdown-inline` renderer and
`parseInline` from `ai/lib/parse-markdown` (the ones `tool-approval` uses), so backticks render as code
(no HTML). Exposes `focus()`, which moves focus to the heading._

## States

- `data-status` mirrors `status`; `data-type` mirrors `type`.
- `pending`: the control for `type`, then Skip (ghost, when `skippable`) and Submit (primary) at the inline end; Submit is disabled while the answer is empty or blank. A `confirm` question shows No (outline) and Yes (primary) instead of Submit, both submit.
- `running`: controls and buttons inert, Submit (or the pressed confirm button) in its loading state, `aria-busy="true"` on the card.
- `error`: like `pending`, plus the error line under the controls in danger text; the field (or radio group) is `invalid` and described by the line.
- `success`: a `StatusIndicator` (success) reading `Answered: <answer>`, where the answer is the picked option's label (or the raw `modelValue` when it matches no option), the typed text, or the label of the confirm button that was pressed (`submitLabel` / `declineLabel` when set, otherwise the catalog Yes / No). The answer is isolated for bidirectional text: the card passes the answer to `{answer}` already wrapped in U+2068 FIRST STRONG ISOLATE … U+2069 POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE, because `StatusIndicator`'s `label` has no slot for a `bdi`; the catalog strings carry no isolates. A long answer is truncated to one line by `StatusIndicator`; the label text in the DOM and the live region carry the full answer. An empty answer reads `Answered`.
- `skipped`, `canceled`: a `StatusIndicator` (neutral) reading `Skipped` or `Question canceled`.
- A polite live region announces each outcome and the error line.
- The answer is kept when the status goes from `error` back to `pending` (or `running`): the model is never cleared by the card.
- A `choice` question with empty `options` renders no radios; Submit stays disabled and only Skip (when `skippable`) can move the run on. The block must pass options.
- States the card does not have: no `disabled` or `readonly` (`status="running"` makes it inert), no `loading` prop (`status="running"` is the loading state), no `invalid` prop (the control is invalid only while the error line shows), and no empty state.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: radios, the field and the buttons keep their own `focus-visible` rings; the heading shows `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` when `focus()` moves focus to it.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` through the body slot, the control, Skip and Submit; arrow keys move the choice inside the radio group; `Space` on a focused radio selects it and does not submit; `Enter` in the text field or on a focused radio submits the answer through the card's form (the browser's implicit submission, with the same guard as Submit: nothing is sent while the answer is empty or the card is `running`); `Enter` / `Space` activates a button. No focus trap, no initial focus.
- Focus across status changes: while `running`, the pressed button keeps focus (its loading state is `aria-disabled`, not native `disabled`). When a status change disables or removes the control that holds focus (`Enter` in the field, then `running`; the receipt replacing the buttons on `success`, `skipped` or `canceled`), focus moves to the heading, never to the body.
- ARIA: the root is a `div` with `role="group"`, labelled by its `h3` title (`aria-labelledby`) and described by the description (`aria-describedby`). The control and the buttons sit in an unnamed `form` (no accessible name, so no form landmark per card), which gives `Enter` in the field its submit. The `h3` carries `tabindex="-1"`: the target of `focus()`, kept out of the Tab order. The question glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`. The radio group and the text field are labelled by the title; the error line is linked with `aria-describedby` and the control is `aria-invalid` (the radio group on `choice`, the field on `text`; on `confirm`, which has no field, the root group's `aria-describedby` adds the error line and the No and Yes buttons are not marked invalid); Skip and No are `type="button"`, so implicit submission only ever uses Submit; `aria-busy` while `running`; a polite live region announces the outcome and the error; outcomes are text, never color alone.
- Contrast from the theme's documented pairs only; touch targets come from `Button`, `RadioGroup` and `Input` (44 px on coarse pointers).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import AgentQuestion from '@aziontech/webkit/agent-question'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const answer = ref('')
  const status = ref('pending')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <AgentQuestion
      v-model="answer"
      title="Which environment should the new `waf-rules` set go to?"
      description="The rule set exists in both workloads. I can add it to one now and copy it to the other later."
      :options="[
        { value: 'staging', label: 'Staging', description: 'Preview traffic only.' },
        { value: 'production', label: 'Production', description: 'Serves live traffic.' }
      ]"
      :status="status"
      submit-label="Use this environment"
      skippable
      @submit="status = 'success'"
      @skip="status = 'skipped'"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/artifact-canvas.md -->

# Artifact Canvas

> The side panel that shows one generated artifact in full next to the conversation: a SQL file, a configuration, a table of results, a document. A header names it (title, meta, Close), a toolbar pages through its versions with `ResponseBranches` and offers Copy and Download, and the body scrolls on its own. It is the full view behind `ArtifactPreview`'s Open: the preview sits in the message, the canvas beside the thread. The owner places it in a `Resizable` pane, so the reader can widen it, narrow it or collapse it from the keyboard; the canvas fills whatever the pane gives it. Benchmarks: the artifact or canvas panel of chat assistants (a document beside the thread with versions), Cloudscape's split panel (a resizable side region with its own header and close).

- Import: `import ArtifactCanvas from '@aziontech/webkit/artifact-canvas'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- An assistant answer produced something longer than a message can show: a file, a long query, a table, a document the reader will copy or keep.
- The reader asks for changes to that thing and each answer makes a new version to compare with the earlier ones.
- The reader reads the artifact and keeps chatting at the same time.

## Do

- Open the canvas from `ArtifactPreview`'s Open, then call `focus()` so the reader lands on its title; on Close return focus to the Open that opened it.
- Put it in a `Resizable.Pane` with a `min` that keeps the toolbar on one row (about 320 px) and a handle named after the canvas (`Resize the artifact`). The handle is the seam between the thread and the canvas, so the canvas draws no edge rule of its own and never doubles the handle's line.
- Show the newest version when a new one finishes (set `v-model:version` to the last index); while it is generated set `streaming`, which locks the pager and marks the body busy.
- Keep Copy and Download about the version shown; `copyValue` and `downloadHref` change with `version`.
- One canvas at a time. Opening another artifact replaces the content and keeps the pane width.

## Don’t

- A short snippet that fits the message → `CodeBlock` or `ArtifactPreview` inside `ChatMessage`.
- A setting or a form the reader must fill → `Drawer` with the form.
- Help text about the page → `HelpPanel`.
- A narrow screen: show the same canvas in a full-height `Drawer` instead of a side pane (see Responsive).

## Related

- `artifact-preview` — the card in the message; its Open opens this canvas.
- `response-branches` — the version pager the toolbar reuses.
- `resizable` — the split the owner puts the canvas in (pane, handle, collapse).
- `chat-message`, `conversation` — the thread beside the canvas.
- `copy-button` — the Copy control.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | File name or title of the artifact (`top-orders.sql`); names the panel. |
| `meta` | `string` | `''` | false | Facts that help recognize it, after the title: language, size, rows (`SQL · 12 lines`). |
| `type` | `'code' \| 'table' \| 'document'` | `'document'` | false | What the artifact is; picks the icon and `data-type`. The body is always the owner's slot. |
| `versions` | `number` | `1` | false | How many versions exist. With more than one, the toolbar shows the `ResponseBranches` pager. |
| `copyValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Text the Copy control puts on the clipboard, of the version shown. Empty hides Copy. |
| `downloadHref` | `string` | `''` | false | URL of the version shown, for Download (`download` takes the title). Empty hides Download. |
| `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | false | A new version is being generated: the pager locks, the body is `aria-busy` and a polite status says so. |
| `version` | `number` | `0` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:version`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `close` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent)` |  |
| `copy` | `(event: MouseEvent, value: string)` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | { version: number } | The artifact of the version shown: a `CodeBlock`, a `TableRoot`, prose. Scrolls inside. |
| `actions` | — | Extra icon actions in the toolbar, before Copy and Download (Insert into editor, Run). |

## Sub-components

_none_ — monolithic. The split and the handle are `Resizable`'s; the pager is `ResponseBranches`. Exposes `focus()`, which moves focus to the panel title (`tabindex="-1"`) for the owner to call after opening.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:version` | `number` | `0` | `update:version` | Zero-based index of the version shown, clamped by `ResponseBranches`. |

## States

- `data-type` on the root (`code`, `table`, `document`); `data-streaming` while a version is generated.
- One version: no pager; the toolbar keeps Copy and Download, and is not drawn when neither is set and the `actions` slot is empty.
- `streaming`: the pager is disabled, the body has `aria-busy="true"`, and the status reads `Generating a new version`.
- No `copyValue` / `downloadHref`: that control is not drawn.

## Accessibility

- The root is a `section` named by its title (`aria-labelledby`), so it is a region landmark (`top-orders.sql`). The title is an `h2` with `tabindex="-1"`, the target of `focus()`.
- Close is an `IconButton` named `Close <title>`; Copy `Copy <title>`; Download `Download <title>`. The pager is `ResponseBranches` (`Artifact versions`, `Previous version`, `Next version`, a polite `2 of 3`).
- The body is a focusable scroll region named `<title> content`, so keyboard readers can scroll a long artifact; it is `aria-busy` while streaming.
- Keyboard: `Tab` order is title actions, then the toolbar, then the body; `Escape` anywhere inside closes the panel unless an inner control already handled it (`defaultPrevented`). Resizing is `Resizable.Handle`'s (arrow keys, Home, End).
- The streaming status is a polite live region, announced once when generation starts.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ArtifactCanvas from '@aziontech/webkit/artifact-canvas'
  import ArtifactPreview from '@aziontech/webkit/artifact-preview'
  import CodeBlock from '@aziontech/webkit/code-block'
  import Resizable from '@aziontech/webkit/resizable'
  import { nextTick, onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, ref } from 'vue'

  const versions = [
    'SELECT * FROM orders;',
    'SELECT id, customer_id, total\nFROM orders\nORDER BY total DESC;',
    'SELECT id, customer_id, total\nFROM orders\nWHERE created_at > now() - interval 7 day\nORDER BY total DESC\nLIMIT 10;'
  ]
  const version = ref(versions.length - 1)
  const open = ref(true)
  const width = ref(420)
  const height = ref(240)
  const narrow = ref(false)
  let narrowQuery = null
  const onNarrowChange = () => {
    narrow.value = !!narrowQuery?.matches
  }
  onMounted(() => {
    narrowQuery = window.matchMedia?.('(max-width: 639px)') ?? null
    onNarrowChange()
    narrowQuery?.addEventListener('change', onNarrowChange)
  })
  onBeforeUnmount(() => narrowQuery?.removeEventListener('change', onNarrowChange))
  const canvasEl = ref(null)
  const openerEl = ref(null)

  const show = async () => {
    open.value = true
    await nextTick()
    canvasEl.value?.focus()
  }
  const hide = async () => {
    open.value = false
    await nextTick()
    openerEl.value?.querySelector('button')?.focus()
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div
    class="w-full rounded-(--shape-card) border border-(--border-default)"
    :class="narrow ? 'h-(--container-md)' : 'h-(--container-xs)'"
  >
    <Resizable
      :orientation="narrow ? 'vertical' : 'horizontal'"
      class="h-full"
      aria-label="Conversation and artifact"
    >
      <Resizable.Pane>
        <div
          ref="openerEl"
          class="flex h-full flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm) overflow-auto p-(--spacing-md)"
        >
          <p class="m-0 text-body-lg text-(--text-default)">
            Here are the ten biggest orders of the last seven days.
          </p>
          <ArtifactPreview
            title="top-orders.sql"
            meta="SQL"
            icon="az az-code"
            openable
            @open="show"
          />
        </div>
      </Resizable.Pane>
      <Resizable.Handle
        v-if="open"
        aria-label="Resize the artifact"
      />
      <Resizable.Pane
        v-if="open"
        :basis="narrow ? height : width"
        :min="narrow ? 160 : 300"
        :max="narrow ? 360 : 720"
        @update:basis="(value) => (narrow ? (height = value) : (width = value))"
      >
        <ArtifactCanvas
          ref="canvasEl"
          v-model:version="version"
          title="top-orders.sql"
          :meta="`SQL · ${versions[version].split('\n').length} lines`"
          type="code"
          :versions="versions.length"
          :copy-value="versions[version]"
          @close="hide"
        >
          <CodeBlock
            :tabs="[{ label: 'SQL', value: 'sql', code: versions[version], language: 'sql' }]"
            :copyable="false"
            :bordered="false"
          />
        </ArtifactCanvas>
      </Resizable.Pane>
    </Resizable>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Artifact Preview

> A card for something the assistant generated — a file, a code snippet, a table, a configuration (Cloudscape artifact previews, AI Elements Artifact). The header names it (title, description, metadata such as size or format, a file-type icon) and carries its actions: Copy (when `copyValue` is set), Download (when `downloadHref` is set) and Open (when `openable`, emitting `open` so the owner shows the full artifact in a side panel — Cloudscape's canvas preview). The body holds a short inline preview (Cloudscape's inline preview): the first lines of code, the first rows of a table.

- Import: `import ArtifactPreview from '@aziontech/webkit/artifact-preview'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The assistant produced an artifact the reader may copy, download or open: a rules file, a CSV export, a command, a generated function.

## Do

- Stack artifacts below the message text, one card each; do not nest them in the bubble.
- Keep artifact actions in the card and message actions in `ChatMessage.Actions`.
- Express sizes in KB, MB or GB in `meta`.
- Long or editable content opens (canvas); the inline body stays a preview.

## Don’t

- Short code inside the prose of a response → fenced code in `StreamingResponse` (rendered as `CodeBlock`).
- A resource that already exists in the product → link to its page; this card is for generated content.
- Uploads the reader attached → `file-dropzone` items or chips in `PromptInput`'s attachments.

## Related

- `code-block` — the usual inline preview body.
- `drawer` — where an `open` artifact is shown in full.
- `chat-message` — artifacts stack under the response, not inside its bubble.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | File name or title of what was generated (`cache-rules.json`). |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One line on what it is or does. |
| `meta` | `string` | `''` | false | Facts that help recognize it: size, rows, language (`2.4 KB · JSON`). |
| `icon` | `string` | `'az az-file'` | false | Icon class for the file type. |
| `copyValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Text the Copy control puts on the clipboard. Empty hides Copy. |
| `downloadHref` | `string` | `''` | false | URL of the file for the Download control. Empty hides Download. |
| `openable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows Open, which emits `open` so the owner shows the full artifact in a side panel or page (a canvas preview). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |
| `copy` | `(event: MouseEvent, value: string)` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The inline preview; scrolls inside a 20 rem body. |
| `actions` | — | Extra icon actions, placed before Copy and Download. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./artifact-preview"`. Composed DS components: `button` (Open), `copy-button`,
`icon-button` (Download)._

## States

- `data-openable`; body rendered only when the default slot is used.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: controls carry their own rings; the scrollable body is focusable with an inset ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` through the header actions, then into the body.
- ARIA: `<article aria-labelledby>` its `h3` title; Copy, Download and Open are named with the title (`Copy cache-rules.json`); the icon tile is `aria-hidden`; the visible `Open` text is contained in its accessible name.

## Examples

### Default

```vue

  import CodeBlock from '@aziontech/webkit/code-block'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

    {
      cache_by_query_string: 'allowlist',
      query_string_fields: ['page', 'lang'],
      browser_cache_ttl: 3600,
      edge_cache_ttl: 86400
    },
    null,
    2
  )
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">

      meta="1 KB · JSON"
      icon="az az-code"
      :copy-value="rules"
      openable
      @open="opened = true"
    >
      <CodeBlock
        :tabs="[{ label: 'JSON', value: 'json', code: rules, language: 'json' }]"
        :show-line-numbers="false"
        :copyable="false"
        :bordered="false"
      />
    </ArtifactPreview>
    <p
      v-if="opened"
      class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
    >
      The full file opens in a side panel here.
    </p>
  </div>
```

<!-- components/chat-message.md -->

# Chat Message

> One message in a generative AI conversation (Cloudscape's chat bubble, AI Elements' Message): the content and — once the response is complete — the action row a reader uses on it (copy, the a Feedback menu with good / bad response, read aloud, share, try again, branch in new chat, the sources), and on the reader's own prompt Copy and Edit. It owns the message lifecycle: `pending` (waiting for the first token: the loading text), `streaming` (content arriving, busy, no actions), `success` (actions shown; announced once to screen readers through the `Conversation`) and `error` (an error line with Try again). Assistant messages are plain text across the reading column at the prose reading size (`.text-body-prose-md`, 16 px on 26 px lines): no avatar, name, time or bubble. User messages are a filled bubble at the inline end, at most 70 % wide; system messages a muted centered line. A user message opens for editing (`v-model:editing`) and Send emits `edit` with the new text for the app's `setMessages` and `sendMessage`. Author and time live in the accessible name (the time also shows on hover over the user's bubble). Alignment comes from the enclosing `Conversation`.

- Import: `import ChatMessageRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/chat-message-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import ChatMessage from '@aziontech/webkit/chat-message'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Every turn of a chat with the generative AI assistant: the person's prompt, the assistant's response, a system note ("Conversation restarted").
- A response that must show its lifecycle (loading, streaming, failure) and its actions.

## Do

- Pass `status` from your request: `pending` until the first token, `streaming` while tokens arrive, then `success` or `error`.
- Turn on the built-in actions with props instead of composing buttons: `copyable`, `show-feedback`, `show-read-aloud`, `shareable`, `retryable`, `branchable` on a response; `copyable`, `editable` on a prompt. The row keeps one order and moves Good response, Bad response and Try again into More when it is narrow.
- Put the `Sources` pill in `#trailing` (it stays on the same line) and a `ResponseBranches` pager in `#leading` once a response or prompt has versions.
- Raise a toast after a rating, and open `FeedbackReasonDialog` after Bad response; the row itself shows no confirmation text.
- Use `grouped` for a second message by the same author so stacked messages read as one turn.
- Never put the feedback thumbs on non-AI content.

## Don’t

- A generated block outside a conversation (a summary on a page) → `StreamingResponse` alone.
- A notification or toast about the product → `alert` / `toast`.
- A comment thread between people → not this component; it carries AI semantics (feedback thumbs, regenerate).

## Related

- `conversation` — the log that holds messages, sets alignment and announces finished ones.
- `streaming-response` — the safe Markdown renderer for assistant content.
- `reasoning`, `sources`, `tool-call`, `artifact-preview` — parts that stack inside an assistant message.
- `copy-button`, `icon-button` — the actions composed into `ChatMessage.Actions`.
- `response-loading` — what `pending` renders.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | `'user' \| 'assistant' \| 'system'` | `'assistant'` | false | Who wrote the message: the person (`user`), the generative AI assistant, or the product (`system`). |
| `author` | `string` | `''` | false | Author name read in the message's accessible name; it is not shown. Empty uses the locale catalog (`You`, `AI assistant`, `System`). |
| `timestamp` | `string` | `''` | false | Time the message was sent, already formatted for display (`10:42`). Added to the accessible name and shown on hover over the user's bubble. |
| `status` | `'pending' \| 'streaming' \| 'success' \| 'error'` | `'success'` | false | Lifecycle: `pending` shows the loading text, `streaming` marks the content busy, `success` shows the actions, `error` shows the error line with Try again. |
| `grouped` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Follows a message by the same author: tightens the gap above it so stacked messages read as one turn. |
| `errorMessage` | `string` | `''` | false | Error text shown while `status` is `error`. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Loading text shown while `status` is `pending`. Empty uses `ResponseLoading`'s own (`Generating a response`). |
| `editing` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:editing`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retry` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |
| `edit` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, text: string)` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The content: text, `StreamingResponse`, `Reasoning`, `Sources`, artifacts. Not rendered while `pending`. |
| `actions` | — | The action row, usually `ChatMessage.Actions`; shown only when `status` is `success`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/chat-message-actions`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chat-message-feedback`

## Sub-components

Compound API through `index.ts` (`ChatMessage.Actions`, `ChatMessage.Feedback`); standalone entries
`chat-message-root`, `chat-message-actions`, `chat-message-feedback`. The root provides
`{ from, status, contentText }` (`injection-key.ts`; `contentText()` reads the `StreamingResponse` text, `lib/content-text.ts`); `useChatMessageContext()` throws outside a `ChatMessage`.

- `chat-message-actions/chat-message-actions.vue` — `role="group"` row of actions on one line (it never wraps); renders nothing unless `status` is `success`.
  - Props: `ariaLabel?: string` (default `''` — empty uses `Message actions`); `copyable?: boolean` (default `false` — shows Copy, a `CopyButton`); `copyText?: string` (default `''` — what Copy copies; empty copies `contentText()`); `editable?: boolean` (default `false` — shows Edit on a user message, which opens the root's editor); `showFeedback?: boolean` (default `false` — shows Feedback, a `ChatMessage.Feedback` bound to `v-model:feedback`); `showReadAloud?: boolean` (default `false` — shows Read aloud); `readAloudText?: string` (default `''` — the text Read aloud speaks; empty reads `contentText()`); `shareable?: boolean` (default `false` — shows Share); `retryable?: boolean` (default `false` — shows Try again); `branchable?: boolean` (default `false` — adds Branch in new chat to More); `disabled?: boolean` (default `false` — locks Edit, Try again and Branch in new chat).
  - v-model: `v-model:feedback` — `'up' | 'down' | null` through `defineModel('feedback')` (default `null`; emits `update:feedback`). Choosing the chosen item again clears it, in Feedback and in More.
  - Events: `share` — `(event: MouseEvent)`, Share pressed; `retry` — `(event: MouseEvent | KeyboardEvent)`, Try again pressed or chosen in More; `branch` — `(event: MouseEvent | KeyboardEvent)`, Branch in new chat chosen.
  - Slots: `leading` — before Copy, a `ResponseBranches` pager; `default` — app actions after the built-in ones; `trailing` — the `Sources` pill, at the end of the same line (`__trailing`, which may shrink and clips past its end rather than widen the row; it keeps 4 px around the pill for its focus ring).
  - Test ids: `__copy`, `__edit`, `__feedback`, `__read-aloud`, `__share`, `__retry`, `__more`, `__trailing`.
  - Read aloud (private part `parts/chat-message-read-aloud.vue`, test id `chat-message-actions__read-aloud`): a 40 px ghost `IconButton` that speaks the text with `speechSynthesis` in the active locale; while speaking it is `Stop reading` (`data-speaking`). Pressing it again, another message's Read aloud or unmounting stops it. Rendered after mount, only where the browser has speech synthesis.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `chat-message-actions`.
- `chat-message-feedback/chat-message-feedback.vue` — one medium ghost `IconButton` named `Feedback` (`__trigger`, a thumbs-up glyph) that opens a `DropdownMenu` (side `bottom`, align `start`) with two items: Good respo…
  - Props: `loading?: boolean` (default `false`).
  - v-model: `'up' | 'down' | null` through `defineModel` (default `null`; emits `update:modelValue`).
  - `data-testid` fallback: `chat-message-feedback`.

The context also carries `editing` and `edit()`, which Edit calls to open a user message.

Exported types: `ChatMessageFrom`, `ChatMessageStatus`, `ChatMessageFeedbackValue`. Composed DS
components: `button`, `response-loading`, `textarea`, `icon-button`, `copy-button`, `tooltip`,
`dropdown-menu`.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:editing` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:editing` | A user message is open for editing. Edit in `ChatMessage.Actions` sets it; Cancel, `Escape` and Send clear it. Ignored on other messages. |

## States

- `data-from` (`user` | `assistant` | `system`), `data-status` (mirrors `status`), `data-alignment` (from the conversation), `data-grouped`.
- A visually hidden line (`__author`, dropped when `grouped`) reads the accessible name; the user bubble has the time as `title`, wrapped in first-strong isolate marks (U+2068 … U+2069) so `03:02 PM` keeps its order inside a right-to-left page.
- `aria-busy="true"` while `pending` or `streaming`.
- `pending`: `ResponseLoading` (inline, no delay — the owner decides when a message exists) in place of the content.
- `error`: the content (whatever streamed) stays; an error line with a danger glyph and a Try again `Button` follows.
- `success`: the `actions` slot renders (`__actions`, `data-from`).
- Editing (`v-model:editing` on a user message): the column takes the full width (`data-editing`) and the bubble becomes `__editor` — a filled `--shape-card` panel holding an auto-growing `Textarea` (`__field`, 1 to 12 rows, `Edit your message`) with Cancel (`__cancel`) and Send (`__send`, disabled while the text is empty). The actions are hidden meanwhile; closing returns focus to the control that opened it.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the composed controls carry their own `focus-visible` rings.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` through links in the content, then the actions in order; Enter / Space activate; Feedback and More open their menus with Enter, Space or the arrow keys (arrows move, Enter chooses, `Esc` closes and returns focus to the button). In the editor, `Escape` cancels and `Ctrl`/`Cmd` + `Enter` sends.
- The user message's actions are transparent, never hidden from the tab order: focusing one shows the row.
- ARIA: `<article aria-label="<author> at <time>">` so each message has a unique name (Cloudscape), repeated in a visually hidden line at its start for browse mode; `aria-busy` while loading or streaming; actions are a `role="group"` named `Message actions`; Feedback is a menu button (`aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`) whose chosen item is `aria-checked`, the feedback status is a visually hidden `role="status"`; the editor field is named `Edit your message`.
- Announcement: when an assistant or system message turns `success` or `error` (or mounts finished after the conversation is ready), its text is read once through the `Conversation` live region.
- Never rely on alignment alone: every message names its author in its accessible name and hidden line (or is `grouped` after one that does).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 on the muted time and system text.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ChatMessageRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/chat-message-root'
  import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--spacing-xl)">
    <ChatMessageRoot
      from="user"
      author="Jane Doe"
      timestamp="10:41"
    >
      How do I purge the cache of one URL?
    </ChatMessageRoot>
    <ChatMessageRoot timestamp="10:41">
      <StreamingResponse
        content="Open **Real-Time Purge**, choose *URL* as the purge type and paste the address. The purge reaches every data center in a few seconds."
      />
    </ChatMessageRoot>
  </div>
</template>
```
