# Citation

> An inline reference in generated text: a small rounded chip with the mark of the source's site (its favicon, its icon, or its first letter on a colour of its own) and the site's name (`Azion`, else the host of `href` without `www.`), and `+N` when one marker cites several sources (`[1][2]`, `[1, 2]`). Hovering, focusing or pressing the chip opens one card that stacks every cited source. `StreamingResponse` renders it for every run of `[n]` markers.

- Import: `import Citation from '@aziontech/webkit/citation'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A statement in a generated response that comes from one or more specific sources.

## Do

- Number in order of first use: [1], [2], [3]; the numbers stay in the accessible name.
- Give each web source a `site` name (`Azion`, `GitHub`) and, when you have one, its favicon as `image`; a bare host reads as a URL.
- Give each source its `publisher` and `publishedAt` when you have them.

## Don’t

- A link the reader is meant to follow as part of the prose → a normal link.
- Footnotes in documentation → `doc-prose` conventions.

## Related

- `sources` — the pill and panel that list every source of the response.
- `streaming-response` — renders citations from `[n]` in Markdown.
- `hover-card` — the card a chip opens.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `indexes` | `number[]` | `—` | true | 1-based numbers of the sources this reference cites, in order: `[1]` gives `[1]`, `[1][3]` and `[1, 3]` give `[1, 3]`. |
| `sources` | `SourcesItem[]` | `[]` | false | The sources of the response, in citation order; `indexes` point into it. A number with no source renders as a plain numbered note. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./citation"`. Composed DS components: `hover-card`, and the `sources` private
parts `sources/parts/sources-mark.vue` (the round mark) and `sources/parts/sources-item.vue` (one
source block, shared with the `Sources` panel)._

## States

- A chip is a `button` that opens the card: after 300 ms of hover or focus, at once on a press; a mouse press keeps it open, a touch or keyboard press toggles it. `Escape`, a press outside or moving the pointer away closes it.
- `data-state="open|closed"` on the chip; `data-slot="citation"` on the root, so `ChatMessage`'s Read aloud skips it.
- The chip text is the first source's site name (else its host, else its title), cut with an ellipsis at `max-w-48`; `+N` counts the other sources.
- The card stacks every cited source in an `<ol>`, dividers between items only. Each item follows the `Sources` menu row: the 24 px mark at the inline start; the title (a link when `href` is safe, external URLs in a new tab), two lines; `site · publisher · date` (`publishedAt` as a medium date in the reader's locale; parts it lacks are left out). No hover fill, no underline, no `description`, no pager.
- No resolvable source: a `role="note"` chip with the numbers and no card.
- The mark is the source's `image` (favicon), else its `icon`, else its first letter on one of seven chart series colours picked by a stable hash of the host, so neighbouring sites rarely share a colour. A favicon that fails to load falls back to the letter.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the chip and the card links show `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the chip and opens the card after the delay; `Enter` / `Space` toggles it; `Tab` from an open chip moves into the card and through every source link in order; `Escape` closes it and returns focus to the chip.
- ARIA: the chip is named with the site first so the name holds the visible text (WCAG 2.5.3): `Source 1, Azion: Real-Time Purge`, `Azion +2, sources 1, 2, 3`, or `Source 1: <title>` without a site; it carries `aria-expanded` and, while open, `aria-controls` and `aria-describedby` to the card. The marks are `aria-hidden`; the card is an `<ol>`.
- Touch target: inline text reference; exempt from the 24 px minimum as inline text (WCAG 2.5.8 exception).
- Unsafe `href` (`javascript:`, `data:`, any non-web scheme, `//host`) or `image`: the title is plain text, the mark falls back to the icon or letter.
- Contrast: the letter is `--text-default` on a 30% tint, well above Lc 60; the series ring is a solid mark (Lc 30).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Citation from '@aziontech/webkit/citation'

  const sources = [
    {
      title: 'Real-Time Purge',
      href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/',
      description: 'Removes a cached object from every data center in a few seconds.',
      site: 'Azion',
      icon: 'az az-azion',
      publisher: 'Azion Technologies',
      publishedAt: '2026-03-02'
    },
    {
      title: 'HTTP Caching (RFC 9111)',
      href: 'https://www.w3.org/Protocols/',
      description: 'How caches store responses and when they must ask the origin again.',
      site: 'W3C',
      publisher: 'World Wide Web Consortium',
      publishedAt: '2022-06-01'
    },
    {
      title: 'aziontech/azion: the Azion command line',
      href: 'https://github.com/aziontech/azion',
      description: 'Purge URLs, wildcards and cache keys from a terminal.',
      site: 'GitHub',
      icon: 'az az-github',
      publisher: 'aziontech'
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <p class="max-w-(--container-md) text-body-lg text-(--text-default)">
    A purge reaches every data center in a few seconds
    <Citation
      :indexes="[1]"
      :sources="sources"
    />, and the next request fetches the object from the origin again
    <Citation
      :indexes="[2, 3]"
      :sources="sources"
    />.
  </p>
</template>
```

<!-- components/conversation.md -->

# Conversation

> The scrolling message log of a generative AI chat. It holds the thread (`ChatMessage` items, then whatever follows the last response: suggestions, an approval card), keeps the newest message in view while the reader is at the end, and stops following the moment they scroll up to read or copy an older message — a "Scroll to the latest message" button brings them back. It is a `role="log"` whose own live behavior is off, so streamed tokens are never read one by one; instead each `ChatMessage` that finishes (or fails) hands its text to the conversation's polite live region, once. With `moreMessages`, a Load earlier messages button opens the thread and the log also emits `load-more` as the reader scrolls near the top; prepended messages never move what the reader sees. It also sets where messages sit for the whole thread (`layout`): `split` for a full chat page, `start` for a dense side panel or drawer (Cloudscape's rule for embedded surfaces). The thread is a centred reading column 752 px wide (`--container-2xl`, closest to ChatGPT's 48 rem) inside a 16 px gutter, with one even gap between messages: 36 px from `sm`, 28 px on a phone. The `composer` slot floats the composer over the bottom of the column: the thread scrolls under it behind a fade and is padded by its height; the Scroll to latest button floats just above it.

- Import: `import Conversation from '@aziontech/webkit/conversation'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Any surface where a person and the generative AI assistant exchange messages: the assistant page, the assistant drawer, an in-flow helper.
- A transcript that grows while the reader watches it (streaming responses, tool calls appearing).

## Do

- Put the prompt input in the `composer` slot; only the log scrolls, and the thread scrolls under the composer.
- Never auto-scroll while the reader is reading an older message: the component already stops following when they scroll up.
- Use `layout="start"` in drawers and side panels, `split` on a full page.
- Keep one conversation per surface; a second thread is a second page or a history list.
- Prepend older messages in the same update that sets `loadingMore` back to `false`.

## Don’t

- A one-shot generated block on a page (a summary card, an explanation beside a chart) → render `StreamingResponse` in place.
- A log of system events with timestamps and filtering → use `log-viewer`.
- A list of past conversations → a `table` or `item` list; this is one thread.
- A lost or resuming connection (`Reconnecting…`) → the app's state, not the log's: an `Alert` or `StatusIndicator` above the prompt input.

## Related

- `chat-message` — the item the log holds; announces itself through this component.
- `prompt-input` — the composer, floated over the bottom of the log through the `composer` slot (outside the log; only the log scrolls).
- `suggestion-group` — follow-up questions after the last response, or support prompts in the empty state.
- `empty-state` — what the panel shows before the first message; render it in the default slot (the thread column is at least the log's height, so `my-auto` centres it) so the composer in `composer` never remounts when the first message is sent.
- `log-viewer` — machine logs, not conversations.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the message log. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Conversation`). |
| `layout` | `'split' \| 'start'` | `'split'` | false | `split` puts the user's messages at the inline end (a full chat page); `start` keeps every message at the inline start (a side panel or drawer). |
| `moreMessages` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Older messages exist above the first one. A Load earlier messages button opens the thread and the log emits `load-more` as the reader scrolls near the top. |
| `loadingMore` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The older messages are loading; the button at the top of the thread shows its spinner and holds further `load-more` requests. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `load-more` | `(event: Event)` | The button's click, or the top row came within 200 px of the viewport (`new Event('load-more')`). Not repeated while `loadingMore`, nor until older messages were prepended (the first message changed); after a failed load only the button asks again. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The thread: `ChatMessage` items in order, oldest first, plus anything that follows the last response (suggestions, an approval card), or the empty state before the first message. |
| `composer` | — | The composer floating over the bottom of the thread, in the reading column: `PromptInput`, with any status, alert or queue above it. Rendered outside the log, after it in the reading order. |

## Sub-components

_None — a single root. Messages reach it through `provide`/`inject` (`injection-key.ts`): the
conversation provides its layout (context member `alignment`), a `ready` flag (true after mount, so only messages added later are
announced) and `announce(author, text)`._

Exports: `"./conversation": "./src/components/ai/conversation/conversation.vue"`. Exported type:
`ConversationLayout = 'split' | 'start'`. Composed DS components: `icon-button` (scroll to latest),
`button` (load earlier messages: ghost, small, `az-arrow-up`, centered first row; its `loading` state).

Announcing: a message announces on mount only while the context's `ready` is true. `ready` is false
from a request (or `loadingMore`) until the render that ends the load, so prepended messages are
never read as new.

## States

- `data-pinned` on the root while the log follows the newest message; absent once the reader scrolled up (the Scroll to latest button shows). Only the reader's own scrolling unpins it (wheel, touch, pointer on the scrollbar, keys): a scroll the browser causes — a host moving the log in the DOM, a drawer opening — is corrected back to the end while pinned.
- `data-layout` mirrors `layout`; each message carries it as `data-alignment`.
- With the `composer` slot, the root sets `--conversation-composer-height` (the measured height of the composer area, its fade included); the thread's bottom padding and the Scroll to latest button's offset read it. `--conversation-composer-fade` is the colour the fade blends into; the root does not set it and falls back to `var(--bg-canvas)`, so a host on another surface sets it on any ancestor (a panel or a drawer body: `class="[--conversation-composer-fade:var(--bg-surface)]"`) and the fade matches that surface.
- `data-loading-more` on the root and `aria-busy` on the log while `loadingMore`; the button is in its `loading` state.
- With `moreMessages` or `loadingMore` the first row (`__older`, observed by an `IntersectionObserver`) holds the button (`__load-more`).
- Scroll anchoring: while not pinned, the first message in view (or the button, while it has focus) is the anchor; growth above it is offset in the scroll position. Native `overflow-anchor` is off.
- Load failure: `loadingMore` returns to `false` with nothing prepended; the idle button is the retry path, nothing is announced, the error is the app's (an `Alert`).
- No `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `empty` or `error` state of its own.
- No `data-state` — nothing opens or closes.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the log is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) so keyboard users can scroll it; it shows an inset `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the log, arrows / Page Up / Page Down scroll it; `Tab` continues into the messages' controls (the Load earlier messages button first); the Scroll to latest button is a normal button.
- Focus: the button stays focusable while loading (`aria-disabled`); if it leaves while focused, the log takes focus.
- ARIA: `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"` (streaming chunks are not read) and `aria-label`; a separate visually hidden `aria-live="polite"` `aria-atomic="true"` region receives `"<author>: <text>"` when an assistant or system message completes or fails. User messages are not announced (the reader just typed them). It also says `Loading earlier messages`, then `Earlier messages loaded` once older messages were prepended.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons) on both buttons, idle and loading (`Button`'s own colors).
- Reduced motion: smooth scrolling is replaced by a jump.
- Touch target: the scroll button is a large `IconButton` (40 px, 44 px on coarse pointers through `IconButton`).
- Reading order: the composer area follows the log in the DOM, so `Tab` leaves the log's last control and reaches the composer.

## Examples

# Conversation History

> The chat list of an assistant, in a side panel or a `Drawer` on phones: rows grouped by last activity (Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 days, Previous 30 days, Older) or by status (Working, Settled), the open one current, pinned chats on top, an optional Projects section of folders that expand in place, and on top a New chat row, a search field or a toolbar whose Search button opens the app's palette. A row is a title or a rich row (tag, description, age, status); per-row actions (pin, rename, share, lock, move, archive, delete) sit on hover and in a `DropdownMenu`. Choosing a row sets `v-model` to its id.

- Import: `import ConversationHistory from '@aziontech/webkit/conversation-history'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- An assistant keeps past conversations and the person returns to one.
- The left rail or a drawer of a chat page.

## Do

- Title each conversation from its first prompt, short.
- Put it beside the conversation on wide screens and in a start-side `Drawer` on phones; close the drawer from `update:modelValue` and `create`.
- Fix `now` on the app's `ConfigProvider` (or here) so groups and ages match on the server and the client.
- The component never changes `items`: apply each action event to the data (flip `pinned`, `archived`, `locked`, set `projectId`, the new `title`).
- Never delete on the first tap: open a `ConfirmDialog` from `remove` / `project-remove`, or remove at once and offer Undo.
- With `showToolbar`, open the app's `Command` palette from `search-open`; a mounted `Command` claims ⌘K, so the Search button does not bind it twice.

## Don’t

- Messages of the open conversation → `Conversation`.
- Navigation between product areas → `Sidebar` or `NavigationMenu`.
- A searchable table of records → `TableRoot`.

## Related

- `conversation` — shows the conversation the history selects.
- `drawer` — holds the history on narrow screens.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `ConversationHistoryItem[]` | `[]` | false | Conversations, any order; sorted newest first in their group or project. |
| `projects` | `ConversationHistoryProject[]` | `[]` | false | Projects shown in a Projects section above Recents; empty keeps the plain groups. |
| `now` | `string \| number \| Date` | `undefined` | false | Reference time for groups and ages. Empty uses the nearest ConfigProvider now, then the current time. |
| `removable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Lets each row be deleted (emits `remove`): a Delete button, or Delete in the row menu when `itemActions` is set. |
| `creatable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows New chat (a row, or a toolbar button with `showToolbar`) that emits `create`. |
| `projectCreatable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows New project (in the Projects header, or the toolbar) that emits `project-create`. |
| `searchable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a search field that hides conversations whose title does not contain the typed text. |
| `showToolbar` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a top toolbar: a Search button that emits `search-open`, then New project and New chat as icon buttons. |
| `itemActions` | `('pin' \| 'rename' \| 'share' \| 'lock' \| 'move' \| 'archive')[]` | `[]` | false | Row actions: a Pin button and a More menu on each row; `move` needs `projects`. |
| `projectActions` | `('pin' \| 'settings' \| 'remove' \| 'chat-create')[]` | `[]` | false | Project row actions: a More menu (pin, settings, remove) and a New chat button (`chat-create`). |
| `groupBy` | `'date' \| 'status'` | `'date'` | false | Groups chats outside projects by last activity, or into Working (`status: 'running'`) and Settled (the rest and archived chats). |
| `showTime` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows each chat's age (`10m`, `15h`, `3d`) at the end of its row. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows placeholder rows while the history loads. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Conversation history`). |
| `modelValue` | `string \| null` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `openKeys` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:openKeys`). |
| `projectsOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:projectsOpen`). |
| `projectSort` | `ConversationHistoryProjectSort` | `'recent'` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:projectSort`). |
| `openSectionKeys` | `string[]` | `—` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:openSectionKeys`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remove` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, id: string)` |  |
| `create` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |
| `project-create` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |
| `search-open` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent)` |  |
| `item-pin` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, item: ConversationHistoryItem)` |  |
| `item-rename` | `(event: KeyboardEvent \| FocusEvent, payload: { item; title: string })` |  |
| `item-share` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, item: ConversationHistoryItem)` |  |
| `item-lock` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, item: ConversationHistoryItem)` |  |
| `item-move` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, payload: { item; project })` |  |
| `item-archive` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, item: ConversationHistoryItem)` |  |
| `project-pin` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, project: ConversationHistoryProject)` |  |
| `project-settings-open` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, project: ConversationHistoryProject)` |  |
| `project-remove` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, project: ConversationHistoryProject)` |  |
| `project-chat-create` | `(event: MouseEvent, project: ConversationHistoryProject)` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` | { item: ConversationHistoryItem } | Replaces a chat row's tag, title and description; the row keeps its button and actions. |
| `item-meta` | { item: ConversationHistoryItem } | Replaces the end of a chat row (age, lock, status). |
| `item-actions` | { item: ConversationHistoryItem } | Replaces the row actions (Pin, More, Delete) with the app's own controls, outside the row button; they show like the built-in actions. The row content keeps its place while they show; set `--conversation-history-item-actions-width` on the list to make the row end that wide while they show (default: the row's own end padding, so nothing moves). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string \| null` | `null` | `update:modelValue` | Id of the open conversation; its row is `aria-current="page"`. |
| `v-model:openKeys` | `string[]` | `[]` | `update:openKeys` | Ids of the expanded projects. |
| `v-model:projectsOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | `update:projectsOpen` | Whether the Projects section is expanded. |
| `v-model:projectSort` | `'recent' \| 'name'` (`ConversationHistoryProjectSort`) | `'recent'` | `update:projectSort` | Project order from the Organize menu: by newest chat (empty projects last) or by name; pinned first. |
| `v-model:openSectionKeys` | `string[]` | `['recents', 'working']` | `update:openSectionKeys` | Expanded sections, of `recents`, `working`, `settled` (`ConversationHistorySection`). |

## States

- Order from the top: toolbar, New chat row and search, Pinned, Projects, then Recents (by date) or Working and Settled (by status). A group renders only with items; inside a group, newest first. Pinned (`pinned`, not `archived`) leaves its project or group. By date, archived chats show nowhere.
- Sections: Projects, Recents (shown with Projects), Working and Settled are collapsible headers (`data-state="open|closed"`, chevron down when open, toward the inline end when closed); Working and Settled show their count. A collapsed section mounts no rows. Pinned and the date groups are labels.
- Projects: one folder row per project (`az-folder`, `az-folder-open` expanded) whose chats indent under it, or `No chats in this project yet.`; a `projectId` matching no project stays outside. Organize (two or more projects) opens a `DropdownMenu` with Sort by, Recent activity and Name.
- Search: matching projects and sections show expanded with only their matches; the models do not change.
- Rows: the `SidebarMenuItem` menu row, 32 px (44 px on coarse pointers), fill inset 1 px top and bottom (`border-y border-transparent bg-clip-padding`, `forced-colors:border-y-0`) for a 2 px gap between filled rows, no list gap. A row with a `description` is 56 px: title over the description (`text-body-xs`, muted, one line), `var(--spacing-xs)` block padding. Hover and focus fill the row; the active row is `data-active`, the selected surface.
- Row end: the age (`showTime`, narrow units in the active locale, `now` under a minute), a lock glyph (`locked`), a `Spinner` (running) or `az-circle-alert` in `var(--text-danger)` (error).
- Row actions: Pin and More (`itemActions`), or Delete alone (`removable` only), at the inline end; with a fine pointer they show on hover, focus inside the row, the active row and an open menu, on touch always. The `item-actions` slot replaces them with the app's own controls (Snooze, Settle), rendered as a sibling of the row button so the row never nests one control in another. More opens Pin (P), Rename (R), Share, Lock, Move to project (a sub-menu of the other projects), Archive (A), then Delete in `var(--text-danger)`; labels flip to Unpin, Unlock, Unarchive. Letter hints are `DropdownMenu.Item` `command`s, mounted only while the menu is open.
- Project actions: New chat (`az-square-pen`) and More: Pin project, Project settings, then Delete project in danger.
- Rename: the row becomes an `Input` holding the title; Enter or blur saves a changed, non-empty title, Escape cancels; Enter and Escape return focus to the row.
- Cut-off title: the row's `title` holds the full title only while it is cut off.
- Empty: `No conversations yet.`; no match: `No conversations match “{query}”.`. Loading: `aria-busy` and five skeleton rows.

## Accessibility

- The root is a `nav` named by `ariaLabel`; each group is a `ul` labelled by its heading (`aria-labelledby`).
- A chat is a `button` named by its title (`aria-labelledby`), described by its description and end (`aria-describedby`: age, `Locked`, `Working`, `Failed`); the open one is `aria-current="page"`.
- Section headers and project rows are `button`s with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the list they open is labelled by them. A header with a count is named `Working 2`.
- Row actions are `IconButton`s named `Pin <title>` / `Unpin <title>`, `More actions for <title>`, `Delete <title>`, `New chat in <project>`; always in the tab order. More and Organize open a `menu` (arrow keys, `Enter`/`Space`, `ArrowRight` opens Move to project, `Esc` closes and returns focus). After Pin, Lock, Archive or Move to project, focus follows the chat to its new place (the row button, marked `data-key`); a chat that no longer shows hands focus to the nearest row, as Delete does.
- The toolbar Search is a `SearchTrigger` (`aria-keyshortcuts`); the search field is a `searchbox` named `Search conversations`; the rename field is named `Rename <title>`.
- Focus after a delete: when the removed row took focus with it, focus moves to the row in its place, else the last, else the list (`tabindex="-1"`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ConfirmDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/confirm-dialog'
  import ConversationHistory from '@aziontech/webkit/conversation-history'
  import Drawer from '@aziontech/webkit/drawer'
  import IconButton from '@aziontech/webkit/icon-button'
  import { computed, onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, ref, watch } from 'vue'

  const now = '2026-11-11T15:00:00Z'
  const items = ref([
    { id: 'c1', title: 'Purge the cache after a deploy', updatedAt: '2026-11-11T14:20:00Z' },
    { id: 'c2', title: 'Why is my function returning 502?', updatedAt: '2026-11-11T09:05:00Z' },
    { id: 'c3', title: 'Set up a WAF rule for login attempts', updatedAt: '2026-11-10T18:40:00Z' },
    { id: 'c4', title: 'Image optimization query parameters', updatedAt: '2026-11-07T11:00:00Z' },
    {
      id: 'c5',
      title: 'Migrate DNS records from another provider',
      updatedAt: '2026-10-28T16:30:00Z'
    },
    { id: 'c6', title: 'Edge storage pricing', updatedAt: '2026-08-02T10:00:00Z' }
  ])
  const active = ref('c2')
  const historyOpen = ref(false)
  const narrow = ref(false)

  let narrowQuery = null
  const onNarrowChange = () => {
    narrow.value = !!narrowQuery?.matches
  }
  onMounted(() => {
    narrowQuery = globalThis.matchMedia?.('(max-width: 767px)') ?? null
    onNarrowChange()
    narrowQuery?.addEventListener('change', onNarrowChange)
  })
  onBeforeUnmount(() => narrowQuery?.removeEventListener('change', onNarrowChange))

  watch(active, () => {
    historyOpen.value = false
  })

  const activeTitle = computed(
    () => items.value.find((item) => item.id === active.value)?.title ?? 'New chat'
  )

  const startChat = () => {
    active.value = null
    historyOpen.value = false
  }

  const pendingId = ref(null)
  const confirmOpen = ref(false)
  const pendingTitle = computed(
    () => items.value.find((item) => item.id === pendingId.value)?.title ?? ''
  )

  const remove = (event, id) => {
    pendingId.value = id
    confirmOpen.value = true
  }

  const confirmRemove = () => {
    const id = pendingId.value
    items.value = items.value.filter((item) => item.id !== id)
    if (active.value === id) active.value = null
    confirmOpen.value = false
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div
    class="flex h-96 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-(--shape-card) border border-(--border-default)"
  >
    <aside
      v-if="!narrow"
      class="flex w-(--container-3xs) shrink-0 flex-col overflow-y-auto border-e border-(--border-default) bg-(--bg-surface) p-(--spacing-xs)"
    >
      <ConversationHistory
        v-model="active"
        :items="items"
        :now="now"
        creatable
        searchable
        removable
        @create="startChat"
        @remove="remove"
      />
    </aside>
    <div class="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-(--spacing-xs) p-(--spacing-sm)">
      <div class="flex items-center gap-(--spacing-xs)">
        <IconButton
          v-if="narrow"
          icon="az az-menu"
          aria-label="Open conversation history"
          variant="ghost"
          @click="historyOpen = true"
        />
        <p class="m-0 truncate text-label-md text-(--text-default)">{{ activeTitle }}</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <Drawer
      v-if="narrow"
      v-model:open="historyOpen"
      side="start"
      size="small"
    >
      <Drawer.Content>
        <Drawer.Header class="w-full">
          <Drawer.Title>Conversation history</Drawer.Title>
        </Drawer.Header>
        <Drawer.Body>
          <ConversationHistory
            v-model="active"
            :items="items"
            :now="now"
            creatable
            searchable
            removable
            @create="startChat"
            @remove="remove"
          />
        </Drawer.Body>
      </Drawer.Content>
    </Drawer>
    <ConfirmDialog
      v-model:open="confirmOpen"
      title="Delete conversation"
      :description="`${pendingTitle} and its messages are deleted. This can't be undone.`"
      confirm-label="Delete conversation"
      size="small"
      @confirm="confirmRemove"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

# Feedback Reason Dialog

> Asks why an assistant response was not helpful, right after Bad response in `ChatMessage.Feedback`: a small dialog with one required reason (radio buttons) and optional details, then Send feedback. It turns a bare thumbs-down into a signal the team can act on, without a page or a form of the owner's own. The owner opens it, sends the payload it emits and closes it.

- Import: `import FeedbackReasonDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/feedback-reason-dialog'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- After a thumbs-down on an AI response, to collect the reason.
- Any rating of generated content that needs a short, categorised reason.

## Do

- Open it only after a thumbs-down; a thumbs-up needs no reason.
- Keep the reasons short and mutually exclusive; the last is `Other`, and details stay optional.
- Close it from the `submit` handler once the request succeeds; keep it open with `loading` while it is sent.

## Don’t

- General product feedback with several fields → a page or `Drawer` form.
- A confirmation with no input → `ConfirmDialog`.

## Related

- `chat-message` — `ChatMessage.Feedback` holds the Bad response choice that opens it.
- `confirm-dialog` — the same dialog anatomy for a yes/no decision.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reasons` | `{ value: string; label: string }[]` | `[]` | false | Reasons offered, in order. Empty uses the catalog's five: inaccurate, not helpful, did not follow the request, unsafe or harmful, other. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The feedback is being sent: Send feedback shows a spinner and the form is locked. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Dialog title. Empty uses the locale catalog (`What went wrong?`). |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: SubmitEvent, payload: { reason: string; details: string })` |  |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Opens the dialog; the reason and details reset each time it opens. Unbound, the dialog keeps it itself and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Idle (open): no reason chosen, Send feedback enabled.
- Invalid: submitted without a reason; the fieldset is invalid and its error is announced.
- Loading: Send feedback spinner, radios, details and Cancel disabled.
- `data-state` on the dialog mirrors `open` / `closed` (from `Dialog`).

## Accessibility

- A modal `Dialog` named by its title and described by its one-line description; focus moves into it and returns to the Feedback button on close.
- The reasons are a `fieldset` with a `legend` (`Reason`), a `RadioGroup` with one `RadioGroup.Item` per reason and its label; the details `Textarea` is labelled `Details (optional)`.
- Submitting without a reason marks the fieldset invalid, shows the error text and focuses the first radio; nothing is sent.
- Keyboard: `Tab` through radios (arrows within the group), details, Cancel, Send feedback; `Enter` in a radio submits; `Escape` closes.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ChatMessage from '@aziontech/webkit/chat-message'
  import FeedbackReasonDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/feedback-reason-dialog'
  import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const answer =
    'Turn on **Image Optimization** in the application settings, then add `?ims=300x` to the image URL.'
  const feedback = ref(null)
  const reasonOpen = ref(false)
  const sending = ref(false)

  const onFeedback = (value) => {
    feedback.value = value
    if (value === 'down') reasonOpen.value = true
  }

  const sendReason = () => {
    sending.value = true
    setTimeout(() => {
      sending.value = false
      reasonOpen.value = false
    }, 600)
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <ChatMessage timestamp="10:44">
      <StreamingResponse :content="answer" />
      <template #actions>
        <ChatMessage.Actions>
          <ChatMessage.Feedback
            :model-value="feedback"
            @update:model-value="onFeedback"
          />
        </ChatMessage.Actions>
      </template>
    </ChatMessage>
    <FeedbackReasonDialog
      v-model:open="reasonOpen"
      :loading="sending"
      @submit="sendReason"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/mcp-app-frame.md -->

# Mcp App Frame

> The safe frame for an interactive widget a tool returns inside a chat answer: an MCP app (MCP Apps, or the older MCP-UI) such as a plan picker, a booking form or a map that a tool call rendered as HTML. It runs the widget in a sandboxed `iframe` with an opaque origin and a strict content policy, gives it an accessible name, shows a loading state while it starts and a blocked state when the resource cannot be shown safely, grows to the height the widget reports, and forwards every well-formed message the widget sends (call a tool, open a link, send a prompt, the start handshake) to the app as a `message` event. It never acts on a message itself: the app decides, and answers through `post()`. Unlike `embed` (a third-party page an author places on purpose and trusts), the content here is written by a tool at run time and is untrusted by default, so the frame owns the sandbox, the content policy, the message checks and the navigation guard instead of leaving them to the consumer. Threat model. The widget is hostile: it comes from an MCP server the reader may not control, through a model hostile content may have steered. - Page access: the `iframe` has exactly `sandbox="allow-scripts"` (no `allow-same-origin`, `allow-top-navigation`, `allow-popups`, `allow-forms`, `allow-modals` or `allow-downloads`), `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` and `allow=""`. Its document has an opaque origin: no parent DOM, cookies, storage or session (`window.parent.document` throws), no device permissions, no tab navigation, windows, forms, downloads or dialogs. - Network: inline HTML is prefixed with `<!doctype html>` and a Content Security Policy `meta` (`default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; media-src data:; font-src data:; connect-src 'none'; frame-src 'none'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'; object-src 'none'`), so it cannot fetch or load remote content. A resolved URL follows its server's policy. An inline widget also inherits the page's own policy: with a nonce, a hash or `'strict-dynamic'` there, its scripts never run (it stays `ready` and silent), so such an app resolves widgets to an https origin of its own. - URLs: the frame never loads a URL taken from the resource; only an absolute `https:` URL that `resolveUrl` returns. - Messages: accepted only from the current `iframe`'s window with the origin `null`, in one of two shapes, and rebuilt from their known keys; the raw `MessageEvent` (its `source` window and `ports`) never reaches the app. `post()` targets `*`, the only target an opaque origin has, and only that window. - Navigation: the widget can navigate its own frame; the second `load` blocks the frame, but the new page runs until then. The app's own `frame-src`, limited to the origins `resolveUrl` returns, stops it before it leaves. - Residual: WebRTC, DNS prefetch and self-navigation can carry out what the widget holds, so everything sent with `post()` counts as disclosed; a widget can draw look-alike controls inside its bordered box (show its `tool-call` row before it, never ask for credentials in it) and can hold keyboard focus. Height is clamped to 48 px–`maxHeight`. - Out of scope: the MCP Apps sandbox-proxy flow (it needs `allow-same-origin` on a second origin) and what the app does with a message (check tool names and arguments; `tool-approval` for a sensitive tool).

- Import: `import McpAppFrame from '@aziontech/webkit/mcp-app-frame'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A tool call returns a UI resource (an MCP app: `text/html;profile=mcp-app`, `text/html`, or a `ui://` resource the app can resolve) and the answer should show it working inside the message.
- Any HTML or remote app produced at run time that the reader should use without it getting access to the page.

## Do

- Write a `title` that says what the widget is (`Plan picker from the billing tool`); it is the frame's accessible name.
- Handle `message` with an allow-list: answer only the methods and types you support, check the tool name and its arguments, and route a sensitive tool through `tool-approval`. Never deep-merge a payload into your own objects: nested values are structured clones and may carry an own `__proto__` key.
- Answer with `post()`; never reach into the frame. An MCP Apps widget waits for the reply to its `ui/initialize` request before it starts; an MCP-UI widget that sends `ui-lifecycle-iframe-ready` or `ui-request-data` waits for its data.
- Treat everything you `post()` as disclosed to the widget's author, and limit how often the handler acts on a widget's messages.
- Show where a widget comes from right before it (its `tool-call` row) and never ask the reader for credentials inside one.
- Resolve `ui://` and `https` resources only from servers you trust, and only to `https:` URLs; return `''` to block one.
- Set the app's own Content Security Policy: `frame-src` limited to the origins `resolveUrl` returns, so a widget cannot navigate its frame elsewhere. An inline widget inherits the app's policy as well as its own: with a nonce, a hash or `'strict-dynamic'` in the page's `script-src` its scripts never run, so such an app resolves widgets to an https origin of its own through `resolveUrl` rather than loosening its policy.

## Don’t

- A third-party page an author places on purpose (a demo, a player, a form) → `embed`.
- A remote multi-page site: the frame blocks a widget that navigates.
- Live WebKit components shown in the documentation → `browser-frame`.
- A generated file the reader may copy, download or open → `artifact-preview`.
- The record of what the tool did (name, input, output, status) → `tool-call`; the app frame sits after it in the same message.

## Related

- `tool-call` — the row that records the call the widget belongs to; render the frame right after it.
- `tool-approval` — ask the reader before acting on a widget's tool request when the tool changes something.
- `chat-message` — the message the frame sits in.
- `embed` — the author-placed, trusted counterpart.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resource` | `McpAppFrameResource` | `—` | true | The UI resource the tool returned: its `uri`, `mimeType`, and the HTML as `text` or base64 `blob`. |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | Accessible name of the widget, announced before its content. |
| `resolveUrl` | `(resource: McpAppFrameResource) => string \| Promise<string>` | `undefined` | false | Turns a resource that is not inline HTML into an https URL the frame may load; return an empty string to block it. Without it such resources are blocked. |
| `maxHeight` | `number` | `640` | false | Largest height in pixels the widget may grow the frame to; 48 is the floor. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `(message: McpAppFrameMessage)` | A message the widget sent (a tool call, a prompt, a link, a notification, the start handshake), validated and rebuilt from its known keys. Not a user activation, so it carries no DOM event. Size messages are handled by the frame and not emitted. |

## States

- Visual states: `loading`, `ready`, `error` (blocked). The frame has no `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `empty` or open/closed state.
- `loading` starts on mount and whenever the resource's content changes (its `uri`, `mimeType`, `text` or `blob`); a new `resolveUrl` function alone does not restart it. While `resolveUrl` is pending no `iframe` exists and a `Skeleton` at the starting height holds the place. A `resolveUrl` result that settles after the resource changed or the component unmounted is discarded. Once the document is known (the `srcdoc` built or the URL resolved), a new `iframe` is created for it (keyed, so listeners and posts never cross two widgets) and stays rendered and in layout, with the `Skeleton` absolutely on top, until that `iframe`'s first `load`. The root carries `data-loading` and `aria-busy="true"`, and a polite `role="status"` says `Loading {title}`.
- Messages are accepted from the moment the `iframe` exists, before its `load`, because a widget sends its handshake while it starts; early size messages apply too.
- `ready` follows the first `load` of the current `iframe`: the `Skeleton` goes.
- `error` (`data-error` on the root) replaces the `iframe` with an `Alert` (`severity="warning"`) naming the app that cannot be shown; the root then drops its own border and fill so the Alert's frame is the only line. Recovery (a retry) belongs to the app, next to the `tool-call` row. It happens when the resource is not inline HTML and there is no `resolveUrl`; when `resolveUrl` returns an empty string or a URL that is not absolute `https:`, throws, or rejects; when a `blob` is not valid base64 UTF-8; and on a second `load` of the same `iframe` (the widget navigated). A resolved URL that fails on the network cannot be detected (an `iframe` fires no `error` event), so its failure shows inside the frame and does not become `error`.
- Inline: a resource is shown inline when its `mimeType` is `text/html` (with any parameters, such as `;profile=mcp-app`) and it carries `text` or a base64 `blob`; every other resource goes through `resolveUrl`.
- Height: the frame starts at `max(48, min(240, maxHeight))` px and follows the widget's size message (MCP-UI `ui-size-change` with `payload.height`, MCP Apps `ui/notifications/size-changed` with `params.height`), a finite number clamped between 48 px and `max(48, maxHeight)` (48 px is the floor even when `maxHeight` is smaller), written to `--mcp-app-frame-view-height`; the widget scrolls inside beyond that. A size message whose height is not a finite number is dropped. Size messages are not emitted. A smaller `maxHeight` clamps the current height again.
- Accepted messages: `source` is the current `iframe`'s window, `origin` is `null`, and the data is a plain object that is either an MCP-UI message (a string `type` of 1 to 128 characters, an optional plain-object `payload`, an optional string `messageId`) or a JSON-RPC 2.0 message (`jsonrpc: '2.0'` with a string `method` or a string or number `id`; optional plain-object or array `params`, any `result`, plain-object `error`). Everything else is dropped silently.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the widget draws focus inside its own document; the frame adds no focusable element of its own, and its root shows the ring token (`focus-within:ring-2 focus-within:ring-(--ring-color)`) while focus is inside the widget, so the reader sees they are in third-party content.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves into the widget and on through it; the frame intercepts no key.
- ARIA: `title` renders as the `iframe`'s `title`; the root carries `aria-busy="true"` while loading; the loading text is a `role="status"` region that stays rendered and is emptied when loading ends; the blocked state is an `Alert`.
- Contrast: the `iframe` element keeps the page's `color-scheme` (the theme sets `light` or `dark`). A widget that declares no `color-scheme` gets the browser's opaque light canvas with dark default text in the dark theme (the two schemes differ), and is transparent over `var(--bg-surface)` with dark default text in the light theme, so a default-styled widget reads in both. A widget that declares `color-scheme: light dark` is transparent over `var(--bg-surface)` with the browser's matching default text. Loading (`Skeleton`) and blocked (`Alert`) keep their own token contrast; the frame adds only its border.
- Touch target: not applicable; controls belong to the widget.

<script>
  let next = 1
  const waiting = new Map()
  const send = (message) => parent.postMessage({ jsonrpc: '2.0', ...message }, '*')
  const request = (method, params) =>
    new Promise((resolve) => {
      const id = next++
      waiting.set(id, resolve)
      send({ id, method, params })
    })
  addEventListener('message', (event) => {
    const reply = event.data
    if (reply && waiting.has(reply.id)) {
      waiting.get(reply.id)(reply)
      waiting.delete(reply.id)
    }
  })
  const report = () =>
    send({
      method: 'ui/notifications/size-changed',

        width: Math.ceil(document.body.scrollWidth),
        height: Math.ceil(document.body.getBoundingClientRect().height)

    })
  })

  const resource = {

    mimeType: 'text/html;profile=mcp-app',
    text: widget
  }

  const allowedTools = ['select_plan']
  const frame = ref(null)

  const onMessage = (message) => {
    if (!('jsonrpc' in message) || message.id === undefined) return
    if (message.method === 'ui/initialize') {
      frame.value?.post({
        jsonrpc: '2.0',
        id: message.id,
        result: {
          protocolVersion: '2026-01-26',
          hostInfo: { name: 'Acme console', version: '1.0.0' },
          hostCapabilities: {},
          hostContext: {}
        }
      })
      return
    }
    if (message.method === 'tools/call') {
      const allowed = allowedTools.includes(String(message.params?.name))

        allowed

              jsonrpc: '2.0',

              jsonrpc: '2.0',

# Prompt Input

> The composer of a generative AI chat (ChatGPT, Claude.ai and Gemini composers, AI Elements PromptInput, Cloudscape prompt input): a text area that grows with the prompt up to `maxRows`, a toolbar under it, files attached by a button, by dropping them on the box or by pasting them, a model and mode picker, dictation, a voice-conversation control that stands in for Submit while the prompt is empty, a Submit control that becomes Stop while a response is generated, a secondary row under the box (a context picker, tools, links), an optional character limit with a counter, and constraint text under it all. Enter submits on a fine pointer; Shift+Enter adds a line; on a coarse pointer (a phone keyboard) Enter adds a line and Submit sends; an IME composition never submits. It is controlled: the owner holds the text and the files, receives `submit` with the trimmed prompt, its references and its files, and clears them. While `status` is `pending` or `streaming` the reader can keep typing the next prompt, but cannot submit it until the response ends or they press Stop. With `queueable` the owner keeps a queue of prompts to send after the response (TanStack AI `useChat` queues a `sendMessage` made while it streams): Submit then stays beside Stop, and Enter or Submit sends the next prompt into that queue while Stop still ends the response. The anatomy is composed by the app: the root draws the box, the text area, Submit / Stop / voice and the file tokens; the controls the app wants (attach, dictate, model, context, tools) are sub-components it places in the `actions`, `end` and `footer` slots. Each reads the composer through `provide` / `inject`, so the app wires nothing but its own values. At rest it is one floating bar (Attach `+`, the text, the `end` controls, Submit, voice or Stop) on a translucent raised surface with a shadow and a backdrop blur, so a thread can scroll under it. A second line, attached files or references, or an open shortcut menu stack it into two rows (text on its own row) until the prompt is cleared.

- Import: `import PromptInputRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import PromptInput from '@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- The input of any conversation with the generative AI assistant.
- A single "Ask about this page" box that opens a conversation.

## Do

- Placeholder is a suggested question with no end punctuation (`Ask a question`); never the only instruction.
- Put the disclaimer and the shortcuts in `hint`, not in the placeholder.
- Set `status` from the request so Submit turns into Stop; wire `stop` to abort it.
- Set `queueable` only when the owner queues what is sent while a response runs, and shows the
- Clear `v-model` and `v-model:files` in the `submit` handler and keep focus in the input.
- Use `maxLength` only when the backend has a limit; the counter is the warning, and it stays hidden
- Default to the full composer in blocks and new AI surfaces (`PromptInput.AttachButton` in `actions`, `PromptInput.ModelPicker` and `PromptInput.DictateButton` in `end`, `voice`, `PromptInput.ContextPicker` in `footer`, the tools in one place only — the "+" menu (`PromptInput.AttachButton` with `tools`) or `PromptInput.Tools` in `footer`, never both, since each lists the enabled tools as chips — and the disclaimer in `hint`); omit a control only when the product explicitly does not offer that capability. Attach goes first at the inline start; model, dictate and Submit at the inline end, in that order; the secondary row holds what is not about this prompt (where the chat lives, the tools, a link to the desktop app).
- Show the upload state on each file (`loading`, `progress`, `error`); Submit waits for them.
- Set `voice` only when the product has a voice conversation; Submit replaces it as soon as there is

## Don’t

- A text field in a form → `textarea` inside `field`.
- Search over a list → `input` with a search icon or `property-filter`.
- A command palette → `command`.
- A file upload form → `file-dropzone` with `file-token-group` in a `field`.

## Related

- `textarea` — the form control; this one has no visible label and submits on Enter.
- `conversation` — the log above it; only the log scrolls.
- `suggestion-group` — prompts the reader can send without typing.
- `file-token-group` — what the attached files render as (horizontal, removable).
- `file-dropzone` — the drop target for a page-wide drop; the composer box is its own drop target.
- `dropdown-menu` — what the model, context and tools pickers open.
- `select` (`variant="ghost"`) — a plain single choice the app adds to the toolbar itself.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Hint shown while empty, a suggested question with no end punctuation. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Ask a question`). |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the text area; the input has no visible label. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Prompt`). |
| `maxLength` | `number` | `0` | false | Character limit; an `n/max` counter shows from 80% of it and submit is blocked over it. `0` means no limit. |
| `minRows` | `number` | `1` | false | Rows shown while empty. |
| `maxRows` | `number` | `6` | false | Rows the text area grows to before it scrolls. |
| `status` | `'ready' \| 'pending' \| 'streaming'` | `'ready'` | false | Request lifecycle: `pending` and `streaming` swap Submit for Stop and block another submit (unless `queueable`); typing stays allowed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the text area, the submit control and every control in the slots' rows. |
| `menus` | `PromptInputMenu[]` | `[]` | false | Shortcut menus opened by a trigger character at the start of a word: `/` for commands, `@` for things to reference. Choosing an option inserts `<trigger><label>` and adds it to `references`. |
| `accept` | `string` | `''` | false | File filter in the native accept syntax (extensions, MIME types, wildcards) for picked, dropped and pasted files. Empty accepts every file. |
| `maxFiles` | `number` | `0` | false | Most files attached at once; files past it are rejected. `0` means no limit. |
| `maxFileSize` | `number` | `0` | false | Largest file in bytes; larger files are rejected. `0` means no limit. |
| `voice` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a Start voice conversation control in place of Submit while there is nothing to send; it emits `voice-start`. |
| `voiceActive` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks a live voice conversation as active: swaps the voice control to End voice conversation (`voice-end`) and disables `PromptInput.DictateButton` with a muted microphone icon. |
| `queueable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | While `status` is `pending` or `streaming`, keeps Submit beside Stop and lets Enter submit, so the owner queues the prompt for after the response. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `references` | `PromptInputReference[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:references`). |
| `files` | `PromptInputFile[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:files`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, payload: { value: string; references: PromptInputReference[]; files: PromptInputFile[] })` |  |
| `stop` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |
| `voice-start` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |
| `voice-end` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |
| `reject` | `(event: Event, payload: { files: File[]; reason: PromptInputRejectReason })` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attachments` | — | Attached context the app draws itself, above the text, before the file tokens and the references. |
| `actions` | — | Controls at the inline start of the bar (`PromptInput.AttachButton`); inside a `fieldset` disabled with the input. |
| `end` | — | Controls at the inline end of the bar, before Submit (`PromptInput.ModelPicker`, `PromptInput.DictateButton`); disabled with the input. |
| `footer` | — | A secondary row under the bar (`PromptInput.ContextPicker`, `PromptInput.Tools`, links); wraps on narrow screens; disabled with the input. Optional: for the single-bar look, place the pickers in `actions` / `end` instead. |
| `hint` | — | Constraint text under everything; referenced by `aria-describedby`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input-attach-button`
- `@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input-dictate-button`
- `@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input-model-picker`
- `@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input-context-picker`
- `@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input-access-picker`
- `@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input-tools`

## Sub-components

Compound API through `index.ts` (`PromptInput.AttachButton`, `PromptInput.DictateButton`,
`PromptInput.ModelPicker`, `PromptInput.ContextPicker`, `PromptInput.Tools`, `PromptInput.AccessPicker`); standalone entries
`prompt-input-root`, `prompt-input-attach-button`, `prompt-input-dictate-button`,
`prompt-input-model-picker`, `prompt-input-context-picker`, `prompt-input-tools`, `prompt-input-access-picker`. The root provides
the composer context (`injection-key.ts`): `disabled`, `voiceActive`, `accept`, `maxFiles`, `maxFileSize`,
`fileCount`, the text (read and write), `appendFiles`, `reject`, `setRejection`, `setDragging`,
`registerAttach(handlers)`, `setChips(count)`, `focus()`. `usePromptInputContext()` throws outside a `PromptInput`.
Every part disables with the composer. The compound attaches the three pickers as async
components, so `@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input` does not carry `DropdownMenu` until a picker
renders; their standalone paths are static.

- `prompt-input-attach-button/prompt-input-attach-button.vue` — the attach control: a ghost
  `IconButton` (`az az-plus`) that opens a hidden `input type="file"` with the root's `accept` and
  `multiple` unless `maxFiles` is `1`. Its presence turns on dropping and pasting files into the box:
  it registers drag and paste handlers with the root on setup and takes them back on dispose, sorts
  every picked, dropped or pasted batch against `accept`, `maxFileSize` and `maxFiles`, appends the
  accepted files and reports the rest through the root (`reject`, the line under the box). A
  composer that offers no way to attach does not take files silently. With `tools` the control is
  the composer's "+" menu: after mount it loads a private part (`parts/prompt-input-add-menu.vue`,
  a lazy chunk with `DropdownMenu` and `Chip`) whose `DropdownMenu` opens above the control with an
  `Add` group (Camera on coarse pointers, Photos while `accept` takes images, Files) and a `Tools`
  group of checkbox options. Camera opens a file input with `accept="image/*"` and
  `capture="environment"`, Photos one with `accept="image/*"`, Files the control's own input; every
  pick goes through the same sorting against `accept`, `maxFileSize` and `maxFiles`. The turned-on
  tools follow the control as removable `Chip`s (their icon before the label) in a list named
  `Enabled tools`, and while one shows the box stacks (the root's `setChips`), so the text keeps the
  full width. Until the part has loaded the control is the plain attach `IconButton`.
  - Props: `ariaLabel?: string` (default `''` — empty uses `Attach files`); `icon?: string` (default `''` — empty uses `az az-plus`); `tools?: PromptInputMenuOption[]` (default `[]` — given, the control opens the "+" menu).
  - v-model: `v-model` `string[]` (default `[]`; emits `update:modelValue`) — the turned-on tools, in `tools` order.
  - Events: _none_ (picked files go through the root: `update:files` / `reject`).
  - Slots: _none_.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `prompt-input-attach-button`.
- `prompt-input-dictate-button/prompt-input-dictate-button.vue` — dictation.
  `browser` it uses the Web Speech API (`SpeechRecognition`, `webkitSpeechRecognition`) where the
  browser has it and renders nothing where it does not (checked after mount, so the server HTML
  never shows a control that will not work). While listening the transcript is written into the
  prompt after the text that was there, interim words included, and the control turns into Stop
  dictation. Its name changes with the action (`Dictate` / `Stop dictation`); it carries no
  `aria-pressed`. Errors end dictation: `not-allowed` reads `Microphone access is blocked`,
  `no-speech` and `aborted` read `Dictation stopped`, anything else `Dictation stopped. Try again`. With `transcriber` `app` the control only toggles `v-model:listening`; the app records
  and writes the text into the root's `v-model` itself (its own speech-to-text service).
  - Props: `ariaLabel?: string` (default `''` — empty uses `Dictate` / `Stop dictation`); `lang?: string` (default `''` — empty uses the provider locale); `transcriber?: 'browser' | 'app'` (default `'browser'`).
  - v-model: `v-model:listening` `boolean` (default `false`; emits `update:listening`) — whether dictation is on.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `prompt-input-dictate-button`.
- `prompt-input-model-picker/prompt-input-model-picker.vue` — the model and mode picker: a ghost
  small `Button` showing the selected model's provider icon (when set), the model's label and the
  mode's label (muted), with a chevron, that opens a spacious `Popover` above it with an optional
  vertical provider filter rail (`providers`), a search input (`Search models...`), a scrollable
  `Model` menu of radio options (provider icon, label, checkmark, a favorite star, and shortcut or
  muted description) and, when `modes` is not empty, a side-by-side mode column of radio options.
  Each row has a star `IconButton` (`aria-pressed`, a lazy `Tooltip`) that toggles the model in
  `favoriteKeys`; it shows on row hover or focus, on a coarse pointer and while starred. The rail's
  first button filters to the favorites (`No favorites yet` when none), a provider button to that
  provider; pressing the active one again shows every model. With the
  `footer` slot the panel ends in a bar under its columns (`border-t`, wraps; its last control sits
  at the inline end), for a speed `ToggleGroup`, a toggle `Button` or `PromptInput.AccessPicker`.
  The panel stays open on a choice; Escape or an outside click closes it. Below `md` the trigger
  is an icon-only `IconButton` (the model's icon) that opens a `Dialog` bottom sheet, loaded on
  first open: `Favorites`, then one section per provider (44 px rows, check, star), the modes as a
  `ToggleGroup`, the `footer` slot, and the search at the bottom. With no `models` the
  control is disabled; a `v-model` that matches no model shows `Model`, and a mode that matches
  none shows no mode label.
  - Props: `models?: PromptInputMenuOption[]` (default `[]`); `providers?: PromptInputMenuOption[]` (default `[]` — optional provider rail at the inline start); `modes?: PromptInputMenuOption[]` (default `[]`); `modeLabel?: string` (default `''` — empty uses `Mode`; the mode column's label, such as `Thinking Level` or `Effort`).
  - v-model: `v-model` `string` (default `''`; emits `update:modelValue`) — the model; `v-model:mode` `string` (default `''`; emits `update:mode`); `v-model:favoriteKeys` `string[]` (default `[]`; emits `update:favoriteKeys`) — the starred models' values, in the order they were starred.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `footer` — a bar under the panel's columns.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `prompt-input-model-picker`.
- `prompt-input-access-picker/prompt-input-access-picker.vue` — the access-mode picker (what the
  agent may do without asking, such as Supervised, Auto-accept edits, Auto or Full access): a ghost
  small `Button` with the chosen mode's icon and label and a trailing `az az-chevron-up` (named
  `<title>: <label>`), that opens a `Popover` above it, aligned to the end, holding the `title`
  (muted, `Permissions` by default), a fluid icon-only `ToggleGroup` (`showLabels` false) of the
  modes, and the chosen mode's label and description (`aria-live="polite"`, so a change by arrow
  key is announced). An option without `icon` uses `az az-shield`. It sits in the model picker's
  `footer` or in the composer's `footer`. With no `options` the control is disabled.
  - Props: `options?: PromptInputMenuOption[]` (default `[]` — each with `icon`, `label` and `description`); `title?: string` (default `''` — empty uses `Permissions`).
  - v-model: `v-model` `string` (default `''`; emits `update:modelValue`) — the chosen mode.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `prompt-input-access-picker`.
- `prompt-input-context-picker/prompt-input-context-picker.vue` — the context picker ("Choose
  project"): a ghost small `Button` with the option's icon (else `icon`) and the chosen label (else
  the placeholder) that opens a `DropdownMenu` of options (the chosen one checked; a choice closes
  the panel) and, once one is chosen, a `Remove context` action. With no `options` the control is
  disabled and shows the placeholder.
  - Props: `options?: PromptInputMenuOption[]` (default `[]`); `placeholder?: string` (default `''` — empty uses `Choose context`); `icon?: string` (default `''` — empty uses `az az-folder`).
  - v-model: `v-model` `string` (default `''`; emits `update:modelValue`) — the chosen option; `''` is none.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `prompt-input-context-picker`.
- `prompt-input-tools/prompt-input-tools.vue` — the tools menu ("Plugins"): a ghost small `Button`
  (`az az-wrench`, `label` else `Tools`) that opens a `DropdownMenu` of checkbox options, followed by
  the enabled tools as removable `Chip`s in a list named `Enabled tools`.
  - Props: `tools?: PromptInputMenuOption[]` (default `[]`); `label?: string` (default `''` — empty uses `Tools`).
  - v-model: `v-model` `string[]` (default `[]`; emits `update:modelValue`) — the enabled tools, in `tools` order.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `prompt-input-tools`.

Exported types: `PromptInputStatus`, `PromptInputMenu`, `PromptInputMenuOption`,
`PromptInputReference`, `PromptInputFile`, `PromptInputRejectReason`,
`PromptInputDictateTranscriber`. Composed DS components: `icon-button` (Submit, Stop, voice,
attach, dictate), `file-token-group` (files, loaded on first file), `button`, `dropdown-menu`,
`chip`.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The prompt being written, via `defineModel`. The owner clears it in its `submit` handler. |
| `v-model:references` | `PromptInputReference[]` | `[]` | `update:references` | What the prompt references, added by the menus and shown as removable chips above the text; removing a chip also removes its `<trigger><label>` text. |
| `v-model:files` | `PromptInputFile[]` | `[]` | `update:files` | The attached files, shown as removable tokens above the text. Accepted picks, drops and pastes are appended as `{ file }`; the owner adds `loading`, `progress`, `error` while it uploads them and clears the list in its `submit` handler. |

## States

- `data-status` mirrors `status`; `data-disabled`; `data-invalid` while over `maxLength`; `data-dragging` on the box while files are dragged over it (only with an `AttachButton`).
- `data-multiline` on the root and the box while the composer is stacked (text on its own row): the prompt took a second line (kept until it is cleared), `minRows` is above 1, files, references, the `attachments` slot or a turned-on tool chip of the `AttachButton` are shown, or a shortcut menu is open. Absent, it is the single bar.
- `ready`: Submit (primary `IconButton`, large, `az az-arrow-up`), disabled while there is nothing to send, the prompt is over the limit, a file is loading or failed, or `disabled`. With `voice` and nothing to send (no text, no files), Start voice conversation (secondary `IconButton`, `az az-audio-lines`) takes its place. While `voiceActive` is `true` and there is nothing to send, End voice conversation (primary `IconButton`, `az az-x`) takes its place and `PromptInput.DictateButton` is disabled with `az az-microphone-off`.
- `pending` / `streaming`: Stop (secondary `IconButton`, `az az-stop`) replaces Submit; Enter does nothing.
- `pending` / `streaming` with `queueable`: Stop stays, and Submit (primary, after Stop at the inline end) shows beside it while there is something to send; Enter and Submit emit `submit` as in `ready`. With nothing to send only Stop shows, and the voice control never does.
- Near the limit (the prompt holds 80% of `maxLength` or more): the `n/max` counter shows before Submit and the text area is described by it; below 80% it is not rendered.
- Over the limit: border turns `--danger-border`, the counter turns danger, `aria-invalid="true"`, and a polite live region says how many characters are over.
- Dragging files over the box: a dashed `--border-selected` panel on `--bg-selected` covers the box and reads `Drop files to attach`.
- Rejected files: a danger line under the box says how many were not added and why (`not an accepted type`, `larger than 10 MB`, `up to 3 files`), in a polite live region; it clears on the next accepted file, a removal or a submit.
- Dictating (`DictateButton`): the control is a secondary `IconButton` named `Stop dictation` (`az az-stop`); a polite status reads `Listening` when it starts and `Dictation stopped` (or `Microphone access is blocked`, or `Dictation stopped. Try again`) when it ends.
- No `loading` or `readonly` state on the composer: upload state is per file (`v-model:files`), and a composer that cannot be used is `disabled`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the container shows `focus-within:ring-2 focus-within:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Enter` submits on a fine pointer (while a response runs only with `queueable`), and adds a line on a coarse pointer, where Submit sends; `Shift+Enter` new line; `Tab` moves through the attachments, the toolbar start controls, the toolbar end controls, Submit / Stop / voice, then the footer row. IME composition (`isComposing`, or between `compositionstart` and `compositionend`) never submits.
- Shortcut menus (`menus`): typing a trigger at the start of a word opens a listbox above the input with up to eight options matching what follows it. Focus stays in the text area, which points at the list with `aria-controls` and at the highlighted option with `aria-activedescendant` (a `textarea` cannot take `role="combobox"` or `aria-expanded`, so it carries `aria-autocomplete="list"` while `menus` is set); `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move, `Enter` or `Tab` choose, `Escape` closes, and Enter does not submit while the list is open. A polite status reads `3 suggestions` or `No matches`. The text area lists the triggers in `aria-keyshortcuts`. References are a list named `References` of removable `Chip`s.
- Files: the tokens are `FileTokenGroup`'s list (named `Files`) with a named remove button each; focus moves as that component defines. The drop panel is decorative (`aria-hidden`); the attach button is the keyboard path. Rejections are announced politely and shown as text.
- "+" menu (`AttachButton` with `tools`): a `DropdownMenu` like the pickers; Camera, Photos and Files are `menuitem`s that open the system picker, the tools `menuitemcheckbox`es that keep the menu open. The trigger keeps the name `Attach files`.
- Pickers: each opens a `DropdownMenu` (`menu` with `menuitemradio` / `menuitemcheckbox`), so arrows, typeahead, `Escape` and focus return come from it. The model trigger's name is its visible text (model and mode). Enabled tools are a list named `Enabled tools` of removable `Chip`s.
- Dictation: the control's name says what pressing it does (`Dictate` / `Stop dictation`), with no `aria-pressed`; the listening status is a polite live region. Where the browser has no speech recognition the control is not rendered.
- Queue: with `queueable`, Stop and Submit are two named buttons in tab order (Stop first); the owner announces the queued prompt through `PromptQueue`'s list, so the composer adds no live region of its own.
- Focus: Submit, Stop and Start voice conversation share one place, except with `queueable` while `pending` / `streaming`, when Stop and Submit sit side by side. When the control that has focus is swapped, removed or disabled (the owner clears the prompt after a submit, which hides a queue Submit; a request starts or ends), focus moves to the text area instead of falling to the page.
- ARIA: the `<textarea>` is named by `aria-label` (no visible label, as Cloudscape allows for an input with an action button), described by the counter (while it shows) and the hint, `aria-invalid` over the limit; Submit, Stop and Start voice conversation are named icon buttons.
- The placeholder never carries required information (it disappears on typing).
- Touch target: `IconButton` medium (44 px on coarse pointers); the small picker `Button`s get the 44 px hit area on coarse pointers from `Button`.
- Model picker favorites: each star is a `button` with `aria-pressed`, named with its model (`Add to favorites: Gemini 4 Neon`), reachable by `Tab` and shown while focused. The rail group is `Providers`.
- Model picker on a phone: the trigger is named `Model: <model>, <mode>`; the `Dialog` starts focus on the chosen model.
- Access picker: the trigger is named `Permissions: <mode>`; the modes are a `radiogroup` named by the title, each radio named by its label (visually hidden text); the description under it is `aria-live="polite"`.

# Prompt Queue

> Messages sent while a response is generating, waiting above the prompt input (TanStack AI `useChat` `queue`): each shows its text in send order with a button that removes it before it is sent; changes are announced politely.

- Import: `import PromptQueue from '@aziontech/webkit/prompt-queue'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A chat that lets the reader keep typing while a response streams and holds the extra messages.
- Directly above the `prompt-input`, in the composer area of the conversation.

## Do

- Keep it mounted for the whole chat, so every change is announced.
- Keep each queued message's id, so a removal cancels the right one.
- When the queue empties, move focus back to the prompt input.

## Don’t

- Prompts the reader may choose to send → `suggestion-group`.
- Messages already sent → `chat-message`.

## Related

- `prompt-input` — the composer it sits above.
- `suggestion-group` — prompts to send, not prompts waiting.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `PromptQueueItem[]` | `[]` | false | The waiting messages, in the order they will be sent. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Queued messages`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remove` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: PromptQueueItem)` |  |

## Sub-components

_None. Data-driven. `PromptQueueItem`: `{ id: string; text: string; attachmentCount?: number }` (text parts joined; non-text parts counted, shown above zero)._

## States

- Empty: no box, only the hidden status region; `data-empty` on the root.
- Populated: the box with the count line and one row per item.
- Clamped item: a message longer than two lines shows a `Show more` link under it; it expands that message in place (`data-state="open"` on the text) and reads `Show less` to fold it back, so the reader can review the whole message before it is sent.
- No `disabled`, `loading`, `invalid` or `error` state, and no component-level `open` state: a message leaves only through the owner.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the `IconButton` ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the remove buttons (and the `Show more` toggle of a clamped message) in queue order; `Enter` / `Space` removes or toggles.
- Focus: when a focused row leaves (removed or sent), focus moves to the remove button now at that position, else the last; an empty queue hands focus to the owner.
- ARIA: a native `ol` named `Queued messages` (`ariaLabel`); each remove button is named `Remove from queue` and described by its text; the `Show more` / `Show less` toggle carries `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at its message; glyphs `aria-hidden`.
- Announcements: a hidden polite `role="status"` says `2 messages queued` on each count change after mount and `No messages queued` when empty.
- Touch target: 44 px on coarse pointers.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PromptInput from '@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input-root'
  import PromptQueue from '@aziontech/webkit/prompt-queue'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const prompt = ref('')
  const queue = ref([
    { id: 'q1', text: 'Also purge the cache for app.example.com' },
    { id: 'q2', text: 'Then show me the error rate for the last hour', attachmentCount: 1 }
  ])
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--layout-group-gap)">
    <PromptQueue
      :items="queue"
      @remove="(event, item) => (queue = queue.filter((entry) => entry.id !== item.id))"
    />
    <PromptInput
      v-model="prompt"
      status="streaming"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/prompt-queue.md](components/prompt-queue.md).
