# Reasoning

> Shows the model's thinking before its response (Cloudscape Thinking pattern, AI Elements Reasoning): a disclosure whose label reads `Thinking` (pulsing) while the model reasons and `Thought for 14 seconds` once it is done, with the trace inside. Collapsed by default in a chat, where the response is the main content. The duration comes from the server (`duration`) or is measured from `streaming` turning on to turning off, rounded to whole seconds. An optional `Skip thinking` lets the reader ask for the response now.

- Import: `import Reasoning from '@aziontech/webkit/reasoning'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The model performs extended reasoning before answering, and the trace helps the reader trust or check the response.

## Do

- Keep it collapsed in chat; open it by default only where reasoning is the point (an editor, a review).
- Never show secrets, token counts or system prompts in the trace.
- Do not replace the label with trace text; the label stays `Thinking` until done.
- Offer `skippable` only when the model can answer meaningfully without finishing.

## Don’t

- Ordinary loading with no reasoning → `response-loading`.
- Agent actions with side effects (calls, commands) → `tool-call` and `tool-approval`.
- Progressive steps of a long task → a `stepper` or a list of `tool-call`s.

## Related

- `response-loading` — loading without a trace.
- `tool-call` — what the agent did, rather than what it thought.
- `streaming-response` — renders a Markdown trace inside the slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The model is still reasoning: the label reads `Thinking` and pulses; when it turns false the label shows how long it took. |
| `duration` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Seconds the reasoning took, when the server reports it. Without it the component measures from `streaming` turning on to turning off. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled; collapsed is the default in a chat, where the response is the main content. |
| `skippable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Offers `Skip thinking` while streaming, for a model that can answer before it finishes reasoning. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skip` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The trace: short narration, steps, inline code. Kept as it was once thinking ends. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./reasoning"`. Composed DS components: `button` (Skip thinking)._

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | The trace was expanded or collapsed. Unbound, the state is local and starts from `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- `data-state="open|closed"` (disclosure), `data-streaming`.
- Label: `Thinking` while streaming; `Thought for {n} seconds` with a duration; `Thought for a few seconds` when neither was measured nor given.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the trigger.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` to the trigger, `Enter` / `Space` toggles; `Tab` to Skip thinking.
- ARIA: a `button` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` the trace; glyphs `aria-hidden`; a polite visually hidden status announces the completed label (`Thought for 14 seconds`) when thinking ends. The trace is not live.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 on the muted label and trace.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Reasoning from '@aziontech/webkit/reasoning'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <Reasoning :duration="14">
      <p>The reader asks why the cache hit ratio of storefront dropped this week.</p>
      <p>
        Checking the cache settings of <code>storefront</code>: query strings are part of the cache
        key, and a campaign started on Monday adds <code>utm_source</code> to every link.
      </p>
      <p>Each campaign link is a new cache key, so most requests miss the cache.</p>
    </Reasoning>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/response-branches.md -->

# Response Branches

> Pages through alternative versions of one assistant response or one edited prompt: after Try again, after the reader edits a prompt, or when the model returned several candidates, the message shows one version at a time with a `‹ 2/3 ›` pager under it, or alone in the message's action row when no slot is given. The owner keeps every version and renders the active one in the default slot; the component owns only the position and the pager. It is the AI Elements `Branch` pattern, rebuilt on WebKit's `IconButton` and tokens.

- Import: `import ResponseBranches from '@aziontech/webkit/response-branches'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ResponseBranches to page through alternative versions of one AI response; rows of a table or list use Pagination.
- A response was regenerated and the earlier versions stay available to compare.
- A model returned several candidates and the person picks the one to keep reading.

## Do

- Move to the new version when Regenerate finishes (set `v-model` to the last index) so the person sees what they asked for.
- Keep the versions in the order they were made; the newest is last.
- Do not render the pager inside the slot; it belongs to the component so its position and labels stay the same across versions.

## Don’t

- Pages of one long list → use `Pagination`.
- Steps of a flow → use `Stepper`.
- Different documents side by side → use `Tabs`.

## Related

- `chat-message` — the message whose body the branches wrap; its actions hold Regenerate.
- `streaming-response` — a new version streams in the slot while the pager already counts it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | `number` | `—` | true | How many versions exist. With one or none the pager is not drawn. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the pager group. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Response versions`). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Locks the pager, for example while a new version streams. |
| `modelValue` | `number` | `0` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | { index: number } | Optional. The active version. Rendered once; the owner switches its content by `index`. Left out, only the pager renders, as in `ChatMessage.Actions`' `#leading` slot. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `number` | `0` | `update:modelValue` | Zero-based index of the version shown, clamped to `0 … count - 1`. |

## States

- `data-count` on the root; `data-index` mirrors the clamped index.
- First version: Previous is disabled; last version: Next is disabled.
- `disabled`: both buttons are disabled and the counter is muted.
- `count` ≤ 1: only the slot renders.

## Accessibility

- The pager is `role="group"` named by `ariaLabel` (`Response versions`); Previous and Next are `IconButton`s named `Previous version` / `Next version`.
- The visible counter (`2/3`, `__position`) is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden polite live region (`__status`, `Version 2 of 3`) announces the new position once; the slot is not live.
- Keyboard: `Tab` reaches Previous and Next; `Enter`/`Space` move; a disabled end button leaves the tab order. When the focused arrow reaches an end and turns disabled, focus moves to the other arrow instead of falling to the page.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ChatMessage from '@aziontech/webkit/chat-message'
  import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'
  import IconButton from '@aziontech/webkit/icon-button'
  import ResponseBranches from '@aziontech/webkit/response-branches'
  import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const versions = ref([
    'Purge the cache from **Cache › Purge**: choose *URL*, paste the paths and confirm.',
    'Use a **wildcard purge** (`/assets/*`) when many files changed at once; it clears every match in one request.',
    'If the files change on every deploy, add a **version to the file name** instead of purging: the new name is a new cache entry.'
  ])
  const active = ref(2)
  const regenerating = ref(false)

  const regenerate = () => {
    if (regenerating.value) return
    regenerating.value = true
    setTimeout(() => {
      versions.value = [
        ...versions.value,
        'Purge by **cache key** from the API (`POST /purge/cachekey`) to automate it in your pipeline.'
      ]
      active.value = versions.value.length - 1
      regenerating.value = false
    }, 800)
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <ChatMessage timestamp="10:44">
      <ResponseBranches
        v-model="active"
        :count="versions.length"
        :disabled="regenerating"
      >
        <template #default="{ index }">
          <StreamingResponse :content="versions[index]" />
        </template>
      </ResponseBranches>
      <template #actions>
        <ChatMessage.Actions>
          <CopyButton
            size="small"
            :value="versions[active]"
          />
          <IconButton
            icon="az az-refresh"
            aria-label="Regenerate response"
            variant="ghost"
            size="small"
            :loading="regenerating"
            @click="regenerate"
          />
        </ChatMessage.Actions>
      </template>
    </ChatMessage>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/response-loading.md -->

# Response Loading

> Use ResponseLoading only while a generative AI answer is being produced; never for loading product data, which uses Skeleton (known shape), Spinner (inline) or Progress (measurable). The loading state of a generative AI response (Cloudscape generative AI loading states and loading bar, AI Elements Loader): visible loading text — `Generating a response`, `Loading list of workloads` — paired with three pulsing dots (`inline`, for text) or an indeterminate bar (`bar`, where a table, list or code block is about to appear). It waits `delay` milliseconds before showing anything, so a response that arrives within a second never flickers a loading state.

- Import: `import ResponseLoading from '@aziontech/webkit/response-loading'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Processing: the model has the prompt but has produced nothing yet (`ChatMessage` renders it for `state="pending"`).
- Generation of mixed content: a bar where a table or code block will appear while text streams.

## Do

- Text says `[Generating|Loading] <what>` without end punctuation: `Generating a response`, `Loading list of workloads`.
- Keep the default 1 s delay; set `delay` to 0 only when the owner already delayed.
- Use the bar only for non-text content; stream text instead of loading it.

## Don’t

- Model reasoning with a trace → `reasoning`.
- Loading a page or table of product data → `skeleton`, `spinner`, `progress`.
- Determinate progress → `progress`.

## Related

- `chat-message` — renders this while `pending`.
- `progress` — the indeterminate bar it draws.
- `reasoning` — thinking with a trace.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible loading text, `Generating <what>` or `Loading <what>`, with no end punctuation. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Generating a response`). |
| `variant` | `'inline' \| 'bar'` | `'inline'` | false | `inline` pulses three dots beside the text (text responses); `bar` draws an indeterminate bar under it, where a table, list or code block is about to appear. |
| `delay` | `number` | `1000` | false | Milliseconds to wait before showing anything, so a fast response never flickers a loading state. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./response-loading"`; type `ResponseLoadingVariant`. Composed DS components: `progress`._

## States

- `data-variant`; `data-state="closed"` until the delay has passed, then `data-state="open"`. Before that the `role="status"` region exists but is empty, so the text is announced when it appears.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: nothing focusable.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: `role="status"` (polite) holds the visible text; dots and bar are `aria-hidden`. Loading is always conveyed in text, not only in motion.
- Reduced motion: dots stop pulsing; the bar stops sweeping.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ResponseLoading from '@aziontech/webkit/response-loading'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <ResponseLoading />
  </div>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/response-loading.md](components/response-loading.md).

<!-- components/sources.md -->

# Sources

> The sources a generative AI response drew on (ChatGPT's Sources, Cloudscape's sources section, AI Elements Sources): a small `Sources` pill with the overlapping marks of up to three cited sources that opens, in place, a `DropdownMenu` of link items, one per source. Sources the answer searched but did not cite (`cited: false`) are listed under More, after the Citations. The pill ends the message's action row (`ChatMessage.Actions` `#trailing`), on the same line as the actions. Each mark is the site's favicon (`image`), its icon, or its first letter on a colour of its own, so three sources never look alike.

- Import: `import Sources from '@aziontech/webkit/sources'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A response is grounded in documents, pages or records the reader may want to open or verify.

## Do

- Order items as the response first cites them, so `[1]` is item 1; put uncited items (`cited: false`) last so the numbers stay aligned.
- Use the page title as the title and the site's own name as `site` (`Azion`, `GitHub`); without `site` the host of `href` shows.
- Pass `publisher` and `publishedAt` when you have them.
- Keep the panel closed by default; the inline citations are the primary path.
- Give `image` the site's favicon URL when the app has one (from the search tool's result); otherwise `icon` for a site in the icon set, or nothing for the lettered mark.

## Don’t

- Related links that the response did not use → `help-panel` links or a plain list.
- A single source → cite it inline with `Citation`; a list of one is noise.

## Related

- `citation` — the inline chip whose numbers point at these items.
- `streaming-response` — renders the citations; pass it the same items.
- `chat-message` — the pill goes in the `#trailing` slot of `ChatMessage.Actions`, after the icon actions.
- `dropdown-menu` — the menu the pill opens; its items draw every row.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `SourcesItem[]` | `[]` | false | The sources behind the response, in citation order; item `n` is what `[n]` points at. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the pill that opens the panel. Empty shows `Sources` and names the pill with the count (`3 sources`). |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Sub-components

_None. Data-driven: a source list is a record set the response already holds, like table rows.
Exports: `"./sources"`; exported type `SourcesItem` (`title`, `href?`, `description?`, `site?`,
`image?`, `icon?`, `publisher?`, `publishedAt?`, `cited?`) from `sources/types.ts`, shared with
`StreamingResponse` and `Citation`. Private parts: `parts/sources-mark.vue` draws one round mark
(also the leading slot of each menu item), and `parts/sources-item.vue` the `Citation` card row.
Composed DS components: `dropdown-menu` (`Trigger`, `Group`, `Item`)._

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | The panel's open state, by the pill, `Escape` or a press outside the panel. Unbound, the state is local and starts from `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- `data-state="open|closed"` on the root and the pill (an open pill keeps the hover fill); renders nothing when `items` is empty.
- The root is `display: contents` and the pill does not wrap (`whitespace-nowrap`, `shrink-0`), so it sits at the end of the action row.
- The pill's marks are the first three cited items (all items when none is cited).
- Panel: a `DropdownMenu` (`side="auto"`, `align="start"`) on every width, never a `Drawer`; it scrolls when taller than the room left.
- Row: one `DropdownMenu.Item` per source: `value` its index, `label` the title, `href` (a safe URL), `target="_blank"` for an external URL, the 24 px mark in `#leading`, and `description` the line `site · publisher · date` (medium date in the reader's locale; parts it lacks are left out; none, a one-line row). Hover, focus, the highlighted fill with its 2px inset gap, padding and type are the menu item's; no underline. The item `description` (snippet) is not drawn.
- Groups: when some items have `cited: false`, the menu shows a Citations and a More `DropdownMenu.Group` with their labels and divider; otherwise one unlabelled group.
- Mark: favicon (`image`, a safe URL), else `icon`, else the first letter of the site on one of seven `--chart-series-*` colours picked by a stable hash of the host; a favicon that fails to load falls back to the letter.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the pill shows `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`; rows show the menu item's inset ring.
- Keyboard map: `DropdownMenu`'s: `Enter` / `Space` / `Down` on the pill opens and focuses the first source, `Up` the last; `Down` / `Up` / `Home` / `End` and typeahead move; `Enter` opens the link; `Escape` closes and returns focus to the pill; `Tab` closes.
- ARIA: the pill is a `button` with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, named `3 sources` (it holds the visible `Sources`, WCAG 2.5.3) or by `title`; the marks are `aria-hidden`; the `menu` is labelled by the pill; each source is a link `menuitem` named by its title and described by its meta line; groups are `role="group"` named Citations or More.
- Touch: the 32 px pill carries an invisible 44 px hit area on coarse pointers.
- External links open in a new tab (`target="_blank"` on the item: `rel`, glyph and `common.newTab` hint).
- Unsafe `href` (`javascript:`, `data:`, any non-web scheme, `//host`): a plain item; an unsafe `image` is dropped.
- Contrast: the letter is `--text-default` on a 30% tint; the series ring is a solid mark (Lc 30).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Sources from '@aziontech/webkit/sources'

  const items = [
    {
      title: 'Real-Time Purge',
      href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/products/cache/real-time-purge/',
      description: 'Removes a cached object from every data center in a few seconds.',
      site: 'Azion',
      icon: 'az az-azion',
      publisher: 'Azion Technologies',
      publishedAt: '2026-03-02'
    },
    {
      title: 'aziontech/azion: the Azion command line',
      href: 'https://github.com/aziontech/azion',
      description: 'Purge URLs, wildcards and cache keys from a terminal.',
      site: 'GitHub',
      icon: 'az az-github',
      publisher: 'aziontech'
    },
    {
      title: 'HTTP Caching (RFC 9111)',
      href: 'https://www.w3.org/Protocols/',
      description: 'How caches store responses and when they must ask the origin again.',
      publisher: 'World Wide Web Consortium',
      publishedAt: '2022-06-01'
    },
    {
      title: 'Cache-Control',
      href: 'https://www.npmjs.com/package/cache-control',
      description: 'A package that writes Cache-Control headers.',
      cited: false
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <Sources :items="items" />
  </div>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/sources.md](components/sources.md).

<!-- components/streaming-response.md -->

# Streaming Response

> Renders a model's Markdown as it streams in (AI Elements Response / Streamdown), safely. The content is parsed by a small Markdown parser into a tree and rendered with Vue elements — never `v-html` — so raw HTML in model output shows as text, `javascript:`, `data:` and protocol-relative links are dropped (only `http(s)`, `mailto`, `tel`, relative and `#` links survive, checked by the shared `safeHref`), and images render as their alt text. It covers what responses use: paragraphs, headings, bold, italic, inline code, links, lists (nested by indenting an item's lines under it, to any depth), block quotes, GFM tables, rules and fenced code (rendered with `CodeBlock`, copyable). Incomplete Markdown is tolerated while streaming: an unclosed `**` renders bold to the end, an unclosed code fence stays a plain `<pre>` until it closes (no highlighting churn), and a half-written link shows its text only. Text renders at the prose reading size (`.text-body-prose-md`, 16 px on 26 px lines, ChatGPT's answer size) with a full step (`--spacing-md`) between blocks, the plain answer column of a chat. Headings are bold, one step larger than the text, 24 px below the block above and 8 px above their first line: `#` at `.text-heading-md`, every deeper level at `.text-body-lg`. Lists indent 32 px from `sm` (24 px on a phone) with no extra gap between items. Inline code is `.text-label-code-md` (14 px) in medium weight. A fenced code block is a filled `CodeBlock` card with the language and copy in a sticky header, the same while the fence is still open. Numbered citations become `Citation` chips resolved against `sources`: `[1]` one chip with the site's mark and name, and a run of markers (`[1][2]`, `[1] [2]`, `[1, 2]`) one chip with `+1` whose card pages through both sources. A blinking caret marks the end while `streaming`; the region is `aria-busy` until the stream ends.

- Import: `import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use StreamingResponse for model Markdown that arrives while it renders; a whole documentation page written in MDX uses DocMarkdown.
- The content of every assistant `ChatMessage`.
- Any generated text on a page (an explanation, a summary) that arrives token by token.

## Do

- Pass the accumulated text on every chunk; the parser is cheap and the output is keyed by block.
- Keep `streaming` true until the stream closes, then false (removes the caret, highlights an open fence).
- Pass the response and its `Sources` the same array, so `[n]` is item `n` in both.
- Do not post-process model output into HTML; there is no HTML path.

## Don’t

- Authored documentation prose → `doc-prose`.
- Code alone → `code-block`.
- Trusted HTML from your own CMS → render it with your CMS pipeline; this component deliberately renders no HTML.

## Related

- `chat-message` — the host of a response.
- `citation`, `sources` — inline references and the panel that lists every source.
- `code-block` — what fenced code renders as.
- `response-loading` — the loading text before the first token, or a bar where a table is coming.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `string` | `''` | false | The model's Markdown so far. Parsed into elements, never injected as HTML: raw tags render as text and only http(s), mailto, tel, relative and hash links survive. |
| `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Tokens are still arriving: shows the caret, marks the region busy and keeps an unclosed code fence as plain text until it closes. |
| `sources` | `SourcesItem[]` | `[]` | false | Sources the `[n]`, `[n][m]` and `[n, m]` citations in the content resolve against: each becomes a chip with the site's favicon and name that opens a card of the sources it cites. |

## Sub-components

_None public. Internals shared by the AI family in `src/components/ai/lib/`: `parse-markdown.ts`
(`parseMarkdown`, `parseInline`, `safeHref`, `plainText`), `markdown-inline.ts` (recursive inline
renderer, also used by `ToolApproval` and `AgentQuestion`, where a citation marker stays plain `[n]` text),
`markdown-inline-cited.ts` (the same renderer with `Citation` chips, used here) and `markdown-list.ts`
(recursive list renderer: nested lists render inside their item). Exports: `"./streaming-response"`. Composed DS
components: `code-block`, `citation`._

## States

- `data-streaming` and `aria-busy="true"` while `streaming`.
- `data-slot="streaming-response"` on the root marks the answer text, which `ChatMessage.Actions` Read aloud speaks.
- Caret: inside the last paragraph or heading, else after the last block; only while `streaming`.
- Open fence while streaming: the card `data-testid="…__pending-code"` (language header over a `<pre>`); closed fence or stream ended: `CodeBlock` with `show-label`, `:bordered="false"` and no height cap (`--code-block-max-height: none`).
- Lists: a nested list carries `data-nested` (an unordered one uses circles); `data-ordered` switches to decimals.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: links and the table scroller carry `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches links, citations, the copy control of each code block and a wide table's scroller.
- ARIA: `aria-busy` while streaming (screen readers wait); the caret is `aria-hidden`; headings start at `h3` (`#` → `h3`) so a response never outranks the page; tables use `th scope="col"`. Announcing the finished text is the `Conversation`'s job.
- External links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, followed by an `aria-hidden` `az-external-link` glyph and the sr-only `common.newTab` text, so the new tab is seen and heard.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for body, muted quote and link text.

## Examples

### Default

````vue
<script setup>
  import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'

  const content = [
    '## Purge one URL',
    '',
    'Use **Real-Time Purge** when one object changed at the origin. Purges by `URL` take effect in a few seconds.',
    '',
    '1. Open Real-Time Purge from the products menu.',
    '2. Choose *URL* as the purge type.',
    '   - `URL` removes one object.',
    '   - `Wildcard` removes everything under a path.',
    '3. Paste the address and select Purge.',
    '',
    '| Purge type | When to use it |',
    '| --- | --- |',
    '| URL | One object changed |',
    '| Wildcard | A folder changed |',
    '',
    'The same purge from the CLI:',
    '',
    '```bash',
    'azion purge urls --urls https://www.example.com/styles.css',
    '```',
    '',
    '> A purge does not change the origin. Update the file there first.'
  ].join('\n')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <StreamingResponse :content="content" />
  </div>
</template>
````

# Subagent Card

> One helper agent the main agent handed part of the work to, shown inside the conversation (TanStack AI `subagent` parts, AG-UI sub-agent runs; benchmarks: Vercel AI Elements Task, Cloudscape generative AI progressive steps). A card names the helper agent, says in plain words what it is doing, shows its status (`Waiting`, `Running`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Stopped`) and how long it has been working, offers `Stop` while it runs, and opens to the helper's own messages. The component renders no messages itself: the owner puts the child run's messages (a `StreamingResponse`, a `ToolCall`, a nested `SubagentCard`) in the default slot. It is its own component, not new props on `tool-call`: a helper run carries its own message stream (the default slot), a stop action, an elapsed clock, a summary line and a `canceled` status, which would add three props, an event, a slot and a status value that a single tool call never uses.

- Import: `import SubagentCard from '@aziontech/webkit/subagent-card'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A response delegates a step to a helper agent (a researcher, a reviewer, a planner) whose run has its own status and its own messages.
- The reader may need to stop the helper without stopping the conversation.

## Do

- Name the helper as it is defined (`researcher`) and say what it is doing in the reader's words (`Comparing cache plans`).
- Keep the card collapsed while the main answer is the point; open it when the helper fails so the reader sees why.
- Offer `Stop` only when the host can stop the helper (`stoppable`), and set the status to `canceled` once it stops.
- Put the error message in `description` when the helper fails.

## Don’t

- One tool or command the agent called → `tool-call`.
- Asking the reader to allow an action → `tool-approval`.
- The model's own reasoning → `reasoning`.
- A long job outside a chat → `progress` or `status-indicator` on the resource.

## Related

- `tool-call` — the same row for a single tool call; a helper's tool calls go in this card's slot.
- `status-indicator` — the status the row shows.
- `streaming-response` — the helper's text in the slot.
- `reasoning` — same elapsed time and skip pattern for thinking.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `—` | true | The helper agent's identifier, shown in code font (`researcher`). |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | What the helper is doing in the reader's words (`Comparing cache plans`). Empty shows only the name. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One summary line under the row: the latest step, the result, or the error message. Empty hides the line. |
| `status` | `'pending' \| 'running' \| 'success' \| 'error' \| 'canceled'` | `'running'` | false | `pending` waits on the reader, `running` is in flight, then `success`, `error` or `canceled` (stopped). |
| `duration` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Seconds the helper has worked, when the host knows it. Without it the card counts its own running time, held while `pending`, frozen once the run ends. |
| `stoppable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Offers `Stop` while the status is `running` or `pending`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled; the helper's messages start collapsed. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stop` | `(event: MouseEvent)` | The reader pressed `Stop`; the owner stops the helper and sets `status` to `canceled`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The helper's own messages (`StreamingResponse`, `ToolCall`, a nested `SubagentCard`). |
| `input` | — | The task the main agent gave the helper (`CodeBlock`, `KeyValueList`, or a sentence). |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./subagent-card"`; type `SubagentCardStatus`. Composed DS components: `status-indicator`, `button`._

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Messages expanded or collapsed. Unbound, the state is local and starts from `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- `data-status` mirrors `status`; `data-state="open|closed"` only when a slot makes the card expandable.
- Status mapping: `pending` neutral, `running` info with spinner, `success` success, `error` danger, `canceled` warning.
- Without `default` / `input` content the row is static (no toggle button).
- `Stop` renders only when `stoppable` and the status is `running` or `pending`.
- Elapsed time: `duration` when given; otherwise counted live on the client, once a second, while `running`. The count adds up running time across `running → pending → running` (a helper that waits on the reader) and shows its held value while `pending`; it freezes when the status becomes `success`, `error` or `canceled`. Hidden when unknown (a restored card with no `duration` and no running time seen). Format: `12s`, `2m 5s`, `1h 2m`.
- The `Task` section and its heading render only when the `input` slot is passed; the `Activity` section and its heading only when the default slot is passed.
- Error: `data-status="error"`, a danger `StatusIndicator`, and the error message in `description`.
- `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `loading` and `empty` do not apply.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the toggle; `Button` owns its own ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` to the toggle, `Enter` / `Space` opens or closes the messages; `Tab` to `Stop`, `Enter` / `Space` stops. The toggle and `Stop` are siblings, never nested.
- ARIA: the toggle is a `button` with `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`; the status is a `StatusIndicator` inside a `role="status"` region the card owns, so a change from Running to Completed is announced; the live elapsed time sits outside that region so its ticking is not announced; the `Stop` button's name includes the helper (`Stop researcher`); Task and Activity are `section`s labelled by their `h4`.
- Status is conveyed in text, never by color alone.
- Focus: when `Stop` leaves the DOM while it holds focus (the status becomes `canceled`), focus moves to the toggle, or to the card root (`tabindex="-1"`) when the row is static; the `role="status"` region announces `Stopped`.
- Accessible name of the toggle: its text, the title and the helper name; the status is announced by the status region.
- Contrast: `--text-default` and `--text-muted` on the canvas (`--bg-canvas`), and `--text-muted` on `--bg-surface-raised` (the name chip), pass WCAG 2.1 AA and their APCA targets; status colours come from `StatusIndicator`, and the status is always text. No disabled state.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SubagentCard from '@aziontech/webkit/subagent-card'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--spacing-xs)">
    <SubagentCard
      name="deployer"
      title="Deploying the new cache rules"
      description="Waiting for you to allow the deploy to production."
      status="pending"
      :duration="18"
    />
    <SubagentCard
      name="researcher"
      title="Comparing cache plans"
      description="Reading the pricing page of each plan."
      status="running"
      :duration="42"
    />
    <SubagentCard
      name="reviewer"
      title="Reviewing the function code"
      description="Found two places that read the request body twice."
      status="success"
      :duration="95"
    />
    <SubagentCard
      name="analyst"
      title="Reading the error rate of www.example.com"
      description="The metrics service did not answer in 30 seconds."
      status="error"
      :duration="31"
    />
    <SubagentCard
      name="planner"
      title="Planning the migration of acme-store"
      description="Stopped by Jane Doe."
      status="canceled"
      :duration="7"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

# Suggestion Group

> A group of prompts the reader can send without typing (Cloudscape support prompt group, AI Elements Suggestion): support prompts on an empty conversation, follow-up questions after a response, or the choices of a clarifying question. Each prompt is a button; choosing one emits `select` with the click event and the item, and the owner either sends it or places it in the prompt input to edit.

- Import: `import SuggestionGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/suggestion-group'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The empty state of an assistant, to show what it can do (vertical, ideally up to three, each with an icon).
- After a broad response, to narrow it (horizontal chips, ideally up to three, most likely first, each with an icon).
- A follow-up question with predefined answers.

## Do

- Ideally three or fewer, ordered by likelihood.
- Always include an icon on every item (the component falls back to `az az-sparkles` when `icon` is omitted).
- Write prompts as the reader would ask them, under 72 characters, sentence case, no end punctuation needed for questions you send verbatim.
- Disable the group while a response is generating.
- Remove follow-ups once the reader sends anything else.

## Don’t

- Navigation or filters → `tabs`, `toggle-group`, `property-filter`.
- Choices that are a form value → `radio-group`.
- More than three options → keep the set focused or let the reader type; the prompt input stays available.

## Related

- `prompt-input` — the open-ended alternative that must stay reachable.
- `empty-state` — hosts the vertical support prompts before the first message.
- `chip`, `button` — visual cousins; prompts are their own control because they send text.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `SuggestionGroupItem[]` | `[]` | false | Up to five prompts, most likely first. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the group. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Suggested prompts`). |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | false | `horizontal` wraps chips in a row (follow-up questions under a response); `vertical` stacks them (support prompts on an empty conversation). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables every prompt, while a response is being generated. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: SuggestionGroupItem)` |  |

## Sub-components

_None. Data-driven (`items`), like Cloudscape's support prompt group. Exports: `"./suggestion-group"`;
types `SuggestionGroupItem`, `SuggestionGroupOrientation`._

## States

- `data-orientation`, `data-disabled`; renders nothing when `items` is empty.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between prompts (each is a native button; five at most keeps the tab order short); `Enter` / `Space` chooses.
- ARIA: `role="group"` with `aria-label`; icons `aria-hidden`; native `disabled`.
- Touch target: 40 px rows, 44 px on coarse pointers.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SuggestionGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/suggestion-group'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const sent = ref('')
  const items = [
    { id: 'ttl', label: 'What TTL should my images use?', icon: 'az az-image' },
    { id: 'wildcard', label: 'How do I purge a whole folder?', icon: 'az az-bolt' },
    { id: 'origin', label: 'Why does the origin still get requests?', icon: 'az az-globe' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <SuggestionGroup
      :items="items"
      aria-label="Follow-up questions"
      @select="(event, item) => (sent = item.label)"
    />
    <p
      v-if="sent"
      class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
    >
      Sent: {{ sent }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Tool Approval

> A user-authorized action in a conversation (Cloudscape user-authorized actions, AI Elements Confirmation): the agent proposes something with consequences — call a tool, run a command, deploy, delete — and the reader approves or denies it before anything runs. The card states the action as a question (``Allow `npm test`?``), says what will happen, shows exactly what will run in its body (a `CodeBlock` with the command, `KeyValueList` with parameters), and offers Deny and Approve. Once decided, the buttons give way to the outcome in text (`Approved`, `Denied`, `Request expired`) so the decision stays in the thread. Irreversible actions (`variant="danger"`) turn Approve destructive and can require typing a phrase first. With `editable` (opt-in) the reader corrects the call's arguments in a code field before approving; the edit comes back through `v-model` and `approve`. It is a card in the conversation, not a dialog: it does not trap focus and does not take initial focus; `focus()` moves focus to its heading when the owner wants to bring the reader to it.

- Import: `import ToolApproval from '@aziontech/webkit/tool-approval'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ToolApproval only inside an AI conversation when an agent asks permission to run a tool or command; for a person confirming an action they started use ConfirmDialog.
- One-time authorization of a consequential action proposed by an agent: a production deployment, a purge, a command.
- An irreversible action (delete): add `confirmationPhrase`.
- Arguments the reader may want to correct first (a URL list, a limit): add `editable`.

## Do

- Title is a question naming the action and target; put tool and command names in backticks (code).
- Match the approve label to the title verb (`Deploy`, `Delete`) when it is not a generic tool call.
- Never pre-focus or pre-select Approve for a risky action.
- Do not leave a request pending forever: expire it (`status="expired"`) and have the assistant say nothing ran.
- After Deny, the assistant acknowledges in the conversation ("Skipping that step.").
- With `editable`, bind `v-model` to the arguments as formatted JSON, set `invalid` while they do not parse, and run the call with the `input` that `approve` carries.
- Keep `editable` off for irreversible actions unless the edit is the point: the phrase confirms the target, the edit can change it.

## Don’t

- Tools already trusted for the session → record the call with `tool-call`, do not ask again.
- A destructive action the reader started themselves in the UI → `confirm-dialog`.
- A form → this card only approves or denies.

## Related

- `tool-call` — the record of the call after it is approved (or `denied`).
- `confirm-dialog` — confirmation of the reader's own destructive action.
- `code-block`, `key-value-list` — what will run, in the body.
- `chat-message` — the assistant acknowledges the decision in the next message.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The question, naming the action: ``Allow `npm test`?``, `Approve deployment to production?`. Backticks render as code. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One or two sentences on what will happen and to what; backticks render as code. |
| `status` | `'pending' \| 'approved' \| 'denied' \| 'expired'` | `'pending'` | false | `pending` asks; `approved`, `denied` and `expired` replace the buttons with the outcome in text. |
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'danger'` | `'primary'` | false | `danger` for an action that cannot be undone: the approve button turns destructive. |
| `confirmationPhrase` | `string` | `''` | false | A word the reader must type before Approve enables, for irreversible actions (the resource name). Empty asks for no typing. |
| `approveLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the approve button, the verb of the title (`Deploy`, `Delete`). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Approve`). |
| `denyLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the deny button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Deny`). |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | A decision is being sent; both buttons are inert and Approve shows its loading state. |
| `editable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Lets the reader edit the call's input in a code field before approving; the edit comes back through `v-model` and `approve`. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The edited input cannot be used (it does not parse): the field shows an error and Approve stays disabled. Has no effect without `editable`. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `approve` | `(event: MouseEvent, input: string)` |  |
| `deny` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | What exactly will run: a `CodeBlock`, or `KeyValueList` with parameters. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./tool-approval"`; types `ToolApprovalStatus`, `ToolApprovalVariant`.
Composed DS components: `button`, `status-indicator`; for `editable`, `field-root`, `textarea` and `field-error` under a plain `<label>` (no `field-label`, to keep its `Hint` out of the bundle); the title and description reuse
`StreamingResponse`'s inline renderer so backticks render as code (no HTML). Exposes `focus()`._

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The call's arguments as text (usually JSON); the reader edits them with `editable`. Unbound, local and empty. |

## States

- `data-status` mirrors `status`; `data-variant`.
- `pending`: phrase field (when `confirmationPhrase`; the phrase in its label is inline code), Deny (outlined) and Approve (primary, or danger with `variant="danger"`); Approve disabled until the phrase matches. Once the typed text is as long as the phrase and still differs, the field is `aria-invalid` with a `FieldError` (`toolApproval.phraseMismatch`).
- `editable` + `pending`: a monospace `Textarea` labelled `Arguments` under the body, growing to 12 lines, then scrolling; disabled while `loading`.
- `invalid` (with `editable` + `pending`): the field is `aria-invalid` with its `FieldError`; Approve is disabled (with `confirmationPhrase`, it also needs the phrase).
- `editable` once resolved: the field stays `readonly` as the record of the arguments that ran.
- `approved` (success), `denied` (warning), `expired` (neutral): a `StatusIndicator` with the outcome; the typed phrase resets when the card returns to `pending`. When the status leaves `pending` while focus was inside the card (or on the page body), focus moves to the heading so it never falls to the page.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: buttons and the phrase input show `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`; the heading shows a ring when `focus()` moves focus to it.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` through the body, the arguments field (with `editable`), the phrase field, Deny, Approve; in the arguments field `Enter` adds a line and `Tab` leaves it; `Enter` / `Space` activate Deny and Approve. No focus trap, no initial focus (Cloudscape: the one-time decision card is not a dialog).
- ARIA: `role="group"` labelled by its `h3` title and described by the description; both fields have visible `<label>`s; the invalid arguments field and a mismatched phrase field are `aria-invalid` and described by their `FieldError` (`role="alert"`); the phrase field sets `autocapitalize="off"`; a polite live region announces the outcome; outcomes are text, never color alone.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import KeyValueList from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-list'
  import ToolApproval from '@aziontech/webkit/tool-approval'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const status = ref('pending')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <ToolApproval
      title="Allow `azion deploy --env production`?"
      description="Deploys the current build of storefront to production. The previous version stays available for rollback."
      approve-label="Deploy"
      :status="status"
      @approve="status = 'approved'"
      @deny="status = 'denied'"
    >
      <KeyValueList aria-label="Command to run">
        <KeyValueList.Item label="Command">
          <code
            class="rounded-(--shape-control) bg-(--bg-surface-raised) px-(--spacing-xs) py-(--spacing-2xs) text-body-code-sm [overflow-wrap:break-word] text-(--text-default)"
            >azion deploy <span class="whitespace-nowrap">--env production</span>{{ ' '
            }}<span class="whitespace-nowrap">--workload storefront</span></code
          >
        </KeyValueList.Item>
        <KeyValueList.Item label="Environment">production</KeyValueList.Item>
        <KeyValueList.Item label="Workload">storefront</KeyValueList.Item>
      </KeyValueList>
    </ToolApproval>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/tool-call.md -->

# Tool Call

> One tool or command the agent invoked, shown in the conversation (AI Elements Tool, Cloudscape progressive steps): a row with the tool name in code font, an optional plain description, and a status (`Waiting`, `Preparing…`, `Running…`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Canceled`, `Denied`), with the call's input and output in a collapsible panel. It is the record of what the agent did; authorization before it runs is `ToolApproval`.

- Import: `import ToolCall from '@aziontech/webkit/tool-call'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- An agent calls a tool, an MCP server, an API or a CLI command during a response, and the reader should see what ran and what came back.

## Do

- Name the tool exactly as it is (`list_workloads`) and describe it in plain words (`Listing your workloads`).
- Collapse details by default; open them on error so the reader sees why.
- Redact secrets from inputs and outputs.
- Map an SDK's states: arguments arriving → `streaming`; executing → `running`; awaiting approval → `pending`; result → `success`; failure → `error`; stopped by the reader (outcome cancelled) → `canceled`; approval refused (outcome denied) → `denied`.

## Don’t

- Asking the reader to allow a call → `tool-approval` (then a `tool-call` records it).
- The model's reasoning → `reasoning`.
- A long-running job outside a chat → `progress` / `status-indicator` on the resource.

## Related

- `tool-approval` — the authorization step before a sensitive call.
- `status-indicator` — the status the row shows.
- `code-block`, `key-value-list` — what goes in the input and output slots.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `—` | true | The tool or command identifier, shown in code font (`list_workloads`). |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | What the call does in the reader's words (`Listing your workloads`). Empty shows only the name. |
| `status` | `'pending' \| 'streaming' \| 'running' \| 'success' \| 'error' \| 'canceled' \| 'denied'` | `'running'` | false | `pending` waits for authorization, `streaming` receives its arguments, `running` is in flight, then `success`, `error`, `canceled` (stopped before it finished) or `denied` (the reader refused it). |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled; details start collapsed. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | — | The parameters the tool is called with (`CodeBlock`, `KeyValueList`). |
| `output` | — | What the tool returned, or the error it failed with. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./tool-call"`; type `ToolCallStatus`. Composed DS components: `status-indicator`._

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Details expanded or collapsed. Unbound, the state is local and starts from `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- `data-status` mirrors `status`; `data-state="open|closed"` only when a slot makes it expandable.
- Status mapping: `pending` neutral, `streaming` neutral with spinner (`Preparing…`), `running` info with spinner (`Running…`), `success` success, `error` danger, `canceled` neutral, `denied` warning. Every status is distinct in text, never by color or spinner alone.
- Without `input` / `output` the row is static (no button).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the trigger.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` to the trigger, `Enter` / `Space` toggles the details.
- ARIA: the trigger is a `button` with `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`; the status is a `StatusIndicator` inside a `role="status"` region the ToolCall owns (StatusIndicator itself is not live), so a change from Preparing to Running to Completed (or Canceled) is announced; Input and Output are `section`s labelled by their `h4`.
- Status is conveyed in text, never by color alone.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>

</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--spacing-xs)">
    <ToolCall
      name="purge_urls"
      title="Purging one URL"
      status="pending"
    />
    <ToolCall
      name="create_cache_rule"
      title="Creating a cache rule for images"
      status="streaming"
    />
    <ToolCall
      name="list_workloads"
      title="Listing your workloads"
      status="running"
    />
    <ToolCall
      name="get_cache_settings"
      title="Reading the cache settings of storefront"
      status="success"
    />
    <ToolCall
      name="get_metrics"
      title="Reading the error rate"
      status="error"
    />
    <ToolCall
      name="list_certificates"
      title="Listing your certificates"
      status="canceled"
    />
    <ToolCall
      name="delete_domain"
      title="Deleting www.example.com"

    />
  </div>

# Bar List

> Use BarList for a ranked top-N breakdown inside a chart card; a list of mixed rows with actions is Item rows. A ranked list of named values: each row is a tinted bar whose length is the value against the largest one, with the name inside the bar and the formatted value in a right-aligned column. It reads as a list, not a chart — no axes, no grid — so it suits top-N breakdowns inside a card, where a horizontal `chart` would spend its width on an axis gutter.

- Import: `import BarList from '@aziontech/webkit/bar-list'`
- Category: chart · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Top-N breakdowns inside a card: top paths, top countries, top user agents, top rules triggered.
- A ranking where the name matters as much as the size, and names are long enough to need the bar's full width.
- Rows that lead somewhere — a filtered view of that path or country — via `href` or `item-click`.

## Do

- Keep it to about ten rows; fold the tail into an "Other" row in the data rather than scrolling.
- Leave `sort` on `descending` for rankings; use `none` only when the order itself carries meaning (pipeline steps, weekdays).
- Pass the same `formatValue` as the chart beside it so a number reads the same in both.
- Give interactive rows a destination the user expects — a filtered view of that item — not a detail drawer of the whole list.

## Don’t

- Several series per category, or values over time → use `chart`.
- A share of a whole where the parts sum to 100% → use `donut-chart`.
- One value against a limit (quota, usage) → use `progress`.

## Related

- `chart` — horizontal bars with an axis, for comparing several series per category.
- `donut-chart` — the share view of the same breakdown when the parts sum to a whole.
- `chart-card` — the box a BarList sits in on a dashboard.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `BarListItem[]` | `[]` | false | Rows to rank; each item is `{ id?: string; name: string; value: number; href?: string }`. An item with `href` renders as a link. |
| `sort` | `'descending' \| 'ascending' \| 'none'` | `'descending'` | false | Row order; `none` keeps the order of `items`. |
| `color` | `ChartColor` | `1` | false | Hue of the bars: a categorical slot (1–8), `other`, or a status. The fill is that hue tinted over the surface. |
| `clickable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders rows without an `href` as buttons that emit `item-click`. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | `formatCompact` | false | Formats the value column. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders Skeleton rows in place of the list. |
| `refetching` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Holds the previous rows at reduced opacity while new data loads (the same as `chart`). |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Error message; when set, the list renders an error state in an `alert` region instead of rows: a bordered small `EmptyState` with the error mark, `barList.errorTitle` and the message (the `error` slot replaces it). |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the empty state shown when `items` is empty. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No data available`). |
| `emptyDescription` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting line under the empty title: why the list is empty, or what to do next. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item-click` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: BarListItem)` | A row activated — a clickable row, or a link row (the link still navigates). `item` is the consumer's own item object. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the default `EmptyState` shown when `items` is empty. |
| `empty-actions` | — | Actions under the default empty state (a Clear filters or Retry). |
| `error` | — | Replaces the default error state shown while `error` is set. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` (interactive rows only), `loading` (Skeleton rows), `refetching` (previous rows at 60% opacity), `error` (error state in an `alert` region), `empty` (`EmptyState`). Precedence: loading, then error, then empty.
- `data-loading` mirrors `loading`; `data-refetching` mirrors `refetching`; `data-error` is set while an error shows
- `data-interactive` on a row that is a link or a button
- Bar width: `value / max`, at least 2% when the value is above zero, 0 when it is zero

- Its root carries `data-plain-ground`: it is content that must sit on a plain ground, so a `Texture` beside it hides itself, and the texture-backdrop check blocks placing it on a textured band (a texture is a backdrop for text only, RV-T2-1).

## Accessibility

- The root is an `<ol>` named by `ariaLabel`; each row is an `<li>` whose text reads "name, value" in order. The bar is decorative.
- A link row is a native `<a>`; a clickable row is a native `<button>`; a static row is neither, and is not focusable.
- Keyboard map: Tab moves between interactive rows; Enter activates (Space too on buttons).
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-1 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-surface)` on interactive rows (the offset takes the surface color, so it never shows as a white gap in the dark theme).
- `aria-busy` on the root while `loading` or `refetching`.
- Name and value text clear 4.5:1 on the tinted fill and on the bare surface in both themes.
- The bar is underlined by a 2px rule in the full hue along its bottom edge (a solid mark, APCA Lc 30 or more on the surface in both themes), so the length reads in dark, where the tint alone stays under the mark target, and the rule never crosses the row label the way an inline-end cap did on short bars. The name and the value are `dir="auto"`, so a path or a number keeps its own order in right-to-left.
- Interactive rows are 32px tall and full width; a transparent hit area (`before:` pseudo-element, 4px above and below) makes the pointer target 40px without changing the look.
- Forced colors: the bar fill keeps its colour (`forced-color-adjust: none`); forced to `Canvas` it vanished and left only the labels (`src/test/forced-colors-charts.test.ts`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import BarList from '@aziontech/webkit/bar-list'

  const items = [
    { name: '/home', value: 843 },
    { name: '/documentation', value: 384 },
    { name: '/blocks', value: 108 },
    { name: '/imprint', value: 46 },
    { name: '/cancellation', value: 3 }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <BarList
      aria-label="Top paths"
      :items="items"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/bar-list.md](components/bar-list.md).

# Chart

> A cartesian chart — lines, areas, stacked areas, bars, mixed bars and lines, and scatter dots over one category axis — composed from parts the consumer places by hand. The root owns the data model (series + labels), the scales, the hover/keyboard state and the loading / empty / error surface; each part (`Chart.Grid`, `Chart.Axis`, `Chart.Brush`, `Chart.Line`, `Chart.Area`, `Chart.Bar`, `Chart.Scatter`, `Chart.Reference`, `Chart.Crosshair`, `Chart.Tooltip`, `Chart.Legend`) reads that state through context, so the consumer wires nothing. Rendering is in-house SVG and every color comes from the `--chart-*` role, so a chart re-themes with no per-theme code and adds no charting dependency.

- Import: `import ChartRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/chart-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Chart from '@aziontech/webkit/chart'`
- Category: chart · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A measure over time — requests, threats, bandwidth per bucket — as one or more lines or areas.
- Comparing magnitudes across ordered categories — top countries, attack families — as vertical or horizontal bars.
- Parts of a total over time — allowed / blocked / logged — as stacked areas or stacked bars.
- Any chart that must read the same as Azion Console Real-Time Metrics: crosshair, one tooltip listing every series, legend toggles, totals.
- Two measures of one unit where one is the total and one a part — requests as bars, cached requests as a line (mixed).
- How one measure spreads against another — response time by object size — as scatter dots on a `linear` label scale.
- A volume histogram that filters a log or a table to a time span: add `Chart.Brush` and read `v-model:range`.
- A measure against the limit it must stay under or the range it should stay in — a quota, an SLO, an alert threshold, a normal band: add `Chart.Reference` with a `value` (a line) or `from` and `to` (a band).

## Do

- Pass series in a stable order: the slot follows the series position, so color follows the entity. A filter that hides a series keeps the others' colors.
- Keep one value axis. Index two measures to a common base or split them into two charts.
- Let the legend carry identity for two or more series; a single series needs no legend, its title names it.
- Leave `color` unset by default: each series takes the next categorical slot (`--chart-series-1` … `-8`) in order, and the palette follows the theme. Most series name an entity (a host, a country, a metric), not a state.
- Set a status `color` only when the series itself means a state, and keep it to that series: blocked requests or an error rate take `color: 'danger'`, while the series around it keep their categorical slots. Never reuse a status color as series 4.
- Color a series that counts one severity level with `color: 'severity-critical'` (`-high`, `-medium`, `-low`, `-info`) so stacked bars and legends match the `SeverityTag` in the table below the chart.
- Keep filters and the time range in one row above the dashboard, never inside a chart.
- While data reloads, set `refetching` so the previous marks hold at reduced opacity instead of flashing a skeleton. Only the SVG marks dim (`data-[refetching]:[&_svg]:opacity-60`); legend values and other text stay at full contrast, because text at 60% opacity drops `--text-muted` under 4.5:1 (2.78:1 light, 3.14:1 dark).
- Place `Chart.Brush` before the marks so the selection band sits under them. The page owns what a range means: bind `range` to `null` and filter on `update:range` when the data changes with the selection.
- Use `labelScale="linear"` only with numeric or Date labels; keep `category` for buckets that are evenly spaced.
- Name every `Chart.Reference` with a `label` (`SLO 300 ms`, `Quota`): the label is drawn at the inline end of the line and read in the chart summary, so the limit never rests on a dashed line alone. Color it with a `severity` only when crossing it means that state (`danger` for a hard limit, `warning` for an alert threshold); a plain target stays `neutral`. Place a labelled `Chart.Reference` after the series it frames: parts paint in order, so the label's canvas halo then sits over the line instead of under it, and the band's light tint does not hide the line.
- Place a band (`from` + `to`) before the marks so it sits under them, and a line after the marks so it stays readable over them.
- Draw event volume over contiguous time buckets (a log's histogram, requests per minute) with `Chart.Bar type="histogram"`: solid columns that touch, segments without gaps, the tallest column at the top. Keep the default bars for separate categories that are compared one against another.

## Don’t

- A single headline number with a delta → use `stat-tile`.
- Share of a small whole (six slices or fewer) with the total in the center → use `donut-chart`.
- More than about seven classes that all carry meaning → use `table`; color stops separating past the eight series slots.
- Two measures on different scales → two charts side by side; this component never draws a second value axis.
- One reading against its range (CPU, cache hit ratio) → use `gauge-chart`.
- Values by country or location → use `map-chart`.

## Related

- `chart-card` — the box a dashboard chart sits in: title, description, controls, drag and resize.
- `donut-chart` — part-to-whole at a glance, sharing this chart's palette, legend and states.
- `stat-tile` — one figure with a delta and a sparkline, for a KPI row above the charts.
- `table` — the exact numbers; a chart's own table view is the accessible twin, a `table` is the primary surface.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `series` | `ChartSeries[]` | `[]` | false | Series to plot. The first eight take the fixed categorical slots in order; the rest fold into Other. |
| `labels` | `ChartLabel[]` | `[]` | false | One category label per index: a string, a number, or a Date. |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | false | Value axis direction. Horizontal lays categories down the side, for ordered bars. |
| `labelScale` | `'category' \| 'linear'` | `'category'` | false | How categories sit along their axis. `linear` places numeric or Date labels by value, for scatter plots and uneven time buckets. |
| `min` | `number` | `0` | false | Floor of the value axis. Marks grow from one baseline. |
| `max` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Ceiling of the value axis. When absent, the nice ceiling of the visible data. |
| `cap` | `number` | `8` | false | Series kept before the rest fold into Other. |
| `otherLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Name of the folded series. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Other`). |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | `formatCompact` | false | Formats ticks, tooltip values and legend totals. |
| `formatLabel` | `(label: ChartLabel) => string` | `formatLabel` | false | Formats category labels on the axis and in the tooltip. |
| `timeZone` | `string` | `''` | false | IANA time zone the default label format prints Date labels in. Empty prints UTC on the server and in the first client render, then the runtime's zone. |
| `height` | `number` | `240` | false | Minimum plot height in pixels; the plot grows to fill a taller container. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders a Skeleton sized to the plot and suppresses interaction. |
| `refetching` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Holds the previous render at reduced opacity while new data loads. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Error message; when set, the plot renders a danger Alert instead of marks. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the empty state shown when no series has a value. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No data available`). |
| `emptyDescription` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting line under the empty title: why the range is empty, or what to do next. |
| `tableView` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the data table in place of the marks. The table is always present for assistive tech. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the chart when it is not inside a ChartCard with a title. |
| `activeIndex` | `number \| null` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:activeIndex`). |
| `hiddenSeries` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:hiddenSeries`). |
| `range` | `ChartRange \| null` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:range`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `point-click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, point: ChartPoint)` | Click or tap on the plot, or Enter / Space on the focused chart, at the active index (a tap with no active index uses the point under the finger). `point` carries the index, the label and every visible series value. |
| `legend-toggle` | `(event: MouseEvent, series: ChartSeries)` | A legend entry toggled; `series` is the consumer's own series object. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The parts: Grid, Axis, Brush, Line, Area, Bar, Scatter, Reference, Crosshair, Tooltip, Legend, in paint order. |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the default EmptyState. |
| `empty-actions` | — | Actions under the default EmptyState, such as a Clear filters button or a setup link. Ignored when `empty` replaces it. |
| `error` | — | Replaces the default danger Alert. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-area`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-axis`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-bar`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-brush`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-crosshair`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-grid`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-legend`
