# Code Block

> Use CodeBlock to show code, config or JSON the person reads or copies, including read-only diffs (a tab's `original`); for code the person edits use CodeEditor, and for build, deploy or runtime log lines use LogViewer. Read-only code viewer for docs, API examples, and configuration previews. Supports four Figma-documented layouts that share one monolithic shell: 1. **Language switcher** ([4567:33761](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-33761)) — tabbed snippets with a sliding pill, optional filename bar, syntax highlighting, and copy. 2. **Show filename** ([4567:30198](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-30198)) — single snippet with a raised filename bar (language icon + name), no tabs. 3. **Diff** ([4567:29012](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-29012)) — per-line added/removed markers (`+`/`-`), semantic row backgrounds, and a 2 px leading bar; no tabs or filename bar. 4. **Highlighted line** ([4567:31473](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-31473)) — one active line with info background and leading bar; no tabs or filename bar. Two more regions serve docs: a **label header** — a 40 px bar naming the block (`</>` + "Shell", "JavaScript", from the active tab's label or the language's readable name, or `title`) when `showLabel` is on and there is no tab strip or filename bar — and the **output** type (`type="output"`): what a command prints, drawn flat in `--text-muted` on `--bg-canvas` under an "Output" label, with no copy control by default. A command block and its output are always two blocks. The **label header holds the copy control** at its end, and so does the tab strip, or the filename bar when there is one, so the control never covers the first lines of code on a phone (`data-copy-gutter` marks the root only while the block has no header at all and the copy sits in a column of its own at the end of the code instead, so no line runs under it) and is `sticky` at the top of the nearest scroller, so a long block keeps its language and copy in view. Its divider shows only when `bordered`; unbordered, header and code share one fill (the `StreamingResponse` look). The other regions render conditionally from tab data. Tab header appears when `tabs.length > 1`. Filename bar appears when the active tab sets `fileName`. Diff and highlight decorations come from `lineChanges` and `highlightedLine` on the active tab. **Syntax highlighting** is driven by the active tab's `language` and resolves to one of these tokenisers, all of which emit the same seven token types (`keyword`, `string`, `function`, `type`, `punctuation`, `identifier`, `comment`) so every language shares the one `--code-syntax-*` palette:

- Import: `import CodeBlock from '@aziontech/webkit/code-block'`
- Category: code · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Read-only code in docs, API examples or configuration previews that readers copy from.
- The same snippet in several languages, switched by tabs (one `tabs` entry per language).
- Showing a change as a diff (`lineChanges`) or pointing at one line (`highlightedLine`) on the active tab.
- Showing what changed between two versions of a file — a configuration before and after a deploy, the code a release replaces — by passing the previous version as the tab's `original`: the block computes the line diff itself and draws it unified or side by side (`diffView`).

## Do

- Put the source on each tab's `code`. There is no top-level `code` prop, and a tab without a `value` or a `code` is dropped.
- Set `language` on every tab. Only JavaScript/TypeScript, shell, HCL, GraphQL and Markdown are tokenised; anything else renders as flat text.
- Use `default-value` for the initial tab, and `v-model` only when something outside the block must follow the selected tab.
- Prefer `original` to a hand-written `lineChanges` list whenever both versions are at hand: the diff stays right when either version changes. Keep `unified` in narrow columns and use `split` where the block has room for two columns of code.
- Set `:copyable="false"` on decorative blocks, and `:bordered="false"` when the block sits inside a surface that already frames it.
- Keep `animate-lines` for marketing layouts; leave it off in docs and console screens.
- Do: keep a command block to what the reader runs — the copy control copies exactly that. Put what it prints in a second block with `type="output"` (or in prose).
- Don't: write expected output into the command, as a `# HTTP/2 200` comment or as unprompted lines after a `$ ` prompt — the reader pastes it into the terminal. The `webkit/no-output-in-command` lint warns on it.
- Do: turn `show-label` on in docs (`DocCodeGroup` does by default) so every block is titled with its language; set `title` only when the language name is not the right title.

## Don’t

- The content is build or deploy output with timestamps and log levels → use `log-viewer`.
- It is a marketing band that pairs a claim with its code → use `feature-scroll-section` with code items.
- It is a terminal session of CLI commands on a product page → use `cli-terminal-section`.
- You only need to copy one short value (a token, an ID) without showing a block → use `copy-button`.
- The reader edits the new version beside the old one → use `code-editor` in diff mode. A read-only diff is always this block with `original`, never a read-only code editor.

## Related

- `copy-button` — the copy control CodeBlock embeds; use it alone for one-line values.
- `code-editor` — the editable surface; its diff mode is for editing beside an original, while a read-only diff is this block.
- `log-viewer` — terminal-style viewer for CI and deploy logs.
- `feature-scroll-section` — page section whose steps can each pin a code sample (`code`).
- `scroll-area` — the scroll container the code region runs in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tabs` | `CodeBlockTab[]` | `[]` | false | Tab definitions with label, value, code, and optional language, filename, diff, or highlight metadata. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Initial active tab when uncontrolled. |
| `code` | `string` | `''` | false | Code of a single snippet, used when `tabs` is empty. |
| `language` | `string` | `''` | false | Language of the single `code` snippet (highlighting and the label header). |
| `showLineNumbers` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows a fixed-width gutter with zero-padded line numbers before each code line (the same name as `code-editor`). |
| `copyAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the copy control (forwarded to CopyButton's aria-label). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copy code`). |
| `copyable` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Shows the copy control. Unset, a `code` block shows it and an `output` block does not; turn it off for a decorative block nobody copies from. |
| `type` | `'code' \| 'output'` | `'code'` | false | What the block holds: `code` the reader runs or reads, or `output` — what a command prints — drawn flat and muted under an "Output" label, without a copy control. |
| `showLabel` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a header naming the block when there is no tab strip or file name: the active tab's label, else the language's readable name (Shell, JavaScript). Docs blocks show it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the label header; empty uses the tab label or the language name, or "Output" for an `output` block. |
| `animateLines` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Staggered line entrance for website layouts: each line slides from `-8px` with opacity `0 → 1`, `40ms` apart. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draw the outer card border around the block. On by default; set `:bordered="false"` to render the block flush when it sits inside a surface that already frames it. Internal dividers (tab header, filename bar) are unaffected; the label header's divider goes with the border. |
| `diffView` | `'unified' \| 'split'` | `'unified'` | false | How a tab with an `original` draws the diff the block computes: `unified` (one column) or `split` (side by side). |
| `modelValue` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy` | `(event: MouseEvent, code: string)` | Fires after the active tab code is copied to the clipboard. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tab-icon` | { tab: CodeBlockTab } | Leading mark before a tab's label in the tab strip; nothing renders when it is not filled. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | Active tab `value` via `defineModel`. While unbound (`undefined`) the block is uncontrolled: it starts at `defaultValue`, else the first tab. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible` on tabs and copy control
- `data-state` on tabs: `active` | `inactive`; the active tab's text colour switches on `data-[state=active]:` in the tab's flat class, never a `:class` ternary
- `data-state` on code lines: `default` | `added` | `removed` | `highlighted`; in the split view a side with no line opposite a change is `empty` (`var(--bg-canvas)`)
- `data-split` on the panel when the active tab with an `original` draws side by side. A `split` diff draws unified while the content is narrower than 640px (an unmeasured block, as in the server render, draws split)
- `data-disabled` not used (tabs are not disabled in v2)
- `data-copy-gutter` on the root while the copy control floats over the code (no label header, tab strip or filename bar); the scroll area and every line keep its width free
- `data-type` on the root: `code` | `output`; `output` paints the shell `--bg-canvas` and every line flat in `--text-muted`

#### Layout rules (derived from Figma)

| Region | Visible when |
| --- | --- |
| Tab header (`CodeBlockHeader`, 40 px strip: a 32 px tab over a 4 px inset) | `tabs.length > 1` |
| Filename bar (`FileName`, 40 px) | active tab has `fileName` |
| Label header (40 px, `az az-code` / `az az-align-left` + label, copy at the end, sticky) | no tab strip, no `fileName`, and `showLabel`, `title` or `type="output"` |
| Diff gutter (`+`/`-` + 8 px spacer on unchanged lines) | active tab `lineChanges.length > 0`, or the active tab has an `original` |
| Unified diff (removed lines from `original` before the added lines of `code` in each change, numbered on their own side) | active tab has an `original` and `diffView="unified"` |
| Split diff (two columns, Original and Modified, rows aligned, a change paired line for line) | active tab has an `original` and `diffView="split"` |
| Line highlight (info background + 2 px leading bar) | active tab `highlightedLine` is set |

When only one tab is provided and it has no `fileName`, the shell is code content + copy only (minimal block). With a tab strip or a filename bar the copy control (`variant="ghost"` `size="small"`) sits at the end of that header row, the filename bar first.

Code content scrolls inside `@aziontech/webkit/scroll-area` (`orientation="both"`, capped at a `320 px` max height so shorter snippets fit their content and taller ones scroll). Lines never wrap (`whitespace-pre`); on narrow viewports the scroll region grows horizontally so long lines stay on one row.

**The shell is fluid: it takes the width its container gives it and never grows past it.** Long lines are a scroll, never a wider block — so the root is a size container (`@container`, i.e. inline-size containment) and its code width is invisible to the layout above it. Without that, the block's intrinsic width leaks upward: an `auto`-sized grid track or flex row (a one-column `grid` on mobile, a `md:grid-cols-2` panel below its breakpoint) sizes itself to the widest code line and the block overflows the viewport instead of scrolling — a consumer's `min-w-0` on the wrapper cannot fix it, because `min-width` is a floor on the intrinsic contribution, not a cap. In a block with no header, the copy control (a `CopyButton`, `variant="outline"` `size="small"`) is absolutely positioned on the non-scrolling content shell (`__content`) so it stays pinned top-right while lines scroll. **On a single-line block it centres on that row instead** (`data-single-line` on the anchor): the shell is 44 px, the control 28 px, so the `--spacing-sm` top inset would leave it 4 px below the line's own centre. Every line reserves the control's full footprint on its right (`pr-11` = 28 px control + its 12 px inset), so a long line always scrolls clear of it rather than under it. With `copyable` off (`data-copyable` absent on the root) the control is not rendered and lines reserve only `--spacing-sm` on their right.

- Computed diff: the common head and tail are trimmed, then the middle runs the Myers line diff; past 1,000 edits it falls back to the whole middle removed then added, so a rewrite stays linear. A 5,000-line pair with a few hundred edits diffs in a few milliseconds.

- Consumer attributes land on the root (`v-bind="$attrs"`), so a page-JSON scene can mark it `data-plain-ground` (RV-T2-1).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses tabs and copy; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`/`Home`/`End` move between tabs; `Enter`/`Space` activates tab; copy uses `Enter`/`Space` on the CopyButton (native `<button>`); when focus is in the code scroll region, `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`PageUp`/`PageDown`/`Home`/`End` scroll vertically and `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` scroll horizontally via ScrollArea.
- ARIA: tab list uses `role="tablist"` when visible; tabs use `role="tab"` with `aria-selected`; panel uses `role="tabpanel"` with `aria-labelledby`. Tab and panel ids come from `useId()` (`<uid>-tab-<index>`, one `<uid>-panel`), so two tabbed blocks on one page never share an id and a tab value with spaces is still a valid id; only the selected tab carries `aria-controls`, pointing at the one rendered panel; copy uses CopyButton `ariaLabel` (forwarded to its inner IconButton); diff `+`/`-` markers are `aria-hidden="true"` and every added or removed line also carries a visually hidden `Added` / `Removed` so the change is read, not only seen. In the split view each column is a named `group` (`Original`, `Modified`) and a focusable scroll region (`tabindex="0"`, the same focus ring) so its long lines scroll from the keyboard.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for code text on surface, including syntax token colors and diff/highlight row backgrounds in light and dark. Row backgrounds for `added`, `removed` and `highlighted` are the feedback fills at 40% (`bg-(--success)/40`, `bg-(--danger)/40`, `bg-(--info)/40`): at full strength the light fills (`--danger` `#F3A5A5`, `--info` `#99C9FF`) put the line numbers and the `function` and `type` syntax colours under 4.5:1 (3.93:1 for a line number on a removed row); at 40% every syntax colour clears 4.5:1 in light and dark (the lowest, the light `function` orange `#B03C02` on a removed row, is 4.6:1).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on indicator and panel motion.
- When `animateLines` is enabled, line motion is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion` (lines render fully visible immediately).
- Copy control uses CopyButton `size="small"` (28×28 px).

## Examples

### Default


# Code Editor

> Use CodeEditor only when the person edits the code (its diff mode is for editing one side beside the original); to show code, config or JSON the person reads or copies, including read-only diffs, use CodeBlock, and for build, deploy or runtime log lines use LogViewer. An editable code surface with line numbers, diagnostics and a read-only and a diff mode. It is a plain-text editor first: a monospace textarea with a line-number gutter that works on the server, without JavaScript and on any device. When the app passes a `loader` (a function that wires Monaco's workers and returns `import('monaco-editor')`), Monaco is loaded lazily, painted with the design tokens and takes over the same value, markers and options; until it loads, or if it fails, the plain editor stays in place. It differs from `code-block`, which only shows code.

- Import: `import CodeEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/code-editor'`
- Category: code · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Editing a function, a script, a SQL query, a JSON or YAML document inside the product.
- Editing code beside the version it changes (diff mode): the saved version stays on the left, read-only, and the edit happens on the right, for example a function changed before a deploy.
- Code that the server validates: the diagnostics come back as `markers` and show on their lines and in a list.
- A JSON document with a known shape (a function's argument schema, a configuration file): pass its JSON Schema as `schema` and Monaco checks the document against it as the user types.
- A read-only view of code that still needs the editor's navigation (find, folding) once Monaco is loaded.

## Do

- Wrap it in a `Field` with a visible label, or give it an `ariaLabel`; the label names the textarea and the Monaco editor.
- Pass `loader` from the app so Monaco is code-split and never part of the WebKit bundle. The loader sets `MonacoEnvironment.getWorker` before it returns `import('monaco-editor')`; without workers Monaco has no language services. With `monaco-editor` 0.56 and later under Vite the worker imports are `monaco-editor/editor/editor.worker?worker` and `monaco-editor/languages/features/<json|css|html|typescript>/<name>.worker?worker` (`ts.worker` serves `javascript` too); the old `monaco-editor/esm/vs/...?worker` paths fail the build. Copy `loadMonaco` from the Usage block or the `Monaco` example.
- Set `padLineNumbers` on a full-page code editor (`fill`, a function's Code or Arguments document), as the console does (01, 02…); leave it off on a small editor inside a form.
- Function calls are coloured for you (JavaScript and TypeScript, with `--code-syntax-function`); do not register your own Monarch grammar for that.
- Send server diagnostics as `markers` with 1-based lines; keep each message one sentence.
- Pass a JSON Schema as `schema` for a JSON document with a known shape, and listen to `markers-change` to show the first problem in a `Field.Error`; keep `markers` for what only the server knows.
- Set `:bordered="false"` when the editor fills a pane that already frames it (a resizable pane, a full-page function editor, a drawer body); keep the default frame inside a form.
- Give the editor a fixed `height`, or `fill` inside a flex column that has its own height; never let it grow with the content.
- Use `readonly` for code the user may read and select but not change; use `disabled` only when the whole form is locked.
- In diff mode, `original` is the left side and `v-model` the right side, which stays editable. A diff nobody edits is a `code-block` with `original`, which marks every added and removed line without loading an editor.

## Don’t

- Showing a snippet to copy, with tabs and a file name → use `code-block`.
- Showing a read-only change between two versions (what a release or a revert changes, a configuration before and after) → use `code-block` with the tab's `original`; diff mode is for editing beside the original, not for reviewing a change nobody edits.
- A one-line value such as a header, a regex or a path → use `input` inside a `field`.
- Free prose or a description → use `textarea`.
- A stream of log lines → use `log-viewer`.
- A form generated from a JSON schema → use `schema-form` (the arguments tab of a function pairs both).
- In a docs Markdown page or the site's page JSON. CodeEditor is app-only (decision RV-C2-1, rule `webkit-content-channels`): the person edits code in it, so it has no `DocMarkdown` tag and no page JSON entry. A docs page shows code as a code fence (`DocCodeGroup`); the site uses `CodeBlock`.

## Related

- `code-block` — read-only snippets with copy; same syntax colour tokens.
- `textarea` — plain multi-line text; the fallback editor is built in its spirit but keeps code typography and a gutter.
- `field` — wraps the editor with a label, a description and an error; the editor reads id, `aria-describedby`, invalid and disabled from it.
- `toggle-group` — the document switch (Code / Arguments) placed in the `toolbar` slot.
- `log-viewer` — output of a run next to the editor.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | `string` | `'plaintext'` | false | Monaco language id (`javascript`, `typescript`, `json`, `sql`, `lua`, `yaml`…). The fallback ignores it. |
| `loader` | `() => Promise<CodeEditorMonaco>` | `undefined` | false | Loads Monaco lazily; without it the plain editor is the editor. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The code can be read, selected and copied but not changed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Locks the editor; it leaves the tab order. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Paints the danger border; also set by a surrounding `Field`. |
| `diff` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows `original` beside the value as a side-by-side diff. |
| `original` | `string` | `''` | false | The left side of the diff. |
| `markers` | `CodeEditorMarker[]` | `[]` | false | Diagnostics shown on their lines and in the problems list. |
| `height` | `string` | `'16rem'` | false | CSS height of the editing area. |
| `fill` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Fills a flex column instead of using `height`. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draws the frame: border, corner radius and an offset focus ring. Off, the editor sits flush in its pane. |
| `showLineNumbers` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the line-number gutter. |
| `padLineNumbers` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Zero-pads line numbers to two digits (01, 02…), as the console's full-page function and arguments editors do. |
| `path` | `string` | `''` | false | Model path for Monaco language services (`index.ts`, `args.json`). |
| `schema` | `Record<string, unknown>` | `undefined` | false | JSON Schema the value is checked against when `language` is `json` and Monaco is loaded. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name when no `Field` label names it. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` | `unknown` | Monaco mounted; the payload is the editor instance (for actions). |
| `load-error` | `unknown` | The loader rejected; the plain editor stays. |
| `markers-change` | `CodeEditorMarker[]` | The diagnostics Monaco's language services (JSON syntax and `schema`, TypeScript) put on the value, as markers sorted by line, each time they change. The `markers` prop is not echoed back; the plain editor never fires it. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toolbar` | — | A bar above the editing area: a document switch, the file name, a Format or Run action. |

## Sub-components

_none_ — monolithic. The gutter, the fallback textarea, the Monaco host, the toolbar bar and the problems list are fixed parts.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The code via `defineModel`. Updated on every edit, from the plain editor or from Monaco. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `focus-visible` (ring on the frame), `invalid`, `readonly`, `disabled`, `loading` (Monaco on the way, the plain editor is live)
- `data-mode`: `plain` | `loading` | `monaco` — which editor is live
- `data-invalid`, `data-readonly`, `data-disabled`, `data-diff`, `data-fill`, `data-bordered` mirror their props
- Borderless (`bordered` false): no border and no radius; the focus ring is drawn inset so a pane edge never clips it
- Each gutter line with a marker carries `data-severity` (`danger` | `warning` | `info`)
- Diff mode, plain editor: the gutters mark what changed with the same line diff `code-block` draws (`src/utils/line-diff.ts`, one model for both): a removed line carries `data-change="removed"` on the original side, an added line `data-change="added"` on the modified side, tinted `var(--danger)` / `var(--success)` with the `-contrast` number colour; Monaco's diff editor draws its own once it loads
- Load failure: the plain editor stays and a muted note says the full editor could not load

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the frame shows `focus-within:ring-2 ring-(--ring-color)` for both editors; a borderless editor draws the same ring inset.
- Keyboard map (plain editor): typing edits; `Tab` inserts two spaces and `Shift+Tab` removes them at the line start; `Escape` releases the trap so the next `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` leaves the editor (WCAG 2.1.2); the problems list buttons move the caret to the marker's line. Monaco runs in tab-focus mode by default, so `Tab` moves focus out unless the user toggles it with `Ctrl+M`.
- ARIA: the textarea is a native multi-line text box named by the `Field` label or `ariaLabel`; `aria-invalid`, `aria-readonly` and `aria-describedby` (the field's description plus the problems summary); the gutter is `aria-hidden`; the problems list is a named list; the problem count is a polite `status`.
- Diagnostics are never colour only: each one is a list item with its line and severity in text. A problem message wraps onto as many lines as it needs (never truncated), so the full fix text reads on a phone. Schema problems reach the user through Monaco's own hover and, when the app shows them, through `markers-change` in a `Field.Error`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1: code and line numbers use the code syntax tokens tuned for both themes.
- Forced colors: the frame keeps a system border and the gutter marker becomes a system glyph colour.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CodeEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/code-editor'
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const code = ref(`export default async function handler(request) {
  const url = new URL(request.url)
  const name = url.searchParams.get('name')
  return new Response(\`Hello, \${name}\`)
}
`)

  const markers = [
    { line: 3, severity: 'warning', message: 'name can be null; give it a default value.' },
    { line: 4, severity: 'info', message: 'Set a Content-Type header on the response.' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Field>
    <Field.Label>Function code</Field.Label>
    <CodeEditor
      v-model="code"
      language="javascript"
      :markers="markers"
      height="14rem"
    />
    <Field.Description>Runs on every request that reaches this function.</Field.Description>
  </Field>
</template>
```

# Log Viewer

> Composition-based terminal log viewer for CI/deploy output. **LogViewer** is the root shell and context provider; **`LogViewer.Header`**, **`LogViewer.Content`**, and **`LogViewer.Footer`** are composed as children so teams can reorder, omit, or replace the toolbar and footer without forking the log renderer. **`LogViewer.Steps`** shows a run with known steps (build, deploy, provisioning) as a pipeline: one collapsible step per phase, each with its own log, a Phased or Complete switch and an optional flush progress bar. Use LogViewer for build, deploy or runtime log lines, and LogViewer.Steps when the run has named steps; for code the person reads or copies use CodeBlock, and for code the person edits use CodeEditor.

- Import: `import LogViewerRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/log-viewer-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import LogViewer from '@aziontech/webkit/log-viewer'`
- Category: code · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Showing build, deploy or CI output as timestamped lines the reader can search, filter to warnings, and copy.
- A log shell whose toolbar and footer vary by screen — compose `LogViewerHeader`, `LogViewerContent` and `LogViewerFooter` in the order you need, or drop the ones you don't.
- A run log with levels (`debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`), such as what a function printed during a test run: set `level` on each line and `levels` on the root, and the header filters by level with a count per level.
- A log that is still loading from the server — set `loading` to show a spinner and `loading-label` in place of the body.
- A build or deploy run with known steps → `LogViewer.Steps` with one entry per step; every deploy-log block composes it instead of rebuilding the pipeline.

## Do

- Give every line a stable `id` and a `type` (`text`, `folder`, `framework-version`, `success`); the type drives the line's rendering. A warning is a `text` line with `level: 'warn'`; `level` drives the level toggles; the `warn` toggle is the warnings shortcut.
- For a run log, give each line a `level` and put the run offset (`120 ms`, `1.24 s`) in `time`; pass the levels the run can print as `levels` so every level is offered even when it has no line yet. Bind `v-model:level` when the app needs the chosen level.
- Bind `v-model:search` and `v-model:level` when the app needs the filter state; otherwise leave them unbound and the header manages them.
- Set `:bordered="false"` when the log sits inside a surface that already frames it (an accordion panel, a drawer).
- The copy control hides while `disabled` or `loading`, or when there is nothing to copy; listen to `@copy` for the copied text instead of reading the clipboard.
- Use the header's `start` / `end` / `search` slots and the footer's default slot to add actions, rather than rebuilding the toolbar.

## Don’t

- Static, read-only code or configuration snippets → use `code-block`.
- An animated terminal session on a marketing page → use `cli-terminal-section`.
- Rows of structured records with columns, sorting or paging → use `table`.
- The steps of a form or setup the person moves through (no log under each step) → use `stepper`.
- The timed spans of one request or invocation → use `trace`.
- In a docs Markdown page or the site's page JSON. LogViewer is app-only (decision RV-C2-1, rule `webkit-content-channels`): it views a live run log (search, level filter, follow), so it has no `DocMarkdown` tag and no page JSON entry. A docs page or the site shows sample output as a code fence or `CodeBlock`.

## Related

- `code-block` — highlighted source code with a copy action, not a stream of typed log lines.
- `cli-terminal-section` — marketing band that plays a scripted terminal session.
- `stepper` — the steps of a wizard the person moves through; `LogViewer.Steps` is the steps of a run that a machine moves through, each with its log.
- `trace` — the spans of one request on a time axis, not log lines.
- `create/create-deploy-success` — the post-deploy screen that embeds `log-viewer` for the build log.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lines` | `LogViewerLine[]` | `[]` | false | Log entries; filtered in LogViewerContent by search and level. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draw the outer card border and corner radius around the log shell. On by default; set `:bordered="false"` to render the shell flush inside a surface that already frames it (an accordion panel, a drawer). Internal dividers (header/footer edges) are unaffected. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder for the default header search field. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Find in logs`). |
| `copyable` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the copy-to-clipboard control: a CopyButton at the end of LogViewerHeader, or pinned top-right beside the log body when no header is composed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables toolbar controls in LogViewerHeader. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Replaces the LogViewerContent log body with a centered spinner and label. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label shown beneath the spinner while `loading`. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Loading…`). |
| `levels` | `LogViewerLineLevel[]` | `[]` | false | Levels the header offers as filter toggles, each with its line count; a level with no line is still offered. Empty hides the level filter. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Message shown in place of the log body when the log failed to load. Empty shows the log. |
| `search` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:search`). |
| `level` | `LogViewerLineLevel \| ''` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:level`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy` | `(event: MouseEvent, value: string)` | Fires after a successful copy; payload is the copied plain text. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Sub-components (LogViewerHeader, LogViewerContent, LogViewerFooter) composed in the desired order. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/log-viewer-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/log-viewer-footer`
- `@aziontech/webkit/log-viewer-steps`
- `@aziontech/webkit/log-viewer-header`

## Sub-components

LogViewer ships its sub-components attached to the root (`LogViewer.Header`, `LogViewer.Content`, `LogViewer.Footer`, `LogViewer.Steps`, via `index.ts`) and individually importable (each from its own `@aziontech/webkit/log-viewer-*` entry); every sub-component reads the root's shared state through the injected context, so the consumer wires nothing.

- `log-viewer-header.vue` (`LogViewer.Header`) — Default 48px toolbar: line count, the level filter and a search field.
- `log-viewer-content.vue` (`LogViewer.Content`) — Scrollable log body with per-`type` line rendering, search highlighting, `ScrollArea`'s `fade` on the log body (the edges that still have lines beyond them fade out), a…
- `log-viewer-footer.vue` (`LogViewer.Footer`) — Optional footer region for actions (download, follow live, pagination).
- `log-viewer-steps.vue` (`LogViewer.Steps`) — A run with known steps, standalone (it renders its own `LogViewer` per step and needs no parent `LogViewer`).

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:search` | `string` | `''` | `update:search` | Two-way search query; filters LogViewerContent and highlights matches. |
| `v-model:level` | `LogViewerLineLevel \| ''` | `''` | `update:level` | The level the log is filtered to; empty shows every level. A level toggle sets it and pressing the active one clears it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (per log line), `focus-visible`, `disabled`, `loading`, `error`, `empty`
- `data-disabled` / `data-level` / `data-loading` / `data-error` / `data-bordered` on the LogViewer root
- `level` is the one severity axis: the level toggles read and write `level`; the warnings shortcut is the `warn` level toggle (it sets and clears `v-model:level`), offered alone when `levels` is empty
- `error` state: LogViewerContent renders a danger `Alert` with the message in place of the log body; copy is hidden
- `empty` state: the package `EmptyState` (see LogViewerContent above)
- `loading` state: LogViewerContent renders a centered spinner + `loadingLabel` in place of the log body
- Log line `data-type` reflects `line.type` and `data-level` reflects `line.level`; `warn` rows take the warning tint, `error` rows the danger tint and danger text
- Level toggles carry `data-level` and `data-active` (the chosen level); every toggle shows the count of lines at its level in the whole log
- Log line columns: the time and level cells take their width from the longest value in the whole log (`--log-viewer-time-width`, `--log-viewer-level-width` on the line list, counted in `ch` plus the code letter-spacing), so the columns do not move while lines are filtered, appended or mounted in chunks.
- Long logs: above 300 visible lines `LogViewerContent` mounts lines in chunks of 100 as they scroll near view (unmounted chunks keep an estimated 24 px per line), so a 10,000-line log mounts within its runtime budget. Search, the level filter, the line count and copy work on every line, mounted or not.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus on the interactive controls in the header/footer.
- LogViewerContent carries a visually hidden `role="log"` region (`aria-live="polite"`) that holds only the lines appended to `lines` since the last update (filtered by the current search and level). The scrolling log body is not a live region, so the lines already present at mount and the chunks that mount on scroll are never announced; replacing `lines` with a different log clears the region.
- The level filter is a `role="group"` named `Log levels`; each toggle is a button with `aria-pressed` named with its level and line count (`warn, 3 lines`), the level also in visible text, so the state is never colour only.
- The copy control (a CopyButton in LogViewerHeader, or in LogViewerContent when no header is composed) uses `aria-label="Copy logs"` at rest, switching to `"Copied logs"` after a successful copy. Without a header it sits at the top inline end of the content in a column of its own, so no line runs under it.
- The loading state uses `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`; the spinner is `aria-hidden` (from the Spinner component) and the `loadingLabel` text conveys status.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every motion-bearing class.
- LogViewer.Steps: each step is an `Accordion` item (a button with `aria-expanded`); the status glyph is `aria-hidden` and the status is in the trigger's text (`sr-only`), so it is never colour or shape only; the view switch is a named `ToggleGroup`; the progress bar is a `progressbar` named `Run progress`.
- Touch target: level toggles (the `warn` shortcut included) stay 32 px high at every width, so the toolbar keeps its size on a phone; on `pointer: coarse` an invisible layer extends each one's hit area to 44 px tall; the copy control uses CopyButton `size="small"` (28×28 px) to match CodeBlock — a justified deviation for the compact overlay.

```vue
    { id: '1', time: '13:47:33', type: 'text', message: 'Deploy started successfully!' },
    { id: '2', time: '13:47:41', type: 'success', message: 'Build finished' },
    {
      id: '3',
      time: '13:47:42',
      type: 'folder',
      message: 'dist/index.js',
      folderType: 'asset',
      size: '12.4 kB',
      gzipSize: '4.1 kB'
    },
    {
      id: '4',
      time: '13:47:43',
      type: 'text',
      level: 'warn',
      message: 'Bundle larger than recommended'
    }
  ]
  const search = ref('')
  const level = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="h-[640px]">

```

# Trace

> A span waterfall: one row per span of a run (a function invocation, a request through several services), indented under the span it ran inside and drawn as a bar placed against the run's own clock. The rows form a tree grid that expands and collapses, a search narrows them to the spans whose name or service matches, and selecting a row opens its details (service, start, duration, share of the run, outcome message and attributes) under the waterfall. It reads a flat `spans` list with `parentId` links and never fetches anything. With `zoomable`, a minimap under the axis draws the whole run and a window the reader drags or resizes (or moves from the keyboard) to zoom the waterfall into part of it, through `v-model:range`. A span can carry `events` — moments inside it, drawn as markers on its bar and listed in its details — and `highlightSlowest` flags the span that took longest. `highlightCriticalPath` traces the critical path — the chain of work that set the run's end, walked back from the root's end through the child that finished last before each point — and draws a line under each bar along the stretches of that span that lie on it, so the reader sees which work to shorten to make the run faster. The details of a span with children show its self time (its duration less the time its children covered), and of a span on the critical path, its time on that path. The same spans read in three views the reader picks with a `ToggleGroup` in the toolbar, bound to `v-model:view`: `waterfall` (the default: the tree of spans with a bar per row on the run clock), `timeline` (bars only, on one shared time axis: each nesting level is a band, and spans of a level that do not overlap share a lane, so a whole run fits in a few lines) and `tree` (the nesting only, with the start and duration of each span as text instead of a bar). Search, selection and the details are shared by the three views; the zoom applies to the two views with a time axis.

- Import: `import Trace from '@aziontech/webkit/trace'`
- Category: code · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Trace for the timed span waterfall of one request or invocation; a nested data hierarchy without timing is a Tree.
- The test run of a function or the detail of one invocation, to show where the time went.
- A request that crossed several services, each with its own span, where the order and the overlap matter.
- Next to the run's logs (`log-viewer`), on the same clock.

## Do

- Pass `start` and `duration` in milliseconds from the start of the run; the axis spans the latest end.
- Link children with `parentId`; a span whose parent is missing becomes a root, so a partial trace still renders.
- Set `status: 'error'` and a one-line `message` on the span that failed, and on its parents if the failure bubbled up.
- Turn on `zoomable` for a run with many short spans next to one long one, so the short ones can be read; bind `v-model:range` when the logs or a chart beside the trace should follow the same window.
- Use `events` for moments that have no duration of their own (a cache miss, a retry, the first byte), with `at` on the run's clock; keep the names short, they are listed in the details.
- Turn on `highlightCriticalPath` where the question is what to make faster: shortening a span off the path does not shorten the run, shortening one on it does. It reads better than `highlightSlowest` when work runs in parallel, because the longest span is not always the one that held the run up.
- Turn on `highlightSlowest` where the question is where the time went; the flag goes to the longest span under the root, never to the root itself, which always spans the run.
- Bind `v-model:view` when the reader's choice of view should last: the page can keep it across traces or sessions. Unbound, each trace opens in the waterfall.
- Use the timeline view for a run with many spans or a narrow panel, the tree view to read names and durations as text, the waterfall when both the nesting and the timing matter.
- Bind `v-model:selected-key` when another view (a request path, a log line) selects the same span.
- Name the waterfall after the run (`aria-label="Trace of inv_7f21"`).

## Don’t

- A list of log lines with levels → use `log-viewer`.
- Durations to compare across many items with no parent/child relation → use `bar-list` or `chart`.
- Status history of a service over days → use `tracker`.
- A hierarchy without time → use `tree`.
- In a docs Markdown page or the site's page JSON. Trace is app-only (decision RV-C2-1, rule `webkit-content-channels`): it explores one run (expand, search, select a span for its details), so it has no `DocMarkdown` tag and no page JSON entry. A docs page or the site explains where the time went with a `FlowDiagram` or a `Chart`.

## Related

- `log-viewer` — the run's log lines, shown under the trace on the same clock.
- `tree` — the same expand and collapse model without the time axis.
- `bar-list` — ranked durations without nesting.
- `key-value-list` — the facts of the run above the trace.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spans` | `TraceSpan[]` | `[]` | false | Spans of the trace, each `{ id, parentId?, name, service?, icon?, start, duration, status?, message?, attributes? }` in milliseconds. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the waterfall. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draws the outer border and radius. Off for a trace inside a card or panel that has its own. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows placeholder rows while the spans load; search and selection wait. |
| `zoomable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a minimap under the axis to zoom the waterfall into a window of the run. Supports v-model:range. |
| `highlightSlowest` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Flags the span that took longest, other than the root, in its row and its details. |
| `highlightCriticalPath` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Draws the critical path of the run under the bars and flags the spans on it in their rows and details. |
| `selectedKey` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:selectedKey`). |
| `range` | `TraceRange \| null` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:range`). |
| `view` | `TraceView` | `'waterfall'` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:view`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:selectedKey` | `string` | `''` | `update:selectedKey` | Id of the span whose details show under the waterfall, via `defineModel('selectedKey')`. A row was selected, selected again (empty: deselected), or Close used. Unbound, the trace keeps the selection itself. |
| `v-model:view` | `TraceView` | `'waterfall'` | `update:view` | The view the reader picked in the toolbar, via `defineModel('view')`: `waterfall`, `timeline` or `tree`. Unbound, the trace keeps the choice itself. |
| `v-model:range` | `TraceRange \| null` | `null` | `update:range` | The visible window of the run clock, via `defineModel('range')`. `null` shows the whole run. Applied with or without `zoomable`; clamped to the run and widened to at least 1% of it. |

## States

- Views: `data-view` on the root mirrors the model. `waterfall` and `tree` render the tree grid (in `tree` the second column holds the start and duration as text, with no axis, bars, grid lines or minimap); `timeline` renders a listbox of bars in lanes, each bar a named option with its name and duration inside when the bar is wide enough (a narrower bar carries them in its `title`); the first lane of each nesting level below the root starts with a divider (`data-level-start`). While searching, the timeline marks the bars that do not match `data-dimmed` and dims them instead of hiding them; a bar outside the zoom window is `data-outside`, hidden, and left out of the keyboard order. The view switch stays enabled while `loading`.
- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (row), `focus-visible` (row), `selected` (row and details band), `collapsed` / `expanded` (parent rows), `searching` (rows narrowed, every match's ancestors shown), `loading` (placeholder rows in a `role="status"` region, `aria-busy` on the root, search disabled, no details), `empty` (the package `EmptyState`, small: no spans, or no match with a Clear search action).
- Bar colour on `data-status` (`success`, `error`, `running`) plus `data-root` on a successful root span: root (info), `success`, `error` (danger), `running` (warning).
- `data-selected` on the selected row; `aria-expanded` on parent rows; `data-bordered` and `data-loading` on the root mirror their props.
- `zoomed` (a window narrower than the run): the axis, the bars and the event markers are placed against the window; a bar outside it is hidden (`data-outside`) while its row stays; the minimap shows the window and Reset zoom.
- `data-slowest` on the slowest span's row (with `highlightSlowest`).
- `data-critical` on the rows of spans on the critical path (with `highlightCriticalPath`); each stretch of the path is a line under its bar, placed against the visible window like the bar.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: a 2 px inset ring on the focused row.
- View switch: a `ToggleGroup` named View (a `radiogroup` of Waterfall, Timeline and Tree) with its own arrow-key model; switching keeps the selection and the search.
- Timeline: a named `listbox` of `option`s in start order, one in the tab order (roving `tabindex`); `ArrowRight`/`ArrowDown` move to the next span, `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowUp` to the previous (the inline arrows swap under `dir="rtl"`), `Home`/`End` to the first and last, `Enter` or `Space` selects (again: deselects). Each option is named like a row and carries `aria-selected`. Lanes are `role="none"`.
- Keyboard map (waterfall and tree): one row is in the tab order (roving `tabindex`); `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move between visible rows; `Home`/`End` go to the first and last row; `ArrowRight` expands a collapsed parent, or moves into its first child; `ArrowLeft` collapses an expanded parent, or moves to the parent; `Enter` or `Space` selects the row (again: deselects). Close in the details returns focus to the row (in the timeline, to the bar).
- ARIA: the waterfall is a named `treegrid` of `row`s with `aria-level`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-expanded` (parents only) and `aria-selected`; each row is named with its span, service, start, duration and outcome; the details band is a named `region` that describes the grid. The axis, the bars' duration labels and the expand glyph are decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Minimap: the two window edges are `role="slider"` thumbs named Zoom start and Zoom end, with `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` / `aria-valuenow` in milliseconds and the formatted time as `aria-valuetext`. `ArrowRight`/`ArrowUp` move an edge by 1% of the run, `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowDown` back, `PageUp`/`PageDown` by 10%, `Home`/`End` to its limits, `Escape` resets the zoom. Reset zoom is a button. The span lines drawn in the minimap are decorative.
- Event markers are decorative; a row with events is named with their count, and the details list each event with its time. The slowest flag is named in the row (`Slowest`) and shown as a Tag in the details. The critical path lines are decorative; a span on the path is named in its row (`Critical path`), shown as a Tag in the details with its time on the path, so the path never depends on the line alone.
- Rows are 36 px high (44 px on `pointer: coarse`).
- Colour is never the only signal: a failed span also carries an icon in the row and a Failed tag in the details.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens; duration labels use the `-foreground` tokens of their status.

<!-- components/accordion.md -->

# Accordion

> A vertically stacked set of disclosure items: each item has a clickable header that expands or collapses its content panel. Use it to condense long content into scannable sections. Unlike `tabs` (mutually-exclusive panels shown in place), an accordion can keep one item open at a time (`type="single"`) or several at once (`type="multiple"`), and its content expands inline below each header.

- Import: `import AccordionRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/accordion-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Accordion from '@aziontech/webkit/accordion'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Accordion for expandable sections in product UI; the marketing FAQ band is FaqSection.
- Long content splits into independent sections the reader scans by heading and opens on demand (settings groups, help topics, a details list).
- The reader may want one section open at a time (`type="single"`) or to compare several side by side (`type="multiple"`).
- Content should expand inline below its heading, pushing the rest of the page down.

## Do

- Give every `Accordion.Item` a unique `value`; the open state is keyed by it, and `default-value` / `v-model` refer to it.
- Bind `v-model` to a string in `type="single"` and to an array in `type="multiple"`; set `collapsible` to `false` only when one item must always stay open.
- Set the trigger's `headingLevel` to fit the page outline (default `3`) — each trigger is wrapped in a real heading.
- With `icon-position="leading"` the trigger's label keeps its content width but may shrink, so a long label (or a row of label and tags) wraps inside the trigger instead of running out of it on a narrow screen.
- `Accordion.Content` pads its body on the trigger's inset (`--accordion-inset`) with `--spacing-xs` above and `--spacing-md` below, so the answer starts on the question's left edge (after the chevron when `icon-position` is `leading`). Pass `:padded="false"` for edge-to-edge content (a `LogViewer`, a table) that owns its spacing.
- Set `size` and `icon-position` on the root, not per item — they are provided to every item through context.

## Don’t

- The panels are mutually exclusive views shown in the same place → use `tabs`.
- It is the frequently-asked-questions band of a marketing page → use `faq-section` (or `faq` for the band without the page-section wiring).
- It is hierarchical navigation with expandable rows → use `sidebar-menu`.

## Related

- `tabs` — switches between panels in place; one panel visible, headers in a row.
- `faq` — the marketing FAQ band that composes `accordion` with a heading column and hairline register.
- `sidebar-menu` — expanding rows for navigation, not for revealing content.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'single' \| 'multiple'` | `'single'` | false | Whether one or multiple items can be open at the same time. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[] \| null` | `null` | false | Initial open item(s) when uncontrolled. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `true` | false | In single mode, lets the open item collapse so that no item is open. |
| `size` | `'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects header height, padding, and typography. Provided to every item via context. |
| `iconPosition` | `'leading' \| 'trailing'` | `'trailing'` | false | Side of the header the chevron sits on. Provided to every item via context. |
| `modelValue` | `AccordionValue \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The `Accordion.Item` children. Each sub-component's own `default` slot is documented in the Sub-components section. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/accordion-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/accordion-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/accordion-content`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: an `index.ts` (beside `accordion.vue`) attaches every sub-component to the root so `<Accordion.Item>` / `<Accordion.Trigger>` / `<Accordion.Content>` resolve from one import; the standalone imports above remain the tree-shaking path. The root is a disclosure component with `data-state="open|closed"`, so `Trigger` / `Content` are the correct anatomy names. Shared open-state flows through `provide`/`inject` (`injection-key.ts`), so the consumer wires nothing.

- `accordion-item/accordion-item.vue` — One disclosure row.
  - Props: `value: string` (**required** — unique identifier used by the open-state model), `disabled?: boolean` (default `false` — prevents this item from toggling; from the Figma component description).
  - Slot: `default` — the item's `Accordion.Trigger` and `Accordion.Content`.
- `accordion-trigger/accordion-trigger.vue` — The clickable header row (Figma "Header"): renders the title plus the `az az-chevron-down` glyph, toggles the item through the injected context, and exposes `aria-expanded`…
  - Props: `headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` (default `3` — heading level of the wrapping `<h{headingLevel}>` for correct document outline).
  - Slot: `default` — header title content.
- `accordion-content/accordion-content.vue` — The collapsible panel.
  - Props: `padded?: boolean` (default `true` — pads the body on the trigger's inset, after the chevron when it leads, with `--spacing-xs` above and `--spacing-md` below; set false for edge-to-edge content such as a `LogViewer` or table rows).
  - Slot: `default` — panel body content.

Resulting layout (no per-component `package.json` — dropped repo-wide; the root `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` resolves every path; `.d.ts` is generated at publish time, never committed):

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/accordion/
├── accordion.vue                 (root; owns type/modelValue/size/iconPosition, provides context)
├── index.ts                      (compound: attaches Item / Trigger / Content to the root)
├── injection-key.ts              (shared AccordionContext)
├── accordion-item/
│   └── accordion-item.vue
├── accordion-trigger/
│   └── accordion-trigger.vue
└── accordion-content/
    └── accordion-content.vue
```

Exports to add to `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` (flat public names; category lives in the folder only):

```jsonc
"./accordion": "./src/components/content/accordion/index.ts",
"./accordion-item": "./src/components/content/accordion/accordion-item/accordion-item.vue",
"./accordion-trigger": "./src/components/content/accordion/accordion-trigger/accordion-trigger.vue",
"./accordion-content": "./src/components/content/accordion/accordion-content/accordion-content.vue"
```

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string \| string[] \| null \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | Open item(s) via `defineModel`: a single `value` string in single mode, an array of values in multiple mode, `null` when none is open. While unbound (`undefined`) the accordion is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultValue`. |

`./accordion` and `./accordion-root` export the type `AccordionValue` (`string | string[] | null`), the model's value without its unbound `undefined`.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed` — on the item, the trigger, and the content
- `data-disabled` mirrors the per-item `disabled` prop
- `data-orientation`: `vertical`
- Reflow: the trigger label region is `min-w-0`, so long trigger content truncates or wraps instead of overflowing a narrow box.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus (Figma has no focus variant; we own it): `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on each `Accordion.Trigger`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` move between triggers and into open content; `Enter` / `Space` toggle the focused item; `Arrow Down` / `Arrow Up` move focus to the next / previous trigger; `Home` / `End` move focus to the first / last trigger. The order is the document order of the items, and an item disabled after mount drops out of it at once.
- ARIA: each trigger is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` reflecting open state and `aria-controls` referencing its content; the trigger button is wrapped in a heading element (`<h{headingLevel}>`, default `h3`); the content panel has `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` referencing its trigger. A `disabled` item sets `disabled` + `aria-disabled` on its trigger.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for text (title `--text-default`, body `--text-muted` on the surface) / ≥3:1 for the chevron glyph, including the disabled state (`--text-disabled`).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:animate-none` on the chevron rotation and content reveal.
- Touch target: the `large` header is 40px tall and the full-width header row is the hit area (≥40×40). The `medium` header is 32px tall on a fine pointer, matching the Figma `medium` size token; on a coarse pointer every header is at least 44px tall (`pointer-coarse:min-h-11`). It grows instead of carrying an invisible hit area because stacked headers would overlap each other's.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Accordion from '@aziontech/webkit/accordion'
</script>

<template>
  <Accordion
    type="single"
    collapsible
    default-value="overview"
    size="medium"
    icon-position="trailing"
    class="w-full max-w-[40rem]"
  >
    <Accordion.Item value="overview">
      <Accordion.Trigger>What is Azion?</Accordion.Trigger>
      <Accordion.Content>Azion runs your code at the edge, close to users.</Accordion.Content>
    </Accordion.Item>
    <Accordion.Item value="pricing">
      <Accordion.Trigger>How does pricing work?</Accordion.Trigger>
      <Accordion.Content>Pay only for what you use, with no upfront cost.</Accordion.Content>
    </Accordion.Item>
    <Accordion.Item value="support">
      <Accordion.Trigger>Enterprise support</Accordion.Trigger>
      <Accordion.Content>Available on Business and Enterprise plans.</Accordion.Content>
    </Accordion.Item>
  </Accordion>
</template>
```

<!-- components/audio-player.md -->

# Audio Player

> A compact player for one audio clip: play and pause, a seek bar between the current time and the duration, mute and volume, and, when asked for, a playback speed control, a download link and a transcript. It plays what the app hands it (a URL, an object URL or a `data:` URL built from base64 audio) on the browser's own audio element; it fetches and decodes nothing. It owns the generating, buffering and error states, so an AI reply that speaks, or a stored recording, looks the same everywhere.

- Import: `import AudioPlayer from '@aziontech/webkit/audio-player'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- An AI reply that carries audio: speech generated from text, generated music or sound, an audio part of a chat message.
- A voice note or recording a person attached to a message or a ticket.
- Previewing one stored audio file in a detail pane or drawer.

## Do

- Build `src` once from the source the app has: a URL as it is, base64 audio as `data:<mimeType>;base64,<value>`, a `Blob` as an object URL (revoke it when the player unmounts).
- Pass `duration` when the generator reports it, so the time shows before the browser has read the file.
- Set `loading` while the audio is being generated, so the player holds its place in the reply instead of appearing when it is done.
- Pass the text the audio speaks as `transcript`; a reader who cannot hear it reads it instead (WCAG 1.2.1).
- Give each player a `title` when a message holds more than one, so each control group has its own name.
- Never start playback on mount; the reader presses Play.
- In a narrow column only Mute is left for the volume; the device volume covers the rest on a phone.

## Don’t

- Video, or audio that needs a picture → use `DocFrame` (a captured clip) or `Embed` (a hosted player).
- Recording audio or a live voice conversation → use `PromptInput` and its dictate button.
- A file of any type with a type-aware fallback → use `FilePreview`.
- Background or decorative sound that the reader did not ask for → do not autoplay audio; leave it out.

## Related

- `FilePreview` — the preview of a stored file of any type; an audio file can open in an `AudioPlayer` instead.
- `ChatMessage` — the message an audio reply sits in.
- `Slider` — the seek and volume controls inside this component.
- `IconButton` — the play, mute and download controls inside this component.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | `''` | false | Audio source: a URL, an object URL or a data URL built from base64 audio. Empty disables the controls. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Name of the clip, shown above the controls and used as the accessible name of the control group. |
| `duration` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Length of the clip in seconds, shown until the browser reads it from the file. Unset shows a placeholder. |
| `transcript` | `string` | `''` | false | Text the audio speaks, shown in a collapsible Transcript section under the controls. Empty hides the section. |
| `playbackRates` | `number[]` | `[]` | false | Playback speeds the speed control cycles through, in order. Empty hides it; it starts at 1 when listed, else the first. |
| `downloadable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a Download link to `src`. |
| `fileName` | `string` | `''` | false | File name the Download link saves the audio as. Empty lets the browser pick one. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The audio is still being generated or fetched: the play control shows a spinner and the other controls are disabled. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Why the audio cannot play. Set, the controls are disabled and this text replaces the time. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables every control and applies the disabled tokens. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the control group when there is no `title`. Empty falls back to the catalog's Audio player. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `play` | `Event` | Playback started (the audio element's `play` event). |
| `pause` | `Event` | Playback paused, by the reader or because the clip reached its end (the element's `pause` event). |
| `retry` | `MouseEvent` | Try again in the error state was pressed. The button renders only when this event has a listener; an error the audio element reported is cleared and the element loads `src` again, and the app clears or keeps `error`. |

## States

- `data-playing` is set while the audio plays; the play control shows Pause.
- `data-loading` mirrors `loading` (the audio is still being generated or fetched): the play control shows a `Spinner` (through `IconButton`'s `loading`) and is inert, every other control is disabled, the root has `aria-busy`, and a visually hidden `role="status"` line says Loading audio.
- `data-buffering` is set while the browser waits for data after Play (the audio element's `waiting` until `playing`): a small `Spinner` replaces the current time, the root has `aria-busy` and the status line says Loading audio, and every control stays enabled; Play keeps its Pause name so the reader can stop a stalled clip.
- `data-error` is set when `error` is set or the audio element reports an error; the controls are disabled and the error line (`role="alert"`) replaces the time. The app's text wins; with no text the catalog's message shows. With a `retry` listener a small outline Try again `Button` (`az az-refresh`) sits at the end of the error line.
- `data-disabled` mirrors `disabled`; it is also set when `src` is empty and nothing is loading.
- `data-muted` is set while the audio is muted; the mute control shows Unmute and the volume slider reads 0.
- Empty: `src` empty with `loading` false sets `data-disabled`; the times show `--:--` and the Download link is not rendered.
- Unknown duration (no `duration` and the file not read yet): the times show `--:--` and the seek bar is disabled until the browser reports the length.
- The transcript is a native `details` disclosure, closed by default; its `open` attribute is the only open state, with no `data-state` on the root. On a coarse pointer an invisible layer (`data-slot="touch-target"`) extends the summary's hit area to 40 px tall.
- Not applicable: `readonly` and `invalid` (the player takes no value input).
- A new `src` resets the time, the playing state and the error.

## Accessibility

- The root is a `role="group"` named by `title` (`aria-labelledby`), else `ariaLabel`, else the catalog's Audio player.
- Visible focus: every control is an `IconButton`, `Button` or `Slider` with the ring token.
- Play is one toggle `IconButton` whose name follows its state (Play / Pause); its glyph is decorative. It is inert only under `loading`, `error`, `disabled` or an empty `src`; while buffering it stays operable.
- The seek bar is a `Slider` named Seek, from 0 to the duration in whole seconds, with a spoken `aria-valuetext` (`42 seconds of 3 minutes, 5 seconds`); it changes once a second at most.
- Mute is a toggle named Mute / Unmute; volume is a `Slider` named Volume, 0 to 100, with `aria-valuetext` from `formatNumber` (`style: 'percent'`).
- The speed control is a `Button` whose visible text is the rate (`1.5×`) and whose name is Playback speed 1.5×, so the name contains the visible text.
- Patterns (WAI-ARIA APG): Slider for seek and volume; Button with a name that follows its state for Play/Pause and Mute/Unmute; Button for speed; Link for Download; Disclosure for the transcript.
- Download is an anchor with the `download` attribute, named Download audio.
- The transcript is a native `details`/`summary` disclosure, so it opens with Enter or Space and announces its expanded state.
- Keyboard: `Tab` moves through Play, Seek, Mute, Volume, Speed, Download, Transcript; `Enter`/`Space` press the buttons; on the sliders the arrow keys step 1 second (seek) or 1 % (volume), `PageUp`/`PageDown` take larger steps, `Home`/`End` go to the start or the end.
- No autoplay (WCAG 1.4.2); the audio never starts without a press on Play.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the title, the time and the error line; ≥3:1 for the glyphs and the slider tracks. Disabled controls render `--text-disabled` on `--bg-disabled` through `IconButton`, `Button` and `Slider`; inactive controls are exempt from 1.4.3 and 1.4.11.
- Touch target: Play is drawn 40 × 40 px and the other buttons 32 × 32 px (above the 24 px minimum, WCAG 2.5.8); on `pointer: coarse` `IconButton` and `Button` add their 44 × 44 px hit area, and the `Slider` inputs are 40 px tall.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import speech from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/placeholder-clip.webm'
  import AudioPlayer from '@aziontech/webkit/audio-player'
</script>

<template>
  <AudioPlayer
    :src="speech"
    title="Deployment summary"
    :duration="1.9"
    transcript="Your application acme-store is live. The last deploy finished in 42 seconds and every check passed."
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/avatar.md -->

# Avatar

> Identifies a person, an account or an organization with a small visual mark: their picture when there is one, otherwise their initials, a fallback icon or a generated pattern seeded by the name. It comes in a circle or a square at three sizes, so the same person reads the same way in a header, a list row or a comment thread. An optional presence dot on its bottom inline-end edge says whether the person is online, away, busy or offline.

- Import: `import Avatar from '@aziontech/webkit/avatar'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Identify a person next to their name: comment threads, member lists, "Last modified" cells, quotes.
- The user entry in a header or account menu.
- Show whether a teammate or support agent is reachable now (`presence`): an assignee picker, a ticket's agent list, a conversation header.
- The mark of an organization or account that has no logo: `pattern="marble"` draws a soft generated mark seeded by its name, the same for the same name everywhere (account switcher, create organization, onboarding).

## Do

- Pass initials or the full name in `label`: a name of several words shows the first letter of its first and last word (`"Jane Doe"` shows `JD`), and one word keeps its first two characters (`"JD"` stays `JD`).
- Set `alt` to the person's name ("Jane Doe"). With `src` it is the image's `alt`; without an image it names the initials or icon fallback (`role="img"`), so a screen reader hears "Jane Doe", not "JD". Without `alt` the name falls back to the initials, then "Avatar" for an image or "User avatar" for the icon.
- Content precedence is `src`, then `pattern`, then `label`, then `icon` (default `az az-user`).
- For a generated mark, pass the full name in `label` (`"Acme Inc."`) with `pattern="marble"`: the name seeds the shapes, so one organization keeps one mark. Pass `colors` to pick its palette (three theme colors, such as an accent the person chose); do not inline your own generator or a data-URL image.
- Set `presence` only when the value is live (`online`, `away`, `busy`, `offline`); leave it empty when the app does not know, rather than showing `offline`. The presence joins the accessible name ("Jane Doe, away"), so keep `alt` to the name alone.
- `size` maps to 24 / 32 / 48 px with `medium` as the default; `variant` is `circle` (default) or `square`.

## Don’t

- The Azion logo → use `brand`.
- A count or short status → use `badge`.
- A loading placeholder → use `skeleton`.
- The outcome of a job or a deploy → use `status-indicator`; `presence` is only whether a person is reachable.

## Related

- `badge` — overlay on an avatar to show a count.
- `quote` — composes an avatar for the speaker.
- `brand` — the product mark, not a person.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | `''` | false | Image URL. When set, renders a photo and takes precedence over label and icon. |
| `alt` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name: the image's `alt` with `src`, and the name of the initials or icon fallback without it. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Initials shown when no image: the first letters of the first and last word, or the first two characters of one word, uppercased. |
| `icon` | `string` | `'az az-user'` | false | Icon class for the fallback when no image or label (Azion icon class). |
| `variant` | `AvatarVariant` | `'circle'` | false | Visual shape of the avatar container. |
| `size` | `AvatarSize` | `'medium'` | false | Size preset matching Figma sm / md / lg (24 / 32 / 48 px). |
| `pattern` | `AvatarPattern` | `undefined` | false | Generated fallback drawn when there is no image: `marble` blends three soft shapes seeded by `label` (or `alt`). |
| `colors` | `string[]` | `['var(--primary)', 'var(--warning)', 'var(--brand-blue)']` | false | CSS colors the generated pattern paints with, in order; theme tokens such as `var(--primary)`. |
| `presence` | `AvatarPresence \| ''` | `''` | false | Whether the person is reachable now, drawn as a dot on the bottom inline-end edge and added to the accessible name; empty draws no dot. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- Content: `image` (`src`), `pattern` (`pattern` set, no `src`), `label` (initials), `icon`. `data-pattern` mirrors `pattern` on the root while the pattern renders.
- Root attributes: `data-variant` and `data-size` mirror the props; `data-content` names the content that renders (`image`, `pattern`, `label`, `icon`). Variants are styled from these attributes.
- Image error: when `src` fails to load, the avatar falls back to the next content in the precedence (`pattern`, `label`, `icon`) instead of a broken image; a new `src` tries the image again. An image that already failed before hydration is detected on mount.
- Presence: `presence` is `online`, `away`, `busy` or `offline` (`AvatarPresence`); `''` (default) renders nothing. When set, the root carries `data-presence` and a dot (`data-slot="presence"`, test id `${testId}__presence`) sits inside the avatar's box, in its bottom inline-end corner, overlapping only the picture, at 10 / 12 / 16 px for `small` / `medium` / `large` (its 2 px ring included), the same for `circle` and `square`. On `small` the dot is pushed a quarter of its size past the corner (`translate-1/4`, mirrored under `rtl`), so on a 24 px avatar it no longer covers the second initial; only its ring leaves the box. The content is clipped to the avatar shape by an inner box, so the dot is never clipped by the avatar itself, and a parent that clips its content never cuts it off. Each value has its own shape, so colour is not the only signal: `online` a filled dot, `away` a crescent, `busy` a dot with a horizontal bar, `offline` a hollow ring. A 2 px ring in `--avatar-presence-ring` (default `var(--bg-surface)`) separates the dot from the picture and from the background; an app on another background sets that variable on the avatar or an ancestor.
- Attributes: every consumer attribute (`id`, `title`, `aria-*`, `style`, listeners) lands on the root.
- Marble: three layers seeded by a 32-bit string hash of `label` (falling back to `alt`): a filled square, then two blurred shapes translated, rotated and scaled by the seed, the last blended with `overlay`. Each layer takes the color at `(seed + layer) % colors.length`. The same seed and colors always draw the same mark, on the server and in the browser.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: none; the avatar is not focusable. A parent control (account menu trigger) owns focus.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: with `src` the `img` carries `alt`; without it the root is `role="img"` with `aria-label` (see Internationalization; an `aria-label` the consumer passes, such as the purpose of a menu trigger the avatar sits in, replaces the derived name), and the initials, icon or pattern inside are presentational (`aria-hidden` on the icon and the pattern SVG).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the initials on `var(--bg-surface-raised)`; the generated pattern is decorative and carries no text.
- Presence: the dot is presentational (`aria-hidden`); the presence joins the accessible name of the root (`aria-label`) or of the image (`alt`) through `avatar.withPresence`, for example "Jane Doe, away"; it wraps whichever name applies (`alt`, the label, the initials or the fallback, so "User avatar, away"). The dot colours are the documented `-mark` colours (`--text-muted` for `offline`, the neutral mark), solid marks at APCA Lc 30 and WCAG 3:1 on the surface, and each value differs in shape as well as colour (WCAG 1.4.1). A change of `presence` is not announced (no live region): the avatar is a label, and a live roster announces through the app.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Avatar from '@aziontech/webkit/avatar'
</script>

<template>
  <Avatar
    label="AB"
    variant="circle"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/avatar.md](components/avatar.md).
