<!-- components/file-preview.md -->

# File Preview

> The preview of one stored file in a storage or object browser, or of a document in an AI conversation (a PDF the reader attaches or a model returns): a header with the file's glyph, name, type and size, a Download action, and a body that shows the file the way it can be read. An image renders as the image, a PDF in the browser's own PDF viewer, text as wrapped monospace text, JSON pretty-printed, and any other type a no-preview state that points at Download. Audio and video files are recognized (their glyph and type) and show the file card with Download; this component plays nothing. Long text is cut at `maxLength` characters with a note that says so. The file comes as a URL (`src`), as text (`content`) or as base64 bytes (`base64`, the shape a chat message carries); it renders what the app hands it and fetches nothing.

- Import: `import FilePreview from '@aziontech/webkit/file-preview'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The detail pane or drawer of a file browser when a row is opened (`view/view-file-browser`, an Edge Storage bucket, a KV value).
- Showing an uploaded object before it is published or replaced.
- A document part or an attachment in an AI conversation: a PDF, a text file or an image, from a URL or from base64 bytes.
- Any screen that shows one file and needs a type-aware fallback for files it cannot draw.

## Do

- Pass `mimeType` from the object's `Content-Type`; leave it empty and the file name's extension decides.
- Fetch only the first part of a large text file (a ranged request) and pass `bytes` with the full size, so the header shows the real size while the body shows the first part.
- Handle `download` with the app's own signed or authorized URL; the component never builds one.
- Pass an object URL (`URL.createObjectURL`) or a short-lived signed URL as `src`; revoke an object URL when the preview closes.
- `src` goes through `safeHref` (file schemes allowed): `javascript:`, `file:`, a protocol-relative `//host` URL and any other scheme draw nothing, as every other URL-taking component does. An image or PDF URL loads with no click, so an app that shows URLs a model or a tool returned should allow only its own origins before it passes them, or show a click-to-load placeholder. A `Content-Security-Policy` with `object-src 'none'` blocks the PDF viewer; allow `object-src 'self' blob:` where PDFs are previewed.
- When the app holds the bytes rather than a URL (a chat message part with base64 data), pass them as `base64` with `mimeType`; the component makes its own object URL for an image or PDF and revokes it when the source changes or the preview unmounts. Text and JSON are decoded into the body.
- A PDF is drawn by the browser's own viewer; where there is none (most phones, a viewer turned off), the body shows the no-preview state and Download stays.

## Don’t

- Editing a file — use `CodeEditor`.
- Highlighted source code with tabs and copy — use `CodeBlock`.
- A list of files with upload progress — use `FileTokenGroup` or `UploadProgress`.
- A log stream — use `LogViewer`.
- Playing audio or video — this component shows those files as a card with Download, not a player.

## Related

- `CodeBlock` — syntax-highlighted code; heavier, for a code sample rather than a stored object.
- `EmptyState` — the no-preview and error states inside this component.
- `Skeleton` — the loading placeholder inside this component.
- `DataTable` — the file list a preview opens from.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fileName` | `string` | `—` | true | Name of the file, shown in the header and used as the image's alternative text. |
| `mimeType` | `string` | `''` | false | Media type of the file (`image/png`, `application/json`). Empty reads the type from the file extension. |
| `bytes` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Size of the whole file in bytes, shown beside the type. Unset hides the size. |
| `src` | `string` | `''` | false | URL of an image or PDF file to draw: https, http, blob, data or a relative path; any other scheme draws nothing. Set, it wins over `base64`. |
| `base64` | `string` | `''` | false | Base64 bytes of the file, for an app that holds the file rather than a URL. Text and JSON are decoded into the body when `content` is empty; an image or PDF with no `src` is drawn from them. |
| `content` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of a text or JSON file. JSON that parses is pretty-printed; JSON that does not shows as text. Set, it wins over `base64`. |
| `maxLength` | `number` | `20000` | false | Characters of text shown before the rest is cut, with a note that says how much is shown. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a placeholder in the body while the app fetches the file; the header stays. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Why the preview could not load. Set, the body shows the error state with this text. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `download` | `MouseEvent` | The Download button was pressed; the app starts the download. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | — | More actions in the header, before Download (copy link, delete). |

## States

- `data-type`: `image` | `pdf` | `audio` | `video` | `text` | `json` | `unknown`, the kind of file the body draws (derived from `mimeType`, then the extension: `application/pdf` or `.pdf`, `audio/*` or an audio extension, `video/*` or a video extension).
- Header glyph per type: `image` `az az-image`, `pdf` `az az-file-pdf`, `audio` `az az-headphones`, `video` `az az-video`, `json` `az az-json`, `text` and `unknown` `az az-file`.
- A PDF with a source is an `object` (`type="application/pdf"`) of that source in the browser's PDF viewer, `var(--container-lg)` tall, with the ring token on keyboard focus; its fallback content is the no-preview state. Where the browser reports no PDF viewer (`navigator.pdfViewerEnabled` is `false`), or the PDF has no source, `data-type` stays `pdf` (glyph and type in the header) and only the body shows the no-preview state.
- Server render: `navigator` and `URL.createObjectURL` exist only in the browser, so the server and the first client render show a PDF's body as the no-preview state, and an image or PDF given only as `base64` with no source yet. After mount the component makes the object URL from `base64` and swaps the PDF `object` in when a viewer exists and a source resolves.
- An audio or video file keeps its `data-type` and glyph and shows the no-preview body; no player.
- `base64` is plain base64 or a base64 data URL (`data:application/pdf;base64,…`, the prefix is dropped). Text is decoded as UTF-8. `base64` that does not decode draws nothing: an image falls back to the no-preview state, a PDF shows the no-preview body, text shows the empty-file line.
- `data-loading` mirrors `loading`; the body is a `Skeleton` in a `role="status"` region and `aria-busy` is set.
- `error` set: the body is an `EmptyState` with the error text; Download stays available.
- An image that fails to load, or has no source, falls back to the no-preview state.
- Text over `maxLength` sets `data-truncated` and shows the truncation note.
- A text or JSON file with no content shows the empty-file line.

## Accessibility

- The root is a `section` named by the file name (`aria-labelledby`).
- The image's `alt` is the file name.
- The PDF `object` is named `Preview of <file>` (`title` and `aria-label`), so a screen reader announces the embedded document; the browser's viewer owns the keyboard inside it.
- The text body is a focusable, scrollable region (`tabindex="0"`, `role="region"`, named `Contents of <file>`) so a keyboard user can scroll it.
- Loading is a `role="status"` region named `Loading preview`; the root has `aria-busy`.
- Download is a real `Button` with a visible label; the glyph is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Keyboard: `Tab` reaches the `actions` slot, Download, the text body and the PDF viewer; arrow keys scroll the text body.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the name, the meta line and the text.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  import FilePreview from '@aziontech/webkit/file-preview'

  const settings = JSON.stringify({
    name: 'acme-store',
    domains: ['www.example.com', 'shop.example.com'],
    cache: { ttl: 3600, browser: true },
    origin: { host: 'origin.example.com', protocol: 'https' }
  })

  const onDownload = (event: MouseEvent) => {
    event.preventDefault()
  }
</script>

<template>
  <FilePreview
    class="max-w-(--container-md)"
    file-name="settings.json"
    mime-type="application/json"
    :bytes="182"
    :content="settings"
    @download="onDownload"
  />
</template>
```

# Help Panel

> The content of a help side region: a topic's title, a few sections of short guidance, and the "Learn more" links that leave for the documentation. Guided tutorials belong to `tutorial-panel`. It is the thing that goes **inside** a side region, not the region itself: the consumer places it in a `Drawer` or in the page's side rail, and that host owns opening, closing and the close button. It owns no open state, so it has no `Trigger` / `Content` and no `data-state="open|closed"`. Its anatomy is the anatomy of a help page — `Header`, `Section`, `Links` — composed by hand, so a topic can omit the links or carry one section or five.

- Import: `import HelpPanelRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import HelpPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use HelpPanel for static page help (title, guidance, Learn more links) in the app layout's tools region.
- A Console screen needs contextual help beside the work: what this page is for, what a field means, where the docs are.
- The help content is loaded asynchronously and the region must reserve its space while it arrives (`loading`).

## Do

- One topic per panel. When the reader moves to another part of the page, swap the panel's content — do not stack two headers.
- Keep each `Section` to a short paragraph or a short list. If the reader has to scroll a section, the content belongs in the docs and the panel should link to it.
- Title sections with the question the reader is asking (`What is a workload?`), not with a noun (`Overview`).
- Put links to the documentation in `HelpPanel.Footer`, at the end, not inline in every section.
- Close affordances belong to the host. Do not put a close button in `HelpPanel.Header`; the `Drawer` or side rail already has one.
- How it opens in the console: the panel is the body of `ConsoleLayout`'s `tools` slot, and the page opens it with `ConsoleLayout.ToolsTrigger`, the `Info` link placed first in `PageHeader`'s `meta` slot, right after the page title. The trigger's `click` runs before the region toggles, so the page sets the topic there. Never open help from a boxed icon button, a typed `?` or a `Tooltip`.

## Don’t

- A one-line hint attached to a single control → use `tooltip` or `hint`, or the field's `field-description`.
- A guided tutorial with tasks, progress and hotspots on the real controls → use `tutorial-panel`.
- The region itself (overlay, slide-in, close button, focus trap) → use `drawer`; put `help-panel` inside it.
- Ordered steps the reader navigates between, with the step's form filling the column beside it → use `stepper`.
- Numbered instructions inside a documentation page, read all at once → use `doc-steps` (`DocSteps.Step`).
- A page with nothing configured yet, which needs one call to action → use `empty-state`.

## Related

- `drawer` — the host that opens, closes and traps focus around a help panel shown as an overlay.
- `tutorial-panel` — guided tutorials, drawn with these parts plus its own task list.
- `link` — the standalone link each `HelpPanel.Footer` row is composed from.
- `skeleton` — what the panel renders in place of its content while `loading`.
- `doc-prose` — long-form documentation prose; a help section is a few short paragraphs, not an article.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the complementary landmark the panel renders. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Help`). |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders skeleton lines in place of the content while the help topic loads; sets aria-busy. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The panel's parts — `HelpPanel.Header`, `HelpPanel.Group`, `HelpPanel.Footer` — in reading order. Not rendered while `loading`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-footer`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: an `index.ts` (beside `help-panel.vue`) attaches every sub-component
to the root so `<HelpPanel.Header>`, `<HelpPanel.Group>` and `<HelpPanel.Footer>` resolve from one
import; the standalone imports remain the tree-shaking path. The panel has no open/closed state, so
there is no `Trigger` / `Content` — every member is named after a part of a help page. 6.0 removed the
tutorial mode (`HelpPanel.Tutorial`, `HelpPanel.Task`): `TutorialPanel` owns tutorials.

- `help-panel-header/help-panel-header.vue` — The topic's title and an optional one-line description.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `''` — the topic's name, rendered as the panel's heading), `description?: string` (default `''` — one line under the title saying what the topic covers; not rendered when empty).
  - Slot: `default` — optional extra content under the description (a `Tag` naming the product state, for example).
  - `data-testid` fallback: `help-panel-header`.
- `help-panel-group/help-panel-group.vue` — One block of guidance with its own heading.
  - Props: `label?: string` (default `''` — the question this section answers; the section renders no heading when empty).
  - Slot: `default` — the section's prose: paragraphs, short lists, inline `text-link` anchors.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `help-panel-group`.
- `help-panel-footer/help-panel-footer.vue` — The "Learn more" footer: a heading over a column of `Link` items the consumer composes.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `undefined` — the heading over the links; absent uses the locale catalog, `Learn more` in English, and an empty string renders no heading).
  - Slot: `default` — `Link` items, one per destination.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `help-panel-footer`.
    Resulting layout (no per-component `package.json`; the root `packages/webkit/package.json#exports`
    resolves every path, and `.d.ts` is generated at publish time):

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/help-panel/
├── help-panel.vue                         (root; aside landmark, loading state)
├── help-panel.test.ts
├── index.ts                               (compound: attaches the three parts to the root)
├── help-panel-header/
│   └── help-panel-header.vue
├── help-panel-group/
│   └── help-panel-group.vue
└── help-panel-footer/
    └── help-panel-footer.vue
```

Exports to add to `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` (flat public names; category lives in the
folder only):

```jsonc
"./help-panel": "./src/components/content/help-panel/index.ts",
"./help-panel-root": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel.vue",
"./help-panel-header": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-header/help-panel-header.vue",
"./help-panel-group": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-group/help-panel-group.vue",
"./help-panel-footer": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-footer/help-panel-footer.vue"
```

Composed DS components (all present in `packages/webkit/package.json#exports`, imported by relative path
inside the package): `skeleton` (root, `loading`), `divider` (`Links`).
`link` is composed by the consumer through slots, never imported by the panel.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading`
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors the `loading` prop
- No `data-state` — the panel has no open/closed state (the host owns it)
- No `data-disabled` — nothing in the panel is interactive on its own; interactive content (`Link`, `Button`) is composed by the consumer and carries its own states

The root, while `loading`: the default slot is not rendered; in its place the root renders a title
line and three body lines with `Skeleton` (`variant="rectangle"`; title `width="60%"` `height="1.25rem"`, body
lines `width="100%"`, `width="100%"`, `width="75%"`, each `height="0.875rem"`), and sets
`aria-busy="true"`. The loading lines carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the landmark keeps its accessible
name.

- Responsive: the root is the `@container/help-panel`, so the content in the side panel adapts to the panel width.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the panel itself is not focusable; focus rings belong to the composed `Link` / `Button` controls, which already carry `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the composed links and action buttons in reading order. The panel adds no key handling of its own — no roving tabindex, no arrow navigation. `Esc` and focus trap / restore are owned by the host (`Drawer`), not by the panel.
- ARIA: the root is an `<aside>` (complementary landmark) named by `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`; `aria-busy="true"` while `loading`. Headings form an outline — `HelpPanel.Header` is `<h2>`, `Section` / `Links` titles are `<h3>` — and each `<section>` is `aria-labelledby` its heading via `useId()`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons)
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable to the panel's own markup (nothing in it is interactive); the composed `Link` / `Button` controls meet it

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import HelpPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="max-w-(--container-xs)">
    <HelpPanel aria-label="Help: Cache settings">
      <HelpPanel.Header
        title="Cache settings"
        description="How long content stays at the edge before it is fetched again."
      />
      <HelpPanel.Group label="What does the cache TTL control?">
        <p>
          The TTL sets how many seconds an object is served from the edge before the origin is asked
          for a fresh copy.
        </p>
      </HelpPanel.Group>
      <HelpPanel.Group label="When should I bypass the cache?">
        <p>Bypass it for responses that change per user, such as carts and account pages.</p>
      </HelpPanel.Group>
      <HelpPanel.Footer>
        <Link
          label="Cache settings documentation"
          href="https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/"
          target="_blank"
        />
        <Link
          label="Purging cached content"
          href="https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/"
          target="_blank"
        />
      </HelpPanel.Footer>
    </HelpPanel>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Illustration

> Renders an **official product illustration** — one of the scenes drawn in the Assets library in Figma and exported as an SVG that ships with this package. `name` selects a scene from a closed registry; there is no way to assemble artwork out of markup, so a page can only render illustrations design has actually signed off, and a scene can never drift between the screens that use it. The library is drawn once, in dark mode. The scene is drawn into the page as inline SVG and every colour it carries is repainted from the `illustration` theme foundation of `@aziontech/theme` — `--illustration-*` roles that alias the global tokens — so the one export follows light and dark like the rest of the page.

- Import: `import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Illustration for a static official scene.
- An empty state, error page, onboarding step, or marketing tile needs a diagrammatic illustration of a product concept (a deploy, a request path, a connected service).
- The same concept appears on more than one screen and must be the same drawing every time.
- The artwork must scale to its container without rasterizing or re-exporting.

## Do

- Leave the illustration decorative (no `ariaLabel`) unless it carries information the surrounding copy does not. A decorative illustration is hidden from assistive tech, which keeps screen readers out of a graphic that adds nothing.
- Size the illustration from the call site with a class. The root is `w-full` at the canvas aspect ratio, so a narrower column simply gets a smaller scene.
- Pick the scene that draws the claim next to it, not the one whose filename matches the page title.
- Find the names in `llms/foundations/illustrations.md` (installed under `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/llms/`), the MCP tool `list_assets` (`kind: "illustration"`) or the Assets example. Never guess a name from a file name or a page title: an unknown name renders the placeholder.
- To add a scene, export the frame from the Figma assets library (592×300 for a scene, the tile's own size for a tile or crop), drop the `.svg` into `src/assets/illustrations/`, and register it in `registry.ts`. The test fails while a drawing in the folder is unregistered. Never hand-draw one.
- Leave `<Illustration />` unnamed where a scene is still being drawn: the placeholder frame reserves the space and reads as unfinished on the screen, which is louder than a gap nobody notices.

## Don’t

- A single glyph is enough → use an icon from `@aziontech/icons` (`<i class="az az-…">`).
- The artwork is a brand mark (a client logo, a framework mark) → those are brand assets, not illustrations.
- The whole component is "no data here, with a title and an action" → use `empty-state`, which already owns that layout and may embed an `Illustration`.
- The graphic is a live data visualization → that is a chart, not an illustration.
- The scene you need is not in the registry → it has to be drawn in Figma and exported first. Do not approximate it in markup.

## Related

- `empty-state` — the surrounding layout (illustration + title + description + actions); reach for it first and put an `Illustration` inside it.
- `flow-diagram` — a real interactive node/edge diagram driven by data; `Illustration` is decorative and static by comparison.
- `skeleton` — the loading placeholder; an illustration is never a loading state.
- `brand` — the Azion mark; an illustration never draws it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | no | Name of an official scene in the illustration asset library. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | no | Accessible name; empty keeps the illustration decorative and hidden from assistive tech. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.

## States

- Visual states: `default` — an illustration is decorative and has no `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`, `loading`, or `active` state, and is never interactive.
- Most scenes are drawn on the one 592×300 canvas, so they line up with each other in a grid; a few tiles and crops (listed with their canvas in `src/assets/illustrations/frames.ts`, which the component test checks against every SVG) keep the canvas they were drawn on. The root is in the page from the first render, before the scene's SVG loads, and declares the canvas that scene was drawn on as its intrinsic `width`/`height` from the start (592×300 for the placeholder and every scene on the shared canvas), so the box has its final size and nothing below it moves when the scene arrives. It renders at its container's width at that aspect ratio. Until a scene is painted the empty root stays decorative (`aria-hidden`), and takes its `ariaLabel` once the scene is drawn. A call site that wants it smaller caps it with a class.
- A `name` that resolves to no scene — empty, or not in the registry — renders the **placeholder**: a tinted frame reading `PLACE DESIGN ASSET`, marked `data-placeholder`, on the 592×300 canvas. An unregistered `name` also warns in the console, naming where the valid names are listed; neither case throws, and neither collapses the layout. The placeholder is always decorative, `ariaLabel` or not: it draws no scene, so announcing a description of the missing artwork would describe something that is not on the page.
- While a registered scene's SVG is still resolving, the frame already on screen stays — the placeholder never flashes in front of a scene that is about to arrive.
- Theme: each colour of the export palette maps to one `--illustration-*` role (see § Tokens), resolved where the scene renders, so a scene inside a `[data-theme]` subtree follows that subtree. A translucent ground colour is a drop shadow and stays as drawn; colours that read the same in both themes (window controls, framework marks, the dot map) stay as drawn too. Masks, clip paths and filters are never repainted.
- A dotted scene (a dot map, a pixel grid) is stored with the dots of one paint merged into one path, so it draws a few hundred nodes; a standards test caps every inline asset at 200 paths.
- Every scene fills its frame: the asset's `viewBox` is cropped to the drawn artwork (glows included) with a small margin, at the frame's aspect ratio. Artwork that runs off an edge on purpose keeps the full frame.
- Every instance scopes the SVG's internal ids, so two scenes — or two copies of one — on the same page never resolve each other's gradients, masks or filters.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: _not applicable_ — an illustration is never focusable or interactive, so it declares no focus ring.
- Keyboard map: _none_ — no interactive elements, nothing in the tab order.
- ARIA: the root is an inline `<svg>`. With no `ariaLabel` it carries `aria-hidden="true"` and no role, so assistive tech skips a purely decorative graphic; with an `ariaLabel` it carries `role="img"` and the label as its `aria-label`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the component declares no text and no colour. An exported scene is decorative shape, not information — no meaning is conveyed by the artwork alone, so the copy beside it must carry the claim.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: _not applicable_ — nothing here is a target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'
</script>

<template>
  <Illustration name="modern-frontends" />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/illustration.md](components/illustration.md).

<!-- components/image-gallery.md -->

# Image Gallery

> The images of one response: a responsive grid of thumbnails that opens one image larger in a `Dialog`, with previous, next and Download. It takes each image as a URL or as base64 data with its media type, so a chat can show the images a model returned in a message or a generation finished with. While images are generating it holds one `Skeleton` per expected image, and when the request fails it shows the error in place of the grid. It draws what the app hands it; it generates and fetches nothing.

- Import: `import ImageGallery from '@aziontech/webkit/image-gallery'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The images in an assistant message: one or several image parts, from a URL or base64 data.
- The result of an image generation request: several images, a generating state and a failed state.
- Any set of a few related images a person wants to look at one by one and download.

## Do

- Pass `alt` from what the image shows (a model's revised prompt is a good source); an image with no `alt` is named by its position ("Image 2 of 4").
- Give every item a stable `key` (the message id and the part index) so the grid keeps each image when items arrive one by one.
- Set `expectedCount` to the number of images requested, so the placeholders match the result.
- Base64 data stays in memory as a data URL; for large images prefer a URL the app serves.
- Handle `download` and call `event.preventDefault()` when the image is on another origin or needs a signed URL; a same-origin, `blob:` or `data:` image downloads by itself.

## Don’t

- One stored file with its name, size and type, in a file browser — use `FilePreview`.
- A row of marketing cards or images that scrolls sideways — use `Carousel`.
- A picture you already have at a known size inside text or a card — a plain `img` is enough.
- Files attached to a prompt before it is sent — use `FileTokenGroup`.

## Related

- `Dialog` — the viewer that opens one image larger.
- `Skeleton` — the placeholder per expected image while images generate.
- `EmptyState` — the error state, the empty state and an image that fails to load in the viewer.
- `FilePreview` — one stored file with a type-aware body.
- `ChatMessage` — the message an image gallery sits in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `ImageGalleryItem[]` | `[]` | false | Images to show, each from a URL (`src`) or base64 `data` with its `mimeType`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Images are still generating: placeholders fill the grid after the images already in `items`, up to `expectedCount`. |
| `expectedCount` | `number` | `1` | false | Number of images expected while `loading`; the grid shows a placeholder for each one not in `items` yet. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Why the images could not load or generate. Set, the gallery shows the error state in place of the grid, with this text under its title. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `download` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: ImageGalleryItem)` | Download in the viewer was pressed for `item`. Download is a link with the `download` attribute, so the browser saves a same-origin, `blob:` or `data:` image unless the handler calls `preventDefault()`; browsers ignore `download` on a cross-origin URL and open it instead, so an app with cross-origin images handles this event (`preventDefault()` and its own download). |
| `retry` | `(event: MouseEvent)` | Try again in the error state was pressed. The button renders only when this event has a listener, so a gallery whose app cannot run the request again shows no dead button; the app starts the request again and clears `error`. |

## States

- Precedence: `error` wins over everything (no image, placeholder or empty state shows). Otherwise the images in `items` render first, then, while `loading`, one placeholder for each of `expectedCount - items.length` (none when `expectedCount` is at most `items.length`). With no image and no placeholder the empty state shows.
- `data-layout`: `single` (one tile) | `pair` (two tiles) | `grid` (three or more), counted over the images and the placeholders.
- `data-loading` mirrors `loading`; the root has `aria-busy`, and each placeholder is a `Skeleton` tile hidden from assistive technology.
- `data-error` is set while `error` is set: the grid is replaced by an `EmptyState` titled `The images could not load` with the `error` text as its description, inside a `role="alert"` region. With a `retry` listener the error state also shows a Try again `Button` (`az az-refresh`, outline, medium) under the message.
- `data-empty` is set when there is no image, no placeholder and no error: an `EmptyState` that says `No images`.
- `data-broken` is set on a thumbnail whose image fails to load (it then shows the `az az-image` glyph on the surface and keeps its name) and on the viewer body for that image, which shows an `EmptyState` (`This image could not load`); Download stays.
- Viewer: `Dialog` with `data-state="open|closed"` (from `Dialog`); Previous is disabled on the first image and Next on the last.
- Not applicable: the component has no `disabled`, `readonly` or `invalid` state; it is read-only content.

## Accessibility

- Patterns: the grid is a plain list of buttons (`ul` named `Images`, one `button` per `li`), with no composite widget and no roving tabindex; the viewer follows the APG Dialog (Modal) pattern through `Dialog`.
- Each thumbnail is a native `button` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`; its content is the image, so the image's `alt` (or `Image 2 of 4`) names the button. A broken thumbnail keeps the same name.
- Viewer: `Dialog` traps focus and, on open, moves focus to its first focusable control (the Close button in its header); `Esc` closes and focus returns to the thumbnail that opened it. The title is the image's `alt` (or its position); the `n of total` counter is a polite live region, so moving to another image is announced.
- Previous and Next are `IconButton`s (`az az-chevron-left`, `az az-chevron-right`) named `Previous image` / `Next image`; when one becomes disabled while it has focus (Next on the last image, Previous on the first), focus moves to the other one, so focus is never lost. Disabled, they take their contrast from `IconButton`'s disabled tokens.
- Download is a `Button` with a visible label and the `az az-download` glyph; it renders as a link and the `download` attribute reaches the anchor through its attributes (no prop).
- Keyboard: `Tab` moves through thumbnails; `Enter`/`Space` opens one; in the viewer `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` go to the previous/next image (mirrored under `rtl`) and `Home`/`End` to the first/last; `Tab` follows the `Dialog` order — Close in the header, then Previous, Next and Download — and wraps; `Esc` closes.
- Live announcements: a visually hidden `role="status"` line says `Generating images` while `loading`, and `Images ready` once `loading` turns false with images to show; the error state is a `role="alert"` region, so a failed generation is announced. Placeholders are `aria-hidden`.
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on each thumbnail.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the counter text; ≥3:1 for the broken glyph and the tile border on hover.
- Touch target: see Responsive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  import aiGateway from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/ai-gateway.svg'
  import branches from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/branches.svg'
  import ddosProtection from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/ddos-protection.svg'
  import usageChart from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/usage-chart.svg'
  import ImageGallery from '@aziontech/webkit/image-gallery'

  const items = [
    { key: 'gateway', src: aiGateway, alt: 'AI gateway illustration' },
    { key: 'ddos', src: ddosProtection, alt: 'DDoS protection illustration' },
    { key: 'usage', src: usageChart, alt: 'Usage chart illustration' },
    { key: 'branches', src: branches, alt: 'Branches illustration' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <ImageGallery
    class="max-w-(--container-md)"
    :items="items"
  />
</template>
```

# Integration Card

> Use IntegrationCard for one tile of a catalog of integrations, extensions or plugins; for a bordered box of related content use Card, and for a collection of resource records shown as cards use CardList. A catalog tile laid out from props: a logo mark, the item name, its vendor, a short description, badges, the installed state and one action. The name is the tile's single target: a link when `href` is set, otherwise a button that emits `select`, stretched over the whole tile. `featured` gives the centred, raised layout used for a short row of picks above the full catalog. It was the `integration` variant of `Card` until 6.0, split out because a tile shares neither the header nor the footer of a content card.

- Import: `import IntegrationCard from '@aziontech/webkit/integration-card'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A catalog tile for an integration, an extension or a plugin: the logo, the name, the vendor, a short description, badges, the installed state and one action.
- A short row of highlighted integrations above the full catalog (Featured): add `featured` for the centred, raised layout with the badges in the corner.
- A starter template or next-step tile that carries a mark, a name and a short description and links somewhere.

## Do

- The tile is laid out from props: `title`, `logo` (or the `logo` slot), `vendor`, `description`, `badges` and `installed`. The title becomes a link when `href` is set, otherwise a button that emits `select`, and it stretches over the whole tile so the tile is one target. Put a single action (Install, Configure) in the `actions` slot; it sits above the stretched target and stays reachable on its own.
- Keep the description to one or two sentences; the tile clamps it to three lines.
- Show at most two badges (category, context, plan). The installed state is a prop, not a badge, so it reads the same everywhere.
- Tiles sit under a section heading, so their title is an `h3`.
- `featured` centres the mark, the name, the vendor and the description on a raised surface with a primary glow at the top, and moves the badges to the top end corner, and a badge without `severity` or `variant` stays `info`, as on the plain tile. Use it for a row of at most three or four picks above the full catalog, never for every tile; the full catalog keeps the plain tile.

## Don’t

- A bordered box of related content with a title, a body and a footer → use `card`.
- One record of a resource list shown as cards, with selection and fields → use `card-list` (with `useCollection`).
- One tier of a pricing comparison → use `pricing-card`.
- A single row of title, description, media and actions → use `item`.

## Related

- `card` — the content box this tile was split from; shares its surface tokens.
- `tag` — renders the badges and the Installed state.
- `card-list` — the resource list in card form, with selection.
- `view/view-marketplace` — the block that lays these tiles out in a filtered grid.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The item name; the tile's single target. |
| `logo` | `string` | `''` | false | Icon class for the logo mark. The `logo` slot takes an image instead. |
| `vendor` | `string` | `''` | false | Who publishes the item, shown as "by {vendor}". |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One or two sentences on what the item does. |
| `badges` | `IntegrationCardBadge[]` | `[]` | false | Small tags such as the category or the context (`{ label, variant?, severity? }`, `variant` a `TagVariant` and `severity` a `TagSeverity` (`IntegrationCardBadgeVariant` and `IntegrationCardBadgeSeverity`); a badge with neither is `info`, in the plain and the featured layout). |
| `installed` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the Installed tag. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | The title links here; without it the title is a button that emits `select`. |
| `featured` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The featured layout, centred on a raised surface with a primary glow at the top and the badges in the top end corner. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `event: MouseEvent` | Without `href`: the title (the whole tile) was activated. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Extra content under the description. |
| `logo` | — | Replaces the logo mark, for an `img` with an empty `alt`. |
| `actions` | — | One action at the end of the tile, above the stretched title target. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`
- `hover` shades the surface, `focus-visible` rings the whole tile (the ring sits on the stretched title target), `installed` adds the success Installed tag.
- Featured (`featured`): the surface is raised; `hover` strengthens the border and brightens the top glow instead of shading the surface; the layout is centred and the badges sit in the top end corner. `data-featured` on the root drives the styles.
- Test ids: `integration-card` on the root, with `__logo`, `__title`, `__vendor`, `__installed`, `__actions`, and `__glow` and `__badges` when featured.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the stretched title target draws an inset `focus-visible:after:ring-2 focus-visible:after:ring-(--ring-color)` around the whole tile, so `overflow-clip` on the tile never cuts it.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the title (a link or a button) and then the action; `Enter` activates the title (`Space` too when it is a button).
- ARIA: the root is a `section`; the title is an `h3` holding the link or the button; the logo mark is `aria-hidden`; the featured glow is `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the hover and glow transitions.
- Touch target: the whole tile is the title's target; the action is a regular `Button`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import IntegrationCard from '@aziontech/webkit/integration-card'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const opened = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-[400px] flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <IntegrationCard
      title="Request Signer"
      vendor="Acme Inc."
      logo="az az-key"
      description="Sign every request at the edge with a rotating key, so the origin only answers traffic that passed through."
      :badges="[{ label: 'Firewall' }]"
      @select="opened = 'Request Signer'"
    >
      <template #actions>
        <Button
          label="Install"
          variant="outline"
          size="small"
        />
      </template>
    </IntegrationCard>
    <p
      class="m-0 text-body-xs text-(--text-muted)"
      role="status"
    >
      {{ opened ? `Opened ${opened}` : '' }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Item

> Use Item rows for a short list of mixed rows (title, description, actions) that do not share columns; read-only label/value facts about one resource are KeyValueList, records compared across columns are a Table, and what a plan includes is a PlanFeatureList. Versatile flex row for title, description, media, and actions. Mirrors the shadcn-vue Item anatomy so consumers can reorder or omit regions. Compose with `ItemGroup` for gapped off-card lists, `ItemList` for divided in-card lists (inside a `Card`), and `ItemSeparator` between rows. Reference: https://www.shadcn-vue.com/docs/components/item (adapted to Webkit tokens and naming).

- Import: `import ItemRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/item-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Item from '@aziontech/webkit/item'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A row that pairs a title and description with leading media (icon, avatar, image) and trailing actions — settings entries, team members, next steps, notifications.
- A list of such rows: `Item.Group` for gapped rows off a card, `Item.List` for divided rows inside a `card`.
- A whole row that is one link or button — set `href` and the row renders as an anchor, or set `clickable` and bind `@click` and it renders as a native button.
- A compact option in a chooser list (a workload, a host, an application picked under a search field): `variant="option"` with `clickable`, so the row is a native button. The row is 38 px — `--spacing-xs` block padding, `--spacing-sm` inline padding and gap, the title at `text-body-md` — and paints `var(--bg-selected)` when the row is `aria-pressed="true"` or `aria-selected="true"`.

## Do

- Use `Item.Group` off-card and `Item.List` inside a `card` with `:padded="false"`; both force their child items' `variant` (`inline` in a group, `default` in a list), so do not set `variant` on rows inside them.
- `Item.List` draws its own dividers — do not add `Item.Separator` inside it.
- With `href` or `clickable` the whole row is one focusable control with the row's hover, active and focus ring, so do not also put buttons or links inside that row.
- Set `Item.Media` `type="icon"` for a glyph and `type="image"` for a picture; the frame sizes and clips the content.
- Use `size="small"` for dense lists; `medium` is the default.
- For the rows of a picker under a search field use `variant="option"` (not `size="small"` plus your own padding): it sets its own density and the selected fill from `aria-pressed` / `aria-selected`, so `size` does not change it. Keep option rows in a plain column, not in `Item.List` or `Item.Group`, which force their own variant.

## Don’t

- Records that share columns and need sorting, selection or paging → use `table`.
- Hierarchical navigation rows in a sidebar → use `sidebar-menu`.
- A grid of selectable option cards → use `radio-group` with `variant="card"`.
- A single surface that frames arbitrary content → use `card`.

## Related

- `card` — the surface an `Item.List` sits in (with `:padded="false"`).
- `table` — columnar data; below `sm`, `listing-table-section` swaps its table rows for `item` rows.
- `sidebar-menu` — navigation rows with nesting and drill levels.
- `avatar` — the usual leading media for people rows inside `Item.Media`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'outline' \| 'muted' \| 'inline' \| 'option'` | `'default'` | false | Item root surface variant. `inline` removes the row's outer padding (transparent surface) for inline placement and divided in-card lists. `option` is a compact chooser row (38 px, title at body-md) that fills when its element is pressed or selected. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Item root density (padding and gap). |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | When set, the whole row renders as an anchor link to this URL. |
| `clickable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the whole row as a button; bind the click handler on the Item. Ignored when href is set. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Every sub-component exposes `default` for its region. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/item-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-list`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-separator`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-media`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-actions`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-footer`

## Sub-components

- `item.vue` — Root row container (`variant`, `size`).
- `item-group.vue` — Vertical list wrapper (`role="list"`) with a gap between rows; for off-card lists.
- `item-list.vue` — Vertical list wrapper (`role="list"`) that draws full-width dividers between rows and no gap; for in-card lists (inside a `Card` with `padded=false`).
- `item-separator.vue` — Horizontal divider between rows in a group.
- `item-media.vue` — Leading media slot (`type` for icon/image frames).
- `item-content.vue` — Main text column (title + description).
- `item-title.vue` — Primary label line.
- `item-description.vue` — Secondary muted text.
- `item-actions.vue` — Trailing actions cluster.
- `item-header.vue` — Optional top band (e.g.
- `item-footer.vue` — Optional bottom band.

## States

- Visual states on Item shell: `default` only, **except with `href` or `clickable`**, where the root is the whole-row anchor or button and gains row-level `hover`, `active`, and `focus-visible`
- With `href` or `clickable`, the row paints `var(--bg-selected)` while it carries `aria-pressed="true"`, `aria-selected="true"` or `aria-checked="true"` (a row with `role="radio"` in a one-of-many pick list), whatever its `variant`: a pressed chooser row binds `:aria-pressed` on the Item and adds no fill class of its own
- Without `href` or `clickable`, the root is a `div` and slotted controls (`Button`, `a`, etc.) own hover, active, and `focus-visible`
- `data-variant` on Item root: `default` | `outline` | `muted` | `inline` | `option` (an Item inside `ItemGroup` is forced to `inline`; inside `ItemList` to `default`)
- `variant="option"`: `--spacing-xs` block padding, `--spacing-sm` inline padding and gap whatever the `size`, `Item.Title` at `text-body-md`, and `var(--bg-selected)` on the row while it carries `aria-pressed="true"`, `aria-selected="true"` or `aria-checked="true"`
- `data-size` on Item root: `small` | `medium`
- `data-type` on ItemMedia: `default` | `icon` | `image`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: on slotted links and buttons. The Item shell draws no focus ring on its own, except with `href` or `clickable`, where the row itself (an anchor or a native button) receives the `focus-visible` ring (`focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`) and hover/active feedback.
- Keyboard map: slotted links and buttons supply Tab order; with `href` the row is one link (`Enter` follows it), with `clickable` one native button (`Enter` and `Space` activate it).
- ARIA: `ItemGroup` and `ItemList` use `role="list"` and tell their direct Items, through context, that they are list members; the consumer wires nothing. A member Item renders `role="listitem"` on its root. A member Item with `href` or `clickable` renders a `role="listitem"` wrapper (`data-slot="item-listitem"`) around its anchor or button root, so a link row stays a link. An Item outside a list, or nested inside another Item, gets no list role. `ItemSeparator` uses `role="separator"`, and `role="none"` when it sits directly inside a list, where a separator is not an allowed child.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for title and description text.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on color transitions.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on slotted actions (owned by children).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Item from '@aziontech/webkit/item'
</script>

<template>
  <Item>
    <Item.Content>
      <Item.Title>storefront-prod</Item.Title>
      <Item.Description>Deployed from main</Item.Description>
    </Item.Content>
    <Item.Actions>
      <Button
        label="Open"
        variant="outline"
        size="small"
      />
    </Item.Actions>
  </Item>
</template>
```

<!-- components/kbd.md -->

# Kbd

> Kbd renders keyboard input — a single key or a shortcut combination — as a compact, non-interactive keycap. It reads like a real key: a bordered surface with a thicker bottom edge for depth. Modifier keys are passed as boolean props (`meta`, `shift`, `alt`, `ctrl`) and rendered with the correct OS-aware glyph (⌘ on macOS, the catalog's `Ctrl` elsewhere), and named keys (`keyName`) print their localized name, so consumers never hardcode platform symbols or English key names. The platform is read once mounted: the server and the first client render print the non-Mac names, then a Mac swaps in its glyphs, so hydration never mismatches. Use it for shortcut hints in prose, menus, and control suffixes (e.g. the ⌘K hint in `command`). A sequence can also be passed as a `keys` list (`['meta', 'shift', 'p']`, `['arrow-up', 'arrow-down']`), drawn either as one keycap (`variant="combined"`, the default) or as one keycap per key (`variant="separate"`, each a nested `<kbd>` as HTML specifies for key combinations). Arrow keys and the Return glyph (`↵`) are named keys like `escape`.

- Import: `import Kbd from '@aziontech/webkit/kbd'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Show a keyboard shortcut or a single key inline (a ⌘K hint on a search button, an `Esc` hint in a dialog, `/` to focus search).
- Present a modifier combination whose glyph should adapt to the user's OS.

## Do

- Keep the default slot to a single key or glyph (`K`, `7`, `Enter`, `Esc`, `/`); avoid lowercase words or sentences.
- Pass modifiers as boolean props rather than hardcoding `⌘`/`⇧` so the glyph adapts to the OS.
- Name a key with `key-name` (`<Kbd key-name="escape" />`) instead of typing `Esc` or `Enter`: the text comes from the locale catalog (`kbd.*`), so it follows `ConfigProvider` (`Espaço` in pt-BR, `Intro` in es) and a consumer renames it with `messages` (`{ kbd: { ctrl: 'Strg' } }`). The macOS symbols `⌘`, `⌃`, `⌥` and `⇧` are never translated.
- Place surrounding punctuation outside the element, not inside the keycap.
- Use `keys` when the shortcut comes from data (a command list, a settings table); use the boolean props when you write it by hand. Pick `variant="separate"` for a sequence pressed key by key or for arrow pairs (`↑` `↓` to navigate), `combined` for a chord pressed at once.
- Name the Return key `return` (`↵`) in compact hints (a footer "↵ to select"); keep `enter` (`Enter`) where the word reads better.

## Don’t

- The token is a status/category label, not a key → use `tag` or `badge`.
- You need an interactive control that fires on click → use `button` / `icon-button`; Kbd is a presentational hint only.

## Related

- `command` — consumes Kbd for its per-item shortcut hints and its ⌘K trigger affordance.
- `badge` — compact non-interactive indicator for counts/status; Kbd is specifically for keyboard keys.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `meta` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the meta/command modifier glyph (⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere). |
| `ctrl` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the Control modifier glyph (⌃ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere). |
| `shift` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the Shift modifier glyph (⇧). |
| `alt` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the Alt/Option modifier glyph (⌥ on macOS, Alt elsewhere). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `small` is a denser keycap for menus, command bars, and table cells. |
| `keyName` | `'' \| 'ctrl' \| 'alt' \| 'shift' \| 'escape' \| 'enter' \| 'space' \| 'tab' \| 'backspace' \| 'delete' \| 'return' \| 'arrowUp' \| 'arrowDown' \| 'arrowLeft' \| 'arrowRight'` | `''` | false | Named key printed from the locale catalog (`escape` → `Esc`, `enter` → `Enter`); the slot still renders after it. |
| `keys` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | A key sequence drawn after the modifier props and `keyName`: `meta`/`ctrl`/`alt`/`shift` print their OS-aware glyph, a named key prints from the catalog (matched without case or hyphens, so `arrowUp`, `arrow-up` and the DOM's `ArrowUp` are one key), a single character is upper-cased, anything else prints as written. |
| `variant` | `'combined' \| 'separate'` | `'combined'` | false | Visual variant: one keycap holding every key, or one keycap per key. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The single key or glyph rendered after any modifier glyphs (`K`, `Enter`, `Esc`). |

## States

Kbd is non-interactive: it has no hover, focus, active, or disabled states and emits no events. Variants are exposed as `data-*` attributes on the root for Tailwind variant styling and for test/Code-Connect hooks:

- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop (`small` | `medium`).
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop (`combined` | `separate`). With `separate` the root drops its keycap chrome (border, surface, shadow, padding) and each key renders as a nested `<kbd>` keycap with the same size tokens, separated by `--spacing-2xs`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — Kbd is non-interactive (no focus, no keyboard, no tab stop).
- Keyboard map: none — Kbd is a presentational hint and exposes no interactive affordance.
- ARIA: the root is the native `<kbd>` element so assistive tech announces it as keyboard input; modifier glyphs render as text so a combination like ⌘K is announced in reading order.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-surface)` is theme-guaranteed in both light and dark.
- `motion-reduce:*`: not applicable — Kbd is static (no motion).
- Touch target: not applicable — Kbd is non-interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Kbd from '@aziontech/webkit/kbd'
</script>

<template>
  <Kbd meta>K</Kbd>
</template>
```

# Key Value List

> Use KeyValueList to show read-only label/value facts about one resource, including its tags; rows with their own actions are Item rows. A grid of labelled facts about one subject: each pair is a key (the term) and its value, which may be plain text or a composed component such as a `Link`, `Tag`, `CopyButton` or `StatusIndicator`. It renders a native description list laid out in 1 to 4 responsive columns, optionally split into titled groups, and owns its loading and empty-value surfaces. It replaces the hand-rolled label/value grids the resource detail templates (`ResourceSummary`, the detail Overview tabs) draw today.

- Import: `import KeyValueListRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-list-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import KeyValueList from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-list'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- The facts band of a resource detail or Overview page: ID, status, region, created at, domain.
- A read-only summary of settings before a confirm step (review step, deploy summary).
- Any set of named attributes of a single subject where the reader scans keys to find a value.
- Facts that fall into named clusters (General, Networking, Source) shown side by side as titled columns.
- The rows of a summary card, label on the left and value on the right (a subscription plan: Plan Price, Billing Period, Next Invoice): `variant="split"`.

## Do

- Keep keys short nouns in sentence case ("Created", "Region"), never sentences or trailing colons.
- Order pairs by what the reader looks for first: identity, status, then the rest.
- Pick `variant` by the box: `stacked` (label over value) for a facts band that spans a page; `split` (label at the start, value at the end of one row) for a narrow summary card where each row reads as a line of a receipt. Do not hand-write a `<dl>` with `justify-between` for it.
- Use `columns` for width, not for grouping; use `KeyValueList.Group` when the facts form named clusters, one group per column.
- Do not mix bare Items and Groups at the same level; pick one shape per instance.
- Leave the value slot out (or render nothing in it) when a value is absent; the component shows the em dash and its accessible "Not set". Do not type your own "-", "N/A" or "None".
- Put a `CopyButton` after an ID or key, never in place of the visible value.
- Use the `info` slot for a short `Hint` that explains the key; long explanations belong in the page, not in a tooltip.
- Drive `loading` from the data request so the labels stay in place and only the values shimmer.

## Don’t

- Rows of many subjects compared attribute by attribute → use `table`.
- Editable fields → use the form field components (`field` with `input`, `select`, …); this component is read-only.
- A single headline figure with a trend → use `stat-tile`.
- A list of items with no key/value relation → use a plain list or `item`.

## Related

- `table` — many subjects, one row each; KeyValueList describes one subject.
- `card` — the surface a KeyValueList usually sits in; KeyValueList brings no surface of its own.
- `copy-button` — the trailing copy affordance for IDs and keys inside a value.
- `status-indicator`, `tag` — status and category values.
- `link` — a value that navigates (a domain, a linked resource).
- `hint` — the info glyph composed into an Item's `info` slot.
- `skeleton` — rendered in place of each value while the root is `loading`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'stacked' \| 'split'` | `'stacked'` | false | How each pair is laid out: `stacked` puts the label over the value, `split` puts the label at the start and the value at the end of one row. |
| `columns` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4` | `1` | false | Columns at full width; fewer columns when a cell would get narrower than `--container-3xs`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Replaces every value with a skeleton while the data loads; labels stay visible. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list when no visible heading names it. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | `KeyValueList.Item` children, or `KeyValueList.Group` children — one shape per instance. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/key-value-list-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/key-value-list-group`

## Sub-components

The root `key-value-list.vue` renders a `<dl>` that is the grid. It provides a context (`injection-key.ts` + `composables/use-key-value-list-context.ts`) holding the root test id and the `loading` state, read-only. Every part throws a clear error when used outside `<KeyValueList>`.

Markup is valid HTML in both shapes: an Item is a `<div>` wrapping one `<dt>` and one `<dd>` (allowed as a direct child of `<dl>`). A Group is also a `<div>` child of the root `<dl>`: its title is the `<dt>`, and its `<dd>` holds a nested `<dl>` with the group's Items — a term whose description is a list of pairs. A heading element is not used for the group title because `<dt>` does not allow heading content.

- `key-value-list.vue` — the root: the `<dl>` grid, the `columns` layout, `aria-label`, `aria-busy`, the context.
- `key-value-list-item/key-value-list-item.vue` — one pair: `<div>` → `<dt>` (label + `info`) + `<dd>` (value).
  - Props: `label: string` (required — the key, rendered in the `<dt>`).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the value (text or composed components); fallback is the empty-value marker (`<span aria-hidden="true">—</span><span class="sr-only">Not set</span>`), shown when the slot is omitted or renders nothing. `info` — optional affordance after the label text inside the `<dt>`, such as a `Hint`.
  - While the root is `loading`, the `<dd>` renders a `Skeleton` in place of the value; the label stays visible. In the `split` variant the value cell shrinks to its content, so the skeleton there is `6rem` wide instead of the full cell.
  - `data-testid` fallback `${rootTestId}__item`; a consumer `data-testid` on the Item wins.
- `key-value-list-group/key-value-list-group.vue` — a titled column: `<div>` → `<dt>` (label) + `<dd>` → nested `<dl>` stacking its Items in one column.
  - Props: `label: string` (required — the group's term, shown above its Items).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the group's `KeyValueList.Item` children.
  - Occupies one cell of the root grid, so `columns` sets how many groups sit side by side.
  - `data-testid` fallback `${rootTestId}__group`; a consumer `data-testid` on the Group wins.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading`, empty value (per Item)
- `data-variant` on the root and on each Item mirrors `variant`; `split` turns each Item into one row (label start, value end, wrapping under the label only when the value does not fit)
- `data-columns` on the root mirrors `columns` and drives the grid template through `data-[columns=n]:` variants
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors `loading`; `aria-busy="true"` while loading
- Empty value: the Item's `<dd>` shows `—` (`aria-hidden`) plus a visually hidden "Not set"
- Responsive columns follow the list's own box, not the viewport: the grid is `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(100%, max(--container-3xs, share)), 1fr))`, where the share is the box divided by `columns`. It shows `columns` columns when every cell gets at least `--container-3xs` (256 px), fewer otherwise, and one column in a narrow box; a list in a drawer or split view lays out for that box.

- No `disabled`, `invalid`, `readonly`, `error`, `open` states: the component is read-only and fetches nothing. An error loading the facts is the page's surface (e.g. `message`), not this component's.

## Accessibility

- Native description list: root `<dl>`, each Item `<div>` → `<dt>` + `<dd>`; each Group `<div>` → `<dt>` + `<dd>` → nested `<dl>`. Screen readers announce term/definition pairs with no ARIA roles added.
- `ariaLabel` is applied as `aria-label` on the root `<dl>` only when non-empty; when a visible heading precedes the list, the consumer names it with `aria-labelledby` through `$attrs` instead.
- Loading: `aria-busy="true"` on the root; each `Skeleton` is decorative (`aria-hidden`), so assistive tech reads the labels and waits for the values.
- Empty value: `—` is `aria-hidden="true"`; a `sr-only` "Not set" gives the `<dd>` an announced value.
- Keyboard map: the component itself has no tab stop. Focus moves only through interactive values and `info` affordances (`Link`, `CopyButton`, `Hint`) in reading order, each with its own focus ring and key handling.
- Reading order follows source order: row by row across the grid, top to bottom inside a group.
- Contrast: `var(--text-muted)` keys and `var(--text-default)` values at ≥4.5:1 on `var(--bg-surface)` and `var(--bg-canvas)` in both themes.
- No motion of its own; the composed `Skeleton` carries `motion-reduce:animate-none`.
- Touch targets belong to the composed interactive values; the component adds none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'
  import KeyValueList from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-list'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
  import StatusIndicator from '@aziontech/webkit/status-indicator'
</script>

<template>
  <KeyValueList aria-label="Workload details">
    <KeyValueList.Item label="Workload ID">
      <span>1752167890</span>
      <CopyButton
        value="1752167890"
        aria-label="Copy workload ID"
        size="small"
      />
    </KeyValueList.Item>
    <KeyValueList.Item label="Status">
      <StatusIndicator
        severity="success"
        label="Active"
      />
    </KeyValueList.Item>
    <KeyValueList.Item label="Created">Nov 10, 2026, 2:32 PM</KeyValueList.Item>
    <KeyValueList.Item label="Region">US East (Virginia)</KeyValueList.Item>
    <KeyValueList.Item label="Domain">
      <Link
        label="shop.example.com"
        href="https://shop.example.com"
        inline
      />
    </KeyValueList.Item>
  </KeyValueList>
</template>
```
