# Message Thread

> The conversation of a support ticket, oldest first, as Help Scout, Front, Plain and the Zendesk Agent Workspace show it: each message names its author (avatar, name, customer or agent), the channel it came by, when it was sent and, for email, who received it; then the body, the attachments and the quoted previous messages behind a toggle. Three types of item share the list: a public reply, an internal note (a warning band labelled "Internal note", so it never reads as a reply sent to the customer), and a system event line ("Jane Doe changed status to Pending"). A long middle collapses behind "Show 6 earlier messages". It is not `ChatMessage`, which is the generative AI chat (decision SUP-03).

- Import: `import MessageThreadRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/message-thread-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import MessageThread from '@aziontech/webkit/message-thread'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: composition
- Stability: preview. The API may still change in a minor release, named in the changelog, until the owner marks it GA.

## When to use

- The conversation on a support ticket or a customer case: the customer's emails and chats, the agents' replies, the internal notes agents leave each other, and the status changes in between.
- An email-style message history where each message shows its sender, recipients (To, Cc), channel, attachments and the quoted text of earlier messages.
- A ticket that mixes public replies and private notes, where an agent must see at a glance which messages the customer can read.

## Do

- Render the items oldest first; the newest message sits at the end, next to the reply composer.
- Put every message after the first two and before the last three in a `MessageThread.Group` once a thread holds more than eight, so the newest messages stay in view.
- Pass `count` on the Group with the number of items it holds; the button reads it.
- Use `type="note"` for anything only agents can read; never colour a reply to make it look private.
- Put the text of earlier messages that an email quotes in the `quoted` slot, not in the body, so the reader sees only what is new.
- Keep the `actions` slot short: Reply as an `IconButton`, Forward and the rest as items of a More `DropdownMenu`.
- Write an event line as one short sentence that names who did what ("Jane Doe changed status to Pending").

## Don’t

- A chat with the generative AI assistant → `chat-message` inside `conversation`.
- A log of what happened to a resource, with no messages (deploys, status changes, audit entries) → the Timeline component planned in SUP-01.
- A single notice on a page → `alert`.
- Comments on a code line or a review → not this component; it carries support semantics (channels, recipients, internal notes).

## Related

- `chat-message` — the AI conversation turn (`from: user | assistant | system`, feedback thumbs, regenerate). A ticket has customers and agents, notes, channels and recipients instead (SUP-03).
- Timeline (planned in SUP-01) — an activity log of events; a thread interleaves a few event lines between messages.
- `timestamp` — the sent time of each item; it opens the full date in every zone.
- `avatar` — the author's picture or initials.
- `file-token-group`, `file-preview` — the attachments composed into an item's `attachments` slot.
- `icon-button`, `dropdown-menu` — the Reply button and the More menu (Forward, …) composed into an item's `actions` slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `timestampFormat` | `TimestampFormat` | `'local'` | false | How every item's sent time reads: `relative` (`2 hours ago`), `local` date and time, `utc`, or `time` (hour and minute only) — Timestamp's own union. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows three placeholder messages in place of the items while the thread loads, and marks it busy. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Conversation`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The `MessageThread.Item` and `MessageThread.Group` children, oldest first. Not rendered while `loading`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/message-thread-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/message-thread-group`

## Sub-components

Compound API through `index.ts` (`MessageThread.Item`, `MessageThread.Group`); standalone entries
`message-thread-root`, `message-thread-item`, `message-thread-group`. The root provides
`{ timestampFormat }` (`injection-key.ts`, `MessageThreadInjectionKey`, type `MessageThreadContext`);
`useMessageThreadContext()` (`composables/use-message-thread-context.ts`, a public named export of `index.ts`
with its type, `CODE_QUALITY.md` § 3.5 point 6, so an app can write its own context-aware part) throws outside a `MessageThread`, so a part rendered loose fails loudly.

The root is an `ol` (`role="list"`): every Item is an `li`, and a Group is an `li` holding a nested
`ol` of its Items once open. The parts never read their slot vnodes.

- `message-thread-item/message-thread-item.vue` — one item of the thread, an `li`.
  - `type="reply"` and `type="note"`: an `article` card. Header, three columns: the author's `Avatar` (`medium`, decorative, initials from `author` when `avatarSrc` is empty) at the inline start; in the middle a wrapping meta block of the identity (the name `__author`, the role `Customer` / `Agent` `__role`, the channel `via Email` with its glyph `__channel`, replies only) followed by the sent `Timestamp` (`__time`); and the `actions` slot (`__actions`) at the inline end, outside the meta block, so it never wraps away from the first line. Under the header, for a reply with recipients, a line `To: …` and `Cc: …` (`__recipients`, one `To` and one `Cc` line, the address list isolated). Then the body (`__content`, the default slot), the quoted-text toggle and region (`__quoted-toggle`, `__quoted`) when the `quoted` slot is given, and the `attachments` slot (`__attachments`).
  - `type="note"` adds a band across the top of the card (`__note`): a lock glyph and the words `Internal note`, on the warning fill. Channel and recipients are not shown on a note.
  - `type="event"`: no card, no article; one muted line (`__event`) with a history glyph, the default slot (the sentence) and the `Timestamp`. Author, avatar, role, channel, recipients, `quoted`, `attachments` and `actions` are not rendered.
  - Props: see the table below (`MessageThreadItemProps`).
  - v-model: `v-model:quotedOpen` — `boolean`, `defineModel('quotedOpen')`, default `false`, emits `update:quotedOpen`. The quoted-text toggle flips it.
  - Slots: `default` — the body (plain text keeps its line breaks, or composed content); `actions` — a Reply `IconButton` and a More `DropdownMenu` (Forward, …) at the end of the header; `attachments` — a read-only `FileTokenGroup` or `FilePreview`s under the body; `quoted` — the earlier messages an email quotes, hidden until the toggle opens it.
  - `data-testid` fallback `message-thread-item`; `data-slot="message-thread-item"`.
- `message-thread-group/message-thread-group.vue` — a run of items collapsed behind one button, an `li`.
  - Closed: a `Button` (`variant="outline"`, `size="small"`, `__toggle`) reading `Show {count} earlier messages`, centred between two hairlines. It reveals and is then replaced, like a load-more button, so it carries no `aria-expanded` or `aria-controls`; focus moves into what it revealed.
  - Open: a nested `ol` (`role="list"`, `__list`, named `Earlier messages`) holding the default slot. Opening moves focus to the first item's `article` (or `li` for an event) inside it, so a keyboard or screen reader user lands on the first revealed message.
  - Props: `count?: number` (default `0` — how many items the group holds, read in the button; `0` reads `Show earlier messages`).
  - v-model: `v-model:open` — `boolean`, `defineModel('open')`, default `false`, emits `update:open`.
  - Slots: `default` — the hidden `MessageThread.Item`s.
  - `data-testid` fallback `message-thread-group`; `data-slot="message-thread-group"`; `data-state="open|closed"`.

Exported types: `MessageThreadProps`, `MessageThreadItemProps`, `MessageThreadGroupProps`,
`MessageThreadItemType` (`'reply' | 'note' | 'event'`), `MessageThreadFrom`
(`'customer' | 'agent'`), `MessageThreadChannel` (`'email' | 'chat' | 'phone' | 'web' | 'api'`),
`MessageThreadContext`; `timestampFormat` reuses `TimestampFormat` exported by `timestamp`. Composed DS components: `timestamp`, `avatar`, `icon-button`, `button`,
`skeleton`.

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/message-thread/
├── message-thread.vue
├── message-thread.test.ts
├── index.ts
├── injection-key.ts
├── composables/use-message-thread-context.ts
├── message-thread-item/message-thread-item.vue
└── message-thread-group/message-thread-group.vue
```

Exports: `./message-thread` → `index.ts`, `./message-thread-root` → `message-thread.vue`,
`./message-thread-item`, `./message-thread-group` → their `.vue` files.

#### MessageThread.Item props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | JSDoc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'reply' \| 'note' \| 'event'` | `'reply'` | false | What the item is: a public reply, an internal note only agents read, or a system event line. |
| `author` | `string` | `''` | false | Name of who wrote the message, shown in the header and read in the item's accessible name. |
| `avatarSrc` | `string` | `''` | false | Image URL of the author's avatar. Empty shows the initials of `author`. |
| `from` | `'customer' \| 'agent'` | `'customer'` | false | Whether the author is the customer or an agent; shown as the role beside the name. |
| `channel` | `'email' \| 'chat' \| 'phone' \| 'web' \| 'api'` | `undefined` | false | How a reply came in or went out, shown as `via Email` with its glyph. Unset shows no channel. |
| `timestamp` | `string \| number \| Date` | `undefined` | false | When the item was sent: an ISO string, an epoch in milliseconds or a `Date`, rendered by `Timestamp`. |
| `to` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Email addresses the reply was sent to, shown on the recipients line. |
| `cc` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Email addresses copied on the reply, shown on the recipients line. |

## States

- Root: `data-testid` fallback `message-thread`, `data-slot="message-thread"`, `data-loading` and `aria-busy="true"` while `loading`; `data-timestamp-format` mirrors `timestampFormat`.
- Loading: three `li` placeholders (`__placeholder`), each an avatar circle and two text lines built from `Skeleton`, in place of the slot. When `loading` turns on, `Loading conversation` is announced through `useAnnouncer`; when it turns off, `Conversation loaded`.
- No empty state (`emptyTitle` is not taken, the second exception to § 3.7): a ticket always holds its first message; an app with nothing to show renders `EmptyState` instead of the thread.
- Item: `data-type` (`reply` | `note` | `event`), `data-from` (`customer` | `agent`, not on events), `data-channel` when `channel` is set. The quoted region (`__quoted`) carries `data-state` (`open` | `closed`).
- Group: `data-state` (`open` | `closed`).
- Quoted region: always rendered once the `quoted` slot is given, with the `hidden` attribute while closed, so the toggle's `aria-controls` always points at an element.
- States the thread does not own: `disabled`, `readonly` and `invalid` do not apply (the items are display-only; the controls in `actions` carry their own); there is no `error` / `retry` either. The thread is one region of a ticket page that loads the ticket as a whole, so a failed load is the page's own state (an `Alert` or `EmptyState` with Try again in place of the thread), as the `detail` blocks do. This is the explicit exception to the list state contract of `CODE_QUALITY.md` § 3.7, which is written for pickers and data lists that fetch and page their own rows; the thread keeps only its `loading`.
- Invalid or missing `timestamp`: the item shows no time (Timestamp is not rendered) and its accessible name is the author alone.

## Accessibility

- Structure: the root is an `ol` with `role="list"` (kept under `list-style: none`), named by `ariaLabel` or `Conversation`; each Item is an `li`. A reply or note is an `article` named by `aria-labelledby`: for a note the `Internal note` band, then the author name, then the Timestamp's text — so every message has a unique name ("Internal note Jane Doe Nov 20, 2026, 10:05 AM"). An event line is plain text in its `li`. It is a list of articles, not the APG Feed pattern (`role="feed"`): the thread does not load more as the reader scrolls; it collapses its middle behind a Group button instead.
- Never colour alone: a note carries the visible words `Internal note` and a lock glyph; the role is written (`Customer`, `Agent`); the channel is written beside its glyph. Every glyph is `aria-hidden`.
- The avatar is decorative (`aria-hidden`): the name beside it is the text.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the controls in reading order — each Timestamp, the item's actions, the quoted-text toggle, links and attachments in the content, the Group button. `Enter` / `Space` activate. Opening a Group moves focus to the first revealed item (`tabindex="-1"` on its `article` or `li`); nothing else moves focus.
- Quoted text: the toggle follows the WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure (Show/Hide) pattern: a small ghost `IconButton` (ellipsis glyph) named `Show quoted text` / `Hide quoted text`, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the region (`useId`), which is `hidden` while closed.
- Group: the button is a native `Button` that reveals and is replaced (no `aria-expanded`); open, the nested list is named `Earlier messages` and focus is on its first item.
- Loading: `aria-busy="true"` on the list; the placeholders are `aria-hidden`; the start and end are announced through `useAnnouncer`.
- Visible focus: the composed controls draw the ring token; the focused `article` after opening a Group draws `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Contrast: `--text-default` and `--text-muted` on `--bg-surface`, `--warning-foreground` on `--warning` — documented pairs in both themes.
- Touch target: the quoted toggle and the app's `IconButton`s are 32 px with a 44 px hit area on a coarse pointer; the Group button is a `Button` with the same hit area.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DropdownMenu from '@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu'
  import FileTokenGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/file-token-group'
  import IconButton from '@aziontech/webkit/icon-button'
  import MessageThread from '@aziontech/webkit/message-thread'

  const attachments = [{ file: { name: 'invoice-1042.pdf', size: 84000, type: 'application/pdf' } }]
  const body =
    'Hi, I was charged twice for the November invoice. Can you refund one of the payments?\n\nThanks,\nAlex'
```

<!-- components/network-map.md -->

# Network Map

> A decorative, full-bleed layer that paints the dotted world map with Azion's data centers lit in the brand accent. It is a material — it takes no content and claims no space — but unlike a static illustration it is tuned by the consumer (region, data center density, landmass opacity, static or animated) to sit behind a band's copy.

- Import: `import NetworkMap from '@aziontech/webkit/network-map'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use NetworkMap as a decorative world-map backdrop; for data by location use MapChart.
- As the backdrop of a band whose subject is the network (reach, data centers, latency, resilience), composed as a sibling under the band's copy inside a positioned, clipping ancestor.
- When a band is about one part of the network, so only that region's data centers should light (`region`) while the whole world stays drawn.
- When the same artwork has to read with more or fewer data centers lit, or with none at all (`density="none"`), from one component instead of separate exports.

## Do

- Give the layer a positioned ancestor (`relative overflow-hidden`); it fills that box and nothing else.
- Never offset or resize the layer with utilities (`left-*`, `w-*`, `inset-*`). It always fills its positioned ancestor, and `position` + `fade` place the map inside that box — so a fade measures from the band's own edges. An offset box moves the fade's edges off the band's and makes the two placements fight.
- To make the map smaller or larger inside its box, set `scale` instead of resizing the layer. The map shrinks toward its `position` corner, so there is no hard edge and the fade keeps measuring from the band's edges.
- Keep `opacity` low (the default `0.4`) when copy sits over the landmass; the data centers keep full strength so the network still reads.
- For copy on one side of a band, park the map on the other side with `position` and fade it toward the copy (`position="right"` + `fade="left"`); the default stops need no consumer class.
- Tune where a fade holds and ends with `--network-map-fade-start` / `--network-map-fade-end` only when the default stops do not fit, instead of adding masks.
- Leave `animated` off by default; turn it on for the one band per page whose subject is the network.
- To nudge the map or let it run off the band, set `offsetX` / `offsetY` (for example `:offset-x="0.15"` to bleed right, `:offset-y="-0.1"` to bleed up) instead of offsetting the layer.
- The landmass is the design's pixel map cell for cell (4,987 cells on a 10-unit grid), and the default `medium` density lights the design's data center field exactly: 172 cells, each metro a capital with up to two satellites, pulsing in the design's three phases. `low` lights the capitals alone (71); `high` adds 31 outlying data centers.
- `asia` and `oceania` hold no data centers — the artwork carries no accent field there — so either region lights none and the map reads as landmass alone, which looks like a broken map or no coverage on a page: do not place them, and the Regions example leaves them out.

## Don’t

- For a real node/edge diagram driven by data → use `flow-diagram`.
- As a wrapper around content. The layer is absolutely positioned and paints only itself; content is a sibling above it.

## Related

- `registration-frame` — the ruled box a network band usually sits in; it supplies the positioned, clipping ancestor.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `region` | `'world' \| 'atlantic' \| 'americas' \| 'north-america' \| 'south-america' \| 'europe' \| 'africa' \| 'asia' \| 'oceania'` | `'world'` | false | Which part of the world has its data centers lit; the map always frames the whole world. |
| `density` | `'none' \| 'low' \| 'medium' \| 'high'` | `'medium'` | false | How many data centers are lit, from `none` to `high`. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Pulses the data centers in three staggered waves that settle within five seconds; static when false. |
| `opacity` | `number` | `0.4` | false | Opacity of the landmass dots, from 0 to 1; the data centers stay at full strength. |
| `position` | `'center' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'top-left' \| 'top-right' \| 'bottom-left' \| 'bottom-right'` | `'center'` | false | Where the map parks in the space the box leaves over. |
| `scale` | `number` | `0.85` | false | Size of the map relative to the box; 1 fits it, below 1 shrinks it toward its position, above 1 enlarges it. |
| `offsetX` | `number` | `0` | false | Horizontal shift as a fraction of the map width; negative moves it left, positive right, past the box edge if large enough. |
| `offsetY` | `number` | `0` | false | Vertical shift as a fraction of the map height; negative moves it up, positive down, past the box edge if large enough. |
| `fade` | `'none' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'edges' \| 'vignette'` | `'none'` | false | Fades the map out along an axis so it meets content without a hard edge. |
| `traffic` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Draws traffic between lit data centers: faint links and, while `animated`, packets that cross them; the links alone under reduced motion. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-region`, `data-density` and `data-fade` on the root mirror their props; `data-fade` drives the mask that fades the layer out
- `density="none"` draws the landmass alone, with no hole where a data center would be — every data center cell is also a landmass cell
- `density` levels are cumulative: `low` (65 data centers) ⊂ `medium` (186) ⊂ `high` (275); `core` carries a data center on every main Brazilian capital, so they light at every density
- Each data center path carries `data-animated` (present only when `animated` is set) and `data-phase` (`0` / `1` / `2`), which select the pulse and its wave delay
- The map always frames the whole world; `region` only chooses which data centers light — a data center renders when its cell falls inside the region's bounds, and a phase with no data center left renders no path
- `scale` sizes the map around the `position` anchor, so it renders at that fraction of its fitted size while the anchored edge stays put; a value of 0 or below falls back to `1`
- `offsetX` / `offsetY` translate the map after `position` and `scale` place it, by that fraction of the map's own width / height; the sign is the direction (negative left / up, positive right / down), so each axis moves independently of the anchor
- The default `scale` of `0.85` leaves room on both axes, so every `position` moves the map in any box shape. At `1` the fitted map fills one axis edge to edge, so `position` acts only on the other axis: `top` / `center` / `bottom` render alike in a wide box, and `left` / `center` / `right` in a tall one
- `top` / `bottom` / `left` / `right` fade the map out toward that edge: full ink from the opposite edge up to `--network-map-fade-start`, zero at `--network-map-fade-end`, both measured from the opposite edge. `top` / `bottom` default to 16% / 55%; `left` / `right` default to 50% / 80%, which clears a copy column on that side of a band
- Custom properties tune the fade in place, set from the consumer's class: `--network-map-fade-start` / `--network-map-fade-end` (where the fade holds full ink and where it reaches zero)

## Accessibility

- Decorative: the root is `aria-hidden="true"` and `pointer-events-none`; the network's claims are carried by the band's copy, never by the artwork
- Keyboard map: none — the layer is not focusable and has no interactive parts
- Visible focus: not applicable (nothing receives focus)
- Contrast: not applicable to the artwork (decorative); the copy above it keeps its own ≥4.5:1 against the band, which the low default `opacity` protects
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` stops the pulse under reduced motion
- Pause, Stop, Hide (WCAG 2.2.2): with `animated`, the data center pulse and the traffic packets stop by themselves within 5 seconds of mount (pulses by 4.7 s, packets by 4.8 s) and rest on the static map, so the layer needs no pause control
- Touch target: not applicable (no interactive parts)

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import NetworkMap from '@aziontech/webkit/network-map'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="relative h-80 w-full overflow-hidden bg-(--bg-canvas)">
    <NetworkMap
      region="world"
      density="medium"
      :opacity="0.4"
      position="center"
      :scale="0.85"
      fade="none"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/network-map.md](components/network-map.md).

<!-- components/overflow-count.md -->

# Overflow Count

> Use OverflowCount for the '+N' that opens the hidden items of a truncated list; a plain number attached to something else is a Badge. A small `+N` chip that stands for the items a slot cannot show, and opens a popover with the whole list. It replaces the design sample's `DomainOverflowPopover`, the overflow badge of `TagListCell` and `WorkloadCell`, and the Console Kit's `OverflowCountButton`. The popover follows the overflow rule of `webkit-ux-heuristics`: a summary line (`12 domains`, `10 of 34 domains` while paged), a search box once the list holds more than 7 items, a scrolling list, a **Load N more** footer while items remain, a no-match line quoting the query, and a polite status region that announces the summary. Closing it clears the query and the paging.

- Import: `import OverflowCount from '@aziontech/webkit/overflow-count'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A table cell or a detail row shows the first value of a list and the rest hide behind a count: the domains of a workload, the tags of a row, the workloads a rule applies to.
- A card or a header names one item of many and the reader may want the full list without leaving the screen.

## Do

- Show the first item (or as many as fit) beside the chip; the chip counts only the hidden ones, and `items` passes only those.
- Name the items with `noun` (`{ one: 'domain', other: 'domains' }`) so the summary reads `12 domains`, not `12 items`.
- Give an item an `href` only when it opens something; an item without one renders as plain text.
- Use the `item` slot for a router link or a richer entry; keep every entry to one truncating line.

## Don’t

- The list is the content of the page → render it as a `Table` or an `Item` list.
- The reader picks from the list → use `Select`, `Combobox` or `MultiSelect`.
- A single count without a list behind it → use `Badge`.

## Related

- `table` — `TableCellTags` and `TableCellLink` put this chip after the values they fit.
- `tag` — the chip is a small secondary `Tag`.
- `popover` — the list opens in a `Popover`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Array<string \| { label: string; href?: string }>` | `[]` | false | The hidden items. The chip reads a plus sign and the count; an item with `href` opens in a new tab. |
| `noun` | `string \| { one: string; other: string }` | `''` | false | What the items are, for the summary and the trigger's name. Empty uses the catalog (`item` / `items`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` |  | One list entry; replaces the built-in text or link. |

## States

- `data-state` on the trigger: `open` | `closed` (from `Popover`).
- Search shows when `items` holds more than 7 entries; Load more shows while entries beyond the loaded batches (10 per batch) match.
- Empty `items` renders nothing.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a button named `Show all <count> <noun>` (the visible `+N` alone does not say what it counts); `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` come from `Popover`.
- On a coarse pointer the trigger answers a tap across 44px (an invisible `data-slot="touch-target"` layer, as `Button` has), while the chip keeps its drawn size.
- Keyboard: `Enter`/`Space` opens, `Esc` closes and returns focus to the chip, `Tab` moves through the search box, the links and Load more.
- A polite `role="status"` region announces the summary after a search or Load more.
- A link that opens a new tab carries a visually hidden `(opens in a new tab)`.
- The trigger stops its click from bubbling, so opening the list inside a clickable table row does not fire the row's `row-click`; the wrapper itself is not interactive and lets other clicks through.
- Contrast: the secondary `Tag` and the muted summary meet 4.5:1 in both themes.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
  import OverflowCount from '@aziontech/webkit/overflow-count'

  const domains = ['shop.example.com', 'api.example.com', 'img.example.com', 'docs.example.com']
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-xs) min-w-0 items-center gap-(--spacing-xs)">
    <Link
      :href="`https://${domains[0]}`"
      :label="domains[0]"
      target="_blank"
      size="small"
    />
    <OverflowCount
      :items="domains.slice(1).map((label) => ({ label, href: `https://${label}` }))"
      :noun="{ one: 'domain', other: 'domains' }"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

# Payment Brand

> The card-brand plate shown beside a payment card: a small bordered plate with the network's mark (Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Diners Club, JCB, Discover, Elo, Hipercard, UnionPay) drawn in one colour in theme tokens, so it reads in light, dark and forced colors without a raster image or a brand hex. It replaces the design sample's `CardBrandMark` (a Visa plate on a hard-coded blue fill), the Console Kit's card flag block (six colored SVG logos) and the inline Visa SVG the account blocks repeated. A brand it does not draw (Maestro, Hiper, or any unknown value) shows a generic card glyph and keeps the brand's name for assistive technology.

- Import: `import PaymentBrand from '@aziontech/webkit/payment-brand'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use PaymentBrand for the card network plate next to a payment card.
- A payment method row, a checkout summary or a billing table names the card on file: the plate sits before `Ending in 4242` or `Visa •••• 4242`.
- A list of saved cards where the brand helps the reader tell them apart.

## Do

- Pass the brand as the payment API returns it; the plate normalizes `American Express`, `american_express`, `Diners Club` and casing.
- When the row text already says the brand (`Visa •••• 4242`), set `decorative` so the name is not read twice; when the text says only `Ending in 4242`, leave the plate named.
- Keep the plate at `medium` in rows and forms, `small` inside dense tables.

## Don’t

- The Azion logo → use `Brand`.
- A partner or integration logo (Git providers, clouds) → use the product's logo asset or an `Avatar`.
- A status or category of the card (expired, default) → use `Tag` beside the plate.

## Related

- `brand` — the same idea for the Azion lockup: an inline mark, sized by token.
- `tag` — put `Default` or `Expired` next to the plate, not inside it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brand` | `string` | `''` | false | The card network as the payment API names it (`visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`, `American Express`, `diners`, `jcb`, `discover`, `elo`, `hipercard`, `unionpay`…). Unknown values draw the generic card glyph. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Plate size: `small` 20 × 32 px for dense tables, `medium` 28 × 40 px for rows and forms. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name. Empty uses the brand's name (`Visa`), or the catalog's `Card` for an unknown brand. |
| `decorative` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Hide the plate from assistive technology when the text next to it already names the brand. |

## States

- `data-brand` on the root: `visa` | `mastercard` | `amex` | `diners` | `jcb` | `discover` | `elo` | `hipercard` | `unionpay` | `unknown`.
- `data-size`: `small` | `medium`.
- `data-glyph`: `mark` when the brand has a drawn mark, `generic` otherwise.
- The Mastercard mark is two equal circles at the same opacity whose overlap reads darker, the network's own one-colour form; one solid circle beside a faded one would read as a switch knob in its track.
- The plate has a card's corner (`--radius-sm`, 2 px), not the control radius: at 20 × 32 px the 6 px control radius made a pill, and two discs inside a pill read as a toggle switch.

## Accessibility

- The root is `role="img"` named by `ariaLabel` (the consumer writes `aria-label`) or the brand's name; with `decorative` it is `aria-hidden="true"` and has no role.
- The SVG inside is `aria-hidden` and not focusable; the plate takes no focus.
- Contrast: the mark is `--text-default` on `--bg-surface` (above 4.5:1 in both themes); forced colors draw it in `CanvasText` because it uses `currentColor`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PaymentBrand from '@aziontech/webkit/payment-brand'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex items-center gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <PaymentBrand brand="visa" />
    <span class="text-label-md text-(--text-default)">Ending in 4242</span>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Plan Feature List

> Use PlanFeatureList only for what a plan includes; any other list of rows is Item rows, and facts about one resource are KeyValueList. The features a plan, product or upgrade includes, each behind a check mark, in one or two columns. It is the "what you get" list of a plan card, an upgrade card or a change-plan drawer: short labels, an optional one-line description under each, and a check that says "included", never "done". It replaces the hand-written `ul` with a `az az-check` per row that the billing pages and the change-plan drawer drew with different icon colours.

- Import: `import PlanFeatureList from '@aziontech/webkit/plan-feature-list'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The perks of an upgrade card (Upgrade to Pro: Unlimited Applications, Unlimited Workloads, Custom Domains).
- The features a plan includes in a change-plan or upgrade drawer, each with a short description.
- Any short list of included capabilities where the check is the only marker.

## Do

- Keep each label to a few words in title case or sentence case, one capability per row; put the detail in `description`, not in the label.
- Use `columns: 2` for six or more short labels in a wide card; it falls back to one column in a narrow box on its own.
- Name the list with `ariaLabel` (for example "Pro plan features") when no visible heading right above it says what the features belong to.
- Do not hand-write the list with your own check icons: the check colour and spacing are part of the component.

## Don’t

- Steps or tasks with a done/not-done state (a production checklist, a setup guide) → use `outcome-icon` per row, or the `stepper`.
- A comparison of features across plans → use `plan-comparison-section` or `table`.
- Label and value facts → use `key-value-list`.
- Rows that navigate or carry actions → use `item`.
- Marketing pricing cards on the site → use `pricing-card` / `pricing-plans-section`, which carry their own feature lists.

## Related

- `key-value-list` — the plan facts that sit next to the feature list in a billing card.
- `card` — the surface the list sits in; PlanFeatureList brings no surface of its own.
- `outcome-icon` — the mark for a step that finished, which this check is not.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `PlanFeatureListItem[]` | `[]` | false | The features, in order; each item is `{ label: string; description?: string }`. |
| `columns` | `1 \| 2` | `1` | false | Columns when the list's own box is at least the md container; a narrower box always shows one column. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list when no visible heading names it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-columns` on the list mirrors `columns`
- Empty: with no `items` the component renders nothing (no empty list, no placeholder); the card around it decides what to say
- No `loading`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `readonly`, `error` or `open` states: the list is static, read-only text

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: none; the list has no interactive part.
- Keyboard map: no tab stop.
- ARIA: a native `ul` with `role="list"` (so the list semantics survive `list-style: none` in Safari); each feature is an `li`; the check glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`; `ariaLabel` is set as `aria-label` on the `ul` only when non-empty.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the label and the muted description, ≥3:1 for the check glyph, on `var(--bg-surface)` in both themes.
- No motion.
- No touch target: nothing is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PlanFeatureList from '@aziontech/webkit/plan-feature-list'

  const features = [
    { label: 'Unlimited applications' },
    { label: 'Unlimited workloads' },
    { label: 'Custom domains' },
    { label: 'Priority support' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <PlanFeatureList
    :items="features"
    aria-label="Pro plan features"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/pricing-card.md -->

# Pricing Card

> One tier of a pricing table: what it is called, what it costs, what that price includes, and the one action that moves the account onto it. The card owns the typographic hierarchy of a price — an overline plan name, the amount as the headline figure, and the billing caveat under it in muted body copy — so a row of tiers reads as a comparison rather than as three differently-typeset cards. `actionsPosition` is the axis that decides which of the two compositions the card is. **`bottom`** is the compact tier: the name, a `medium` amount and the caveat stack at the top, the action follows, and the slot sits under it — a card sized by its own content, for a row of tiers a reader scans. With nothing in the default slot the `bottom` card renders no slot region at all, so it ends at its action instead of under an empty band. **`middle`** is the full tier: the amount becomes the `large` headline figure, the caveat moves up to `body-md`, the slot grows to fill the card, and the action is pinned to the bottom edge so a row of `middle` cards has its buttons on one line whatever each tier's feature list holds. The `middle` slot reserves a 160px band (`min-h-40`) only with `equalHeight`; a lone card is sized by what it holds. The built-in action is `outline` (`bottom`) or `secondary` (`middle`); on the card that shows its tag (`showTag`, the tier the row singles out, such as Popular) it is `primary`, so the recommended plan carries the one filled button in the row. The default period is `/ month`: `/ mon` read as Monday. `variant` decides only whether the card draws its own surface (`contained`) or sits on the one behind it (`ghost`); it never changes the composition. The name, the amount and the caveat are **one column**, capped at `--container-xs` (348px) rather than at the card's full width: the caveat is a sentence about the price directly above it, so it wraps on the price's measure. The cap shipped as `--container-3xs` (256px) — two rungs down the ladder, and too narrow for the copy it holds. 256px sets `body-md` at roughly 33 characters, under the 45–75 a prose measure wants, and all three billing caveats on the sample pricing page (66, 69 and 84 characters) ran to three lines there. At 348px the measure is ~46 characters and the same three set in two, while the card's own content box at 1440 is 413px — so the caveat is still held to the price's column instead of the card's. The card carries **one** prose region — the pricing caveat, below the amount. It used to carry a second paragraph above the amount as well, and with `equalHeight` reserving a band for each, a row of tiers showed two two-line muted blocks around every price doing the same visual job. The Figma component (`3605:2260`) has a single prose region, `Pricing Details`, positioned below the amount, so that is the one the card keeps; a tier's positioning sentence belongs to whatever the consumer puts in the slot. `equalHeight` makes a ROW of cards read as one comparison. Every region is content-sized by default, which is right for a single card and wrong for three side by side — a tier with a two-line caveat and a tier with none put their feature lists on different lines, and the reader has to re-find the row in every column. It reserves **three** lines for the caveat, in `lh` so the reservation follows the type token rather than a hard-coded height. Three is the design's 64px band expressed in whole lines of the region's own token (`body-md` is a 22px line box, so `3lh` is 66px; `2lh` is 44px and twenty short) — it shipped as `2lh`, and the shortfall stayed invisible until a tier's caveat ran to three lines at the region's then-256px measure, overflowed the band, and pushed that column's feature list 22px below the other two. Opt-in, because reserving empty lines is wrong for a lone card; set it on every card in the row. A caveat past three lines still pushes the row down, like any overflow. The plan title is an **overline** (`.text-overline-md` on an `<h3>`): the token carries the display face, the uppercase transform and the widest tracking step, so the tier reads as a label on the card rather than as a title competing with the price beneath it. It stays an `<h3>` for the document outline — the tier is the section heading — while looking like an overline. There is no built-in plan name: set `title` on every card. When the price already names the plan (`value` equals `title`, ignoring case and spaces, as `Free` over `Free`), the overline is visually hidden (`data-in-price`, `sr-only`): the heading stays in the outline for a screen reader, and the card stops printing the plan name twice.

- Import: `import PricingCard from '@aziontech/webkit/pricing-card'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- One tier in a row of plans: plan name, price, billing caveat, one action and the tier's feature list.
- A compact tier sized by its content (`actions-position="bottom"`), or a full tier whose action is pinned to the bottom so a row's buttons line up (`actions-position="middle"`).
- A tier set on the surface behind it (`variant="ghost"`) inside a section that already draws the frame.

## Do

- In a row of tiers, set `equalHeight` on every card so each caveat reserves the same band and the feature lists start on one line.
- Keep `pricing-details` to the billing caveat. A tier's positioning sentence goes in the default slot with the feature list.
- The card emits no events, and the built-in button has no handler. To act on the click, fill the `actions` slot with your own `Button`.
- Hide the symbol or the period with `:show-prefix="false"` / `:show-suffix="false"` (for example on a custom-quote tier) instead of clearing `prefix` / `suffix`.
- Mark at most one card in a row with `show-tag` and `tag-label`.

## Don’t

- You need the whole plans band of a pricing page, with the billing-period toggle and the framed row → use `pricing-plans-section`.
- You need a feature-by-feature comparison across plans → use `plan-comparison-section`.
- You only need to show an amount, in a table cell or a summary → use `currency-amount`.
- The card holds general content rather than a price → use `card`.

## Related

- `currency-amount` — typesets the amount inside the card; use it directly for prices outside a tier card.
- `pricing-plans-section` — the page section that lays out a row of plan cards with the billing toggle.
- `plan-comparison-section` — the matrix that sits under the plan cards.
- `card` — generic bordered card with header, content and footer regions.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Plan name shown as the card heading. |
| `pricingDetails` | `string` | `''` | false | Caveat under the price, such as the billing terms. |
| `showPricingDetails` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the pricing details line. |
| `showTag` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the tag beside the plan name. |
| `tagLabel` | `string` | `'Popular'` | false | Text of the tag beside the plan name. |
| `equalHeight` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Reserves the caveat's band so a row of cards aligns row-for-row. Set it on every card in the row. |
| `actionsPosition` | `'bottom' \| 'middle'` | `'bottom'` | false | Composition of the card: `bottom` stacks the actions under the price, `middle` puts the price and actions between the header and the default slot. |
| `variant` | `'contained' \| 'ghost'` | `'contained'` | false | Whether the card draws its own surface: `contained` has a border and a surface, `ghost` sits on the page. |
| `value` | `string` | `'20'` | false | Price amount, already formatted, without the currency symbol. |
| `prefix` | `string` | `'$'` | false | Text before the amount, usually the currency symbol. |
| `suffix` | `string` | `'/ month'` | false | Text after the amount, usually the billing period. |
| `showPrefix` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the prefix. |
| `showSuffix` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the suffix. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | `'Label'` | false | Label of the default action button. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Fades the old price out and the new one in when the price changes, such as on a billing-period switch. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | — | Named slot. |
| `default` | — | Main content. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- Title in the price: `data-in-price` on the title when `value` equals `title` (ignoring case and spaces); the title is visually hidden and stays the card's heading.
- Animated: with `animated`, a change of `value`, `prefix` or `suffix` fades the old price out and the new one in (`data-animated` on the root); without it the price swaps in place

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states; the `animated` price fade pairs each class with `motion-reduce:animate-none`, so the price swaps in place under reduced motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PricingCard from '@aziontech/webkit/pricing-card'
</script>

<template>
  <PricingCard
    title="Pro"
    pricing-details="Billed annually or $25/mo billed monthly."
    actions-position="bottom"
    variant="contained"
    value="20"
    prefix="$"
    suffix="/ month"
    action-label="Start with Pro"
  />
</template>
```

# Priority Tag

> Use PriorityTag only for the priority of a ticket, task or request on the urgent → low scale, or for "no priority"; the severity of a finding or alert is a SeverityTag, and the state of a ticket is a StatusIndicator or a Tag. PriorityTag labels a work item with how soon it should be handled: urgent, high, medium, low or none. The level reads from a three-bar signal glyph (the filled bars count the level), from a distinct alert mark for urgent, from three flat dots for none, and from the label, so no level depends on colour alone. Its accessible name always says the axis ("Priority: High"), which is why it is its own component and not a SeverityTag (decision SUP-05).

- Import: `import PriorityTag from '@aziontech/webkit/priority-tag'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic
- Stability: preview. The API may still change in a minor release, named in the changelog, until the owner marks it GA.

## When to use

- Show how urgent a support ticket, task, issue or request is, in a ticket list row, a table cell, a board card or a ticket detail header.
- Rank work on the fixed urgent, high, medium, low scale used by help desks and issue trackers, with "no priority" for items nobody has triaged yet.

## Do

- Keep the default label (the level name from the locale catalog, translated under `ConfigProvider`); override `label` only when the product glossary names a level differently (`Normal` for medium).
- Show `none` for an untriaged item instead of leaving the cell empty, so the column reads the same on every row.
- Use one PriorityTag per row, in its own column, so the glyphs line up and the scale reads down the column.
- Do not add a toned `tag` beside it for the same level; the glyph and the label already carry it.

## Don’t

- The value is how severe a finding, alert, incident or vulnerability is → use `severity-tag`.
- The value is the state of the ticket (open, pending, solved) → use `status-indicator` or `tag`.
- The user picks or changes the priority (a priority field or filter) → use `select` or `chip`; show the chosen value with this tag elsewhere.
- The value is a count on an icon or avatar → use `badge`.

## Related

- `severity-tag` — the same frame and bar glyph for the critical → info findings scale; its accessible name is the level alone.
- `tag` — a toned status or category label with no order between values.
- `status-indicator` — the live state of a resource or ticket.
- `chip` — an interactive or removable token, for priority filters.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `priority` | `'urgent' \| 'high' \| 'medium' \| 'low' \| 'none'` | `'none'` | false | Priority level (exported as `PriorityTagPriority`); sets the glyph (alert mark, filled bars or dots) and the default label. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the tag. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Urgent`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `No priority`). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `medium` is 24px tall, `small` is 20px. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Replaces the visible label text; the hidden `Priority:` prefix remains. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (static, non-interactive)
- `data-priority` mirrors the `priority` prop: `urgent` | `high` | `medium` | `low` | `none`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop: `small` | `medium`
- Glyph per level: urgent the `az-circle-alert` mark; high 3 filled bars of 3; medium 2; low 1; none three flat dots
- `none` ("No priority", three dots) is the empty, untriaged value: the tag never renders blank
- Loading, error, disabled, readonly and invalid do not apply: the tag is static and non-interactive (a loading row shows a `skeleton` in its place)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not focusable; the tag is static text and takes no `tabindex`.
- Keyboard map: none; the tag has no interaction.
- ARIA: the glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`; a visually hidden prefix (`sr-only`, locale key `priorityTag.prefix`, `Priority:`) sits before the label, so the text a screen reader reads is "Priority: High". No `role` or `aria-label` on the root (a generic element takes no name); the hidden prefix stays when the default slot replaces the label.
- Contrast: label `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-canvas)` ≥4.5:1; filled bars `var(--text-default)` and the urgent mark `var(--danger-mark)` meet the mark and icon targets (Lc 30 / Lc 45, WCAG ≥3:1) in both themes; only documented token pairs (`rules/webkit-tokens.md` § Contrast).
- Never colour only: every level differs by glyph shape and by text.
- No motion, so no `motion-reduce:*` fallback is needed.
- Touch target: not applicable; the tag is not interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PriorityTag from '@aziontech/webkit/priority-tag'
</script>

<template>
  <PriorityTag
    priority="high"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/qr-code.md -->

# Qr Code

> A QR code drawn as SVG from a string, with no image request and no dependency: WebKit's own encoder (byte mode, UTF-8, versions 1–40, error correction L/M/Q/H) turns the value into modules, and the component draws them as one path. It is for setup flows that hand a URI to a phone, first the `otpauth://` URI of an authenticator app in `auth#MfaSetup`, where it replaces the image the API returned and the framed placeholder of the demo. The code is always dark on a light plate (the plate pins the light theme), because several authenticator scanners do not read an inverted code.

- Import: `import QrCode from '@aziontech/webkit/qr-code'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A phone has to pick up a value the screen shows: an authenticator `otpauth://` URI, a pairing link, a short download URL.
- Next to a typed alternative: the same value (or its secret) as text with a `CopyButton`, for people who cannot scan.

## Do

- Always give the code a typed alternative next to it: the setup key or the link as text.
- Name the code after what it does (`QR code to add jane.doe@example.com to an authenticator app`), not `QR code`.
- Keep the default `M` error correction; raise it only when the code is printed or shown small.

## Don’t

- The value is only for reading or copying on the same device → show it as text with `CopyButton`.
- A brand or partner logo → use `Brand` or the partner's asset.
- A long payload (over a few hundred characters) → link to it; a dense code is hard to scan from a screen.

## Related

- `copy-button` — the typed alternative beside the code.
- `otp-input` — the 6-digit code the app shows after the scan.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `—` | true | The text the code carries (a URI, a key), encoded as UTF-8 bytes. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the image. Empty uses the catalog's `QR code`; name it after what the scan does. |
| `errorCorrection` | `'L' \| 'M' \| 'Q' \| 'H'` | `'M'` | false | Error-correction level: `L` 7 %, `M` 15 %, `Q` 25 %, `H` 30 % of the code can be lost and still read. Higher levels make denser codes. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Rendered width: `small` 128 px, `medium` 160 px, `large` 224 px, quiet zone included. |

## States

- `data-size`: `small` | `medium` | `large`.
- `data-version` on the root: the QR version the encoder picked (1–40); `data-modules`: the module count per side.
- An empty value draws no code: the plate keeps its size and `data-version` is absent. A value too long for version 40 at the chosen level draws no code either and logs one warning.

## Accessibility

- The root is `role="img"` named by `ariaLabel` (the consumer writes `aria-label`; catalog `QR code` when empty); the SVG inside is `aria-hidden` and not focusable; the code takes no focus.
- The code is never the only way: the page puts the value or its secret beside it as text.
- Contrast: dark modules on a light plate in both themes (the plate sets `data-theme="light"`); `forced-color-adjust: none` keeps the code dark on light in forced colors, so a scanner still reads it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'
  import QrCode from '@aziontech/webkit/qr-code'

  const account = 'jane.doe@example.com'
  const secret = 'JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP'
  const uri = `otpauth://totp/Azion:${encodeURIComponent(account)}?secret=${secret}&issuer=Azion`
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-col items-start gap-(--spacing-md)">
    <QrCode
      :value="uri"
      :aria-label="`QR code to add ${account} to an authenticator app`"
    />
    <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-2xs)">
      <p class="text-label-sm text-(--text-default)">Can't scan the code?</p>
      <div class="flex items-center gap-(--spacing-xs)">
        <code
          class="text-label-code-sm text-(--text-default)"
          dir="ltr"
          >{{ secret.match(/.{1,4}/g).join(' ') }}</code
        >
        <CopyButton
          :value="secret"
          aria-label="Copy setup key"
          copied-label="Setup key copied"
          size="small"
        />
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/qr-code.md](components/qr-code.md).

# Severity Tag

> Use SeverityTag only for a level on the critical → info scale of findings and alerts; the state of a resource is a StatusIndicator, and any other category word is a Tag. SeverityTag labels an item with its place on an ordered severity scale: critical, high, medium, low or info. The level reads from a four-bar glyph, where the filled bars count the level, and from the label, so two levels never depend on colour alone to differ. It differs from `tag`, whose `severity` prop is a colour tone (success, warning, danger) with no order between values.

- Import: `import SeverityTag from '@aziontech/webkit/severity-tag'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Show how severe an alert, finding, detection, incident or vulnerability is, in a table cell, a list row or a detail header.
- Rank items on a fixed five-step scale where critical and high must stay visibly distinct.

## Do

- Keep the default label (the level name from the locale catalog, translated under `ConfigProvider`) so the text always names the level; override `label` only when the product glossary names the level differently.
- Use one SeverityTag per row, in its own column, so the glyphs line up and the scale reads down the column.
- Do not pair the tag with a toned `tag` for the same level; the glyph and the ramp already carry it.

## Don’t

- The value is an outcome or a status with no order (allowed, blocked, healthy) → use `tag`.
- The value is a count or a one-word indicator on an icon or avatar → use `badge`.
- The user can select or remove the value (a severity filter) → use `chip`.

## Related

- `tag` — a toned status or category label; use it for outcomes and states, not for an ordered level.
- `badge` — a dense count or short-label indicator.
- `chip` — an interactive or removable token, for severity filters.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `severity` | `'critical' \| 'high' \| 'medium' \| 'low' \| 'info'` | `'info'` | false | Severity level on the findings scale (exported as `SeverityTagSeverity`, distinct from the shared status `Severity`); sets how many glyph bars fill, their colour and the default label. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the tag. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info`). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `medium` is 24px tall, `small` is 20px. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Replaces the label text. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (static, non-interactive)
- `data-severity` mirrors the `severity` prop: `critical` | `high` | `medium` | `low` | `info`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop: `small` | `medium`
- Filled bars per level: critical 4, high 3, medium 2, low 1, info 0

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not focusable; the tag is static text and takes no `tabindex`.
- Keyboard map: none; the tag has no interaction.
- ARIA: the glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`; the visible text names the level, so the tag needs no `role` or `aria-label`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the label (`var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-canvas)`) and ≥3:1 for every filled bar on `var(--bg-canvas)` in both themes.
- No motion, so no `motion-reduce:*` fallback is needed.
- Touch target: not applicable; the tag is not interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SeverityTag from '@aziontech/webkit/severity-tag'
</script>

<template>
  <SeverityTag
    severity="info"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

# Status Code

> Use StatusCode only for an HTTP status code or method (200, 404, GET); for resource state use StatusIndicator, and for any other word use Tag. StatusCode shows the HTTP status of a request, optionally preceded by its method, as one compact monospace pill whose colour comes from the status class: informational, success and redirect responses (1xx, 2xx, 3xx) stay neutral, client errors (4xx) take the warning colour and server errors (5xx) the danger colour, so failures stand out in a long request log without every successful row competing for attention. Anything that is not a status from 100 to 599 renders muted, as written. It composes `Tag` for the surface, so its sizes, shape and colours are the tag's; the component owns only the mapping from status to colour and the method plus code layout that every logs table would otherwise repeat.

- Import: `import StatusCode from '@aziontech/webkit/status-code'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A request log, an invocation list or a trace detail shows the HTTP status of each request (`GET 200`, `POST 503`).
- A detail panel summarizes the response of one request next to its timing and size.

## Do

- Pass the status as it comes from the log (`404` or `'404'`); the component derives the colour, so do not pick a colour per row.
- Pass `method` only when the list mixes methods; a list of `GET` requests reads better with the code alone.
- Keep the column narrow: the pill never wraps and is at most `GET` plus three digits wide for real traffic.

## Don’t

- The status is a resource lifecycle (`Active`, `Pending`, `Failed`) → use `tag` or `TableCellStatus`.
- The value is a security or incident level → use `severity-tag`.
- A dot that says whether a service is up → use `status-indicator`.

## Related

- `tag` — the surface StatusCode composes; use it directly for statuses that are not HTTP codes.
- `table` — place StatusCode inside a `#cell-<id>` slot of a request log.
- `severity-tag` — ordered severity levels with a bar glyph.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `number \| string` | `''` | false | HTTP status, as a number or a string (`404`, `'404'`). 1xx to 3xx render neutral, 4xx warning, 5xx danger; anything else renders muted as written, empty a dash. |
| `method` | `string` | `''` | false | Request method shown before the code (`GET`, `POST`), upper-cased. Empty shows the code alone. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token forwarded to `Tag`; `medium` is 24px tall, `small` is 20px. |

## States

- `data-status-class` on the root: `informational` (1xx), `success` (2xx), `redirect` (3xx), `client-error` (4xx), `server-error` (5xx) or `invalid` (anything else, including empty).
- `data-size` mirrors `size` (set by `Tag`).
- The `Tag` severity follows the class: `neutral` for 1xx to 3xx and `invalid`, `warning` for 4xx, `danger` for 5xx.
- `invalid` mutes the text; an empty `code` shows a dash, any other invalid value shows as written.
- Non-interactive: no hover, focus, active or disabled state.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — StatusCode is non-interactive.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: plain text inside a `span`; the status number carries the meaning, so the colour is never the only cue (WCAG 1.4.1). Screen readers read `POST 503`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1: the `Tag` severity pairs (`--warning` / `--warning-foreground`, `--danger` / `--danger-foreground`, `--text-default` on `--bg-canvas`) and `--text-muted` on `--bg-canvas` are theme-guaranteed in light and dark.
- `motion-reduce:*`: not applicable — no motion.
- Touch target: not applicable — non-interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import StatusCode from '@aziontech/webkit/status-code'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <StatusCode
      :code="101"
      method="GET"
    />
    <StatusCode
      :code="200"
      method="GET"
    />
    <StatusCode
      :code="301"
      method="GET"
    />
    <StatusCode
      :code="404"
      method="POST"
    />
    <StatusCode
      :code="503"
      method="PUT"
    />
    <StatusCode :code="201" />
    <StatusCode code="n/a" />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/tag.md -->

# Tag

> Use Tag for a read-only category or outcome word on an item (Production, Beta, Allowed) that is not a lifecycle state. The state of a resource is a StatusIndicator, a number is a Badge, a removable or selectable token is a Chip, and a level on the critical → info scale is a SeverityTag. A compact, read-only word on an item, colored by its brand look `variant` or its status colour `severity` so the category or outcome reads at a glance (Production in `variant="primary"`, Blocked in `severity="danger"`). It takes an optional leading icon and two sizes, and has one shape; it is never interactive and never counts.

- Import: `import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Label or categorize an item with a short descriptive text, optionally with a leading icon.
- Pick the colour from one of two sets, never both on one tag: `severity` when the word is an outcome or a status (`neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`), `variant` when it is a category that needs emphasis (`primary`, `accent`, `contrast`). `severity` wins when both are set.
- The logo orange (`variant="primary"`) marks **one** value per list or card. When several values need emphasis, use `severity` or `accent`.

## Do

- Colour comes from `variant` or `severity`; the optional icon is decorative — keep it `aria-hidden`.
- Pick the colour by meaning with the table in When to use. Do not use `danger` for a state that is only off (Inactive): it reads as an error.
- Do not restyle a Tag with colour classes to get a tint; every tint is a `variant` or a `severity`.
- Do not round a Tag into a pill with a class: every Tag has the one control shape, so tags in a row line up.

## Don’t

- It is purely a count or one-glance status label → use `badge`.
- The user can select or remove it (filters, multi-select values) → use `chip`.

## Related

- `badge` — denser count/short-label indicator with no icon affordance.
- `chip` — interactive/removable token.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback text when the default slot is empty. |
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'accent' \| 'contrast'` | `'primary'` | false | Emphasis look of the tag surface and label, used when `severity` is not set: `primary` (the logo orange, one value per list), `accent` and `contrast` (`var(--bg-contrast)` / `var(--text-contrast)`). |
| `severity` | `'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `—` | false | Status colour of the tag surface and label, the shared `Severity` scale exported from this component; wins over `variant` when set. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `medium` is 24px tall, `small` is 20px. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Azion icon class for the leading icon. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Main content. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`. A tag is static text: it takes no focus and has no hover or active state.
- `data-severity` mirrors `severity` when it is set; otherwise `data-variant` mirrors `variant`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: none; the tag is not focusable. A focusable control that holds a tag draws its own ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state; the `primary` label is `--primary-foreground` on the logo orange fill (6.7:1).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'
</script>

<template>
  <Tag
    label="Label"
    variant="primary"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

# Third Party Logo

> A third-party mark (a client, a competitor, an analyst firm, a standard or certification, a coding agent) drawn right on both themes. The asset registries already hold the files (`@aziontech/webkit/assets/client-registry`, `@aziontech/webkit/assets/competitor-registry` and the `@aziontech/webkit/assets/<file>.svg` exports); every surface that drew one repeated the same theme rule by hand (two `img` tags revealed per `[data-theme]`, a `brightness-0` silhouette, a CSS mask in `currentColor`) and none had every route. `ThirdPartyLogo` holds the rule once: a light/dark pair of files, or one file inverted on the theme where it would vanish, or one ink (the theme's black or white, the surrounding `currentColor`, or black pinned for a coloured fill), and the company's name as a typographic wordmark when there is no file yet. It replaces the design sample's `AgentMark` and `ClientMark`. It is a renderer: it takes the file URLs from a registry entry and imports no registry itself, so a page pays only for the marks it shows.

- Import: `import ThirdPartyLogo from '@aziontech/webkit/third-party-logo'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ThirdPartyLogo for any other company's mark (client, competitor, agent, certification).
- A logo wall, a trust strip, a client story card, a quote attribution, a comparison column head: any place that shows another company's mark.
- The coding agents a prompt works with (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor), drawn in the ink of the surface they sit on.
- A list of standards or analyst firms (SOC, PCI DSS, Gartner, Forrester).

## Do

- Pass a registry entry as it stands: `name`, `src` from `logo`, `src-light` from `logoLight`, `artwork` from `artwork`. The registry knows which theme each file is drawn for.
- Set the height with `size`: `small` (16 px) beside a label or in a table cell, `medium` (24 px, the default) in a card or a list, `large` (32 px) in a logo wall or a quote attribution. The width follows each file's own aspect ratio. Cap wide wordmarks with `max-w-*`.
- In a list of many clients, use `variant="monochrome"`: per-brand colour reads as noise next to twenty others.
- On a coloured fill (white, `--primary`), use `variant="knockout"`: a fill does not follow the theme, so the ink must not either.
- On a surface that is dark in both themes, or among drawn diagram parts, use `variant="current"` so the mark takes the surface's own ink.
- When the text beside the mark already names the company, set `decorative`.

## Don’t

- The Azion logo → use `Brand`.
- A card network beside a payment method → use `PaymentBrand`.
- A person or an account → use `Avatar`.
- A product icon or a UI glyph → use an icon from `@aziontech/icons`.
- A grid of client marks → use `LogoWall`; it renders each mark and can render `ThirdPartyLogo` in its `mark` slot.

## Related

- `brand` — the Azion lockup; `ThirdPartyLogo` is everyone else's.
- `payment-brand` — card-network plates, drawn in tokens.
- `logo-wall` — the grid that lays marks out; `ThirdPartyLogo` draws one mark.
- `avatar` — a person's or an organization's picture with initials.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `—` | true | The company or product the mark belongs to; the accessible name, and the typographic wordmark drawn when no file is set. |
| `src` | `string` | `''` | false | URL of the mark; on its own it serves both themes, and with `srcLight` it is the dark-theme file. Empty draws the wordmark. |
| `srcLight` | `string` | `''` | false | URL of the light-theme file; with `src` both files render and the theme reveals one. |
| `artwork` | `'color' \| 'light' \| 'dark'` | `'color'` | false | The ink a single file is drawn in: `light` art (for dark surfaces) is inverted on the light theme, `dark` art is inverted on the dark theme, `color` is kept as is. Ignored when `srcLight` is set or `variant` is not `color`. |
| `variant` | `'color' \| 'monochrome' \| 'current' \| 'knockout'` | `'color'` | false | Ink: `color` keeps the vendor's colours, `monochrome` paints one silhouette black on light and white on dark, `current` paints it in the surrounding text colour, `knockout` pins it black for a mark on a coloured fill. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name when it should differ from `name`. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Height of the mark: `small` 16 px, `medium` 24 px, `large` 32 px; the width follows the file's aspect ratio. |
| `decorative` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Hides the mark from assistive technology when the text beside it already names the company. |

## States

- `data-variant` on the root: `color` | `monochrome` | `current` | `knockout`.
- `data-route` on the root: `pair` (both files in the DOM, the theme reveals one), `single` (one file, filtered by `artwork` or the ink of `variant`), `wordmark` (no file: the name in type).
- `data-artwork` on the root mirrors `artwork`.
- `data-size` on the root mirrors `size`: `small` is `h-4`, `medium` is `h-6`, `large` is `h-8`.
- `data-sized` on the root when the caller's class sets a height (`h-*` or `size-*`, with or without a breakpoint); it then wins over `size`.
- Not applicable: `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `open`/`closed` (a static mark).

## Accessibility

- Pattern: an image (`role="img"` on the root) named by `ariaLabel`, else `name`. The files inside have empty `alt` and are `aria-hidden`, so a light/dark pair is announced once.
- With `decorative` the root is `aria-hidden="true"` and has no role.
- Not focusable; no keyboard map (a static mark).
- Contrast: marks are logos (WCAG 1.4.3 exempts logotypes); the `monochrome` route makes a mark pure black or white against the page, and `knockout` pure black on a light fill.
- Forced colors: the `current` route paints `currentColor`, so it follows `CanvasText`.
- No motion.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import { CLIENTS } from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/client-registry'
  import ThirdPartyLogo from '@aziontech/webkit/third-party-logo'

  const client = CLIENTS.find((entry) => entry.name === 'Agibank')
</script>

<template>
  <ThirdPartyLogo
    :name="client.name"
    :src="client.logo"
    :src-light="client.logoLight"
    :artwork="client.artwork"
    size="large"
    class="max-w-40"
  />
</template>
```
