# Timeline

> Use Timeline for the history of one record: a vertical list of dated events joined by a line, newest or oldest first, such as the activity of a ticket (status changed, assigned, SLA breached, merged), the audit trail of one resource or the deployment history of an application. Each event is a `Timeline.Item`: a marker (a dot or an icon in its severity's `-mark` colour, or any small component the app puts in its `marker` slot), a title that says what happened, an optional description, who did it, when it happened (a `Timestamp`) and any content the app adds under it (a quoted comment, a diff summary, a link). `Timeline.Group` gathers the events of one day (or any period) under a label. It is read-only and has no current position: unlike `Stepper` it does not move anyone through steps, unlike `Trace` it does not place spans on a clock, and unlike `LogViewer` it does not stream lines.

- Import: `import TimelineRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/timeline-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Timeline from '@aziontech/webkit/timeline'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: composition
- Stability: preview. The API may still change in a minor release, named in the changelog, until the owner marks it GA.

## When to use

- Show the activity history of one ticket, order or incident: who changed the status, who it was assigned to, when an SLA was breached, when it was merged or closed.
- Show the audit trail of one resource on its detail page: created, settings changed, key rotated, deleted.
- Show the deployment or version history of one application, each deploy with its outcome and who started it.
- Group a long history by day ("Today", "November 21, 2026") so a reader finds when something happened.

## Do

- The title says what happened in plain words, past tense, with the changed value ("Status changed to Solved", "Assigned to Sam Lee"). Colour and icon only reinforce it; a reader who cannot see them still knows what happened.
- Pick the severity from what the event means for the reader: `danger` for a breach or a failed deploy, `warning` for something that needs attention soon, `success` for a resolved or merged event, `info` for a notable but neutral change, `neutral` (the default) for routine changes. Most events are `neutral`, so the few coloured ones stand out.
- Keep one order per timeline (newest first for activity people check often, oldest first for a history read as a story) and say which in the surrounding heading or copy when it is not obvious.
- Use `Timeline.Group` for histories longer than a screen; format its `label` in the app with `useLocale` (a date, "Today", "Yesterday").
- Put long content (a full comment, a diff) in the default slot, short and quoted; link to the full record rather than rendering it all.
- `size="small"` is for a side panel or a drawer; the page body uses `medium`.
- When the history is empty, render an `EmptyState` in place of the timeline, not a timeline with no items.

## Don’t

- A searchable, sortable log of many records or a whole account (filter by user, export as CSV) → use `data-table` (the `account/account-activity-history` block).
- Moving the reader through the ordered steps of a task, with a current step → use `stepper`.
- The timed spans of one request or invocation → use `trace`.
- Streaming build or runtime log lines with levels → use `log-viewer` (`log-viewer-steps` for known steps).
- The state of a service across many periods at a glance (uptime) → use `tracker`.
- The current state of one resource → use `status-indicator`.
- The messages of an AI conversation → use `chat-message`; a timeline lists events about a record, not the messages themselves.
- An agent's progress while it works → use `agent-activity`.

## Related

- `timestamp` — every item's `time` renders through it, so the reader can open the exact UTC and local value and copy it.
- `status-indicator` — the current state of the record, usually in the detail header above its timeline.
- `outcome-icon` — a small outcome mark the app can put in an item's `marker` slot when an event is a finished run.
- `avatar` — the actor's picture, in an item's `marker` slot, when the people matter more than the event type.
- `stepper` — the look-alike: a vertical rail of dots too, but for steps the reader moves through.
- `empty-state` — what the page shows instead of a timeline that has no events.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Density of every item: `small` for a side panel or drawer, `medium` for a page body. |
| `timeFormat` | `'relative' \| 'local' \| 'utc'` | `'local'` | false | How every item's `time` reads, passed to `Timestamp` as its `format`; inside a `Timeline.Group`, `local` reads as Timestamp's `time` (hour and minute only), because the group label carries the date. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders three placeholder items in place of the slot while the history loads; sets `aria-busy`. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | What a screen reader hears while loading. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Loading activity`). |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Activity`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | `Timeline.Item` children, or `Timeline.Group` children, in display order. Hidden while `loading`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/timeline-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/timeline-group`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: `index.ts` attaches `Item` and `Group` to the root so `<Timeline.Item>` and `<Timeline.Group>` resolve from one import. The timeline has no open/closed state, so there is no `Trigger` / `Content`; `Item` and `Group` are the closed-list part words for what the parts are. The root provides a read-only context (`injection-key.ts`, `TimelineInjectionKey = Symbol('Timeline')`) holding `size` and `timeFormat`; `composables/use-timeline-context.ts` exports `useTimelineContext` and the `TimelineContext` type (`CODE_QUALITY.md` § 3.5) and throws a clear error outside `<Timeline>`. No part registers itself or reads its slot: the line under the last item is hidden by CSS (`:last-child`).

Markup: the root is an `<ol>`. An Item is an `<li>`. A Group is an `<li>` holding its label and a nested `<ol>` of Items, named by that label (`aria-labelledby`).

- `timeline-item/timeline-item.vue` — one event: `<li data-slot="timeline-item">` → the marker column (`data-slot="timeline-marker"`, `aria-hidden="true"`, then the connector line `data-slot="timeline-connector"` runnin…
  - Props:

    | Prop          | Type                                                        | Default     | Required | JSDoc                                                                                                                               |
    | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    | `title`       | `string`                                                    | `''`        | false    | What happened, in plain words ("Status changed to Solved").                                                                         |
    | `description` | `string`                                                    | `''`        | false    | One or two lines of detail under the title.                                                                                         |
    | `actor`       | `string`                                                    | `''`        | false    | Who did it (a person, a team or a system); shown before the time.                                                                    |
    | `time`        | `string \| number \| Date`                                  | `undefined` | false    | When it happened, rendered by `Timestamp` in the root's `timeFormat`; a `Date`, an epoch or an ISO string. Absent renders no time. |
    | `severity`    | `'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'neutral'` | false    | What the event means for the reader; colours the marker with its `-mark` token.                                                     |
    | `icon`        | `string`                                                    | `''`        | false    | Icon class (`az az-clock`) drawn as the marker instead of the dot.                                                       |

  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — content under the description (a quoted comment, a link, a small key-value list); `marker` — replaces the dot or icon (an `Avatar`, an `OutcomeIcon`), sized by the app to the marker box.
  - Marker precedence: the `marker` slot, then `icon`, then the dot.
  - `data-testid` fallback `timeline-item`; inner `${testId}__title`, `${testId}__marker`. A consumer `data-testid` wins.
- `timeline-group/timeline-group.vue` — the events of one period: `<li data-slot="timeline-group">` → the label (`data-slot="timeline-group-label"`, with an id from `useId()`) and an `<ol aria-labelledby="<that id>">` h…
  - Props:

    | Prop    | Type     | Default | Required | JSDoc                                                        |
    | ------- | -------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
    | `label` | `string` | `''`    | false    | The period's header ("Today", "November 21, 2026"), formatted by the app. |

  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the `Timeline.Item` children of this period.
  - The line joins the items of one group; a group's label starts a new run of the line.
  - `data-testid` fallback `timeline-group`; inner `${testId}__label`. A consumer `data-testid` wins.

The same change rewrites the `timeline` entry of `packages/webkit/src/cli/migrations/v6.json` (`legacy.manual`) to "PrimeVue Timeline; use Timeline with Timeline.Item and Timeline.Group (different API)", so `webkit migrate` points v3 apps at the new export.

`./timeline` and `./timeline-root` export `TimelineProps`, `TimelineSize`, `TimelineTimeFormat`; `./timeline-item` exports `TimelineItemProps` and `TimelineItemSeverity` (derived from `Severity`); `./timeline-group` exports `TimelineGroupProps`; `./timeline` also exports `useTimelineContext` and `TimelineContext`.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading`. No hover, focus, selection or disabled state of its own: only the `Timestamp` and slotted content are interactive. No `readonly` or `invalid` state either: it is display-only, with no field and no validation.
- `data-size` on the root mirrors `size`; items read it from the context and carry their own `data-size`.
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors `loading`; `aria-busy="true"` while loading. The placeholders are three `aria-hidden` `<li>` with a circle `Skeleton` as the marker and two line `Skeleton`s as the content, plus one visually hidden `<li>` with the loading label.
- `data-severity` on each Item mirrors `severity`; the marker colour switches on it.
- `data-marker="dot" | "icon" | "custom"` on each Item says which marker renders.
- Part markers: `data-slot="timeline"`, `timeline-item`, `timeline-marker`, `timeline-connector`, `timeline-title`, `timeline-meta`, `timeline-description`, `timeline-body`, `timeline-group`, `timeline-group-label`.
- `data-orientation="vertical"` on the root.
- Empty: the app renders `EmptyState` instead of the timeline; the component does not inspect its slot (`CODE_QUALITY.md` § 3.6). Error: the page's `Alert` with Retry; the component fetches nothing.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the timeline adds no focusable element; the `Timestamp` buttons and slotted controls keep their own ring (`focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through each item's `Timestamp` and any interactive slotted content, in reading order. No roving focus and no arrow keys: it is a list, not a widget.
- ARIA: the root is an `<ol>` named by `aria-label` (default `Activity`), so a screen reader announces "list, N items". Each Group is an `<li>` with a nested `<ol aria-labelledby>` pointing at its label. Markers and the connector are `aria-hidden="true"`; the severity is carried by the title text, never by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1). While `loading`, the root has `aria-busy="true"` and a visually hidden item reads the loading label.
- Contrast: text uses `--text-default` / `--text-muted` on the canvas or surface; markers use the documented `-mark` tokens (OI-02) and `--text-muted`, which meet 3:1 for graphics and APCA Lc 30 for marks; the connector is a border (`--border-default`, Lc 15) and carries no meaning.
- Motion: none of its own; `Skeleton` honours `motion-reduce`.
- Touch target: no target of its own; `Timestamp` owns its 44 px coarse-pointer hit area.

<!-- components/timestamp.md -->

# Timestamp

> Timestamp shows one moment — when a request ran, a deployment finished, a key was created — in the form the reader needs: the local date and time, the same in UTC, or a relative phrase (`5 minutes ago`) that updates every minute. Activating it opens a small panel that lists the moment as UTC (ISO 8601), local time with its time zone, the reader's browser time when the app's time zone differs from it, the relative phrase and the raw value it was given, each with a copy button, so an operator can paste the exact value into a query or a ticket. It accepts a `Date`, an epoch in milliseconds or microseconds, or an ISO string, and reads the app-wide time zone from the nearest `ConfigProvider` (`time-zone`), so an app-level time zone picker changes every timestamp at once. Use it anywhere outside a table: log details, cards, side panels, activity lines. `TableCellTime` keeps its own author-plus-relative-time layout and shares the parsing and the relative phrasing with Timestamp.

- Import: `import Timestamp from '@aziontech/webkit/timestamp'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Timestamp to display a moment in time in the app's time zone, copyable; to pick a date use DatePicker or DateRangePicker.
- A detail panel, card or log line shows when something happened and people may need the exact or UTC value.
- An app lets people pick a display time zone and every absolute time must follow it.
- A list outside `Table` shows relative times that should stay current.

## Do

- Pass the value from your data as it comes (`'2026-11-14T12:04:31Z'`, `1794657871000`, or the microseconds a log store returns); do not pre-format it.
- Set the app's time zone once on `ConfigProvider` (`time-zone`) rather than on each Timestamp; use the `time-zone` prop only for a value that belongs to another zone (a schedule in the customer's zone).
- Use `format="relative"` for recent activity, `local` for audit records and logs, `utc` for values people compare across teams, and `time` for a row under a header that already names the day (a timeline grouped by date), so the row reads `8:20 AM` instead of repeating the date.
- In an example, a test or a server render, fix `now` on the provider and give a time zone, so the text does not depend on when or where it renders.

## Don’t

- A table column of modification times with the author → use `TableCellTime` in a `#cell-<id>` slot.
- A date the person edits → use `date-picker` (one date) or `date-range-picker` (a range).
- A duration (`1.2 s`, `3 days`) → plain text formatted with `useLocale().formatNumber`; Timestamp is a point in time.

## Related

- `config-provider` — `time-zone` sets the zone every Timestamp below it reads; `now` fixes the reference time of relative phrases.
- `table` — `TableCellTime` is the table preset for modification times; it shares Timestamp's parsing and relative phrasing.
- `copy-button` — the copy control on every row of the panel.
- `popover` — the panel Timestamp opens.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string \| number \| Date` | `undefined` | false | The moment: a `Date`, an epoch in milliseconds (microseconds when the number has 15 digits or more), a numeric string, or an ISO string. Empty or unparseable renders a muted dash with no panel. |
| `format` | `'relative' \| 'local' \| 'utc' \| 'time'` | `'local'` | false | What the text shows: the relative phrase that updates every minute, the date and time in the time zone, the date and time in UTC, or only the hour and minute in the time zone (for a row under a date header). The panel always lists every form. |
| `timeZone` | `string` | `''` | false | IANA time zone of the local time (`America/New_York`). Empty reads the nearest `ConfigProvider`'s `time-zone`, then the browser's zone. |

## States

- `data-format` on the root mirrors `format`.
- `data-state` on the root: `open` while the panel shows, `closed` otherwise (from `Popover`).
- Invalid or empty `value`: the root shows a muted dash, renders no trigger and no panel, and carries `data-invalid`.
- Before mount, with no time zone from the prop or the provider, the text renders in UTC so the server and the first client render agree; after mount it switches to the browser's zone. With a time zone, server and client render the same text.
- The relative phrase reads the provider's `now` when set, else a shared clock that ticks each minute; under 45 seconds it reads `just now`, under an hour in minutes, beyond that in the largest whole unit.
- `time` reads only the hour and the minute in the effective time zone (`Intl` `hour: numeric`, `minute: 2-digit`: `8:20 AM`, `08:20`), with no date, seconds or zone name; the `time` element keeps the full ISO value in `datetime` and the panel lists every form, so nothing is lost.
- An unknown time zone name falls back to UTC instead of throwing.
- The browser row appears only after mount and only when the effective time zone differs from the browser's.

## Accessibility

- The text is a native `button` wrapping a `time` element whose `datetime` is the ISO 8601 UTC value; the button has `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded` (from `PopoverTrigger`).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the trigger; `Enter` or `Space` opens the panel; inside the panel `Tab` moves between the copy buttons and wraps back to the trigger; `Esc` closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger.
- The panel is a non-modal `dialog` named by a visually hidden title (`Timestamp details`); the rows are a description list (`dl`), so each value is read with its label.
- Every copy button is named after its row (`Copy UTC`, `Copy Local`); the copied state is announced by `CopyButton`.
- Visible focus: the trigger and the copy buttons draw the ring token.
- Contrast: `var(--text-default)` and `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-surface-raised)` are theme-guaranteed.
- `motion-reduce:*`: the panel and the hover colour transition both pair with a reduced-motion fallback.
- Touch target: the copy buttons use the `small` `IconButton` size with the row padding around them; the trigger is inline text and grows with the text it sits in; on a coarse pointer an invisible layer (`data-slot="touch-target"`) extends its hit area to 40 px tall, the WebKit floor, without moving the text.

<!-- components/tutorial-panel.md -->

# Tutorial Panel

> The guide that runs tutorials beside the real product. It lives in the page's tools or help region, lists the tutorials a reader can take, and while one runs it shows the tutorial's tasks and the reader's place in them. The steps themselves happen on the page: each step points at a `TutorialPanelHotspot` placed beside the real control, and the current step opens there in a popover. `TutorialPanel.Provider` wraps the whole page (the content and the tools region), holds the running tutorial and the current step, and is what the panel and every hotspot read. A tutorial starts on a reader's action (the panel's Start); only one step is open on a page at a time. It is the stateful layer over `help-panel`: the panel is a `HelpPanel` with its `Header`, and draws each tutorial with its own internal task list (6.0 moved the former `HelpPanel.TutorialPanelTutorial` and `HelpPanel.Task` here; `HelpPanel` no longer has a tutorial mode). Design call (M2.9, WP app-layout): neither the design sample nor the Console Kit has a guided tutorial, so the model is Cloudscape's tutorial panel, hotspot and annotation context, rebuilt on WebKit parts. Design call (2026-11-18): the hotspot is a part of this component, not a component of its own. It renders nothing without the provider's running tutorial and reads only this component's context, so it belongs to this family the way Atlassian's `SpotlightTarget` belongs to its onboarding `SpotlightManager`; Shepherd.js and Driver.js have no separate target component at all (a step names its element), and the standalone hotspots of Appcues and Pendo work without a tour, which ours never does. Cloudscape ships `Hotspot` as its own export, but it too only works inside its annotation context. It is a companion part (it composes `Popover`), so it is imported on its own and not attached to the compound.

- Import: `import TutorialPanelRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import TutorialPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use TutorialPanel for guided tutorials whose steps point at real controls through TutorialPanelHotspot.
- A reader learns a product task by doing it on the real screen, step by step, with the instructions pointing at the control they need next.
- A product offers several tutorials in its help region and records which ones the reader finished.
- A first-run or onboarding flow guides the reader through a real create and deploy, not a mock.

## Do

- Wrap the whole page in `TutorialPanel.Provider`, so the panel and every hotspot share one state.
- Start a tutorial on a reader's action (the panel's Start, or a call to action that sets `activeKey`), never by presetting `activeKey` on the page's first render: a step popover over the page before the reader asked for it hides what they came to read.
- One step is open on a page at a time. When a provider starts or moves a tutorial it takes the open step, and the step another provider had open closes (its marker stays and reopens it).
- Keep tutorials as data (`TutorialPanelTutorial[]`): the panel lists them and the hotspots on the page read the same steps. This is the one place a config array is right — the step content is shown away from where it is declared.
- One step, one control. Write the step title as the action (`Name the service`) and the content as one or two sentences.
- Place every `TutorialPanelHotspot` a tutorial names on the page that runs it. A step whose hotspot is missing still shows in the panel, and focus moves to it there.
- Set `completed` on a tutorial from what the product recorded (the `complete` event), not from a click.
- Bind `v-model:activeKey` and `v-model:step` and persist them when a tutorial must survive a navigation.

## Don’t

- Static help beside the page, with no guided run → use `help-panel`.
- The step rail of a multi-step task in the app → use `stepper`, or `wizard` for a create flow with its footer.
- A multi-step create flow whose steps are forms in one surface → use `wizard`.
- Ordered steps the reader navigates inside a page → use `stepper`.
- A single tip pinned to one control → use `popover` or `hint`.
- An empty page that needs one call to action → use `empty-state`.

## Related

- `help-panel` — the parts the panel draws with; use it alone for help without a guided run.
- `popover` — what a `TutorialPanelHotspot` opens; the step's title, content and Previous / Next live in it.
- `drawer` — the host of the tools region on narrow screens; the panel goes inside it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The panel's heading. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Tutorials`). |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One line under the heading. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the panel's landmark. Empty uses the title. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders skeleton lines in place of the content while the tutorials load. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `completion` | { tutorial: TutorialPanelTutorial } | Extra content on the completion screen, such as a feedback link. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel-provider`
- `@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel-hotspot`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: `index.ts` attaches the provider to the panel, so
`<TutorialPanel.Provider>` resolves from the same import. The panel has no open state (the tools region
that hosts it owns that), so there is no `Trigger` / `Content`. State flows through `provide`/`inject`
(`injection-key.ts`, provided by the provider): the panel reads it through
`composables/use-tutorial-panel-context.ts`, which throws outside a provider, and `TutorialPanelHotspot` reads it
through the optional variant, which returns null so a hotspot outside a provider renders only its content.
Which provider holds the page's one open step is a module-level owner in `lib/open-step-owner.ts`: a
provider takes it when it starts or moves a tutorial (or, on mount or when `activeKey` is set from
outside, only if no provider holds it), and gives it back on exit and unmount. A provider that does
not hold it reports its step as dismissed, so its popover is closed and its marker stays.

- `tutorial-panel-provider/tutorial-panel-provider.vue` — Holds the tutorials, the running tutorial (`v-model:activeKey`), the current step (`v-model:step`, flat across tasks), whether the reader dismissed the current s…
  - Props: `tutorials?: TutorialPanelTutorial[]` (default `[]`).
  - Models (`defineModel`): `v-model:activeKey` (`string \| null`, default `null` — the parent owns it when bound, the provider keeps it locally when not), `v-model:step` (`number`, default `0`, same rule; equals the step count once the tutorial is finished).
  - Events: `update:activeKey` (`string \| null`) and `update:step` (`number`) from the models; `start` (`(event: Event, id: string)` — the tutorial id, on Start and Restart), `exit` (`(event: Event, id: string)` — on Exit or Back to tutorials), `complete` (`(event: Event, id: string)` — on Finish of the last step). Each fires from a button the reader activated (in the panel or a hotspot popover, through the context), so the DOM event comes first and the tutorial id second.
  - Slot: `default` — the page, with the panel and every hotspot inside.

- `tutorial-panel-hotspot/tutorial-panel-hotspot.vue` — **companion part** (composes `Popover` and `Button`; exported on its own, not attached): marks a real control as a step.
  - Props: `hotspotId: string` (required) — matches the `hotspotId` of a tutorial step; `side?: 'start' | 'end'` (default `'end'`, type `TutorialPanelHotspotSide`) — which side of the wrapped control the marker sits on, in reading direction.
  - Events: none — moves go through the provider.
  - Slot: `default` — the real control the step is about.
  - States: `idle` (no marker), `marked` (static marker), `active` (the current step: filled, pulsing, popover open), `dismissed` (the current step closed by the reader, or by another provider taking the open step: filled, no pulse, popover closed). `data-marker` on the root when the marker shows; `data-active` on the root and the marker for the current step; `data-side` mirrors `side`; the popover's `data-state` is owned by `Popover`.
  - `data-testid` fallback `tutorial-panel-hotspot`; inner parts `__marker`, `__popover`, `__trigger`, `__step`, `__title`, `__close`, `__previous`, `__next`.
  - Keyboard and ARIA: the marker is a `button` in the tab order after the wrapped control (before it with `side="start"`), named `Tutorial step: <title>`, with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` from `Popover.Trigger`; `Enter` / `Space` opens its step and makes it current. The popover is a non-modal `dialog` labelled by the step title and described by `Step n of N`; `Tab` cycles Close, Previous and Next; `Esc` closes the step and returns focus to the marker. Next, Previous and the marker move focus into the new step's popover. The pulse ring and dot are `aria-hidden`; the ring pings three times and stops (WCAG 2.2.2).
  - Touch: a 24 px marker with a `before:` pseudo-element that extends the hit area to 40 px; the root reserves `--spacing-xs` on the marker's outer side so a hotspot flush with a narrow row does not scroll the page sideways.

- `parts/tutorial-panel-tasks.vue` — internal, not exported: a tutorial's title, description, a progress line derived from the registered tasks (`2 of 3 complete`, `aria-live="polite"`), the ordered task `<ol>` and an a…
- `parts/tutorial-panel-task.vue` — internal, not exported: one task, a numbered marker, a title and its steps.

Exported types: `TutorialPanelTutorial` (`id`, `title`, `description?`, `completed?`, `tasks`), `TutorialPanelTaskData` (`title`, `steps`), `TutorialPanelStep` (`title`, `content`, `hotspotId`), `TutorialPanelHotspotSide`.

```
├── tutorial-panel.test.ts
```

Exports:

```jsonc
"./tutorial-panel": "./src/components/content/tutorial-panel/index.ts",
"./tutorial-panel-root": "./src/components/content/tutorial-panel/tutorial-panel.vue",
"./tutorial-panel-provider": "./src/components/content/tutorial-panel/tutorial-panel-provider/tutorial-panel-provider.vue",
```

Composed DS components (relative imports): `help-panel` (root, `Header`), `button`, `empty-state`, `tag`, `popover` (the hotspot's step).

## States

- Visual states: `list`, `running`, `complete`, `empty` (no tutorials, rendered by a small `EmptyState` titled with `tutorialPanel.emptyTitle`), `loading`
- `data-view` on the root: `list` | `running` | `complete`
- `data-completed` on each list item mirrors the tutorial's `completed`
- In `running`, each task's status is derived from the current step: `success` when every step of the task is behind it, `pending` otherwise; the task that holds the current step is `active`. The current step's row carries `aria-current="step"`.
- `complete` shows a completion section (check icon, `TutorialPanelTutorial complete`, `You finished <title>.`, the `completion` slot, Restart and Back to tutorials) above the task list, every task complete.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the composed `Button`s carry the standard ring; focus targets that are not controls (the list heading, the completion heading, the current step row) take `tabindex="-1"` and `outline-none` because they receive focus only programmatically.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through Start / Restart, Exit, Restart and Back. Focus management: Start moves focus to the current step's popover (through its hotspot) or, when that hotspot is not on the page, to the step's row in the panel; Finish moves focus to the `TutorialPanelTutorial complete` heading; Exit and Back move focus to the list's heading.
- ARIA: the panel is a `HelpPanel` complementary landmark named by `ariaLabel` or the title. Each list item's Start button is described by its tutorial's heading (`aria-describedby`), so repeated buttons are distinct. The task progress line is `aria-live="polite"`. The current step row carries `aria-current="step"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 on muted ink over `--bg-surface` in both themes.
- Touch target: the composed `Button`s (small) meet 24 px; the panel adds no other control.

# Video Player

> A native video player with play and pause, seek with time, mute and volume, captions and full screen. It also shows the states of a generated video before it plays: generating (with an optional percentage) and error. It plays the URL the app hands it (https, `blob:` or `data:`) and fetches nothing.

- Import: `import VideoPlayer from '@aziontech/webkit/video-player'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A generated or attached video in a chat message or artifact, from generating to playing.
- A recorded clip in an app screen.

## Do

- Give a `poster` and an `aria-label`.
- Mark the caption track in the page's language as `default`.
- Pass `progress` only when the generator reports one.

## Don’t

- A third-party player page (YouTube, Vimeo) → use `embed`.
- A docs clip → use `doc-frame`.
- A stored file of any type → use `file-preview`.

## Related

- `embed` — third-party players.
- `file-preview` — stored files of any type.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | `''` | false | URL of the video: https, blob or data. |
| `mimeType` | `string` | `''` | false | Media type, such as video/mp4. |
| `poster` | `string` | `''` | false | Still image shown before play. |
| `captions` | `VideoPlayerCaption[]` | `[]` | false | WebVTT caption tracks. |
| `status` | `'pending' \| 'running' \| 'success' \| 'error'` | `'success'` | false | Generation status; success plays. |
| `progress` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Percent done while generating; unset is indeterminate. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Message of the error state. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name; empty reads Video. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retry` | `MouseEvent` | Try again in the error state was pressed. The button renders only when this event has a listener; a file that failed to load is loaded again, and the app sets `status` back to `pending` or `running` when it generates the video again. |

## States

- `data-status` mirrors `status`; a file that fails to load, or no `src`, shows `error`.
- `pending` / `running`: `Skeleton`, a `role="status"` message, `Progress` and the percentage; no controls.
- `error`: `EmptyState` with `error` or the default message; no playback controls. With a `retry` listener it shows a Try again `Button` (`az az-refresh`, outline, medium) under the message.
- `success`: the video and its controls; `data-paused`, `data-muted`.

## Accessibility

- `role="group"` named by `ariaLabel` (or Video). Native buttons and range inputs, each labelled; the seek bar reads like 1:05 of 3:20.
- Keyboard: `Tab`, `Enter` / `Space`, arrows (seek 1 s, volume 5), `Home` / `End`; `Esc` leaves full screen.
- No autoplay; status changes are announced, never move focus. Buttons 40 px (44 px coarse), bars 40 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import placeholderClip from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/placeholder-clip.webm'
  import placeholderImage from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/placeholder-image.svg'
  import VideoPlayer from '@aziontech/webkit/video-player'

  const vtt = 'WEBVTT\n\n00:00.000 --> 00:05.000\nCreate an application for Acme Store.'
  const captions = [
    {
      src: `data:text/vtt,${encodeURIComponent(vtt)}`,
      srclang: 'en',
      label: 'English',
      default: true
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <VideoPlayer
    class="max-w-(--container-xl)"
    :src="placeholderClip"
    mime-type="video/webm"
    :poster="placeholderImage"
    :captions="captions"
    aria-label="Creating an application for Acme Store"
  />
</template>
```

# Card List

> Use CardList to show a collection of records as selectable cards instead of table rows; for one bordered box use Card, and for the frame of a dashboard chart use ChartCard. A collection shown as cards, after Cloudscape's cards: one card per item, named by its `header` slot, with the item's fields in the default slot. It follows Cloudscape's collection model — `items`, `itemKey`, `selectedKeys` (a key array) — which is not yet the same as Table's (`data`, `rowKey`, `rowSelection` record); `useCollection` binds it through `cardListProps`, and selection (single or multiple, with a visible select-all) survives paging. Four cards a row in a wide container, then three, two and one as the container narrows.

- Import: `import CardList from '@aziontech/webkit/card-list'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Items people recognise by a few fields or a picture rather than compare column by column (applications, templates, environments).
- The card form of a list page (`view/view-card`), filtered and paged by `useCollection`.

## Do

- Put the item's name, as a link to the item, in the `header` slot: it also names the selection control.
- Keep each card to a handful of label and value pairs; let `collection-preferences` choose which.
- Use `selectionMode="multiple"` only when a bulk action exists next to the list.
- Pass items typed with your own interface (`Domain[]`): the slots read `item.name` with that type, so never cast `item` in a slot or widen the items to `Record<string, unknown>[]`.

## Don’t

- Records compared, sorted or scanned across many fields → use `table`.
- A fixed marketing grid of features or links → use `card-grid`.
- A single content box → use `card`.

## Related

- `use-collection` — filters, pages and selects; `cardListProps` is the binding.
- `table` — the same collection as rows; same item and selection model.
- `property-filter`, `collection-preferences`, `pagination` — the controls around it.
- `card` — one standalone card.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `TItem[]` | `[]` | false | The items, one card each. |
| `itemKey` | `string` | `'id'` | false | Field that identifies an item; selection keys read it. |
| `selectionMode` | `'none' \| 'single' \| 'multiple'` | `'none'` | false | No selection, one card, or several cards with a select-all above them. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows placeholder cards and sets aria-busy while true. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `selectedKeys` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:selectedKeys`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `header` | CardListItemSlotProps<TItem> | Card title; names the card and its selection control. |
| `default` | CardListItemSlotProps<TItem> | Card body: the item's fields. |
| `empty` | — | Shown when there are no items. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:selected-keys`** — `string[]`, default `[]`. Keys (`item[itemKey]`) of the selected cards; keys of items not on the current page are kept.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `selected`, `loading`, `empty`
- `data-state` on each card: `selected` | `unselected`; `data-selected` when selected
- `data-selection` on the root mirrors `selectionMode`; `aria-busy` while loading

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the checkbox, the radio and the links in the header slot.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the select-all, each card's control and its content; `Space` toggles a control.
- ARIA: the cards are a named `list` of `listitem`s; each checkbox is labelled by its card's header (`aria-labelledby`), and in single mode each card's `RadioGroup.Item` has no label text and forwards `aria-labelledby` (the header id) to its radio; the select-all has a visible label; the root sets `aria-busy` while loading.
- Selection is never conveyed by color alone: the control is checked.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) and ≥3:1 for the selected border.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
```

<!-- components/collection-preferences.md -->

# Collection Preferences

> The preferences panel of a collection, after Cloudscape's collection preferences: a cog button opens a dialog (or a drawer) with the page size, the columns (shown, hidden and ordered; a locked column always shows), wrapped lines, striped rows and density. Changes are a draft until Confirm; Cancel, `Esc` and the close button discard them. It holds no saved state itself: `useCollection` saves the confirmed value in `localStorage` and `preferencesProps` binds the value, the columns and the page sizes in one `v-bind`. It is the one column chooser of a table. Placed in a DataTable's `toolbar` slot with no `columns`, it reads the table through context: the columns are the table's hideable leaf columns (a column with `hideable: false` is listed locked), the draft starts from the table's column visibility and order, and Confirm writes both back to the table (`update:columnVisibility`) besides emitting `confirm` and `update:preferences`. Bound to `useCollection`, `preferencesProps` supplies `columns` and the context is not read.

- Import: `import CollectionPreferences from '@aziontech/webkit/collection-preferences'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use CollectionPreferences for every 'how this list looks' setting: page size, visible and ordered columns, density, wrap.
- A table or card collection whose people choose how many items a page shows and which fields they see.
- Any collection driven by `useCollection`, which saves the result per collection.

## Do

- Lock the column that names the item (`locked: true`): a row without its name is unreadable.
- Show only the sections the collection uses (`sections`): cards have no striped rows.
- Keep the trigger at the end of the controls row, after Refresh and Download.

## Don’t

- Settings of the resource itself (not of how the list shows it) → use a form page or `dialog`.

## Related

- `use-collection` — saves the preferences; `preferencesProps` is the binding.
- `data-table` — takes `density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`, the visible columns and their order; inside its toolbar this panel edits its columns with no wiring.
- `card-list` — takes the page size and the visible fields.
- `property-filter` — sits beside it in the controls row.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `CollectionPreferencesColumn[]` | `[]` | false | Columns to show, hide and order. Empty reads the enclosing DataTable's columns, or hides the columns section outside one. |
| `pageSizeOptions` | `number[]` | `[]` | false | Page sizes offered. Empty hides the page size section. |
| `sections` | `CollectionPreferencesSection[]` | `['page-size', 'columns', 'wrap-lines', 'striped', 'density']` | false | Sections the panel shows, in this order. |
| `container` | `'dialog' \| 'drawer'` | `'dialog'` | false | Opens in a centered dialog or a side drawer. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Panel title and trigger label. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |
| `preferences` | `CollectionPreferencesValue` | `—` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:preferences`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | `(event: MouseEvent, value: CollectionPreferencesValue)` | Same value, for a handler that is not a model. |
| `cancel` | `(event: MouseEvent)` | Cancel was activated; the draft is discarded. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | { open: () => void } | Replaces the cog button; call `open` to open the panel. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:open`** — `boolean`, default `undefined`, via `defineModel('open')`. Whether the panel is open; the trigger, Confirm, Cancel, the close button and `Esc` update it. Unbound, the panel keeps it itself and starts at `defaultOpen`.
- **`v-model:preferences`** — `CollectionPreferencesValue`, default `{}`, via `defineModel('preferences')`. Set on Confirm with the sections shown (`update:preferences`). Unbound, the panel keeps the confirmed values itself, so it reopens on them.

## States

- Visual states: `closed`, `open`; the trigger reflects `disabled`
- `data-state` on the root: `open` | `closed`
- Move up is disabled on the first column, move down on the last; a locked column's switch is disabled and on, and its label carries `data-locked` (muted, default cursor)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the buttons, switches, radios and the toggle group.
- Keyboard map: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens; `Tab` is trapped in the panel; `Esc` closes; focus returns to the trigger on close; after a move, focus stays on the moved column's button.
- ARIA: the trigger has `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`; the panel is a dialog named by its title; the page size and the columns are `fieldset`s with a `legend`; each move button is named `Move <column> up|down`; the density group is labelled by its heading.
- Columns reorder with buttons, never by drag only (WCAG 2.5.7).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CollectionPreferences from '@aziontech/webkit/collection-preferences'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const columns = [
    { id: 'name', label: 'Name', locked: true },
    { id: 'status', label: 'Status' },
    { id: 'region', label: 'Region' },
    { id: 'requests', label: 'Requests' }
  ]

  const preferences = ref({
    pageSize: 25,
    columns: [
      { id: 'name', visible: true },
      { id: 'status', visible: true },
      { id: 'region', visible: false },
      { id: 'requests', visible: true }
    ],
    wrapLines: false,
    striped: false,
    density: 'comfortable'
  })
</script>

<template>
  <CollectionPreferences
    v-model:preferences="preferences"
    :columns="columns"
    :page-size-options="[10, 25, 50, 100]"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/data-grid.md -->

# Data Grid

> An editable, spreadsheet-like grid: rows of records and typed columns where people move a cell cursor with the keyboard, edit cells in place, select ranges, copy them and paste a block of cells from a spreadsheet, the way an SQL editor's results and a database table editor work. It shares the table's visual language (header band, row dividers, row selection, a pinned first column, the same tokens) but renders the WAI-ARIA **grid** pattern (`role="grid"`, `gridcell`, one roving tab stop), not a read-only table. **Why a component of its own.** DataGrid is not an `editable` mode of `data-table` and is not composed from `table`'s parts, for three reasons. Table's parts render the **table** pattern (`role="table"`, `cell`, every link and button its own tab stop), while a grid needs `gridcell`s inside one roving tab stop with a cell cursor; switching the roles and the focus model inside the same parts would make every read-only table pay for it. In-cell editors must be borderless and fill the cell, so they are a bare `input` and `select` styled with the tokens, not the package's `Input` and `Select`, whose frames and overlays fight a 40 px cell. And DataGrid needs no sorting, filtering or paging engine: it loads no `@tanstack/vue-table` and no virtualization library, so an editing screen stays at about 9 KB. **The rows are the edited value.** Where `data-table` takes `data` and only emits `update:data` when rows are reordered, DataGrid's rows are what the person edits, so they are its `v-model`: every committed edit writes a new array with a copy of the edited row, and `change` reports the cell, the new value and the previous one. A paste is the same edit over many cells: one new array for the whole paste, one `change` per changed cell. Adding and deleting rows are hooks: the grid emits `row-add` and `row-remove` and the app changes the rows. Thousands of rows scroll natively inside `maxHeight`, each row is laid out lazily with CSS `content-visibility: auto`, and each row re-renders only when its cells, its cursor or its range change.

- Import: `import DataGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/data-grid'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use DataGrid only when people edit many cells of many records in place, spreadsheet-style; for a short list of rows in a form use AttributeEditor, for read-and-act lists use DataTable (a hand-composed Table for small static ones).
- A database table editor or the editable results of a query: typed cells (text, number, boolean, a choice), keyboard-first editing, copy of a cell range and paste of a block copied from a spreadsheet.
- Bulk corrections across rows, where opening a drawer per record would be slower than editing the cells.

## Do

- Give every row a stable id under `row-key` (default `'id'`): the cursor, the selection and the edits follow it.
- Type each column (`text`, `number`, `boolean`, `select`) so the editor matches the value; mark computed or key columns `editable: false`.
- Freeze the first column (`frozen-first-column`) when it names the row and the grid scrolls sideways.
- Keep adding and deleting in the app: handle `row-add` and `row-remove`, then write the new rows to the `v-model`. Confirm a delete of more than a few rows in a `confirm-dialog`.
- Use `readonly` while saving or for people who may not edit; the cursor, selection and copy still work, and a paste writes nothing.
- Save on `change`, not on `update:modelValue`, when each cell is stored on its own: a paste fires one `change` per changed cell, so a per-cell save keeps working.

## Don’t

- People read, sort, filter, select and act on records but do not edit cells → use `data-table` (or a hand-composed `table`).
- A short list of same-field rows added and removed inside a form (environment variables, headers) → use `attribute-editor`.
- One record edited field by field → use a form with `field` controls.
- Key and value pairs shown for reading → use `key-value-list`.

## Related

- `data-table` — the read-and-act table (sorting, filters, paging, toolbar parts); DataGrid is its editable counterpart.
- `table` — the parts and tokens DataGrid shares its look with.
- `attribute-editor` — a few rows of the same fields inside a form.
- `collection-preferences` — the display preferences of a list; DataGrid's column widths are dragged in place instead.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `DataGridColumn[]` | `[]` | false | Columns in order: `{ id, header, type?, options?, editable?, width?, minWidth?, align? }`; `type` picks the editor (default text). |
| `rowKey` | `string` | `'id'` | false | Field used as the stable row id (cursor, selection and edits follow it). |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Adds a leading checkbox column with Select all. |
| `frozenFirstColumn` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Pins the first data column to the inline start edge while the grid scrolls sideways. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | No cell can be edited; the cursor, range selection and copy still work. |
| `maxHeight` | `string` | `''` | false | Max height (CSS length) of the scrolling viewport; the header stays on top. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the grid when no visible heading names it. |
| `modelValue` | `TRow[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `selectedKeys` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:selectedKeys`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `change` | `(event: Event, edit: DataGridCellEdit)` | A cell edit was committed (Enter, Tab, blur, a toggle), or once per changed cell of a paste (`event` is the `ClipboardEvent`); `edit` is `{ row, columnId, value, previous }`. |
| `row-add` | `(event: Event)` | The `add` function of the toolbar slot ran; the app appends a row to the `v-model`. |
| `row-remove` | `(event: Event, rows: TRow[])` | The `remove` function of the toolbar slot ran with rows selected; the app removes them from the `v-model`. |
| `copy` | `(event: ClipboardEvent, text: string)` | Ctrl+C or Cmd+C copied the selected cell range as tab-separated text (rows by line), written to the clipboard through the `copy` event's `clipboardData`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toolbar` | { selectedRows: TRow[]; selectedCount: number; add: (event: Event) => void; remove: (event: Event) => void } | Action band above the grid (add and delete buttons); `add` and `remove` emit the row hooks. |
| `empty` | — | Shown in place of the rows when there are none. Defaults to a small `EmptyState`. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `TRow[]` | `[]` | `update:modelValue` | The rows. A committed edit writes a new array with a copy of the edited row; a paste writes one new array for the whole block, copying only the changed rows. |
| `v-model:selected-keys` | `string[]` | `[]` | `update:selectedKeys` | Keys of the selected rows, read from `rowKey` (the same shape as DataTable's `selectedKeys`). Space on the checkbox column and Select all change it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (row), `focus-visible` (the cursor ring on the active cell or header), `selected` (cells in a range of two or more cells: `data-selected`, `aria-selected="true"`; the cursor cell alone is shown by its focus ring and is not painted as selected, so a grid nobody touched shows no selection; rows checked: `data-state="selected"`), `editing` (`data-editing` on the cell with the editor open), `readonly` (`data-readonly` on the root; non-editable cells carry `aria-readonly`).
- `invalid`: a number cell whose text is not a number stays in its editor on Enter or Tab, with `data-invalid` on the cell and the editor, `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` pointing to a message (`dataGrid.invalidNumber`, `role="alert"`) under the cell; nothing is committed until the text parses or Escape restores the value. Blur with an invalid text discards it and keeps the previous value.
- `paste`: Ctrl+V or Cmd+V on the cell cursor reads the `paste` event's `text/plain` (no clipboard permission prompt) as tab-separated text: rows by line break (CRLF or LF), cells by tab, one trailing line break ignored, and a cell wrapped in double quotes may hold tabs and line breaks (`""` is a quote), the way Excel and Google Sheets copy. The block is written from the top-left cell of the selected range (the cursor cell when there is no range), clipped at the last row and column (a paste never adds rows; rows are the app's, through `row-add`); a single value with a range of several cells selected fills every cell of the range. Each value is read the way an in-cell edit commits it: `number` parses a number (empty clears it), `boolean` takes `true` / `false`, `1` / `0`, `yes` / `no` or the localized Yes / No (case-insensitive), `select` takes an option value or an option label (case-insensitive), `text` takes the text as is (empty clears it). A value that does not fit, a cell of a non-editable column and every cell of a `readonly` grid are skipped and keep their value. Afterwards the selected range is the pasted area, the cursor on its top-left cell, and a polite status announces the result (`dataGrid.pasted`, `dataGrid.pastedSkipped`, `dataGrid.pasteReadonly`). While an in-cell editor is open the grid does not handle the paste, so the editor's native paste inserts the text; on the header row a paste does nothing.
- `copy`: Ctrl+C or Cmd+C on the cell cursor writes the selected range to the native `copy` event's `clipboardData` as `text/plain` and cancels the event, so it needs no clipboard permission and works on an insecure (plain http) origin. When the browser fires no `copy` event for the shortcut, the grid runs the copy command itself. Rows go by `\n`, cells by tab, and a cell holding a tab, a line break or a double quote is wrapped in double quotes with each quote doubled, the way Excel and Google Sheets copy, so a copied range pastes back into the grid cell for cell. While an in-cell editor is open the grid does not handle the copy, so the editor's native copy takes its selected text.
- `empty`: no rows, the `empty` slot (default `EmptyState`, `dataGrid.emptyTitle`) under the header, outside the grid's rows; the header and toolbar stay.
- No `disabled` state: a grid people may not edit is `readonly` (the cursor, ranges and copy keep working). No `loading` or `error` state of its own: the app shows a `Skeleton` or an `Alert` around the grid while it loads; DataGrid never fetches.
- `data-frozen="start"` on the first column's cells with `frozenFirstColumn`; `data-resizing` on a header while its width is dragged.
- Scroll cue: the viewport sits in a `__scroll` frame that sets `data-overflow-start` / `data-overflow-end` from the scroll position (re-measured on scroll and on resize). While content is hidden past an inline edge, an `aria-hidden` gradient as wide as the hidden distance (at most 24 px, none when 4 px or less, so it never sits over text that is otherwise in view) (`__fade-start` / `__fade-end`, `from-transparent` to `var(--bg-surface)`, pointer events off) covers that edge; the start fade begins after the frozen columns. It follows the inline direction under `dir="rtl"`, has no motion, and keeps its gradient under forced colors (fading to `Canvas`).

## Accessibility

- Pattern: the WAI-ARIA APG **data grid**. The grid element is `role="grid"` with `aria-rowcount` (rows + header) and `aria-colcount`, named by `ariaLabel`, or by an `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby` passed to DataGrid (both are forwarded to the grid element, not the frame), `aria-multiselectable="true"` (a cell range can always be selected) and `aria-readonly="true"` while `readonly`. Rows are `role="row"` with `aria-rowindex` (1-based, header is 1) and `aria-selected` when row selection is on; header cells `role="columnheader"`, body cells `role="gridcell"`, each with `aria-colindex`; every gridcell carries `aria-selected` (`true` in a range of two or more cells, `false` outside it and on a lone cursor cell) and a cell that cannot be edited `aria-readonly="true"`. The empty state renders outside the grid's rows, so `aria-rowcount` stays exact.
- One tab stop: exactly one cell of the grid has `tabindex="0"` (the active cell, the first body cell at start; the header row is part of the cursor), every other cell, checkbox and resize handle `-1`. `Tab` enters the grid on the active cell and `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` leave it. The editor inside a cell takes focus while editing and returns it to the cell when it closes.
- Keyboard map (cell cursor): `Arrow` keys move one cell, up into the header row and back (inline arrows follow the reading direction); `Home` / `End` the first / last cell of the row; `Ctrl+Home` / `Ctrl+End` the first / last cell of the grid; `PageUp` / `PageDown` ten rows; `Shift` with an arrow, `Home` or `End` extends the range over body cells; `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` leave the grid. `Enter` or `F2` opens the editor of a body cell and, on a header cell, moves focus to its resize handle; typing a character opens a text or number editor with that character (select and boolean cells do not open on typing); `Space` toggles a boolean cell, the row checkbox, or Select all on its header; `Delete` / `Backspace` clears an editable text or number cell; `Ctrl+C` / `Cmd+C` copies the range; `Ctrl+V` / `Cmd+V` pastes a tab-separated block from the top-left cell of the range, or fills the range with a single value (see States); `Ctrl+A` / `Cmd+A` selects every cell.
- Keyboard map (editing): `Enter` commits and moves down; `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` commit and move to the next / previous cell (wrapping across rows), the one case where Tab moves inside the grid; `Escape` cancels and restores the value; blur commits. A select editor is a native `select`: its arrow keys change the choice without committing, and Enter, Tab or blur commit it. An invalid number keeps the editor open (see States).
- Paste result: a visually hidden `role="status"` `aria-live="polite"` region outside the grid's rows announces `Pasted {count} cells`, `Pasted {count} cells, {skipped} skipped`, or `Read-only, nothing pasted`.
- Row checkboxes are named after the row: `dataGrid.selectRow` (`Select row {row}`) filled with the first column's text, else the row key.
- Resize handles are `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`, `aria-valuenow` (the width in px), `aria-valuemin` (`minWidth`, 64 by default), `aria-valuemax` (960) and a name (`dataGrid.resize`: `Resize Name`); they are reached with Enter from their header cell, `Arrow Left` / `Arrow Right` change the width by 16 px, and `Escape` or `Enter` return focus to the header cell.
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` inset on the active cell or header; the editor uses the same ring (`--danger-border` while invalid).
- Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for text (muted header text included); the selected surface keeps the text contrast.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch: cells and headers are 40 px high, 44 px under `pointer: coarse`; tapping a cell moves the cursor there, a second tap opens the editor; the resize handle has a 24 px hit area, 44 px under `pointer: coarse`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue

  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const rows = ref([
    { id: '1', name: 'Acme Inc.', plan: 'business', seats: 12, active: true },
    { id: '2', name: 'Jane Doe', plan: 'free', seats: 1, active: true },
    { id: '3', name: 'John Smith', plan: 'pro', seats: 3, active: false },
    { id: '4', name: 'Priya Patel', plan: 'pro', seats: 5, active: true },
```
