<!-- components/data-table.md -->

# Data Table

> The data-driven table: pass `data` + `columns` and it renders the header, rows, selection, sorting, empty / loading / error states itself, through the same `Table` parts (`Table.Header`, `Table.Row`, `Table.HeadCell`, `Table.Cell`), so its markup, tokens and accessibility are those of `table`. The headless **`@tanstack/vue-table`** engine lives here and only here: a hand-composed `Table` never loads it. A top **toolbar band** (`title` / `toolbar` / `filters` slots) sits above the scroll viewport for a title, the context-aware `Table.*` toolbar parts (search, filter, export, refresh, live) and removable filter chips; the `toolbar` and `filters` slots are scoped with the TanStack `table` instance so the consumer can drive filtering, global search and column visibility through the table's own methods. Optional features are **companion parts** that read the table's context (`compound-api.md`, CODE_QUALITY 3.4): `DataTablePagination` in the `footer` slot pages the rows with `Pagination`, `DataTableLoadMore` in the `load-more` slot asks for the next rows, and the toolbar parts own the search text, the structured filters, the live tail and the export rows. A root-only table loads none of them. **Engine.** DataTable is driven by **`@tanstack/vue-table`** (`useVueTable` + `getCoreRowModel` / `getSortedRowModel` / `getFilteredRowModel` / `getPaginationRowModel`), covering sorting, pagination, row selection, column visibility, and global filtering — client- and server-side (`manualSorting` / `manualFiltering` on the root, `manual` on `DataTablePagination`). It is a pure-logic library (no markup/styles/positioning/animation), granted narrowly to the table family (this component and the editable `data-grid` that builds on it) per [`contributing/rules/dependencies.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/contributing/rules/dependencies.md) § Exceptions; rendering stays 100% in our primitives. State is exposed via v-model in webkit shapes: `sorting`, `selectedKeys`, `columnVisibility` and `openKeys` on the root, `page` + `pageSize` on `DataTablePagination`, the search text on `TableSearch`, the structured filters on `TableFilter` and the live tail on `TableLiveButton`; the component adapts them to the engine internally, and `getSnapshot()` / `setSnapshot()` read and write all of them at once. `@tanstack/virtual` remains forbidden: the opt-in `virtual` mode windows the rows itself (spacer padding above and below the rendered slice, sized from a height index: each rendered row is measured with a `ResizeObserver`, rows not yet rendered take the average of the first rows measured (48 px before the first row is measured), and when a row above the rows in view changes height the scroll position moves by the same amount so the rows in view stay still). Without `virtual`, a list of more than 200 rows renders its first 50 rows and mounts the rest as a spacer below them nears the viewport (an `IntersectionObserver`), so a long page costs what is on screen. **Toolbar & imperative API.** The toolbar band composes context-aware controls that drive the table through the injected context with no wiring: `TableFilter` (the slot that hosts `FilterMenu` with `type="menu"`, or `PropertyFilter` with `type="property"`, over its `fields`), `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` with no `fields` in the `filters` slot (the applied fields of the menu type, labelled by the fields the mounted `TableFilter` registers), `CollectionPreferences` with no `columns` (visible columns and their order, written back on Confirm), `TableSearch` (the global text filter, `v-model`), `TableExportButton` (CSV download, `rows` for every match), `TableRefreshButton` and `TableLiveButton` (the live tail, `v-model`). Structured filters are a first-class model (`TableFilter` `v-model`, a `TableAppliedFilter[]` distinct from the free-text search) mapped to the TanStack column filters client-side, or emitted for a server refetch under `manualFiltering`. A `loading` prop renders skeleton rows for dynamic (server-side) data. The root exposes a **curated imperative API** via `defineExpose` (`reload`, `clearFilters`, `exportCsv`, `getSnapshot`, `setSnapshot`) so controls or logic outside the table can drive it through a template ref, and a serializable `TableStateSnapshot` (`sorting` / `page` / `pageSize` / `columnVisibility` / `columnOrder` / `globalFilter` / `filters`) is read with `getSnapshot()` and written back with `setSnapshot()` — the component stays router-agnostic, so the consuming app owns any URL / localStorage persistence. CSV serialization lives in a pure util at [`@aziontech/webkit/utils/csv`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/packages/webkit/src/utils/csv.ts) (`toCsv` + `downloadCsv`). **Types** (declared in `injection-key.ts`, re-exported for consumers): `TableFilterOperator` = `'eq' | 'neq' | 'contains' | 'not-contains' | 'starts-with' | 'ends-with' | 'gt' | 'gte' | 'lt' | 'lte' | 'in' | 'not-in' | 'is-empty' | 'is-not-empty' | 'within' | 'between'` (`within` holds a period id — `24h`, `7d`, `30d`, `3m` — and matches dates inside that window ending now; `between` holds `[start, end]` epoch milliseconds, either one `''` for an open bound; both read the cell as a `Date`, a timestamp or a parseable date string); `TableFilterType` = `'menu' | 'property'`; `TableFilterField` = `{ id: string; label: string; type: 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'multi-select' | 'boolean' | 'date'; operators?: TableFilterOperator[]; options?: { label: string; value: string | number | boolean }[] }`; `TableAppliedFilter` = `{ field: string; operator: TableFilterOperator; value: string | number | boolean | Array<string | number>; label?: string }`; `TableStateSnapshot` = `{ sorting?: SortingState; page?: number; pageSize?: number; columnVisibility?: VisibilityState; columnOrder?: string[]; globalFilter?: string; filters?: TableAppliedFilter[] }` (every field optional so `setSnapshot` accepts a partial; JSON-serializable). **Collections.** `useCollection` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-collection`) drives DataTable in both client and server modes: `tableProps` binds `data` (one page), `columns` (ordered by the saved preferences), `rowKey`, `loading`, `sorting`, `manualSorting` / `manualFiltering`, `selectable`, `selectedKeys`, `columnVisibility` and the three display preferences (`density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`) together with their update handlers, in one `v-bind`; `paginationProps` binds `DataTablePagination` (`v-bind="paginationProps" manual`: `page`, `total`, `pageSize`, `pageSizeOptions` and their handlers). The table keeps rendering one page; the composable owns filtering, sorting, paging and selection across pages, so `exportItems` given to `TableExportButton` `rows` hands the export every match rather than the page: in client mode the matching items (or every item for the `all` scope), in server mode what the collection's `exportAll` callback loads (the loaded page when there is none). **Cell presets and reordering.** The six `TableCell*` presets (each its own import, `@aziontech/webkit/table-cell-<name>`) render the cells every list repeats, each inside a `#cell-<id>` slot: `TableCellLink` (a name that leaves the screen: an optional muted leading glyph (`icon`) for the provider or resource type, a 12 px external mark, a tooltip naming the destination, underline on hover, no mark without a destination; optional `+N` overflow through `OverflowCount` and a copy button pinned to the end edge), `TableCellId` (an identifier with its copy button), `TableCellStatus` (one semantic `Tag`), `TableCellTags` (as many tags as fit, the rest behind `+N`), `TableCellTime` (avatar of the author plus a relative time that updates every minute, or counts from the nearest `ConfigProvider`'s `now`, the absolute time on the tooltip and for screen readers; with no provider `now`, a server render prints the UTC date and the cell switches to the relative time once mounted, so hydration never mismatches) and `TableCellActions` (the row menu named after the row). `reorderable` adds a leading grip column: drag a grip with the pointer, or focus it and press Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home or End; the table emits `update:data` with the reordered records and `reorder` with `{ from, to, row }`, announces every move in a polite status region and locks while a sort is applied; `rowReorderable` keeps chosen rows (a pinned default) in place.

- Import: `import DataTable from '@aziontech/webkit/data-table'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use DataTable for records that share columns — any console list of resources people scan, sort and act on.
- Records with the same fields shown in rows and columns, where the reader compares, sorts, selects or acts on rows (resource lists, logs, usage breakdowns): use DataTable for read-and-act lists of repeated records.
- A list needs a toolbar for search, structured filters, column visibility, CSV export or refresh — the `Table.*` toolbar parts drive the DataTable through context.
- Server-backed data that pages, sorts or filters on the API: `manual-sorting`, `manual-filtering` and a `manual` `DataTablePagination` emit the state instead of slicing locally.
- Thousands of rows (`virtual`), tree rows (`get-sub-rows`), reorderable rows, infinite loading or a live tail.

## Do

- For repeated data, pass `data` + `columns` and customize cells with the `cell-<columnId>` / `header-<columnId>` slots instead of composing N rows by hand. Compose `Table` by hand only for small, static tables.
- Give rows a stable id under `row-key` (default `'id'`); selection and `v-model:selected-keys` are keyed by it.
- When the principal cell repeats another column's value in a phone summary line (a status under the name), set `narrow: false` on that column so a narrow table shows the principal and the actions columns only, never a clipped sliver of the repeated one.
- Mark the row-actions column `type: 'action'` so it pins to the trailing edge; give chip or short-token columns a `minWidth` rather than a fixed `width`.
- Give `TableCellTime` dates from your data. Where the text must not depend on when it renders (an example, a test, a server render the browser hydrates), set `now` on the app's `ConfigProvider` and count sample dates back from that constant; never build them from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup.
- Drive loading through the `loading` prop (skeleton rows, `aria-busy`) and keep the `empty` slot for no-data copy — do not swap the table for a spinner.
- On a phone a console list keeps its grid and scrolls sideways (the default). Set `stackable` only for a short list read one record at a time on a narrow, phone-first surface (a marketing listing, a summary in a side panel), where a card per row reads better than a scroll; never on a resource index, a log or a list compared across columns.
- Type the rows, not the slot: pass a typed `data` (`ref<Domain[]>([])`, or a literal array) and destructure `#cell-name="{ row, value }"` — `row` is a `Domain` and `value` is `Domain['name']`. Keep a column's `id` equal to its `accessorKey` (or leave `id` out) so the typed `value` is the field the cell shows. Do not annotate the slot scope by hand or cast `row as Domain`; a wrong field (`row.nmae`) should be a type error.
- Place `TableSearch`, `TableFilter`, `CollectionPreferences`, `TableExportButton` and `TableRefreshButton` in the `toolbar` slot with no `v-model` wiring — they read the table from context. Import each from its own entry (`@aziontech/webkit/table-search`); they are not attached to the `table` compound.

## Don’t

- A small, static table or one whose cells need a layout the column model cannot express → compose it by hand with `table` (no engine in the bundle).
- People edit many cells of many records in place, spreadsheet-style → use `data-grid`.
- A short list of same-field rows added and removed inside a form (environment variables, headers) → use `attribute-editor`.
- A short titled preview of a longer listing on a marketing page → use `listing-table-section`.
- A feature-by-feature comparison of Azion with a competitor → use `competitor-comparison-section`.
- Rows of mixed content (media, title, description, actions) that do not share columns → use `item`.
- The same records as a grid of cards → use `card-list` (same collection, card layout).
- In a docs Markdown page or the site's page JSON. DataTable is app-only (decision RV-C2-1, rule `webkit-content-channels`): it drives app state (sorting, selection, paging, filters) through its engine, so it has no `DocMarkdown` tag and no page JSON entry. A docs page writes a Markdown pipe table; the site uses `listing-table-section`.

## Related

- `table` — the parts DataTable renders through, and the hand-composed table for small static content; its toolbar parts and cell presets go in DataTable's slots.
- `data-grid` — the editable, spreadsheet-like grid; use it when cells are edited in place.
- `pagination` — the page strip; `DataTablePagination` in the `footer` slot renders and wires it.
- `listing-table-section` — marketing section that composes `table` for a linked preview of a list.
- `empty-state` — the pattern behind the table's default `empty` slot; override the slot for resource-specific copy and actions.
- `item` — list rows without a column structure.
- `filter-menu` — Use FilterMenu when people filter by picking known values per field (status, region, owner) and see them as chips — the default console list filter; `TableFilter` hosts it by default.
- `property-filter` — Use PropertyFilter when people type queries with operators (Status = Active, Requests > 100) or free text they want to keep; `TableFilter type="property"` hosts it wired to the table (AND only).
- `collection-preferences` — Use CollectionPreferences for every 'how this list looks' setting: page size, visible and ordered columns, density, wrap; with no `columns` inside the toolbar it edits this table's columns.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxHeight` | `string` | `''` | false | Max height (CSS length). The viewport scrolls dynamically: horizontal scroll appears automatically when columns overflow the width; vertical scroll appears only when `maxHeight` is set smaller than the content (under the sticky header). |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Draw the outer card border around the table. Off by default (the table is typically framed by a surrounding surface); set `bordered` / `:bordered="…"` to draw the `var(--border-default)` outline. The internal row dividers are unaffected. |
| `columns` | `TableColumn[]` | `[]` | false | column definitions (`{ id?, accessorKey?, header?, label?, sortable?, grow?, principal?, frozen?, width?, minWidth?, align?, type?, resizable?, hideable?, narrow?, orderable? }`; `width` (px) sets a fixed pixel column (also needed when a frozen column precedes another frozen column on the same edge, so sticky offsets can be summed); **`minWidth`** (px) sets a **floor** instead: the table measures the column's own content — its header, including the sort affordance, and every rendered body cell — and pins the column to the larger of the two, as **one** width applied to the header and every body cell (a per-cell `min-width` would let each row size to its own content and drift the header away from the body). It is for a column whose content is a chip or a short token: a fixed `width` there is a bet in both directions — too generous and it reserves space the rest of the row needs, too tight and the chip inside it truncates. The measured width tracks the **rendered page**, so a column can change width when paging or sorting brings longer content into view; Until the first measurement (and while loading placeholders draw) the column holds its floor, so a loading table on a phone shows the same columns it shows once loaded. `width` wins when both are set, and a user resize wins over both. a `grow` column without `width` keeps a shared fixed basis so the header and body stay aligned and the cell never wraps. A column with no `grow` defaults to weight `2` for the **principal** column and `1` for the rest, so the columns fill the available space proportionally. The principal column is the one flagged `principal: true`, or — when none is flagged — the first non-action column. A `type: 'action'` column is automatically pinned to the trailing (right) edge — staying reachable while the rest scrolls horizontally — and is never resizable. **Every column is resizable by default**: its header carries a live mouse/touch drag-to-resize handle (native pointer events; the `@tanstack/vue-table` exception covers sorting/pagination/selection/visibility, not sizing); **`resizable: false`** opts a column out. On the first drag of any divider every flexible column freezes at its current rendered width; from then on dragging changes **only that column** and the table grows (horizontal scroll) — the others are untouched. The drag floor is the column's own content width (header label + visible body cells), so a column never shrinks past its content. Frozen and action columns never resize. When a drag that moved ends, the table emits `column-resize` with that column's id and new width; a click on the handle that does not move emits nothing. To keep the width, the app saves it and passes it back as the column's `width`; only the dragged columns get one, so the others stay flexible and the table still fills a wider screen. `useCollection` does this by default (its stored preferences). **`label`** names the column in `CollectionPreferences` when `header` is not a string; **`hideable: false`** lists the column locked in `CollectionPreferences`; **`orderable: true`** opts the column into `columnOrder`. **`narrow: false`** drops the column (its header, its cells and its loading placeholders) while the table's own box is narrower than `var(--container-sm)`, for a column whose value the principal cell already repeats there in a phone summary line; the column comes back in a wider box. |
| `rowKey` | `string` | `'id'` | false | Field used as the stable row id (for selection). |
| `sortable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Sorts every column on header click; a column's own `sortable` overrides. |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Adds a leading selection-checkbox column. |
| `rowSelectable` | `(row: TRow) => boolean` | `undefined` | false | decides per row whether it can be selected (`(row) => row.type === 'file'`). A row it rejects draws no checkbox, ignores row clicks and stays out of Select all. |
| `selectOnRowClick` | `boolean` | `false` | false | clicking a row toggles its selection (requires `selectable`); interactive cells still own their own click. |
| `manualSorting` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Server-side sorting: emit events, do not sort locally. |
| `manualFiltering` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Server-side filtering: emit events, do not filter locally. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | render skeleton rows in the body (aligned to the visible columns) and set `aria-busy`; `TableRefreshButton` disables/spins while true. Precedence: `loading` → skeleton, else rows, else `empty`. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | message of a failed load, shown in place of the rows in an `alert` region (an `EmptyState` with the error mark and `table.errorTitle`, the message as its description); the `error` slot replaces it. `loading` wins over it. Empty shows the rows. |
| `stackable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | opt in to stacked rows. When the table's own box is narrower than `--container-lg`, each row renders as label and value lines instead of the horizontally scrolling grid. Off by default: a console list scrolls sideways on a phone. |
| `wrapLines` | `boolean` | `false` | false | cell text wraps onto several lines instead of truncating. |
| `striped` | `boolean` | `false` | false | every other body row takes the raised surface. |
| `density` | `'comfortable' \| 'compact'` | `'comfortable'` | false | Density of the header and the body rows: `compact` shrinks their height and padding (the header through `Table.Header`'s `density`). A saved `CollectionPreferences` density therefore covers the whole table. |
| `virtual` | `boolean` | `false` | false | render only the rows in view, for thousands of rows. The viewport scrolls vertically within `maxHeight` (40rem when empty). Ignored in the stacked layout. |
| `reorderable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | a leading grip column lets people drag rows, or move the focused grip's row with Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home and End, into a new order. Emits `update:data` (bind `v-model:data`) and `reorder`; locked while a sort is applied. |
| `rowReorderable` | `(row: TRow) => boolean` | `undefined` | false | With `reorderable`: decides per row whether it can move (`(row) => !row.locked`). A rejected row keeps its place: its grip is disabled, and no row is dropped onto it or moved past it with the keys. |
| `getSubRows` | `(row: TRow) => TRow[] \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | tree rows. Returns a row's children (`(row) => row.children`); a row with children gets an expand toggle in the principal column, its children render under it indented one step (`--spacing-md`) per level, and the grid element takes `role="treegrid"`. Sorting and filtering keep each child under its parent; selection is per row (selecting a parent does not select its children). `reorderable` is ignored in tree mode. |
| `data` | `TRow[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:data`). |
| `sorting` | `SortingState` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:sorting`). |
| `selectedKeys` | `string[]` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:selectedKeys`). |
| `columnVisibility` | `VisibilityState` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:columnVisibility`). |
| `openKeys` | `string[]` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:openKeys`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `row-click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, row: TRow)` | Fires when a rendered row is clicked, or when `Enter` is pressed on a focused row (keyboard rows, below). `event` is the click or the key press; `row` is the record. |
| `row-remove` | `(event: KeyboardEvent, row: TRow)` | `Delete` (or `Backspace`, which a Mac keyboard's delete key sends) was pressed on a focused row. The table removes nothing: the app asks first (a `ConfirmDialog`) and then drops the record from `data`. |
| `filter-apply` | `(event: Event, filters: TableAppliedFilter[])` | `TableFilter` committed a pick or a token — the explicit re-query signal for `manualFiltering`. |
| `filter-remove` | `(event: Event, filter: TableAppliedFilter)` | One applied filter was removed (a `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` chip). |
| `refresh` | `(event: Event)` | Refresh requested; the app refetches. `event` is the click of `TableRefreshButton`, or `new Event('refresh')` when `reload()` is called. |
| `export` | `(event: Event, rows: TRow[])` | Export requested with the resolved rows; `event` is the click of `TableExportButton`, or `new Event('export')` when `exportCsv()` is called; a consumer may handle it server-side (otherwise the built-in CSV util downloads). |
| `reorder` | `(event: KeyboardEvent \| PointerEvent, payload: { from: number; to: number; row: TRow })` | `reorderable`: a row moved from index `from` to index `to` of `data`. |
| `column-resize` | `(event: MouseEvent \| TouchEvent, column: { id: string; width: number })` | A drag of a column's resize handle ended after moving; `column` is the column id and its new width in px. The table keeps the width for the session; to keep it across reloads save it and pass it back as the column's `width` (`useCollection` does, under `preferences.storageKey`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `caption` | — | caption content (wrapped in TableCaption), fixed above the scroll viewport. |
| `title` | — | Title text shown at the start of the toolbar band, fixed above the scroll viewport. |
| `toolbar` | { table, selectedRows, selectedCount, clearSelection, loading } | Action band (search, filter, refresh, export, column preferences) above the scroll viewport, end-aligned beside the title. `table` is the TanStack instance; `selectedRows` / `selectedCount` / `clearSelection` expose the selection for bulk-action toolbars, and `loading` mirrors the prop. |
| `filters` | { table, selectedRows, selectedCount, clearSelection, loading } | Active-filter chips row below the toolbar; same scope as `toolbar`. |
| `empty` | — | shown when there are no rows. Defaults to an empty-state block (illustration + title + description) following Figma; override the slot for custom copy/actions. |
| `error` | { message: string } | shown in place of the rows while `error` is set; `message` is the `error` prop. Defaults to a small `EmptyState` with the error mark, `table.errorTitle` and the message. |
| `load-more` | — | content after the last row that scrolls with the rows, inside the viewport: `DataTableLoadMore`. |
| `footer` | — | band below the scroll viewport, outside `role="table"`: `DataTablePagination`. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:data` | `TRow[]` | `[]` | `update:data` | Row records (`defineModel`, default `[]`). One-way `:data` is the common case; `reorderable` writes the records in their new order back, so bind `v-model:data` to keep the order. |
| `v-model:sorting` | `SortingState` | `undefined` | `update:sorting` | TanStack `SortingState` (`defineModel`). Uncontrolled it starts unsorted; `setSnapshot()` writes it too. |
| `v-model:selected-keys` | `string[]` | `undefined` | `update:selectedKeys` | Keys of the selected rows, read from `rowKey` (`defineModel`), the same shape as DataGrid, Tree and CardList. |
| `v-model:column-visibility` | `VisibilityState` | `undefined` | `update:columnVisibility` | TanStack `VisibilityState` (`defineModel`). |
| `v-model:open-keys` | `string[]` | `undefined` | `update:openKeys` | Tree rows: keys of the open rows (`defineModel`), the same shape as Tree and SidebarMenu. Uncontrolled it starts collapsed; written after a toggle by pointer or keyboard. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `selected`
- Data states: `loading` (skeleton rows, `aria-busy`; as many rows as are already shown, or with no rows yet the page size capped at 10, so a first load is no taller than a typical page; `DataTablePagination` states no count it does not know, see Sub-components), `error` (the `error` prop set: rows replaced by the `error` slot in an `alert` region, `__error`), `empty` (no rows: the `empty` slot, `__empty`). Precedence: loading, then error, then empty.
- The viewport is always a scroll container (`overflow: auto`): horizontal scroll is automatic when columns overflow; vertical scroll engages only when `maxHeight` constrains the content.
- `data-frozen` on TableHeader (`true`), TableHeadCell / TableCell (`start` | `end`), and TableRow (`true`). A frozen head/body cell renders a CSS-only fade (gradient pseudo-element) just outside its inner edge that dissolves the horizontally scrolling content into the row background (`from-transparent` → `var(--table-row-bg)`, the row-published color, so it matches the row on hover/selected) — `frozen=start` fades on the right, `frozen=end` on the left. The fade tints nothing; it only masks the content sliding under the pinned column.
- Scroll cue: the scroll viewport sits in a `__scroll` frame that sets `data-overflow-start` / `data-overflow-end` from the scroll position (re-measured on scroll and on resize). While content is hidden past an inline edge, an `aria-hidden` gradient as wide as the hidden distance (at most 24 px, none when 4 px or less, so it never sits over text that is otherwise in view) (`__fade-start` / `__fade-end`, `from-transparent` to `var(--bg-surface)`, pointer events off) covers that edge of the viewport, so a phone shows that columns continue; it follows the inline direction under `dir="rtl"`, has no motion, and keeps its gradient under forced colors (fading to `Canvas`). A frozen column on that edge draws its own fade and paints over the cue, which sits below frozen cells and the sticky header (`z-5`).
- `data-state` on TableRow: `selected` | `unselected`; `data-selected` mirrors the `selected` prop; `aria-selected` set when selected.
- `data-type` on TableHeadCell (`default` | `checkbox` | `action` | `slot`) and TableCell (`default` | `checkbox` | `action`).
- `data-align` on head/body cells: `start` | `center` | `end`.
- `data-grow` on head/body cells: `1` | `2` | `3` (flex weight).
- `data-sortable` and `data-sort` (`none` | `ascending` | `descending`) on TableHeadCell; `aria-sort` mirrors `data-sort`.
- `data-sort` (`none` | `ascending` | `descending`) on TableSortButton.
- `data-clickable` on TableCell mirrors the `clickable` prop.
- Stacked rows (opt-in `stackable`): by default the grid scrolls sideways at every width, as the console does on a phone. With `stackable`, the table measures its own box; below `--container-lg` (552 px) it sets `data-stacked` and each body row stacks its cells. Stacked rows draw no frame of their own: they keep the row rule between them and sit flush in the table, so a stacked table inside a card or a bordered table shows one frame, never a card inside a card (`styling.md`, never double a line). The checkbox, the principal column and the action column share the first line; every other column takes its own line as a label (the column `label` or `header`, `aria-hidden`) and its value. The header row stays in the DOM visually hidden, so screen readers keep the column headers; frozen offsets and fades are dropped. A hand-composed table never stacks.
- Stacked select-all (`selectable`): in the stacked layout the header checkbox is not rendered; a visible, labelled **Select all rows** checkbox sits above the stacked rows (`__stacked-select-all`) and toggles the page, with the same indeterminate state.
- Per-row selectability (`rowSelectable`): a row the function rejects renders an empty selection cell, ignores `selectOnRowClick` and is skipped by Select all; the header checkbox reads `all` when every selectable row is selected.
- Density and wrapping: `data-density="compact"` on the root shrinks the header (through `Table.Header`'s `density`) and the body cells (`min-h-9`, `--spacing-2xs` block padding); `data-wrap` lets cell text (and any `.truncate` inside a cell) wrap. `striped` shades odd body rows with `var(--bg-surface-raised)` (selected and hover still win).
- Virtual rows (`virtual`): only the rows in view plus 8 above and below render; the slice starts on an even row so stripes stay put; rows of different heights (`wrapLines` with long text) are measured as they render and the rows in view do not shift while scrolling; the root sets `aria-rowcount` and each row `aria-rowindex`. Skeleton and stacked layouts render every row.
- Long lists (more than 200 rows, not `virtual`): the first 50 rows render, a spacer (`__lazy-rows`, `aria-hidden`) stands in for the rest and more rows mount as it nears the viewport, until every row is in the DOM; while rows are still missing the root sets `aria-rowcount` and each row `aria-rowindex`. When `data`, the sort or a filter changes, the mounted rows drop back to the ones within reach of the viewport (at least 50), so a sort after scrolling to the end and back does not patch every row.
- Infinite loading: `DataTableLoadMore` in the `load-more` slot (see Sub-components).
- Live tail (`TableLiveButton` `v-model`): turning it on scrolls the viewport to the top and remembers the first row; once newer rows arrive above it, that row carries `data-live-boundary` and draws a 2 px success-coloured line on its top edge. While live and scrolled to the top, new rows keep the viewport at the newest row; scrolled down, the rows in view stay still. Turning it off clears the boundary.
- Responsive toolbar: the root is the `@container/table`; the toolbar wraps, and below `@md` of the table the `toolbar` slot moves under the title and starts at the start edge. `Table.Toolbar` wraps its controls.
- Hover-free devices: a sortable header shows its sort affordance where the pointer cannot hover (`@media (hover: none)`).
- Reorderable rows (`reorderable`): a 40 px leading column holds a grip `IconButton` per row (`data-reorder-handle`), frozen at the start edge when other columns are; the row being dragged sets `data-dragging` (dashed accent outline, 60% opacity) and the row under the pointer `data-drop="before" | "after"` (a 2 px accent line on that edge). While a sort is applied every grip is disabled and its description says to clear the sort.
- Tree rows (`getSubRows`): the grid element is `role="treegrid"` and sets `data-tree`. Each body row carries `aria-level` (1-based depth), `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset` among its siblings, `aria-expanded` when it has children, and `data-depth`; the principal cell starts with one `aria-hidden` gutter (`data-tree-gutter`) `calc(var(--spacing-md) * depth + var(--size-7))` wide, which holds the 28 px chevron toggle (`__expand-toggle`, `az-chevron-right` mirrored in RTL, `az-chevron-down` when open) at its end on rows with children, so the content of every row at one depth starts on one column and each level shifts it by exactly one step. Rows use a roving tab stop (one row has `tabindex="0"`, the rest `-1`) and draw an inset `var(--ring-color)` outline on `focus-visible`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the sort button and any interactive cell content.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the sort button of each sortable column (one tab stop per column, as in the APG sortable table: the header cell itself is not focusable and carries `aria-sort`) and interactive cell content; `Enter`/`Space` on the sort button toggles the sort; row click is mouse/touch (no keyboard trap). The principal column still carries a real link or button (`TableCellLink`, or the `cell-<id>` slot with an anchor, as the Default example does), which keyboard and screen-reader users reach with `Tab` (WCAG 2.1.1).
- Keyboard rows (the console keyboard standard, `rules/webkit-keyboard.md`): when the table has a `row-click` or a `row-remove` listener (or tree rows), body rows become one roving tab stop (one row `tabindex="0"`, the rest `-1`, the last focused row kept as the stop) with the same inset ring as tree rows. `Arrow Down` / `Arrow Up` move between rows, `Home` / `End` go to the first / last row, `Enter` emits `row-click` with the key press, `Space` toggles the row's selection when `selectable` allows it, and `Delete` / `Backspace` emits `row-remove` (never with `⌘`, `Ctrl`, `Alt` or `Shift` held). Keys pressed on a control inside the row (a checkbox, the row menu) belong to that control. When the row that held focus leaves `data` and focus fell to the page (the delete was confirmed in a dialog that closed, or the row itself was focused), focus moves to the row now at its index, else the previous row, else the table element (`tabindex="-1"`, ring on `focus-visible`); it waits while a modal layer is open, and leaves focus alone when the person moved it elsewhere. Without those listeners body rows are not focusable. Tests: `data-table.test.ts` › keyboard rows.
- ARIA: `role="table"` sits on the grid element inside the scroll viewport (testid `<testid>__table`), not on the root: the root also holds the toolbar, applied filters, the focusable scroll viewport, the stacked select-all, the empty state and the pagination, and any of those inside a `table` is an unallowed child (`aria-required-children`). Every `aria-*` attribute passed to `DataTable` (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`…) is forwarded to that element, as are `aria-busy` (loading) and `aria-rowcount` (windowed); every other attribute stays on the root. The pagination is a plain region under the viewport (`DataTablePagination`, a `TableFooter`), not a `rowgroup`, and the `caption` slot renders as the table's first child. `table-caption` is a plain element (no `role`) that names the table through `aria-labelledby` unless the consumer names it with `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`. `table-header`/`table-body` `role="rowgroup"`; `table-footer` has no role (it hosts pagination or an action, not rows); `table-row` `role="row"`; `table-head-cell` `role="columnheader"` with `aria-sort` when sortable; `table-cell` `role="cell"`; selected rows set `aria-selected`.
- Virtual rows keep their position for assistive technology: `aria-rowcount` on the `role="table"` element (rows + header) and `aria-rowindex` on each rendered row.
- Reorderable rows: each grip is a button named `Reorder <row name>, position <n> of <total>` and described by a visually hidden hint (`Drag, or press Arrow Up or Arrow Down to move.`, or the lock reason). Arrow Up / Arrow Down / Home / End move the row and keep focus on its grip; `Esc` cancels a drag. A polite `role="status"` region announces `Moved <name> to position <n> of <total>.` (keyboard) or `Dropped …` (pointer). Dragging is never the only way to reorder (WCAG 2.5.7).
- Tree rows follow the APG treegrid row-focus pattern: `Tab` enters the grid on one row (the last one focused, else the first); `Arrow Down` / `Arrow Up` move between visible rows; `Home` / `End` go to the first / last row; `Arrow Right` (inline end, mirrored in RTL) opens a closed row or moves to the first child of an open one; `Arrow Left` closes an open row or moves to the parent; `Enter` toggles the row; `Space` toggles its selection when `selectable` allows it. Interactive content inside the row (checkbox, menus) stays reachable with `Tab`. The pointer toggle is `aria-hidden` (the row's `aria-expanded` is the accessible state), and when a row collapses while one of its descendants holds focus, focus moves to that row.
- Stacked layout: the select-all is a visible checkbox with a `<label>`, not a screen-reader-only header cell (WCAG 2.5.3, label in name).
- Row checkboxes are named after the row: `table.selectRow` (`Select row {row}`) filled with the principal column's value, else the row key.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including muted header text.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the sort button and row action controls.

# Filter Menu

> The list filter of a console list: a Filter button that carries the number of applied filters and opens a drill-in menu. The first level lists the fields, each with a summary of what is applied to it; picking a field slides to its values (check rows for a `multiple` field, radio rows for a `single` one, an optional avatar per value, a search box and a no-match line), and a `date` field offers periods plus a custom whole-day range on a `DateRangePicker` (`range-selector-mode="absolute-only"`, no times, no zone selector). Back returns to the fields, Clear removes the field's filter, and the panel's height follows each level. `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` shows the applied fields as chips under the controls row: the field label in muted ink, an avatar stack, the first value and `+N`; activating a chip reopens the menu at that field, removing it clears the field. The value is a `Record<fieldId, values[]>` bound with `v-model`; the menu never filters anything itself. Inside a DataTable, `TableFilter type="menu"` renders it and `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` with no `fields` renders its chips, both mapped onto the table's `filters` model. It differs from `property-filter` (one text field that builds `property operator value` tokens and combines them with operators and and/or): this menu offers only the values a field has, one click each, which is what most lists need.

- Import: `import FilterMenuRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/filter-menu-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import FilterMenu from '@aziontech/webkit/filter-menu'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use FilterMenu when people filter by picking known values per field (status, region, owner) and see them as chips — the default console list filter.
- A resource list or table filtered by a few closed-set fields (status, owner, region, type) and a modification date.
- A catalog or listing page (marketplace, templates, posts) that narrows by category, author or date, outside a table.
- Filters people pick rather than type, where each field has a short list of values.

## Do

- Put the Filter button first in the controls row, before the search field, and `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` on its own row below the controls.
- Pass the same `fields` array and the same `v-model` to the menu and to its chips: chips reopen the menu that shares their `fields`.
- Give people-like values an `avatar` (an image URL, or `''` for initials) so the chip shows who is filtered.
- Keep each field to the values that exist in the data; a field with no values is noise.
- Filter the data in the page (or on the server) from the model; read a date preset value (`24h`, `7d`, `30d`, `3m`) as a window ending now and a range value as its `start` and `end`.

## Don’t

- Filters typed as text, with operators or and/or logic, or a query people keep as text → use `property-filter`. FilterMenu is for faceted picks from known values; PropertyFilter is for expression search.
- A table that needs comparisons on numbers or text conditions → use `property-filter` (`TableFilter type="property"` inside a DataTable).
- Two to four fixed choices always on screen → use `toggle-group` or selectable `chip`s.
- A single search over names → use `input`, or `table-search` inside a table.

## Related

- `data-table` — `TableFilter type="menu"` and `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` (no `fields`) render this menu and its chips over the table's `filters` model.
- `property-filter` — the token-based filter field for typed queries.
- `popover` — the overlay the menu opens in.
- `date-range-picker` — the range picker the custom date period uses.
- `chip` — each applied filter in `FilterMenu.ChipGroup`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | `FilterMenuField[]` | `[]` | false | Fields the menu lists, in order, each with its type and values. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the trigger button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Filter`). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token of the trigger button. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger: the menu does not open. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `modelValue` | `FilterMenuModel` | `—` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/filter-menu-chip-group`

## Sub-components

The root ships a compound API: `index.ts` attaches `Chips` to the root and re-exports the types. The
menu and its chips are siblings in the page (the controls row and the row below it), so they share
no provider: chips and a menu that receive the **same `fields` array** are linked through a
per-array channel (`composables/use-filter-menu-channel.ts`, module scope, keyed by the raw array),
so activating a chip opens that menu at the chip's field with no wiring. The link is the array's
identity: an inline `:fields="[...]"` literal or a computed that rebuilds the array gives the menu
and the chips two arrays, so a chip that finds no listening menu warns once per activation in the
console (`FilterMenu.ChipGroup: no FilterMenu has these fields.`). When the arrays differ
on purpose, the consumer calls the root's exposed `open(fieldId)`. **Inside a DataTable**, chips
with no `fields` read the table context instead: their fields come from the table's
`filterFields`, their value from its `filters` model, removing a chip removes that field's filter
through the table (`filter-remove`), and activating one reopens `TableFilter type="menu"` at the
field. That is the one applied-filters row of a table.

- `filter-menu-chip-group/filter-menu-chip-group.vue` — One filled, clickable, removable `Chip` per applied field, in `fields` order, inside a `role="group"` named `Applied filters`.
  - Props: `fields?: FilterMenuField[]` (default `[]` — the same array the menu receives; empty inside a DataTable reads the table's filter fields and filters).
  - v-model: `Record<string, FilterMenuValue[]>` (default `{}`); removing a chip deletes the field's key.
  - Events: `edit: [event: MouseEvent | KeyboardEvent, field: FilterMenuField]` (a chip was activated; the linked menu opens at the field), `remove: [event: MouseEvent, field: FilterMenuField]` (a chip's remove button was pressed; the model loses the field).
  - Slots: none.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `filter-menu-chip-group`; each chip `<testid>__chip-<fieldId>`.

Resulting layout:

```
packages/webkit/src/components/data/filter-menu/
├── filter-menu.vue
├── filter-menu.test.ts
├── index.ts
├── types.ts                         (FilterMenuField, FilterMenuOption, FilterMenuValue, FilterMenuRange, FilterMenuModel)
├── summarize.ts                     (field summaries shared by the menu rows and the chips)
├── composables/
│   ├── use-filter-menu-channel.ts   (open requests from chips to the menu sharing their fields)
│   ├── use-filter-menu-labels.ts    (period options, range and summary text from the locale)
│   └── use-animated-height.ts       (height transition between levels; cleans up on scope dispose)
└── filter-menu-chip-group/
    └── filter-menu-chip-group.vue
```

Exports:

```jsonc
"./filter-menu": "./src/components/data/filter-menu/index.ts",
"./filter-menu-root": "./src/components/data/filter-menu/filter-menu.vue",
"./filter-menu-chip-group": "./src/components/data/filter-menu/filter-menu-chip-group/filter-menu-chip-group.vue"
```

Exported types (from `index.ts`):

- `FilterMenuOption = { value: string | number; label: string; avatar?: string }` — `avatar` present (an image URL, or `''` for initials from `label`) draws an `Avatar` on the row and in the chip.
- `FilterMenuField = { id: string; label: string; type?: 'multiple' | 'single' | 'date'; options?: FilterMenuOption[] }` — `type` defaults to `multiple`.
- `FilterMenuRange = { start: Date | null; end: Date | null }` — a custom date range.
- `FilterMenuValue = string | number | FilterMenuRange`.
- `FilterMenuModel = Record<string, FilterMenuValue[]>` — a field with no key (or an empty array) is not applied.

Imperative API (root, `defineExpose`): `open(fieldId?: string, returnFocus?: HTMLElement | null)` — opens the menu, at the given field's values when `fieldId` names a field, and returns focus to `returnFocus` (when still in the document) instead of the trigger when it closes.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `FilterMenuModel` | `{}` | `update:modelValue` | Applied values per field id. Every pick emits a new object; clearing a field (Clear, or a chip's remove) deletes its key. |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Whether the menu is open, via `defineModel('open')`: the trigger, outside click, `Esc`, a chip and the exposed `open()` update it. Unbound, the menu keeps it itself and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: trigger `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`; rows `hover`, `focus-visible`, checked (a check glyph at the end edge).
- `data-state` on the root and the trigger: `open` | `closed` (from `Popover`).
- `data-level` on the panel's level: `fields`, `values:<fieldId>`, `custom:<fieldId>`.
- `data-applied` on a field row when the field has values.
- Count: the trigger shows a small primary `Badge` with the number of applied fields and drops it at 0.
- Empty: a level with no rows matching the search shows `No match for “<query>”.`; a menu with no `fields` shows the same line for the empty query.
- `disabled`: the trigger is disabled (`data-disabled` from `Popover`) and the menu does not open.
- Long value lists: a level renders at most 100 matching values and then a muted line, `<n> more values. Type to narrow the list.` (`__more-values`); the search narrows the rest.
- `loading`, `error`, `readonly`, `invalid`: not states of this component — the page owns the data.

## Accessibility

- Pattern: a disclosure button that opens a non-modal dialog (`Popover`, named by a visually hidden `Popover.Title` with the trigger label). Fields are buttons; a `multiple` field's values are `role="checkbox"` buttons with `aria-checked` inside a `role="group"` named by the field; a `single` or `date` field's values are `role="radio"` buttons with `aria-checked` inside a `role="radiogroup"`. The Custom range row is a plain button.
- Trigger name: the label, plus the count when filters apply (`Filter, 2 applied`); the badge is `aria-hidden`. Field rows read `<field> <summary>`.
- Keyboard map: `Enter` / `Space` on the trigger toggles the panel; `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` move between the rows of the current level and wrap; `Enter` / `Space` on a field row opens its values, on a value row toggles it; focus moves to the first row of every new level; `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` cycle the search box, rows, Back and Clear inside the panel (Popover's trap); `Escape` closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger, or to the chip that opened it while that chip still exists. While the custom range calendar is open, `Escape` closes the calendar first. On a chip, `Enter` / `Space` reopen the menu at its field and the remove button clears it.
- Visible focus: rows and Back use `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`; the trigger, search box, chips and calendar carry their own rings.
- Contrast: row text `--text-default` and muted summaries `--text-muted` on the raised surface meet 4.5:1; the check glyph and chevrons are text-colored (3:1 or more).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition above.
- Touch target: rows are full-width and at least 32 px tall; on `pointer: coarse` they grow to 44 px (`pointer-coarse:min-h-11`).

# Flow Diagram

> The one in-product diagram (owner decision RV-Y1, 2026-11-18): it kept the old FlowDiagram parts and replaced TopologyDiagram in the 6.0 clean break. A naked root lays steps out and draws the connectors. **Data mode** (`nodes` + `edges`): edges set the columns and each node renders the richest card its data allows. **Composed mode**: hand-written parts in the default slot. `orientation="responsive"` lays the steps in a row only when the whole row fits its container, and stacks them into a rail otherwise.

- Import: `import FlowDiagramRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import FlowDiagram from '@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A request path or pipeline: steps in order joined by connectors.
- A deployment or service topology with status, metrics, details and bind controls.

## Do

- Prefer data mode; compose by hand only for markup the card cannot express.
- Join adjacent columns; an edge that skips a column can cross it.
- Put timing or failure on the edge (`label`, `severity`) when the hop failed, on the node when the resource did.
- Use `orientation="horizontal"` for fixed-size scenes and mock-ups.
- Set `:show-ports="false"` on a diagram a reader only views, such as a request path on an error page, so it draws no editor-style port squares.
- A one-resource slot puts `flow-diagram-bind` in the `actions` slot.

## Don’t

- A marketing architecture drawing from the official library → use `diagram`.
- A numbered set of instructions → use `doc-steps`.

## Related

- `diagram` — the marketing figure (closed drawing library).
- `status-indicator` — the status dot and text in a node header.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `FlowDiagramNodeData[]` | `[]` | false | Nodes of a data-driven diagram; each renders as a full card. Leave empty to compose the parts by hand. |
| `edges` | `FlowDiagramEdgeData[]` | `[]` | false | Connectors between nodes by id; they also decide the columns. Empty joins each step to the next. |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical' \| 'responsive'` | `'responsive'` | false | Lays the steps out in a row, in a column, or in a row that stacks when its container is narrow. |
| `align` | `'start' \| 'center'` | `'start'` | false | Vertical alignment of the steps in a row. |
| `uniform` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Gives every step the width and height of the largest one. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows placeholder steps while the diagram loads. |
| `showPorts` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draws the port squares where connectors meet the steps; turn off for a diagram a reader only views. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the diagram. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Diagram`). |
| `openKeys` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:openKeys`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Composed mode: nodes and groups, in flow order. |
| `actions` | { node: FlowDiagramNodeData } | Data mode: controls at the end of a node's title row. |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the `EmptyState` shown when there are no nodes. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram-node`
- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram-anchor`
- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram-footer`
- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram-bind`

## Sub-components

- `flow-diagram-node` — one step: a label box, a card when it holds a `Title`, or `unstyled`.
- `flow-diagram-group` — parallel nodes stacked in one step (was `Parallel` and a topology level).
- `flow-diagram-anchor` — where a connector touches.
- `flow-diagram-header` — props `icon`, `eyebrow`, `status`, `severity`.
- `flow-diagram-title` — prop `href`; `actions` slot.
- `flow-diagram-description`, `flow-diagram-footer`, `flow-diagram-item` (prop `label`).
- `flow-diagram-bind` — companion (not attached): bind with Apply and Cancel.

## v-model

- **`v-model:openKeys`** — `string[]`, default `[]`. Ids of the data-mode nodes whose details are open.

## States

- List: `data-orientation`, `data-direction` (`row` or `column`, the layout in use), `data-align`, `data-uniform`, `data-labelled` (wider gap for edge labels), `data-stacked` (rail drawn, ports hidden), `data-show-ports` (present while `showPorts` is on; without it no port is drawn).
- Node: `data-disabled`, `data-dashed`, `data-terminal`, `data-node-key`, `data-entry` / `data-exit` (ports show only where a connector attaches).
- Title: every row is one small control high (`min-h-7`) with `--spacing-sm` of bottom padding, so a button in the `actions` slot sits as far from the divider below as the header text sits from the border above, and cards with and without controls keep the same anchor height (their connectors stay level).
- Data card: `data-state="open|closed"`; an unbound bindable node is dashed with `Not bound`; a pending bind dashes it too.
- Loading: `aria-busy`, skeleton cards, one `role="status"` line. Empty: `EmptyState` unless the `empty` slot replaces it.
- Edge `severity` colours the connector (`--<severity>-mark`); default `--accent`.
- Scroll area (`__viewport`): `data-overflow-start` / `data-overflow-end` while content lies past that inline edge; it fades that edge and takes `tabindex="0"`, as it does whenever its content is taller than it.

- Its root carries `data-plain-ground`: it is content that must sit on a plain ground, so a `Texture` beside it hides itself, and the texture-backdrop check blocks placing it on a textured band (a texture is a backdrop for text only, RV-T2-1).

## Accessibility

- Root `role="group"` named by `ariaLabel`; steps are a `list`, a group a nested list with a hidden label.
- Connectors, ports and edge labels are `aria-hidden`; data mode adds a hidden `Connections` list (`{from} to {to}, {label}`).
- `Tab` reaches links, the Details toggle (`aria-expanded`, closed details `inert`), copy and bind controls; the scroll area is focusable only when it overflows.
- Status is a dot plus text; the dashes stop after six runs; `motion-reduce:animate-none`; focus ring `--ring-color`.

<!-- components/pagination.md -->

# Pagination

> Pagination controls for tables and lists, pixel-perfect to Figma, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): a three-region landmark — page-info text, navigation buttons (Previous / page numbers / overflow / Next), and a rows-per-page selector — wired by hand through slots, with the consumer owning the current page, total, and page-size state. **Data-driven mode**: pass `total` (and optionally `page` / `pageSize`) and the Pagination renders its own info text, Previous / windowed page numbers / overflow ellipsis / Next, and the rows-per-page selector, emitting `update:page` / `update:pageSize` so the consumer can bind state via `v-model`. This component owns markup, tokens, and a11y; the data engine is a small internal page-window calculation — **no external pagination library**. Pairs with the `Table` component.

- Import: `import PaginationRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Pagination to page through the rows of a table or list; alternative versions of one AI response use ResponseBranches.
- A list or table outside `table`'s own footer needs page navigation and a rows-per-page selector.
- You know the item count — pass `total` and bind `v-model:page` / `v-model:page-size`; the component renders the info text, the windowed page numbers and the selector.
- The page strip needs custom content (a different info line, extra controls) — compose `Pagination.Description`, `Pagination.Button` and `Pagination.PageSize` through the slots.

## Do

- Prefer data-driven mode (`total` set); in composition mode the root emits nothing and you own every button's `active` / `disabled` state and every click.
- `page` is 1-based. Changing the page size through the selector emits `update:pageSize` and resets the page to `1`.
- Keep `page-size-options` aligned with what your data source accepts; the default is `[10, 25, 50, 100]`.
- Tune `sibling-count` (default `1`) instead of hiding buttons — it controls how many numbers sit on each side of the current page before the overflow ellipsis.
- Set `aria-label` when a page carries more than one pagination, so each navigation landmark has a distinct name.

## Don’t

- The rows live in a data-driven `table` → set `paginated` on the table; it renders this pagination in its footer and wires it for you.
- It is the previous / next pair at the end of a documentation page → use `doc-previous-next`.
- The content loads more as the reader scrolls or clicks "Load more" → use a `button` at the end of the list.

## Related

- `table` — renders a wired pagination in its footer when `paginated` is set.
- `doc-previous-next` — previous / next links between documentation pages, not numbered pages of a list.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `total` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Total item count. When set, the Pagination runs in data-driven mode and renders its own controls. |
| `pageSizeOptions` | `number[]` | `[10, 25, 50, 100]` | false | Page-size options offered in the rows-per-page selector. |
| `siblingCount` | `number` | `1` | false | Page numbers shown on each side of the current page before collapsing into an overflow ellipsis. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the navigation landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Pagination`). |
| `page` | `number` | `1` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:page`). |
| `pageSize` | `number` | `10` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:pageSize`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `info` | — | Left region: page-info text (typically PaginatorInfo). In data-driven mode, overrides the default "Showing X to Y of Z entries" text. |
| `default` | — | Center region: pagination navigation buttons (composition mode only — ignored in data-driven mode, where the buttons are rendered internally). |
| `controls` | — | Right region: rows-per-page selector (PaginatorPageSize). In data-driven mode, overrides the internally-rendered selector. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button`
- `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-page-size`

## Sub-components

- `pagination-button/pagination-button.vue` — one segment of the numbers strip, 28px tall with a 28px minimum width and no horizontal padding; it carries no radius of its own except the outer corners at the two ends of…
- `pagination-description/pagination-description.vue` — muted page-info text container (default slot), `.text-body-xs` / `var(--text-muted)`.
- `pagination-page-size/pagination-page-size.vue` — rows-per-page selector (native `<select>`), 64×28 (same height as the numbers strip), `var(--shape-control)` radius, `var(--bg-canvas)` frame over a `var(--bg-surface)…

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:page` | `number` | `1` | `update:page` | Current page, 1-based (data-driven mode), via `defineModel('page')`. Previous / Next / a page number / Arrow keys change it. Unbound, the Pagination keeps the page itself (uncontrolled), so it still moves. |
| `v-model:page-size` | `number` | `10` | `update:pageSize` | Rows per page (data-driven mode), via `defineModel('pageSize')`. Changing it through the selector also resets the page to `1`. Unbound, the Pagination keeps the size itself. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `active`, `focus-visible`, current page (`active` prop), `disabled`
- The page buttons render as one **segmented strip**: a single container carrying the `var(--border-default)` border and the `var(--shape-control)` radius, with the buttons butted against each other at zero gap. Only the two end buttons round their outer corners.
- `data-type` on PaginationButton: `previous` | `next` | `number` | `more`. `number` and `more` carry `var(--bg-surface)`; `previous` and `next` have no surface of their own.
- `hover` and `active` are mutually exclusive: pressing a button drops the hover layer and shows the `var(--bg-active)` layer alone, so the pressed surface reads one step below hover.
- `data-active` on PaginationButton mirrors the current-page `active` prop; `aria-current="page"` set when active.
- `data-disabled` on PaginationButton mirrors the `disabled` prop; `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled` set.
- Data-driven mode: `Previous` is disabled on the first page, `Next` on the last; the current page button is `active` (`aria-current="page"`); the overflow ellipsis (`more`) is non-interactive: an `aria-hidden` `span`, out of the tab order, that emits nothing.
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/pagination`. The page list stays whole at every width (`siblingCount` already caps it at seven slots, e.g. `1 2 3 4 5 … 60`), so a phone footer reads the same numbered strip as a desktop one, as in the design sample; when the box is too narrow for the info text and the controls on one line, the strip and the page-size control wrap together under the info text, aligned to the end.
- Touch: the buttons and the page-size select are drawn at 28 px on every pointer. On a coarse pointer (`pointer-coarse:`) each button carries an invisible, `aria-hidden` hit area that extends it to 44 px tall (vertical only: the buttons are butted, so the width stays the drawn 28 px), and the select itself grows to 44 px tall inside its 28 px frame, which draws the border, surface and focus ring; the select's text steps up to 16 px (`text-body-md`) so iOS Safari does not zoom the page when it takes focus.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on every pagination button.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves across buttons and the rows-per-page selector; `Enter`/`Space` activates a button; disabled buttons and the overflow ellipsis are skipped. In data-driven mode, `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` inside the button group go to the next/previous page, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`useDirection`).
- ARIA: root `<nav>` with `aria-label` (the `ariaLabel` prop); current-page button sets `aria-current="page"`; in data-driven mode each number button is named from the locale catalog (`pagination.page`, "Page 3") instead of the bare digit; disabled buttons set the `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled`; icon glyphs and the overflow ellipsis are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target: each button is drawn 28×28 (above the 24×24 minimum of WCAG 2.5.8) so the strip stays compact in a table footer; on a coarse pointer its hit area grows to 28×44 invisibly and the page-size select's to its full width × 44. The width cannot grow because the buttons are butted with no gap; growing the drawn size instead was rejected because it turned the phone footer into an oversized strip that no longer matched the design sample.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'
</script>

<template>
  <Pagination>
    <template #info>
      <Pagination.Description>Showing 1 to 10 of 87 entries</Pagination.Description>
    </template>

    <Pagination.Button
      type="previous"
      aria-label="Previous page"
      disabled
    />
    <Pagination.Button
      type="number"
      active
      aria-label="Page 1"
      >1</Pagination.Button
    >
    <Pagination.Button
      type="number"
      aria-label="Page 2"
      >2</Pagination.Button
    >
    <Pagination.Button
      type="number"
      aria-label="Page 3"
      >3</Pagination.Button
    >
    <Pagination.Button type="more" />
    <Pagination.Button
      type="number"
      aria-label="Page 9"
      >9</Pagination.Button
    >
    <Pagination.Button
      type="next"
      aria-label="Next page"
    />

    <template #controls>
      <Pagination.PageSize
        :model-value="10"
        :options="[10, 25, 50, 100]"
      />
    </template>
  </Pagination>
```

<!-- components/pagination-button.md -->

# Pagination Button

> PaginationButton is one segment of the pagination's numbers strip: a 28px-tall native `button` that renders a page number or a Previous / Next chevron, or — for `type="more"` — an inert, decorative overflow ellipsis (`span`, `aria-hidden`), chosen by `type`. It is the part `pagination` renders in data-driven mode and the one consumers compose by hand in composition mode, where it is reached as `Pagination.Button` (or imported standalone from `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button`). It owns the segment's surface, current-page (`active`) and `disabled` treatment, but not the strip's frame, border or the page state, which belong to the `pagination` root and the consumer.

- Import: `import PaginationButton from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Compose a custom page strip inside `pagination`'s default slot (composition mode), one button per Previous, page number, overflow and Next.
- Render the current page of a hand-wired pagination with `active`, and the unavailable Previous / Next ends with `disabled`.

## Do

- Place it only inside `pagination`'s default slot: the strip's border and frame come from the root, and the outer radius is applied through `first:` / `last:`, so only the first and last buttons of the strip round their corners.
- Pass `aria-label` on every `previous` and `next` button: those types render an `aria-hidden` icon only and have no accessible name otherwise. `more` is decorative and hidden from assistive tech, so it takes no `aria-label`.
- Put the page number in the default slot of `type="number"` only; the other types ignore the slot.
- Set `active` on exactly one number button (it sets `aria-current="page"`), and `disabled` on Previous at the first page and Next at the last.
- In composition mode you own every click: listen to `click` and update the page yourself; a `disabled` button never emits it.

## Don’t

- You know the item count → pass `total` to `pagination` and bind `v-model:page`; it renders and wires every PaginationButton itself.
- The rows live in a data-driven `table` → set `paginated` on the table instead.
- The control is a previous / next link between documentation pages → use `doc-previous-next`.
- It is a standalone action outside a pagination strip → use `button` or `icon-button`; this button has no radius or frame of its own except at the strip's ends.
- It is a "Load more" control at the end of a list → use `button`.

## Related

- `pagination` — the root that frames the strip and, in data-driven mode, renders these buttons; re-exports this component as `Pagination.Button`.
- `pagination-description` — the page-info text that sits beside the strip.
- `pagination-page-size` — the rows-per-page selector placed in the pagination's `controls` slot.
- `icon-button` — a standalone icon-only action with its own frame and radius.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'previous' \| 'next' \| 'number' \| 'more'` | `'number'` | false | Button role within the pagination. |
| `active` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the current page (filled surface + aria-current). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `MouseEvent` | Fires on activation. Not emitted while `disabled` (the native `disabled` attribute also blocks it), and never for `type="more"`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The page number. Rendered only when `type` is `number`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `active`, `focus-visible`, current page (`active` prop), `disabled`.
- Root: a native `button` with `type="button"`, or a `span` with `aria-hidden="true"` when `type` is `more` (inert: not focusable, no hover / active layer, no `active` / `disabled` treatment, never emits `click`); attributes (including `aria-label` and `class`) are forwarded to it (`inheritAttrs: false` + `v-bind="$attrs"`).
- `data-type` mirrors `type` (`previous` | `next` | `number` | `more`). `previous` renders `az az-chevron-left`, `next` renders `az az-chevron-right`, `more` renders `az az-ellipsis`; only `number` renders the default slot. `number` and `more` carry `var(--bg-surface)`; `previous` and `next` have no surface of their own.
- `hover` and `active` are two stacked pseudo-element layers (`before:` hover, `after:` active) and are mutually exclusive: pressing hides the hover layer and shows the active layer alone.
- `data-active` is present when `active` is set; it adds `var(--bg-selected)` and a `var(--border-default)` rule on each inline side that faces a neighbouring segment (the strip's own frame draws the top, the bottom and the two outer ends, so the current page never doubles a line), and sets `aria-current="page"`.
- `data-disabled` is present when `disabled` is set; the button also gets the native `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled="true"`, mutes the foreground to `var(--text-disabled)`, shows `cursor-not-allowed`, hides both state layers and keeps the type's own surface.
- Coarse pointer: a `number`, `previous` or `next` button renders an empty `aria-hidden` `span` (`data-slot="touch-target"`) that is shown only under `pointer-coarse:` and extends the hit area vertically to 44 px; the drawn button does not grow.
- Test ids: `<pagination testId>__button` when rendered inside a `pagination` (`data-pagination__button` by default), `data-pagination__button` outside one; a consumer `data-testid` wins.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: native button — `Tab` focuses; `Enter` / `Space` activates; a `disabled` button is skipped by `Tab`; the `more` ellipsis is a `span` and never receives focus.
- ARIA: `aria-current="page"` when `active`; `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled="true"` when `disabled`; the chevron icons are `aria-hidden="true"`, so `previous` and `next` take their accessible name from a consumer `aria-label` (data-driven `pagination` sets one on both); the `more` ellipsis root is `aria-hidden="true"` and decorative, so it needs no name.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons): `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-surface)` / `var(--bg-selected)`; disabled uses `var(--text-disabled)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none`, `motion-reduce:before:transition-none` and `motion-reduce:after:transition-none` on the state transitions.
- Touch target: drawn 28×28 on every pointer (above the 24×24 minimum of WCAG 2.5.8); on a coarse pointer an invisible `aria-hidden` child (`data-slot="touch-target"`) extends the hit area to 28×44. The width stays 28 because the buttons are butted into the strip (see `pagination`). The inert `more` span has no hit area.

## Usage

```vue
<script setup>
  import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'
  import PaginationButton from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button'
</script>

<template>
  <Pagination>
    <PaginationButton
      type="previous"
      aria-label="Previous page"
      disabled
    />
    <PaginationButton
      type="number"
      active
      >1</PaginationButton
    >
    <PaginationButton type="number">2</PaginationButton>
    <PaginationButton type="more" />
    <PaginationButton
      type="next"
      aria-label="Next page"
    />
  </Pagination>
</template>
```
