<!-- components/property-filter.md -->

# Property Filter

> One field that filters a collection by properties and free text, after Cloudscape's property filter. Typing suggests a property, then an operator, then a value, and each choice becomes a removable token (`Status = Active`); text typed without a property becomes a free-text token. Two or more tokens combine with Match all (and) or Match any (or). With `mode="query"` the same field edits one query string instead (`level = Error AND method = GET`), after the Console Kit events query bar: suggestions follow the word at the caret (a field, an operator, a value, then AND or OR), a check explains what is wrong under the field, and Enter submits the text with its flat token list. Since spec v4, tokens mode also builds one level of nested conditions (`grouped`: each group has its own Match all / Match any, and the groups combine with the query's operation — `(Status = Active or Status = Paused) and (Region = US East or Region = EU West)`), fetches the values of a property as the person types (`loadValues`, with a loading and an error row and a count per value), groups the operator suggestions (Equality, Comparison, Text match), and hands the value of a property marked `customValue` to the `value` slot (a date picker, a number range). It edits a `PropertyFilterQuery` and never filters anything itself: `useCollection` (or the server) applies the query, and `propertyFilterProps` binds the query, the properties and the match count in one `v-bind`.

- Import: `import PropertyFilter from '@aziontech/webkit/property-filter'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use PropertyFilter when people type queries with operators (Status = Active, Requests > 100) or free text they want to keep.
- A list or table that people narrow by several fields at once (status, region, owner) and by text.
- Any collection driven by `useCollection`, client or server mode.
- Filters that must survive a reload or a shared link: the query serializes into the URL through `useCollection`.
- With `mode="query"`: an explorer (events, logs) whose users type queries by hand, keep and reuse them as text, or need a grammar of the product (pass `validate` and `suggest`).

## Do

- Give every property with a closed set of values its `options`, so values are suggested and tokens print labels.
- Set `type: 'number'` or `type: 'date'` on ordered properties to offer `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`.
- Bind `totalCount` so people hear how many items match after each change.
- Turn on `grouped` only when people need both and and or in one filter; most filters read better flat.
- Use `loadValues` when a property has too many values to ship (hostnames, users); return at most a few dozen per call, already filtered by the typed text, with `count` when the server knows it.
- Mark a property `customValue` when its value is easier to pick than to type (a date), and render the editor in the `value` slot; call `apply` with the value text.
- Name the field after the collection (`aria-label="Filter resources"`).
- In query mode, fields are written by `key` (no spaces); quote values that hold spaces or operator characters (`"edge cache"`). Apply the `query` of `submit` when it is not null; keep the `text` for saved and recent queries.
- A product grammar (`like`, `between`, parentheses) passes `validate` and `suggest`; `submit` then carries `query: null` for text the built-in grammar cannot flatten, and the product parses `text` itself.

## Don’t

- A single text search over a short list → use `input` bound to `filterProps`.
- A few fixed choices always on screen → use `toggle-group` or `chip` filters.
- Inside a DataTable toolbar, `TableFilter type="property"` renders this field wired to the table's filters; bind PropertyFilter to `useCollection` yourself only for OR queries or free text.
- Faceted picks from a known set of values per field (status, region, owner), shown as chips → use `filter-menu`. PropertyFilter is for expression search: typed tokens, operators, free text and a query people keep as text.

## Related

- `use-collection` — applies the query; `propertyFilterProps` is the binding.
- `table` — the collection it usually filters.
- `card-list` — the card form of a collection.
- `collection-preferences` — the panel that sits beside it in the controls row.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `properties` | `FilteringProperty[]` | `[]` | false | Properties the suggestions offer, with their operators and values. |
| `totalCount` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Items that match the query, announced next to the tokens. Hidden when unset. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder of the field. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the field. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `freeText` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Accepts typed text with no property as a free-text token. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the field and the tokens. |
| `mode` | `'tokens' \| 'query'` | `'tokens'` | false | `tokens` turns each choice into a token; `query` edits one query string. |
| `validate` | `(text: string) => string` | `undefined` | false | Checks the query string in query mode: '' when valid, else the message shown under the field. Replaces the built-in check. |
| `suggest` | `(text: string, caret: number) => PropertyFilterQuerySuggestion[]` | `undefined` | false | Suggestions for the word at the caret in query mode. Replaces the built-in field, operator, value and AND / OR suggestions. |
| `grouped` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Tokens mode: tokens go into groups with their own Match all / Match any; Add group starts the next one. |
| `showOperations` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the Match all / Match any toggle; false keeps the tokens combined with AND (a model that holds only AND conditions, such as a table's filters). |
| `loadValues` | `(property: FilteringProperty, text: string) => Promise<PropertyFilterOption[]>` | `undefined` | false | Fetches the values of a property for the typed text, after the operator. Replaces its `options` in the suggestions. |
| `query` | `PropertyFilterQuery` | `—` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:query`). |
| `text` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:text`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: KeyboardEvent, payload: PropertyFilterSubmit)` | Enter with no active suggestion and a valid query; `event` is the Enter keydown. Query mode only. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | { property: FilteringProperty, operator: PropertyFilterOperator, apply: (value: string) => void } | Tokens mode. Rendered under the field, in a named `group`, once the typed text has a property marked `customValue` and an operator; `apply` adds the token and returns focus to the field. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:query` | `PropertyFilterQuery` | `{ tokens: [], operation: 'and' }` | `update:query` | Via `defineModel('query')`. A token was added or removed, the operation changed, or all cleared. Tokens mode only. Unbound, the field keeps its own tokens. |
| `v-model:text` | `string` | `''` | `update:text` | Via `defineModel('text')`. The query string changed (typing, a suggestion, Escape clearing). Query mode only. Unbound, the field keeps its own text. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `focus-visible`, `open` (suggestions shown), `disabled`, `invalid` (query mode: after Enter or blur on a query that fails the check, then live until it passes or is cleared)
- `data-mode` on the field wrapper mirrors `mode`; query mode sets the typed text in the code type through the field's `monospace` prop (`text-label-code-sm`, 16 px `text-label-code-lg` on coarse pointers)
- `aria-expanded` on the field mirrors the open suggestions; `data-active` marks the active option
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop; while disabled nothing is added, removed or submitted (no `update:query`, no `submit`)
- `loading` (values): a `Loading values` row with a spinner in the suggestions while `loadValues` is pending, `aria-busy` on the listbox; `error`: a `Could not load values` row when it rejects. A newer call wins over a stale one.
- Grouped (`grouped`): each group is a bordered `group` (`data-testid="…__group"`); a pending new group shows a dashed `New group` chip until its first token.
- `data-side` (`bottom` | `top`) and `data-align` (`start`) on the suggestion panel mirror where it landed after flipping; `start` follows the text direction, so under `rtl` the panel lines up with the field's right edge

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the field's own `focus-within` ring (from `input`); tokens and buttons keep theirs.
- Page search key: while mounted and not `disabled`, the filter registers `/` with `useShortcuts` (listed in `ShortcutsDialog` as `propertyFilter.focusShortcut`, Focus search), so `/` focuses the field from anywhere on the page, never while typing in another field, with `⌘`, `Ctrl` or `Alt` held, or from inside a modal layer that does not hold the filter (the console keyboard standard, `rules/webkit-keyboard.md`). Tests: `property-filter.test.ts` › page search key.
- Keyboard map (query mode): typing opens the suggestions for the word at the caret; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the active option (wrapping); `Enter` applies the active option (it replaces the word and moves the caret after it) or submits the query; `Escape` closes the suggestions, then clears the text; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`, `Home`/`End` and clicks move the caret and the suggestions follow it; `Backspace` only edits text.
- In query mode an invalid query sets `aria-invalid` on the field and `aria-describedby` to the message, which sits in a polite live region under the field; the token group is not rendered.
- Keyboard map (tokens mode): typing opens the suggestions; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the active option (wrapping); `Enter` applies the active option or commits the typed text; `Escape` closes the suggestions, then clears the text; `Backspace` in an empty field removes the last token (with `grouped`: cancels a pending new group first, then removes the last token of the last group).
- Operator suggestions sit in named `group`s (Equality, Comparison, Text match) inside the listbox; the arrows move across groups as one list.
- `grouped`: each group is a `group` named `Filter group <n>`; its Match all / Match any toggle is named `Combine filters in group <n>`; Add group is a button that returns focus to the field.
- `value` slot: its wrapper is a `group` named `Value of <property>`; the editor inside owns its own keyboard.
- ARIA: the field is a `combobox` (`aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant`); the suggestions are a named `listbox` of `option`s with `aria-selected` on the active one; the tokens sit in a named `group`; each token's remove button is named `Remove <token>`; the match count is a `status` region.
- Option targets are 32 px high (44 px on `pointer: coarse`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PropertyFilter from '@aziontech/webkit/property-filter'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const properties = [
    {
      key: 'status',
      label: 'Status',
      options: [{ value: 'Active' }, { value: 'Inactive' }, { value: 'Degraded' }]
    },
    {
      key: 'region',
      label: 'Region',
      options: [{ value: 'sa-east' }, { value: 'us-east' }, { value: 'eu-west' }]
    },
    { key: 'name', label: 'Name' },
    { key: 'requests', label: 'Requests', type: 'number' }
  ]

  const query = ref({
    tokens: [{ propertyKey: 'status', operator: '=', value: 'Active' }],
    operation: 'and'
  })
</script>

<template>
  <PropertyFilter
    v-model:query="query"
    :properties="properties"
    :total-count="12"
  />
</template>
```

# Table

> The table's parts and its markup-only root. Compose the anatomy by hand (`Table.Header` / `Table.Body` / `Table.Row` / `Table.HeadCell` / `Table.Cell`): the component owns markup, tokens, accessibility, column sizing (an emphasized principal column), sortable headers, selectable rows and a **freeze system** for sticky columns (an actions column) and a sticky header. The root is light: it frames the scroll viewport, the toolbar band (`title` / `toolbar` slots) and the `footer`, and loads no table engine. For repeated records pass `data` + `columns` to `data-table` instead: DataTable renders through these same parts, and the context-aware toolbar parts (`TableSearch`, `TableFilter`, `TableExportButton`, `TableRefreshButton`, `TableLiveButton`) and the cell presets (`TableCellLink`, `TableCellId`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTags`, `TableCellTime`, `TableCellActions`) go in its slots. Inside a hand-composed `Table` the toolbar parts have no rows to act on. **What the compound carries.** `@aziontech/webkit/table` attaches only the structural parts (`Header`, `Body`, `Footer`, `Caption`, `Row`, `HeadCell`, `Cell`, `SortButton`, `Toolbar`), so a hand-composed table costs what its parts cost. The toolbar controls and the cell presets compose `Tooltip`, `DropdownMenu`, `Popover`, `Input` and `CopyButton`; each is imported from its own entry (`@aziontech/webkit/table-search`, `@aziontech/webkit/table-cell-status`, …) and is not attached to the compound, so a screen pays only for the ones it renders. **Cell presets.** Six presets render the cells every list repeats, each inside a cell (or a DataTable `#cell-<id>` slot): `TableCellLink` (a name that leaves the screen: an optional muted leading glyph (`icon`) for the provider or resource type, a 12 px external mark on an address outside the app only (never on an in-app route), a tooltip naming the destination, underline on hover; optional `+N` overflow through `OverflowCount` and a copy button pinned to the end edge), `TableCellId` (an identifier with its copy button), `TableCellStatus` (one semantic `Tag`), `TableCellTags` (as many tags as fit, the rest behind `+N`), `TableCellTime` (avatar of the author plus a relative time that updates every minute, or counts from the nearest `ConfigProvider`'s `now`, the absolute time on the tooltip and for screen readers; with no provider `now`, a server render prints the UTC date and the cell switches to the relative time once mounted, so hydration never mismatches) and `TableCellActions` (the row menu named after the row). **Types** (declared in `injection-key.ts`, re-exported by `./table`): the column and slot types DataTable takes (`TableColumn`, `TableCellSlotProps`, `TableHeaderSlotProps`, `TableToolbarSlotProps`, `TableStateSnapshot`, `TableExposed`, `TableAppliedFilter`, `TableFilterField`, `TableDensity`), so a page can type its columns from the compound it already imports. Their shapes are documented in `data-table`.

- Import: `import TableRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/table-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Table from '@aziontech/webkit/table'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Table for records that share columns when you compose the rows by hand; for any console list of resources people scan, sort and act on, pass `data` + `columns` to DataTable, which renders through these parts.
- A small, static table, or one whose cells need a layout the column model cannot express: compose `Table.Header` / `Table.Row` / `Table.Cell` by hand. The root loads no engine.
- The parts of a DataTable: the toolbar controls and cell presets go in its slots, each imported from its own entry (`@aziontech/webkit/table-search`, `@aziontech/webkit/table-cell-status`).
- Use Table for read-and-act content; for repeated records pass `data` + `columns` to `data-table`, and when people edit cells in place use `data-grid`.

## Do

- Compose `Table` by hand only for small, static tables; for repeated data use `data-table`, which renders through these parts.
- Mark the row-actions cell `type="action"` with `frozen="end"` so it pins to the trailing edge, and give the principal cell `principal` (or `grow="2"`).
- Name the table: a `Table.Caption` labels it (`aria-labelledby`), or pass `aria-label` on the root.
- Give `TableCellTime` dates from your data. Where the text must not depend on when it renders (an example, a test, a server render the browser hydrates), set `now` on the app's `ConfigProvider` and count sample dates back from that constant; never build them from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup.
- Import the root alone from `table-root`, or each part from its own entry (`table-row`), when only a few parts are used.

## Don’t

- Repeated records with sorting, selection, paging, filtering, virtual rows or tree rows → use `data-table` (`data` + `columns`).
- People edit many cells of many records in place, spreadsheet-style → use `data-grid`.
- A short list of same-field rows added and removed inside a form (environment variables, headers) → use `attribute-editor`.
- A short titled preview of a longer listing on a marketing page → use `listing-table-section`.
- A feature-by-feature comparison of Azion with a competitor → use `competitor-comparison-section`.
- Rows of mixed content (media, title, description, actions) that do not share columns → use `item`.
- A grid of selectable cards or options → use `radio-group` with `type="card"`.
- The same records as a grid of cards → use `card-list` (same collection, card layout).

## Related

- `data-table` — the data-driven table (`data` + `columns`, TanStack engine) that renders through these parts.
- `data-grid` — the editable, spreadsheet-like grid; a separate grid (`role="grid"`, one roving tab stop, in-cell editors) that shares these tokens, not built on these parts.
- `pagination` — the page strip; put it in a `Table.Footer` in the `footer` slot.
- `empty-state` — compose it in a full-width row when a hand-composed table has no rows.
- `item` — list rows without a column structure.
- `listing-table-section` — marketing section that composes a DataTable for a linked preview of a list.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxHeight` | `string` | `''` | false | Max height (CSS length). The viewport scrolls dynamically: horizontal scroll appears automatically when columns overflow the width; vertical scroll appears only when `maxHeight` is set smaller than the content (under a frozen header). |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Draw the outer card border around the table. Off by default (the table is typically framed by a surrounding surface); the internal row dividers are unaffected. |
| `density` | `'comfortable' \| 'compact'` | `'comfortable'` | false | Density of the body cells: `compact` shrinks their height and padding. Set `density` on `Table.Header` too for a compact header. |
| `wrapLines` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Cell text wraps onto several lines instead of truncating. Identifiers stay on one line and truncate: `code`, `kbd`, `samp`, a `dir="ltr"` span (the `TableCellId` value) and code-typography text (`text-label-code-*`). |

| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The scrollable region: `Table.Caption`, `Table.Header`, `Table.Body`. |
| `title` | — | Title text shown at the start of the toolbar band, fixed above the scroll viewport. |
| `toolbar` | — | Action band above the scroll viewport, end-aligned beside the title. |
| `footer` | — | Footer region rendered below the scroll viewport (`Table.Footer` + `Pagination`), so it never scrolls with the body. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `selected`
- The viewport is always a scroll container (`overflow: auto`): horizontal scroll is automatic when columns overflow; vertical scroll engages only when `maxHeight` constrains the content.
- `data-frozen` on TableHeader (`true`), TableHeadCell / TableCell (`start` | `end`), and TableRow (`true`). A frozen head/body cell renders a CSS-only fade (gradient pseudo-element) just outside its inner edge that dissolves the horizontally scrolling content into the row background (`from-transparent` → `var(--table-row-bg)`, the row-published color, so it matches the row on hover/selected) — `frozen=start` fades on the right, `frozen=end` on the left. The fade tints nothing; it only masks the content sliding under the pinned column.
- Scroll cue: the scroll viewport sits in a `__scroll` frame that sets `data-overflow-start` / `data-overflow-end` from the scroll position (re-measured on scroll and on resize). While content is hidden past an inline edge, an `aria-hidden` gradient as wide as the hidden distance (at most 24 px, none when 4 px or less, so it never sits over text that is otherwise in view) (`__fade-start` / `__fade-end`, `from-transparent` to `var(--bg-surface)`, pointer events off) covers that edge of the viewport, so a phone shows that columns continue; it follows the inline direction under `dir="rtl"`, has no motion, and keeps its gradient under forced colors (fading to `Canvas`). A frozen column on that edge draws its own fade and paints over the cue, which sits below frozen cells and the sticky header (`z-5`).
- `data-state` on TableRow: `selected` | `unselected`; `data-selected` mirrors the `selected` prop; `aria-selected` set when selected.
- `data-type` on TableHeadCell (`default` | `checkbox` | `action` | `slot`) and TableCell (`default` | `checkbox` | `action`).
- `data-align` on head/body cells: `start` | `center` | `end`.
- `data-grow` on head/body cells: `1` | `2` | `3` (flex weight).
- `data-sortable` and `data-sort` (`none` | `ascending` | `descending`) on TableHeadCell; `aria-sort` mirrors `data-sort`.
- `data-sort` (`none` | `ascending` | `descending`) on TableSortButton.
- `data-clickable` on TableCell mirrors the `clickable` prop.
- Density and wrapping: `data-density="compact"` on the root shrinks the body cells (`min-h-9`, `--spacing-2xs` block padding); `data-wrap` lets cell text (and any `.truncate` inside a cell) wrap, except identifiers: `code`, `kbd`, `samp`, `[dir=ltr]` and `text-label-code-*` elements, and any `.truncate` inside them, keep `white-space: nowrap`, so a token such as `p-(--spacing-2xl)` or an ID never splits at a hyphen; they truncate instead. A compact header is `Table.Header density="compact"`.
- Responsive toolbar: the root is the `@container/table`; the toolbar wraps, and below `@md` of the table the `toolbar` slot moves under the title and starts at the start edge. `Table.Toolbar` wraps its controls.
- Hover-free devices: a touch screen shows the sort glyph only on the sorted column, as on a pointer screen with no hover; tapping a sortable header sorts it, and keyboard focus reveals the sort button.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the sort button and any interactive cell content.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the sort button of each sortable column (one tab stop per column, as in the APG sortable table: the header cell itself is not focusable and carries `aria-sort`) and interactive cell content; `Enter`/`Space` on the sort button toggles the sort; row click is mouse/touch (no keyboard trap). Body rows are not focusable, so `row-click` is never the only way to open a record: the principal column carries a real link or button (`TableCellLink`, or the `cell-<id>` slot with an anchor, as the Default example does), which keyboard and screen-reader users reach instead (WCAG 2.1.1).
- ARIA: `role="table"` sits on the grid element inside the scroll viewport (testid `<testid>__table`), not on the root: the root also holds the toolbar band, the focusable scroll viewport and the footer, and any of those inside a `table` is an unallowed child (`aria-required-children`). Every `aria-*` attribute passed to `Table` (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`…) is forwarded to that element; every other attribute stays on the root. `table-caption` is a plain element (no `role`) that names the table through `aria-labelledby` unless the consumer names it with `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`. The default slot is the table's content, so it holds rowgroups (and a caption) only; anything else goes in `footer` or around the `Table`. `table-header`/`table-body` `role="rowgroup"`; `table-footer` has no role (it hosts pagination or an action, not rows); `table-row` `role="row"`; `table-head-cell` `role="columnheader"` with `aria-sort` when sortable; `table-cell` `role="cell"`; selected rows set `aria-selected`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including muted header text.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Pause, Stop, Hide (WCAG 2.2.2): the `TableLiveButton` dot pulses for as long as the live tail runs. The pulse is an essential status signal (it shows the stream is running, and stops when the stream stops), so it takes `animate-status-pulse` (the catalog's status pulse; `animate-pulse` is the Skeleton loading placeholder's); the user stops it with the same button, and `motion-reduce:animate-none` keeps it still.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the sort button and row action controls.
- Filter names: `TableFilter` hosts `FilterMenu` (its trigger counts the applied fields in its name) or `PropertyFilter` (a combobox named by `title`); see their specs.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Table from '@aziontech/webkit/table'

  const items = [
    { id: '1001', name: 'Workload Alpha', status: 'Active', editor: 'user1@example.com' },
    { id: '1002', name: 'Workload Bravo', status: 'Inactive', editor: 'user2@example.com' },
    { id: '1003', name: 'Workload Charlie', status: 'Degraded', editor: 'user3@example.com' },
    { id: '1004', name: 'Workload Delta', status: 'Active', editor: 'user4@example.com' },
    { id: '1005', name: 'Workload Echo', status: 'Inactive', editor: 'user5@example.com' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Table bordered>
    <Table.Header>
      <Table.Row>
        <Table.HeadCell principal>Name</Table.HeadCell>
        <Table.HeadCell>Status</Table.HeadCell>
        <Table.HeadCell>Last Editor</Table.HeadCell>
      </Table.Row>
    </Table.Header>
    <Table.Body>
      <Table.Row
        v-for="item in items"
        :key="item.id"
      >
        <Table.Cell principal
          ><span class="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate">{{ item.name }}</span></Table.Cell
        >
        <Table.Cell
          ><span class="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate">{{ item.status }}</span></Table.Cell
        >
        <Table.Cell
          ><span class="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate">{{ item.editor }}</span></Table.Cell
        >
      </Table.Row>
    </Table.Body>
  </Table>
</template>
```

<!-- components/transfer-list.md -->

# Transfer List

> Dual-list transfer control: a labelled **source** listbox and a labelled **target** listbox with a control column to move items between them. Use it when the consumer needs to build a subset from a pool of options where both the chosen set and the remaining pool stay visible. Named after the MUI Transfer List (Ant Design calls it Transfer; it was PickList before 6.0), written to our conventions (no Figma); the visual surface is a best-effort first draft to validate. Compound, composition API: the root (`<TransferList>`) owns the bound data (`v-model` = `[sourceItems, targetItems]`) and the shared selection/move state, and provides it through `provide`/`inject`. The consumer composes the anatomy — `<TransferList.Source>`, `<TransferList.Controls>`, `<TransferList.Target>` — and the context-aware `<TransferList.Controls>` wires the move buttons with no props. Each list is data-driven: items come from the root's bound pair and render through the list's `#item` slot (repeated data stays as props, not hand-authored rows). Double-clicking an option moves it to the opposite list (emitting `item-double-click`); this auto-move can be turned off with `move-on-double-click`. The two lists sit side by side on wider viewports and stack vertically (with the controls as a horizontal row between them) on narrow ones; the move arrows point left/right side-by-side and up/down when stacked.

- Import: `import TransferListRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import TransferList from '@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use TransferList only when the person builds a large subset and must see the chosen and remaining items side by side. To pick several values in a compact form field use MultiSelect; for two to five options use a Checkbox per option.
- Building a subset from a pool where both the chosen and the remaining items stay visible (domains assigned to an application, members of a team).
- Moving many items at once with move-all and multi-selection.
- Lists that load separately, each with its own `loading` state.

## Do

- Set `item-key` to a unique item field so rows keep stable keys across moves and the selection follows the record when the lists change; without it rows and the selection are keyed by their index.
- Set `title` on both `TransferList.Source` and `TransferList.Target`; it is the listbox's accessible name.
- Listen to `move` for side effects such as saving the assignment instead of diffing `v-model`.
- Set `:move-on-double-click="false"` when double-click should do something else; `item-double-click` still fires.

## Don’t

- Picking a few values in a compact field → use `multi-select`.
- Selecting rows of tabular data with columns, sorting, or pagination → use `table` with row selection.
- A handful of fixed options → use a horizontal `field` with a `checkbox` for each.

## Related

- `multi-select` — compact dropdown for multi-pick when the remaining pool does not need to stay visible.
- `table` — row selection over tabular data.
- `checkbox` — independent boolean or small-set multi-pick.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `itemKey` | `string` | `''` | false | Item field that identifies a record, the same name as `card-list`: each row's render key and the key of the selection, so an external change to the v-model pair keeps the selection on its records. Empty falls back to the index. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables all selection and move controls and applies disabled tokens. |
| `moveOnDoubleClick` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, double-clicking an item moves it to the opposite list. Set false to keep `item-double-click` firing without the move. |
| `modelValue` | `TransferListValue` | `—` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `move` | `(event: Event, payload: { direction: 'to-target' \| 'to-source'; items: unknown[] })` | Fired after items move between lists; the DOM event of the control (or the double-click) first, then the direction and the moved items. |
| `item-double-click` | `(event: MouseEvent, payload: { list: 'source' \| 'target'; item: unknown; index: number })` | Fired when an option is double-clicked. `event` is the dblclick; `payload` carries the item, its index, and which list it was in. Fires regardless of `moveOnDoubleClick`, but not while the component is disabled or a list is loading. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | { move, moveAll, hasSelection, count, disabled, loading } | Composition slot; receives `<TransferList.Source>`, `<TransferList.Controls>`, and `<TransferList.Target>` in flow order. The scope exposes the move actions plus selection/loading state, so a consumer can render custom controls inside the root in place of `<TransferList.Controls>`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list-source`
- `@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list-target`
- `@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list-controls`

## Sub-components

- `transfer-list-source/transfer-list-source.vue` — The source listbox (the left/top list).
- `transfer-list-target/transfer-list-target.vue` — The target listbox (the right/bottom list).
- `transfer-list-controls/transfer-list-controls.vue` — The context-aware control column between the lists.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `[unknown[], unknown[]]` | `() => [[], []]` | `update:modelValue` | Bound pair of lists as `[sourceItems, targetItems]`, two-way through `defineModel`. Each move writes the new pair back; without a bound `v-model` the component keeps the pair as local state. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (option), `focus-visible` (option / control), `selected` (option), `disabled`, `loading`
- `data-disabled` on the root mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-loading` on a list (`transfer-list-source` / `transfer-list-target`) mirrors that list's `loading` prop
- A loading list renders a centered spinner instead of its options and sets `aria-busy="true"`; while any list is loading, both the move controls and double-click-to-move are disabled until loading clears
- Each option carries `data-selected` mirroring its selection and `aria-selected`
- Empty list (not loading, no items): the package `EmptyState` (small, `transferList.emptyTitle`, `No items`) is laid over the list box, outside the listbox element (a `status` region is not an allowed listbox child); test id `<list testid>__empty`
- Server render and hydration: the options are the direct `v-for` children of the `TransitionGroup` list (an empty list while loading) and the spinner a sibling `v-if`, so the server renders no fragment markers inside the list and the HTML hydrates as is.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on each option and on every move control.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the two listboxes and the control column, one tab stop per listbox (roving `tabindex`: the last focused option, the first by default); within a listbox `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move focus, `Home`/`End` go to the first and last option, `Space`/`Enter` toggle the focused option's selection, and `Shift`+`ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` extend the selection to the next option; the move controls are activated with `Enter`/`Space`. Double-click on an option is a pointer affordance for moving it to the opposite list; the same move is reachable via select + the move controls (no keyboard-only feature is double-click-only).
- ARIA: each list is `role="listbox"` with `aria-label` from its title text; options are `role="option"` with `aria-selected`; the source/target listboxes set `aria-multiselectable="true"`; every move control is an icon-only button with an explicit `aria-label`; `aria-disabled` mirrors `disabled` on both listboxes, and a disabled root becomes `role="group"` with `aria-disabled="true"`, so the titles dimmed by the root's `opacity-60` belong to a disabled control (WCAG 1.4.3 inactive-component exemption) instead of reading as low-contrast live text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (borders + icons), including the disabled state.
- A loading list sets `aria-busy="true"`; its `Spinner` is decorative (`aria-hidden`) and carries its own reduced-motion fallback. Control hover transitions pair with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px for every move control (large icon-button height).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import TransferList from '@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const model = ref([
    [
      { id: 1, label: 'Functions' },
      { id: 2, label: 'WAF' },
      { id: 3, label: 'Image Processor' }
    ],
    [{ id: 4, label: 'Cache' }]
  ])
</script>

<template>
  <TransferList
    v-model="model"
    item-key="id"
  >
    <TransferList.Source title="Available">
      <template #item="{ item }">{{ item.label }}</template>
    </TransferList.Source>

    <TransferList.Controls />

    <TransferList.Target title="Selected">
      <template #item="{ item }">{{ item.label }}</template>
    </TransferList.Target>
  </TransferList>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/transfer-list.md](components/transfer-list.md).

# Tree

> A hierarchical list of nodes, each row a name with an optional glyph and one line of detail, where a parent row folds its children open and closed under a chevron. It renders a nested `items` data structure on its own (recursively, through one internal row template) and follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern, so it fits file and object browsers: the objects of a bucket, the source files of a deployment, the routes of an application. Unlike `sidebar-menu` it navigates data, not the app, and unlike `accordion` its nodes are rows of the same kind at any depth, not panels of free content.

- Import: `import Tree from '@aziontech/webkit/tree'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Tree for a nested data hierarchy (files, resources) the person expands and selects in, not for app navigation; for the navigation tree of the app use SidebarMenu inside Sidebar.
- Browsing a hierarchy whose depth is not fixed: bucket objects under folders, the source tree of a deployment, functions grouped by application.
- Picking one node out of a hierarchy (`selectable`) to show its detail beside the tree, or several (`selectable="multiple"`) to act on them together (move, delete, download).
- A hierarchy too large to send at once: mark unloaded parents `lazy` and fetch their children when they open.
- A file browser where people rename nodes where they are (`editable`) and open a node with a double-click (`item-double-click`).
- A hierarchy the user expands piece by piece, where showing every level at once would bury the node they are after.

## Do

- Give every node an `id` that is unique across the whole tree, not only among its siblings; `v-model:open-keys`, `v-model:selected-key` and focus are keyed by it.
- Seed `v-model:open-keys` with the path to the node the user is most likely after (the open folder, the selected file), not with every parent.
- Keep labels short and put secondary detail (size, count, modified date) in `description` so rows scan as names first.
- Use `selectable` only when the selection drives something on the screen (a detail pane, a preview); for a tree whose rows only lead somewhere, listen to `item-click` instead.
- Put per-row controls in the `actions` slot (an `IconButton` that opens a `dropdown`), never inside the `item` slot, so they do not take over the row's activation.
- For children loaded on demand, mark the node `lazy`, listen to `update:openKeys`, set `loading` on the node while the request runs, then patch `children` in (an empty array when it has none) and clear `loading`.
- With `editable`, apply the new label from the `rename` event yourself (the tree does not mutate `items`); offer a `Rename` entry in the row actions that calls the exposed `startRename(id)` so the feature is discoverable beyond F2.
- Use `item-double-click` for a secondary "open" action only; single click and Enter stay `item-click`, so nothing requires a double-click.

## Don’t

- Navigation between views of the app → use `sidebar-menu` inside `sidebar`.
- Flat records with several attributes each → use `table`.
- A few sections of free content that open and close → use `accordion`.
- A two- or three-level directory of destinations on a marketing page → use `link-directory`.

## Related

- `table` — the flat, multi-column view of the same records; switch to it when columns matter more than nesting.
- `sidebar-menu` — the hierarchical list for app navigation, with routes and active state instead of selection.
- `accordion` — disclosure of free content panels rather than rows of one kind.
- `empty-state` — what the tree renders when `items` is empty.
- `skeleton` — the rows the tree renders while `loading`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `TreeItem[]` | `[]` | false | Nodes to render; each is `{ id: string; label: string; icon?: string; description?: string; disabled?: boolean; children?: TreeItem[] }`. A node with a non-empty `children` array is a parent. |
| `selectable` | `boolean \| TreeSelectable` | `false` | false | Enables selection: `true` or `'single'` writes one id to `v-model:selected`; `'multiple'` writes ids to `v-model:selected-keys`. Every treeitem then carries `aria-selected`. |
| `editable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Lets the user rename a node in place with F2, or through the exposed `startRename(id)`; the result arrives as the `rename` event. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders Skeleton rows in place of the tree and sets `aria-busy`. |
| `size` | `TreeSize` | `'medium'` | false | Row density: `small` is 24px rows, `medium` 32px, `large` 40px. Height, padding, type, glyph size and indentation step together (see Tokens). |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the default empty state shown when `items` is empty. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No items`). |
| `emptyDescription` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting line under the empty title. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the tree. Empty uses the locale catalog (`tree.label`, `Tree`), so the `tree` role always has a name. |
| `openKeys` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:openKeys`). |
| `selectedKey` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:selectedKey`). |
| `selectedKeys` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:selectedKeys`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item-click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, item: TreeItem)` | A node activated: click on its row, or Enter / Space on the focused node. `item` is the consumer's own node object. Fires after `update:selectedKey` when `selectable`. Not fired for a `disabled` node, nor for a click on the chevron, inside the `actions` region or in the rename field. With `selectable="multiple"`, Space toggles selection without firing it. |
| `item-double-click` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: TreeItem)` | A row was double-clicked, to open or preview the node. Not fired for a `disabled` node, the chevron, the `actions` region or the rename field. The two clicks before it still fire `item-click`. |
| `rename` | `(event: KeyboardEvent \| FocusEvent, payload: TreeRenamePayload)` | An in-place rename was submitted (Enter, or the field losing focus) with a trimmed label that is non-empty and differs from `item.label`. `payload.item` is the consumer's node. Escape, an empty label or an unchanged one closes the field without emitting. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` | { item: TreeItem; level: number; expanded: boolean } | Replaces the label region of every row (glyph + label + description). The fallback inside the slot renders `item.icon`, `item.label` and `item.description`. `level` is 1 for top-level nodes; `expanded` is false for leaves. The chevron, indentation, row states and the `actions` region stay owned by the tree. |
| `actions` | { item: TreeItem; level: number } | Trailing per-row controls, end-aligned in the row (e.g. an `IconButton` that opens a `dropdown`). Clicks and keys inside it do not activate the row nor move tree focus. No fallback; when unused, the region is not rendered. |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the default empty state. The fallback inside the slot is `EmptyState` titled by `emptyTitle` with `emptyDescription`. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open-keys` | `string[]` | `[]` | `update:openKeys` | Ids of the open parents, via `defineModel<string[]>('openKeys', { default: () => [] })`. Uncontrolled when unbound. Ids of leaves or of unknown nodes are ignored. Collapsing a parent removes only its own id: descendants keep theirs, so re-expanding restores the subtree as it was. Always emits a new array. |
| `v-model:selected-keys` | `string[]` | `[]` | `update:selectedKeys` | Ids of the selected nodes while `selectable="multiple"`, via `defineModel<string[]>('selectedKeys', { default: () => [] })`. Ordered by selection (range and select-all in visible order), without duplicates; emits only when the set changes. Disabled nodes are never added. |
| `v-model:selectedKey` | `string` | `''` | `update:selectedKey` | Id of the selected node, via `defineModel<string>('selectedKey', { default: '' })`. Written only while `selectable`; read only while `selectable` (otherwise no node is marked selected). `''` means nothing is selected. Emits only when the id changes. Single selection only; activating the selected node again does not clear it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; row `hover`, `focus-visible`, `selected`, `disabled`; parent `expanded` / `collapsed`; `loading` (Skeleton rows); `empty` (`EmptyState`).
- Precedence: `loading` → Skeleton rows, else `items` empty → `empty` slot, else the tree.
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors `loading`; `data-empty` on the root when `items` is empty and not loading.
- `data-selectable` on the root while selection is on; `data-multiple` while `selectable="multiple"`; `data-size` on the root mirrors `size` and drives every density utility through the `group/tree` variant.
- A click on a row while Shift, Ctrl or Cmd is held does not start a native text selection (the tree prevents the default of that `mousedown`), so a range or toggle selection never highlights the labels; a plain drag still selects label text for copying, and the rename field and the `actions` region are left alone.
- Lazy loading: a `lazy` node is a parent (chevron, `aria-expanded`) even with no `children`; while it is expanded and `loading`, its group renders one loading row — a Skeleton bar plus a visually hidden `role="status"` reading the locale's `tree.loadingChildren` (`Loading`) — instead of the children, and carries `aria-busy="true"`. The loading row is not a treeitem and is not part of keyboard navigation (`<testId>__loading`).
- Renaming: the label region of the node being renamed is a text field (`<testId>__rename`, `data-slot="tree-rename"`), focused with its text selected; the chevron, glyph slot and `actions` stay. One field at a time.
- `data-state="open|closed"` on each parent row and its chevron (drives the rotation); absent on leaves. The tree is not an overlay, so this is disclosure state only.
- `data-selected` on the selected row (only while `selectable`); `data-disabled` on a disabled row.
- Collapsed children are not rendered (`v-if`), so they cost nothing and are out of the accessibility tree.
- A disabled node can still be focused (arrow keys) and, if it is a parent, expanded and collapsed; it cannot be selected, renamed, or emit `item-click` / `item-double-click`.
- `data-testid`: the root falls back to `data-tree` (a consumer `data-testid` wins); parts derive from the resolved root id — `<testId>__item` on every treeitem, `<testId>__toggle` on every chevron. Each treeitem also carries `data-item-id="<item.id>"` so a test reaches one node without depending on DOM order.
- Loading renders five Skeleton rows (`variant="rectangle"`, the row height of `size`, descending widths) at top level.

## Accessibility

- Structure (WAI-ARIA tree pattern): the tree is a `<ul role="tree">` named by `ariaLabel` (or `tree.label` when it is empty), inside the root wrapper that carries `data-testid` and `$attrs`. Each node is an `<li role="treeitem">` with `aria-level` (1-based), `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset` (among its siblings), and `aria-labelledby` pointing at its label region (ids from `useId()`), so the name excludes the children and the actions. A parent carries `aria-expanded="true|false"` and, when expanded, renders its children in a nested `<ul role="group">` inside its `<li>`. Leaves carry no `aria-expanded`. A tree of more than 300 nodes renders its visible nodes as one flat list of treeitems instead (no `role="group"`; the indent guides are `role="none"` wrappers inside each row), mounted in chunks as they near the viewport: every rendered treeitem keeps `aria-level`, `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset`, so a screen reader still hears the full tree, as the WAI-ARIA tree pattern requires when not every node is in the DOM.
- Selection: while `selectable`, every treeitem carries `aria-selected="true|false"`; otherwise none does. With `selectable="multiple"` the tree carries `aria-multiselectable="true"`.
- Disabled: a disabled node carries `aria-disabled="true"`.
- Roving tabindex: exactly one treeitem has `tabindex="0"`, every other `-1`. The tab stop is the selected node when it is visible, else the last focused node when visible, else the first node. When the tab-stop node is hidden by a collapse (from the keyboard or from a `v-model:open-keys` change), the tab stop moves to its nearest visible ancestor. Clicking a row moves the tab stop and focus to it.
- Keyboard map (required, on the focused treeitem):
  - `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` — focus the next / previous visible node, without wrapping.
  - `ArrowRight` — on a collapsed parent, expand it (focus stays); on an expanded parent, focus its first child; on a leaf, nothing.
  - `ArrowLeft` — on an expanded parent, collapse it (focus stays); otherwise focus the parent node; on a top-level collapsed parent or leaf, nothing.
  - `Home` / `End` — focus the first / last visible node.
  - `Enter` / `Space` — activate the node: select it when `selectable`, then emit `item-click`; nothing on a disabled node. `Space` does not scroll the page. With `selectable="multiple"`, `Enter` selects only the node and `Space` toggles it in the selection (no `item-click`).
  - `Shift+ArrowDown` / `Shift+ArrowUp` (multiple only) — move focus and add the node reached to the selection.
  - `Ctrl+A` / `Cmd+A` (multiple only) — select every visible, enabled node.
  - `F2` (`editable` only) — open the rename field on the focused node. In the field `Enter` submits, `Escape` cancels and both return focus to the node; leaving the field submits. Tree keys are not handled inside the field.
  - Pointer, multiple only: click selects only the node, `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+click toggles it, `Shift`+click selects the visible range from the last clicked node (adding to the selection with `Ctrl`/`Cmd`).
  - `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` — leave the tree from the tab stop; the tree is one tab stop.
  - Type-ahead — a printable character focuses the next visible node whose label starts with it; characters typed within 500 ms add up to a prefix. Tests: `tree.test.ts` › moves focus to the next visible node whose label starts with the typed text.
  - `*` (expand siblings) is not part of v1.
- Row actions (WAI-ARIA treegrid pattern): when the `actions` slot is used, the tree renders as a `<div role="treegrid">` so screen readers reach each row's controls. Each node's row is the focusable `role="row"` (carrying `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-selected`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-labelledby` and the roving `tabindex`); it holds two `role="gridcell"`s: the label cell (chevron, glyph and label, `tabindex="-1"`) and the actions cell. The nesting wrappers (`li`, the children `ul`) are `role="none"`, so rows stay owned by the treegrid while the indent guide and the nested layout stay the same; the lazy loading row is a `role="row"` with `aria-busy`. Every `actions` control is parked at `tabindex="-1"` so the treegrid stays one tab stop. Keyboard map on top of the tree map:
  - On a row, `ArrowRight` expands a collapsed parent; on an expanded parent or a leaf it moves focus into the row's first cell (the label cell). `ArrowLeft` on a row behaves as in the tree.
  - In a row, `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` move between the label cell and each `actions` control; `ArrowLeft` on the label cell, or `Escape` anywhere in the row, returns focus to the row. `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` move to the same cell of the next / previous visible row. `Enter` on the label cell activates the row; `Enter` / `Space` on a control are the control's own.
  - Without the `actions` slot the tree keeps the `tree` / `treeitem` / `group` structure above.
- Chevron: a `<button type="button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true">` that toggles the parent on click (pointer affordance; keyboard expansion is ArrowRight / ArrowLeft on the treeitem). It never receives focus and is not announced.
- Visible focus: the indicator is drawn on the focused node's own row (in the treegrid, on the focused row or cell), not around its whole subtree — `focus-visible:outline-none` on the treeitem and a 1px `var(--ring-color)` border on the row's `after:` layer, inset in the row (an arbitrary variant scoped to `:focus-visible > row`); the label cell of a treegrid row takes `ring-1 ring-inset`. `var(--ring-color)` against the canvas and `var(--bg-selected)` is at least 3:1 in both themes (dark gray-500 on black 5.3:1, on gray-750 3.4:1; light gray-600 on gray-100 5.3:1, on gray-200 4.6:1), so the 1px indicator meets WCAG 2.1 1.4.11.
- Loading: the root carries `aria-busy="true"`; the Skeleton rows are `aria-hidden`, and no `role="tree"` is rendered without treeitems.
- Glyphs (`item.icon`), the chevron and the indent guide are decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`).
- The rename field is named `Rename <label>` (`tree.renameLabel`); the loading row announces `Loading` once through its polite status.
- Double-click is never the only way: `item-double-click` duplicates an action the app also offers through `item-click`, `Enter` or the row actions.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for label and description on the canvas, the hover fill and `var(--bg-selected)` in both themes; disabled text follows the disabled-token exemption.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the chevron and selection transitions; `motion-reduce:before:transition-none` on the hover layer.
- Touch target: rows are 24 / 32 / 40px tall by `size` and full width on a fine pointer, justified by row density in file trees; on a coarse pointer (`pointer-coarse:`) every row grows to 44px, and the chevron carries an invisible, `aria-hidden` hit area 44px wide (`data-slot="touch-target"`), so a folder opens from a 44 x 44 target. The whole row is the activation target, and in a tree without selection a row tap on a parent also toggles it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Tree from '@aziontech/webkit/tree'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const items = [
    {
      id: 'assets',
      label: 'assets',
      icon: 'az az-folder',
      children: [
        {
          id: 'assets/images',
          label: 'images',
          icon: 'az az-folder',
          children: [
            {
              id: 'assets/images/hero.webp',
              label: 'hero.webp',
```

<!-- components/alert.md -->

# Alert

> Use Alert for a persistent message on a console page or section (info, warning, error) — the answer for 'banner' or 'notice'. A short confirmation after an action that disappears on its own is a Toast. Inline feedback banner that communicates status, alerts, or progress. Presents a severity-marked box (a neutral box for info, a soft tint for success, warning and danger, always with default text) with a leading icon, an optional bold `title` over the copy, and message copy that may carry inline links, plus an optional secondary action button.

- Import: `import Alert from '@aziontech/webkit/alert'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A status, warning or error that belongs to a page, section or form and should stay visible in context.
- A notice with an inline link, or with one follow-up action (`actionLabel` or the `actions` slot).
- A notice that needs a short headline and a sentence of detail (`title` over the copy): "Maintenance scheduled" over the window and what changes.

## Do

- Pick `severity` by meaning. `danger` and `warning` render with `role="alert"`.
- Use `label` for plain copy and the default slot when the copy needs inline links; each link is a `Link` with `inline`.
- Set `title` when the alert says two things: what happened (the title, a few words, no end period) and what it means or what to do (the copy). A one-sentence alert needs no title. A title alone, with no copy, is allowed for a short notice that still wants the heading weight.
- Use either the built-in action (`actionLabel` with `@action`) or the `actions` slot, not both. The slot replaces the button.
- The `life` timer pauses while the pointer is over the alert or focus is inside it, and resumes with the time left when both leave, so the alert never disappears while it is being read or used. Keep `life` for `info` and `success` status messages.
- Once `closable` or `life` dismisses the message, it stays hidden until it is remounted. Listen to `close` to keep your own state in sync.
- Use `size="small"` inside dense surfaces such as cards and drawers.

## Don’t

- A transient confirmation of an action → use `toast`.
- Validation feedback under one form field → use `field-error`.
- An admonition inside documentation prose → use `doc-callout`.
- A promotional band between page sections → use `call-to-action` with `variant="announcement"`.

## Related

- `toast` — overlay stack raised imperatively, auto-dismissing and not anchored to content.
- `field-error` — field-level guidance and errors below an input.
- `doc-callout` — docs admonition rendered on the `Alert` surface.
- `empty-state` — a full zero-data block, not a status banner.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `severity` | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'info'` | false | Visual severity variant. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token. Drives the banner height, inline padding, copy scale, and the trailing control sizes. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback message copy when the default slot is empty. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Bold heading above the message copy; hidden when empty. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Azion icon class override for the leading icon. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label for the built-in secondary action button; hidden when empty. |
| `closable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, shows a close control that dismisses the message. |
| `life` | `number` | `0` | false | Duration in milliseconds before auto-dismiss; `0` disables auto-dismiss. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `MouseEvent` | Emitted when the built-in action button is clicked. |
| `close` | `(event: Event)` | Emitted when the message is dismissed, after the fade. Carries the originating event: the close button's `MouseEvent`, the `Escape` `KeyboardEvent`, or an `Event` of type `timeout` after `life` expires. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | — | Custom action control; replaces the built-in Button when provided. |
| `default` | — | Alert copy. Inline content — plain text plus anchors, which the message region styles with the `.text-link` token — or flow content such as paragraphs and a list. The copy region is a flow container (a `div`, not a `p`), so block markup arriving from a server render stays inside it instead of being closed out beside the copy. Falls back to `label` when empty. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: default (per severity)
- `data-titled` on the root mirrors a non-empty `title`: the title renders above the copy in `.text-title-sm` (`__title`), and the copy keeps its size below it. With a title and no copy (no default slot, empty `label`), only the title renders.
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/alert`. Below `@sm` of its box the action (built-in or the `actions` slot, wrapped in `[data-slot=alert-actions]`) moves to its own line under the message while the close button stays on the message line.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses inline links in the message copy, then the action and close controls when present; `Enter` follows a link, `Enter`/`Space` activates the controls; `Escape` dismisses when `closable` is true.
- ARIA: root uses `role="alert"` for danger/warning severities and `role="status"` for info/success. The title is text inside the live region, read before the copy; it is not a document heading, so it does not enter the page outline.
- Inline links are underlined, not colour-only, so they stay distinguishable against every severity surface (WCAG 1.4.1); the `.text-link` token supplies the focus outline.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the dismiss fade; nothing sets the transition inline.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Alert from '@aziontech/webkit/alert'
</script>

<template>
  <Alert
    severity="info"
    label="Your workload finished deploying in 42 seconds."
    action-label="View workload"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/alert.md](components/alert.md).

<!-- components/empty-state.md -->

# Empty State

> Centered placeholder shown when a resource list or section has no content yet. Stacks an optional standardized adornment, a title, an optional description, and a consumer-composed actions area (buttons + documentation link) to guide the user toward a first action. The adornment is a standardized, size-scaled featured-icon tile driven by the `icon` prop; the consumer may instead supply custom content via the `icon` slot, or omit both for no adornment. Unlike `Alert`, which is an inline severity banner, `EmptyState` is a full-region zero-data state and renders either inside a bordered surface card or on a plain transparent background.

- Import: `import EmptyState from '@aziontech/webkit/empty-state'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A list, table or section that has no items yet, with a first action that fills it.
- A search or filter that returned nothing, with an action to clear it.

## Do

- `title` is required. Say what is missing ("No domains yet"), not that something went wrong.
- Keep the `actions` slot to one primary action, plus an optional documentation link.
- Leave the actions at their own width, centred, on every screen size (the design sample's look). Do not add `w-full` to a button in the slot to make it span a phone screen.
- Use the `icon` prop for the standard featured-icon tile. Use the `icon` slot only for custom art, and omit both when the context already explains the state.
- Use `bordered` when the block sits directly on the page. Leave it off inside a card or panel that already has a border, and use `size="small"` there.

## Don’t

- The data is still loading → use `skeleton`.
- An inline warning or error about content that is present → use `alert`.
- The empty body of a data-driven `table` → use the `table` `empty` slot, which already renders this block by default.

## Related

- `skeleton` — the loading placeholder shown before the empty state is known.
- `alert` — inline severity banner, not a zero-data block.
- `table` — renders an empty-state block in its `empty` slot.
- `button` — the usual content of the `actions` slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | Primary heading announcing the empty resource. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting body copy below the title. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Azion icon class for the standardized adornment (e.g. `az az-inbox`). When set, renders a size-scaled featured-icon tile; when empty and the `icon` slot is unused, no adornment renders. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token (subset — only `small` and `medium`; no `large`). Scales the whole block on one harmonic ramp — the adornment size, the title and description typography, the surrounding padding, and the gaps between adornment, text, and actions all step up together. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, wraps the content in a dashed-bordered surface card; otherwise renders on a transparent background. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | — | Custom adornment centered above the title, rendered inside an `aria-hidden` container. Overrides the `icon` prop's featured-icon tile. When neither this slot nor the `icon` prop is provided, no adornment renders. |
| `actions` | — | Action area below the description; consumer composes buttons and the documentation link. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-bordered` mirrors the `bordered` prop
- Responsive: the actions keep their own width and stay centred at every box width, as the design sample draws them (a phone included); the action column is capped at `max-w-full`, so a long label wraps inside the box instead of overflowing it.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the consumer-supplied controls in the `actions` slot in DOM order; the region itself is non-interactive.
- ARIA: root uses `role="status"` so assistive tech announces the empty-data message; the `icon` slot container is `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import EmptyState from '@aziontech/webkit/empty-state'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
</script>

<template>
  <EmptyState
    title="No applications yet"
    description="Create an application to start serving your site from Azion."
    icon="az az-inbox"
  >
    <template #actions>
      <div class="flex flex-wrap justify-center gap-(--spacing-xs)">
        <Button
          variant="primary"
          label="Create application"
        />
        <Button
          variant="outline"
          label="Import from GitHub"
        />
      </div>
      <Link
        label="Docs"
        icon="az az-arrow-right"
        size="medium"
        href="#"
      />
    </template>
  </EmptyState>
</template>
```

<!-- components/error-boundary.md -->

# Error Boundary

> Guards one region of a page. When a component inside the region throws while it renders, sets up or runs a lifecycle hook, the boundary catches the error, reports it through its `error` event, and puts a recoverable message in the region's place: a danger `Alert` that says the section failed and offers **Try again**, which mounts the region again. The rest of the page keeps working. A `fallback` slot replaces the built-in message when the region needs a different shape (a card-sized `EmptyState`, for example).

- Import: `import ErrorBoundary from '@aziontech/webkit/error-boundary'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A dashboard card, a side panel, a tab body or any region whose failure should not take the whole page down.
- A region that renders data you do not control (a third-party widget, a chart fed by a remote response, a plugin).
- Around each route's content inside the app shell, so a failing page leaves the navigation usable (pass the route path as `resetKey`).
- When the app reports render errors to a monitoring service: the `error` event carries the error and where it was thrown.

## Do

- Wrap regions, not the whole app. One boundary per card, panel or route body keeps the blast radius small.
- Report every error: listen to `error` and send it to your monitoring service. The boundary stops the error from reaching the app error handler unless `propagate` is set.
- Make Retry mean something. Listen to `retry` and reset the state that broke the region (refetch, clear the bad value) before it mounts again; a retry that renders the same bad data fails again.
- Pass `resetKey` when the region shows different content for different keys (route path, record id), so moving on from a failed record clears the fallback.
- Keep the fallback the size of the region. In a card, use a small `EmptyState`; in a page body, the built-in `Alert` is right.

## Don’t

- A request that failed (a fetch, a mutation): that is data state, not a render error. Show it in the region with an `alert` and a Retry, as `state/state-form-validation` (SectionRejected) and `skills/webkit-ui-states` describe.
- A whole page that cannot be shown (missing route, no access, server failure) → use the `state/state-error-page` block.
- A field that failed validation → use `field` with its error message.
- Errors thrown in click or submit handlers you can catch yourself: catch them where you call the action and show the outcome with `toast` or `alert`.

## Related

- `alert` — the built-in fallback; also what a failed request shows inside a region that rendered fine.
- `empty-state` — a common custom fallback for a card-sized region.
- `skeleton` — what the region shows while it loads; the boundary only covers the failed case.
- `toast` — reports the outcome of an action; never use it for a region that failed to render.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Heading of the built-in fallback. Empty uses the locale catalog (`This section failed to load`). |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Sentence under the heading of the built-in fallback. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `retryLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the built-in Retry action. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Try again`). |
| `resetKey` | `string \| number` | `undefined` | false | When this value changes while the fallback shows, the region is mounted again (pass the route path or the record id). |
| `propagate` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, the error keeps travelling to the parent boundaries and the app error handler after this boundary handles it. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `error` | `ErrorBoundaryErrorEvent` | Fires once per failure with `{ error, info }`: what was thrown and Vue's description of where. Report it from here. |
| `retry` | `(event: Event)` | Fires when the region is mounted again (Retry, the slot's `retry`, or a `resetKey` change). Reset the broken state here. Carries the click event when the built-in Retry button (or a slot `retry(event)` call) triggered it, an `Event` of type `retry` when the slot calls `retry()` with no event, and an `Event` of type `reset` for a `resetKey` change. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The region the boundary guards. Mounted again, from scratch, on every retry. |
| `fallback` | { error: unknown, retry: (event?: Event) => void } | Replaces the built-in `Alert` while the region is failed. Call `retry` to mount it again; pass the click event to forward it on the `retry` event. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (the region renders), `error` (the fallback renders in its place)
- `data-error` on the root is present while the fallback shows
- A second error captured while the fallback already shows (a failing custom fallback) is not handled again: it travels to the parent, so a broken fallback can never loop.
- What the boundary catches is what Vue's `onErrorCaptured` catches from descendant components: errors in render, setup, watchers, lifecycle hooks and component event handlers. Errors thrown directly in the slot's own markup belong to the component that owns the markup, and errors in native DOM listeners or promises outside Vue are not caught.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the root is focusable only by script (`tabindex="-1"`, `outline-none`) and never in the tab order; the Retry button carries the `Button` focus ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the Retry action in the fallback; `Enter` / `Space` runs it. No key handling of its own.
- Focus: when the region fails while focus was inside it, or focus falls to the document body or sits on a control the failure disabled, focus moves to the fallback `Alert`, which is announced; with a custom `fallback` it moves to the boundary's root, so the reader lands on the custom message and its actions. After a retry from inside the boundary, focus moves to the boundary's root so it is not lost to the body.
- ARIA: the built-in fallback is an `Alert` with `role="alert"` (danger), so the failure is announced once when it appears. A custom fallback is responsible for its own announcement (`EmptyState` is `role="status"`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): inherited from the `alert` danger tokens.
- No motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the Retry action is a `Button`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import BarList from '@aziontech/webkit/bar-list'
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Card from '@aziontech/webkit/card'
  import ErrorBoundary from '@aziontech/webkit/error-boundary'
  import { useLocale } from '@aziontech/webkit/use-locale'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const items = [
    { id: 'web-app-prod', name: 'web-app-prod', value: 11420000 },
    { id: 'payments-api', name: 'payments-api', value: 6240000 },
    { id: 'storefront-checkout', name: 'storefront-checkout', value: 4910000 }
  ]

  const broken = ref(false)
  const reported = ref('')

  const { formatNumber } = useLocale()

  const format = (value) => formatNumber(value, { notation: 'compact', maximumFractionDigits: 1 })

  const failingFormat = () => {
    throw new Error('The response held a value the list could not read.')
  }

  const report = ({ error }) => {
    reported.value = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
  }

  const recover = () => {
    broken.value = false
    reported.value = ''
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-lg) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <Card title="Top services">
      <template #default>
        <ErrorBoundary
          @error="report"
          @retry="recover"
        >
          <BarList
            :items="items"
            :format-value="broken ? failingFormat : format"
            aria-label="Top services by requests"
          />
        </ErrorBoundary>
      </template>
    </Card>
    <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-(--spacing-xs)">
      <Button
        label="Simulate a failure"
        variant="outline"
        size="medium"
        :disabled="broken"
        @click="broken = true"
      />
      <p
        v-if="reported"
        class="m-0 text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
      >
        Reported: {{ reported }}
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/error-boundary.md](components/error-boundary.md).

<!-- components/outcome-icon.md -->

# Outcome Icon

> Use OutcomeIcon for the bare round glyph that says how one run ended, with no label; with a label, the state of a resource is a StatusIndicator. A small round mark that states how something ended: a check for success, a cross for danger, an exclamation for warning and a dash for neutral (not set, not run). With `animated` the disc scales in and the glyph draws itself when the mark appears and every time its severity changes, so an outcome screen or a finished row can mark the moment a run lands; under reduced motion it shows at once.

- Import: `import OutcomeIcon from '@aziontech/webkit/outcome-icon'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- At the head of an outcome screen (deploy succeeded or failed), at the large size, animated.
- In a checklist of finished items, at the small size, to say one is done or not set.
- Beside a label that reports a finished run, when the run's state turns from running to an outcome.

## Do

- Pair the mark with words that say the same thing; the mark is not the only cue.
- Animate only the mark that just changed; a list of animated marks on load is noise.
- Give a specific `ariaLabel` (`Deployed`, `Done`) when the catalog name is too generic.

## Don’t

- A state that is still running → use `spinner` or `status-indicator` with `loading`.
- Steps that can still be running, or a static icon → an `az-circle-*` icon in `-mark`.
- A labelled status pill in a table cell → use `tag` or `status-indicator`.
- A message with text and actions → use `alert` or `toast`.

## Related

- `status-indicator` — a coloured dot with a label, for live states.
- `tag` — a labelled pill for a state.
- `toast` — reports the outcome of an async action wherever the user is.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `severity` | `'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'neutral'` | `'success'` | false | The outcome the mark shows: a check, a cross, an exclamation or a dash. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token: 16, 20 or 48 px. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Scales the disc in and draws the glyph when it appears or its severity changes; static under reduced motion. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name. Empty uses the locale catalog name of the severity. |

## States

- `data-severity`: `success` | `danger` | `warning` | `neutral`; `data-size`: `small` | `medium` | `large`
- `data-state`: `pending` (disc scaled down and transparent, glyph undrawn) | `settled`; a static mark is always `settled`
- `data-animated` mirrors the `animated` prop

## Accessibility

- Not focusable; no keyboard map.
- ARIA: the root `svg` is `role="img"` named by `ariaLabel` or the catalog name of the severity.
- The shape of the glyph tells the outcomes apart without colour (WCAG 1.4.1); the disc is a mark-weight status colour (`--*-mark`) that meets 3:1 and APCA Lc 45 on every surface, and the glyph (`--text-contrast`) meets the same against the disc, in both themes (WCAG 1.4.11; `packages/theme/test/status-mark-role.test.mjs`).
- Motion is decorative and skipped under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import OutcomeIcon from '@aziontech/webkit/outcome-icon'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-(--spacing-lg)">
    <OutcomeIcon severity="success" />
    <OutcomeIcon severity="danger" />
    <OutcomeIcon severity="warning" />
    <OutcomeIcon severity="neutral" />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/outcome-icon.md](components/outcome-icon.md).
