<!-- components/progress.md -->

# Progress

> Use Progress when the work has a measurable amount (value/max), or for a long task with no layout to reserve (indeterminate). A region with a known shape loads with Skeleton, an inline busy mark is a Spinner, and a background file transfer is an UploadProgress. Communicates the progress of an ongoing task as a horizontal bar. Use it for a determinate value within a range (`value` / `max`) or, when progress can't be measured, as an indeterminate loading indicator. Unlike `skeleton` (placeholder geometry) or `status-indicator` (discrete state), it expresses a continuous quantity.

- Import: `import Progress from '@aziontech/webkit/progress'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A task with measurable progress: an upload, a build, a multi-step import.
- A bar-shaped busy indicator at the top of a region when progress can't be measured (`indeterminate`).

## Do

- Pass `value` on the scale of `max`, for example `:value="3" :max="5"` for steps. Don't convert it to a percentage yourself.
- Switch to `indeterminate` when progress is unknown. `value` is then ignored and `aria-valuenow` is dropped.
- There is no label prop. Give the bar an accessible name with an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` attribute, and show the percentage in text next to it if users need the number.
- Set `severity` when the bar reports a status that is good or bad, such as a goal that is on track (`success`), at risk (`warning`) or off track (`danger`), so the fill agrees with the status tag next to it. Without it the fill is the brand orange, which is not a status colour.
- The default is the `medium` bar with `flat` corners. Set `size="small"` for a thin inline strip (table rows, upload rows, the top of a region); use `variant="rounded"` and a larger `size` only when the bar stands alone.

## Don’t

- A placeholder for content that is still loading → use `skeleton`.
- A busy state inside a button or another compact control → use `spinner` (or the control's own `loading` prop).
- A discrete state with no quantity, such as Active or Failed → use `status-indicator`.

## Related

- `skeleton` — reserves the layout of loading content instead of showing task progress.
- `spinner` — compact, always-indeterminate busy glyph.
- `status-indicator` — labelled dot for a settled or transitional state.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | `0` | false | Current progress, relative to `max`. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | false | Upper bound; percentage = `value / max * 100`. |
| `variant` | ``ProgressVariant` (`'rounded' \| 'flat'`)` | `'flat'` | false | Track and fill corner-radius variant. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Bar height token. |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Loading state; animates a sliding segment and ignores `value`. |
| `severity` | ``ProgressSeverity` (`'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'`)` | `—` | false | Status colour of the fill; unset keeps the brand fill. The values are the shared `Severity` scale. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `indeterminate`
- `data-variant` mirrors `variant`: `rounded` | `flat`.
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop: `small` | `medium` | `large`
- `data-indeterminate` is present while `indeterminate` is `true`
- `data-severity` mirrors the `severity` prop when it is set (`neutral` | `info` | `success` | `warning` | `danger`), on the root and the fill.

## Accessibility

- Non-interactive: the bar is not focusable and takes no keyboard input.
- Name: the bar takes `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` from the consumer; with neither it is named by the locale catalog (`progress.label`, "Progress"), so a bare bar never fails `aria-progressbar-name`.
- ARIA: root uses `role="progressbar"`. Determinate sets `aria-valuemin="0"`, `aria-valuemax="<max>"`, `aria-valuenow="<value>"`; indeterminate omits `aria-valuenow` and sets `aria-busy="true"`.
- Contrast ≥3:1 between the fill (`var(--primary)`) and the track (`var(--bg-placeholder)`). The track is an alpha overlay, not an opaque surface, so it keeps that contrast on any background the bar is placed over (canvas, surface, raised, overlay).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the determinate width morph and `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the indeterminate animation (under reduced motion it holds a still segment over the middle third of the track, never a full bar, so an unfinished task never reads as done).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Progress from '@aziontech/webkit/progress'
</script>

<template>
  <Progress
    :value="60"
    aria-label="Uploading site-assets.zip"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/progress.md](components/progress.md).

<!-- components/skeleton.md -->

# Skeleton

> Use Skeleton when a region with a known shape (text, table rows, cards, avatars) is still loading — the default answer to 'show a loading state'. For an inline busy mark use Spinner, for work with a measurable amount use Progress, and for a generative AI answer use ResponseLoading. A loading placeholder that reserves the space of content while it loads, gently pulsing to signal activity. Use it in place of text lines, media, or avatars during fetches; unlike `status-indicator` (which communicates a settled state) the skeleton is a transient, decorative stand-in. Two geometries cover the common cases: a rounded rectangular block (`rectangle`) and a `circle` (for avatars / icons).

- Import: `import Skeleton from '@aziontech/webkit/skeleton'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Content is loading and its final layout is known: text lines, cards, media blocks.
- Avatar and icon placeholders, with `variant="circle"`.

## Do

- Size each skeleton like the content it stands in for (`width`, `height`) so nothing shifts when the data arrives.
- For `variant="circle"`, set `width` and `height` to the same value.
- The skeleton is `aria-hidden`. Mark the container you own with `aria-busy="true"` while it loads.
- Keep `animated` on (the default). The shimmer already turns off under reduced motion; use `:animated="false"` only for static captures.

## Don’t

- The duration is unknown and no layout is reserved → use `progress` with `indeterminate`, or `spinner`.
- Rows in a data-driven `table` → use the `table` `loading` prop, which renders aligned skeleton rows.
- Loading finished with no data → use `empty-state`.
- A settled state such as Active or Failed → use `status-indicator`.

## Related

- `progress` — measured or indeterminate progress of a task, not a placeholder.
- `spinner` — compact busy glyph for buttons and inline status.
- `empty-state` — what replaces the skeleton when the request returns nothing.
- `table` — its `loading` prop renders skeleton rows for you.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'rectangle' \| 'circle'` | `'rectangle'` | false | Geometry: a rounded rectangular block (`rectangle`) or a circle. |
| `width` | `string` | `'100%'` | false | CSS width (any length); a rectangle never grows past its container. |
| `height` | `string` | `'1rem'` | false | CSS height (any length); for a circle, set equal to `width`. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shimmer while loading; suppressed under reduced motion. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (a single decorative placeholder; no hover/focus/active — it is not interactive)
- `data-variant` mirrors `variant` (`rectangle` | `circle`)
- `data-animated` is present when `animated` is true (drives the shimmer)

## Accessibility

- The skeleton is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"` so assistive tech skips it. The loading status is conveyed by the surrounding region (e.g. `aria-busy="true"` on the container the consumer owns), not by the placeholder itself.
- Not focusable, not interactive: no keyboard map, no focus ring.
- The shimmer is gated behind `motion-safe:` and `motion-reduce:animate-none` suppresses it for users who prefer reduced motion (static flat fill).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Skeleton from '@aziontech/webkit/skeleton'
</script>

<template>
  <Skeleton
    variant="rectangle"
    width="240px"
    height="100px"
    animated
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/skeleton.md](components/skeleton.md).

<!-- components/spinner.md -->

# Spinner

> Use Spinner only for an inline busy mark in a row, log line or custom control that has no loading prop; buttons use their own `loading`, a loading region with a known shape uses Skeleton, and measurable work uses Progress. A small rotating mark that says work is in progress, for a row, a log line or a custom control that has no loading state of its own. It is decorative by default; with an `aria-label` it becomes a `status` region that announces the work, and it stops rotating under reduced motion.

- Import: `import Spinner from '@aziontech/webkit/spinner'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- An inline busy mark inside a row, log line or custom control that has no loading state of its own.
- A small in-progress indicator next to text in a toast or status row.

## Do

- Its one prop is `ariaLabel`: size it with a `size-*` class (`size-3`, `size-4`) and color it through the inherited text color (it strokes `currentColor`).
- `class` on its tag is its sizing API, not a restyle: the spec is a `style_seam`, so `webkit/no-style-override` accepts `<Spinner class="size-4" />`. Keep the class to a `size-*` and, when it must differ from the surrounding text, a text color token.
- Without `ariaLabel` it is `aria-hidden`: announce the busy state on the surrounding element (`aria-busy`, a live region or visible text). A standalone Spinner that is the only sign of the wait sets `ariaLabel` (`aria-label="Loading"`); it then renders `role="status"` with that name, so the wait is announced. Do not set it inside a control that already announces its own busy state (a `loading` button).
- The spin stops under reduced motion, so pair it with text when the wait matters.

## Don’t

- A button waiting on its action → set `loading` on `button`, `icon-button` or `highlight-button`.
- Content that is still loading → use `skeleton`.
- Progress you can measure → use `progress`.
- A status with a color and a label → use `status-indicator`.
- Built to be personalized (style seam): any class is accepted on the tag.

## Related

- `skeleton` — reserves the shape of content while it loads.
- `progress` — determinate progress.
- `button` — renders a Spinner itself when `loading` is set.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name; when set the spinner renders role status with this name, otherwise it stays aria-hidden. Size and color come through `class`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: `aria-hidden="true"` by default (decorative, the surrounding element announces the wait); with `ariaLabel` set, `role="status"` and `aria-label` instead. Not focusable.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Spinner from '@aziontech/webkit/spinner'
</script>

<template>
  <Spinner class="size-4 text-(--text-default)" />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/spinner.md](components/spinner.md).

<!-- components/status-indicator.md -->

# Status Indicator

> Use StatusIndicator for the current state of one resource (Active, Failed, Deploying) in a table column or detail header — the default answer for 'status'. A category or outcome word is a Tag, a number is a Badge, a level on the critical → info scale is a SeverityTag, and an HTTP code is a StatusCode. Shows the settled or transitional state of one resource as a colored dot (or a spinner while `loading`) beside a short label: Active, Failed, Paused, Deploying. It is the status column of tables and lists and the status line of a detail header, so it is static text, not a live region.

- Import: `import StatusIndicator from '@aziontech/webkit/status-indicator'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The state of a resource in a table cell, a list row or a detail header: Active, Failed, Paused.
- A transitional state such as Deploying or Propagating, with `loading`.

## Do

- Always pass `label`. The default is the literal `'Status'`, and the color alone does not carry the meaning.
- Map `severity` to meaning and keep it consistent across the app: `success`, `info`, `warning` and `danger` follow their tokens and `neutral` is muted.
- With `loading`, pass the bare verb (`"Deploying"`). The component appends the ellipsis character (`…`, not three periods) and swaps the dot for a spinner. A label that already ends in `…` or `...` (copy pasted from a design: `"Building..."`) is trimmed first, so it renders `Building…`, never `Building......`.
- It is a non-interactive element with no role, no click and no keyboard behavior. Don't attach handlers to it. When a status change must be announced (a single deploy you are watching), announce it through a toast or a live region the page owns, not by making every indicator live.

## Don’t

- A count or a very short label attached to another element → use `badge`.
- A category or status chip with an optional icon → use `tag`.
- A page or section notice with copy and actions → use `alert`.
- Measurable progress → use `progress`.

## Related

- `badge` — filled count indicator, usually overlaid on an icon or avatar.
- `tag` — labelled chip for categories and statuses.
- `spinner` — replaces the dot while `loading` is true.
- `progress` — continuous progress instead of a discrete state.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `severity` | ``Severity` (`'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'`)` | `'success'` | false | Severity token driving the status dot color. `Severity` is the shared status scale, exported from this component (and from `badge` and `tag`). |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Transitional state: a spinner replaces the dot and the label gains a trailing ellipsis (`…`), so pass the bare verb; a trailing `…` or `...` already in the label is not doubled. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible label text. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Status`). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- Narrow container: the indicator shrinks to its container and the label ends in an ellipsis instead of overflowing.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: no role on the root. It is plain text (the dot is `aria-hidden`; the label carries the meaning), because a table of 1k rows would otherwise hold 1k live regions and announce every change. `aria-busy="true"` while `loading`. Tests: `src/test/live-regions.test.ts`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.
- Forced colors: the dot opts out of forced colour adjustment and paints `CanvasText`, so it stays visible when backgrounds are forced to `Canvas`; the severity is still carried by the label text, never by the dot's colour alone. Tests: `src/test/forced-colors.test.ts`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import StatusIndicator from '@aziontech/webkit/status-indicator'
</script>

<template>
  <StatusIndicator
    severity="success"
    label="Healthy"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/status-indicator.md](components/status-indicator.md).

<!-- components/toast.md -->

# Toast

> Use Toast for a short confirmation after an action that disappears on its own; a persistent message on a page or section (a banner, a notice) is an Alert. A transient, non-blocking notification system: mount the `<Toaster>` region **once** near the application root, then raise notifications imperatively from anywhere via the exported `toast()` function (`toast('Saved')`) and its type shortcuts (`toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.info`, `toast.warning`, `toast.loading`, `toast.progress`, `toast.promise`, `toast.dismiss`). Each notification is a self-dismissing card that stacks in a corner, animates in and out, and is announced to assistive technology — without stealing focus. Unlike the sibling `Alert`, which is an **inline** banner the consumer places in the document flow and controls with `v-model`-style props, Toast is a **transient overlay** stack driven by an imperative call and a shared reactive store, so the call site needs no local visibility state and no markup of its own. The card surface, typography, and severity icons follow the Figma design (see `figma` in the frontmatter). The interaction model follows the established mount-once toast pattern (a single anchored region + imperative trigger + auto-dismiss stack that groups collapsed and expands on hover), built on our tokens, our semantic animation utilities, and our composition/compound-API conventions per [`contributing/rules/migration.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/contributing/rules/migration.md); nothing is inherited from any external library. Each severity tints only its leading **icon** via the matching `-contrast` token (`var(--success-foreground)` / `var(--warning-foreground)` / `var(--danger-foreground)` / `var(--info-foreground)`) over the shared `var(--bg-surface-raised)` surface.

- Import: `import ToastRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/toast-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Toast from '@aziontech/webkit/toast'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## Setup

One-time app-level wiring before the first toast() call — service (recommended): import { ToastPlugin } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast' and chain .use(ToastPlugin) onto createApp() in the app entry; the plugin mounts the toast region automatically. Alternative: mount a Toaster component once near the app root. `webkit doctor` flags toast usage with no wired region.

## When to use

- Confirming the result of an action that finished out of view or in the background: saved, deployed, copied.
- Following an async operation from start to finish with `toast.promise`, or `toast.loading` plus a dismiss by id.
- Following an operation whose completion is known (an upload, an import, a migration) with `toast.progress`: a bar and its percentage, updated in place by id, with a Cancel action.
- A short notice that is not tied to one place on the page and can disappear on its own.

## Do

- Mount `Toaster` once at the app root (in `App.vue`, before the layout or `RouterView`), or install `ToastPlugin`. Never render a `Toaster` in a page, a view or a page-body block: only the first `Toaster` to mount is active and it gives the role up when it unmounts, so a page's copy is either inert or, when it mounted first, silences every toast in the app once the user leaves that page. A page only imports `toast`. A full page routed outside the console layout is still a route of the same app, not a root. `check:blocks` fails a block outside `blocks/shells/` that renders one.
- Leave the stack at the default `bottom-end` corner (bottom right in a left-to-right page, bottom left in right-to-left). It is the corner a reader reaches last, so a toast never covers the page title, the navigation, the primary action or the text being read, and every Azion app, the docs site included, puts toasts in the same place so the user learns where to look. Don't set `position` on the `Toaster` or the plugin to move the whole stack; a single toast may take another corner only when it must sit next to what it reports.
- Use the typed shortcuts (`toast.success`, `toast.error`, …). The type sets the icon and how it is announced: `toast.error` (severity `danger`) interrupts the screen reader through the Toaster's assertive live region, every other type waits its turn in the polite one. Both regions are fixed, so no region ever switches between polite and assertive (switching made screen readers drop or repeat the stack).
- Keep the message text to one line and move detail to `description`. Offer at most two actions: one `action`, or `actions` with two entries when a failure has two ways forward (**Edit** and **Redeploy**).
- A toast with an `action` (or `actions`) stays at least 10 s unless it sets its own `duration`, so a keyboard or screen-reader user has time to reach the action.
- `duration: 0` keeps a toast until it is dismissed. Keep the returned id and call `toast.dismiss(id)`, or pass the same `id` to update the toast in place.
- Use `toast.progress(message, value, { id })` when the percentage is known; keep calling it with the same `id` as the value moves (the card updates in place, no new announcement per step), and finish with `toast.success` or `toast.error` on that `id`. Use `toast.loading` when it is not known. Give a long operation a Cancel `action`.
- Don't make a toast the only path to an important action. It auto-dismisses and never takes focus.

## Don’t

- The message must stay visible next to the content it concerns → use `alert`.
- The user must decide something before continuing → use `dialog`.
- Validation feedback for a single field → use `field-error`.

## Related

- `alert` — inline severity banner placed in the page flow; it stays until it is closed.
- `dialog` — blocking modal for decisions and confirmations.
- `spinner` — rendered while a toast is `loading`.
- `progress` — rendered under the copy of a `toast.progress` toast.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `'top-start' \| 'top-center' \| 'top-end' \| 'bottom-start' \| 'bottom-center' \| 'bottom-end'` | `'bottom-end'` | false | Corner (or edge-center) the stack is anchored to; `start` and `end` follow the reading direction. |
| `duration` | `number` | `4000` | false | Default auto-dismiss time in ms each toast inherits; a per-toast `duration` overrides it, and `0` keeps the toast until dismissed. |
| `max` | `number` | `3` | false | Maximum simultaneously visible toasts per corner before the rest queue behind. |
| `expand` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Lay the stack out fully expanded with a gap; when `false` the resting stack overlaps into a peek. |
| `closable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Show an always-visible close control on every toast; a per-toast `closable` option overrides it. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | { toast, dismiss } | Optional override for a single toast's body. `toast` is the store entry (`{ id, severity, loading?, message, description?, action?, actions?, duration, progress? }`); `dismiss` dismisses that entry. When omitted, the `Toaster` composes `ToastItem` + `Title`/`Description`/`Action`/`Close` from the entry, rendering one `Action` per entry of `actions` (the first two) or the single `action`, and a `Progress` row when the entry has `progress`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/toast-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/toast-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/toast-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/toast-action`
- `@aziontech/webkit/toast-close`

## Sub-components

- `toast.vue` — the mount-once region, at the component root.
- `toast-item/toast-item.vue` — a single notification card (outer flex row, `items-center` so the content and its `trailing` action/close share one centered line; the leading icon and the content column sit in an inner…
- `toast-title/toast-title.vue` — the primary line of a toast (`text-body-xs` `var(--text-default)`).
- `toast-description/toast-description.vue` — the supporting line below the title (`text-body-xs` `var(--text-muted)`).
- `toast-action/toast-action.vue` — the inline action control, rendered as the webkit `Button` (`variant="ghost"`, `size="small"`).
- `toast-close/toast-close.vue` — the dismiss control, rendered as the webkit `IconButton` (`az az-x`, `variant="ghost"`, `size="small"`, `aria-label="Close notification"`).

The imperative API is backed by a small reactive store composable, declared here (undeclared composables are forbidden):

- `composables/use-toast-store.ts` — a singleton reactive store (one module-level reactive list of toast entries) exposing `add(entry)`, `update(id, patch)`, `dismiss(id?)`, and the reactive `toasts` list.

## States

- `data-severity` on `ToastItem` (and mirrored on the `Toaster`'s items): `neutral` | `info` | `success` | `warning` | `danger`. Drives the leading icon and its severity color (the `-foreground` icon token).
- `data-loading` on `ToastItem` while the toast is `loading` (`toast.loading`, a pending `toast.promise`); the spinner replaces the icon.
- `toast.error()` keeps its Sonner-style name and raises a `danger` toast.
- `data-removing` on a `Toaster` item while its exit transition runs (switches the transition to the exit token).
- Progress: an entry with `progress` (set by `toast.progress(message, value, options?)`, which defaults `duration` to `0`) renders `__progress` under the copy: a rounded `Progress` bar named by the toast message (`role="progressbar"`, `aria-valuenow` clamped to 0–100) and the percentage formatted with `Intl.NumberFormat` (`style: 'percent'`) in the provider's locale, `aria-hidden` so the region does not announce every step. A later call with the same `id` replaces the entry in place; a typed toast with that `id` drops the bar.
- `data-position` on the `Toaster` container: one of the six `position` values; drives the fixed anchoring (`top`/`bottom` × `start`/`center`/`end`, where `start` is the left edge under `ltr` and the right edge under `rtl`) and the enter/leave translate direction.
- Safe areas: every inset is `max(var(--spacing-md), env(safe-area-inset-<edge>))`, so on a phone with a notch or a home indicator (`viewport-fit=cover`) the stack stays clear of the status bar, the indicator and a landscape notch.
- Bottom offset: a `bottom-*` region sits that inset above the viewport bottom plus `--toast-offset-bottom` (set by the app for its own bottom chrome) plus `--save-bar-height` (published by a mounted `SaveBar`), so a toast never covers either. Test: `src/test/save-bar-toast.test.ts`.
- `data-state="open|closed"` on each `Toaster` region: `open` while the stack is laid out expanded (the `expand` prop, hover or focus), `closed` while it overlaps into a peek.
- The dismiss control (`ToastClose`) renders, and is **always visible**, only when `closable` is set — the per-toast `closable` option, or the Toaster's `closable` default (the per-toast option overrides). When unset, no close control is shown.
- Announcements go through the two hidden live regions: `danger` to `__live-assertive`, every other severity to `__live-polite`; items inside a Toaster carry no role of their own and the visible regions are not live, so each toast is announced once and never twice. A `ToastItem` rendered outside a Toaster keeps `role="status"` (or `role="alert"` for `danger`). Focus is never stolen (the region is not focused on mount). Tests: `toast.test.ts` › live region (spec), Escape dismisses the focused toast.
- Visual states on interactive controls (`ToastAction`, `ToastClose`): `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active` (inherited from `Button` / `IconButton`).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-1` on the action and close controls (inherited from `Button` / `IconButton`).
- Keyboard map: `Alt+T` (the Sonner hotkey, matched on `event.code` so it works on every layout) moves focus to the front toast's first control (its action, else its close control, else the card itself); `Escape` while focus is inside a toast dismisses that toast and returns focus to the control that had it before `Alt+T`; `Tab` reaches the action then the close control of each visible toast; `Enter`/`Space` activates them. The region itself is not a focus trap and is not focused on mount, so toasts never steal focus from the current task.
- Timing (WCAG 2.2.1): auto-dismiss pauses while the pointer is over a region **and** while focus is inside it, and resumes when both leave; a toast with an action stays at least 10 s unless it sets its own `duration`.
- ARIA: `danger` toasts are announced assertively (`__live-assertive`, `role="alert"`), every other severity politely (`__live-polite`, `role="status"`); items inside a Toaster have no role (a standalone `ToastItem` is `role="status"`, or `role="alert"` for `danger`); the close control has an `aria-label`; the severity icon is `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the muted description text and severity icons.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the enter/leave fades and `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the move transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the action and close controls (from `Button` / `IconButton` `size="small"`).
- Progress: the bar is a `progressbar` named by the toast message; only the toast's arrival is announced, not each percentage step (the visible percentage is `aria-hidden`; the bar's value is read when the user reaches it).
- Teleported content: each teleported toaster region binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `ConfigProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import { toast, Toaster } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast'

  const show = () =>
    toast('Application deleted', {
      description: 'acme-store was removed from your account.',
      action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => {} }
    })
</script>

<template>
  <Toaster position="bottom-end" />
  <Button
    label="Delete application"
    variant="outline"
    @click="show"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/upload-progress.md -->

# Upload Progress

> Use UploadProgress for a floating card that tracks a background transfer while the person keeps working; the files picked in a form field are a FileTokenGroup, and one measurable task in place is a Progress. A card that follows a file transfer to its end while the person keeps working: uploading files into a bucket, moving objects between folders or deleting them. Its header says what is happening and how far it got (`Uploading 2 of 5 files`) over one overall bar; below it each file has its own bar, its state and a Cancel or Retry button. When every file has finished the header turns into the outcome (`5 files uploaded`, or `4 files uploaded, 1 failed` with Retry failed) and the card can be closed. It floats at the inline-end bottom corner by default, so it survives route changes in the console shell. Taken from the Console Kit's object storage progress card, extended with the per-file list the design sample's bucket browser needs.

- Import: `import UploadProgress from '@aziontech/webkit/upload-progress'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A bucket upload that keeps running after the upload dialog closes.
- A move or delete of many objects that takes more than a second or two.
- Any batch of file transfers where the person should be able to cancel one file, or retry the ones that failed.

## Do

- Keep the card until the person closes it when anything failed; close it yourself a few seconds after a clean finish if you like.
- Send `error` as the reason (`Connection lost`, `Larger than 300 MB`), not a status code.
- Update `progress` no more than a few times a second; the bars animate between values.
- Report the outcome with a toast only when the card is not in view (for example, after the person collapsed it and left the page).

## Don’t

- The files picked in a form before it is submitted → use `file-token-group`.
- A single action with no per-file parts (a deploy, a build) → use the async-submit toast (`toast` with Edit and Redeploy).
- Progress of a page load or a determinate step inside a form → use `progress`.

## Related

- `file-token-group` — the files picked for upload, before the transfer starts.
- `progress` — the bar used for the overall and per-file progress.
- `toast` — reports the outcome of a single async action.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `UploadProgressItem[]` | `[]` | false | The files in the transfer, in order, with their state and progress. |
| `operation` | `'upload' \| 'move' \| 'delete'` | `'upload'` | false | What the transfer does; picks the header wording and the glyph. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Overrides the header text. Empty builds it from the operation and the counts. |
| `floating` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Fixes the card to the inline-end bottom corner of the viewport; false renders it in the flow. |
| `cancelable` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows Cancel on running and waiting files and Cancel all in the header. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cancel` | `(event: MouseEvent, id?: string)` | Cancel on one file (its `id`) or Cancel all (no `id`). The parent stops the transfer. |
| `retry` | `(event: MouseEvent, id?: string)` | Retry on one failed file (its `id`) or Retry failed (no `id`). |
| `close` | `(event: MouseEvent)` | Close was pressed; offered only once every file has finished. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | — | Buttons for the finished transfer beside Close (for example `Open folder`). Shown when done. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` (resolves to `true`) | `update:open` | Shows the file list; `false` hides it and keeps the header and overall bar. While it is unbound the card starts open. |

## States

- Root `data-status`: `running` (some file pending or running) | `success` (all finished, none failed) | `error` (all finished, at least one error).
- Root `data-floating` when floating; `data-state="open|closed"` for the file list.
- Row `data-status`: `pending` | `running` | `success` | `error` | `canceled`.

## Accessibility

- The card is a `section` named by the catalog (`File transfers`), a region landmark that screen-reader users can jump to.
- The header text is mirrored in a visually hidden `role="status"` region (polite), so each file finishing and the final outcome are announced; percentages are not announced.
- The overall bar is a `progressbar` named by the header text; each row bar is named `<file> progress`.
- Keyboard map: Tab reaches the collapse toggle (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` the list), Cancel all or Retry failed and Close, then each row's Cancel or Retry. After Close the card unmounts in the parent; the parent returns focus to the control that started the transfer.
- State is never colour alone: rows carry a status word (`Waiting`, `Done`, `Canceled`) or the error text, and an `OutcomeIcon` in the header when finished.
- Contrast: text ≥ 4.5:1 on `--bg-surface-raised` in both themes.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import UploadProgress from '@aziontech/webkit/upload-progress'
  import { onBeforeUnmount, ref } from 'vue'

  const initial = () => [
    { id: 'logo', name: 'logo.svg', size: 4210, status: 'success' },
    { id: 'app', name: 'app.js', size: 248_320, status: 'running', progress: 64 },
    { id: 'styles', name: 'styles.css', size: 52_100, status: 'running' },
    { id: 'hero', name: 'hero.webp', size: 1_482_000, status: 'pending' }
  ]

  const items = ref(initial())
  let timer = 0

  const tick = () => {
    let started = false
    items.value = items.value.map((item) => {
      if (item.status === 'running') {
        const progress = Math.min(100, (item.progress ?? 0) + 18)
        return progress >= 100 ? { ...item, status: 'success', progress } : { ...item, progress }
      }
      if (item.status === 'pending' && !started) {
        started = true
        return { ...item, status: 'running', progress: 0 }
      }
      return item
    })
    if (items.value.every((item) => item.status !== 'running' && item.status !== 'pending')) {
      clearInterval(timer)
    }
  }

  const start = () => {
    clearInterval(timer)
    items.value = initial()
    timer = setInterval(tick, 600)
  }

  const cancel = (id) => {
    items.value = items.value.map((item) =>
      (id === undefined || item.id === id) &&
      (item.status === 'running' || item.status === 'pending')
        ? { ...item, status: 'canceled' }
        : item
    )
  }

  onBeforeUnmount(() => clearInterval(timer))
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-xs) flex-col items-start gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <Button
      label="Start upload"
      variant="secondary"
      size="medium"
      icon="az az-upload"
      @click="start"
    />
    <UploadProgress
      :items="items"
      :floating="false"
      @cancel="(_event, id) => cancel(id)"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/upload-progress.md](components/upload-progress.md).

# Attribute Editor

> An editable list of rows with the same fields, after Cloudscape's attribute editor: key and value pairs (environment variables, headers, metadata) or any set of columns given by a `definition`. It owns the row anatomy every hand-built editor repeats: a label per cell, one control per cell, a per-cell error under the field, Add and Remove, an item limit, the empty text, focus after add and remove, and a polite announcement of each change. A grouped mode lays rows out as AND groups joined by OR, the shape of rule criteria. With `reorderable`, rows (and groups) carry a grip and Move up / Move down buttons, so the order itself is part of the value, as in rule criteria evaluated top to bottom. It edits an array and validates nothing itself: the consumer passes `errors`.

- Import: `import AttributeEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/attribute-editor'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use AttributeEditor for a short list of same-field rows the person adds and removes inside a form (environment variables, headers). For key/value tags on a resource use TagEditor; to edit many cells of many records in place, spreadsheet-style, use DataGrid; for read-and-act lists use Table.
- Users add, edit and remove a variable number of pairs or tuples: environment variables, request headers, query arguments, labels, metadata.
- Rule criteria: conditions inside a group must all match (and), groups are alternatives (or).
- A bulk form where each row has the same two to four fields and a row-level error can occur.
- An ordered list of rows where the order matters (criteria evaluated top to bottom, header precedence): turn on `reorderable`.

## Do

- Keep two to four columns; more columns belong in a drawer per row.
- Pass `errors` only after the first Save (rule of the form-validation block), then keep them live while the user fixes the rows.
- Use `minItems: 1` when the form needs at least one row, so the last row keeps its fields and loses its Remove.
- Set `limit` when the backend has one; the component says how many rows are left and disables Add at the limit.
- Replace a cell's control through `cell-<key>` (a `Select` for an operator, a `Switch` for secret) instead of drawing rows by hand; use `row` only when the row needs a layout of its own.
- Type the rows with your own interface (`ref<Header[]>`): `value` in `cell-<key>` and `item` in every slot then carry the field types, so a `Select` or `Switch` binds `value` without `as string` / `as boolean`.
- Name the editor (`ariaLabel`) after what the rows are: "Environment variables", "Request headers".
- Turn on `reorderable` only when the order changes behavior; an unordered list (environment variables) stays without grips.

## Don’t

- Key and value tags with limits, reserved prefixes and removal of saved tags → use `tag-editor`, which is built on this component.
- A fixed set of named settings on one resource → use `field` controls in a form.
- Many records the user browses, filters and acts on → use `data-table` with row actions.
- Many cells of many records edited in place, spreadsheet-style → use `data-grid`.
- An ordered list of actions whose argument fields change per type → compose it by hand as in the behaviors of the `edit/edit-rule-builder` block.

## Related

- `tag-editor` — key and value tags with limits and validation, on top of AttributeEditor.
- `field` — every cell is a `Field` with its label, control and error.
- `input` — the default control of a cell; any control can replace it through `cell-<key>`.
- `button`, `icon-button` — Add and Remove.
- `separator` — the "or" between groups in grouped mode.
- `edit/edit-rule-builder` (block) — its criteria are this component in grouped mode (AND rows inside a group, OR between groups), with a `Combobox` variable cell.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `definition` | `AttributeEditorColumn[]` | `[]` | false | Columns of every row: key of the item field, label, placeholder, required. |
| `errors` | `AttributeEditorErrors` | `[]` | false | Error per cell, aligned with the rows (nested per group in grouped mode). Empty shows none. |
| `addButtonLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the Add button. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `removeButtonLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the Remove button, followed by the row number. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `addGroupLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the Add group button in grouped mode. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Text shown when there are no rows. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `limit` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Most rows allowed (per group in grouped mode); Add is disabled at the limit and the rows left are announced. |
| `groupLimit` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Most groups allowed in grouped mode. |
| `minItems` | `number` | `0` | false | Fewest rows kept; rows at the minimum lose their Remove button. |
| `newItem` | `() => TItem` | `undefined` | false | Builds a new row. Unset creates an item with an empty string per column key. |
| `itemRemovable` | `(item: TItem) => boolean` | `undefined` | false | Hides Remove on the rows it returns false for. Unset makes every row removable. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size of the default controls and the Remove button, on the 28 / 32 / 40 rhythm. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables every control, Add and Remove. |
| `addDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables Add only, for example until the last row is filled in. |
| `reorderable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a grip and Move up / Move down on every row (and every group in grouped mode) when there is more than one; rows move by dragging the grip, with the buttons, with Arrow Up / Arrow Down on the grip or Alt+Arrow Up / Alt+Arrow Down anywhere in the row. The new order goes out through v-model. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list of rows. |
| `items` | `TItem[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:items`). |
| `groups` | `TItem[][] \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:groups`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add` | `(event: MouseEvent, detail: { index: number; groupIndex?: number })` | After a row is added; `groupIndex` only in grouped mode. |
| `remove` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, detail: { index: number; item: TItem; groupIndex?: number })` | After a row is removed. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | { item, index, groupIndex, errors, update, remove, removable, removeLabel, move } | Replaces the whole row; the column header and the reorder controls are not drawn. `remove` takes the activating event (`@click="remove"`); `move(event, offset)` moves the row when `reorderable` is on. |
| `row-actions` | { item, index, groupIndex, remove, removable, removeLabel } | Replaces the Remove button at the end of a default row (for example Remove / Undo that marks a row instead of deleting it). `remove` takes the activating event. |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the empty text. |
| `actions` | — | Extra buttons after Add (for example Upload or Paste .env). |
| `info` | — | Extra help text under the buttons, after the limit text. |
| `limit` | { count, limit, left } | Replaces the limit text in list mode (for example "You can add 3 more tags."). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:items` | `TItem[]` | `[]` | `update:items` | Rows in list mode, via `defineModel('items')`. A row added, removed, edited or moved goes out as the new array; unbound, the editor keeps its own rows. |
| `v-model:groups` | `TItem[][] \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:groups` | Rows in grouped mode, via `defineModel('groups')`: every inner array is an AND group, groups are joined by OR. Setting it (even to `[]`) switches the editor to grouped mode. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `empty`, `at limit` (Add disabled), `invalid` (per cell), `disabled`
- `data-size` mirrors `size`; `data-disabled` mirrors `disabled`; `data-mode` is `list` or `grouped`; `data-fit` is the container width (`md`, `xl` or `3xl`) from which the row layout applies (see Responsive)
- Each row carries `data-row` with its index (and `data-group` in grouped mode)
- With `reorderable`: the row or group being dragged carries `data-dragging` (dimmed, dashed `var(--accent)` outline) and the one under the pointer carries `data-drop` (`before` or `after`, a 2 px `var(--accent)` line on that edge); Move up is disabled on the first row of a group and Move down on the last; every reorder control is disabled with `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: every control and button keeps its own ring.
- Keyboard map: Tab moves through the cells of a row, its reorder controls, its Remove, then the next row; Add moves focus to the first control of the new row; Remove moves focus to the same position in the next row, else the previous row, else Add. With `reorderable`: Arrow Up / Arrow Down on a grip, or Alt+Arrow Up / Alt+Arrow Down on any control of a row, move the row one position inside its group (on a group's grip, the group); focus follows the moved row (the same control, or its grip when that control is now disabled). Drag and drop is a pointer shortcut only; every move is reachable by keyboard and by the buttons.
- ARIA: the rows are a `list` named by `ariaLabel`; each cell is a `Field` whose label is programmatically tied to its control (visually hidden on wide containers, where one header row shows the labels, with the same `*` after a required column's label as the stacked label, and is `aria-hidden`); an error is a `FieldError` referenced by `aria-describedby` and sets `aria-invalid`; each Remove is named by the row's first-column value, "Remove item API_BASE_URL" (or `removeButtonLabel` and the value), and by its position, "Remove item n", only while that value is empty; each grip is a button named "Reorder item n" ("Reorder group n") and described by the hint "Drag, or press Arrow Up or Arrow Down to move."; Move up / Move down are named "Move item n up" / "Move item n down" ("Move group n up" / "down"); groups are `group`s named "Group n"; a polite `status` region announces "Item n added", "Item n removed" and "Item n moved to position m." ("Group n moved to position m.").
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens, including the disabled state.
- Touch target: Remove follows `size` (40 px at `large`); the stacked layout keeps it at the row's end.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import AttributeEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/attribute-editor'
  import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

  const definition = [
    { key: 'key', label: 'Key', placeholder: 'MY_VARIABLE', required: true },
    { key: 'value', label: 'Value', placeholder: 'my-value' }
  ]

  const items = ref([
    { key: 'API_BASE_URL', value: 'https://api.example.com' },
    { key: 'max uploads', value: '25' }
  ])

  const errors = computed(() =>
    items.value.map((item) => {
      if (!item.key.trim()) return { key: 'Key is required.' }
      if (!/^[A-Z0-9_]+$/.test(item.key))
        return { key: 'Use only uppercase letters, numbers, and underscores.' }
      return undefined
    })
  )
</script>

<template>
  <AttributeEditor
    v-model:items="items"
    :definition="definition"
    :errors="errors"
    :limit="10"
    :min-items="1"
    add-button-label="Add variable"
    remove-button-label="Remove variable"
    aria-label="Environment variables"
  />
</template>
```

# Checkbox

> Binary selection control. Supports a single boolean (no `value`), a scalar paired with `value`, and array-based multi-select (adds or removes its `value` in the `modelValue` array) (used by `MultiSelect` and `DataTable` to drive bulk selection). The new `indeterminate` prop renders a third visual state (horizontal bar) and sets the native `indeterminate` property, which exposes the mixed state — used by parents that own a partial-selection summary (e.g. "select all" rows where some children are selected). Aligned with Figma frame `2027:7311`.

- Import: `import Checkbox from '@aziontech/webkit/checkbox'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use a Checkbox per option inside Field.Set for two to five options that all fit on screen; use Checkbox alone for an on/off choice submitted with a form. For a longer list use MultiSelect; for an on/off setting that applies at once use Switch.
- A bare boolean control whose label lives outside it: a table row-selection cell, an option row in a list, a settings matrix.
- Picking several values from a short set: give each box its own `value` and bind them all to one array `v-model`.
- A "select all" control over a partial selection: set `indeterminate` while only some children are checked.

## Do

- Leave `value` unset for a plain true/false model. With `value`, the checkbox adds or removes it in an array model, or sets a scalar model to `value` (checked) and `null` (unchecked).
- Give every checkbox an accessible name: point a `label` element's `for` at the `id` you pass (or wrap it in a `Field`), or pass `aria-label` (attributes land on the inner input).
- `indeterminate` only changes the visual and sets the native `indeterminate` property (exposed as mixed); the parent computes it and decides what a click does.
- Use `readonly` for a value that cannot change in this context and `disabled` for an option that is unavailable.

## Don’t

- A form field that needs its own label, description, or helper text → wrap it in a horizontal `field` (`Field orientation="horizontal"` + `Field.Content`).
- Each option needs a bordered card with a label and description → use a `field` choice card (`Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field`).
- An on/off setting that applies as soon as it flips → use `switch`.
- Only one option of the set may be chosen → use `radio-group`.

## Related

- `field` — `orientation="horizontal"` puts the checkbox beside its label and description (the default inside forms); a `Field.Label` wrapping that Field turns it into a bordered choice card.
- `switch` — on/off toggle for settings that take effect immediately.
- `multi-select` — renders this checkbox in every option row; use it when the option list is long.
- `data-table` — uses this checkbox for row selection and the select-all header.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `unknown` | `undefined` | false | Identifier for this checkbox in a group: compared against a scalar model, or added to and removed from an array model. Unset, the model is a boolean. |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the indeterminate visual (horizontal bar). Does not affect `modelValue`; the parent owns the tri-state logic. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only; value is visible but cannot change via interaction. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the control invalid: sets `aria-invalid` and the danger border (unchecked). An enclosing `Field`'s `invalid` sets it too. |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | false | HTML name for form submission. |
| `modelValue` | `TModel` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `TModel` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | The bound value via `defineModel`: a boolean when `value` is unset; with `value`, an array (adds or removes `value`; an undefined model counts as an empty array) or a scalar (set to `value` when checked, to `null` when unchecked). Uncontrolled when unbound. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `checked`, `indeterminate`, `disabled`, `readonly`
- `data-state` on the root: `unchecked` | `checked` | `indeterminate`
- `data-checked` mirrors `isChecked` (legacy; kept for backwards compatibility with existing `data-[checked]:` styling)
- `data-indeterminate` mirrors the `indeterminate` prop
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors `invalid` (own prop or the enclosing `Field`); with `aria-invalid` on the control, it paints the danger border while unchecked
- `data-readonly` mirrors the `readonly` prop
- Touch: the native input that receives the click extends past the 18 px box to 24 × 24 px, and to 44 × 44 px on a coarse pointer; the drawn box does not change.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Space` toggles. (The native `<input type="checkbox">` carries the semantics.) When `readonly`, `disabled`, or the parent refuses the change, the native `checked` is put back to the model's state, so assistive tech never announces a state the model does not hold; `readonly` also sets `aria-readonly` and cancels the click.
- ARIA: native `<input type="checkbox">` is the source of truth. No `aria-checked` is set on it: the checked state comes from `checked`, and the mixed state from the `indeterminate` DOM property, which browsers expose as mixed (an `aria-checked` on a native checkbox conflicts with its real state, axe `aria-conditional-attr`). The wrapping `<span>` is decorative.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons + borders), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition-bearing class.
- Touch target — the `1.125rem` size is below 40×40 px; consumers should wrap it in a horizontal `Field` (the label extends the target) or expand the parent click area when the control sits on its own.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Checkbox from '@aziontech/webkit/checkbox'
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const checked = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <Field orientation="horizontal">
    <Checkbox
      v-model="checked"
      name="email-notifications"
    />
    <Field.Label>Email notifications</Field.Label>
  </Field>
</template>
```

# Chip

> Use Chip when the person can remove or select the token (applied filters, picked values); a read-only word is a Tag, and a number is a Badge. A Chip is a compact, pill-shaped token that labels a discrete value the user has applied — most often a filter on a data view. Unlike `tag` (a read-only status/category badge with severity color coding), a Chip carries no severity and exposes an optional trailing remove control: when `removable` is set, it renders a real `<button>` that emits `remove`, so the consumer can drop the value from a collection. This is the token consumed by the data table's `#filters` slot (`<Chip :label="f.label" removable @remove="dropFilter(f)" />`): each active filter becomes one removable Chip, and dismissing it removes that filter. Reach for a Chip when a value is user-applied and dismissible; reach for `tag` when it is a static status or category indicator. `variant` covers the three jobs a chip does in a filter surface, so a consumer never restyles the component to get one of them: - **`filled`** — a value that IS applied. The grey `--bg-selected` fill on the shared border, plus `--shadow-sm`: the loudest of the three, because it is state. This is the applied-filter chip of the console's filter bar. - **`outline`** — a value the user COULD apply. The `--bg-surface` fill and the shared border, no shadow: it recedes to an offer without becoming disabled, so a filter vocabulary can stay on screen instead of hiding inside a menu. - **`dashed`** — the control that CREATES a chip ("Add filter"). A dashed outline is the standing convention for "add another one of these", which is what separates the thing that makes filters from the things that are filters. **Selected is a mode, not a variant.** `selectable` turns the chip into a toggle: activating it flips the `selected` model (`v-model:selected`), and the state stays after the click until the chip is activated again. It is independent of `variant` — `filled` marks an applied filter and never means "selected", so a selectable chip of any variant paints its selected state the same way (`--bg-selected` fill, `--border-selected` outline) and announces it as `aria-pressed`. Because `filled` already wears the `--bg-selected` fill, a `filled` toggle shows its on state by the outline alone; a row of toggles is `outline`. Reach for `selectable` when a set of chips is a row of toggles (quick filters, facets); keep `clickable` when activation opens or does something without holding a state. **Presence is the consumer's, not the chip's.** `remove` fires the moment the control is activated; the chip does not animate itself away or unmount itself. A chip that hid itself on remove could only ever serve the one case where removing it also destroys it — a filter bar where a removed value stays on screen as an `outline` offer was impossible, because the instance stayed invisible forever. Exit motion, if wanted, belongs to whatever owns the list (a `TransitionGroup` around the group).

- Import: `import Chip from '@aziontech/webkit/chip'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Represent a selectable or removable token — active filters, multi-select values, entered keywords.
- Represent a value that is _available_ but not applied (`variant="outline"`), so the set of things a view can be narrowed by stays visible.
- Represent the "add another" affordance for such a set (`variant="dashed"`).
- Represent a row of toggles that each hold an on/off state (`selectable` + `v-model:selected`).
- The element is interactive (clickable / dismissible).

## Do

- When removable, expose an accessible remove control with a clear label.
- Group related chips in a `chip-group` rather than ad-hoc layout.
- Do: draw an applied filter as `variant="filled"` (the default) — the grey fill is what says "this narrows the view"; draw the values it could still take as `outline`, and "Add filter" as `dashed`.
- Do: make a row of toggles `outline` + `selectable`, so off reads as surface and on as the selected fill and outline.
- Don't: restyle a chip's fill with a class (`bg-(--bg-muted)`, `bg-(--bg-surface)`) to get the applied or the available look; pick the `variant`.
- Don't: use `filled` for a value that is merely offered; the fill would claim it is applied.

## Don’t

- It is a static count or one-glance status → use `badge`.
- It is a static descriptive label/category with no interaction → use `tag`.

## Related

- `badge` — static count/short-value indicator.
- `tag` — static labelled status/category chip.
- `tooltip` — composed by the remove control to name what it removes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback text when the default slot is empty. |
| `variant` | `'filled' \| 'outline' \| 'dashed'` | `'filled'` | false | Visual variant. Filled (grey fill) is an applied value, outlined an available one, dashed the control that adds one. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `small` is a fixed 24px, `medium` a fixed 32px. |
| `removable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, renders a trailing remove button that emits `remove`. |
| `clickable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, the chip body becomes interactive (`role="button"`, focusable) and emits `click` on activation (click / Enter / Space). |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, the chip becomes a toggle: activating it flips the `selected` model and emits `click`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Suppresses activation, toggling and removal. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:selected`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remove` | `(event: MouseEvent, label: string)` | Fires when `removable` is true and the remove button is activated (click / Enter / Space), **immediately** — the chip does not hide or unmount itself first, so the consumer decides whether the chip disappears, stays, or becomes an `outline` offer. `label` is the chip's `label` prop, identifying which chip was removed. |
| `click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, label: string)` | Fires only when `clickable` or `selectable` is true, `disabled` is false, and the chip body is activated — by pointer, or `Enter` / `Space` while the root is focused. `label` identifies which chip was clicked. When `selectable`, the `selected` model is already flipped when `click` fires. The trailing remove button stops propagation, so activating it emits `remove` only, never `click`. `update:selected` comes from `v-model:selected` (see above). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Chip content; falls back to `label` when empty. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:selected` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:selected` | Whether a selectable chip is toggled on. Flipped on every activation while `selectable` and not `disabled`; ignored otherwise. Uncontrolled when unbound. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop (`filled` | `outline` | `dashed`)
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop (`small` | `medium`)
- `data-removable` is present when the `removable` prop is true
- `data-clickable` is present when the chip is interactive (`clickable` or `selectable`) and not `disabled`
- `data-selected` is present when `selectable` is true and the `selected` model is true
- `data-disabled` is present when the `disabled` prop is true
- When `selectable`, the chip is interactive exactly like `clickable`, and additionally carries `aria-pressed="true|false"` mirroring `selected`. Selected paints the `--bg-selected` fill and the `--border-selected` outline on top of whichever `variant` the chip has; `variant` keeps its own meaning (elevation, dash), so a `filled` chip is an applied value whether or not it is selected. Hover and active keep their `--border-strong` affordance over the selected outline.
- When `disabled`, the root is not focusable, activation, toggling and removal are suppressed, the text drops to `--text-disabled` with `cursor-not-allowed`, and the remove button is a disabled `<button>`. The root carries `aria-disabled="true"` (an interactive chip keeps `role="button"`), so the dimmed text is exposed as part of a disabled control, the case WCAG 1.4.3 exempts from contrast.
- When `clickable`, the root is an interactive `role="button"` with `tabindex="0"`: it shows `cursor-pointer`, a `::before` ghost-layer darkening overlay (`--bg-hover`) on `hover` and `active`, a `--border-strong` border on `active` (the pressed state, per Figma), and a visible focus ring on `focus-visible`. When not clickable, the root stays a non-interactive container.
- The remove button (when `removable`) is always independently focusable and shows its own focus ring on `focus-visible`. It carries a **`tooltip`** naming what it removes, shown on hover and on keyboard focus — in a row of chips four identical `×` controls sit side by side, and the field name is what tells them apart.
- All three variants share the `--border-default` border at rest, so a row of chips reads as one family. `filled` fills with `--bg-selected` (grey: `#E5E5E5` on the light theme's white surface, `#1A1A1A` on the dark theme's `#0A0A0A`) and adds `--shadow-sm`; `outline` and `dashed` fill with `--bg-surface` and carry no shadow, so an applied value is louder than an available one in both themes. `dashed` is `outline` with a dashed border. When `clickable`, hover raises the border to `--border-strong` — the same rest→hover pair `input` and `select-trigger` use. That pair is what makes the outline read as interactive at all: `--border-default` is 8% black, the _same value_ as `--border-muted` in the light theme, so a static border of either token is indistinguishable.
- **Why `--bg-selected` and not `--bg-surface-raised`.** `filled` once specified `--bg-surface-raised`, which resolves to the _same value_ as `--bg-surface` in the light theme (the contrast existed only in dark), and the utility carried a stray space inside the paren shorthand, so it compiled to no CSS at all; for a while every chip then shared `--bg-surface` and `--shadow-sm` alone carried the state, which read as a white pill on white cards. The design sample's filter bar draws the applied chip on `--bg-selected`, which differs from `--bg-surface` in both themes; that is the fill.
- The remove control's glyph sits at `--text-muted` at rest and rises to `--text-default` on hover: at rest it is punctuation after a label, and on hover it is the thing being aimed at. It stays above the 3:1 non-text contrast minimum in both themes (3.95:1 light, 5.02:1 dark).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: both the clickable root (when `clickable`) and the remove button use `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Keyboard map: when `clickable` or `selectable` (and not `disabled`), the root is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) and `Enter` / `Space` **dispatch a real DOM click** on the root (`preventDefault`ed first, so `Space` does not scroll), which in turn emits `click` (and, when `selectable`, toggles `selected`). Dispatching rather than emitting directly is what lets a chip serve as an overlay trigger — `Popover.Trigger` and friends open on the DOM click that bubbles out of their child, so a chip that only emitted a Vue event would work with the mouse and do nothing from the keyboard. When `removable`, `Tab` reaches the remove button and `Enter` / `Space` activate it and emit `remove`. Keystrokes that originate on the remove button do not bubble to the root activation (the handler ignores events whose `target` is not the root itself). When a chip is both interactive and `removable`, the button role, `tabindex`, `aria-pressed` and the `Enter` / `Space` handler move from the root to an inner body element (`data-slot="chip-body"`, testid `<testid>__body`) that holds the label, and the remove button sits beside it, not inside it: a `role="button"` with a `<button>` inside is `nested-interactive`, and screen readers flatten the inner control away. The root keeps the click handler and draws the focus ring when the body is focused (`has-[[data-slot=chip-body]:focus-visible]`). Tab order is body, then remove button.
- ARIA: when neither `clickable` nor `selectable`, the root is a non-interactive `<span>` container; when either is set, it is `role="button"` with `tabindex="0"`. A `selectable` chip is a toggle button: `aria-pressed="true|false"` mirrors the `selected` model and flips on every activation, so the state is announced, not only painted. When `disabled`, the root carries `aria-disabled="true"` (interactive or not) and an interactive root drops `tabindex`; the remove control is a native disabled `<button>`. The remove control is a real `<button type="button">`; the `az az-x` glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`. Its `aria-label` and its tooltip text are **the same derived string** — `Remove <label>` when `label` is set, `Remove` otherwise — so what is shown and what is announced cannot drift.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the remove icon.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition the chip declares (variant/border colour, remove-button colour). The chip declares no dismiss animation at all, so there is nothing to suppress there.
- Touch target: the remove control is drawn at 24×24 px at `medium` and 16×16 px at `small`; a `[data-slot=touch-target]` span extends its hit area to at least 24×24 px at both sizes (WCAG 2.5.8), and to 44×44 px on a coarse pointer; the chip root does not clip it (no `overflow-hidden`: the label truncates on its own), so the target may extend past the chip's edge. A clickable or selectable chip carries its own `[data-slot=touch-target]` span on its root (a split chip's taps there toggle it, the remove button's own target stays on top) that grows its hit area to 44 px tall on a coarse pointer; a static or disabled chip has none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Chip from '@aziontech/webkit/chip'
</script>

<template>
  <Chip
    label="Label"
    variant="filled"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```
