# Combobox

> A text field with a list of suggestions under it: typing filters the options, picking one fills the field, and a value that is not in the list is accepted as typed. It holds one string value, after the design sample's `ComboboxInput` and the ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern. It differs from `Select`, whose value must be one of its options and whose trigger is a button, and from `Command`, which runs commands from a palette instead of filling a form field. Naming: this is the ARIA 1.2 combobox (an editable field with suggestions, free text by default). In shadcn, `Combobox` is a searchable select whose value must come from the list; get that here with `allow-custom="false"` (or `Select` with a search field). `allowCustom` and `filter` default to `true` and are recorded as exceptions to the default-false rule: inverting them would break every consumer. `emptyTitle` is the empty-list text prop, the name `table` and `select` use; AttributeEditor's `empty` names the same idea.

- Import: `import Combobox from '@aziontech/webkit/combobox'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Combobox when the person may type a value that is not in the list and the list only suggests. When the value must come from the list use Select; for several values use MultiSelect.
- A form field whose usual values are known but a new one is valid: an environment variable name, a header, a path, a region tag, a branch.
- A long option list the user would rather type than scroll, with the list as a reminder.
- Options that come from the server as the user types (`search` event, `loading`, `filter: false`).
- Suggestions grouped by origin (Recent, Suggested, System) in one field.

## Do

- Put the Combobox in a `Field` so it gets a visible label; use `ariaLabel` only where no label can be shown.
- Keep `allowCustom` on only when a new value is genuinely valid; with it off, the field restores the last valid value when the typed text matches nothing.
- Give options a `description` for what tells them apart (a scope, a count), not a second copy of the label.
- For server data set `filter` to `false`, listen to `search` (debounce on your side), and drive `loading` from the request.
- Validate the committed value (`update:modelValue`) in the form, not each keystroke; `search` is for suggestions only.
- Use `group` when options come from distinct sources; keep group titles one or two words.

## Don’t

- The value must be one of a short fixed list → use `select` (or `radio-group` for two to seven visible choices).
- Several values at once → use `multi-select`.
- Searching and running commands or jumping to a page → use `command`.
- Filtering a collection by properties → use `property-filter`.
- Key/value pairs or tags → use `attribute-editor` or `tag-editor` (their key cells may hold a Combobox).

## Related

- `select` — closed list, button trigger, no free entry.
- `input` — the field Combobox is built on; use it alone when there are no suggestions.
- `field` — label, description and error around the Combobox; it reads id, invalid, disabled and required from it.
- `command` — palette of actions, not a form value.
- `property-filter` — token-based filtering with the same listbox look.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `ComboboxOption[]` | `[]` | false | Suggestions: `{ value, label?, description?, group?, disabled? }`. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder of the field. |
| `icon` | `string` | `'az az-search'` | false | Leading icon of the field. Empty shows none (a time field passes `az az-clock`). |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name when no `Field` label names the field. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token, as `Input`: 28 / 32 / 40 px. |
| `allowCustom` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Accepts a typed value that matches no option, offered as `Use "…"`. |
| `filter` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Filters `options` by the typed text. Turn off when the server filters on `search`. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a clear button while the field has a value. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a spinner and the loading row while options are fetched. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the list when nothing matches. Empty uses the locale catalog. Same name as `table`, `select` and the other empty states. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the field. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the value without the list or editing. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field required (`aria-required`). |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field invalid (`aria-invalid`, danger border). |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | `string` | The typed text, on each keystroke while the list is open (server filters). |
| `create` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent \| FocusEvent, value: string)` | A value that matches no option was committed (`allowCustom`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `option` | { option: ComboboxOption, active: boolean, selected: boolean } | Replaces the content of one option row. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## Sub-components

_none_ — one `.vue` file. The list is rendered by the component itself (teleported to `body`, positioned with `usePlacement`); options are data, rendered through the optional `option` slot.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The committed value via `defineModel`. Changes on pick, Enter, Tab, blur and clear, not on each keystroke. |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Whether the list is open, via `defineModel('open')`: focus, typing, ArrowDown / ArrowUp, Alt+ArrowDown / ArrowUp, Escape, pick and blur update it. The list shows while it is open and has rows, is loading or has a no-match row. Unbound, the field keeps it itself and starts at `defaultOpen`; bound, the parent can open or close it, and every open and close the combobox makes emits `update:open`. Opening is refused while `disabled` or `readonly`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `open`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `loading`, empty list
- `data-state` on the root: `open` | `closed`
- `data-disabled`, `data-invalid` on the root mirror the resolved props (prop or `Field`)
- Option rows: `data-active` (the keyboard/pointer highlight), `data-selected` (equals the committed value), `data-disabled`
- The field shows the selected option's `label` when the value equals an option's `value`, otherwise the value itself
- `data-side` (`bottom` | `top`) and `data-align` (`start`) on the listbox panel mirror where it landed after flipping; `start` follows the text direction, so under `rtl` the panel lines up with the field's right edge

## Accessibility

- ARIA 1.2 combobox: the `<input>` has `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` (the listbox id) and `aria-activedescendant` (the highlighted option); the list is `role="listbox"`, rows are `role="option"` with `aria-selected` and `aria-disabled`; grouped rows sit in `role="group"` named by their title (`aria-labelledby`).
- Keyboard map: focus or `ArrowDown` opens the list, scrolled so the committed option (when the value is one of the options) sits in the middle of the list; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the highlight (wrapping, skipping disabled rows); `Home`/`End` move it to the first/last option while the list is open (otherwise the caret moves); `Enter` commits the highlighted option, or the typed text when nothing is highlighted (`allowCustom`); `Escape` closes the list, and a second `Escape` restores the last committed text; `Tab` commits the highlighted option or the typed text and moves on; `Alt+ArrowUp` closes.
- Nested overlays: the open list joins the shared overlay layer stack (`useOverlayLayer`) as a transient layer (focus stays in the input), so inside a `Popover`, `Dialog` or `Drawer` picking a suggestion or pressing `Escape` closes only the list; the host overlay stays open.
- Focus stays in the input the whole time; pointer clicks on rows do not move focus (`mousedown.prevent`).
- A polite status region announces the number of options after each change of the typed text ("3 options"), "No matches" and "Loading options"; it is visually hidden.
- The clear button is a real button with an accessible name ("Clear"), reachable by Tab only while there is a value, and returns focus to the input.
- `Field` integration through `Input`: label `for`/`id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required`, disabled.
- Contrast: option text and muted descriptions ≥4.5:1 on `--bg-surface-raised` in both themes; the active row is marked by its fill and `aria-activedescendant`, never colour alone for selection (a check icon marks the selected row).
- Touch targets: rows are 32 px tall, 44 px on `pointer: coarse`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Combobox from '@aziontech/webkit/combobox'
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const name = ref('API_URL')

  const options = [
    { value: 'API_URL', description: 'Suggested' },
    { value: 'API_TOKEN', description: 'Suggested' },
    { value: 'NODE_ENV', description: 'System' },
    { value: 'LOG_LEVEL' },
    { value: 'CACHE_TTL' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Field class="max-w-(--container-xs)">
    <Field.Label>Variable name</Field.Label>
    <Combobox
      v-model="name"
      :options="options"
      placeholder="Search or type a name"
      clearable
    />
    <Field.Description>Pick a known variable or type a new one.</Field.Description>
  </Field>
</template>
```

# Date Picker

> DatePicker picks **one date**, optionally with a time, in a form field. A trigger button opens a popover that holds a month grid, a typed date field (and a time field with `showTime`), an optional footer and a Cancel / Apply pair. The selection is staged in a draft inside the popover and committed to `v-model` only on Apply (or immediately when `show-apply` is false); Cancel closes, drops the draft and refocuses the trigger, as in `date-range-picker`. Date math uses the native `Date` API only — no date library; the trigger formats the value with `Intl` in `v-model:time-zone` (the local zone when empty), and the panel shows and edits it in that zone too: the grid, the date and time fields and the `min` / `max` bounds are wall-clock time there, and `v-model` stays the instant. Before 6.0 this component was `Calendar` and also picked ranges, periods and presets; every range — relative or absolute, with or without times — now belongs to `date-range-picker`, which reuses this component's month grid and fields as internal parts. The name follows Cloudscape DatePicker and the shadcn "Date Picker".

- Import: `import DatePickerRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/date-picker-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import DatePicker from '@aziontech/webkit/date-picker'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use DatePicker to pick one date (optionally with a time) in a form field. For any start–end range use DateRangePicker; to display a moment in time use Timestamp.
- A due date, a start date, an expiry date, a birthday.
- A date and a time of day together (`show-time`): a scheduled maintenance window start, a release time.

## Do

- `modelValue` is committed only on Apply; read the final value from `update:modelValue` or the second argument of `apply`, and set `:show-apply="false"` when every edit should commit at once.
- Bind a `Date` or `null`.
- Bound the selectable days with `min` and `max` instead of validating after commit. Unlike `date-range-picker` (five years back to the end of today by default), DatePicker is unbounded by default: a single date is often in the future (a token expiry, an alert schedule), so a page sets `min` to today there, and sets `max` only when the date must be in the past.
- Send `toISOString()` (or the ISO date `2026-11-15`) to the server, never the printed label.

## Don’t

- A start and an end, whole days or with times, relative or absolute → use `date-range-picker`.
- Displaying a date the person does not edit → use `timestamp`.
- A duration or count (retention days, TTL) rather than a date → use `number-input`.

## Related

- `date-range-picker` — every range: relative windows (`last 15 minutes`) kept relative, absolute ranges down to the minute, and whole days with `:show-time="false"`. It is built on this component's grid, fields and time zone selector.
- `timestamp` — shows a moment in time in the app's time zone.
- `field` — inside a `Field`, the trigger takes the field's label (`for` points at it), description, `invalid` and `disabled`.
- `select` — the Month and Year selects in the calendar caption (`variant="ghost"`, `size="small"`).
- `combobox` — the time field: a typed time or a pick from the 30-minute list, which opens under the field so the panel stays as thin as the grid.
- `input` — the trigger and the date field share its heights, hover, and disabled treatment, so they align side by side.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects the trigger, day-cell hit-area, and typography. |
| `min` | `Date \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Earliest selectable date; earlier days render disabled. |
| `max` | `Date \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Latest selectable date; later days render disabled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger, grid, and all controls, applying disabled tokens. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the trigger invalid: sets `aria-invalid` and the danger border. An enclosing `Field`'s `invalid` sets it too. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Trigger text shown when there is no selection. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Select a date`). |
| `showFields` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the date field (and the time field with `showTime`) in the panel. Set false when the grid is the whole interaction and typing a date is not offered. |
| `showTime` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a time field beside the date field, so the value carries a time of day. |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | false | Places the fields and Apply column below the calendar (vertical) or beside it (horizontal). |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the trigger; the current value is appended (`Due date: Nov 15, 2026`). Empty leaves the name to the Field label or the trigger text. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a clear control on the trigger that empties the committed selection. |
| `showApply` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Stages edits in a draft and shows Cancel and Apply; when false, every edit commits immediately and neither button renders. |
| `split` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the trigger as a split control with a separate chevron affordance. |
| `modelValue` | `DatePickerValue` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |
| `timeZone` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:timeZone`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `month-change` | `DatePickerMonth` | Emitted when the first visible month changes via navigation or keyboard paging. Payload is `{ year, month }` (month is 0-indexed). |
| `apply` | `(event: Event, value: Date \| null)` | Emitted when the draft selection is committed via Apply; `event` is the activating click or key event, `value` the committed date. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | { open, value, displayValue } | Replaces the default trigger button; scope exposes the open state, raw value, and formatted label. |
| `footer` | — | Custom footer/action-bar content (e.g. `<DatePicker.Clear>`) alongside Apply. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/date-picker-clear`

## Sub-components

- `date-picker-clear/date-picker-clear.vue` — context-aware button that clears the draft selection through injected context; disabled when there is no selection.

Internal parts, not exported, shared with `date-range-picker`, in `parts/`: `parts/date-picker-grid.vue` (the month grid; its caption reads `‹ Month ⌄ Year ⌄ ›`: the previous and next month arrows, and between them two ghost `Select`s, Month (the twelve month names, a month fully outside `min`/`max` disabled) and Year (from `min`'s year to `max`'s year, or ten years either side of today when unbounded, always including the shown year); picking a month or a year moves the grid there and emits `month-change`, a year that would land outside `min`/`max` keeps the month inside them), `parts/date-picker-fields.vue` (the date and time fields, a Start/End pair for a range; each time field is a `Combobox` with `allow-custom` that lists the day in 30-minute steps under the field — plus the current time when it is between two steps, so the list opens on it — shows a clock icon and takes any typed time), `parts/date-picker-timezone.vue` (the time zone selector `date-range-picker` shows, a `Combobox` with `allow-custom` off that filters the zones by city, zone id or offset as the person types), and the trigger shell both pickers render: `parts/date-picker-control.vue` (the bordered control box), `parts/date-picker-trigger.vue` (the trigger button: icon, value, chevron), `parts/date-picker-control-button.vue` (a button inside the control box, such as the clear and split buttons here and the Previous and Next buttons of `date-range-picker`) and `parts/date-picker-popover.vue` (the panel: placement, backdrop on small screens, focus trap, Escape and outside click close it). No part renders a native `select`. A private part lives in `parts/`, so it is not mistaken for a public `date-picker-<part>`.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `Date \| null` | `null` | `update:modelValue` | The committed date via `defineModel`; `null` on clear. Only updated on Apply (or immediately when `showApply` is false). Uncontrolled when unbound. |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state of the popover via `defineModel`. Fires when the popover opens or closes. Unbound, the popover keeps its own state and starts at `defaultOpen`. |
| `v-model:time-zone` | `string` | `''` | `update:timeZone` | IANA time zone the value is shown and picked in, via `defineModel('timeZone')`: the trigger formats in it, and the grid, the fields and `min` / `max` are its wall-clock time, so picking 16:00 commits 16:00 there. Empty resolves to the local zone. Same name as on `date-range-picker`. |

**Booleans that default to true.** `showFields` and `showApply` default to `true`: they switch off parts of the default panel. Inverting them (`hideFields`, `instant`) would break every consumer, so they are recorded here as the exceptions to props.md's default-false rule.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `selected`, `disabled`, `today`, `outside` (adjacent-month), popover `open` / `closed`
- **Field contract parity.** Every field-shaped surface — the trigger and the date + time fields — follows the shared `inputs` field contract used by `input`, `number-input`, `select-trigger` and `textarea`, so a DatePicker reads identically to a text field placed beside it: heights are `small=28px` / `medium=32px` / `large=40px`, the value renders at `.text-label-sm`, and `disabled` applies `var(--bg-disabled)` + `var(--text-disabled)` + `cursor-not-allowed` rather than an opacity wash.
- **Hover is identical to `input`.** The whole trigger is one field with one border, so hover raises **only** that border to `var(--border-strong)` — no background wash on any segment. It is suppressed while the control is focused and while `disabled`, via the same selector `input` uses: `[&:not(:focus-within):not([data-disabled])]:hover:border-(--border-strong)`. Hovering any segment — the date, clear, or split — raises the single shared border.
- `data-state` on the root and trigger mirrors the popover open state (`open` | `closed`)
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop on the root, trigger, and each day cell (`small` | `medium` | `large`)
- `data-selected` mirrors the selected day cell
- `data-band` on each day cell is `single` on the selected day and `none` elsewhere (the `start` / `middle` / `end` bands are `date-range-picker`'s)
- `data-today` marks the current date, taken from the nearest `ConfigProvider` `now` when set (so a server render and the hydrating client agree), else the current time; the grid also opens on that month when there is no value; `data-outside` marks an adjacent-month day cell
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on the root, unselectable day cells, and the clear control when there is no selection
- `data-invalid` mirrors `invalid` (own prop or the enclosing `Field`'s) on the root and the trigger shell, with `aria-invalid` on the trigger and the danger border
- Reflow: the root is capped at the width of its container (`max-w-full`), so the trigger never overflows a 320 px box.
- `data-side` (`bottom` | `top`) and `data-align` (`start`) on the calendar panel mirror where it landed after flipping; `start` follows the text direction, so under `rtl` the panel lines up with the field's right edge

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the trigger and `focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-surface-raised)` inside the popover. The date and time fields reuse `input`, whose ring offset resolves `var(--input-ring-offset, var(--bg-canvas))`; the fields container declares `--input-ring-offset: var(--bg-surface-raised)` once and it inherits to every field.
- Field labels: the visible Date label is a `<label for>` bound to its date field through `useId()`; the time field beside it carries its own `aria-label` (`Time`), so every field has a programmatic accessible name.
- Keyboard map: the trigger toggles the popover with `Enter`/`Space` and exposes `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`; `Escape` and click-outside close it and return focus to the trigger; focus is trapped in the open popover. Opening focuses the selected day (else today, else the first enabled day); `Shift+Tab` reaches the month controls. In the grid, `Tab` enters at the focused day, `Arrow` keys move focus (paging the visible month when crossing its first/last day), `Enter`/`Space` selects, `Home`/`End` move to the first/last day of the week (the grid starts on Sunday; logical, so the same under `dir="rtl"`), `PageUp`/`PageDown` change month, `Shift+PageUp`/`Shift+PageDown` change year. The caption's Month and Year selects keep the `select` keyboard map (`Enter`/`Space`/`ArrowDown` open the list, the arrows move, typing jumps to an option, `Escape` closes only the list and leaves the popover open). Tests: `date-picker.test.ts` › Home and End, Shift+PageDown and Shift+PageUp; jumps to the month and year picked in the caption selects; bounds the year list by min and max. Cancel, Apply, Clear and the fields are all reachable by `Tab`.
- ARIA: the month grid uses `role="grid"` with `role="row"` and `role="gridcell"` descendants; the selected cell sets `aria-selected="true"`; the current date sets `aria-current="date"`; navigation buttons carry `aria-label`; the caption's Month and Year selects are `combobox` buttons named `Month` and `Year` from the catalog, showing the visible month and year; the popover is a `dialog` named by the catalog (`Choose date`); decorative icons are `aria-hidden="true"`.
- In a required `Field`, the trigger's `aria-describedby` adds the Field's `requiredId`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the popover and `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px (or justified deviation): day cells use a 32×32 px (`small`), 36×36 px (`medium`), or 40×40 px (`large`) hit area; `small`/`medium` are a justified deviation for dense month-grid layouts, `large` meets the 40 px target.

<!-- components/date-range-picker.md -->

# Date Range Picker

> A time range for queries over time: logs, events, traces and metrics. After the Console Kit date-time range (quick ranges, a custom duration, absolute range with times, a range that ends now, previous and next, auto refresh, the time zone) and Cloudscape's date range picker. The value is one of three shapes: - **relative** — `{ type: 'relative', amount: 15, unit: 'minute' }`, read as "the last 15 minutes" and re-resolved against the clock on every query, so a live view keeps moving. With `snap: true` the start is rounded down to the start of the unit in the time zone: `{ amount: 1, unit: 'day', snap: true }` is **Today** (midnight to now), `unit: 'week'` is **This week** (from Sunday, like the month grid). - **absolute** — `{ type: 'absolute', start, end }`, two ISO 8601 instants. - **since** — `{ type: 'since', start }`, an ISO 8601 start and an end that is always now ("from the incident until now"). The trigger prints `Last 15 minutes`, `Today`, the absolute range in the selected time zone with its UTC offset (`Nov 10, 16:00 – 17:00 (UTC+00:00)`; the date is printed once when both ends are on the same day), or `Nov 10, 2026, 9:30 – now`. It never cuts the text off: a long value wraps onto a second line. The panel switches between Relative (first) and Absolute. Absolute has two views of one draft. It opens on the **calendar view**: the `DatePicker` month grid with only the weeks the month needs (five rows for most months; click a start day and an end day; its caption has Month and Year selects between the previous and next month arrows). A blue link-variant button under it, **Enter dates** (pencil icon), swaps the grid for the **fields view**: the Start and End rows, each label before its date and time on one line, typed or picked (each time field a `Combobox` that takes a typed time or lists the day in 30-minute steps, plus the current time when it falls between two, opened under the field and scrolled to the current time; the times are hidden with `showTime` off); there the link reads **Show calendar** and swaps back. Days picked on the grid fill the fields and typed values show on the grid. When the picker also offers relative ranges, an **End at now** checkbox sits beside the link in both views and makes a `since` range. Relative shows the quick ranges first, two columns when there is room (read down the first column, then the second), then, directly under them with no divider, a blue link-variant **Custom range** button (sliders icon; the custom duration in use is printed beside it); choosing it replaces the quick ranges with the Duration and Unit fields and a **Back to quick ranges** button, so the form stays out of the way until someone asks for it (owner decision RV-P2-1: the custom range reads as an action, not as one more quick range). The default quick ranges are Today, This week, Last minute, Last 5, 15 and 30 minutes, Last hour, Last 24 hours, Last 7, 30 and 90 days and Last year; `relativeOptions` replaces them. The panel opens on Relative unless the committed value is absolute or `since` (then Absolute). The panel does not name the time zone: the page states it beside the picker, always visible (`Times in UTC` or a Time zone select in the toolbar, see `blocks/view/events-explorer`), and the trigger of an absolute range carries its UTC offset. With `showTimeZone` the panel shows the time zone selector above Apply (a `Combobox`: type a city or a zone to filter the list), for a page that has no toolbar of its own to hold it. The footer starts with a compact **Refresh every** select, a ghost `Select` with a refresh glyph and a short label (`↻ 5 min`; Off, 10 sec … 1 hr; **5 minutes** by default), before Cancel and Apply on both tabs; it sets the auto-refresh interval whenever the panel offers relative ranges (`showRefresh` turns it off). Every select in the panel (Unit, Refresh every, the calendar's Month and Year) is the WebKit `Select`, never a native `select`. The panel commits only on Apply; Cancel and Escape drop the draft. Absolute boundaries are typed as wall-clock time in the selected zone and stored as instants, so the same value reads correctly in every zone. With `showStep`, Previous and Next move the range by its own length. On a phone (below 640 px) the panel is a full-width sheet at the bottom of the screen. Every range stays inside limits the page can set: `min` (unset: the start of the day five years ago), `max` (unset: the end of today; a later date allows future dates, for a maintenance window or an alert schedule) and `maxDuration` (unset: any length). They disable the days, months and years outside them in the calendar, drop the quick ranges that do not fit, and refuse a typed range or a custom duration that does not fit with a message. Date math uses `Intl` and the native `Date` only.

- Import: `import DateRangePicker from '@aziontech/webkit/date-range-picker'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use DateRangePicker for any start–end range: relative ('last 24 hours') or absolute, with or without times; turn times off for whole-day reports and billing periods. For one date use DatePicker; to display a moment in time use Timestamp.
- Filtering events, logs, traces or metrics by time, where "the last N minutes" must stay relative.
- Any range that needs times of day and a time zone, not only dates.
- Investigations that page through time window by window (`show-step`).
- Whole-day ranges for a report or a billing period: `range-selector-mode="absolute-only"` with `:show-time="false"`.
- Dashboards and live logs that re-run their query on a timer (`v-model:refresh-interval`, `@refresh`). Auto refresh is **on by default** (every 5 minutes), so every page must handle `@refresh` by re-running its query; a page that cannot re-run it passes `:show-refresh="false"` (or binds `v-model:refresh-interval` to `0` to start with it off).

## Do

- Keep relative and `since` values relative: resolve them to instants when the query runs (`now - amount × unit` to `now`, or `start` to `now`), never when the user picks them. `useTimeRange(value, { timeZone })` from `@aziontech/webkit/use-time-range` returns `from` and `to`, rounds `snap` ranges in the zone, and holds the window until `refresh()`; call that `refresh()` from `@refresh`. Its `TIME_RANGE_PRESETS` (last hour, 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days) go in `relative-options`.
- Fix the reference clock in tests, demos and server-rendered pages so labels and step limits are deterministic: `now` on the app's `ConfigProvider` covers every picker below it; the `now` prop overrides it for one picker.
- Bind `v-model:time-zone` to the user's saved preference, and show times elsewhere on the page in the same zone.
- Set `min` to the retention limit and `maxDuration` to the longest window the query can answer, instead of validating after Apply. The defaults (five years back to the end of today) suit logs and metrics; pass a later `max` only where a future range makes sense (a maintenance window, an alert schedule).
- State the time zone on the page, beside the picker and always visible (`Times in UTC`, or a Time zone `Select` when the person can change it), on every page that shows metrics and logs; the picker panel does not repeat it.
- Name the picker after what it filters (`aria-label="Events time range"`).
- Always handle `@refresh`: the picker refreshes every 5 minutes unless the page turns it off, so a page that ignores the event offers a refresh that does nothing.

## Don’t

- A single date or a date and time → use `date-picker`.
- A fixed list of named intervals and nothing custom → use `select` or `toggle-group`.

## Related

- `date-picker` — the trigger control, the panel, the month grid, the date and time fields and the time zone selector come from its internal parts, so both pickers look and behave the same. Split: DatePicker picks one date (optionally with a time); DateRangePicker owns every range and keeps a relative window relative.
- `timestamp` — displays a moment in time; both read the `ConfigProvider` `timeZone`.
- `config-provider` — its `timeZone` is the zone the picker formats in while `v-model:time-zone` is unbound.
- `field` — inside a `Field`, the trigger takes the field's label (`for` points at it), description, `invalid` and `disabled`.
- `property-filter` — the query bar it sits next to in an events toolbar.
- `chart` — the histogram whose brush usually writes an absolute range back into this picker.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `v-model:timeZone` | `string` | `''` | `update:timeZone` | IANA time zone the absolute range is typed and shown in; empty uses the local zone. Set on Apply after the zone changed in the panel. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `open`, `disabled`; the panel shows an inline error after an Apply that the draft cannot satisfy, and at once (without waiting for Apply) when both ends of an absolute range are set and the end is not after the start.
- `data-state="open|closed"` on the root and the panel; `data-size`; `data-disabled`; `data-invalid` on the root and the trigger shell (own `invalid` or the enclosing `Field`'s, with `aria-invalid` on the trigger and the danger border); `data-empty` on the trigger with no value; `data-selected` on the chosen quick range.
- The Next button is disabled while the range ends now (relative or `since`) or when the step would pass `max` (or now); Previous is disabled when the step would pass `min`.
- `data-view="quick|custom"` on the Relative tab body: `quick` lists the quick ranges and the Custom range row, `custom` shows the Duration (a `number-input` with no stepper buttons) and Unit fields in their place. `data-selected` on the Custom range row and on the custom duration group when the draft is a custom duration (no quick range picked); the row then also shows that duration (`Last 2 days`).
- Limits: days, months and years outside `min`/`max` are disabled in the calendar; while a start day is picked and the end is not, the days further than `maxDuration` from it are disabled too; quick ranges that start before `min` or run longer than `maxDuration` are not listed.
- With an auto-refresh interval above 0 the trigger's accessible name ends with the interval (`…, refreshes every 30 seconds`); the trigger draws no refresh glyph (owner 2026-11-18: the interval lives in the panel's Refresh every select).
- `data-view="calendar|fields"` on the Absolute tab body; `data-inline-labels` on its date fields.
- `data-side` (`bottom` | `top`) and `data-align` (`start`) on the calendar panel mirror where it landed after flipping; `start` follows the text direction, so under `rtl` the panel lines up with the field's right edge

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: a 2 px `--ring-color` ring inset on each trigger segment; the quick ranges ring their row when the radio inside has focus.
- Keyboard map: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens the panel and the focus trap moves into it; `Tab` cycles inside the panel; the range type is a `ToggleGroup` (arrow keys); the quick ranges are native radios (`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` move and select, down the first column and then the second, the order they are read in); Custom range is a link-variant button after them (`Enter`/`Space` shows the Duration and Unit fields and moves focus to Duration), and Back to quick ranges is the first button of that view (it returns to the list and focuses Custom range); on the Absolute tab the order is the grid (or the Start and End fields), End at now, then the view button: **Enter dates** (`Enter`/`Space` shows the fields and moves focus to the Start date) and **Show calendar** (`Enter`/`Space` shows the grid and moves focus to its focusable day); the End at now checkbox toggles with `Space`; then Refresh every, Cancel and Apply in the footer; Unit, Refresh every and the calendar's Month and Year are WebKit `Select`s (`Enter`/`Space`/`ArrowDown` open the list, the arrows move, typing jumps to an option, `Escape` closes only the list); the time zone selector is a `Combobox`; the range type lists Relative before Absolute; the grid keeps the `date-picker` keyboard map; a time field keeps the `combobox` keyboard map (focus or `ArrowDown` opens the 30-minute list, `Enter` takes the highlighted time or the typed one, `Escape` closes only the list); `Escape` closes without committing and returns focus to the trigger. On a phone a tap on the backdrop closes the sheet like Cancel.
- ARIA: the trigger has `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and a name that starts with the picker's label and contains the visible range and, with auto refresh on, the interval (inside a `Field` with no `ariaLabel`, the Field label names it and the trigger also carries the Field's `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`, plus `requiredId` when required); the panel is a named `dialog`; the custom duration is a `group` named "Custom range" whose duration and unit have visible labels; the quick ranges are a `fieldset` with a `legend`; End at now is a `checkbox` named by its visible `label`; the view switch is a native `button` named by its visible text; Unit is a `combobox` button (WebKit `Select`) labelled by its visible text through `aria-labelledby`, and Refresh every is a `combobox` button named "Refresh every" by `aria-label` (it shows only the glyph and the short interval); the calendar's Month and Year selects are named `Month` and `Year`; the error is `role="alert"` and described from the duration field; Previous and Next are named buttons; the sheet backdrop is `aria-hidden`.
- Targets: options are 32 px high (44 px on `pointer: coarse`); the selects are 44 px high and the step buttons 44 px wide on `pointer: coarse`.
- The custom duration is one two-column grid (a third for the duration, two thirds for the Unit select); Refresh every, Cancel and Apply share the footer row, Refresh every at the start edge and the buttons at the end edge, in both directions (checked at 320, 390 and 1280 px, and right-to-left at 390 px, in `src/test/date-picker-readability.test.ts`).
- Quick ranges layout: the `legend` and every option are padded `var(--spacing-xs)` inline, so the heading and the option labels start on one inline edge in both directions (checked left-to-right and right-to-left in `src/test/date-picker-readability.test.ts`).
- Initial focus: with `rangeSelectorMode="relative-only"` (no range-type toggle) the focus trap lands on the checked quick range, the one the trigger shows, or on Custom range when the value is a custom duration.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

# Field

> One composable form field that wraps **any** control — `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `NumberInput`, `PasswordInput`, `PhoneInput`, `InputGroup`, `Combobox`, `DatePicker`, `DateRangePicker`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `Slider` — with its label, description and error. The root `Field` owns the field state (`invalid`, `disabled`, `required`) and the ids, and shares them through `provide`/`inject`: the control picks up its `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `disabled` and `required` from the Field, `Field.Label` points its `for` at the control and shows the Required marker, and `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` register themselves so the control is described by them. Grouping parts (`Field.Set`, `Field.Legend`, `Field.Group`, `Field.Content`, `Field.Title`, `Field.Separator`) build fieldsets, choice cards and settings rows. One anatomy serves every control, so there is no per-control field wrapper.

- Import: `import FieldRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/field-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Field (Field.Label, Field.Description, Field.Error) around every form control; it wires the id, the required marker and the error for you. Field.Description and Field.Error also work alone, under a control that is not inside a Field; for an optional explanation beside a label (a click-open note) use Hint; information needed to fill the field goes in Field.Description.
- Any labelled form control: a text input, a select, a textarea, a password, a phone number, a slider.
- A checkbox, radio or switch with its label beside it (`orientation="horizontal"`).
- A selectable checkbox or switch card: `Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field` (replaces the v5 `*-block` variants). For one choice among cards use `RadioGroup variant="card"`, never a radio inside a `Field.Label`.
- A group of related controls under one caption (`Field.Set` + `Field.Legend`), or a form section (`Field.Group`).

## Do

- Put the state on the `Field`, not on the control: `<Field invalid>` sets `aria-invalid` on the control and the invalid tone on `Field.Description`.
- Set `required` on the `Field` from the first render, never only after a submit: it shows the Required marker on `Field.Label` and sets `required` on the control, and nothing turns a warning colour. A required field submitted empty is `invalid`, with a `Field.Error` that says what to enter; it turns red only then.
- Let the Field own the ids. Pass an explicit `id` on the control and `for` on `Field.Label` only when another part of the page needs the id (focusing the first invalid field, an error summary link).
- Render `Field.Description` for guidance and `Field.Error` for a validation message; both are announced through `aria-describedby`. `Field.Error` has `role="alert"`, so render it only when there is an error.
- Choice cards: `<Field.Label><Field orientation="horizontal">control + Field.Content</Field></Field.Label>`. Never nest a choice card inside another `Field`; group cards with `Field.Set`.
- Use `orientation="responsive"` for settings rows that stack in a narrow container and sit side by side in a wide one; it follows the nearest container (a `Field.Group`, a Card, a dialog or drawer body).

## Don’t

- A control with no visible label inside a toolbar or a table cell → render the control alone with an `aria-label`.
- A group of mutually exclusive cards with icons → use `radio-group` with `type="card"`.
- A static key/value read-out → use `key-value-list`.

## Related

- `input-group` — wraps an input with addons; put it inside a `Field` and use `InputGroup.Input` as the control.
- `phone-input`, `password-requirements` — a phone number control and the live password rules row, each placed inside a `Field`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'responsive'` | `'vertical'` | false | Layout axis: label above the control, beside it, or beside it once the enclosing container (a FieldGroup, Card, drawer or dialog body) is wide enough. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field invalid: the control sets aria-invalid and FieldDescription switches to the invalid tone. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the wrapped control and dims the field. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the Required marker on FieldLabel and sets required on the wrapped control. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | `Field.Label`, the control, `Field.Description`, `Field.Error` (or `Field.Content` beside the control in a horizontal field). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/field-label`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-error`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-set`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-legend`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-separator`

## Sub-components

The root `Field` provides `FieldInjectionKey` (`injection-key.ts`): a generated `controlId`, the reactive `invalid` / `disabled` / `required` flags, `describedBy` (the ids of the mounted `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` parts), `labelledBy` (the ids of the mounted `Field.Title` parts), `requiredId` (id of the hidden "Required" text in `Field.Label`) and `register`. Controls read it through the shared `useFieldControl` composable (`src/composables/use-field-control`); an explicit prop or attribute on the control always wins over the Field, except `aria-describedby`: the control's own ids are joined with the Field's description and error ids (deduplicated), so a consumer description never hides the Field's error. Composite controls (`Select`, `MultiSelect`, `PhoneInput`) consume the context on their root and provide `null` below it, so their inner search inputs never take the field id. Every part works outside a `Field` too (it then reads no state). Member names mirror the anatomy; there is no `Trigger`/`Content` pair because the field has no open/closed state.

- `field-label/field-label.vue` — `<label>` whose `for` defaults to the Field's `controlId`; appends the Required marker (a lone `*`, hidden from assistive tech) and, in a required Field, a `hidden` "Required" text (`re…
  - Props: `hint` (`string`, default `''`) — short explanation, one to three sentences, in a `Hint` glyph that opens it on click. Clicking the glyph never toggles or focuses the labelled control.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — label text, or a horizontal `Field` for a choice card.
- `field-description/field-description.vue` — guidance line in the label-sm text style; registers its id with the Field.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-error/field-error.vue` — validation message in `--text-danger` led by an `az az-circle-alert` icon (`aria-hidden`, test id `${testId}__icon`), with `role="alert"`; registers its id with the Field, and while it…
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-group/field-group.vue` — vertical stack of fields; it is a `@container/field-group`, one of the containers `orientation="responsive"` can follow.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-set/field-set.vue` — native `<fieldset>` without browser chrome, for a group of related fields or choices.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-legend/field-legend.vue` — native `<legend>` captioning a `Field.Set`.
  - Props: `type` (`'legend' \| 'label'`, default `'legend'`) — `legend` titles a section, `label` matches a `Field.Label` for a group of choices.
  - Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-content/field-content.vue` — column that holds the label/title and descriptions beside a control in a horizontal Field.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-title/field-title.vue` — title inside a choice card; registers its id with the Field so the card's `Checkbox` or `Switch` is named by it through `aria-labelledby` (the wrapping `Field.Label` makes the whole car…
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-separator/field-separator.vue` — horizontal rule between fields, with optional centred text.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default` — optional text.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `required`
- `data-orientation`: `vertical` | `horizontal` | `responsive`
- `data-invalid`, `data-disabled`, `data-required` mirror the props on the root; `data-invalid` is also set while a `Field.Error` is mounted
- `data-slot` identifies every part (`field`, `field-label`, `field-description`, `field-error`, `field-group`, `field-set`, `field-legend`, `field-content`, `field-title`, `field-separator`)
- Responsive: `orientation="responsive"` queries the nearest container (`@md:`), not only `Field.Group`: inside a Card, a drawer or dialog body (`@container/panel`), a settings section or a `Field.Group` it stacks the label above the control in a narrow box and puts them side by side from `@md`. With no container ancestor it stays vertical.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the control keeps its own ring; a choice card shows `has-[:focus-visible]:ring-2 ring-(--ring-color) ring-offset-1 ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` around the whole card.
- Keyboard map: the Field adds no keys; `Tab` reaches the control, and clicking `Field.Label` focuses or toggles it.
- ARIA: root `role="group"`; `Field.Label` `for` → control `id`; control `aria-describedby` → every mounted `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` id; control `aria-invalid` when the Field is `invalid` or a `Field.Error` is mounted; `required` / `aria-required` when it is `required`; `Field.Error` `role="alert"`; `Field.Set` is a native `fieldset` named by its `legend`; the `*` is `aria-hidden`; a control whose role cannot take `aria-required` (DatePicker, DateRangePicker, FileDropzone, TagEditor) adds `requiredId` to its `aria-describedby`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for label, description and error text in every tone, including disabled.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the choice card transition.
- Touch target: the whole choice card is the target; a horizontal Field's label extends the control's target.

# File Dropzone

> A FileDropzone is the target a user drags files from the operating system onto. It owns the drag lifecycle (only drags carrying `Files` count), the `accept` / `multiple` filtering, and the idle/active look, and it hands the result back as two activation events: `drop` with the accepted files, `reject` with the files it filtered out. It holds no value and renders no file list. The list, upload progress and validation messages belong to the consumer (typically a `Field` around this component, whose `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` carry the messages). `variant` covers the two places a drop target lives: - **`inline`**: a dashed region that is always visible (icon, title, description, plus a default slot for the "Browse files" action the consumer composes). It switches to the active look while files are dragged over it. This is the Cloudscape FileDropzone / Cloudflare Pages "Upload assets" shape. - **`overlay`**: invisible at rest. When files are dragged into the window it fades in over its nearest positioned ancestor (`absolute inset-0`), and it fades out on window drag-leave, drop or `Escape`. This is the Vercel "drag and drop a folder to deploy" shape, and it replaces the sample app's page-level `ProjectDropZone` and the drop target in the project intake block (`Blocks/State/StateProjectIntake`). The drop target itself is pointer-only. It is never a keyboard control. The keyboard (and screen-reader) path to the same outcome is a real button the consumer puts in the default slot (`inline`), or elsewhere on the page (`overlay`).

- Import: `import FileDropzone from '@aziontech/webkit/file-dropzone'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A form or settings surface accepts one or more files and should also accept them by drag (`variant="inline"` with a Browse button in the slot).
- A whole page or card should accept a project, folder contents or assets dropped anywhere on it, with no permanent drop region taking up space (`variant="overlay"` inside a `relative` container).
- The consumer needs the accepted and rejected files separated by an `accept` filter before it uploads anything.

## Do

- Always give the user a non-drag path. In `inline`, put a `Button` in the default slot that opens the system file picker through `useFilePicker`. In `overlay`, keep an upload button somewhere on the page. The drop target is pointer-only by design.
- Pass the same `accept` string to the dropzone and to the native input behind your Browse button, so both paths filter the same way.
- Handle `reject`. Tell the user which files were skipped and why (e.g. a `toast` naming the files and the accepted types). A silent rejection reads as a broken drop.
- Announce the outcome of a drop yourself (a toast, or a live region on your file list). The dropzone does not announce drag states (see Accessibility).
- Render one `overlay` dropzone per positioned container, and make the container `relative`. Without a positioned ancestor the overlay covers the nearest positioned element up the tree, which may be the whole page.
- Place the `overlay` dropzone as the last child of its container, so it paints above the container's other positioned content (see Theme gaps).
- When the consumer's own flow is busy (an upload in progress), set `disabled` and disable the Browse button too.
- Put the accepted types and limits in `description` ("PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB"). The title is the instruction, the description is the constraint.

## Don’t

- Picking files by keyboard or click only, with no drag affordance → a `button` that opens a native file input is enough.
- Showing the chosen files, their progress or their errors → render them yourself with `progress`, `message` or `field-error`. The dropzone renders none of these.
- Dragging items inside the page (reordering rows, moving cards) → this component only reacts to OS drags that carry `Files`. In-page drag and drop is out of scope.
- A static "nothing here yet" panel with no drop behavior → use `empty-state`.

## Related

- `button`: the "Browse files" action composed into the default slot. It is the keyboard path to the same outcome as a drop.
- `empty-state`: a no-data panel. Compose a FileDropzone inside or beside it when the empty state's call to action is "upload".
- `progress`: the consumer renders per-file progress after `drop`. The dropzone does not track uploads.
- `toast`: confirms the result of a drop or reports rejected files to everyone, including users who never see the drag.
- `card`: a positioned container (`class="relative"`) that hosts an `overlay` dropzone.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'inline' \| 'overlay'` | `'inline'` | false | Placement. Inline is an always-visible dashed region; overlay stays hidden until files are dragged over the window, then covers its nearest positioned ancestor. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Instruction shown under the icon. Empty uses the locale catalog: `Drop files to upload`, or `Choose files to upload` inline on a coarse pointer. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Secondary line under the title, typically the accepted types and limits. Not rendered when empty. |
| `accept` | `string` | `''` | false | Comma-separated file filter using the native input accept syntax (extensions, MIME types, type wildcards). Files that do not match are rejected. Empty accepts every file. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When false, only the first accepted file of a drop is accepted and the rest are rejected. `true` by default (recorded exception to the default-false rule; inverting it would break consumers). |
| `directories` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Accepts dropped folders: walks every dropped folder and emits the files inside, each with its `webkitRelativePath` (`assets/img/logo.svg`). The events fire after the walk. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Ignores drags and drops: no active state, no events. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Paints the inline region with the danger border so a wrapping field can show a validation error. Drops still work. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Azion icon class for the glyph above the title. Empty draws the cloud-upload glyph (`az az-cloud-upload`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `drop` | `(event: DragEvent, files: File[])` | Activation event. Fires when files are dropped on the target (the inline root, or the visible overlay) and at least one passes `accept` / `multiple`. `files` holds only the accepted files, in `dataTransfer.files` order, and is never empty. Not emitted when `disabled`. Declaring `drop` means a consumer `@drop` listener binds to this event, never to the native DOM `drop` on the root. |
| `reject` | `(event: DragEvent, files: File[])` | Activation event. Fires on the same drop when one or more files were filtered out, because they do not match `accept` or exceed `multiple="false"`. `files` holds only the rejected files and is never empty. When a drop has both variants of file, `drop` fires first, then `reject`, with the same `event`. Not emitted when `disabled`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Actions or extra content under the description, typically a "Browse files" `Button`. Rendered only in `variant="inline"`. The overlay is `aria-hidden` decoration, so interactive content there would be unreachable and is not rendered. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `idle`, `active` (files dragged over the target), `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `idle` | `active`
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop (`inline` | `overlay`)
- `data-disabled` is present when the `disabled` prop is true. A disabled dropzone is always `data-state="idle"`.
- `data-invalid` is present when the `invalid` prop is true.
- **Inline / invalid**: the dashed border turns `--danger-border` while idle; the active state still wins while files are dragged over it. Overlay ignores `invalid`.
- **Inline / idle**: dashed `--border-input` border (the field outline, so it reads like the other inputs and never glares) on a `--bg-surface` fill; on hover the dashes step up to `--border-strong`, as an input outline does. Icon, title, description and slot are centered.
- **Inline / active**: the border turns `--border-selected` and the fill `--bg-selected`. Layout does not move (same border width in both states).
- **Inline / disabled**: `--border-default` dashed border, `--bg-disabled` fill, icon, title and description in `--text-disabled`, `cursor-not-allowed`. The slot still renders, and the consumer disables its own Browse button.
- **Overlay / idle**: not displayed (`v-show`). The root stays in the DOM so `data-testid` and `$attrs` are always present.
- **Overlay / active**: `absolute inset-0` over the nearest positioned ancestor. 2px dashed `--border-selected` border on a `--bg-canvas` fill, `--shape-card` radius. The content column sits in a `sticky top-0` wrapper capped at the viewport height (`h-dvh max-h-full`), so the prompt stays centered in the viewport even when the ancestor is taller than the screen (the page-level case). It receives pointer events while active so the drop lands on it, and `data-[state=idle]:pointer-events-none` keeps the fade-out from swallowing clicks.
- No `loading`, `empty` or `error` state: the dropzone does not upload, validate or list anything. `invalid` only paints the border; the message and the file list belong to the consumer (compose it inside a `Field`).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the dropzone root is **not focusable** and has no focus ring. Focus belongs to the controls in the default slot, which carry their own `focus-visible` ring (e.g. `Button`).
- Keyboard map: none on the dropzone. Drag and drop from the OS is a pointer gesture with no keyboard equivalent on the target. The keyboard path is the consumer's Browse button, which opens a native file input and reaches the same outcome. `Escape` during a drag hides the overlay (window `keydown` fallback; browsers also cancel the drag natively).
- No `@click` on the root: clicking the region does nothing, so there is no click-without-key handler. The Browse button is the click target.
- ARIA, inline: the root is a `<div role="group">` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title and `aria-describedby` pointing at the description (only when `description` is non-empty), both ids from `useId()`. A screen reader therefore reads the slotted Browse button in context ("Drop files to upload, group, PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB each, Browse files, button"). The title is a `<p>`, not a heading: the page owns its heading outline. When `disabled`, the group carries `aria-disabled="true"`, so the dimmed title and description are announced as part of a disabled control and fall under the WCAG 1.4.3 exemption for inactive components.
- Inside a `Field` (inline): the group reads the field through `useFieldControl` — it takes the field's `id`, prepends `Field.Title` to `aria-labelledby`, appends `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` to `aria-describedby`, sets `aria-invalid` from the field's (or its own) `invalid`, adds `requiredId` to `aria-describedby` when required, and the field's `disabled` disables it (`aria-disabled`, drops ignored).
- ARIA, overlay: the root is `aria-hidden="true"`. It is a pointer-only duplicate of an affordance that must exist elsewhere on the page, and it renders no interactive content.
- No `aria-live` in the component. Announcing every drag that crosses the window is noise, and the outcome that matters (files accepted or skipped) is the consumer's to announce from `drop` / `reject` (a `toast`, or a live region on its file list). `aria-dropeffect` / `aria-grabbed` are deprecated in WAI-ARIA 1.1 and are not used.
- The icon is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"`.
- `data-disabled` has no ARIA mirror because the root is not a control. The slotted button carries its own `disabled` / `aria-disabled`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the title and description in both themes, including `--text-muted` on `--bg-selected` (inline active) and on `--bg-canvas` (overlay). The `webkit-ui-verifier` must confirm the active state in both themes, since the unit suite has no CSS. The dashed border (`--border-strong` idle, `--border-selected` active) must meet 3:1 non-text contrast against the surrounding surface.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on both overlay fades, `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the inline colour transition.
- Touch target: not applicable. The region is not a control (touch devices cannot drag OS files into a page), and the slotted Button carries its own ≥40×40 px target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import FileDropzone from '@aziontech/webkit/file-dropzone'
  import { useFilePicker } from '@aziontech/webkit/use-file-picker'

  const picker = useFilePicker({ multiple: true })
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <FileDropzone description="Or browse for files on your computer.">
      <Button
        label="Browse files"
        variant="secondary"
        size="medium"
        @click="picker.open()"
      />
    </FileDropzone>
  </div>
</template>
```

# File Token Group

> Use FileTokenGroup for the files picked in a form field, before and during upload; a transfer that runs in the background while the person keeps working is an UploadProgress. The files a person picked for upload, shown as removable tokens before or while they upload: each token names the file with a glyph for its type, its size and, when asked, its last-modified date, carries a progress bar while it uploads and its own error or warning line when it cannot be sent. It pairs with `file-dropzone` (which receives the files) and with a Browse files button: the product keeps the list, the group renders it and reports which token was removed. Taken from Cloudscape's file token group; the Console Kit and the design sample list files by hand.

- Import: `import FileTokenGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/file-token-group'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Under a `FileDropzone` or a Browse files button in a form, to show what will be uploaded and let the person drop a file before submitting.
- In an upload dialog, to show each file's progress and the files that were refused (too large, wrong type) with the reason.
- Read-only, in a review step, to list the attachments that will be sent.

## Do

- Keep the refused files in the list with their error, so the person sees why and can remove them; do not drop them silently.
- Write each error as the reason and the limit (`Larger than 300 MB`), not as a code.
- Use `limit` when more than five files are common, so the form below stays in view.
- Remove the file from your list on `remove`; the group moves focus to the next token for you.

## Don’t

- A running transfer that should follow the person around the console → use `upload-progress`.
- Files already stored in a bucket or a repository → use `table` (the file browser block).
- Free-text tags or labels → use `tag-editor` or `chip`.

## Related

- `file-dropzone` — receives dropped files; the group lists them.
- `upload-progress` — the floating card for transfers that keep running after the dialog closes. Split: FileTokenGroup lists the files picked in a form, before and while they are sent, and dies with the form; UploadProgress tracks transfers that outlive the dialog, with Cancel and Retry. Both draw a file row with a progress bar; when a transfer must survive navigation, hand it to UploadProgress instead of keeping the token.
- `chip` — a removable label without file details.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `FileTokenGroupItem[]` | `[]` | false | The files, in order; each with its optional upload state, error and warning. |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | false | Vertical stacks full-width tokens; horizontal wraps compact tokens in rows. Same name as `field`'s axis. |
| `limit` | `number` | `0` | false | Shows this many tokens and a Show more toggle for the rest. 0 shows them all. |
| `showFileSize` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the size beside the name, formatted for the locale. |
| `showFileLastModified` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the last-modified date, formatted for the locale. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Hides the remove buttons; the list is for reading only. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Files`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remove` | `(event: MouseEvent, payload: { index: number; item: FileTokenGroupItem })` | The remove button of the token at `index` was pressed. The parent removes it from `items`. Same name as Chip and AttributeEditor. |

## States

- Root `data-orientation`: `vertical` | `horizontal`; `data-readonly` when read-only.
- Token `data-status`: `idle` | `loading` | `warning` | `error` (error wins over warning, both over loading).
- Show more toggle: `aria-expanded` `true` | `false`.
- A file with a `webkitRelativePath` (picked with a folder picker or dropped as a folder on `FileDropzone directories`) is named by that path (`site/css/main.css`) in the token, its title, the remove button and the progress bar; otherwise by `name`.

## Accessibility

- The root is a `ul` (`role="list"`) named by `ariaLabel` or the catalog; each token is a `li`.
- Each remove button is an `IconButton` named `Remove <file name>`, and `Cancel upload of <file name>` while the file uploads (the same `remove` event); its `aria-describedby` points at the token's error or warning line, so the reason is read with it.
- Keyboard map: Tab reaches each remove button and the Show more toggle in order; Enter or Space removes. After a removal focus moves to the remove button now at the same index, else the previous one, else the list itself (`tabindex="-1"`).
- An error or warning is shown as text with an icon, never by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1); the uploading bar is a `progressbar` named `Uploading <file name>`, and the meta line states the amount as text beside the size (`242.5 kB · 64%`, or `Uploading…` while the progress is unknown), so a stuck upload reads apart from a moving one.
- Contrast: name and meta ≥ 4.5:1 on `--bg-surface` in both themes; the danger border ≥ 3:1.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import FileDropzone from '@aziontech/webkit/file-dropzone'
  import FileTokenGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/file-token-group'
  import { useFilePicker } from '@aziontech/webkit/use-file-picker'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const LIMIT = 300 * 1024 * 1024

  const picker = useFilePicker({ multiple: true })
  const items = ref([
    { file: { name: 'logo.svg', size: 4210, type: 'image/svg+xml' } },
    { file: { name: 'index.html', size: 18432, type: 'text/html' } },
    { file: { name: 'site-backup.tar', size: 412_000_000 }, error: 'Larger than 300 MB' },
    { file: { name: 'notes.txt', size: 0, type: 'text/plain' }, warning: 'This file is empty' }
  ])

  const toItem = (file) => ({
    file,
    error: file.size > LIMIT ? 'Larger than 300 MB' : undefined,
    warning: file.size === 0 ? 'This file is empty' : undefined
  })

  const add = (files) => {
    items.value = [...items.value, ...Array.from(files).map(toItem)]
  }

  const browse = async () => add(await picker.open())

  const remove = (index) => {
    items.value = items.value.filter((_, position) => position !== index)
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-md) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <FileDropzone
      description="Up to 300 MB per file."
      @drop="(event, files) => add(files)"
    >
      <Button
        label="Browse files"
        variant="secondary"
        size="medium"
        @click="browse"
      />
    </FileDropzone>
    <FileTokenGroup
      :items="items"
      @remove="(_event, { index }) => remove(index)"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/hint.md -->

# Hint

> Click-open note (a "toggletip") on a small muted `az az-circle-info` glyph. A click, a tap, `Enter` or `Space` on the glyph opens a small panel, anchored below the glyph and aligned to its start, that holds one to three sentences and an optional "Learn more" link to the docs. It is level C of the in-product help standard: the way to attach a "why does this matter?" note to a field name, a setting or a column header without spending a line of vertical space on it. `Field.Label`, `SettingsRow` and `SettingsGroup` render it from their own `hint` prop.

- Import: `import Hint from '@aziontech/webkit/hint'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A field, switch or setting whose name is clear but whose consequence is not (what "Sensitive" does to a stored value).
- A note of one to three sentences that is useful but not needed to complete the task, optionally with a link to the docs page that explains more.
- Beside a label, a heading, a stat or a column header, where a permanent line of helper text would add noise.

## Do

- One to three plain sentences, each ending in a period.
- Place the glyph 4px after the label text, on the same line. Never at the end of the row, never on its own line.
- One Hint per label. Never stack two glyphs, and never put a Hint inside a Tooltip or another Hint.
- Never draw a typed "?" or a boxed icon button as a help trigger; Hint is the only help glyph.
- Add `href` when a docs page explains more; leave `linkLabel` empty for the localized "Learn more".
- Never hide required information behind a Hint.

## Don’t

- Information needed to fill the field → `field-description`, which stays on screen.
- Naming a control or expanding an abbreviation → `tooltip`.
- Help longer than three sentences, steps or several links → `help-panel`.
- Validation messages → `field-error`.

## Related

- `field-description` — level A, the default: a short muted line under the field that is always visible.
- `tooltip` — level B: names a control or expands an abbreviation in a few words (about 80 characters at most).
- `help-panel` — level D: page-level help in the console's tools region, opened from an "Info" link after the page title.
- `popover` — the overlay Hint composes; use it for interactive content.
- `Field.Label`, `settings-row`, `settings-group` — render a Hint from their `hint` prop.
- `/webkit-in-product-help` — the consumer skill that picks the level of help.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `string` | `''` | true | The note, one to three sentences, shown when the glyph is clicked and read as the glyph's description. |
| `side` | `'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'start' \| 'end' \| 'auto'` | `'bottom'` | false | Side of the glyph the note opens on, flipped when it does not fit; `'auto'` picks the side with the most room. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | Docs URL linked under the note; empty renders no link. |
| `linkLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the docs link; empty uses the locale catalog (`Learn more`). |
| `target` | `'_blank' \| '_self'` | `'_blank'` | false | Where the docs link opens. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the glyph button; empty uses the locale catalog (`More information`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`. Fires on every open and close: glyph click, `Enter`, `Space`, `Esc`, outside click. Unbound, the Hint keeps its own state. |

## States

- Visual states of the glyph: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, open (`aria-expanded="true"`, the glyph takes `var(--text-default)`).
- `data-state` values (on the root, owned by `Popover`): `open` | `closed`.
- `data-side` (on the root and the panel, owned by `Popover`): the side the panel landed on.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a native `<button type="button">` named by `ariaLabel` (fallback `More information`, from the locale catalog). It carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` (from `Popover.Trigger`).
- The note is also in an always-rendered `hidden` element the button points at with `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader reads the note on focus without opening the panel.
- The panel is `role="dialog"` (non-modal), named by the trigger. It opens on activation only, never on hover.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the glyph; `Enter` or `Space` opens and closes the note; opening moves focus to the docs link when there is one; `Esc` closes and returns focus to the glyph. A second click or an outside click also closes it.
- The click default is prevented, so a Hint inside a `<label>` never toggles or focuses the labelled control.
- The glyph is decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`); the focus ring uses `var(--ring-color)`.
- Touch target: a `[data-slot=touch-target]` span extends the 20 px glyph's hit area to 24 px, and to 44 px on a coarse pointer.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Hint from '@aziontech/webkit/hint'
</script>

<template>
  <Hint content="Values are encrypted at rest and never displayed again after saving." />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/hint.md](components/hint.md).
