<!-- components/input.md -->

# Input

> Single-line text input for forms and inline editing. Renders a bordered field with optional leading/trailing icon slots. Visual states (hover, focus, filled) are driven by native CSS pseudo-classes, not props. The component is the field only — labels, helper text, and error messages live in the wrapping form-field layer. Aligned with Figma frame `562:6774` (Webkit / Input).

- Import: `import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Capture a single line of free-form text (names, titles, search terms).
- Use Input with a search icon to filter a list in place; to open the ⌘K palette use SearchTrigger.

## Do

- Wrap it in `Field` when you need a label, helper text, or validation message.
- Set an appropriate `type`/`inputmode` for the content (email, url, …).
- Set `monospace` on a field whose value is code-like: a CLI command, an ID, a token, a hash, a path. Pair it with `:spellcheck="false"`.
- A read-only command or ID the user copies: `readonly` + `monospace` inside an `InputGroup` with a `CopyButton`, and a description saying why it cannot change.
- Do not set `monospace` on prose values (names, titles, e-mails, domains typed by the user).
- Do not restyle a read-only field (dashed border, transparent fill): it is the same filled field, made non-editable; the reason belongs in the field's description.

## Don’t

- The value spans multiple lines → use `textarea`.
- The value is strictly numeric → use `number-input`.
- The user must choose from a fixed set → use `select` / `multi-select`.

## Related

- `textarea` — multi-line free text.
- `number-input` — numeric input with stepper semantics.
- `field` — wraps this input with label, description and error; the input reads its id, `aria-describedby` and state from it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder shown when the field is empty. |
| `type` | `'text' \| 'email'` | `'text'` | false | Native input type. Restricted to single-line text variants the field treats identically; a number is `number-input`, a secret `password-input`, a phone `phone-input`, a date `date-picker`. |
| `maxLength` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `maxlength` — maximum number of characters allowed. |
| `autocomplete` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `autocomplete` token on the `<input>` (e.g. `email`, `username`, `off`). Omitted when unset. |
| `spellcheck` | `boolean \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `spellcheck` on the `<input>`. Set `false` for slugs, IDs and domains; `false` also sets `autocapitalize="none"` and `autocorrect="off"`, so a phone does not capitalize a case-sensitive key (a passed attribute wins). Omitted when unset: the default is an explicit `undefined`, because Vue would otherwise cast an absent boolean to `false` and render `spellcheck="false"` on every field. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects height only — padding and typography are constant. Heights: small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only: value is visible, focusable and copyable but not editable. Keeps the filled field (surface and solid border) with no hover border and a default cursor (`data-readonly`); distinct from the disabled field. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; sets native `required` and `aria-required`. Visual indicator (asterisk) is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid`. |
| `monospace` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Sets the value and placeholder in the monospace code face (`.text-label-code-sm`) for CLI commands, IDs, tokens and hashes (`data-monospace`). |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` |  | Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). Logical: it sits on the right under `dir="rtl"`. |
| `trailing` |  | Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The field value via `defineModel`; updates on every native `input` event. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`
- Password managers: the `<input>` carries `data-1p-ignore`, `data-lpignore`, `data-bwignore` and `data-form-type="other"` unless it is a credential or identity field — `autocomplete` set to any token but `off`. `type="email"` alone does not count: a profile or settings address is not a sign-in, so a login or contact field states `autocomplete` (`username`, `email`). A read-only field always carries them. This keeps 1Password, LastPass, Bitwarden and Dashlane from offering a sign-in on ordinary fields (names, IDs, searches) while login fields stay fillable. A consumer attr (e.g. `data-1p-ignore="false"`) wins.
- `data-readonly` mirrors the `readonly` prop: a read-only field keeps the editable field's fill (`var(--bg-surface)`) and solid `var(--border-default)` border, as the design sample draws it; it only drops the hover border and takes a default cursor. The value keeps `var(--text-default)` (readable and copyable, unlike `disabled`) and the field stays focusable. Why the value cannot change is said by the field's description, not by a different chrome.
- `data-monospace` mirrors the `monospace` prop: the value and the placeholder render in `.text-label-code-sm` instead of `.text-label-sm`.
- `data-slot="input"` marks the root, so an `InputGroup` that holds the field drops its border and radius and the group's own frame is the only line around it
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop; it draws no border of its own: the Required marker on the wrapping `Field.Label` says a field is required, and a missing value is shown as `invalid` after a failed submit
- `data-leading` / `data-trailing` mirror slot presence (driven by `$slots.leading` / `$slots.trailing`), read at render time: an icon slot passed behind a `v-if` adds or removes its icon box when the condition changes, never leaving an empty box behind
- `filled` is detected via the native `:not(:placeholder-shown)` selector — no JS state

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2`, with the offset color resolving `var(--input-ring-offset, var(--bg-canvas))` — applied via `focus-within` on the field wrapper so the ring covers the whole control including icon slots. A host that places the field on a surface other than the canvas (a raised popover, a drawer) declares `--input-ring-offset` on any ancestor; custom properties inherit, so one declaration retunes the ring gap of every field inside it (this is how `date-picker`'s fields panel matches its raised popover).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the input; standard text-editing keys apply.
- Direction: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"` so a value typed in another script keeps its own direction inside right-to-left UI; a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: `aria-invalid` is bound to the `invalid` prop; `aria-required` to the `required` prop; icon slots are `aria-hidden="true"` (decorative).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition-bearing class.
- Touch target: drawn 28 / 32 / 40 px tall by `size` on every pointer; on a coarse pointer an invisible `aria-hidden` child (`data-slot="touch-target"`) shown only under `pointer-coarse:` extends the hit area to at least 44 px tall (a tap on it focuses the field). The drawn field does not grow, so it keeps lining up with the buttons beside it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <Field class="w-full max-w-(--container-xs)">
    <Field.Label>Project name</Field.Label>
    <Input
      v-model="value"
      placeholder="my-project"
    />
  </Field>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/input.md](components/input.md).

<!-- components/input-group.md -->

# Input Group

> Composition container that joins an input primitive with any number of adjacent controls (buttons, selects, static addons) into a single visual field (an input group, as other UI kits call it). The root only orchestrates: it draws the outer border, the `focus-within` ring, and applies inline Tailwind child-selectors so the first child rounds only on the left, the last only on the right, and internal borders collapse between siblings. Everything else is a **child**: the middle input is a raw `<input>` in the root's `default` slot; sibling controls (`<Button>`, `<Select>`, `<Input>`, or an `<InputGroup.Addon>` for static text like `https://` / `.com` / `$`) are dropped in directly alongside it. This is a breaking change from v3: the `#left` and `#right` named slots are gone — their static-text role moves to `<InputGroup.Addon>`, and their interactive role is served by placing the real component (`Button`, `Select`) as a direct child. Consumers therefore never wrap `Button`/`Select` in an inner `<div>` — the root's child selectors do that job.

- Import: `import InputGroupRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import InputGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A text input that needs static prefix or suffix content inside the same border (`https://`, `.com`, a currency symbol).
- An input joined to a control: a search field with a trailing `button`, an amount with a leading currency `select`.

## Do

- Put static text and icons in `InputGroup.Addon`; place real controls (`button`, `select`) as direct children with no wrapper `div`.
- Set the same `size` on the group and on its child controls so heights line up.
- `disabled` and `invalid` on the group reach every field control inside (`InputGroup.Input`, `Input`, `Select` and the other controls that read the Field context); a `Button` or `IconButton` in the group needs its own `disabled`. `required` only mirrors to `data-required` on the group; set it on the input or on the enclosing `Field`, whose label carries the Required marker. Inside a `Field`, the Field's state reaches the root and the controls the same way.
- Use `InputGroup.Input` for the middle input: it is borderless, picks up the enclosing `Field`'s wiring, and spares the long raw-`<input>` class string. An `Input` placed in the group loses its own border and radius (the group reads its `data-slot="input"`), so the group's frame and its dividers stay the only lines: the group never doubles a line.
- The root is `role="group"`; label the inner input itself, or give the group an `aria-label`.

## Don’t

- A phone number with a dial code → use `phone-input`.
- A single input with only a decorative icon → use `input` and its `iconLeft` / `iconRight` slots.

## Related

- `field` — wrap the group in a `Field` for a label and description/error; `InputGroup.Input` takes the field's id, `aria-describedby` and state, and the root takes `invalid` / `disabled` / `required` from it.
- `phone-input` — input group with a dial-code select and a per-country mask.
- `input` — the single-field primitive with icon slots.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects the root's height and inner addon padding. Heights: small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px. Matches the sibling input primitives (`Input`, `Select`) — set the same `size` on child controls to keep them visually aligned. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the error border and marks the field controls inside invalid (`aria-invalid` on the input, never on the `role="group"` root, where ARIA does not allow it). |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Mirrors to `data-required` on the group and draws no border of its own. `aria-required` is not allowed on `role="group"`, so the required state belongs on the input (`InputGroup.Input` reads it from the Field). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the disabled visual, sets `aria-disabled="true"` on the root and disables the field controls inside (`InputGroup.Input`, `Input`, `Select`, …) through the Field context. A `Button` or `IconButton` inside needs its own `disabled`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | On the **root**: the full row of children in visual order — any mix of `<InputGroup.Addon>`, `<Button>`, `<Select>`, `<Input>`, raw `<input>`. Order in the template is the order rendered left-to-right. On **`<InputGroup.Addon>`**: the addon content — text (`https://`, `.com`, `$`), an Azion icon `<i>`, or any small inline node; kept short by convention (long content breaks the fixed row height). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-addon`
- `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-input`

## Sub-components

Folder layout:

```
packages/webkit/src/components/input/input-group/
├── input-group.vue                      # root
├── input-group-addon/
│   └── input-group-addon.vue            # <InputGroup.Addon>
├── input-group-input/
│   └── input-group-input.vue            # <InputGroup.Input>
└── index.ts                             # compound wire-up (Object.assign)
```

Public members of the compound:

| Member | Attached name | Standalone export | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Root | — (the compound itself) | `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-root` | The container. Orchestrates borders, seams, focus ring, and states. |
| `<InputGroup.Addon>` | `Addon` | `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-addon` | Static-content island (icon, text like `https://`, `.com`, `$`) rendered with the darker `--bg-canvas` fill and muted text. |
| `<InputGroup.Input>` | `Input` | `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-input` | Borderless middle `<input>`, with the same inline padding as `Input` (`--spacing-sm`). Props: `modelValue` (`''`), `type` (`'text' | 'email' | 'number' | 'password'`, default `'text'`: the restricted set of `Input`, plus `password`to mask a secret value that a reveal control in an addon toggles back to`text`), `placeholder` (`''`), `autocomplete`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `required`, `invalid`(all`false`); emits `update:modelValue`. Reads `id`, `aria-describedby`, `invalid`, `disabled`and`required`from an enclosing`Field` (an explicit prop/attribute wins). |

The root reads `invalid`, `disabled` and `required` from an enclosing `Field` too, OR-ed with its own props, so a `Field`'s state styles the whole group. The root then provides the Field context to its children with `invalid` and `disabled` OR-ed with the group's own (the parent Field's id, description, title and `required` pass through), so the group's state reaches the controls inside.

## States

- Visual states on root: `default`, `hover`, `focus-within`, `invalid`, `required`, `disabled`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop and drives the root height (`small`=`h-7`, `medium`=`h-8`, `large`=`h-10`); every direct child is capped at the root height (`max-h-full`), so a child left at a larger size cannot stick out of the frame
- Only one focus indicator is visible when a descendant is focused: the group draws the single `focus-within` ring on its root, and the inner input primitives' own focus rings are suppressed via `[&_*]:focus-visible:!ring-0 [&_*]:focus-within:!ring-0` so `Button`, `Select.Trigger`, `Input` wrappers, and raw `<input>` share the group's ring instead of stacking their own on top
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop; `aria-invalid` lands on the controls inside, not on the root
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop (no `aria-required` on the group root)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop; sets `aria-disabled="true"`
- Border semantics mirror `input` (independent, not compound):
  - `data-invalid` → `var(--danger-border)`
- Hover (only when not focus-within, not invalid, not disabled): `border-(--border-strong)`
- Focus-within: 2-ring at `var(--ring-color)` with `var(--bg-canvas)` offset (suppressed when `data-disabled`)
- Disabled: `bg-(--bg-disabled)`, `text-(--text-disabled)`, `cursor-not-allowed`, hover ignored, focus-within ring suppressed
- Child seams (applied by the root via Tailwind child selectors):
  - `[&>*:first-child]:rounded-l-(--shape-control)` and `[&>*:not(:first-child)]:rounded-l-none`
  - `[&>*:last-child]:rounded-r-(--shape-control)` and `[&>*:not(:last-child)]:rounded-r-none`
  - `[&>*:not(:last-child)]:border-r-(color:--border-default) [&>*:not(:last-child)]:border-r` — a single vertical seam between adjacent children, drawn on the left child so child components keep their own left border intact
  - Child components' own outer borders remain — the root's outer border sits on top, so double lines are avoided by the child selector removing the _inner-facing_ border only
- No clip: the root does not set `overflow`, so the `aria-hidden` touch-target layers of the controls inside (`data-slot="touch-target"`, shown under `pointer-coarse:`) reach the 44 px hit height past the frame. Instead of being clipped to the rounded frame, fills stay inside it by rounding: the outer corners of the first and last child are the frame's `--shape-control` radius (`!` so a child `Button` cannot override them), and every control inside a child (`button`, `a`, `[role=combobox]`, `[data-slot=input]`) and every wrapper between them takes `rounded-[inherit]`, so a hover or selected fill follows the frame's corner.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the root shows a `focus-within` ring (`ring-2 ring-(--ring-color) ring-offset-2 ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`) whenever any descendant (any child control or the middle input) has focus. The middle input renders `focus:ring-0 outline-none` so the group's ring is the only visible focus indicator. Suppressed when `data-disabled` is present. Child components (`Button`, `Select`) retain their own focus behavior internally but the group's ring is visually authoritative.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the children in DOM order. No custom keybindings on the group.
- ARIA: root uses `role="group"` with `aria-disabled`; `aria-invalid` is set on the controls inside (ARIA 1.2 does not allow it on `group`); `required` is styling only on the root. Each child keeps its own `aria-*` — the group does not duplicate.
- `<InputGroup.Addon>` is decorative-by-default; when its content is not conveyed elsewhere the consumer should annotate it (`aria-hidden="true"` for pure decoration, or a visible-only label the middle input references via `aria-describedby`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for addon text against `var(--bg-canvas)`; ≥3:1 for the border in every state.
- Motion: color transitions on state changes are `duration-150 ease-out` and pair with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target ≥32×32 px for interactive children (matches root height `h-8`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import InputGroupInput from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group-input'
  import InputGroupRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group-root'
</script>

<template>
  <InputGroupRoot class="w-full max-w-(--container-xs)">
    <InputGroupInput
      aria-label="Domain"
      placeholder="domain"
    />
  </InputGroupRoot>
</template>
```

# Language Select

> A searchable picker for the interface language, built like the country picker inside `phone-input`: every option is a BCP 47 language tag (`en`, `pt-BR`, `es`, `en-GB`), shown with its country's round flag and the language named in itself (`English`, `Português (Brasil)`, `Español`), and a search box at the top of the list filters by name, tag or country. `v-model` holds the BCP 47 tag of the picked option, ready to hand to `ConfigProvider`'s `locale`. It comes in two forms: the full field (`variant="outline"`, round flag and name, field-sized) for a form or a settings page, and the compact switcher (`variant="ghost"`, round flag and the tag in capitals such as `EN` or `PT-BR`, no border until hover) for a header, a toolbar or a footer. It offers the languages WebKit ships catalogs for and takes the consumer's own list through `options`.

- Import: `import LanguageSelect from '@aziontech/webkit/language-select'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A language switch in a header, a toolbar or a footer: `variant="ghost"`, the compact round flag and short code, beside the search and the icon buttons.
- A language setting on a settings page or a form field that asks which language a user, a page or a notification is written in: the default `variant="outline"` inside a `Field` or a `SettingsRow`.

## Do

- Bind `v-model` to the same value as `ConfigProvider`'s `locale`, so the picker and the strings move together.
- Name languages in their own language (`Português (Brasil)`, not `Portuguese (Brazil)`): a reader who cannot read the current language still finds theirs.
- Name every option with a BCP 47 tag (RFC 5646): the ISO 639 language, then the ISO 3166-1 region only when the option is a regional variant. The main variant of a language is the bare language (`en`, `es`); each regional variant adds its region (`en-GB`, `en-CA`, `pt-BR`), never an invented one (`en-UK` is not a tag; the United Kingdom is `GB`). The compact switcher shows the tag as it is, in capitals (`EN`, `EN-GB`, `PT-BR`).
- A regional variant needs no catalog of its own: `ConfigProvider` reads `en-GB` from the `en-GB` catalog when one is registered, else from `en`. Register one only where the wording differs.
- A tag with no region takes the flag of its likely region (`en` → `US`, `ar` → `EG`); set `country` when that is not the one you mean (`ar` → `SA`).
- Use `variant="ghost"` in a header, a toolbar or a footer, never the field: a field outline next to the toolbar's buttons draws two border colours in one row. Use the default `outline` in a form, where the field outline is the control's boundary (WCAG 1.4.11).
- Put it in a `Field` with a `Field.Label` in a form; on a toolbar or a footer, give it an `aria-label` only if the built-in `Language` name does not fit.

## Don’t

- Two or three languages that must stay visible side by side on a toolbar → use `toggle-group`.
- Picking a country (for a phone number, an address) → use `phone-input` or `select`.
- Setting the language of WebKit's own strings → that is `config-provider`'s `locale`; bind this picker's `v-model` to it.

## Related

- `config-provider` — takes the picked tag as `locale` and translates everything below it.
- `select` — the picker this component is built on; use it directly for any other list of choices.
- `phone-input` — the same flag sprite and searchable list, for the dial code of a phone number; LanguageSelect draws the flags round.
- `field` — wraps the picker with a label and a description when it sits in a form.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `LanguageSelectOption[]` | `(the languages WebKit ships — see Notes)` | false | Languages offered, in order: `{ value, label?, country? }` where `value` is a BCP 47 tag, `label` the language named in itself (derived from the tag when omitted), and `country` the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the flag (taken from the tag's region, else its likely region, when omitted). |
| `variant` | `'outline' \| 'ghost'` | `'outline'` | false | Trigger look: `outline` is the full field (round flag and name) for forms and settings; `ghost` is the compact switcher (round flag and the BCP 47 tag in capitals, such as EN or PT-BR, no border until hover) for a header, a toolbar or a footer. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Trigger text while no language is picked. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Language`). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token forwarded to the Select trigger. Heights: small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger and keeps the list closed. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the trigger when no Field labels it. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Language`). |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder and accessible name of the search box. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Search language`). |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Shown in the list when no language matches the search. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No language found.`). |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | BCP 47 tag of the picked language (`'pt-BR'`). Empty shows the placeholder. Via `defineModel`, so the picker also works unbound. |

## States

- Visual states delegated to `Select`: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `open`, `disabled`, and the `invalid` / `required` / `disabled` of an enclosing `Field`.
- `data-state="open|closed"` lives on the `Select` trigger; `data-disabled` mirrors `disabled`; `data-variant` on the root, the trigger and the panel mirrors `variant`.
- `variant="outline"`: the trigger is the field (`--border-input` outline, fills its container's width) and shows the picked option's round flag in its `#leading` slot and its name as the value; with nothing picked it shows the placeholder and no flag.
- `variant="ghost"`: the trigger is Select's `ghost` trigger (no border or fill until hover, sized to its content) and shows the round flag and a short code, both `aria-hidden`; the name stays in the value as visually hidden text, so the combobox still announces `Português (Brasil)`. The short code is the option's BCP 47 tag in capitals, exactly as the option names it: `EN` for `en`, `PT-BR` for `pt-BR`, `EN-GB` for `en-GB` (an underscore reads as a hyphen). With nothing picked the placeholder shows.
- Flags are round: the sprite flag cropped to a 16 px circle with a 1 px inset `--border-muted` ring, so a white flag keeps its edge on a white panel.
- `invalid` and `required` have no prop of their own: they come only from an enclosing `Field`, which `Select` reads, and show as the trigger's `data-invalid` / `aria-invalid` and `aria-required`.
- States that cannot occur: `loading` and `error` (the options are static data, never fetched), and `readonly` (no prop; a fixed language is shown as text, or with `select` and its `readonly`).
- An empty `options` array: the trigger still opens, and the list shows only the empty line (`No language found.`).
- Each row shows the round flag and the language name; the picked row carries the Select's check mark. The tag is not shown; the search still matches it.
- Search: typing in the open list filters by the language name, its tag, its country code, and its name in English and in the active locale (`Intl.DisplayNames`), accent-insensitive. No match shows the empty line as a `role="status"`.
- The flag sprite (`src/images/country-flags.webp`, shared with `phone-input`) loads with a dynamic `import()` after mount in the browser; until it arrives the flag boxes stay blank.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the `Select` trigger ring (`focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`); inside the list, the active row is highlighted (`data-active`) and announced through `aria-activedescendant` on the search box.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the trigger; `Enter`, `Space` or `ArrowDown` opens the list with focus in the search box; typing a printable key on the closed trigger opens it and starts the search; `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` move the active row; `Home` / `End` jump to the first / last; `Enter` picks and returns focus to the trigger; `Esc` closes and returns focus to the trigger; `Tab` closes the list without picking and focus moves on in page order; `Space` and every other printable key type into the search box and never pick.
- ARIA: the WAI-ARIA APG select-only combobox with a listbox popup: the trigger is the `Select` combobox button with `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, and its name from the enclosing `Field.Label`, else `ariaLabel`, else the catalog (`Language`); rows are `role="option"` with `aria-selected`; the search box inside the listbox popup has an accessible name and drives `aria-activedescendant`; flags are `aria-hidden="true"` (the name carries the meaning).
- Each option row renders the label inside the row with `lang` set to its own tag, so a screen reader reads `Español` with Spanish pronunciation.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for names and short codes, including the disabled trigger. The `outline` field keeps the `--border-input` outline (3:1 against the surface, WCAG 1.4.11); the `ghost` switcher is identified by its flag, code and chevron like every ghost control.
- In `variant="ghost"` the visible short code is `aria-hidden`; the trigger's value is the full name in visually hidden text.
- Touch target follows `size` (40px at `large`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ConfigProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/config-provider'
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import LanguageSelect from '@aziontech/webkit/language-select'
  import { es } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/es'
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-root'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const locale = ref('en')
  const page = ref(1)
  const catalogs = { 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }
</script>

<template>
  <ConfigProvider
    :locale="locale"
    :catalogs="catalogs"
  >
    <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md)">
      <Field class="max-w-(--container-xs)">
        <Field.Label>Language</Field.Label>
        <LanguageSelect v-model="locale" />
      </Field>
      <Pagination
        v-model:page="page"
        :total="120"
        :page-size="10"
      />
    </div>
  </ConfigProvider>
</template>
```

# Markdown Editor

> The text area of a reply composer: a person writes Markdown in a `Textarea`, formats it from a toolbar (bold, italic, link, bulleted list, numbered list, quote, code) or with Ctrl/⌘+B, I and K, checks the result on a Preview tab, and mentions a teammate by typing `@`, which opens a filtered list of people. It is the GitHub comment box pattern (decision SUP-02): plain Markdown text with helpers, never a rich-text (WYSIWYG) editor, so no editor library enters the package. The value is the Markdown string.

- Import: `import MarkdownEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/markdown-editor'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic
- Stability: preview. The API may still change in a minor release, named in the changelog, until the owner marks it GA.

## When to use

- Write a reply to a support ticket, a customer or a teammate.
- Add an internal note or a comment that can carry bold text, links, lists, quotes and code.
- Let the writer mention a teammate with `@` so the app can notify them.
- Any long free-text field whose content is shown later as formatted Markdown (a release note, an incident update).

## Do

- Wrap it in a `Field` with a visible label ("Reply", "Internal note"); without one, the field is named by the built-in "Message" label.
- Pass `mentions` only with the people who can be mentioned in this ticket; the menu shows the first eight matches, so a long list is filtered by typing.
- Listen to `mention-select` to record who was mentioned; the inserted text is `@` plus the person's `value`, so `value` is a handle with no spaces (`jane.doe`).
- Put the send button and the attachment control in the `footer` slot, not above the field.
- Render the posted message with `StreamingResponse` so it reads as the preview did.
- Keep `maxRows` so a long reply scrolls inside the field instead of pushing the page down.
- The preview and the posted message read `[1]` or `[2, 3]` as a citation chip (the `StreamingResponse` rule); write a bracketed number as `\[1]` when it is plain text.

## Don’t

- Plain text that is never formatted (a description, a reason) → use `textarea`.
- A question to an AI assistant, with send, model picker and attachments → use `prompt-input`.
- Code that people edit with highlighting and line numbers → use `code-editor`.
- Showing Markdown that nobody edits → use `streaming-response` (or `doc-markdown` on a docs page).

## Related

- `textarea` — the field this component is built on; every field prop (`placeholder`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `required`) means the same here.
- `prompt-input` — the AI prompt box; it shares the `@` menu list with this component (the private part `prompt-input/parts/prompt-input-menu-list.vue`, imported across components as `doc-layout` imports a `console-layout` part; it moves to a shared folder only if a third component needs it).
- `streaming-response` — the Markdown renderer the Preview tab uses; render the sent message with it so the preview and the posted message match. This build changes its root to merge the consumer `class` with `cn` (no API change, its test extended).
- `tabs` — Write and Preview are a controlled `Tabs` (the editor owns the value, `data-tab`, so a disabled editor still shows Write). This build moves `Tabs.Content`'s `tabindex="0"` before its attribute passthrough, so a panel whose first content is focusable can take `tabindex="-1"` (APG tabs pattern; no API change, its test extended).
- `prompt-input`/composables/use-prompt-input-menu.ts` exports its pure `findQuery` and `filterOptions` (the `@` token before the caret, at the start of the text or after whitespace; case-insensitive match on label or value; at most eight), which the editor reuses. The editor keeps its own small pick and key handler, because it inserts `@value` (not the label) through the undo-friendly path and stops Escape from propagating.
- `prompt-input`/parts/prompt-input-menu-list.vue` renders each option's label and description with `dir="auto"`.
- `streaming-response`/streaming-response.vue` merges the consumer `class` with `cn`.
- `navigation/tabs/tabs-content.vue` lets a consumer `tabindex` replace its default `0`.
- `field` — wraps the editor with its label, description and error.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder shown in the empty field. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the field when no Field label or aria-labelledby names it; empty uses the built-in Message label. Write it as the aria-label attribute. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the field, the toolbar, the tabs and the mention menu. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the value without letting it change: opens on the Preview tab, hides the toolbar and never opens the mention menu; the Write tab still shows the source. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border to the field and the preview and sets aria-invalid on the field. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required and sets aria-required. |
| `mentions` | `MarkdownEditorMention[]` | `[]` | false | People the menu offers after `@`; each is `{ value, label, description?, icon? }` and inserts `@` plus its `value`. Empty turns the menu off. |
| `minRows` | `number` | `4` | false | Lines the empty field shows; the field grows with its content from here. |
| `maxRows` | `number` | `12` | false | Lines the field grows to before it scrolls; `0` sets no limit. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mention-select` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, mention: MarkdownEditorMention)` | Fires when a person is picked from the `@` menu (click, Enter or Tab), after `@value` is inserted into the text. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `footer` | — | A row under the field for attachments and actions (an attach button, a Send button); omitted when empty. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The Markdown text via `defineModel`; updates on every input, toolbar action and mention. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus`, `filled`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `required` (no visual change: the wrapping `Field` label carries the Required marker); the field's own states come from `Textarea`.
- `data-tab` on the root: `write` | `preview`, the open tab.
- `data-disabled` and `data-invalid` on the root mirror the props or the wrapping `Field`'s state; `data-readonly` mirrors the `readonly` prop only (`Field` has no read-only state).
- Write tab: the toolbar shows; each button inserts its Markdown at the selection. Preview tab: the toolbar hides and the Markdown renders in a box the shape of the field (`data-slot="preview"`); an empty value shows the muted text "Nothing to preview".
- Mention menu: `data-mention-state="open|closed"` on the root. Open while the `@` token before the caret matches at least one person and the field is editable: the listbox renders above the field (or below it, when there is not enough room above and more below), the match count is spoken in the polite live region, and the field carries `aria-controls` (the listbox) and `aria-activedescendant` (the highlighted option). Closed: no listbox in the DOM, and the field carries neither attribute (`aria-autocomplete="list"` stays while `mentions` is not empty). No match, Escape, a pick, or the caret leaving the token closes it.
- `disabled`: field, toolbar buttons and tab triggers disabled; the mention menu never opens.
- `readonly`: the editor opens on the Preview tab, so a reader sees the rendered note first; the toolbar is not rendered (nothing in it could act), keyboard shortcuts do nothing, the mention menu never opens; the Write tab still shows the source for copying.
- Preview loading: the renderer is a lazy chunk (see Performance). Until it arrives the preview box keeps its `minRows` height, carries `aria-busy="true"` and `data-loading`, and shows the muted text "Loading preview" (`markdownEditor.previewLoading`). If the chunk fails to load, the box shows the Markdown source as plain text (`whitespace-pre-wrap`), so the writer still reads what they wrote; there is no retry button.
- Empty: an empty value shows the muted "Nothing to preview" (`markdownEditor.emptyTitle`). A send error belongs to the host's `Field` error, not to the editor.
- Every insertion (toolbar buttons, Ctrl/⌘+B, I, K, a picked mention, and `insert()`) keeps the browser's undo history: text goes in through `document.execCommand('insertText')`; where that returns false the component falls back to `setRangeText` plus an `input` event, which is not undoable.
- What each action inserts (GitHub's markers), on the selection or at the caret:
  - Bold `**text**`, Italic `_text_`; with no selection the empty markers go in with the caret between them; a selection already wrapped in the markers is unwrapped.
  - Link `[text](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/url)` with `url` selected; with no selection `[](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/url)` with the caret between the brackets. The `url` word is the `markdownEditor.linkPlaceholder` string.
  - Bulleted list `- `, Numbered list `1. `, `2. `…, Quote `> `: the selection grows to whole lines and every line gets the prefix; when every line already has it, it is removed.
  - Code: a selection inside one line becomes `` `text` ``; a selection over several lines becomes a fenced block (three backticks on their own lines around it).
- Switching to Preview unmounts the field (a `Tabs.Content` panel renders only when active), so the browser's undo history does not survive a round trip through Preview; the value does.
- The preview box has the field's minimum height (`minRows` lines), so switching tabs on a short reply does not change the height.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the field, tabs and toolbar buttons keep the focus rings of `Textarea`, `Tabs.Trigger` and `IconButton`. Both panels take `tabindex="-1"`, so neither `Tabs.Content` panel is a stop of its own: in Write the first content is the field; in Preview the preview box (`data-slot="preview"`, `tabindex="0"`) is the one focus stop, with `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the box itself.
- Keyboard map:
  - Tab order: the active tab (Write or Preview), then the toolbar (one stop, Write only), then the field (Write) or the preview box (Preview), then the controls in the `footer` slot.
  - In the field: Ctrl+B (⌘B on Apple) bold, Ctrl+I (⌘I) italic, Ctrl+K (⌘K) link; each wraps the selection, or inserts the empty markers with the caret between them.
  - `@` opens the menu only at the start of the text or after whitespace, so an email address (`jane@example.com`) never opens it mid-word; the text typed after `@` up to the caret filters the people by label or value, case-insensitively.
  - With the mention menu open: ArrowDown / ArrowUp move the highlight (wrapping), Enter or Tab insert `@value` and a space, Escape closes the menu and stops there (a surrounding dialog stays open); typing keeps filtering; the menu closes when the caret leaves the `@` token.
  - Toolbar (`role="toolbar"`, WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern): Tab enters on one button (roving `tabindex`), ArrowRight / ArrowLeft move to the next / previous button (swapped under `dir="rtl"`), Home / End go to the first / last; Enter or Space applies the format and returns focus to the field with the new selection.
  - Tabs: the `Tabs` keyboard map (arrows between Write and Preview, automatic activation).
- ARIA: the toolbar carries `aria-label` "Formatting" and `aria-controls` the field; each button has its accessible name ("Bold") and `aria-keyshortcuts` (`Meta+B Control+B`) for the three with shortcuts. The field keeps its native textbox role (ARIA in HTML allows no `combobox` role on `textarea`) and takes the combobox attributes the role allows: `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-controls` (the listbox, while open) and `aria-activedescendant` (the highlighted option). The menu is `role="listbox"` with `aria-label` "People"; options are `role="option"` with `aria-selected`. The match count is announced in a polite live region ("3 people").
- Accessible name: from the wrapping `Field` label, or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` passed to the editor (forwarded to the field); with neither, the built-in "Message".
- Contrast: only documented token pairs (`rules/webkit-tokens.md` § Contrast); the muted empty-preview text is `--text-muted` on `--bg-surface`; the disabled preview is `--text-disabled` on `--bg-disabled`, the pair `Textarea` uses (disabled text is outside the WCAG 1.4.3 minimum).
- Motion: none of its own (see Motion).
- Touch targets: toolbar buttons are `IconButton` size `small` with its 44 × 44 px hit area on a coarse pointer (TT01); menu options take `min-h-11` on a coarse pointer.

## Examples

### Default

  import MarkdownEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/markdown-editor'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const reply = ref('')

    { value: 'jane.doe', label: 'Jane Doe', description: 'jane.doe@example.com' },
    { value: 'john.smith', label: 'John Smith', description: 'john.smith@example.com' },
    { value: 'alex.morgan', label: 'Alex Morgan', description: 'alex.morgan@example.com' },
    { value: 'priya.patel', label: 'Priya Patel', description: 'priya.patel@example.com' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Field class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <Field.Label>Reply</Field.Label>
    <MarkdownEditor
      v-model="reply"

      :mentions="people"
    />
  </Field>

<!-- components/multi-select.md -->

# Multi Select

> Select control specialised for choosing many options from a list. The trigger field mirrors `Input`'s visual API (size, hover/focus/filled/disabled/invalid/required states) so a MultiSelect sits next to other form fields without visual drift. The dropdown panel is teleported to `body` and anchored to the trigger by the shared `usePlacement` composable — no `@floating-ui` runtime. Every option row carries a checkbox indicator (the `Checkbox` webkit component), optionally a leading slot/icon and a trailing tag. Search and "Create new" footer are exposed as slots on `<MultiSelectContent>`. Since spec v4 the trigger can also show the selection as removable chips (`variant="chips"`, capped by `chipLimit` with a `+N more` chip), take typed text to filter the options in place (`searchable`), offer an `Add "…"` row for a typed value that matches no option (`allowCustom`, emits `create`), and render its own loading, error and empty list states (`loading`, `error`, `emptyTitle`) — the same vocabulary as `combobox`. MultiSelect is the one multi-pick field (`Select` picks exactly one): `modelValue` is always an array and the indicator is always a checkbox. Aligned with Figma frame `3899:29362` (options panel). The trigger reuses the `Input`/`Select` trigger visuals.

- Import: `import MultiSelectRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import MultiSelect from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use MultiSelect whenever the person picks several values from a list in a form field; the chosen ones show as a count or chips in the trigger. For two to five options that fit on screen use a Checkbox per option; to build a large subset with both sides visible use TransferList.
- Choosing several values from a long list (regions, tags, permissions) in a compact field.
- A filter whose selected values stay editable from the same dropdown.
- Grouped options with icons or trailing tags, optionally with search.
- Tagging a record with labels people pick or type (`variant="chips"` + `searchable` + `allowCustom`).
- Options fetched from a server as the person types (`searchable`, `:filter="false"`, `@search`, `loading`, `error`).

## Do

- `modelValue` is always an array; start it as `[]`, never `null`.
- Pass `displayValue` to summarise long selections (e.g. "3 regions") instead of a list that overflows the trigger.
- Keep each option's `value` stable and unique; selection is matched by value.
- Put a search input in the `search` slot and a create action in the `footer` slot of `MultiSelect.Content` — or set `searchable` (and `allowCustom`) to type in the trigger itself; do not combine the two.
- With `variant="chips"`, set `chipLimit` when the field sits in a dense row; leave it `0` in a form so every chip wraps and stays removable.
- `create` only reports the typed value: add the new option to your list and its value to the model in the handler.
- For a server-side search, set `:filter="false"`, fetch on `search`, and drive `loading` and `error` from the request.

## Don’t

- Only one value may be chosen → use `select`.
- A labelled form field with helper/error text → put it inside a `field`.
- A handful of options that fit on screen → use a horizontal `field` with a `checkbox` for each.
- The user builds a subset and needs the chosen and remaining items side by side → use `transfer-list`.
- Free-form tags with no list of options to pick from → use `tag-editor`.

## Related

- `select` — single-choice counterpart.
- `field` — wraps this control with its label, description and error; it hands the trigger its id and state.
- `transfer-list` — dual-list transfer for building larger subsets.
- `checkbox` — the indicator every option row renders.
- `combobox` — single-value field with typed text; `searchable`, `allowCustom`, `filter`, `loading` and `emptyTitle` share its meaning.
- `chip` — each selected value in `variant="chips"`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Trigger placeholder shown when no option is selected. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects trigger height (small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px) matching `Input`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger and prevents opening; applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only; the current selection is visible but the dropdown cannot open. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; sets `aria-required` on the trigger. Visual indicator (asterisk) is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid` on the trigger. |
| `displayValue` | `(value: TValue[]) => string` | `undefined` | false | Custom formatter used by the trigger to render the selected labels; receives the current `modelValue` array. |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | false | Form field name. Set, the root renders one hidden input per selected value so a native `form` and `FormData` submit every selection under that name; `required` then adds a hidden required proxy that blocks an empty submit, and `disabled` leaves the values out. |
| `variant` | `'summary' \| 'chips'` | `'summary'` | false | How the trigger shows the selection: `summary` joins the labels (or `displayValue`), `chips` renders one removable chip per value. |
| `chipLimit` | `number` | `0` | false | With `variant="chips"`, the most chips shown before a `+N more` chip; `0` shows every chip and wraps. |
| `searchable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Types in the trigger: the text filters the options, `Backspace` in an empty field removes the last value. |
| `filter` | `boolean` | `true` | false | With `searchable`, hides the options whose label does not contain the typed text. Turn off when the server filters on `search`. |
| `allowCustom` | `boolean` | `false` | false | With `searchable`, offers typed text that matches no option as an `Add "…"` row that emits `create`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the loading row in place of the options while they are fetched. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Message shown in place of the options when they failed to load; empty shows the options. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the list when no option is visible. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `modelValue` | `TValue[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | `string` | The typed text, on each keystroke (`searchable`), and `''` when the panel closes and the text is cleared. Value event: no DOM event. |
| `create` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, value: string)` | The `Add "…"` row was activated (`allowCustom`), by click or by `Enter` in the field or on the row; `value` is the trimmed typed text. The typed text is cleared; the consumer adds the option and the value. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Composition slot; receives `<MultiSelectTrigger>` and `<MultiSelectContent>` (and the option tree inside it). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-item`

## Sub-components

- `multi-select-trigger/multi-select-trigger.vue` — With the default `variant="summary"` and no `searchable`, a bordered trigger button; otherwise a bordered field (`min-h` of the size, wrapping) that holds the chips (`…
- `multi-select-content/multi-select-content.vue` — Popover panel teleported to `body` and anchored with `usePlacement`; exposes `default` (the options), `#search` and `#footer` slots, typed with `defineSlots`, and scro…
- `multi-select-group/multi-select-group.vue` — Section wrapper for a labelled group of options; hidden while the typed filter hides every one of its options; renders a `text-label-sm` heading in `--text-muted` when `la…
- `multi-select-item/multi-select-item.vue` — Selectable option row; hidden (`v-show`) while `searchable` + `filter` and its label text does not contain the typed text (case and accent insensitive, in the active locale)…

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `TValue[]` | `[]` | `update:modelValue` | The selection via `defineModel`. Always an array; each item is the `value` of a selected `<MultiSelectItem>`. Fires when an option is toggled with the next selection array. Uncontrolled when unbound. |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state of the dropdown via `defineModel`. Fires when the dropdown opens or closes. Unbound, the dropdown keeps its own state, seeded by `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `opened`
- `data-state` on the root and trigger: `open` | `closed`
- `data-size` on the trigger mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-required`, `data-readonly`, `data-filled` mirror the matching props (or the selection state for `data-filled`)
- `data-selected` on `<MultiSelectItem>` when the option's value is part of the current selection
- `data-variant` on the root and trigger mirrors `variant`; `data-searchable` on the trigger mirrors `searchable`
- `loading`: `aria-busy` on the listbox and the loading row; `error`: the message row; `empty`: the empty row — each in place of the options, in the panel
- `data-variant="create"` on the `Add "…"` row
- Typed filter: while the typed text is not empty, every chunk is mounted so the filter sees every option.
- Long lists: above 300 options the list mounts in chunks of 100 as they scroll near view (unmounted chunks keep their height, 32 px per option), so opening a 1,000-option list stays within its runtime budget. The first arrow, `Home` or `End` key in the list mounts every option before moving focus, so keyboard navigation always reaches every option.
- `data-side` (`bottom` | `top`) and `data-align` (`start`) on the listbox panel mirror where it landed after flipping; `start` follows the text direction, so under `rtl` the panel lines up with the field's right edge

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on trigger and on every option row.
- Keyboard map (trigger): `Tab` focuses; `Space`/`Enter`/`ArrowDown` opens the panel; `Escape` closes it.
- Keyboard map (closed trigger): `Enter`, `Space`, `ArrowDown` and `ArrowUp` open the list (focus lands as described below); `Home` opens it on the first enabled option and `End` on the last; typing a printable character opens it on the first enabled option whose label starts with that character (with a search field, focus goes to the search field instead). Clicking the trigger while the list is open closes it. Tests: `multi-select.test.ts` › Select keyboard and naming (APG select-only combobox).
- Keyboard map (`searchable` field): typing filters and opens the panel; `ArrowDown` opens and focuses the first visible option, `ArrowUp` the last; `Enter` activates the `Add "…"` row when it is offered, else opens the panel; `Backspace` in an empty field removes the last selected value; `Escape` closes the panel, then clears the text; `Tab` closes and moves on. From the list, `Escape`, `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` return focus to the field instead of a trigger button.
- Chips: each chip's remove button is in the tab order and named `Remove <label>` (from `Chip`); removing one never opens the panel. The `+N more` chip is plain text.
- Keyboard map (open panel): opening focuses the search field when there is one, else the first selected option, else the first enabled option; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move between enabled options and wrap; `Home`/`End` jump to first/last enabled; `Enter`/`Space` toggles the focused option and keeps the panel open; typing a printable character moves focus to the next enabled option whose label starts with the typed text (characters typed within 500 ms add up; ignored while the search field has focus); `Escape` closes and returns focus to the trigger; `Tab` closes and moves focus to the control after the trigger; `Shift+Tab` closes and returns focus to the trigger. Tests: `multi-select.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: trigger uses `role="combobox"` with `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded` bound to open state, `aria-controls` pointing to the list. The teleported content is a plain panel holding the optional search field, the list and the optional footer; the list (not the panel) carries `role="listbox"`, so the search field sits outside it, and is named by the root's `aria-label`, else by the root's `aria-labelledby`, else by the enclosing `Field` label, else by the trigger (which always has an `id`). The list uses `role="listbox"` with `aria-multiselectable="true"`. Each option uses `role="option"` with `aria-selected` mirroring its selection. Decorative icons (`az az-chevron-down`, `az-heart`, etc.) are `aria-hidden="true"`. The checkbox indicator is decorative for screen readers (the `role="option"` + `aria-selected` carries the semantic); the inner `Checkbox` sits in an `inert`, `aria-hidden="true"` wrapper, so the option has no focusable descendant.
- Nested overlays: the open list joins the shared overlay layer stack (`useOverlayLayer`), so inside a `Popover`, `Dialog` or `Drawer` an option click or `Escape` in the list closes only the list; the host overlay stays open.
- `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` on the trigger mirror the matching props.
- With `variant="chips"` or `searchable`, the `combobox` role, `id`, name and `aria-*` move from the field to its control (the `input` gets `aria-autocomplete="list"`); the field itself is a plain container.
- List states sit in `role="presentation"` rows; a visually hidden `role="status"` region announces `Loading options`, the error message, the empty text, or `{count} options` after typing.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons + borders), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:animate-none` on every transition/animation-bearing class.
- Touch target: the trigger is drawn 28 / 32 / 40 px tall by `size`; on a coarse pointer an invisible `aria-hidden` child (`data-slot="touch-target"`) shown only under `pointer-coarse:` extends its hit area to at least 44 px tall. Option rows are 32 px on a fine pointer and 44 px on a coarse pointer, fills inset 1 px.
- Teleported content: the teleported `role="listbox"` content binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `ConfigProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import MultiSelectContent from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-content'
  import MultiSelectItem from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-item'
  import MultiSelectRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-root'
  import MultiSelectTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-trigger'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref(['opt-1'])
  const options = [
    { value: 'opt-1', label: 'Option 1' },
    { value: 'opt-2', label: 'Option 2' },
    { value: 'opt-3', label: 'Option 3' },
    { value: 'opt-4', label: 'Option 4' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-70">
    <MultiSelectRoot
      aria-label="Options"
      v-model="value"
      placeholder="Select options"
    >
      <MultiSelectTrigger />
      <MultiSelectContent>
        <MultiSelectItem
          v-for="o in options"
          :key="o.value"
          :value="o.value"
          >{{ o.label }}</MultiSelectItem
        >
      </MultiSelectContent>
    </MultiSelectRoot>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Number Input

> Numeric input field with optional increment/decrement spinner buttons. Use when the value is strictly numeric (counts, quantities, ports, thresholds, currency without formatting). Distinct from `input` because it enforces numeric type, supports `min`/`max`/`step`, and renders chevron-up/chevron-down controls on the trailing edge.

- Import: `import NumberInput from '@aziontech/webkit/number-input'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Capture a strictly numeric value (counts, quantities, ports, prices).

## Do

- Set `min` / `max` / `step` to constrain input rather than validating after the fact.
- Use `inputmode="numeric"` semantics for mobile keyboards.
- Set `nullable` on an optional field (a port, a limit) so a cleared field stays unset (`null`) instead of falling back to `min ?? 0`.

## Don’t

- The value is free text → use `input`.
- The user picks from a fixed set of numbers → use `select`.

## Related

- `input` — free-text sibling with the same field API.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Text shown when the input is empty. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects height, padding, and typography. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as read-only; spinner buttons are inert. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border/ring tokens. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required for assistive tech. |
| `min` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Minimum allowed value; spinner stops at this bound. |
| `max` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Maximum allowed value; spinner stops at this bound. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | false | Increment used by the spinner buttons and arrow keys. |
| `showButtons` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Renders the chevron-up/chevron-down spinner controls. |
| `nullable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Lets a cleared field emit null instead of falling back to min or 0. |
| `modelValue` | `NumberInputValue<TNullable>` | `0 as NumberInputValue<TNullable>` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `change` | `number` | Emitted when the user commits the value (blur or Enter). With `nullable` the payload is `null` when the field is committed empty. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` | — | Content rendered before the input (e.g. `$`). Both slots: `aria-hidden`. |
| `trailing` | — | Content rendered after the input, before the spinner buttons (e.g. `%`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `number` (`number \| null` with `nullable`) | `0` | `update:modelValue` | The value via `defineModel`, clamped to `min`/`max`; updates on typing and on the spinner. A cleared field falls back to `min ?? 0`; with `nullable` it emits `null` and shows the placeholder, and the spinner on a `null` value starts at `min ?? 0` (clamped). The component is generic over `nullable`, so the model and `change` are typed `number` unless `nullable` is set. A comma typed or pasted as the decimal separator is read as a decimal point (`12,5` is `12.5`): the native number field would drop it and read `125`. A second separator is ignored. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `filled`, `empty` (a `nullable` field whose value is `null` shows the placeholder)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-readonly` mirrors the `readonly` prop (no hover border, default cursor, as on `Input`)
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop
- The frame, its states, adornments and touch target are the private frame `Input` renders

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2` on `var(--input-ring-offset, var(--bg-canvas))`, as on `Input`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the input; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` increment/decrement by `step`; `Home`/`End` jump to `min`/`max` when defined; `Enter` commits and emits `change`.
- Direction: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"` (digits resolve to left-to-right inside right-to-left UI); a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: `role="spinbutton"` on the input (native `<input type="number">` provides this); `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` mirror the props; `aria-invalid` mirrors `invalid`; `aria-required` mirrors `required`; spinner buttons have `aria-label` ("Increment" / "Decrement") and `tabindex="-1"` so keyboard users use arrow keys.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated state changes.
- Touch target: on a coarse pointer the two steppers sit side by side in an 80 px column (about 40 px each), and each carries an invisible `aria-hidden` child (`data-slot="touch-target"`) shown only under `pointer-coarse:` that extends its hit area to 44 px tall (the frame stops clipping on a coarse pointer so the hit area is not cut). On a fine pointer the steppers stay stacked at the drawn size; arrow keys are the primary interaction. The field also has `Input`'s touch target; a press on the frame focuses the input.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import NumberInput from '@aziontech/webkit/number-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref(1)
</script>

<template>
  <Field class="w-full max-w-(--container-xs)">
    <Field.Label>Quantity</Field.Label>
    <NumberInput
      v-model="value"
      :min="0"
      :max="100"
      :step="1"
    />
    <Field.Description>From 0 to 100.</Field.Description>
  </Field>
</template>
```

<!-- components/otp-input.md -->

# Otp Input

> The field for a one-time code: the six digits an authenticator app shows, or a code sent by email or SMS. It looks like a row of boxes, one character each, but it is **one real text input** laid over the boxes, so the browser's one-time-code autofill (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`), password managers, paste and screen readers all see a single field. Typing fills the next box (auto-advance), Backspace empties the last one, and a pasted code (`123 456`, `123-456`, with a line break) keeps only its valid characters and fills every box. When the last box fills it emits `complete`, so the screen can submit without a button press. It replaces six hand-wired text inputs with focus moves between them; the `account/account-mfa-settings` block uses it to set up and confirm an authenticator.

- Import: `import OtpInput from '@aziontech/webkit/otp-input'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Multi-factor authentication: set-up confirmation and sign-in challenge.
- Verifying an email address or a phone number with a short code.
- Any short, fixed-length code the user copies from somewhere else.

## Do

- Label it with what the code is and where it comes from: `Authentication code`, and a description `The 6-digit code from your authenticator app.`
- Submit on `complete` only when the code is the last thing to fill; keep a Verify button for keyboard users and for a failed attempt.
- After a rejected code, mark it `invalid`, clear it, and keep focus in it.
- Use `group="3"` for codes people read aloud or copy from a phone; it draws a separator between groups and does not change the value.

## Don’t

- A password or a secret of free length → use `PasswordInput`.
- A long token or API key → use `Input` with a copy affordance.
- A number with a range → use `NumberInput`.

## Related

- `field` — wrap it in a `Field` for the label, the description and the error; the label names the input.
- `password-input` — the other credential input of the auth screens.
- `input` — the plain text field it shares tokens with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `length` | `number` | `6` | false | How many characters the code has; one box each. |
| `mode` | `'numeric' \| 'alphanumeric'` | `'numeric'` | false | `numeric` keeps digits and opens the number keypad; `alphanumeric` keeps letters and digits, upper case. |
| `group` | `number` | `0` | false | Draw a separator after every `group` boxes (`3` gives `123 – 456`). `0` draws none. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the field while a code is being checked. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Danger borders on every box and `aria-invalid`; set after a rejected code. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Native `required` and `aria-required`. |
| `autofocus` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Focus the field on mount, for a screen whose only task is the code. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `complete` | `string` |  |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The code typed so far, via `defineModel`, already filtered by `mode` and cut to `length`. |

## States

- `data-state` on each box: `empty` | `filled`; `data-active` on the box the next character goes to while the field has focus (the last box when the code is full).
- `data-invalid`, `data-disabled` on the root.
- Separators render between groups when `group` > 0.

## Accessibility

- One `input` carries the value, the name (from the `Field` label, an `aria-label`, or the catalog's `One-time code` when nothing else names it), `aria-describedby` from the `Field`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required`, `maxlength`, `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, `inputmode` (`numeric` or `text`) and `enterkeyhint="done"`. The boxes and separators are `aria-hidden`; a screen reader reads the input's value as typed.
- Keyboard: type to fill, Backspace to clear the last character, Tab leaves the field in one stop; the caret stays at the end, so Arrow and Home keys do not move it into the middle of the code.
- Focus: the active box takes the focus ring; the whole field takes one focus stop.
- Contrast: characters `--text-default` on `--bg-surface`, borders `--border-default` (3:1 non-text) in both themes.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import OtpInput from '@aziontech/webkit/otp-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const code = ref('')
  const complete = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <Field>
      <Field.Label>Authentication code</Field.Label>
      <OtpInput
        v-model="code"
        name="code"
        @update:model-value="complete = false"
        @complete="complete = true"
      />
      <Field.Description>The 6-digit code from your authenticator app.</Field.Description>
    </Field>
    <p
      class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
      role="status"
    >
      {{ complete ? 'Code complete. Verifying…' : '' }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/otp-input.md](components/otp-input.md).
